title: 3D Cerebrovascular Shape Completion from Biplane Angiography and CTA Prior
motivation: CTA provides patient-specific 3D cerebrovascular geometry for neurovascular planning, but its 0.5-1 mm resolution can omit small distal vessels and subtle pathology. Biplane DSA depicts vessels at substantially higher spatial resolution but supplies only a few 2D views, making direct 3D reconstruction underconstrained. Existing two-view methods either do not directly use patient-specific CTA as a reconstruction prior or assume CTA already contains all DSA-visible anatomy, motivating completion of the incomplete CTA vascular structure with DSA evidence.
method: The method formulates CTA-DSA fusion as 3D vascular shape completion. It initializes 3D Gaussians from CTA-derived vessel geometry and adds spatial and opacity primitives seeded from two biplane DSA projections. The Gaussians jointly represent vessel geometry and X-ray attenuation and are optimized to fit the DSA images while remaining consistent with the patient-specific CTA anatomy, allowing missing branches to be completed without rotational or temporal DSA data.

title: 3D Classification of Paramagnetic Rim Lesions in Multiple Sclerosis via Asymmetric QSM–FLAIR Modeling
motivation: In Multiple Sclerosis, paramagnetic rim lesions (Rim+) indicate chronic active inflammation and are associated with greater axonal damage and worse long-term disability progression. QSM is important for identifying Rim+ lesions, whereas routinely acquired structural MRI has limited tissue specificity; yet QSM interpretation is time-consuming, expertise-dependent, and affected by veins and imaging artifacts. Automated lesion-level classification is therefore needed, but the low prevalence of Rim+ lesions, limited data, and heterogeneous clinical imaging conditions make it challenging.
method: FRODO is an end-to-end 3D lesion-level Rim+/Rim- classifier that processes co-registered QSM and FLAIR patches. It explicitly treats QSM as the primary susceptibility signal and conditions its features with FLAIR structural context through spatial feature-wise linear modulation (FiLM). To improve robustness with limited, highly imbalanced data, the framework uses self-supervised cross-modal pretraining followed by supervised fine-tuning with contrastive regularization.

title: A 3D Unrolling Framework for Joint Sodium MRI Reconstruction and Concentration Quantification
motivation: Sodium MRI can non-invasively quantify tissue sodium concentration (TSC), an early biomarker of cellular viability and tissue integrity, but its intrinsically low signal-to-noise ratio makes accelerated imaging and accurate quantification difficult. Existing reconstruction and denoising approaches are slow, regularization-sensitive, may require registered proton MRI, or denoise conventionally reconstructed images as a separate post-processing step. This separation can accumulate errors and prevents direct optimization of TSC quantification from undersampled k-space.
method: SoReCon is a 3D deep-unrolling framework that takes gridded undersampled radial k-space as input and jointly reconstructs sodium MRI and estimates TSC. It uses sharpness-enhanced training data to learn vendor-style image appearance without post-processing. A differentiable concentration-mapping module performs B1 inhomogeneity correction, automatic phantom detection, and linear conversion to a TSC map, with concentration loss enabling end-to-end optimization.

title: A Clinical Guideline-Grounded Hybrid Agentic Framework for Holistic Epilepsy Management

categories.value: Multimodal Integration with Clinical / Genomic / Biomarkers

motivation: Epilepsy management spans seizure and syndrome diagnosis, prognostication, medication selection, epileptogenic-zone localization, and surgical decision-making, requiring coordinated interpretation of EEG, MRI, clinical factors, genomics, and other evidence. Existing automated models are generally restricted to a single task or modality and therefore do not represent multidisciplinary clinical care. Purely generative multi-agent systems can coordinate reasoning but may hallucinate or be poorly grounded in quantitative modality-specific signals, motivating a framework that combines reliable task models with clinically grounded coordination.
method: EPI-GUIDE is a guideline-grounded hybrid multi-agent framework for multi-modal, multi-task epilepsy management. Modality-specific discriminative models produce structured task predictions, which are transformed into textual auxiliary evidence, while modality-specific generative models produce clinical interpretations. The system aggregates both evidence types and supplies them to a central orchestrating agent that retrieves international epilepsy guidelines, follows structured clinical pathways, and coordinates iterative cross-agent reasoning to reconcile inconsistent findings and make final decisions.

title: A Confounder-aware Representation Learning Framework for Alzheimer’s Disease Classification
motivation: Early AD diagnosis is clinically important, but early neuroimaging changes are subtle and brain structure varies substantially across individuals. Existing deep models can exploit scanner, acquisition, demographic, or other spurious cues rather than disease-relevant signals, limiting robustness across cohorts and sites.
method: The proposed multimodal framework combines a ResNet-based imaging backbone with an MLP for tabular covariates. Its Mask Decoupling Module (MDM) masks individual 3D patches and measures prediction changes to emphasize structurally informative regions, while confounder-aware patch modulation conditions local visual features on covariates to attenuate confounder-linked variation.

title: A Counterfactual Framework for Directional Cell–Cell Interaction Analysis in Spatial Transcriptomics
motivation: Spatial transcriptomics can reveal cell-cell interactions in situ, but inferring which neighboring cell type directionally influences another cell remains difficult from single snapshots. Existing approaches are largely correlational or depend on predefined ligand-receptor pairs, so they do not explicitly test directional, sender-specific influence.
method: The framework trains a neighborhood-conditioned graph model to predict a receiver cell's state from its local spatial context. It then counterfactually replaces neighbors of a selected sender type and quantifies the displacement in the predicted receiver state with the Counterfactual Directionality Score (CDS); sender type-swap and within-type shuffle operators separate sender identity effects from intra-type heterogeneity.

title: A Deep Learning Surrogate Model for Microwave Thermal Ablation: From Preoperative Planning to Intraoperative Re-planning
motivation: MWA outcomes depend on treatment settings and patient-specific anatomy, especially vascular perfusion and the heat-sink effect. Manufacturer charts ignore these factors, whereas high-fidelity FEM simulations are too slow to repeatedly solve the inverse optimization problems required for clinical planning or intraoperative correction.
method: The method learns a real-time surrogate for liver MWA from simulated ablations on synthetic anatomies containing tumors and vascular structures. Conditioned on antenna position, power, duration, and patient-specific 3D perfusion maps, it predicts thermal damage maps and necrosis volumes; this prediction is embedded in a physics-based optimization loop for planning and re-planning after antenna misplacement.

title: A Flexible Structure-Guided Feature Aggregation Paradigm for Efficient Vascular Representation
motivation: Vascular images contain thin, branching, tortuous structures with large scale variation, making continuity and topology difficult to preserve. Existing structural priors are often implicit, local, or isotropic, and lack a backbone-agnostic mechanism for explicitly aggregating long-range anatomical dependencies while selectively reinforcing difficult regions.
method: The method adds a lightweight Vascular Structural Prior Branch to hierarchical backbone features. It constructs structure-aligned sampling paths, samples and fuses features along those paths to create a residual structural update, and uses a learned difficulty gate to inject that update more strongly in challenging regions; the module can be integrated with CNN, transformer, or state-space backbones.

title: A Guideline-Aware AI Agent for Zero-Shot Target Volume Auto-Delineation
motivation: CTV delineation requires complex, non-isotropic margins that account for tumor location and anatomical barriers, making manual work laborious and variable. Supervised segmentation models are tied to costly expert annotations and require retraining when clinical guidelines or institutional protocols change.
method: OncoAgent uses a two-phase planning-and-execution architecture to convert free-text guidelines into an executable delineation plan and then into 3D target contours. It combines an LLM agent with pretrained OAR segmentation models and geometric operations, allowing the agent to apply guideline-specified margins and anatomical barriers without target-volume annotations.

title: A Heterogeneous Prognosis Prediction Framework with Global Brain Connectivity and Local Image Features
motivation: Diffuse glioma prognosis is highly heterogeneous, and accurate risk prediction is important for personalized treatment. Most radiomics and deep learning approaches focus on local tumor features, overlooking tumor-induced disruptions and compensatory changes in global brain connectivity that may be prognostically relevant.
method: The framework couples a DTI-based GNN for global brain connectivity with an sMR-based local feature network (LFN). In an iterative pipeline, connectivity guides regional feature extraction and the resulting regional features refine GNN nodes; the connectivity model explicitly incorporates tumor-related compensatory reorganization.

title: A Hierarchical Multi-Task Framework for Dementia Diagnosis via Pathological Feature Learning from Multi-Organ Data
motivation: Dementia involves systemic dysfunction beyond the brain, and mixed etiologies are common despite overlapping clinical manifestations. Existing diagnosis models are predominantly brain-centric, can confuse normal aging with pathology, and commonly frame etiology as a mutually exclusive single-label task.
method: MoMmNet aligns heart, gut, liver, kidney, and clinical-text features with a brain-anchored semantic space through feature alignment. A normative-memory-based Pathological Feature Decoupling module uses statistical priors to isolate pathology-related features from demographic variation, and Progressive Multi-Etiology Inference first stages cognition then applies parallel binary classifiers to detect single or co-occurring etiologies.

title: A Modality-Aware Mixture-of-Experts Framework for Clinical Multimodal Breast Ultrasound Diagnosis

categories.value: Multimodal Integration with Clinical / Genomic / Biomarkers

motivation: B-mode breast ultrasound is routinely complemented by functional imaging, but many CADx models remain B-mode-centric. Their robustness is insufficiently established under clinical uncertainty, lesion-position variation, long-tailed phenotypes, multi-vendor acquisition shifts, and incomplete multimodal availability.
method: The work constructs a paired clinical benchmark for B-mode ultrasound with CDFI, elastography, or CEUS under heterogeneous acquisition conditions. MA-MoE extracts complementary features with CLIP and SAM, then uses constrained Shared-Specific Mixture-of-Experts routing so modality-specific experts retain functional cues while shared experts model cross-modal pathological consensus.

title: A Multi-center Benchmark for Abdominal Disease Diagnosis and Report Generation from Non-Contrast CT

categories.value: AI for Neglected Diseases & Limited-Resource Settings
AI for Population Health, Public Health & Epidemiology

motivation: Multiphasic CECT is the clinical standard for abdominal lesion characterization but can be contraindicated or inaccessible because of contrast risks, cost, and supply constraints. Existing NCCT research is largely confined to isolated organs or pathologies, and there has been no public benchmark for multi-organ diagnosis and comprehensive report generation from NCCT alone.
method: This work releases a multi-center benchmark of paired single-phase NCCT, triphasic CECT reference information, and contrast-enhanced radiology reports. It formalizes multi-label abdominal disease classification and free-text report generation from NCCT, and evaluates five chest-specific, generic multimodal 3D, and abdominal CT-oriented architectures under a unified protocol.

title: A Multimodal 3D Foundation Model for Light Sheet Fluorescence Microscopy Enables Few-Shot Segmentation, Classification, and Deblurring
motivation: LSM produces rich, high-resolution 3D data, but its size and the cost of voxel-level, expert, or paired restoration annotations make supervised analysis difficult to scale. Existing task- or structure-specific models do not generalize well across diverse organisms, stains, and imaging protocols, while volumetric LSM foundation models remain underexplored.
method: The authors pretrain a 3D LSM foundation model on heterogeneous unannotated volumes paired with textual descriptions. Joint masked reconstruction and image-text alignment learn structural and semantic representations, which are then fine-tuned with few annotations for segmentation, classification, and deblurring.

title: A Multi-view, Hybrid, Hypergraph Learning Framework with Causal Perturbation for Early Alzheimer’s Disease Diagnosis
motivation: MCI is a critical window for early AD intervention, but rs-fMRI diagnosis remains limited by subtle and complex network alterations. Common models rely on static, undirected pairwise functional connectivity and naive multiview fusion, missing directional relations, high-order coordination, and subject-specific noise variation.
method: HyperBrainNet derives whole-brain effective connectivity and combines it with five complementary rs-fMRI feature views. Adaptive Reliability Fusion computes sample-specific quality assessments together with global weights, while a hybrid hypergraph combines anatomical network priors with learnable hyperedges; node-hyperedge attention pooling identifies influential functional hubs.

title: A Neurosymbolic Framework for Interpretable Skeleton-Based Seizure Detection via Concept-Driven Logical Reasoning
motivation: Video-based seizure detection can support epilepsy care, but existing deep models are largely black boxes and therefore do not expose the motor signs underpinning a decision. Binary seizure versus non-seizure training also collapses heterogeneous normal activities, increasing false positives during movement-intensive non-seizure segments.
method: The neurosymbolic pipeline uses prompt-guided foundation models to obtain patient-centered skeleton sequences, then predicts ILAE-grounded spatiotemporal semiology concepts. Differentiable logic composes these concepts into Boolean seizure rules with auditable contributions, and fine-grained normal-activity subclasses provide more discriminative non-seizure supervision.

title: A Real-World Evaluation of Failure Detection for Liver CT Segmentation
motivation: Reliable liver CT segmentation is essential for volumetry, surgical planning, and lesion analysis, but deployed models can fail under real-world distribution shifts and unusual anatomy. Most OOD methods are assessed only on controlled research datasets, leaving their ability to identify clinically relevant segmentation failures uncertain.
method: The study evaluates six OOD or failure-detection methods on a deployed 3D nnU-Net liver CT segmentation model using internal and multi-site external clinical data. It introduces Pairwise Surface DSC, a surface-based adaptation of Pairwise DSC intended to measure contour quality more consistently with clinical acceptability, and calibrates thresholds on an independent cohort.

title: A Unified Few-Shot Framework for Multi-Atlas Neuroimaging Segmentation Leveraging Vision Foundation Models
motivation: Accurate brain MRI segmentation is needed for clinical and neuroscience applications, but atlas protocols use different anatomical label definitions. Atlas-specific supervised models require costly large-scale labels and retraining, while slice-wise transfer of 2D foundation models loses 3D context and can break inter-slice topology.
method: The framework adapts foundation-model features to 3D T1w segmentation through spatial-aware masked autoencoding, anatomical atlas anchoring, a 3D ConvNeXt adapter, and an O(N) Linear Transformer matcher for dense support-to-query label transfer. For an unseen atlas, its Lock-and-Finetune strategy freezes the heavy encoder and matcher and updates only a lightweight super-resolution refinement module; Gaussian-weighted volumetric inference yields seamless whole-brain outputs.

title: A Unified Framework for Joint Detection of Lacunes and Enlarged Perivascular Spaces
motivation: EPVS and lacunes are important CSVD markers with distinct pathology but similar CSF-like MRI appearance, making tubular EPVS difficult to distinguish from ovoid lacunes. Isolated or conventional joint segmentation methods miss useful inter-marker context, suffer from severe sparse-lacune imbalance, and can produce anatomically implausible false positives.
method: The proposed shared-encoder, dual-decoder framework uses zero-initialized Gated Cross-Task Attention to transfer dense EPVS context unidirectionally to sparse lacune detection while keeping their morphology-specific representations separate. It combines dense and weak EPVS supervision with Mutual Exclusion and Centerline Dice losses, then applies tissue-semantic Distance-Field Calibration at inference to suppress anatomically implausible predictions.

title: A Versatile Prompt-Driven Framework for Brain Segmentation, Parcellation, and Surface Reconstruction from Diverse Modalities
motivation: Brain segmentation, parcellation, and surface reconstruction are commonly handled by separate, modality-specific models, which limits shared anatomical learning and complicates deployment. Existing joint approaches are mainly limited to T1W MRI, and methods addressing acquisition variability generally do not jointly solve multimodal input adaptation and multiple output tasks.
method: uBrain is a single prompt-driven model for volumetric tissue segmentation, ROI parcellation, and surface reconstruction across T1W, T2W, FLAIR, PD, and CT. Modality and task prompts guide a Mixture-of-Modality-Experts encoder and Automatic Pathway task decoder, while GMM-based synthesis augments heterogeneous imaging characteristics during training.

title: AbdomenGen: Sequential Volume-Conditioned Diffusion Framework for Abdominal Anatomy Generation
motivation: Computational phantoms should provide realistic, diverse, and clinically targeted anatomy for imaging studies and stress-testing, especially in rare or pathological regimes underrepresented in retrospective data. Existing abdominal generators do not provide calibrated, habitus-aware, independent control of multiple organ shapes while maintaining inter-organ consistency.
method: AbdomenGen generates 11 organ masks sequentially with diffusion models conditioned on the body mask and previously generated structures. Its Volume Control Scalar (VCS) represents organ-size residuals decoupled from body habitus, enabling calibrated single- and multi-organ control while preserving global anatomical coherence; VCS distributions can also be selected to target a desired population.

title: ACA: Post-hoc Adaptive Logit Alignment for 3D Medical Image Segmentation
motivation: Even large 3D segmentation foundation models can degrade on unseen data because voxel-level prediction-confidence distributions shift between training and testing. Conventional UDA methods typically require costly gradient-based adaptation or auxiliary modules, which is impractical for dense 3D deployment and can cause catastrophic forgetting.
method: Adaptive Cliff Alignment (ACA) operates post hoc in logit space without labels, retraining, or gradient updates. It identifies the uncertain logit region, termed the cliff, and uses isotonic-regression-based quantile matching to align training and test voxel-level confidence distributions only within that region, preserving highly confident predictions.

title: Accurate Reconstruction of the Standard 12-Lead ECG from a Single Lead Based on Inherent Principles of ECG
motivation: Wearable ECG devices commonly record only one limb lead, which restricts their diagnostic value relative to hospital-standard 12-lead ECG. End-to-end learning approaches for reconstructing all missing leads underuse physiological relationships among limb leads and lack the richer limb information needed to reconstruct precordial leads reliably.
method: AURORA first uses the IGUANA learning model to reconstruct one additional limb lead from the measured lead. It derives the other limb leads through Einthoven and Goldberger vector equations, then feeds the complete limb-lead set to a second IGUANA model for six precordial-lead reconstruction; IGUANA combines lead representation learning with a target-lead generator.

title: ACMap: Across-scales Connectivity Mapping of Primate Brain
motivation: Brain connectivity must be understood across cellular, mesoscale, and macroscale resolutions, for which virus tracing and dMRI provide complementary information. Virus tracing is spatially local and densely labeled, but available methods cannot efficiently generate faithful large-scale streamlines from tracer projections or directly bridge them with dMRI-derived pathways.
method: ACMap formulates virus-tracer streamline reconstruction as a source-constrained shortest-path problem originating at the injection site. It uses a fast marching method with an interpretable tracer-intensity-based speed function to propagate fronts, compute a time-of-arrival map, and recover dense fiber streamlines that can be integrated with dMRI tractography.

title: AC-MIL: Weakly-Supervised Atrial LGE-MRI Quality Assessment via Adversarial Concept Disentanglement
motivation: Atrial LGE-MRI quality is essential for fibrosis assessment and atrial-fibrillation treatment planning, but motion, breathing, acquisition, and contrast issues often make scans non-diagnostic. Manual assessment is burdensome, whereas standard weakly supervised MIL gives only an opaque global quality prediction. Clinicians need localized, actionable explanations of whether failure arises from blur, contrast, or inadequate anatomical context.
method: AC-MIL decomposes weakly supervised volume-level quality assessment into clinically defined concept branches plus an unsupervised residual branch. An adversarial erasure mechanism prevents predefined-concept information from leaking into the residual, and a spatial diversity constraint separates concept attention maps. The resulting concept maps identify localized causes of poor image quality while supporting ordinal grading.

title: Active Evaluation-Induced Graph Network Based Medical Hyperspectral Image Classification for Tumor Diagnosis
motivation: MedHSI combines spatial and spectral tissue information for tumor diagnosis, but tissue heterogeneity, imaging noise, and spectral aliasing complicate classification. Conventional graph construction assumes correlations from spatial proximity or fixed spectral thresholds, which can connect tumors to normal tissue incorrectly. These erroneous edges corrupt message passing and blur diagnostic decision boundaries.
method: AEGNet uses a graph-network backbone and learns graph edges through an adversarial discriminator trained to distinguish intra-class from inter-class node pairs. The discriminator outputs dynamically refined edge weights, with sparsity and graph-smoothness regularization. A hierarchical calibration loss aligns hidden-layer features with final-layer features to limit propagation of errors caused by misconnections.

title: Active Source-free Domain Adaptation in Open-set Medical Image Segmentation via Decomposed Uncertainty and Prototype Discrepancy
motivation: Medical segmentation models degrade under domain shift, and active adaptation can reduce annotation burden by labeling only informative target samples. In practice, target data may contain anatomical or pathological classes absent from the source, while source data may be unavailable because of privacy constraints. Existing active source-free approaches do not assess the informativeness of such unknown classes, leaving open-set segmentation adaptation unaddressed.
method: ASFOSDA ranks target samples with an active open-set query strategy combining Class-aware Decomposed Uncertainty and Class-agnostic Prototype Discrepancy. CDU uses test-time augmentation to estimate aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty for unknown target classes, while CPD selects representative, nonredundant high-uncertainty samples using cross- and self-domain discrepancies. A target-refined self-training stage generates pseudo-labels for unqueried samples and combines them with annotated samples in semi-supervised adaptation.

title: AdaBIMBA: Adaptive Token Compression for Long Endoscopy Video Understanding
motivation: Endoscopy VLMs are commonly trained on static images or short, clinically limited clips, despite interpretation of full procedures requiring long-range temporal reasoning. Full-length videos provide necessary context but exceed practical transformer memory and compute budgets. Uniform subsampling can discard brief but critical findings such as bleeding or ulceration.
method: AdaBIMBA uses a two-stage adaptive token-compression module for question-aware long-video reasoning. A Token Scorer is trained with input-token gradients to estimate frame importance, then a Mamba-based compressor assigns each frame an importance-dependent compression ratio. This preserves clinically relevant frames and transitions while allowing substantially longer endoscopy sequences within a fixed memory budget.

title: ADAPT: Adaptive Profiling Transformers for Efficient Alzheimer’s Disease Diagnosis
motivation: Structural MRI supports AD diagnosis by showing distributed atrophy patterns, but manual volume review is laborious and variable. Fully 3D models retain volumetric context at high memory and computational cost, while efficient 2D models lose important context. Existing multi-view models also allocate equal computation to all planes despite their differing diagnostic value.
method: ADAPT factorizes a 3D MRI volume into sagittal, coronal, and axial slice sequences and processes them with four view-specialized transformer encoders. The encoders model within-slice, within-view, and cross-view relationships, while adaptive view profiling reallocates the fixed slice budget according to learned view importance. Pathology-driven morphological dilation and erosion augment atrophy-related variation during training.

title: Adapting Ordinal-Risk Alignment for Clinically Safe Diabetic Retinopathy Grading
motivation: DR grading guides scalable screening and timely referral, yet its five severities form an ordered disease spectrum. Standard multiclass objectives treat all errors symmetrically, neither representing grade distance nor reflecting that underestimating severe disease is more harmful than overestimation. Clinically safe grading therefore requires optimization aligned with ordinal progression and asymmetric risk.
method: RAO-RL first pretrains an ordinal representation using ordinal-inductive feature learning with a monotonicity constraint and cumulative probability regularization. It then applies group relative risk-averse policy optimization with clinic-guided rewards. The reward design incorporates ordinal distance and asymmetric penalties, particularly discouraging clinically dangerous underestimation of severe DR.

title: Adapting Without Access: Black-Box Bayesian Adaptation for Trustworthy Cross-Center Medical Image Segmentation
motivation: Segmentation models often fail across centers because imaging protocols, devices, and populations shift the input distribution. Clinical deployments may prohibit both source-data access and access to model parameters or gradients, making conventional adaptation infeasible; they also require reliable uncertainty estimates. The problem is thus to improve a streaming target-domain model's behavior without altering or inspecting its internals.
method: The framework keeps the deployed segmenter fixed and performs approximate Bayesian adaptation through a learned distribution of input-space perturbations. Latent posterior samples generate frequency-domain amplitude perturbations while preserving phase-based anatomy, and the black-box model's ensemble predictions provide uncertainty. Semantic anchors and an uncertainty- and similarity-gated memory bank form an empirical prior that constrains posterior updates and limits drift.

title: Adaptive Frequency-Guided Parallel Mamba Network for Polyp Segmentation
motivation: Polyp segmentation is important for early cancer prevention but is difficult under variation in polyp size, shape, texture, illumination, and boundary clarity. Visual Mamba can be efficient, yet flattening images disrupts 2D topology and its low-pass behavior can oversmooth small polyps and fuzzy boundaries. Fixed frequency partitions also fail to accommodate sample-specific spectral variation.
method: Polyp-AFMamba combines an adaptive parallel visual 2D-Mamba layer with dynamic frequency decoupling and frequency-guided decoder modules. Parallel multidirectional 2D scans preserve spatial continuity and capture complementary context; sample-adaptive DCT masks separate low- and high-frequency features. High-frequency processing enhances edges, while low-frequency regional priors generate region-specific dynamic convolution kernels for decoder refinement.

title: AdaSurvMamba: Dynamic Fusion and Semantic Scanning for Multimodal Survival Analysis

categories.value: Multimodal Integration with Clinical / Genomic / Biomarkers

motivation: Cancer survival prediction benefits from complementary morphology in WSIs and molecular information in genomic profiles. Existing fusion methods usually impose static multimodal interactions, although modality relevance varies across patients and regions. Fixed Mamba scan orders also separate semantically related but spatially scattered tissue patches and unordered genomic features, weakening long-range context modeling.
method: AdaSurvMamba integrates WSI and genomic features through Dual-Scale Importance-Aware Reconstruction and Semantic Aggregation Scanning. DSIR estimates modality relevance at sequence and token scales to reconstruct representations with patient-specific cross-modal interaction strength. SAS uses a shared prototype pool to reorder scattered tokens into semantically continuous sequences and modulates Mamba state transitions with global modality context and semantic priors.

title: Addressing Gradient Conflicts in Multimodal Fundus Disease Recognition with Fusion-Guided Learning
motivation: OCT and CFP provide complementary structural and surface information for fundus disease diagnosis. Conventional two-stream fusion emphasizes architecture but tightly couples encoders and fusion during training, causing gradient suppression, instability, and inter-modal optimization conflict. Limited strictly paired data and insufficient modeling of global cross-modal lesion correlations further constrain performance.
method: The method uses separate OCT and CFP encoders, a CMSA module, and fusion-guided gradient decoupling learning. CMSA applies intra-modal non-local attention and bidirectional cross-modal attention to align structural OCT and textural CFP features. FGDL separates optimization paths and uses conflict-aware gradient projection to guide unimodal encoders toward the multimodal optimum; category-consistent loose pairing increases training-pair diversity.

title: Addressing Tissue and Appearance Heterogeneity in Text-Guided Few-Shot WSI Classification
motivation: Text-guided few-shot WSI MIL can use vision-language priors with scarce labels, but still trails strongly supervised methods. Slide-to-slide shifts in tissue composition, staining, artifacts, and background destabilize key-instance selection and aggregation, especially for raw 5x features. Robust few-shot prediction needs both composition-balanced evidence and global context less sensitive to appearance variation.
method: HAT adds a Tissue-Composition Balancing Module and an Appearance-Robust Aggregation Module to text-guided MIL. TCBM clusters patches by tissue-related feature similarity and selects instances in a cluster-balanced manner. ARAM avoids raw 5x appearance features, instead selecting and aggregating stable 20x local structural patterns into a contextual representation of tissue organization.

title: AEGIS: Anatomy-Embedded Group-Invariant Segmentation for Fair Medical Foundation Models
motivation: Medical foundation models can show demographic- and site-related segmentation disparities, which may affect HNSCC radiotherapy planning. Under PEFT, direct fairness reweighting can conflict with limited adaptable features and reduce general accuracy, while adversarial disentanglement is unstable. A method is needed to reduce non-biological group bias without erasing meaningful anatomical variation or sacrificing core segmentation performance.
method: AEGIS adapts a frozen foundation-model encoder through trainable PEFT adapters and mask decoder under Dual-Synergistic optimization. Attribute-Conditional Feature Alignment aligns foreground prototypes across groups and aligns background prototypes only for non-biological site attributes, preserving biological anatomy. History-Aware Dynamic Weighting uses historically stabilized temperature scaling to prioritize poorly performing subgroups after a warm-up stage.

title: AffordTissue: Dense Affordance Prediction for Tool-Action Specific Tissue Interaction
motivation: Learning-from-demonstration and vision-language-action systems can automate manipulation, but do not explicitly predict where a tool should safely contact deformable tissue. Semantic segmentation identifies anatomy but not action-specific safe engagement zones, leaving limited controllability and verification before harmful contact. Surgical automation needs spatially explicit, tool-action-conditioned interaction guidance.
method: AffordTissue predicts dense tissue-affordance heatmaps conditioned on a surgery, instrument, and action prompt. A language encoder represents the tool-action specification, a temporal Video Swin encoder captures motion and tissue dynamics over past frames, and a DiT-style AdaLN decoder fuses them for per-pixel prediction. The framework is trained for action-specific safe interaction regions across cholecystectomy tool-action pairs.

title: Age Conditional Longitudinal Forecasting of Adolescent Functional Connectivity via Brownian Bridge Diffusion Models
motivation: Adolescence involves rapid functional-brain-network reorganization, and longitudinal FC prediction could address temporal sparsity and irregular sampling while modeling individual development. Existing FC studies often use cross-sectional analysis or SC-FC mapping and rarely incorporate age in longitudinal FC-to-FC forecasting. Traditional models may not simultaneously match the target state and preserve intrinsic network geometry.
method: The proposed framework encodes FC graphs with a Graph Attention Autoencoder into topology-preserving low-dimensional node features, then decodes them back to connectivity. Brownian Bridge diffusion operates in this latent space, anchoring trajectories at initial- and target-age domains rather than sampling from pure noise. Age conditioning guides direct prediction and generation of subject-specific FC at an arbitrary target age.

title: AGE-MIL: Anchor-Guided Evidence Learning for Patient-Level Prediction
motivation: Clinical pathology decisions integrate evidence across multiple heterogeneous WSIs for each patient, whereas conventional MIL is designed for slide-level bags. Direct patch-to-patient aggregation is computationally prohibitive, disrupts the patch-slide-patient hierarchy, and struggles with sparse distributed evidence. Patient-level supervision therefore mismatches conventional MIL evidence organization and can yield unstable, unreliable predictions.
method: AGE-MIL constructs a patient-level anchor by aggregating foundation-model slide representations to summarize global pathology. The anchor guides patient-aware retrieval of diagnostically relevant patches from the slides, which are refined and integrated by an evidence-aware representation module. Patient risk is modeled as progressive evidence accumulation to stabilize weakly supervised patient-level training.

title: Agent-Guided Relational Concept Discovery: Toward Interpretable Surgical Margin Assessment
motivation: Real-time REIMS could support intraoperative surgical-margin assessment, but models trained on small labeled ex vivo spectra may overfit and generalize poorly to noisy unlabeled operating-room data. End-to-end models also provide little insight into their biochemical reasoning. Supervised concept learning is attractive for interpretability but impractical because mass-spectrometry concept annotations are difficult to obtain.
method: Agent-Guided Relational Concept Discovery maps REIMS embeddings to learned concept activations without concept labels. A reasoning agent examines discriminative spectral patterns, refines concept descriptions, and adaptively adjusts their diagnostic weights through an auxiliary alignment loss. The concepts are grounded against metabolic knowledge to form an evolving graph linking concepts, metabolites, pathways, and tissue states.

title: AGGRNet: Selective Feature Extraction and Aggregation for Enhanced Medical Image Classification
motivation: Fine-grained medical-image classification, including severity grading and disease-subtype recognition, is hindered by high intra-class variability and subtle inter-class similarity. Models may attend to background or redundant regions rather than consistently diagnostic cues, while local features alone cannot resolve many distinctions. Better classification requires selective evidence extraction together with global spatial context.
method: AGGRNet introduces a Feature Extraction and Aggregation module with a Feature Extraction Module and a Feature Aggregation Module. Spatial and channel attention, together with a learned threshold, split feature maps into informative and complementary non-informative features. Cross-attention uses the two streams to aggregate global contextual relationships while biasing the representation toward diagnostically informative cues.

title: AHPR-Net: Anatomy-aware Hierarchical Prompting Refinement Network for Spine Image Segmentation
motivation: Spine segmentation is vital for surgical planning but difficult because vertebrae, discs, and nerves have complex structure and ambiguous boundaries. Conventional deterministic models do not quantify uncertainty, while single-level SAM prompts offer limited semantics and anatomical consistency. Reliable segmentation needs richer anatomical guidance and explicit treatment of boundary uncertainty.
method: AHPR-Net supplies a SAM-based segmentation network with hierarchical prompts encoding class semantics, anatomical relations, and multi-atlas shape priors. A dynamic prompt-tuning module adaptively selects and enhances heterogeneous prompt features before coarse-mask prediction. An uncertainty-guided refinement strategy explicitly models boundary uncertainty during training to improve structural reliability.

title: AI-Driven Pulmonary Congestion Assessment for Lung Ultrasound via Segmentation-Guided Transformers
motivation: Lung ultrasound can assess pulmonary congestion at the bedside through B-lines, but manual quantification requires expertise and varies substantially between operators. Clip-level classifiers often lack spatial interpretability, whereas pixel-level methods provide localization but can overlook temporal evolution. A clinically useful system must combine reproducible localization with temporal severity assessment.
method: The framework first segments B-lines in individual ultrasound frames, then converts segmentation-derived embeddings into temporal sequences for a transformer. The transformer aggregates inter-frame dynamics to produce interpretable clip- and case-level congestion severity scores. This two-stage design retains pixel-level B-line localization while incorporating their evolution across a clip.

title: ALFA: Biplanar X-Ray Reconstruction via Anatomy-Latent Field Adaptation
motivation: Biplanar X-ray reconstruction could provide CT-like 3D anatomy at lower dose and cost, but inferring a volume from two projections is severely ill posed. End-to-end supervised approaches entangle anatomy with acquisition geometry, require paired data, degrade under changed imaging settings, and can hallucinate population-average structures. Reconstruction needs both patient-specific anatomical consistency and projection consistency under the true device geometry.
method: ALFA first auto-decodes CT volumes with a shared implicit neural representation, learning a continuous anatomical latent manifold and one latent vector per subject. At inference, it freezes this decoder and optimizes the latent code using a differentiable forward model so synthesized projections match measured biplanar X-rays under the actual geometry. Separating anatomy-prior learning from geometry-aware fitting enables adaptation across acquisition setups without retraining.

title: Aligning Prototypes and Updating Null Spaces for Continual WSI Learning
motivation: Whole Slide Image analysis must adapt to sequentially arriving disease categories or modalities while avoiding catastrophic forgetting and respecting patient privacy. Large bags, absent instance labels, visually similar classes, and the inability of frozen old prototypes to adapt cause confusion and interference in existing continual MIL methods, motivating a discriminative and updateable representation strategy.
method: AlignMIL-NS is a rehearsal-free prototype-based continual MIL framework with two components. Prototype-Class Feature Alignment aligns class prototypes with within-task visual features while increasing separation between tasks. Null Space Class Feature Update refines prior-task representations only in task-specific null spaces, reducing interference from new tasks without retaining patient data.

title: All-in-One Augmented Reality Guided Head and Neck Tumor Resection
motivation: Positive margins in head and neck cancer often require intraoperative re-resection, but complex anatomy and specimen disorientation make relocation difficult. Pathologists usually communicate margin locations verbally, providing coarse spatial information, while manual or marker-based AR registration adds workflow burden; an accurate markerless solution is therefore needed.
method: The system relocalizes positive margins from a resected head-and-neck specimen onto the resection bed using HoloLens 2 depth sensing. It performs fully automated markerless registration through curvature-biased sampling, global alignment, automatic coarse-pose ROI cropping, and point-to-plane ICP, then overlays the margin locations in situ for AR guidance.

title: ALSAnchorNet: Biologically Informed Multimodal MRI Fusion for Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis Diagnosis

categories.value: AI for Neglected Diseases & Limited-Resource Settings

motivation: ALS diagnosis would benefit from subject-level integration of complementary structural and functional MRI biomarkers, but prior studies often use single modalities, population-level statistics, or generic fusion designs. Limited multimodal cohorts and the omission of ALS-specific neuroanatomical priors, such as early frontal vulnerability, restrict representation quality and clinical applicability.
method: ALSAnchorNet integrates resting-state fMRI, diffusion tensor imaging, structural MRI connectivity, and glymphatic/CSF biomarkers. Modality-specific projections feed a Frontal Anchor Attention module, which uses intra-frontal connectivity as a query to modulate whole-brain interactions and amplify disease-relevant features. A Biomarker Projection Network and Fusion Refinement Encoder combine the resulting representations for classification.

title: AMFG: Anatomy-Grounded Multi-finding Guidance for Training-Free Chest X-Ray Generation
motivation: Text-conditioned diffusion models can synthesize chest X-rays, but multi-finding reports often lead to omitted findings or anatomically misplaced abnormalities. Training-based reinforcement or adapter methods reduce portability across base models, while incorrect finding–anatomy associations can mislead downstream classifiers, motivating portable training-free spatial guidance.
method: AMFG guides a frozen text-conditioned CXR diffusion model only at inference time. A pathology classifier supplies finding-presence guidance, segmentation masks constrain cross-attention to anatomically correct regions, and an interaction signal enforces spatial consistency among co-occurring findings. These signals use existing public models and require no additional training.

title: An Artifact-Based Agent Framework for Adaptive and Reproducible Medical Image Processing
motivation: Applying imaging algorithms to real clinical datasets requires extensive, heterogeneous curation and cohort-specific workflow configuration beyond model design. Existing workflow engines provide deterministic execution only after configurations are specified and offer little dataset-aware adaptation or semantic inspection, while privacy constraints often prevent cloud-based assistance; a locally deployable solution must combine adaptability with reproducibility.
method: The framework adds a semantic layer above deterministic medical-image workflows through an artifact contract that records intermediate and final states with provenance. A semantic query module inspects contract-compliant artifacts, while a constrained agent assembles goal-conditioned configurations from a modular rule library. A workflow executor performs deterministic graph construction and execution, and the entire system runs locally.

title: Anatomically Accurate 3D Vessel Generation via 3-Phase Chebyshev Curve Diffusion
motivation: Large 3D vascular datasets are scarce, yet anatomically accurate synthetic vessels are needed for segmentation and intervention simulation. Existing skeleton-based generators use discrete point sequences that do not guarantee smooth curves, produce implausible curvature, and lose millimeter-scale size information through normalization; a continuous representation with physical-scale recovery is needed.
method: The method diffuses vessel curves directly in a continuous Chebyshev polynomial coefficient space. A three-phase polar decomposition separately models coefficient magnitude, direction, and radius, producing fixed-dimensional, length-independent C-infinity-smooth curves. Auxiliary mechanisms recover millimeter-scale dimensions, preserve trajectories, and calibrate per-edge diversity.

title: Anatomically Consistent TMJ Disc Segmentation via Semantic Anchoring and Clinical Priors
motivation: TMJ disc segmentation on MRI is needed for objective assessment of disc displacement and morphology, but the disc is tiny, low-contrast, and morphologically variable. General segmentation networks often mislocalize displaced discs and produce fragmented or over-segmented boundaries, causing unreliable measurements; robust localization and clinically informed refinement are needed.
method: TISC first localizes the TMJ disc in foundation-model feature space with Prototypical Semantic Anchoring, which aggregates adjacent-slice MedDINOv3 features and forms a prototype-driven similarity map. Clinical-Metadata Point Refinement then adjusts boundaries pointwise. Mouth Open Limitation metadata guides PSA attention and modulates refinement features through FiLM layers to account for displacement pathology.

title: Anatomy- and Site-Guided 3D Patch Diffusion for Robust MRI Harmonization
motivation: Pooling T1-weighted MRI from different sites introduces scanner effects that bias analyses and reduce reproducibility. Existing image harmonization methods may alter anatomy, blur fine structures through latent decoding, or require memory-intensive full-volume diffusion, and many are tested only on healthy cohorts; a scalable method must preserve detail and remain reliable in pathological data.
method: The framework performs conditional diffusion on overlapping, native-resolution 3D patches, conditioned on learnable site embeddings and site-invariant anatomical maps derived from gradients and high-frequency features. Randomized gamma perturbations reduce site-intensity leakage into the anatomical prior. Manifold-constrained classifier-free guidance stabilizes sampling while preserving subject-specific structure.

title: Anatomy-Anchored Self-Supervision: Distilling Vision Foundation Models for Invariant Ultrasound Representation
motivation: Ultrasound self-supervised methods often learn from whole frames or generic regions, which can encode speckle and background artifacts rather than clinically meaningful anatomy. Generic region proposals also fail under low-contrast, speckled boundaries, creating a gap between learned representations and anatomy-centered clinical reasoning; scalable anatomical supervision is needed without expert labels.
method: ANAUS uses LP-SAM with a learnable latent prompt engine and one-time domain adaptation to obtain anatomy masks without manual annotations. Its self-supervision combines inter-view, semantics-aware anatomy-separating alignment, which enforces invariance within the same structure and separation across structures, with contextual prediction that reconstructs corrupted core regions. Both objectives operate across a multi-scale feature hierarchy.

title: Anatomy-Aware Hierarchical Multiple Instance Learning for Interpretable COPD Diagnosis and Phenotype Analysis
motivation: COPD causes subtle, diffuse, and heterogeneous structural changes that are difficult to assess consistently from CT, while pulmonary function tests may miss early disease and do not provide regional information. Existing weakly supervised MIL models often treat slices as an unstructured set and focus on accuracy with limited anatomical interpretability, hindering phenotype understanding and clinical trust.
method: AnatoMIL segments the lungs into lobes and hierarchically aggregates slice features to produce lobe-level contributions. A dual-head design jointly performs COPD classification and ordinal severity prediction. The resulting lobe attention profiles are analyzed across stages to characterize spatial phenotypes and regional disease involvement.

title: Anatomy-Aware Prediction of Bronchoscopic Accessibility from 3D CT
motivation: Pre-operative bronchoscopy accessibility assessment is clinically important but currently relies on subjective, time-consuming CT inspection with substantial inter-observer variability. Prior work addresses airway segmentation, lesion detection, or handcrafted geometric associations rather than the functional accessibility outcome, and no standardized benchmark or end-to-end model exists.
method: The Anatomy-Aware Mixture-of-Experts model combines three specialized experts: a CT Expert for local lesion morphology, a Lobe Expert for regional anatomical priors, and a Path Geometry Expert for sequential bronchial-tree constraints. A gating mechanism performs case-dependent weighting and fuses these representations for accessibility prediction.

title: Anatomy-Aware Reverse Symmetric Self-paced Learning for Prostate Cancer Detection
motivation: csPCa detection in mpMRI has both severe lesion-to-background voxel imbalance and heterogeneous case difficulty, but existing methods mainly reweight voxels and present cases randomly. Conventional easy-to-hard curriculum learning may expose abundant easy cases before rare difficult cancers, while whole-volume difficulty signals can be dominated by background; anatomy-aware case scheduling is needed.
method: RSSPL is a model-agnostic case-level scheduling strategy that presents training cases from hard to easy, complementing voxel-level loss reweighting. It estimates difficulty from input gradients restricted to the prostate region, using anatomy to suppress misleading background signals. The schedule can be combined with different network backbones and imbalance-aware losses.

title: Anatomy-Aware Standard Plane Localization in 3D Ultrasound with Geometric Constraints
motivation: Localizing fetal-brain standard planes in 3D ultrasound is important for diagnosis but is labor-intensive, sensitive to poor image quality and large search spaces, and subject to inter-observer variation. Slice-classification methods ignore 3D geometry, while iterative or multi-stage methods suffer from initialization bias, error propagation, and cost; joint anatomy- and geometry-aware localization is needed.
method: The framework formulates localization of multiple fetal-brain standard planes as a joint multi-task problem. A segmentation stage supplies masks of key anatomical structures, which are fused with the 3D ultrasound volume to guide feature extraction and plane parameter prediction. An inter-plane geometric constraint loss regularizes the jointly predicted planes using their known spatial relationships.

title: Anatomy-Conditioned Domain Randomization for Zero-Shot 3D Cerebrovascular Segmentation
motivation: 3D cerebrovascular segmentation must generalize across modalities and acquisition protocols, yet supervised models often fail on unseen domains and require new annotations. Domain adaptation needs target data, while generic foundation models remain weak for vessels; existing vascular randomization largely ignores organ-level context despite extreme vessel sparsity, motivating anatomy-conditioned synthetic training.
method: The domain-randomization pipeline generates synthetic images conditioned on whole-brain anatomical label maps to preserve organ-level context. It adds vascular-specific morphology enrichment and contrast-aware randomized label-to-image synthesis, addressing vessel sparsity and limited morphological priors. A 3D CNN is trained only on these synthetic images and masks and evaluated without target-domain data.

title: Anatomy-Grounded Synthetic Coronary Angiography for Geometry-Informed Multi-view Matching
motivation: Cross-view correspondence in coronary angiography is fundamental for 3D reconstruction and intervention guidance, but overlapping projections, tubular repetition, viewpoint changes, and missing 3D ground truth make matching difficult. Dense expert annotations are expensive and ambiguous, leaving no scalable benchmark; physically grounded synthetic supervision is needed.
method: The framework synthesizes multi-view Digital Reconstructed Radiographs from patient-specific CCTA while simulating realistic C-arm geometries, yielding dense 3D-to-2D correspondence labels. GIMM performs coarse-to-fine matching by incorporating global C-arm angles for view orientation and epipolar information for localized pixel correspondences. The resulting dataset supports objective evaluation without manual correspondence annotations.

title: Anatomy-Guided Residual Motion Diffusion for Controllable 4D Cardiac MRI Synthesis
motivation: 4D cine cardiac MRI synthesis is limited by scarce annotations, privacy restrictions, inter-device shifts, and the need for physiologically coherent motion. Existing methods often entangle anatomy and dynamics, generate only intensities, or require dense proprietary labels, limiting controllability, aligned supervision, and cross-vendor utility.
method: The pipeline uses a semi-supervised VAE to learn a shared anatomical latent representation while jointly generating cardiac MR volumes and aligned segmentation masks. A static latent diffusion model generates subject-specific anatomy from diagnosis and volume priors, then a residual motion diffusion model predicts ED-referenced latent dynamics. This decoupling provides controllable anatomy and temporally coherent 4D sequences.

title: Anatomy-Structured Hierarchical MIL for Weakly-Supervised Thoracic Disease Detection in Chest X-Rays
motivation: Weakly supervised CXR detection must localize subtle abnormalities despite overlap and limited bounding-box annotations. CAMs and proposal methods search globally and may produce anatomically implausible evidence, while static coordinate or proxy-task priors do not restructure instance discovery for patient-specific anatomy; a dynamically anatomy-structured approach is needed.
method: ASH-MIL uses parallel cardiac, pulmonary, and agnostic observation branches built on a CXR-pretrained backbone. Patient-specific organ priors are injected as soft biases into decoder cross-attention, and hierarchical MIL first aggregates query hypotheses within branches before class-dependent fusion across branches. Localization is obtained directly from MIL-weighted cross-attention maps without box annotations.

title: Anatomy-Texture Aware Safe Gradient Guidance for Source-Free Domain Adaptive Echocardiography Video Segmentation
motivation: Source-free adaptation is needed for echocardiography because privacy rules prevent sharing source data, yet device, protocol, and population shifts degrade left-ventricle segmentation. Entropy minimization can become overconfident on speckle, shadows, and artifacts, causing catastrophic drift; adaptation must separate stable anatomy from variable texture and gate unsafe updates.
method: ATASGG-SFDA builds an anatomy-texture pseudo-label branch using a frozen source model as a coarse anatomical anchor and a momentum-driven adapter for target textures. Its Safe Gradient Guidance compares ATPSL and entropy-minimization gradients, suppressing EMSSL updates when they conflict with anatomical supervision. This preserves structural fidelity while adapting to target appearance.

title: Angio-Stitch: An Unsupervised Coarse-to-Fine Framework for Sequential Stitching of Confocal Laser Endomicroscopy Images
motivation: CLE provides cellular-resolution liver microvascular imaging, but its very small field of view prevents assessment of macroscopic continuity. Low contrast, repetitive textures, speckle, and non-rigid probe-induced deformation cause handcrafted and natural-image stitching methods to misalign and accumulate errors over long sequences, risking loss of pathological topology.
method: Angio-Stitch extracts masked multi-scale features with a ResNet encoder and aligns adjacent CLE frames using a Vascular-aware Perception Transformer. The transformer combines noise suppression, vessel enhancement, and dense non-local matching to regress global homography followed by local mesh deformation. A multi-scale Hessian-based vascular structure loss preserves topology, and chained transformations stitch the sequence with intensity-weighted fusion.

title: Angular-Constrained Hyperbolic Learning for Hierarchical Multimodal Survival Prediction
motivation: Multimodal survival prediction must integrate genomic signals with multiscale pathology, but token-and-fuse models often miss hierarchical semantics. Existing hyperbolic approaches mainly use geodesic proximity, over-aligning modalities despite intrinsic discrepancies and weakening modality-specific structures, which can compromise hierarchy-aware risk modeling.
method: HyperGP represents WSI patches, regions, slides, and pathway-level genomic anchors in a shared Lorentz hyperbolic manifold. Attention selects and aggregates important patches hierarchically, while risk-specific genomic prototypes provide prognostic anchors. A unified angular contrastive objective aligns modalities and prototypes using entailment-aware angular relations, and an angular hyperbolic decoder predicts survival.

title: Anomaly Detection in Fetal Echocardiography via Cross-Modal Translation and Region-Discriminated Error Calibration

categories.value: Multimodal Integration with Clinical / Genomic / Biomarkers

motivation: Congenital heart disease screening must detect many individually rare phenotypes, for which exhaustive labels are difficult to obtain. Reconstruction-based anomaly detection can confuse pathology with scanner and acquisition variation, especially because CFD signals are sparse and intermittent. A calibrated, acquisition-aware anomaly score is therefore needed for reliable multi-modal fetal echocardiography triage.
method: The framework couples a cross-modal video translator that reconstructs CFD from B-mode with an outer error estimator in a bi-level optimization scheme. The estimator predicts clip-conditioned reconstruction-error statistics to reweight translator training, while translation errors supervise the estimator. At inference, observed errors are standardized by these statistics and aggregated separately inside and outside anatomical regions into a participant-level anomaly score.

title: AnomExpert: Identifying and Selecting Anatomical Planes for Prenatal Ultrasound Anomaly Diagnosis
motivation: Prenatal anomaly diagnosis requires identifying which anatomical planes are present and which are diagnostically useful for each anomaly. Staged systems need costly plane annotations, while conventional MIL mixes heterogeneous planes and ignores disease-specific relevance. A weakly supervised method must therefore represent plane identity and selectively use relevant planes from unordered examinations.
method: AnomExpert uses learnable plane prototypes to softly organize unordered ultrasound images into latent anatomical-plane representations with only case-level labels. Sinkhorn-balanced assignments and a prototype loss encourage consistent and diverse plane grouping. Disease-aware queries then sparsely select the planes relevant to each anomaly, and the complete model is trained end to end for diagnosis.

title: APEX-SAM: Anatomy-Aware Prompting with Expert Retrieval for Training-Free Medical Image Segmentation
motivation: Training-free few-shot segmentation is attractive for unseen anatomies, but current support-driven prompting often selects supports randomly, models geometric alignment poorly, and uses only one prompt modality. These weaknesses make adaptation unstable under cross-domain shifts in scanners, modalities, and institutions. A practical approach should ensure support quality, exploit anatomical geometry, and combine complementary prompts without parameter updates.
method: APEX-SAM builds a dual-stream DINO/SigLIP expert bank and retrieves diverse, quality-assured support exemplars. Its anatomy-aware prompt mining aligns style and geometry, uses orientation and morphology priors, and samples informative points. Three SAM branches using point, text, and box prompts are combined through training-free feature-consensus weighting.

title: ARCH-Net: Aligned 3D Teeth Reconstruction via Counterfactual-Enhanced Hierarchical Framework
motivation: Radiation-free 3D dental models from sparse, uncalibrated intra-oral photographs could make orthodontic planning more accessible than IOS. Classical parametric approaches have weak anatomical priors, limited parameter spaces, and slow iterative inference, while generative methods may sacrifice geometric rigor and cross-view consistency. A method is needed that combines strong dental geometry priors with efficient, consistent reconstruction.
method: ARCH-Net first pretrains a VQ-VAE on 3D teeth point clouds to establish an anatomically constrained latent space. A latent diffusion model uses cross-attention to map 2D contours to 3D geometry, while counterfactual contrastive supervision compares predicted codes with mismatched negatives to strengthen cross-view consistency. Sequential rigid and non-rigid registration with statistical tooth templates then refines coarse points into topologically coherent high-resolution meshes.

title: Are Foundational Models Less Biased Than Specialized Models? An Ultrasound Study
motivation: Foundation models are expected to generalize better and reduce bias through large, diverse self-supervised pretraining, but this assumption is unresolved in medical imaging. Bias may persist or even worsen across patient and acquisition subgroups, and the impact of pretraining data composition is unclear. A controlled ultrasound study is needed to determine whether scale and diversity actually improve subgroup fairness.
method: The study performs a controlled comparison of self-supervised foundation models and a classically supervised baseline fine-tuned on the same prenatal ultrasound data. Bias is characterized with radar-based profiles across clinical and acquisition subgroups for preterm-birth prediction and fetal scan-weight estimation. It additionally varies the foundation-model pretraining data regime, including targeted cervical-image sampling, large-scale data, and device balancing, to assess how data composition affects fairness.

title: Arrhythmia-Robust Cine-MRI via Latent Motion Artifact Characterization
motivation: Segmented cardiac cine-MRI assumes periodic heartbeats, so arrhythmia-induced R-R variability mixes different cardiac phases and causes blur, ghosting, and signal voids. These nonlinear, nonrigid artifacts make pixel-wise denoising and methods designed for mild undersampling insufficient, while preserving true myocardial motion is essential for functional assessment. Robust latent motion modeling is needed to separate physiological dynamics from arrhythmia-related deviations.
method: LDE-MAR represents cine-MRI motion in latent space using orthogonality-constrained sparse dictionaries for motion regions and directions, plus a dedicated noise dictionary for arrhythmia deviations. Motion dictionaries are pretrained on clean cine sequences, then only the noise dictionary is fine-tuned with paired clean and corrupted data while physiological priors remain fixed. The refined latent trajectory is decoded into motion fields for artifact-reduced reconstruction that preserves anatomy and plausible myocardial motion.

title: Artery and vein segmentation on brain CTA using CTP for contrast-phase augmentation
motivation: Separate segmentation of distal intracranial arteries and veins is needed to compute objective collateral scores for stroke prognosis, but annotations are laborious and existing methods often omit veins, small vessels, or contrast-timing variation. CTA appearance changes with bolus timing, degrading segmentation across sites. CTP offers detailed vessel information that can support realistic phase augmentation and reduce annotation burden for robust CTA models.
method: The method trains artery-and-vein segmentation models using CTAs simulated from temporally resolved CTP source data, varying contrast timing to provide phase augmentation and semi-automatic reference labels. Models are compared with and without this augmentation and across training-from-scratch and foundation-model fine-tuning regimes. Hemisphere-specific vessel volumes are then converted into automated arterial and venous quantitative collateral scores for clinical comparison.

title: Artifact-aware Prompt Learning for Domain Generalization
motivation: Dermoscopic classifiers often fail when hairs, illumination, dark corners, and acquisition noise differ between training and deployment. Enforcing only domain-invariant features can discard fine-grained lesion information and may not remain stable for unseen artifact patterns. Domain generalization therefore needs to model artifact-specific variation while preserving lesion semantics and exploiting learned domains without target labels.
method: APDG treats common dermoscopic artifacts as multiple source domains and introduces domain-specific visual prompts in a Vision Transformer. A soft-mask disentanglement module separates invariant lesion semantics from artifact-specific features, while prototype learning imposes joint domain and class structure. At test time, prototype similarity drives prompt fusion so the model can combine domain knowledge without target-domain labels or additional training.

title: ASTAR: Automated Induction of STAndardized Radiology Reporting Templates from Large-Scale Clinical Free-Text Corpora
motivation: Structured radiology reporting enables searchable data, cohort assembly, longitudinal tracking, and label generation, but converting free text requires a predefined template. Existing templates depend on slow expert consensus, are static, and can miss rare findings or institution-specific language in large, evolving corpora. An automated, data-driven way to induce comprehensive templates is therefore needed.
method: ASTAR uses LLM-based processing to mine and consolidate standardized reporting structures from large collections of clinical free-text reports. The pipeline automatically discovers keys and permissible values, progressively consolidating long-tail findings as more reports are included. It is designed as an upstream template-induction stage that can support subsequent information extraction without relying on prolonged expert committee construction.

title: AS-TIME: Time-Conditioned Multimodal Modeling of Aortic Stenosis Progression

categories.value: AI for Neglected Diseases & Limited-Resource Settings

motivation: Aortic stenosis follows highly heterogeneous trajectories: some patients remain stable while others deteriorate rapidly, making fixed surveillance intervals and intervention timing difficult. Existing studies commonly predict events within static windows and use extensive tabular variables rather than patient-specific temporal conditioning from imaging. A model that predicts progression from one baseline echo and a queried elapsed time could support personalized monitoring.
method: AS-TIME encodes a baseline echocardiogram video and report with modality-specific encoders, aggregates instances using attention-based MIL, and uses the queried follow-up interval Δt to gate multimodal fusion. A Δt-guided mixture-of-experts head routes predictions among heterogeneous progression dynamics. The architecture exposes instance attention, modality contributions, and expert probabilities for multi-level interpretation.

title: Asym-MSF: Asymmetric Multi-scale Structural Fusion for Robust BCVA Prediction with Self-supervised Fidelity Constraints

categories.value: Multimodal Integration with Clinical / Genomic / Biomarkers

motivation: Postoperative BCVA prediction benefits from multimodal data, but OCT provides high-fidelity retinal structure whereas SLO and text are often noisy or missing. Symmetric fusion treats these modalities as equally reliable, allowing corrupted auxiliary information to contaminate OCT representations. The task needs an asymmetric fusion strategy that exploits complementary context while protecting structural evidence.
method: Asym-MSF treats OCT as the structural anchor and generates spatial-aware latent seeds from it to compress SLO and text through a two-stage cross-attention bottleneck. A multi-scale hypernetwork produces position-specific dynamic kernels, complemented by global spectral filtering, to modulate OCT features using localized auxiliary context. A self-supervised feature restorer reconstructs OCT representations under amplitude, gradient, and frequency constraints to preserve anatomical fidelity.

title: AsynDiff: Asynchronous-Timestep Diffusion with Noise-Aware Attention for Multi-sequence MRI Synthesis
motivation: Complete multi-sequence MRI acquisition is often infeasible because of scan time, artifacts, contraindications, and protocol differences, so missing-sequence synthesis is important for downstream analysis. Existing diffusion methods use observed sequences as fixed conditions and denoise predefined targets, limiting adaptation to arbitrary missing patterns and potentially causing inconsistencies when multiple sequences are synthesized. The diffusion process should explicitly encode which sequences are reliable sources and which are uncertain targets.
method: AsynDiff assigns sequence-specific diffusion timesteps during training, creating controlled noise disparities between observed and missing MRI sequences. Cross-sequence noise-aware attention uses relative noise levels to emphasize reliable low-noise features and suppress misleading noisy cues. The framework also studies sampling strategies for arbitrary missing patterns while maintaining cross-sequence anatomical consistency.

title: AtomiMed: Hierarchical Atomic Fact-Checking for Universal Clinical-Aware Medical Report Evaluation
motivation: Medical report generation metrics based on n-gram overlap can miss clinically catastrophic errors and do not explain which findings are wrong. Existing structured metrics are often modality-specific, while LLM judges are expensive and lack auditable per-finding traces. Evaluation needs a universal, hierarchical measure of disease presence and attributes that correlates with radiologist judgment and supports interpretable error attribution.
method: AtomiMed decomposes reference and generated reports into Disease-level and Attribute-level Atomic Clinical Facts. An agentic cross-verification loop queries each report as evidence for the other’s fact questions, producing precision, recall, and F1 at both levels and separating detection from descriptive correctness. MRGEvalKit operationalizes the extraction and scoring, while OmniMRG-Bench provides expert annotations across X-ray, CT, MRI, and ultrasound.

title: Attention is Matter for Inclusiveness: Generating Synthetic CT for Patients with Hip Implants

categories.value: AI for Neglected Diseases & Limited-Resource Settings

motivation: MR-only radiotherapy workflows rely on sCT for electron-density and dose calculation, but metal implants create signal voids and geometric artifacts that models can misinterpret as air. Hip-implant patients are therefore underrepresented or excluded, and paired MR-CT data for these cases are scarce. Inclusive sCT generation requires implant-aware attention and realistic augmentation tailored to metal artifacts.
method: The framework derives implant attention masks directly from MR images and embeds them into an sCT generation model. It introduces physics-guided MR augmentations that simulate metal-induced distortions together with corresponding CT augmentations, and systematically compares attention mechanisms and augmentation choices. The resulting pipeline is evaluated with implant-focused reconstruction and dosimetric criteria, including rare implant types.

title: Attention-Based Prototype Calibration for Multi-Rater Few-Shot Medical Image Segmentation
motivation: Few-shot segmentation usually assumes one ground-truth mask, although clinical images commonly contain systematic differences between expert delineations. Averaging annotations loses plausible rater-specific styles, while independent training wastes shared semantics and is unreliable with few supports. A few-shot method must model structured inter-rater variability and produce personalized predictions without sacrificing semantic consistency.
method: The framework represents each rater’s support annotations as prototypes and calibrates them toward a consensus prototype with a lightweight attention operator, without changing the feature backbone. Calibration regularization stabilizes personalized prototype updates, while superpixel-based pseudo-style generation supplies multiple rater-style variants for training. A two-stage optimization strategy produces one personalized query segmentation for each rater style.

title: Attenuation-Resilient Alternating Optimization for Laparoscopic Liver Landmark Detection
motivation: Reliable liver-surface landmark detection is needed to register laparoscopic views with preoperative models for surgical guidance. Underexposed regions blur boundaries, while pixel-wise segmentation can fragment continuous curvilinear landmarks and curve priors can over-smooth endpoints. The task requires representations resilient to illumination and a decoder that jointly balances localization accuracy with geometric continuity.
method: A2ONet first applies illumination field compensation to normalize spatially varying low-light effects, then extracts RGB-D representations and uses a frequency–orientation selective filter to emphasize curvilinear cues while suppressing repetitive textures. Its alternating seg–curve optimization decoder jointly maintains a dense segmentation branch and an explicit curve branch. Curve-to-mask and mask-to-curve exchanges iteratively refine continuity and endpoint localization under joint mask, curve, and illumination supervision.

title: Attribute-Aware Federated Learning with Pseudo-Bag Augmentation for Multi-Center WSI Classification
motivation: Federated WSI classification must handle staining, scanning, and digitization differences across centers while keeping gigapixel slides private. Standard FL often uses coarse statistics or parameter averaging and misses fine-grained intra-bag pathology structure; synthetic-slide exchange is costly. A compact distribution-aware mechanism is needed to provide external morphological diversity and align centers without sharing raw WSIs.
method: FedGMM-Bag has each center fit a compact multi-attribute GMM group to its local WSI feature distributions and communicate that representation once. Centers use received models to synthesize cross-domain pseudo-bags for local MIL training, replaying external morphology and applying covariance-aligned feature mapping for fine-grained alignment. The design avoids sharing raw slides or repeatedly transmitting synthetic images while addressing instance- and bag-level heterogeneity.

title: AutoLand: A Data-Efficient Automated Agentic Workflow for Universal Medical Landmark Detection
motivation: Medical landmark detection changes substantially across modalities, anatomies, and acquisition protocols, making one bespoke model per dataset difficult to scale. General-purpose heuristic configuration lacks semantic reasoning and performs poorly under complex variation or few-sample supervision. An automated workflow is needed to infer physically appropriate preprocessing and expert training strategies with minimal manual redesign.
method: AutoLand uses a Vision Language Model as an analysis agent that interprets images and extracted physics fingerprints to characterize a new dataset. During reasoning, it queries a medical deep-learning library for compatible architectures, preprocessing choices, optimization protocols, and validation procedures. The agent instantiates an end-to-end training workflow from only a few annotated samples and adapts it across modalities and anatomical targets.

title: Automated Disentangling Analysis of Skin Colour for Lesion Images
motivation: Dermatology models can lose accuracy when skin colour captured during deployment differs from training, because perceived colour entangles skin tone with illumination and camera factors. A single scalar skin-tone descriptor cannot represent these influences or provide controlled editing, while naive manipulation may alter scars or ink marks.
