A structured, faithful colour representation is needed for equitable visualization, augmentation, and normalization.
method: The framework adapts disentanglement-by-compression to encode perceived skin colour captured in images into a low-bitrate, manipulable latent representation conditioned on a randomized decolourized image. Randomized mostly monotonic mappings prevent luminance shortcuts from leaking skin-darkness information, while geometry-aligned post-processing rejects unintended changes in localized patterns. The learned representation supports counterfactual colour editing, image-to-image transfer, controlled physical traversals, augmentation, and normalization.

title: Automated Optical Density Normalization for Myelin Quantification: Cross-Modal Validation with 7T Ex Vivo MRI

categories.value: Multimodal Integration with Clinical / Genomic / Biomarkers

motivation: Optical density from Luxol Fast Blue staining could provide a continuous proxy for myelin loss in white-matter hyperintensities, but staining and tissue-processing batches introduce intensity differences unrelated to biology. Existing normalization methods rely on external or global colour statistics and do not identify biologically intact tissue as a reference, while manual annotations are burdensome. An annotation-free, tissue-grounded calibration is needed for reliable comparison with MRI and across slides.
method: The pipeline uses an existing attention model to identify white-matter regions with low pathology attention as candidate intact-myelin references, avoiding manual annotations. Blind stain deconvolution produces optical-density heatmaps, which are calibrated against the automatically selected internal references to reduce batch effects. The calibrated maps are then compared with expert myelin-loss ratings and co-registered ex vivo 7T MRI to validate biological and cross-modal relevance.

title: Automated Scope Pose Estimation in Real-World Robotic-Assisted Bronchoscopy with Integrated C-Arm Imaging
motivation: Robotic-assisted bronchoscopy needs accurate bronchoscope pose to register intraoperative CBCT with the navigation coordinate frame and correct CT-to-body divergence from motion, deformation, and tracking errors. Existing semi-automated workflows require manual tip localization and pose refinement, causing operator variability, added time, and user-induced errors. A fully automatic and efficient estimator is therefore needed for reliable navigation updates.
method: The pipeline uses two-stage inference to segment the bronchoscope tip rapidly from CBCT, followed by a context-aware robust pose estimator that combines scope geometry with surrounding anatomy. It is designed to handle metal and motion artifacts, indistinct boundaries, and working-channel instruments without manual correction.

title: Automatic LV Localization and Short-Axis Plane Estimation from Arbitrary CMR Slice
motivation: Accurate 3D short-axis orientation is important for LV analysis, cross-view registration, cardiac modeling, and automated plane prescription. Existing CMR methods either classify a few discrete views or combine multiple slices geometrically, so they cannot represent continuous orientation from a single arbitrary slice. A single-slice formulation with an unambiguous continuous representation is needed.
method: The authors adapt orientation-aware detection frameworks with a ResNet-50/FPN backbone to jointly localize the LV and regress 3D orientation from one arbitrary CMR slice. Their Polar-Coupled Circular (PCC) embedding maps the ground-truth normal to a continuous, unit-magnitude, unique representation covering the full orientation hemisphere, then decodes it back during inference. This avoids 180-degree ambiguity, angular boundary discontinuities, and polar instability found in prior formulations.

title: B² Loss for Evidential Classification of Critical View of Safety in Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy
motivation: The Critical View of Safety in laparoscopic cholecystectomy is clinically important, but expert disagreement reflects genuine perceptual ambiguity rather than simple annotation error. Majority-vote hard labels discard this information and assume minority expert opinions are wrong. Standard frame-level metrics also treat false positives and false negatives equally, despite the greater clinical risk of false-positive safety judgments.
method: The method treats annotator votes as Binomial samples from a latent criterion-visibility probability and predicts that probability with an evidential Beta distribution. A conjugate Beta-Binomial (B²) loss learns directly from vote distributions while estimating both visibility and evidence strength. The work also evaluates achievement at video level under a precision-critical protocol that measures recall at precision 1.0.

title: Bayesian Temporal Pose Networks for Uncertainty-Calibrated Laparoscopic Tool Pose Tracking
motivation: Monocular tracking of laparoscopic tool pose is needed for computer-assisted surgery and skill assessment, but non-robotic tools lack CAD models, kinematic chains, and standardized geometry. Existing approaches often rely on markers, bounding boxes, or single-frame predictions and provide little temporal reasoning or uncertainty calibration. A geometry-free, temporally aware probabilistic tracker is therefore required.
method: BTPN combines a segmentation and keypoint-detection front end with visual features, monocular depth cues, and a kinematic foundation model. Hierarchical multi-scale temporal attention and quaternion-aware bimanual cross-attention model motion continuity and inter-tool coordination, while gated fusion predicts probabilistic future position, orientation, and jaw-angle distributions. Geometry-specific distributions include Gaussian position and jaw terms and a von Mises–Fisher quaternion distribution for calibrated uncertainty.

title: Bayesian Topological Analysis of Brain Networks
motivation: Persistent-homology representations can characterize multi-scale brain-network topology, but group comparisons typically rely on permutation tests. Permutation testing gives thresholded binary decisions and requires costly resampling, offering limited information about evidence strength and uncertainty. A Bayesian framework is needed to provide richer posterior inference for subtle clinical network alterations.
method: The framework models within- and between-group topological dissimilarities probabilistically and uses Markov chain Monte Carlo sampling to obtain posterior distributions of test statistics. It reports Bayes factors and credible intervals, providing graded evidence and uncertainty rather than a binary threshold decision. Simulations and fMRI application are used to assess consistency with permutation testing and sensitivity to subtle network differences.

title: BCER Agent: Reliable Long-Horizon MRI Workflow Execution via Compilation, Artifact Binding, and Bounded Local Recovery
motivation: Practical MRI analysis involves long, interdependent workflows over 3D or 4D data, unlike the short image or tool-calling tasks common in current medical-agent evaluations. Reactive agents can accumulate failures from incorrect artifact references, incompatible arguments, and broken dependencies, preventing completion even when individual tools work. Reliable execution and auditable links from outputs to intermediate evidence are therefore needed.
method: BCER separates goal-level planning from constrained workflow execution. The Brain produces a plan sketch, the Cerebellum compiles it into an executable graph and dispatches MRI tools through the Extremity while recording artifacts, and the Reflector performs bounded step or sub-workflow repair and retry. Explicit artifact binding and task contracts preserve traceability and constrain cross-step dependencies.

title: BC-MultiSet: A Multi-target Dataset and Benchmark for Clinical Tasks in Breast Cancer
motivation: Breast-cancer treatment depends on molecular receptor status and tumor-microenvironment composition, both assessed from H&E-related material but usually studied separately in computational pathology. Existing datasets often provide either cell annotations without clinical labels or molecular profiles without spatial cellular context. A paired resource is needed to develop and evaluate integrated morphology–biomarker analysis.
method: BC-MultiSet pairs H&E patches with consensus polygon annotations for tumor, inflammatory, and fibroblast nuclei and slide-level ER, PR, and HER2 labels from the same patients. It establishes patient-level cross-validation benchmarks for six biomarker-classification architectures, three instance-segmentation models, and multi-task models that jointly optimize both objectives. This design enables direct study of links between cellular morphology and molecular status.

title: BDFR-Net: Boundary-Aware Dual-Domain Feature Reconstruction Network for Fetal Ultrasound Image Segmentation
motivation: Segmenting the fetal head and pubic symphysis in transperineal ultrasound supports quantitative obstetric assessment, but speckle noise, acoustic shadowing, and low signal-to-noise ratio obscure boundaries. Conventional skip connections can also leave cross-level semantic misalignment, harming structural fidelity. A method that jointly separates boundary cues from noise and aligns hierarchical features is needed.
method: BDFR-Net introduces DDBE, which decouples frequency-domain edge responses from spatial contextual cues and recombines them through channel-attentive cross-domain fusion. An Adaptive Context Alignment Module in skip connections applies dual spatial-channel attention to recalibrate encoder and decoder features before fusion, reducing semantic gaps and feature drift. The network therefore combines boundary-sensitive spectral information with spatial structural continuity.

title: Be Indiscrete: The Benefits of Learning Continuous Spine Degeneration Severity Scores
motivation: Lumbar degeneration is a continuous biological process, but MRI assessment commonly uses ordinal categories that treat grades as independent and penalize all errors equally. Fixed boundaries discard within-grade variation, make borderline decisions unstable, and can bias models toward common classes when severe disease is rare. Continuous ranking could preserve severity ordering and make large clinical mistakes more costly.
method: SpineNetRank uses a shared 3D ResNet-18 encoder with task-specific continuous ranking heads for multiple degeneration measures. Pairwise severity-aware hinge losses enforce the correct ordering with larger penalties for larger grade gaps, while same-grade pairs are constrained to have similar scores. The model outputs both a continuous severity value and a grade recovered from that score.

title: Benchmarking Foundation Models for Early Multi-retinopathy Detection at National Scale: Performance, Generalization, and Bias

categories.value: AI for Neglected Diseases & Limited-Resource Settings
AI for Population Health, Public Health & Epidemiology

motivation: Early screening for diabetic retinopathy, AMD, pathological myopia, and retinal vein occlusion is limited by specialist shortages, heterogeneous devices and workflows, class imbalance, and label uncertainty. Existing foundation-model evidence often comes from clean, homogeneous cohorts and standard i.i.d. metrics, leaving real-world generalization and subgroup bias unclear. A national, screening-oriented benchmark is needed to evaluate deployment reliability and equity.
method: OphFM-bench assembles a national-scale fundus-photo cohort and evaluates retina-specific FMs, medical VLMs, and general vision backbones under linear probing and full fine-tuning. Its protocol reports AUC together with high-recall operating points, tests North–South geographic transfer, and audits performance across age, sex, and urban–rural residency. The benchmark therefore links transfer efficiency with screening workload, generalization, and fairness.

title: Benchmarking Pathology Foundation Models for Spatial Domain Understanding
motivation: Pathology foundation models are usually judged by downstream endpoints, which do not reveal whether their embeddings separate meaningful tissue regions or preserve spatial neighborhoods. Spatial domain identification on paired WSI and transcriptomics data offers a representation-level diagnostic, but no standardized benchmark compares encoders and partitioning choices. Such evaluation is needed to understand the spatial semantics encoded by PFMs.
method: SpaPath-Bench extracts spot-aligned PFM embeddings from paired WSI–ST slides and treats embedding dimensions as pseudo-expression variables. It standardizes spatial representation learning with PCA or SDI methods, followed by controlled clustering, and scores partitions using spatial coherence, transcriptomics-referenced agreement, and expert-referenced agreement. The benchmark spans many encoders and SDI pipelines to diagnose spatial organization in representations independently of downstream task heads.

title: Benchmarking Video Foundation Models for Remote Parkinson’s Disease Screening
motivation: Remote video assessment could make Parkinson’s screening more accessible, but specialist examinations are difficult to scale and traditional systems depend on handcrafted task-specific features. Video foundation models may learn transferable motion representations, yet their relative suitability for the varied clinical tasks used in PD screening is poorly understood. A systematic task-by-architecture comparison is needed before selecting models for remote monitoring.
method: The study freezes seven video foundation models and evaluates their embeddings with task-specific linear classifiers across 16 standardized webcam tasks. Comparing architectures such as VideoPrism, V-JEPA, ViViT, VideoMAE, and TimeSformer reveals which learned representations are salient for speech, facial expressivity, upper-limb movement, and rhythmic actions. The protocol provides task-model baselines without task-specific video pretraining.

title: Better Said Than Seen: Exposing and Mitigating Modality Collapse with ICD-11-Grounded Evaluation
motivation: Teledermatology depends on subtle visual morphology, but MLLMs may produce plausible diagnoses while relying mainly on textual priors rather than the image. Increasingly strong prompts can therefore suppress visual evidence, creating a clinical safety risk that standard benchmark scores may miss. Existing surface-form metrics also penalize near-miss diagnoses and mishandle negated conditions, motivating controlled modality audits and clinically faithful evaluation.
method: DermDetail varies the amount and specificity of diagnostic text while holding images constant, measuring image-token attention to expose prior-induced modality collapse. The authors introduce dermatologist-designed structured vignettes that encode morphological and contextual information as language and benchmark them against image inputs under matched conditions. ICDLens normalizes free-text diagnoses to ICD-11 and applies assertion-aware, hierarchy-aware F1 scoring to distinguish negations and clinically proximate errors.

title: Beyond Clean Test Sets: Spurious Correlations in Medical Vision-language Models and the Role of Concept Supervision
motivation: Medical VLMs may encode acquisition artifacts alongside pathology, yet clean test sets cannot isolate or expose this reliance. Domain-specific contrastive pretraining is expected to provide clinical grounding, but whether explicit concept supervision adds robustness remains untested. A controlled evaluation across artifact removal and inversion is needed to determine when models follow shortcuts and which concept strategies mitigate them.
method: The framework injects synthetic, class-specific acquisition artifacts at controlled prevalence and evaluates models after artifact removal and artifact–class inversion. Five architectures range from a standard vision backbone and VLM baseline to auxiliary concept supervision, a post-hoc concept bottleneck, and multi-level image–concept alignment. This design separates reliance on clinical signal from shortcut following and tests whether concept integration reshapes features and shields prediction from non-clinical cues.

title: Beyond Landmarks: Anchor-Guided Orientation Regression for Robust Spinopelvic Measurement
motivation: Spinopelvic measurements guide deformity assessment and surgical planning, but manual readings vary and automated pipelines commonly localize vertebrae, crop regions, and then detect landmarks, allowing stage-wise errors and limiting global reasoning. Direct point prediction can swap adjacent vertebral landmarks, while point-wise losses do not match the angular measurements ultimately required. A task-aligned orientation representation is needed for accurate, resolution-tolerant measurement.
method: The study compares landmark detection, anchor-guided landmark detection, and anchor-guided orientation regression using the same DINOv3 encoder, lightweight heatmap decoder, and training protocol. The proposed AGOR represents each measurement through anchor-centered orientation primitives, directly supervising vertebral orientation rather than independent point locations. Parameter-efficient fine-tuning is evaluated across ViT and ConvNeXt encoders and reduced input resolution to test representation robustness.

title: Beyond Stochastic Diffusion: Trajectory-Consistent Deterministic Flow Matching for Fluorescence Molecular Tomography

categories.value: AI for Population Health, Public Health & Epidemiology

motivation: FMT reconstruction is a severely ill-posed inverse problem in which scattering and absorption cause non-unique solutions, poor resolution, and unstable source localization. Deterministic regression blurs sparse sources, while diffusion models require long stochastic denoising chains and can become unstable when compressed to few steps. A fast, reproducible reconstruction process that preserves geometric fidelity is needed.
method: TCDFlow-FMT reformulates reconstruction as deterministic continuous-time transport and samples the learned velocity field with an ODE instead of stochastic diffusion denoising. A spatially guided flow Transformer aligns multi-view fluorescence measurements with sparse source structure and modulates decoding spatially. Gibbs-based geometric consistency reweighting approximates optimal-transport coupling to straighten trajectories and stabilize few-step reconstruction.

title: Beyond the Batch: Momentum-Updated Virtual Cohorts for 3D PET-CT Prognosis
motivation: Cox survival learning needs broad risk sets, but whole-body 3D PET-CT forces very small batches because of memory demands, producing sparse comparisons, noisy gradients, and weak optimization. Gradient accumulation does not enlarge the within-iteration risk set, while cropping can lose dispersed lesions and patient context. A memory-compatible mechanism is needed to approximate global risk comparisons and stabilize ranking.
method: MCSF maintains a momentum-updated Virtual Cohort Bank using an evolving reference encoder, enlarging the effective Cox risk pool without increasing the 3D mini-batch memory footprint. A time-aware ranking objective gives informative weights to event comparisons according to survival-time differences and reduces ambiguous comparisons. The framework can be attached to 3D PET-CT backbones and trained end to end, with lesion-guided input modulation.

title: Beyond Visual Cues: CoT-Enhanced Reasoning for Semi-supervised Medical Image Segmentation
motivation: Semi-supervised segmentation typically relies on pixel-level visual similarity, which can fail for low-contrast lesions, ambiguous boundaries, artifacts, or anatomically similar structures with different clinical meanings. Clinicians use recalled cases and diagnostic reasoning, but existing text-based references often contain only superficial descriptions and do not resolve visual-semantic mismatch. Incorporating high-level reasoning is therefore needed to guide segmentation beyond appearance alone.
method: CERS builds a knowledge pool of LLM-generated, segmentation-aware Chain-of-Thought descriptions and retrieves historical references using morphology followed by CoT-consistency filtering. A multi-scale coordinate attention module injects the reasoning-derived context into the decoder, while a dual-decoder consistency design supports semi-supervised learning. The approach is intended to reject visually similar but pathologically inconsistent references and resolve ambiguous boundaries.

title: Beyond Visual Forensics: Auditing Multimodal Robustness for Synthetic Medical Image Detection
motivation: Synthetic medical images can enable diagnostic deception and insurance fraud, and VLMs increasingly judge images together with clinical records rather than in isolation. Image-only detection benchmarks cannot reveal whether record context changes the authenticity decision for the same image. A controlled multimodal audit is needed to characterize text-induced shifts and deployment robustness.
method: The benchmark keeps each medical image fixed while swapping a controlled provenance field in the accompanying record, then measures changes in VLM authenticity judgments across modalities and model families. This paired design quantifies text-induced decision shift and directly tests whether metadata can override visual evidence. It includes open-weight and frontier API VLMs and supports comparison of image reliance at the image–record interface.

title: BiC-ODE: Bidirectionally Coupled Neural ODEs for Rapid Laminar Surface Reconstruction of the Human Cortex from 5T MRI
motivation: The intracortical hypointense band visible in 5T FLAIR can support laminar morphology analysis, but 3T lacks sufficient contrast and 7T is less clinically feasible. Optimization-based surface reconstruction is accurate but too slow for large cohorts, whereas existing deep models mainly reconstruct white-matter and pial surfaces rather than band boundaries. A fast method must accurately follow the band while preserving the ordering of all nested cortical surfaces.
method: BiC-ODE uses Neural ODE deformation to move the white-matter surface outward and the pial surface inward toward the inner and outer boundaries of the intracortical hypointense band. It combines optimization-generated supervision with band-specific image-driven losses and bidirectional coupling to maintain the ordering of four nested surfaces. Direct ODE inference avoids iterative optimization while preserving cross-surface consistency.

title: Bidirectional Anatomy-Aware Post-Training for Longitudinal Chest X-Ray Progression Modeling
motivation: Longitudinal CXR comparison is needed to assess disease evolution and guide treatment decisions. Existing temporal models usually use fixed prior-to-current ordering and global image representations, so they do not enforce temporal symmetry or explicitly localize evidence to anatomical structures. A method incorporating both properties is needed for reliable progression assessment.
method: BAAP is a lightweight post-training strategy built on a pretrained CXR encoder. Bidirectional Progression Training augments each pair with its reversed temporal order and inverted label, enforcing directional consistency. An Anatomy-aware Perception Layer pools patch features within predefined anatomical regions, fuses prior/current features and their differences, and predicts progression per region.

title: BIGUS: Beam Integrated Gaussian Scattering for Continuous Ultrasound View Synthesis
motivation: Ultrasound novel-view synthesis could provide arbitrary anatomical planes for assessment, training, and tracking, but realistic rendering is difficult because speckle arises from complex wave–tissue interactions. Existing NeRF- and Gaussian-based methods do not explicitly model speckle, often oversmoothing or distorting texture that carries diagnostic and motion information. A physics-aware reconstruction method is therefore needed to preserve speckle fidelity.
method: BIGUS is a 3D Gaussian Splatting framework redesigned for ultrasound scattering. Its differentiable renderer uses signed reflectivities and exact elevation-beam integration, while structure-aware initialization samples Gaussian primitives from tissue regions. Error-guided densification concentrates additional primitives in uncertain areas, and a speckle-sensitive Backscatter Fidelity Score evaluates preservation of diagnostic texture.

title: BiM-GeoAttn-Net: Linear-Time Depth Modeling with Geometry-Aware Attention for 3D Aortic Dissection CTA Segmentation
motivation: Accurate 3D CTA segmentation of aortic dissection lumens supports morphological assessment and monitoring, but tortuous anatomy, appearance variation, and low contrast make delineation difficult. CNNs have limited long-range context, full 3D attention is expensive, and generic SSM scans do not align with anatomical continuity or provide sufficient boundary refinement. An efficient model must address cross-slice discontinuity and ambiguous vessel boundaries together.
method: BiM-GeoAttn-Net augments a 3D nnU-Net bottleneck with two modules. Bidirectional Depth Mamba scans depth-wise sequences in both directions with near-linear complexity to capture long-range inter-slice coherence. Geometry-Aware Vessel Attention combines plane-aligned anisotropic convolutions with spatial and channel attention to refine tubular boundaries and suppress background interference before decoding.

title: BioFact-MoE: Biologically Factorized Mixture of Experts for Vision–Language Prognostic Modeling in Hepatocellular Carcinoma
motivation: HCC prognosis reflects two interacting but distinct axes: hepatic functional reserve and tumor biology. Existing vision–language prognostic models entangle these factors in one representation, limiting accuracy, attribution, and biological interpretability, while generic MoE adaptation lacks pathway structure. Explicitly separating the biological drivers is needed for heterogeneous risk modeling and personalized treatment insight.
method: BioFact-MoE first uses LLM-guided report decomposition and anatomical patch masking during contrastive pretraining to train pathway-specific LoRA experts for hepatic and tumor factors. The frozen experts are combined in a residual MoE survival head with gated, patient-specific routing of pathway contributions for Cox-based prediction. This design provides factorized representations and phenotype-aware risk attribution.

title: BioFlow: A Biologically Valid Support-Preserving Flow for Histology-Conditioned Spatial Transcriptomics Prediction
motivation: Predicting spatial transcriptomics from histology offers a scalable alternative to costly sequencing, but expression is sparse, zero-inflated, and intrinsically non-negative. Existing diffusion and flow models evolve in unconstrained Euclidean spaces, allowing biologically invalid negative intermediate states; output-level correction cannot repair trajectories already biased by those states. Support constraints therefore need to be embedded directly into the generative dynamics.
method: BioFlow reparameterizes the velocity field in flow matching so continuous-time trajectories remain within the non-negative expression domain. A lightweight token-based Transformer models spatial interactions while learning these support-preserving dynamics. By constraining evolution itself rather than projecting final outputs, the framework respects sparse, zero-inflated transcriptomic geometry.

title: BioGait-VLM: A Tri-Modal Vision–Language–Biomechanics Framework for Interpretable Clinical Gait Assessment
motivation: Video-based clinical gait analysis could scale screening and follow-up beyond instrumented laboratories, but standard video models often learn environmental shortcuts and provide little biomechanical evidence. LVLMs add language capabilities yet remain weak at fine-grained temporal abnormalities and kinematic quantification. A robust assessment framework must isolate motion mechanics while retaining visual context and interpretable reporting.
method: BioGait-VLM combines a frozen visual encoder, a Temporal Evidence Distillation branch, and a Biomechanical Tokenization branch within a pretrained LVLM. Query-based temporal decoding aggregates frame features into gait descriptors, while a kinematic tokenizer projects 3D skeleton sequences into language-aligned semantic tokens. Lightweight adapters support joint pathology classification and generation of evidence-grounded clinical descriptions.

title: BioGuide: Biomedically-Guided Segmentation for Medical Tasks
motivation: Brain lesion segmentation can miss subtle or phenotypically heterogeneous lesions when models rely mainly on voxel-level appearance. Existing multi-task approaches often use high-level labels or complex task-specific architectures that are weakly linked to radiological evidence and hard to adapt. A flexible framework is needed to inject fine-grained clinical descriptors into diverse segmentation backbones.
method: BioGuide attaches a lightweight multi-label MLP head to the encoder bottleneck of an existing segmentation network. The auxiliary head predicts fine-grained radiological signs and lesion distributions, and a joint Dice-Tversky plus binary cross-entropy loss backpropagates this biomedical guidance into the encoder. The plug-and-play design supplies clinical regularization without changing the decoder or requiring pixel-level sign localization.

title: BiSA-DiT: A Bidirectional Spatially-Aware Diffusion Transformer for Sparse Tomographic Magnetic Particle Imaging
motivation: Full 3D system-matrix calibration for MPI is prohibitively time-consuming, motivating reconstruction from sparse measurements. Sparse reconstruction is ill-posed: slice-wise diffusion methods lose axial continuity, while handcrafted axial priors and local 3D context do not adequately capture global structure. A method must combine rich in-plane detail, robust axial consistency, and physical fidelity.
method: BiSA-DiT alternates a spatially aware diffusion prior with a physics-driven ADMM data-consistency update for sparse-SM MPI reconstruction. Parallel Planar and Axial Spatial Transformer blocks condition a DiT denoiser on in-plane structure and inter-slice continuity. The ADMM step enforces the MPI forward model and includes axial total-variation regularization to stabilize the ill-posed inverse problem.

title: Boosting Ultrasound Image Classification via Attribute-Guided Dual-Branch Framework
motivation: Ultrasound classification is clinically useful but is hindered by speckle, low contrast, operator dependence, and distribution shifts. Conventional black-box classifiers may rely on superficial textures, whereas existing attribute-guided methods often require dense annotations, task-specific designs, or costly prompt tuning. A lightweight plug-and-play approach is needed to improve both generalization and interpretability.
method: The framework retains the original classifier as a baseline branch and adds a parallel attribute-guided branch that injects domain-agnostic medical attributes as semantic priors. An adaptive decision module fuses global baseline predictions with interpretable attribute cues in a data-dependent manner. The modular design requires minimal architectural changes and can be attached to multiple ultrasound backbones.

title: Born Different: A Multi-level Individualized Modeling Framework for Embryo Euploidy Prediction
motivation: Non-invasive euploidy prediction could reduce reliance on costly and invasive embryo biopsy. Most existing time-lapse models assume embryos follow synchronized trajectories in one representation space, overlooking individual differences in morphology, developmental timing, and deviation from typical development. Explicit individualized modeling is needed for reliable embryo assessment.
method: The framework models embryo individuality at three levels. It adaptively composes shared morphological components for embryo-specific spatial structure, learns embryo-conditioned temporal weights to emphasize critical developmental stages, and predicts sample-specific variance for heteroscedastic reliability-aware learning. These components combine population regularities with individual morphology, developmental rhythm, and trajectory deviation.

title: Boundary-Aware Multi-Granularity Learning for Depression Severity Estimation
motivation: Depression severity estimation is usually optimized as continuous regression, while clinical decisions use discrete severity grades. Point-wise losses treat errors equally even when one crosses a clinical threshold, and they impose no ordinal structure on features. The mismatch calls for supervision that captures both precise scores and clinically meaningful boundaries.
method: Multi-Granularity Supervision jointly trains continuous depression-score regression with ordinal severity information. Ordinal Consistency Regularization encourages boundary-aware predictions, while Prototype-based Severity Contrastive Learning organizes feature representations according to severity order. The formulation preserves continuous estimation and uses ordinal supervision as a complementary regularizer rather than replacing regression with ordinal classification.

title: BRAIN: Bi-directional Motion Reasoning with Dynamic Memory Pruning for Surgical Video Segmentation
motivation: Reliable instrument tracking and segmentation are safety-critical for robot-assisted surgery. Existing video models struggle when an instrument abruptly reappears at a new location, causing motion-inertia misidentification, and when long absences fill memory with redundant frames that weaken re-identification. These failures reveal a need for bidirectional motion checks and adaptive long-term memory management.
method: BRAIN combines bidirectional motion reasoning (BMR) with dynamic memory pruning (DM) for surgical video segmentation. BMR compares forward and backward instrument trajectories to detect abrupt positional shifts and reselects masks when motion is inconsistent. DM removes redundant frames captured during prolonged instrument absence, retaining a compact and diverse memory bank for long-term re-identification.

title: BrainACU: Asynchronous Coordination Unit Modeling for Dynamic Brain Network Analysis
motivation: Dynamic rs-fMRI analysis is useful for psychiatric disorder recognition, but many methods impose fixed template-based subnetworks that can hide disease-specific coordination. They also assume strictly time-aligned interactions, ignoring physiologically plausible delays and weakening delayed signals. Data-driven units with explicit asynchronous modeling are needed for more flexible and interpretable brain-network representations.
method: BrainACU forms temporally consistent patches with sliding windows, learns ROI-to-coordination-unit assignments through subject-level clustering and cross-sample consensus, and projects variable-size units into a shared latent space. An asynchronous interaction module uses directed attention to model both zero-lag and time-lagged dependencies between units. Diversity and lag-related regularizers discourage collapsed units and excessive reliance on synchronous interactions.

title: Brain-Adapter: A Dual-Stream Vision-Language MIL Framework for Comprehensive 3D CT Diagnosis of Acute Intracranial Pathologies
motivation: Automated diagnosis of acute intracranial pathologies from 3D CT is important for rapid triage, but dense annotations are expensive and conventional models lack broad diagnostic semantics. Native 3D VLMs are scarce because paired 3D-text data are limited, while standard visual MIL has no explicit concept guidance for subtle lesions. An annotation-efficient method must adapt 2D VLM knowledge to volumetric scans using reports as weak supervision.
method: Brain-Adapter transfers slice-level 2D biomedical VLM features to 3D CT through a dual-stream MIL architecture. A Text-Conditioned Attention stream uses report sentences as semantic queries, while a visual MIL stream learns from LLM-extracted logic-set labels; a consistency loss aligns their representations. Uncertainty-Aware Refinement dynamically calibrates and fuses the two predictions at inference.

title: BrainAnytime: Anatomy-Aware Cross-Modal Pretraining for Brain Image Analysis with Arbitrary Modality Availability
motivation: Clinical brain-imaging workups acquire modalities sequentially, so patients often have heterogeneous and incomplete MRI/PET subsets rather than a fixed panel. Existing pretraining is commonly MRI-only, assumes fixed inputs, and masks space uniformly, missing structural–molecular correspondences and disease-vulnerable anatomy. A unified model must handle arbitrary modality availability while learning cross-modal and anatomy-aware representations.
method: BrainAnytime uses a shared 3D masked autoencoder that accepts randomly sampled subsets of MRI sequences and amyloid-PET. Reciprocal Cross-Modal Distillation aligns structural MRI and PET representations, while Pathology-Aware Curriculum Masking uses atlas-guided schedules to emphasize AD-vulnerable anatomy. The resulting single model supports inference with any available modality subset without architectural switching.

title: Brain-DiT: A Universal Multi-state fMRI Foundation Model with Metadata-Conditioned Pretraining
motivation: Existing fMRI foundation models are often trained mainly on resting-state data and use reconstruction or alignment objectives that may overfit low-SNR noise or require substantial adaptation. They also underuse clinical and demographic metadata, making it difficult to disentangle intrinsic neural dynamics from population variability. A broadly transferable model should learn across brain states with a generative objective and multi-scale representations.
method: Brain-DiT pretrains a Diffusion Transformer on ROI time-series windows from many brain states, conditioning denoising on demographic and clinical metadata. The denoising trajectory provides hierarchical features, and downstream representations aggregate tokens from selected layers and noise timesteps. This design uses diffusion generation to capture both local functional structure and global semantics while separating neural dynamics from population variability.

title: BrainHTF: Learning Causal Graph Representation of Brain Connectome with Hyperbolic Transformer
motivation: Brain-connectome disease analysis needs to use both regions and their connections to explain abnormal mechanisms. Transformer methods mainly learn node representations and often operate in Euclidean geometry, which poorly represents the connectome’s modular hierarchical structure and limits interpretability. A causal, geometry-appropriate representation is needed to identify invariant disease-related connectivity patterns.
method: BrainHTF first uses a mask generator to separate a brain connectome into causal and bias subgraphs. A hyperbolic Transformer learns disentangled representations of these subgraphs in Poincare-ball geometry, which better represents modular and hierarchical topology than Euclidean space. Causal intervention on the learned representations then targets invariant patterns for disease prediction and biomarker interpretation.

title: BrainKODE: Controlled Koopman Dynamics over Longitudinal Structure–Function Coupling for Early Prediction of Adolescent Substance Use

categories.value: Multimodal Integration with Clinical / Genomic / Biomarkers
AI for Population Health, Public Health & Epidemiology

motivation: Adolescent substance-use initiation risk depends on evolving interactions among structural connectivity, functional connectivity, and environment. Existing models often fuse modalities statically, ignore the SPD geometry of functional connectivity, and append contextual factors only at the classifier, limiting longitudinal consistency and mechanistic insight. A controlled geometric dynamical model is needed to forecast developmental vulnerability.
method: BrainKODE maps functional connectomes and diffusion-derived structural operators into a shared Riemannian tangent space anchored by a cohort Fréchet mean. Adaptive cross-modal gates build a multiplex graph whose GAT layers learn network-specific structure–function coupling. A semigroup-constrained Koopman operator evolves baseline latent states, with contextual variables entering as control inputs for multistep forecasting.

title: Brain-Specialized Self-supervised Learning: Neuroanatomy-Aware Spatial Priors for 3D Brain MRI
motivation: Large unlabeled 3D brain MRI cohorts motivate self-supervised pretraining, but objectives borrowed from natural images often treat patch tokens as exchangeable. Because brain MRI has weak texture cues and regular anatomy, distant regions can appear similar, reducing patch distinctiveness and transfer quality. Spatially informed SSL is needed to encode neuroanatomical organization at patch granularity.
method: The method builds an iBOT-style 3D ViT with an EMA teacher and combines latent masked-token alignment with InfoNCE-style discrimination of CLS tokens. A distance-modulated patch decorrelation objective penalizes similarity more strongly for spatially distant patches while remaining tolerant of nearby anatomy. This supplies neuroanatomical spatial priors without relying on pixel reconstruction or fixed ROI assumptions.

title: BrainSTR: Spatio-Temporal Contrastive Learning for Interpretable Dynamic Brain Network Modeling
motivation: Dynamic functional connectivity can reveal when and where neuropsychiatric disease signatures emerge, but those signals are subtle, sparse, and mixed with abundant nuisance fluctuations. Fixed temporal windows and whole-network contrastive representations may obscure critical phases and disease-relevant edges, weakening both diagnosis and interpretability. A framework must jointly isolate informative time periods and sparse topology before learning similarities.
method: BrainSTR learns state-consistent temporal boundaries with an Adaptive Phase Partition module and attends to diagnostically critical phases. An Incremental Graph Structure Generator selects disease-related connectivity within each phase under binarization, temporal-smoothness, and sparsity regularization. Spatio-temporal supervised contrastive learning then organizes these selected patterns into a diagnosis-relevant semantic space.

title: Brain-TM: Decoding Brain States from Functional Networks Using a Hierarchical Spatiotemporal Transformer-Mamba
motivation: Decoding dynamic brain states from functional networks is needed to understand how cognition is supported by time-varying brain interactions. Static connectivity misses these changes, while existing GNNs and Transformers can be costly for long sequences and do not clearly explain how functional hubs drive state transitions.
method: Brain-TM combines a hierarchical Transformer with Mamba to model long-range spatiotemporal dependencies in functional networks efficiently. It back-projects temporal features onto spatial attention weights, enabling analysis of latent task-specific states and the topology of their functional hubs.

title: BrainWeaver: Weaving Dynamic Brain Networks with ROI-Guided Attention for Cognitive Assessment
motivation: Objective cognitive assessment from neuroimaging is needed because behavioral assessments are indirect, subjective, and lack neurophysiological interpretability. Existing graph methods often assume static connectivity, insufficiently use known cognitive-network priors, and are vulnerable to noisy fMRI data and inter-subject variation.
method: BrainWeaver uses ROI-guided dynamic multi-graph temporal attention fusion to model spatial dependencies and temporal fluctuations in fMRI connectomes. A key-ROI-specific hierarchical graph module injects neuroscience priors, and individual-invariance contrastive learning separates shared cognitive patterns from modality noise and subject variability.

title: Breaking Annotation Dependency in Coronary Stenosis Segmentation via Physics-Driven Sim2Real Learning
motivation: Coronary stenosis segmentation in XA is clinically important but difficult because vessel overlap, contrast variation, and projection ambiguity complicate interpretation. Supervised methods depend on scarce, subjective lesion labels whose limited pathological diversity and annotation biases impair generalization, while annotation-efficient methods remain weak for subtle localized stenoses.
method: The framework creates patient-specific coronary models from CTA, deliberately introduces diverse 3D stenosis morphologies and severities, and uses physics-based projection to generate aligned synthetic XA images and labels. A segmentation model trained on this balanced synthetic supervision is adapted to real XA through online uncertainty-based pseudo-label selection and confidence-aware consistency learning.

title: Breaking Teacher’s Mean Regression Bias: Boundary-Aware Contrastive Distillation for Endoscopic Super-Resolution
motivation: Endoscopic super-resolution must preserve subtle mucosal and microvascular details, but L1/L2 optimization of this ill-posed task produces mean-regression blur. Uniform, weakly textured endoscopic backgrounds make this especially severe, and conventional knowledge distillation further suppresses high-frequency variation by forcing a lightweight student to imitate an already smoothed teacher.
method: BACD replaces rigid teacher-student feature or output matching with boundary-aware contrastive distillation. It obtains a low-fidelity negative anchor by severely degrading the input to a frozen teacher, and obtains a high-fidelity positive anchor through teacher-gradient-based optimization of an input constrained to the valid LR manifold; an InfoNCE objective uses these anchors to counter bias inheritance.

title: BREIT: A Framework for Brain Stroke Reconstruction using Multi-frequency 3D EIT
motivation: Rapid stroke assessment requires distinguishing ischemic and hemorrhagic stroke, yet CT/MRI can be costly, infrastructure-dependent, and unsuitable for continuous bedside monitoring. MF-EIT is portable and low cost, but 3D reconstruction is limited by scarce paired ground truth and inconsistent data-generation, simulation, and evaluation pipelines.
method: BREIT provides a unified pipeline that registers CT/MRI to a common space, creates frequency-dependent 3D brain admittivity volumes, and simulates MF-EIT voltages with a Python 3D CEM forward solver on realistic meshes. It also implements 3D D-bar reconstruction for non-uniform electrodes and introduces dFNO-bar, which learns the mapping from D-bar scattering data to conductivity using Fourier Neural Operators.

title: Bridging EEG to fMRI: Semi-Supervised Functional Connectivity Translation via Latent Alignment
motivation: Inferring fMRI-derived functional representations from portable EEG could extend network-level assessment beyond the cost and logistical limits of fMRI. Existing signal-level EEG-to-fMRI regression is unstable under hemodynamic variability, ignores whole-brain consistency, and cannot make full use of abundant unpaired EEG-only and fMRI-only data.
method: The method reframes translation as graph-to-graph mapping between multi-band EEG FCs and hierarchical-order fMRI FCs. It first reconstructs FC within each modality using paired and unpaired data, then uses paired sessions to train EEG-to-fMRI translation while a frozen fMRI encoder acts as an asymmetric teacher that aligns the EEG latent representation.

title: Bridging Heterogeneous Medical Datasets via Mixture-of-Specialists Adapters for Unified Medical Image Classification
motivation: Medical classification data are fragmented across clinical tasks, acquisition formats, and both 2D and 3D modalities. Naively combining these datasets causes negative transfer because conflicting visual priors become entangled, whereas existing unified foundation-model approaches often require costly full-model pretraining.
method: MOSAIC adapts a frozen ImageNet-pretrained ViT using modality-aware tokenizers and a Mixture-of-Specialists adapter. Explicit modality routing separates texture-dominant, shape-driven, and volumetric feature subspaces, while teacher-student consistency stabilizes joint multi-task training.

title: Bridging Research and Practice: A Systematic Evaluation of Generalist and Dermatology-Specific Models in Clinical Skin Lesion Classification
motivation: Clinical skin-lesion classification is difficult because lesions, imaging devices, acquisition conditions, and patient demographics vary substantially. Strong performance on curated datasets does not establish safe or equitable clinical generalization, so the relative robustness of modern generalist, foundation, VLM, and dermatology-specific models must be systematically assessed.
method: This work conducts a structured benchmark for binary skin-lesion malignancy prediction across dermoscopic and smartphone clinical datasets. It compares dermatology-specific and general embedding models, end-to-end CNN/ViT models, and general or medical VLMs under individual, modality-merged, all-data-merged, and cross-dataset settings, including prompt and metadata variants for VLMs.

title: Bridging Single Distortion Artifacts and Multifactorial Clinical Quality: Few-Shot Biparametric MRI Quality Assessment via Distortion-Trained Prototypical Networks
motivation: Prostate MRI quality assessment is needed because DWI distortion can compromise lesion localization and diagnostic interpretation, while PI-QUAL scoring is subjective and time-consuming. Low-quality cases are scarce and heterogeneous, with available poor DWI examples dominated by geometric distortion, making direct supervised learning for multifactorial clinical quality unreliable.
method: The proposed two-stage prototypical network meta-trains on more readily available DWI distortion labels and adapts to PI-QUAL assessment by recomputing prototypes from five clinical support samples per class. Its dual-branch 3D ResNet fuses T2WI and DWI so anatomy can distinguish true morphology from distortion, while FiLM and a gradient reversal layer manage b-value variation and acquisition bias.

title: Bridging the Markerless Tracking Validation Gap: Intraoperative X-Ray Workflow Integration
motivation: RGB-D-based markerless spinal tracking could avoid invasive bone-anchored fiducials used in navigation. However, existing clinical datasets provide only approximate surface-based labels rather than independent subsurface vertebral pose ground truth, leaving no clinically viable way to quantify translational and rotational tracking error.
method: The pipeline recovers per-vertebra 6-DoF poses from routine multi-view C-arm fluoroscopy through 2D-3D CT-to-fluoroscopy registration. A multimodal fiducial array and calibrated transform chain co-register these subsurface poses with RGB-D recordings, enabling direct evaluation of markerless registration estimates without changing the surgical workflow.

title: Bridging Vision Foundation Model Priors with CLIP for Spatial-aware Few-shot Anomaly Detection in Medical Images
motivation: Few-shot medical anomaly detection can reduce the need for large normal-image collections, but CLIP-based methods often localize lesions poorly. CLIP's global image-text pretraining lacks explicit spatial supervision, patchification and limited resolution lose detail, and existing support-memory methods underuse abnormal examples while storing costly dense features.
method: Spatial-FAD refines CLIP patch features using a DINO-derived structural-affinity prior through a VFM-enhanced adapter, retaining text-semantic alignment while improving boundary adherence. It aggregates overlapping sliding-window features for denser high-resolution embeddings and stores compact normal and abnormal prototypes whose patch similarities are fused with image-text similarity at inference.

title: B-spline Activations as Intrinsic Uncertainty Estimators in Medical Image Segmentation
motivation: Clinical segmentation needs uncertainty estimates to flag predictions requiring review, but dominant Bayesian methods require repeated inference that conflicts with real-time workflows. Existing single-pass alternatives modify training objectives or impose global architectural constraints that may distort learned representations.
method: The method uses activation dispersion in locally supported B-spline bases of KAN layers as a deterministic pixel-level uncertainty signal. It adds a lightweight Residual KAN Head to an existing segmentation backbone, allowing uncertainty to be read in one forward pass without modifying the backbone or training objective.

title: C²RM-Seg: Causal Counterfactual Reasoning with Structural-Semantic Priors for Weakly Supervised Histopathological Tissue Segmentation
motivation: Weakly supervised histopathology segmentation reduces the cost of dense annotations, but depends on imperfect CAM pseudo-masks. CAM activations can be biased by staining and background context rather than causal tissue morphology, while conventional models struggle to jointly maintain detailed boundaries, global semantics, and robustness to label noise.
method: C²RM-Seg uses a causal counterfactual reasoning module to project features into latent factors, learn a causal structure matrix, and subtract confounding effects when generating CAM pseudo-masks. It then trains a dual-path model that fuses local ResNeSt morphology with frozen DINOV3 semantic priors through cross-path gating, using an uncertainty-gated margin loss to tolerate residual pseudo-label noise.

title: CAG-WM: A Synthetic-Data-Driven Coronary World Model for Autonomous Guidewire Navigation
motivation: Autonomous coronary guidewire navigation could reduce radiation exposure, workload, and operator variability during PCI. Existing reinforcement-learning and planning methods lack explicit guidewire-vessel dynamics, limiting sample efficiency, anticipation of action consequences, and generalization across coronary anatomy; paired angiography-3D data are also scarce.
method: CAG-WM constructs dynamic synthetic full-view coronary angiography and paired 3D voxelized coronary models, then trains a world model in a SOFA-based simulator. By learning vessel-guidewire dynamics and internally rolling out multiple future steps, it maps angiographic observations to continuous guidewire controls for long-horizon navigation.

title: CalCErt: Bin-wise Certification of Confidence Calibration in Medical Image Classification
motivation: Adversarial perturbations can alter both medical-image predictions and confidence scores, threatening safety-critical calibration. Existing certification mainly guarantees class stability, but a prediction can remain correct while becoming severely overconfident or underconfident, and there are no guarantees for bin-wise calibration deterioration.
method: CalCErt is a post-hoc method applicable to any pretrained differentiable classifier. It combines empirical bin-wise calibration estimates, statistical concentration bounds, and local Lipschitz estimates of the confidence function to bound worst-case bin-wise miscalibration within an l2 perturbation ball.

title: CalcSeg: Confidence-aware 3D Latent Context Curriculum Learning For Myocardial Scar Segmentation From Single-Stack LGE-CMRs
motivation: Automated myocardial scar segmentation from single-stack LGE-CMR is needed for reproducible fibrosis and infarction assessment, but manual delineation is labor-intensive and variable. Existing approaches struggle with low-contrast, diffuse, and small scars, often use static curriculum definitions, and do not fully capture 3D anatomical context from sparse 2D acquisitions.
method: CalcSeg uses semi-supervised confidence-aware curriculum learning to progressively include more difficult scar cases according to a learned score combining scar-map error, epistemic uncertainty, and scar-burden estimation. A latent fusion module with slice-wise self-attention integrates the single-stack slices to infer 3D contextual dependencies while retaining slice-specific features.

title: CALHippo: Cell Segmentation for Neuronal Density Inference in the Human Hippocampus
motivation: Biologically plausible brain-circuit models require cell-type-resolved maps of cellular composition and spatial distribution. Existing hippocampal reconstructions use low-resolution data without explicit cell-type annotations, limiting quantitative characterization across CA subfields and omitting comprehensive glial modeling.
method: CALHippo combines foundation-model-based cell-instance segmentation, iterative expert correction, and model ensembling to create expert-validated 1 um/px three-class hippocampal annotations. It projects these HR annotations into 20 um/px BigBrain space to supervise a UNet density estimator, then samples the predicted class-specific density maps into a whole-CA mesoscale cellular point cloud.

title: Calibrated Confidence Expression for Radiology Report Generation
motivation: Radiology-report LVLMs can hallucinate findings and are often overconfident, making accurate reports alone insufficient for safe clinical use. Existing multimodal uncertainty approaches commonly require multiple generations or estimate clinical uncertainty language rather than the model's own calibrated confidence, limiting efficient targeted review.
method: ConRad fine-tunes medical LVLMs with GRPO to generate radiology reports jointly with report-level or sentence-level numerical verbalized confidence. Its logarithmic-scoring-rule rewards use external continuous report-quality or sentence-correctness signals and optimize only confidence-expression tokens, encouraging calibrated self-assessment without changing report-generation capability.

title: CalibSleep: Cross-Modal Calibration and Rule-Aware Learning for Automatic Sleep Stage Classification
motivation: Automatic sleep staging is needed because manual PSG annotation is time-consuming and strongly dependent on expert experience. Existing methods often rely on a single signal or only one representation domain, fuse heterogeneous features insufficiently, and may produce stage transitions that conflict with physiological sleep patterns.
method: CalibSleep jointly encodes EEG/EOG waveforms and their time-frequency representations in two modality-specific streams. Its cross-modal calibration and fusion module uses bidirectional cross-attention and a learnable gate to align and balance heterogeneous features, while rule-aware transition regularization adds physiological sleep-stage priors as a soft constraint.

title: CALM: Interpretable Cross-Modal Alignment for Biomarker Discovery from Unpaired Data

categories.value: Multimodal Integration with Clinical / Genomic / Biomarkers

motivation: Discovering brain-genetics biomarkers for disorders such as ASD is important, but large neuroimaging and genetics repositories usually contain completely different participants. Existing multimodal approaches generally require paired samples or obscure feature-level biological interpretation, so they cannot fully exploit these disjoint unimodal resources.
method: CALM pretrains interpretable modality-specific encoders that preserve region- and pathway-level information, then maps MRI and genetic latent representations into a shared space using linear projections. A class-conditional MMD loss aligns modality distributions within diagnostic groups, while contrastive and orthogonality objectives preserve group separation and produce an ROI-pathway association matrix.

title: Can Agents Distinguish Visually Hard-to-Separate Diseases in a Zero-Shot Setting? A Pilot Study
motivation: Zero-shot MLLM agents may be useful for imaging-based diagnosis, but visually confounded diseases can have very different etiologies and management despite overlapping appearances. Single agents can prematurely favor one hypothesis and state unsupported conclusions, while many existing remedies require training data or external tools. The work examines whether agents can distinguish melanoma from atypical nevus and pulmonary edema from pneumonia under imaging-only conditions.
method: CARE uses contrastive adjudication among three zero-shot agents: two agents argue for opposing diagnoses, and a third judge synthesizes their arguments into a final decision. This structures disagreement to counter premature commitment and unsupported claims without extra training or external tools.

title: Can Experts Adapt Without Training? On Test-Time Modality Generalization in MVLMs
motivation: MVLM zero-shot performance can deteriorate on unseen imaging modalities, scanners, and acquisition protocols, although such shifts are common in clinical use. In MoE models, uniform fusion can dilute modality-specific knowledge, whereas relying on one confident expert can fail under distribution shift. Test-time expert reliability therefore needs to be estimated and adapted without costly optimization.
method: MoBE is an optimization-free test-time framework for modality-specialized MVLMs. It dynamically routes each sample to experts with relatively low predictive entropy, weights selected experts by inverse entropy, and refines them through per-expert Bayesian posterior updates from the incoming test stream. This adapts expert confidence, prototypes, and priors online without gradient or parameter updates.

title: Cancer-Type-Agnostic Pan-Cancer Gene Expression Prediction from Histopathological Images

categories.value: Multimodal Integration with Clinical / Genomic / Biomarkers

motivation: Gene-expression profiling is important for precision oncology but tissue sequencing is invasive, costly, time-consuming, and difficult to scale. Image-based prediction methods are commonly developed in closed settings for known cancer types and may not generalize across diverse histology and molecular regulation. Pan-cancer prediction when the cancer type is unknown is therefore an insufficiently addressed open-set generalization problem.
method: PIGP uses a dual-branch architecture for cancer-type-agnostic prediction from histopathology images. A global branch learns shared pan-cancer molecular patterns, while a cancer-specific residual branch models structured heterogeneity after the model preliminarily infers cancer type from image features. Adaptive fusion balances the shared and specific predictions for each case.

title: CancerVerse: A Fully Open Longitudinal and Multimodal Dataset for Multicancer Screening
motivation: CT cancer screening requires early detection while maintaining few false positives per scan, but public datasets rarely reflect the full clinical trajectory. Existing resources are often single-time-point, image-only, limited in cancer coverage, and lack healthy follow-up cohorts for credible specificity assessment. These gaps prevent models from learning tumor evolution and leveraging clinical evidence relevant to multicancer screening.
method: CancerVerse releases a multicancer screening resource that links longitudinal CT examinations with radiology reports, pathology results, clinical variables, and voxel-wise tumor annotations. It includes 13 cancer types and a verified healthy cohort with follow-up, and defines benchmark tasks for tumor detection and segmentation at fixed false positives per scan. The accompanying benchmarks compare longitudinal, multimodal modeling with single-time-point image-only modeling.

title: Cardiac Motion Transfer with Adaptive Physics Constraint
motivation: Cine-MRI captures cardiac motion but provides limited lesion contrast, whereas static LGE-MRI clearly depicts scars but lacks dynamics. Motion transfer can combine these complementary properties, yet data-driven synthesis lacks explicit physiological plausibility. Hard physics losses can also mislead optimization when cine-derived myocardial deformation fields are noisy or inaccurate.
method: The method extracts cine-MRI motion fields and refines them with a probabilistic, noise-adaptive physics constraint based on virtual residual likelihood. It weakens physics guidance when deformation estimates are unreliable and strengthens it in locally stable regions, then warps the static LGE image with the refined field to synthesize dLGE-MRI. Thus, physics information acts as a flexible guide rather than a hard loss.

title: CardiacPULSE: Frequency-Aware Self-supervised Cardiac Phase Detection in Echocardiography
motivation: End-diastole and end-systole identification enables key quantitative echocardiography measurements, but synchronized ECG and frame-level labels are often unavailable on portable ultrasound devices. Video-based inference is complicated by speckle noise, view variation, and probe motion. Existing self-supervised latent-motion methods can be view-specific and computationally burdensome for edge deployment.
method: CardiacPULSE derives a Fourier-based spatial prior by identifying pixels whose temporal signals concentrate at the dominant cardiac frequency. A 103K-parameter CNN learns to predict a compatible motion mask using self-supervised spectral-concentration, phase-coherence, and mask-coverage objectives. At inference, it combines motion-energy extrema with harmonic phase anchors from the mask-weighted temporal signal to localize ED and ES.

title: CardioDiT: Latent Diffusion Transformers for 4D Cardiac MRI Synthesis
motivation: Cine CMR requires both three-dimensional anatomy and cardiac dynamics, but most generative methods do not directly model the full 3D+t distribution. They instead factorize space and time, merge depth into channels, or rely on auxiliary consistency mechanisms. These choices can constrain global context and produce subtle spatiotemporal discontinuities or physiologically inconsistent motion.
method: CardioDiT encodes each 2D+t cine slice with a spatiotemporal VQ-GAN and stacks the slice latents into a complete 3D+t volume. A diffusion transformer partitions this volume into 4D patches and jointly denoises them using 4D positional encodings and global self-attention. The denoised latent slices are decoded and concatenated to reconstruct an unconditional cine CMR volume.

title: CardioGS: Deformation-Driven 4D Gaussian Splatting with Self-supervised Cardiac Clock Learning for Rotational DSA Reconstruction
motivation: Rotational DSA captures moving coronary vessels during a single sweep, where every sparse-view projection combines quasi-periodic cardiac deformation with monotonic contrast-agent transport. Assigning both processes to one acquisition timestamp makes the inverse problem ambiguous: geometry may explain photometric change and appearance may explain motion. Existing approaches that keep geometry static cannot faithfully model cardiac motion under this setting.
method: CardioGS is a deformation-driven 4D Gaussian Splatting model with separate temporal coordinates for geometry and appearance. Its self-supervised ClockNet integrates a bounded instantaneous frequency to learn a smooth monotonic cardiac clock for deformation, while canonical-space appearance is conditioned on acquisition time to model contrast transport. Cycle-consistent sparse deformation control nodes impose quasi-periodicity, and a conditioning curriculum stabilizes co-optimization.

title: CARE: Clinically Aligned Retrieval Evidence for Consistent Radiology Report Generation
motivation: Radiology report generation must tightly ground pathological interpretations in image evidence, yet current models can produce unsupported findings or repetitive generic templates. Retrieval augmentation can provide prior clinical evidence, but end-to-end retriever training causes active queries to drift away from stale queued keys. This representation inconsistency destabilizes retrieval supervision and can weaken clinically grounded generation, especially across datasets.
method: CARE uses a gradient-updated query encoder and a slowly updated momentum key encoder to populate a shared retrieval memory queue with temporally coherent image and report representations. It applies differentiable disease-aware alignment to make retrieval weights favor diagnostically compatible reports. Projected image features and retrieved evidence are then supplied to a frozen LLM for autoregressive report generation.

title: CARE: Confidence-Aware Reasoning for Reliable Medical VQA
motivation: Medical MLLMs for VQA need transparent reasoning because diagnostic errors have serious consequences. Although reinforcement fine-tuning can produce Chain-of-Thought reasoning, existing approaches mainly reward answer correctness and can express confidence that does not match actual accuracy. This miscalibration, including unwarranted certainty on wrong diagnoses, undermines clinical trust and safe decision support.
method: CARE uses a two-stage reasoning pipeline. It first synthesizes structured Medical-CoT data for supervised cold-start training, then applies GRPO with a Confidence-Aware Reward that conditions confidence on answer correctness. The reward jointly encourages accurate VQA answers and confidence that reflects diagnostic reliability.

title: CARformer: Class-Aware Representation Learning for Small-Cohort, Imbalanced Psychiatric Disorder Classification in Brain MRI
motivation: Psychiatric diagnosis is largely based on subjective symptoms, which overlap across disorders and can lead to uncertain or inappropriate treatment. Multi-disorder classification from sMRI must distinguish subtle disorder-specific morphology, but site-level datasets are small, imbalanced, and heterogeneous across acquisition protocols. A robust representation-learning approach is therefore needed for differential diagnosis under limited data.
method: CARformer adapts a domain-pretrained 3D Uniformer encoder for multi-class sMRI classification. Its Class-Aware Bag-of-Queries module learns class-aligned queries to aggregate discriminative evidence, while Class-Aware Contrastive learning strengthens class separation under imbalance. Together, these components adapt pretrained representations to subtle disorder differences in small, heterogeneous cohorts.

title: Case-Specific Priors-Guided Multimodal Fusion for Prognosis Prediction in Head and Neck Cancer
motivation: Head and neck cancer prognosis requires combining heterogeneous clinical and pathological modalities whose correspondence and representation granularity are difficult to align. Existing fusion methods usually learn generic interactions or use case-generic clinical rationale, overlooking how cross-modal relationships vary from patient to patient. Expert case-specific priors are costly to annotate, motivating an automatic way to derive and use them.
method: CPM uses LLM-derived priors describing case-specific intra-modal contexts and inter-modal relations, together with case-generic multimodal rationale. IntraCC calibrates each modality against its context, InterRI conditions pairwise interactions on the current case's relations, and MultiRA learns rationale-conditioned weights to aggregate the interactions for risk prediction. This creates a staged, clinically guided fusion process across the four modalities.

title: CDFP-Net: Cross-Modal Dynamic Fusion with Diffusion Priors for PET-CT Tumor Segmentation

categories.value: AI for Neglected Diseases & Limited-Resource Settings

motivation: Accurate PET-CT tumor segmentation is important for diagnosis and radiotherapy, but high-quality paired annotations are scarce and volumetric 3D processing is expensive. PET and CT also have different physical properties, and simple fusion can suppress metabolic cues or produce boundary errors and false positives. A method is needed that transfers useful priors, models asymmetric cross-modal complementarity, and remains computationally efficient.
method: CDFP-Net uses a frozen self-supervised DDPM as a feature prior and lightweight adapters, including ILN and Dual-SE, to adapt modality-specific representations with limited supervision. Its modality-asymmetric dynamic graph lets metabolically salient PET regions query complementary anatomical boundary information from CT. Multi-Angle Maximum Intensity Projection supplies efficient 2.5D global context while reducing full-3D computation.

title: CDPM-Align: Multi-Scale Guidance-Aligned Diffusion Pretraining for Robust Few-Shot Anatomical Landmark Detection
motivation: Anatomical landmark detectors need calibrated uncertainty and robustness in addition to sub-millimetric localization accuracy for safe clinical use. Conventional supervised or self-supervised pretraining may not capture heterogeneous anatomical structures, and unconditional diffusion can conflate anatomical modes. The effect of representation pretraining on reliability under very limited annotations therefore remains an important gap.
method: CDPM-Align performs conditional diffusion pretraining on heterogeneous small-scale X-ray datasets, using dataset indices as conditioning labels. It treats classifier-free guidance as a structural descriptor and imposes multi-scale alignment across independently sampled diffusion timesteps and U-Net levels. The pretrained backbone is then fine-tuned for landmark detection with only 10 or 25 annotated images.

title: Cell-Division-Aware Category-Enhanced Contrastive Learning Model for Embryonic Cleavage Stage Classification
motivation: Cleavage-stage classification is important for embryo quality assessment, but adjacent stages differ only locally and are obscured by blastomere overlap, occlusion, and morphological confusion. Existing sequence models use temporal information superficially, lack explicit cell-division cues, and struggle with sparse stages and category imbalance. A model that detects developmental changes and uses them to stabilize stage boundaries is needed.
method: 3CL-ECSC combines core-region extraction, a Cell Division Aware module, and a Category-Enhanced Contrastive Learning classifier. The division module predicts whether cell division occurred between frame pairs, using multi-order pairs for global cues and first-order pairs for local transition cues. These predictions correct and recalibrate sequence classifications before a linear-chain CRF enforces transfer and monotonicity constraints.

title: Cervical Vertebral Maturation Staging from a Continuous Perspective
motivation: Cervical vertebral maturation is biologically gradual, although clinical assessment uses six discrete stages. Transitional radiographs cause substantial inter-expert variability, while exact-match classification treats adjacent-stage errors as equally unacceptable and ignores the clinically relevant Tol-1 tolerance. Automated assessment therefore needs a continuous or ordinal formulation aligned with the underlying progression.
method: ORACLE first segments C2-C4 with a U-Net++ model using an EfficientNet-B5 encoder and boundary-aware composite losses. Vertebra-specific and overall masks are encoded and combined for stage prediction. The framework compares regression, EMD-based ordinal classification, and CORAL ordinal classification so that adjacent-stage relationships and clinically meaningful tolerance can be modeled explicitly.

title: CerviThink: A Reinforced Visual Reasoning Framework for Cervical Cancer Cell Classification
motivation: Cervical cytology screening is laborious and subjective, and automated classification is challenged by subtle morphology, overlapping cells, and imaging artifacts. CNN-based systems lack transparent reasoning, while current vision-language models can have unreliable spatial perception and require costly annotations. A context-aware system that reproduces structured pathological observation and explains ambiguous decisions is needed.
method: CerviThink fine-tunes the Qwen2.5-VL model on a RAG-constructed CerviCoT dataset containing image-question pairs and pathology-inspired rationales. Its grounding phase uses focus, transform, and ignore operations to isolate or mask diagnostic regions, while the answering phase classifies cells from the original and manipulated evidence. Dynamic Visual Hybrid Rewards combine consistency and background-normality feedback with format and accuracy rewards to refine reasoning through reinforcement learning.

title: CheXanatomy: Anatomy–Aware Vision–Language Modeling for Chest Radiographs
motivation: Anatomical segmentation in chest radiographs is difficult because projection geometry, overlapping structures, and acquisition variation create domain shifts. U-Net-style models perform well in-distribution but require dense pixel labels and may degrade on real data, whereas VLMs mainly learn global image-text alignment without explicit fine-grained anatomy. Scalable supervision and anatomy-aware representation learning are therefore needed.
method: CheXanatomy fine-tunes a pretrained VLM to generate anatomical segmentation masks through autoregressive next-token prediction, without adding a pixel-space decoder head. It creates scalable supervision by rendering synthetic AP and lateral chest radiographs from CT volumes and projecting CT segmentation labels into consistent 2D masks. Parameter-efficient adaptation and controlled studies of scale, resolution, and encoder tuning assess how anatomical supervision shapes the VLM representation.

title: CHILD: Human-in-the-Loop OOD Detection for Safe Clinical Deployment
motivation: OOD detection is essential because clinical systems encounter unseen diseases and may otherwise produce overconfident errors. Test-time adaptation can improve detection but changes behavior automatically from unlabeled streams, creating safety risks and accumulating errors; reviewing every case is impractical. A streaming method is needed that uses sparse physician feedback selectively and safely.
method: CHILD operates without parameter updates and maintains a compact cache of physician-reviewed ID and OOD features. Its risk-aware sample selection identifies uncertain regions in the streaming score space and spends the limited review budget on samples with the greatest potential risk. Retrieval-based similarity calibration then adjusts OOD scores using the reviewed cache, enabling controlled online adaptation.

title: ChronoSurv: A Clinical Pathway-Guided Graph Framework for Multimodal Survival Analysis

categories.value: Multimodal Integration with Clinical / Genomic / Biomarkers

motivation: Head and neck cancer survival prediction must integrate clinical variables, imaging, pathology, and reports that differ greatly in scale and structure. Existing multimodal models often use static fusion and treat patient data as an unordered feature collection, overlooking the hierarchical and chronological organization of clinical care. Modeling the care pathway explicitly could improve cross-modal integration and progression-aware risk prediction.
method: ChronoSurv represents each patient's care trajectory as a hierarchical directed graph aligned with diagnostic and treatment steps. Fine-grained, coarse, and global nodes capture multiple levels of information, while heterogeneous message passing models asymmetric relationships across modalities and clinical stages. The topology can adapt when modalities are missing, producing a progression-aware representation for survival prediction.

title: CIGTSurv: Clinical Information Guided Tri-Modal Survival Prediction with Local Prototype Association and Global Feature Alignment
