motivation: Survival prediction benefits from combining whole-slide pathology images and genomic data, but clinical information that captures overall patient health is still underused. Its discrete, sparse, low-dimensional representation and the heterogeneity among pathology, genomic, and clinical modalities hinder effective integration, while existing text prompting can ignore dependencies among clinical indicators. A method is needed to encode clinical context coherently and model cross-modal relationships at multiple levels.
method: CIGTSurv converts structured clinical variables into coherent text and high-dimensional token embeddings using a holistic template and pretrained foundation models. With clinical information as an anchor, its local prototype association module uses cross-attention to learn token-level correspondences across pathology, genomic, and clinical modalities. A global feature alignment loss based on Maximum Mean Discrepancy further aligns modality distributions, enabling complementary local and global cross-modal interactions for survival prediction.

title: CiLA: Knowledge-Preserving Self-supervised Adaptation of CLIP for Fundus Imaging
motivation: Self-supervised adaptation of general-purpose CLIP to fundus images can cause representation drift and overwrite knowledge that supports downstream transfer. Generic objectives also emphasize appearance and augmentation invariance rather than fine-grained lesion evidence, while original CLIP predictions may be biased or miscalibrated in medical datasets. Adaptation therefore needs semantic anchors that preserve desired knowledge and reliable pseudo-label guidance.
method: CiLA adapts CLIP to unlabeled fundus images while preserving useful original knowledge. It defines clinically meaningful ophthalmic attributes, obtains attribute pseudo-labels and predictions from the original CLIP, and adds attribute-prediction and consistency objectives alongside standard contrastive or masked-image learning. A Dynamic Debias Module calibrates biased pseudo-labels during training, and the plug-and-play design can be inserted into multiple self-supervised paradigms.

title: CineMesh4D: Personalized 4D Whole Heart Reconstruction from Sparse Cine MRI
motivation: Patient-specific 3D+t whole-heart reconstruction is important for cardiac digital twins and functional assessment, but routine cine MRI samples 3D anatomy sparsely with widely spaced 2D slices. Existing image-to-mesh methods often reconstruct only selected chambers or phases, and whole-heart approaches may require time-consuming 3D acquisitions or fail to model the full coupling of shape and motion. A direct method must recover complete anatomy while maintaining cardiac-cycle temporal coherence from sparse inputs.
method: CineMesh4D directly maps multi-view sparse cine MRI sequences to patient-specific whole-heart mesh sequences. A differentiable rendering loss derived from the Beer–Lambert law supervises 3D+t reconstruction using sparse 2D contours, while a mesh variational autoencoder represents anatomical variability with graph convolutions and long-range graph attention. A dual-context temporal block combines sequence-level and local sliding-window information with residual gating to produce temporally coherent mesh representations.

title: CIPHER: Causal Intervention Pathways for Healthcare Equity and Robustness
motivation: Medical diagnosis models can show large performance gaps across groups defined by race, sex, age, or skin tone, and these gaps may worsen under distribution shifts. Existing augmentation and fairness methods usually target only one or two dependency channels and do not explain which causal source of disparity is corrected; disease-conditioned synthesis can also fail to preserve patient-specific context. A unified intervention framework is needed to address the distinct pathways through which sensitive factors shape observed medical images.
method: CIPHER formalizes medical image formation with a structural causal model in which sensitive attributes affect images through population, manifestation, prevalence, and environment pathways. Its diffusion framework uses global conditioning on sensitive attributes and disease to reshape subgroup composition, while null-text inversion enables instance-anchored counterfactual editing that preserves patient-specific anatomy. Classifier-free guidance supports controllable synthesis so the four dependency pathways can be intervened on individually or in combination.

title: ClinCoT: Clinical-Aware Visual Chain-of-Thought for Medical Vision Language Models
motivation: Medical vision-language models can hallucinate because their conclusions are insufficiently grounded in localized pathological evidence. Existing preference optimization mainly corrects final responses, and text-centric chain-of-thought does not explicitly restructure visual attention around lesions or connect regions to intermediate reasoning. Clinically reliable alignment therefore requires hypotheses-driven, region-aware reasoning supervision rather than response-level correction alone.
method: ClinCoT generates disease-conditioned region proposals from predefined clinical hypotheses and asks the target Med-VLM to produce intermediate reasoning chains using both the full image and each localized region. Multiple medical LLM evaluators score these responses, with consensus-weighted scores reflecting current quality and influence on subsequent reasoning. A margin-aware preference objective uses both rankings and score differences, while iterative regeneration updates preference data as the model policy changes.

title: Clinical-Injection Transformer with Domain-Adapted MAE for Lupus Nephritis Prognosis Prediction
motivation: Pediatric lupus nephritis has severe and variable treatment outcomes, yet biopsy-based prognosis prediction in children remains unexplored. Existing clinical models discard renal morphology, while the only histopathology approach requires multiple costly stains and does not integrate clinical data; multimodal fusion architectures can also overfit small cohorts. A routine single-stain, multimodal framework is needed to combine morphology and clinical context efficiently.
method: The Clinical-Injection Transformer inserts structured clinical features as condition tokens into patch-level self-attention, allowing bidirectional interaction with biopsy representations in one attention space. Domain-adapted MAE pretraining learns morphological representations, while a decoupled adaptation strategy separates this representation learning from pathological classification knowledge extraction. Multi-granularity morphological type injection transfers distilled classification knowledge to prognostic prediction at both patch and patient levels.

title: Clinically Structured Chain-of-Thought Reasoning for Intelligent Guidance in Coronary Artery Disease
motivation: Coronary CT angiography provides detailed anatomy and plaque information for CAD, but most automated systems map images directly to predictions without systematically integrating case context or clinical workflow. Heterogeneous anatomical, lesion, pericoronary, and risk features are difficult to combine, and flat reasoning limits patient-specific interpretability and interaction. A clinically structured reasoning framework is needed to support reliable case-level diagnosis and management.
method: CS-CoT encodes anatomical structures, lesion characteristics, pericoronary features, patient risk profiles, and diagnostic case priors, then projects these heterogeneous semantics into a unified textual space. Its structured diagnostic reasoning module hierarchically orders the features according to the CAD workflow and feeds them through a traceable chain of thought. The resulting vision-language framework supports case-level diagnosis and management guidance that can be interpreted and interacted with clinically.

title: Clinically-Grounded Hierarchical Classification for Consistent Chest X-ray Interpretation
motivation: Chest X-ray interpretation proceeds from broad anatomical localization to specific findings, but most automated systems treat it as flat classification. Existing anatomy-aware or hierarchical methods often use two-stage pipelines, shallow taxonomies, or independent predictions and therefore can produce contradictions between coarse and fine levels, especially when multiple systems are abnormal. A unified model must learn and enforce clinically valid cross-level dependencies.
method: CHASE uses a shared Vision Transformer with a clinically defined hierarchy of 9 anatomical regions, 17 sub-regions, and 28 findings. Its training objective combines supervision at all levels, Global KL Alignment for cross-level probability agreement, and a hierarchy-violation penalty that discourages unsupported fine-grained predictions. This single-stage design enforces anatomically coherent coarse-to-fine interpretation within a multi-label setting.

title: ClinLoop: Human-AI Collaborative Agents for Multimodal Breast Cancer Diagnosis Under Incomplete Clinical Data

categories.value: AI for Population Health, Public Health & Epidemiology

motivation: Breast cancer diagnosis often relies on CT, MRI, and digital mammography, but real-world patients frequently have only a subset of these modalities. Standard multimodal fusion assumes complete inputs, while missing-modality methods do not ensure that insufficient or out-of-distribution evidence is flagged for expert review. A deployable system must operate with arbitrary modality availability, triage uncertainty safely, and learn from limited clinician time.
method: ClinLoop has a diagnosis agent with modality-specific encoders and a missing-modality fusion module that accepts arbitrary subsets of CT, MRI, and mammography. A separate quality-assurance agent uses an ensemble to estimate uncertainty and defers low-confidence, discordant, or out-of-distribution cases to clinicians. Confirmed labels from review are fed back to update the model, creating a selective human–AI learning loop.

title: ClinRAG-GRAPH: Clinical-Prior Retrieval-Augmented Graph Model with Domain Adversarial Learning for Breast pCR Prediction

categories.value: Multimodal Integration with Clinical / Genomic / Biomarkers

motivation: Predicting pathological complete response before neoadjuvant chemotherapy could support treatment stratification, but robust multicenter prediction remains difficult. Existing models often use simple multimodal fusion, insufficiently address scanner and protocol heterogeneity, and provide only scalar probabilities without case-based evidence. A method is needed to model clinically structured relationships, learn domain-invariant features, and ground predictions in analogous clinical cases.
method: ClinRAG-GRAPH builds an intra-patient graph from DCE-MRI, structured clinical variables, and biopsy-derived biomarkers, encoding clinical priors through relation-aware graph convolution. A dual-branch domain-adversarial strategy suppresses multicenter MRI protocol effects while retaining pCR-relevant information. An LLM-driven subgraph retrieval-augmented generation module retrieves clinically analogous historical cases and incorporates their evidence into pCR inference.

title: CMD-AD: Cross-Modality Distillation from fMRI-EEG for Single-Modality Alzheimer’s Disease Diagnosis
motivation: Alzheimer’s disease disrupts both spatial organization and temporal dynamics of brain functional connectivity, which are complementary captured by fMRI and EEG. Clinical acquisitions rarely provide paired modalities, while existing fusion methods often require both at inference and use coarse cross-modality interactions. A method is needed to transfer complementary spatiotemporal knowledge into deployable single-modality diagnosis.
method: CMD-AD is a three-stage cross-modality distillation framework. Hierarchical graph attention aggregation encoders are pretrained separately to learn multiscale fMRI spatial and multiband EEG temporal features. Scale-wise bidirectional cross-modality fusion creates spatiotemporal targets, which are then distilled back into each modality-specific encoder so either fMRI or EEG can support inference without paired inputs.

title: CMSA-Net: Causal Multi-scale Aggregation with Adaptive Multi-source Reference for Video Polyp Segmentation
motivation: Video polyp segmentation is clinically useful for locating and tracking lesions during colonoscopy, but polyps often have weak semantic contrast with mucosa. Large position and scale changes across frames disrupt temporal consistency, and clinical deployment also requires low-latency inference. Existing methods commonly use single-scale fusion and fixed single-source references, limiting robust semantic guidance.
method: CMSA-Net introduces Causal Multi-scale Aggregation (CMA) to aggregate semantic information from reference and adjacent frames at multiple spatial scales. Causal attention enforces chronological propagation and reduces contamination from large inter-frame changes. A Dynamic Multi-source Reference (DMR) strategy selects and updates reliable reference frames using semantic separability and prediction confidence, providing diverse guidance with controlled computation.

title: Coarse-to-Fine Meta-Reweighting with Dynamic Retrieval for Adult-to-Pediatric Domain Adaptation in Tumor Segmentation
motivation: Pediatric brain tumor segmentation suffers from severe annotation scarcity, making augmentation with adult glioma data necessary. Anatomical, tissue, tumor-type, and subregion differences create an adult-to-pediatric domain shift, while mixed training can favor adult-dominant features. Meta-reweighting is promising, but random or noisy pediatric references can make weighting unstable and pediatric relevance weak.
method: The method uses coarse-to-fine meta-reweighting. A coarse stage performs cross-domain binary tumor segmentation for stable localization, while a fine stage refines pediatric-specific subregions through gradient-alignment-based sample weighting. A gradient-similarity retrieval mechanism maintains representative pediatric meta-cases as a stable reference set, avoiding noisy online samples and enabling efficient reweighting.

title: COAST: Context-Aware Differential Learning for Gene Expression Prediction in Spatial Transcriptomics
motivation: Spatial transcriptomics provides spatially resolved gene expression but is costly, low-throughput, and limited in resolution, motivating prediction from H&E images. Morphology-to-expression mapping is nonlinear and depends on local microenvironment and global tissue structure. Existing context-aware models mainly regress absolute expression and rarely supervise relative differences, leaving predictions sensitive to slide and protocol variation.
method: COAST extracts target-spot features together with local nearest-neighbor and global context spots. Type-specific affine modulation conditions context representations according to local or global origin, and a Transformer aggregates the target and modulated context tokens. Joint absolute-expression regression and signed differential regression directly supervise both expression magnitudes and relative spatial relationships.

title: CoGaze: Closed-Loop Eye-Face Alignment for Multi-center Mobile Gaze-Based Cognitive Screening in Older Adults
motivation: Mobile gaze-based screening could provide frequent, low-burden cognitive assessment, but gaze estimation is fragile under aging-related appearance changes, uncontrolled capture noise, and fluctuating engagement. Eyelid and glasses effects, head motion, illumination changes, occlusion, and blur cause frame jitter and long-term drift that corrupt oculomotor features. Robust alignment of ocular and facial evidence with temporal stability is therefore needed.
method: CoGaze formulates gaze estimation as alignment between ocular appearance and facial geometry. A prototype-anchor dictionary retrieved with normalized cosine attention stabilizes ocular representations, while reciprocal cross-attention lets eye and face evidence resolve each other’s ambiguities. Differential spatiotemporal attention and a segment-level consistency objective reduce jitter and drift while preserving genuine saccades.

title: CoGE: Sim-to-Real Online Geometric Estimation for Monocular Colonoscopy
motivation: Monocular geometric estimation is important for 3D perception, navigation, and planning in colonoscopy, but realistic depth, point-cloud, and camera ground truth is difficult and costly to collect in the narrow colon. Simulated data provide supervision, yet artifacts and illumination differences create a substantial sim-to-real feature gap. Existing style-translation pipelines add preprocessing and may not generalize across diverse real scenes.
method: CoGE is a feed-forward sim-to-real framework trained only on simulated colonoscopy data. An illumination-aware supervision module inspired by Retinex adjusts confidence under varying surface illumination, while a wavelet-based structure-aware module extracts shared global and local colon features. A memory-forget mechanism filters redundant sequence memory before producing depth and 3D reconstruction estimates.

title: Collaborative Multiscale Representation Learning for AMD Detection
motivation: AMD lesions vary in morphology, boundary clarity, size, and spatial distribution across the fundus and macula. Single-scale classification compresses these heterogeneous signals, attenuating peripheral lesions and allowing extensive or salient abnormalities to dominate subtle ones. A representation that preserves complementary global-local and multiscale lesion information is needed for robust detection.
method: CoMRep uses dual feature-extraction branches for the global fundus and local macula, producing multiscale lesion representations. Global-local Cross-scale Attention projects features into multiple latent perspectives and enables bidirectional interactions across scales. Collaborative Glocal Feature Aggregation uses perspective-specific experts to refine heterogeneous lesion patterns before combining them for AMD prediction.

title: Collaborative Topology and Connectivity Learning for EM Neuron Segmentation
motivation: EM neuron segmentation must resolve blurred membranes and intricate topologies, yet affinity-based methods relying mainly on local continuity produce severe split and merge errors. Skeletons provide macroscopic continuity and distance transforms provide separation constraints, but naive fusion of their predictions can cause negative transfer in ambiguous regions. Terabyte-scale connectomics also demands an efficient deployment architecture.
method: The framework has two collaborative stages for affinity prediction. Stage I uses an Affinity-Collaborative Weighting Mechanism to stabilize joint extraction of image, skeleton, and distance-transform features. Stage II applies cascaded Block-wise Representation Routing to select reliable streams for conditional fusion, and gradient-based structural filter pruning compresses the shared backbone for large-volume inference.

title: Colon-Bench: An Agentic Workflow for Scalable Dense Lesion Annotation in Full-Procedure Colonoscopy Videos
motivation: Robust AI for colonoscopy is limited by the lack of densely annotated, long-sequence videos with diverse lesions and spatial, temporal, and linguistic supervision. Existing datasets often focus on single-class polyp detection or narrow tasks, while manual dense annotation is labor-intensive and inconsistent. A scalable, verified benchmark is needed to evaluate modern MLLMs and video understanding systems in realistic colonoscopy conditions.
method: Colon-Bench is built through a multi-stage agentic annotation workflow. Vision-language proposals are temporally verified, tracked for bounding boxes, confirmed with AI using visual cues, and passed through human review, yielding dense spatial, temporal, and clinical-text annotations for full-procedure videos. The resulting benchmark supports lesion classification, OV-VOS, and VQA, and the authors derive a colon-skill prompting strategy from observed MLLM errors.

title: Community-Aware Dynamic Graph Learning for Brain Disorder Diagnosis
motivation: Dynamic fMRI connectivity can reveal disorder-related changes in brain interactions, but standard graphs usually assume zero-lag correlations and overlook biologically meaningful propagation delays. Existing models also underuse the brain’s hierarchical modular organization and rarely model disorder-related switching of regions between communities. A unified approach is needed to capture lag-aware spatiotemporal interactions and evolving community structure.
method: CaDGNN first constructs lag-aware dynamic functional-connectivity graphs by explicitly encoding inter-regional time delays. A temporal community co-occurrence encoder captures evolving functional-module memberships and interactions. Its dual-level dynamic learning module jointly models node switching between communities and the temporal evolution of communities for diagnosis.

title: Co-MoCo: Collaborative Learning Enabled Motion Compensation for Weight-Bearing CBCT
motivation: Weight-bearing cone-beam CT provides clinically useful imaging under physiological load, but its relatively long scans make it vulnerable to involuntary patient tremors and motion artifacts. Existing software methods either restore images or estimate motion separately; image restoration can oversmooth fine details, while motion optimization can be computationally expensive or poorly suited to random tremors. A collaborative approach is needed to use image priors and physical consistency together.
method: Co-MoCo jointly optimizes an image-domain prior network and 6-DoF rigid-motion parameters in an end-to-end differentiable reconstruction loop. Its Motion-Aware Dual-Decoder Network (MADN) is trained with Optimal Transport Conditional Flow Matching to produce artifact-free slice priors from corrupted images and motion-intensity information. During iterative correction, the reconstructed volume is matched to the MADN output, allowing restoration and motion estimation to mutually regularize one another.

title: Comparative Analysis of Automated Frame Selection Methods for Glaucoma Detection in Smartphone-Based Low-Quality Fundus Video
motivation: Ultra-low-cost smartphone fundus imaging could expand glaucoma screening, but handheld motion, unstable focus, glare, blur, and limited retinal visibility make individual frames unreliable. Classical quality metrics can be fooled by artifacts, and models trained on clinical-quality images suffer severe domain shift. Since short videos contain intermittent valid views, robust automated frame selection is essential for dependable screening.
method: The framework first localizes the optic disc and uses it as a spatial gate for quality assessment. It then computes complementary spectral and structural measures, including retinal saturation, red-channel dominance, vessel density, and sharpness, and combines them multiplicatively so that failure in any modality penalizes a frame. Selection is evaluated by its downstream effect on MobileNetV3-based glaucoma classification rather than by quality scores alone.

title: Compass: Prostate Cancer Detection Needs Multi-view Context
motivation: Micro-ultrasound can support prostate cancer detection, but most AI methods analyze isolated 2D frames even though clinicians interpret continuous prostate sweeps and biopsy views for three-dimensional context. Single-frame analysis therefore underuses spatially continuous evidence and may be sensitive to operator and view variability. A user-agnostic method that integrates multi-view study context is needed for reliable detection.
method: Compass represents a prostate micro-ultrasound study as a stream of 2D frames and jointly processes rotational sweep cine-loops with biopsy-acquisition frames. A transformer aggregates evidence across the study while conditioning on the probe’s rotational angle, aligning global sweep context with local biopsy evidence. A decoder produces both frame-level and study-level cancer risk scores.

title: Computer-Assisted Intervention in Capsule Endoscopy: A Real-Time Edge-AI Auditing System
motivation: Video capsule endoscopy produces tens of thousands of frames, making manual review lengthy, variable, and prone to missed abnormalities. Most AI systems classify frames independently and impose temporal consistency only through post-processing, which fails to learn sequence dynamics and long-range anatomical transitions from full examinations. A real-time system that jointly audits anatomy and abnormalities while modeling temporal context is needed.
method: The system encodes consecutive capsule-endoscopy frames with an endoscopy-pretrained CNN and feeds the sequence to a lightweight Vision Transformer in a sequence-to-sequence architecture. Multi-task learning jointly predicts gastrointestinal anatomical regions and binary anomalies, with frame-level outputs produced directly and without heuristic post-processing. The design learns temporal coherence and long-range transitions intrinsically while remaining suitable for low-power edge deployment.

title: Concept-Guided Noisy Negative Suppression for Zero-Shot Classification and Grounding of Chest X-Ray Findings
motivation: Vision-language training for chest X-rays commonly treats reports from different patients as negatives, even when they describe the same finding, creating contradictory supervision and semantic ambiguity. Using raw reports preserves clinical language diversity but mismatches short inference prompts, whereas rigid templates improve consistency but lose linguistic detail. A concept-level strategy is needed to identify valid negatives while retaining both report diversity and prompt consistency.
method: CoNNS builds a hierarchical ontology for 41 chest X-ray concepts with presence, location and characteristic attributes, plus evidential segments and standardized presence statements. It relabels cross-patient image-text pairs through fine-grained presence analysis, removes semantically conflicting false negatives, and mines hard negatives with subtle attribute differences. A Concept-Aware NCE loss then aligns images with consistent reports while suppressing the identified noisy negatives.

title: ConceptIL: Concept Incremental Learning for Interpretable Medical AI
motivation: Concept bottleneck models can make medical AI interpretable, but sparse expert concept annotations cause distorted concept predictions, and real clinical knowledge evolves as new signs are recognized. Incrementally adding concepts is difficult because historical data may be inaccessible for privacy reasons and new concepts can have few positive samples. A learning framework is needed to incorporate sequentially observed concepts without retaining old images and while handling imbalance.
method: ConceptIL uses a frozen feature extractor, an analytical concept predictor, and a task predictor to learn newly arriving concepts incrementally. The analytical predictor updates its parameters recursively and stores inverse correlation matrices rather than historical samples, yielding joint-training-equivalent concept prediction while preserving data privacy. A dynamic weighting strategy addresses imbalanced positive frequencies among concepts.

title: Conditional Diffusion Prompting for Ambiguous Medical Image Segmentation
motivation: Ambiguous medical images can support multiple clinically plausible segmentations because of weak boundaries, low contrast, partial volume, and annotator variability, so a single mask cannot represent the uncertainty. Existing stochastic promptable models often introduce coarse prompt noise that is weakly structured and decoupled from image ambiguity, producing diverse but image-inconsistent boundaries. A method is needed to model prompt uncertainty in a structured way while preserving image consistency.
method: Diffusion Prompting models stochastic dense prompt embeddings through iterative denoising before SAM-style decoding. Conditional Diffusion Prompting further conditions this denoising on stochastic image embeddings, coupling prompt-space variability to image-side ambiguity. The resulting prompt samples are decoded into diverse segmentation candidates that remain tied to image-consistent boundaries.

title: Conditional Latent Diffusion Model with Fourier-Based Motion Modelling for Virtual Population Synthesis
motivation: In-silico cardiac device trials require virtual populations with realistic anatomy and full-cycle motion, but most mesh generators model only static anatomy. Existing sequence models encourage periodicity through temporal conditioning, which can cause endpoint drift and imperfect cycle closure that undermine simulation reliability. A controllable generator that enforces periodic motion explicitly is needed.
method: 4D F-MeshLDM first encodes phase-specific cardiac meshes with a convolutional mesh VAE. It fits each latent motion trajectory with a truncated Fourier series, representing periodic motion as coefficient tokens, and trains a Transformer diffusion prior over these tokens conditioned on clinical covariates through adaptive layer normalization. Inverse Fourier synthesis followed by VAE decoding generates controllable full-cycle 3D+t mesh sequences with periodicity built in.

title: Confidence-Aware Supervision for Robust Multi-task Embryo Grading
motivation: Automated embryo grading jointly predicts developmental stage, inner cell mass, and trophectoderm, but these tasks differ in morphology and intrinsic uncertainty. Uniform supervision can make confidence unstable and overconfident, especially for ambiguous localized structures, while conventional calibration methods are mainly post-hoc or designed for single tasks. A supervision strategy that adapts to heterogeneous confidence reliability is needed.
method: The method extracts temporally smoothed features with an exponential-moving-average encoder and clusters them separately for Stage, ICM, and TE tasks. Cluster label purity and feature-to-centroid consistency produce sample confidence, and only high-confidence samples receive soft labels formed by mixing cluster label distributions with their original labels; ambiguous samples retain hard labels. Entropy stability controls when refinements are updated, while temperature scaling can be added afterward for calibration.

title: Conformal 3D Lesion Segmentation with Balanced Risk Control
motivation: Medical segmentation commonly uses a fixed 0.5 threshold without finite-sample guarantees for clinically important false negatives. This is especially risky in sparse 3D lesion segmentation, where under-segmentation or missed small lesions can affect diagnosis and treatment. A statistically valid, model-agnostic method is needed to control per-case voxel-level FNR while limiting excessive mask expansion.
method: CLS is a model-agnostic post-processing procedure that calibrates a single global binarization threshold using a held-out calibration set. For each case, it finds the smallest threshold-related mask expansion that keeps voxel-level FNR below a user-specified tolerance, then applies a finite-sample-corrected conformal quantile of these critical values. Under exchangeability, the resulting threshold controls the probability of violating the per-case FNR constraint while avoiding unnecessary expansion and associated false positives.

title: Confusion-Aware Evidence Calibration for Few-Shot Whole Slide Image Classification
motivation: Whole-slide images are gigapixel-sized, making end-to-end analysis difficult, while conventional multiple-instance learning requires substantial labeled data that is scarce for rare cancer subtypes and constrained by privacy. Few-shot vision-language methods improve local sensitivity through prompt-to-patch matching, but aggregating thousands of interactions amplifies noise from ambiguous morphology and incomplete or mismatched prompts, blurring class boundaries. A robust calibration mechanism is therefore needed for data-scarce WSI diagnosis.
method: CAEC maintains a dynamic category-to-prompt confusion memory that records recurring overactivated non-target prompts. A sample-adaptive calibrator uses visual-text interaction patterns to suppress spurious alignment evidence, while a morphology evidence compensator adds pure visual features when language guidance is weak. Multi-scale logits from these components are fused for slide classification.

title: CONNECT-4: Brain Connectivity-Guided Hyperedge Graph Fusion for Structural MRI to 4D Rest Functional MRI Synthesis
motivation: rs-fMRI provides network-level biomarkers, but its long acquisition time, higher cost, and limited availability mean most patients receive only structural MRI, leaving a clinically important structural-functional gap. Predicting full 4D BOLD dynamics from sMRI is harder than conventional contrast translation because temporal physiology and network topology are only partially determined by anatomy. Existing attempts often ignore the temporal dimension or lose intricate connectivity, motivating a biologically constrained synthesis framework.
method: CONNECT-4 tokenizes T1-weighted sMRI and segmentation masks into aligned patches, encodes image, textual ROI descriptions, radiomics, and foundation-model features, and builds complementary image, mask, and ROI graphs. Connectivity-weighted hyperedges link patch nodes to covered ROI nodes, and graph attention with group-aware Nodes2Token fusion produces connectivity-aware tokens. Diffusion Transformer blocks and a temporal graph U-Net generate a 4D latent and final rs-fMRI volume, guided by losses aligning voxel signals, ROI connectivity, and global network properties.

title: ConnecToMind2: Inter-Subject fMRI Decoding via Whole-Brain Connectome-Guided Alignment
motivation: Although diffusion models have improved fMRI-to-image reconstruction, inter-subject neural variability makes transferable alignment difficult. Existing approaches mainly flatten visual-cortex voxel responses and discard the anatomical and functional organization of distributed whole-brain networks, while often requiring subject-specific adaptation. A decoder that preserves regional organization and models connectome-wide interactions is needed for robust inter-subject reconstruction.
method: ConnecToMind2 aligns fMRI activity to a shared anatomical space and represents it as region-level embeddings that preserve cortical organization. A Connectome-guided Q-Former uses structural connectivity priors in cross-attention to align these embeddings with CLIP image embeddings. The resulting structurally consistent brain representation supports image reconstruction across subjects without subject-specific adapters.

title: ConstTrack: Constellation-Guided Cell Tracking Under Lineage Constraints
motivation: Tracking cells in time-lapse microscopy requires maintaining identities and detecting divisions despite dense packing, non-rigid deformation, appearance drift, and temporary disappearances. Existing approaches rely mainly on per-cell appearance and position and model local neighborhood geometry only weakly, causing identity switches and lineage errors in ambiguous regions. Robust tracking therefore needs contextual geometry, trajectory memory, and biologically plausible lineage constraints.
method: ConstTrack uses a Deformable DETR detector and augments each detection with a constellation signature encoding relative displacements to neighboring cells. A Transformer identity decoder queries a track-pool memory containing active and recently missed tracks, while lineage attributes and a parent-ID head support delayed parent assignment under a temporal window. Halo-based spatial partitioning reduces memory use in dense scenes, with detections merged globally before identity prediction.

title: ContiStain: Cross-Domain Relation-Preserving Distillation for Continual Multi-domain Virtual IHC Staining
motivation: Unified multiplex virtual IHC staining must adapt as new biomarkers arrive over time, but sequential fine-tuning causes catastrophic forgetting of earlier domains. Because biomarkers share the same tissue architecture despite different staining patterns, adaptation can also collapse their latent cross-domain relationships and cause representation drift. Continual learning therefore needs to preserve these structural relations while accommodating new biomarkers.
method: ContiStain first uses a mixture-of-experts feature extractor with biomarker-specific experts and shared morphology-aligned components to create a domain-aware latent space. During sequential adaptation, relational distillation preserves token-level cosine-similarity matrices between previously learned and new biomarker domains. This maintains cross-domain structural coherence while allowing the model to learn incoming staining domains.

title: Contrast-Invariant Reference-Based Slice Thickness Estimation in MRI via Spectral Matching
motivation: In 2D MRI, slice thickness and slice spacing are independent, so assuming they are equal biases resolution estimates and downstream super-resolution. Estimating thickness from reconstructed images is ill-posed, and existing kernel methods may degenerate or require aligned images with matching contrast and subject. A contrast-invariant, correspondence-free estimator is needed to recover the slice selection profile explicitly.
method: PRISM rank-transforms both a low-resolution acquisition and a degraded high-resolution reference to reduce contrast dependence. It averages one-dimensional log power spectra along the slice axis and searches over candidate Gaussian slice profiles for the best spectral match. The exhaustive one-dimensional recovery requires neither registration nor voxel-wise correspondence and directly yields an interpretable thickness estimate.

title: Contrastive and Adaptive Multi-modal Masked Autoencoder for Spatial Transcriptomics

categories.value: Multimodal Integration with Clinical / Genomic / Biomarkers

motivation: Spatial transcriptomics is expensive and morphology alone cannot fully determine gene expression because transcriptomic changes may precede visible tissue changes. Using a small fraction of measured spots as anchors improves imputation, but random or non-adaptive sampling can select uninformative regions and fragmented points that do not match practical profiling hardware. An adaptive strategy must identify informative contiguous regions and integrate their genetic and visual information.
method: CAMMST defines a bio-saliency score for local transcriptional deviation and trains a sampler with learning-to-rank to select informative contiguous regions as genetic anchors. A cross-modal joint encoder contrastively aligns anchor gene expression with corresponding histology features. Within a masked-autoencoder formulation, these aligned representations and the visible anchors are used to impute whole-slide gene expression.

title: Contrastive Learning under Noisy Temporal Self-Supervision for Colonoscopy Videos
motivation: Robust polyp-tracklet representations support many colonoscopy applications, but supervised contrastive learning requires costly expert annotations linking detections to the same polyp. Temporal structure in a procedure offers a scalable self-supervisory signal, yet nearby observations can still belong to different polyps because of motion, viewpoint changes, occlusion, or sequential encounters. Learning must therefore tolerate noisy temporal associations without losing useful invariances.
method: The method derives positive and negative tracklet associations from the sequential structure of complete colonoscopy videos, using temporally close observations as likely views of the same polyp and progressively varying temporal distances during training. A lightweight encoder is trained with a noise-aware contrastive loss that down-weights potentially incorrect associations. The learned tracklet representations support retrieval, re-identification, size estimation, and histology classification.

title: Controllable Generation of Diverse Dermatological Imagery for Fair and Efficient Malignancy Classification

categories.value: AI for Neglected Diseases & Limited-Resource Settings

motivation: Dermatological AI lacks expertly annotated images for darker skin tones and rare diseases, and existing generative datasets may require large or private training sets, omit parts of the skin-tone spectrum, or lack single-sample augmentation. These gaps hinder equitable malignancy classification and make fairness difficult to measure. A controllable and data-efficient generation framework is needed to expand diverse, clinically relevant training data.
method: cgDDI combines latent-diffusion inpainting for realistic healthy skin synthesis with non-parametric lesion mapping that transfers a rare lesion to new skin tones and locations. For efficient parametric generation, textual inversion learns disease concepts and LoRA adapts the diffusion model, with prior-preservation loss anchored on healthy images. The framework accepts either human- or automatically generated lesion masks, enabling scalable dataset construction.

title: Controllable Histopathology Image Synthesis with Training-Free Structural Initialization and Textural Modulation
motivation: Histopathology models depend on large, high-quality expert annotations, motivating synthetic data to reduce annotation burden. Existing GAN and diffusion approaches may introduce artifacts, require paired annotation data, or incur costly unpaired translation, while standard Gaussian initialization can misalign generated structures. A training-free method is needed to provide structural control using unlabeled-image diffusion models.
method: CHIS is a training-free plug-in for a diffusion model pretrained only on unlabeled histopathology images. It initializes reverse sampling by combining the phase of a prior structural mask with the amplitude of Gaussian noise in the frequency domain, then adaptively modulates coarse and fine textures through wavelet components during denoising. This guides generated images toward the mask structure while retaining the reference tissue style.

title: ConVL: Interpretable Concept-Guided Vision-Language MIL for Survival Analysis in Whole Slide Images
motivation: Whole Slide Images contain prognostic information but are difficult to model because of their gigapixel scale, sparse fine-grained annotations, and substantial variation in tumour morphology. Existing MIL can identify informative regions but typically cannot explain which pathological concepts drive a prediction, while vision-language approaches with static prompts may not capture patient-specific morphological differences. A method that grounds survival predictions in adaptable pathological concepts is needed to improve interpretability and handle tissue heterogeneity.
method: ConVL couples visual MIL with a concept stream grounded in pathological concepts. Instance Conditioned Prompt Learning uses slide-level visual context to adapt concept prototypes to each patient, while Concept-Guided Cross Attention relates those concepts to image patches and Distribution Alignment Loss encourages agreement between the visual and concept-based predictions. Together, these components link survival estimates to localized pathological evidence while accounting for tissue heterogeneity.

title: CoRe-DA: Contrastive Regression for Unsupervised Domain Adaptation in Surgical Skill Assessment
motivation: Surgical skill assessment can provide objective, scalable performance evaluation, but producing quantitative labels requires substantial expert time. Existing regression models often generalize poorly across procedures and environments, while prior UDA work for this task has simplified assessment to binary classification or been limited to particular settings. Using available unlabeled surgical videos to adapt fine-grained regression is needed for deployment under realistic annotation budgets.
method: CoRe-DA adapts surgical skill regression from labeled source videos to unlabeled target videos using contrastive learning on pairs drawn from both domains. It trains with absolute and relative score regression on source data and regularizes the regression heads with a consistency constraint. Target-domain self-training with pseudo-labels further supports adaptation under domain shift, without requiring target labels.

title: CortexAdapt3D: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning of General 3D Foundation Models for Cortical Surface Analysis
motivation: Cortical surface analysis captures anatomical geometry relevant to parcellation and neurodevelopment, but current approaches rely on specialized architectures and limited datasets. Generic pretrained 3D models offer transferable geometric priors, yet the cortex's convoluted topology and informative attributes are not well handled by generic fine-tuning methods. An adaptation approach must respect intrinsic surface geometry while incorporating neuroanatomical signals beyond spatial coordinates.
method: CortexAdapt3D adapts pretrained generic 3D geometric representations to cortical surface tasks with parameter-efficient fine-tuning. It samples patches geodesically on the cortical icosahedral sphere and adds relative positional bias to represent intrinsic neighborhoods and fine-scale folding geometry. Its Attribute-aware Spectral Modulation Adapter uses attention in the spectral domain to fuse geometric priors with neuroanatomical attributes such as sulcal depth and curvature.

title: CoSim: Unleashing Eye Movements for EEG-Free Emotion Recognition via Conditional Prompting and Similarity-Guided Augmentation
motivation: EEG and eye movements provide complementary information for emotion recognition, but EEG acquisition is complex and limits practical use, while EYE alone tends to perform less well. Existing feature-generation and cross-modal alignment approaches can struggle to produce representations that are semantically aligned with the available modality and may overlook useful cross-subject information. A way to transfer EEG knowledge during training while relying only on accessible EYE signals at inference is needed.
method: CoSim transfers information from EEG, available only during training, to support emotion recognition from EYE signals at inference. It learns a shared representation from paired EEG-EYE data and augments training with samples from physiologically similar subjects. At test time, a Conditional Prompting Generator produces an EYE-conditioned discriminative representation, with a Fourier-Enhanced Transformer backbone designed to capture time-frequency patterns in physiological signals.

title: Counterfactual Anatomy-Guided Spatial-Temporal Decoding for Annotation-Free Hallucination Mitigation in Medical VLMs
motivation: Medical vision-language models can produce fluent answers that are not supported by image evidence, a serious concern for clinical interpretation. Existing decoding-time mitigation is often anatomy-agnostic, while region-guided methods may depend on costly, scarce, and dataset-specific ground-truth ROI annotations. An inference-time approach that automatically identifies compact, question-relevant anatomy is needed to ground answers without manual annotations.
method: CAST is an inference-time, annotation-free framework that automatically proposes anatomical regions with a medical segmentation model and selects a compact, query-relevant region by measuring the answer-likelihood drop under occlusion while discouraging oversized masks. It then applies unified spatial-temporal contrastive decoding: anatomy-guided classifier-free guidance steers generation toward regional evidence, while stepwise temporal contrast regulates the generated answer. This design provides region-based guidance without requiring expert ROI annotations.

title: Counterfactual Contrastive Analysis
motivation: Visual counterfactual explanations aim to show minimal, realistic image changes that alter a classifier's prediction. Classifier-dependent generation can reproduce model biases, such as reliance on shortcut features or calibration errors, rather than meaningful changes in the underlying data, and may offer limited insight into the semantic factors behind a flip. A classifier-free, distribution-based approach is needed to generate more model-agnostic and interpretable counterfactuals.
method: Counterfactual Contrastive Analysis generates visual counterfactuals from two class-specific datasets by separating shared generative factors from factors salient to each class, then swapping only the salient factors. It operates at the data-distribution level rather than optimizing against a classifier's decision boundary, and uses StyleGAN2 with its intermediate F-space to preserve image detail. The framework adapts the contrastive analysis setup and losses to support salient factors in both datasets.

title: Counterfactual Stress-Testing for Fixing Lung Cancer Segmentation Models
motivation: Accurate lung tumour segmentation on CT is important for radiotherapy planning, but strong average performance can hide failures on clinically relevant phenotypes, such as small lesions or indistinct boundaries. General robustness tests do not necessarily reveal which tumour attributes drive these failures. A controlled way to vary interpretable radiomic features while preserving each patient's context is needed to identify brittle regimes and guide model improvement.
method: The framework learns a conditional 3D tumour generator that creates identity-preserving counterfactual CT crops and pseudo-label masks by intervening on selected radiomic parent features. Sweeping each feature across empirical quantiles yields Counterfactual Robustness Curves that identify feature regimes where a segmentation model falls below a chosen performance threshold. These hard regimes guide selection of counterfactuals for targeted fine-tuning.

title: CPAgents: Agentic Composite Phenotype Generation for Cardiac Disease Association
motivation: Population-scale cardiac imaging cohorts provide many quantitative phenotypes for disease association analysis, but their number, redundancy, and dependencies make candidate selection difficult. Existing PheWAS workflows often rely on expert-defined single variables or manually crafted composites, limiting discovery of non-linear effects and interactions; broad automated search can also yield unstable findings under multiple testing, cohort heterogeneity, or residual confounding. A scalable approach is needed to discover interpretable composites while constraining and validating the search.
method: CPAgents discovers composite cardiac imaging phenotypes through an iterative loop coordinated by Analyst, Proposer, and Verifier agents. The Analyst identifies statistical patterns and candidate transformations; the Proposer constructs constrained formulas, such as polynomial, ratio, or interaction features, under medical, statistical, and numerical-safety rules; and the Verifier screens and validates candidates using multi-stage criteria. Cross-validation, model comparisons, and statistical checks provide evidence trails for retained phenotypes.

title: CPR: Chained Perceptual Refinement for Coarse-to-Fine Medical Image Classification
motivation: High-resolution medical images contain small, fine-grained diagnostic cues, but processing them at full resolution is costly in memory and computation, while downsampling can erase useful detail. Fixed-resolution and multi-scale approaches typically allocate computation uniformly or according to a predefined schedule, rather than selecting informative regions in response to the image. A sequential method is needed to combine global context with adaptive high-resolution inspection efficiently.
method: CPR treats image classification as a sequential coarse-to-fine process. A shared encoder first processes a low-resolution global view; a policy network then predicts the location and scale of a region to extract from the original high-resolution image, and a perceptual state incrementally fuses each observation with accumulated context for subsequent decisions and prediction. Keeping the encoder input size fixed while refining the field of view enables adaptive localization without increasing peak memory through higher-resolution inputs.

title: CPS4: Class Prompt Driven Semi-supervised Spine Segmentation with Class-Specific Consistency Constraint
motivation: Multi-class segmentation of vertebral bodies and intervertebral discs in spine MR images supports diagnosis and treatment planning, but pixel-level annotation is laborious and requires expertise. Semi-supervised methods can use unlabeled images, yet noisy pseudo-labels can mislead training. Although vision-language models could provide class-prompt-guided maps, they lack explicit constraints tying each prompt to its corresponding spine unit, risking class interference and poor pseudo-labels.
method: CPS4 uses a two-stage training design to bring class-prompt information into semi-supervised spine segmentation. First, it pretrains a vision-language model with token- and pixel-level attention losses that align each class prompt with its corresponding spine unit. Then, the pretrained encoders generate class-specific binary maps for unlabeled images, which are combined into a multi-class map to improve the pseudo-labels used by the segmentation network.

title: CRIMSON: A Clinically-Grounded LLM-Based Metric for Generative Radiology Report Evaluation
motivation: Automated radiology report generation has advanced, but existing evaluation metrics often treat errors uniformly or use coarse significance categories. They also assess findings without sufficient patient context, conflating benign discrepancies with omissions that could affect patient safety. A clinically grounded metric is needed to reflect radiologists' severity-aware judgments.
method: CRIMSON evaluates a candidate report against a reference at the individual-finding level in three stages: extracting abnormal findings and assigning context-dependent clinical significance, classifying discrepancies, and computing a severity-aware normalized score. It uses a taxonomy of false, missing, and eight attribute-level errors, with partial credit and separate weights for clinically significant versus negligible attributes. Patient age and indication guide four-level significance weighting, while normal findings are excluded to avoid stylistic score inflation.

title: Cross-Cancer Expert-Routing Knowledge Transfer in Federated Prognosis Prediction
motivation: WSI-based prognosis prediction is difficult to generalize to rare cancers because target cohorts are small and weakly supervised MIL depends on strong initial representations. Sharing knowledge across cancers through a single global model can also cause negative transfer because prognostic features differ substantially between cancer types. A method is needed to transfer useful cross-cancer priors while preserving cancer-specific information.
method: FedERF has two phases. Federated LoRA training across source cancer clients builds a shared backbone and retains cancer-specific low-rank experts that capture distinct prognostic knowledge. During target adaptation, a layer-wise dynamic routing policy selectively aggregates relevant experts while fine-tuning on the target cancer, limiting conflicting transfer without sharing raw WSIs.

title: Cross-channel Consistent Mamba for Extreme Limited-View Photoacoustic Tomography Reconstruction
motivation: Extreme limited-view PAT loses acoustic information, producing strong artifacts, discontinuous structures, blurred boundaries, and missing fine detail. Existing methods often target milder view loss and assume fixed, reliable multi-channel inputs, so they are less robust when channels are missing or acquisition configurations change. Reconstruction therefore needs to preserve weak channel cues while focusing learning on structurally important regions.
method: S²-Mamba separates each acquisition channel into a shared single-channel branch and fuses features through scale-wise averaging, preserving weak cues while accommodating missing or changing channels. A Cross-Channel Consistency Loss aligns latent distributions across channels and applies a uniform-prior constraint to reduce representation collapse. An Adaptive Gradient-Gated Loss progressively emphasizes structurally difficult regions through hard mining and uncertainty-based weighting of amplitude and structural objectives.

title: Cross-domain Controllable Generation Enables Zero-shot Fundus Image Analysis
motivation: Ophthalmic vessel segmentation, registration, and bifurcation detection require extensive annotations across modalities and diseases, making manual labeling costly. Existing label-efficient generation methods either rely on target-domain image-label pairs or trade controllability against realistic appearance, while labels borrowed from another modality may not match target vessel patterns. A unified approach is needed to generate modality-dependent labels and realistic, structurally consistent images for zero-shot analysis.
method: UniVessel first uses vascular-dynamics simulation to generate modality-specific vessel masks and bifurcation coordinates with target field-of-view and density characteristics. Its image-generation component uses two diffusion models that decouple mask-controlled structure generation from modality-specific style synthesis, with phase maps as the intermediate bridge. The resulting paired labels and images provide supervision for zero-shot segmentation, registration, and bifurcation detection without target-domain image-label pairs.

title: Cross-Modal Alignment and Distillation for Retinal Imaging Dementia Screening
motivation: MRI, PET, CSF, and cognitive questionnaires are costly, inaccessible, invasive, or subjective for large-scale dementia screening. Retinal OCTA is non-invasive and linked biologically to brain pathology, but eye-only models usually map peripheral morphology directly to labels without explicit cerebral context, limiting sensitivity and interpretability. A framework is needed to transfer brain structural information into a standalone retinal screening model.
method: EyeDEM trains paired OCTA and MRI networks to learn eye-brain pathological associations, disentangling shared neurodegenerative semantics from modality-specific characteristics. A multi-level alignment module maps retinal representations to brain structural priors, and divide-and-conquer distillation transfers hierarchical diagnostic knowledge from a fused multimodal teacher to the retinal student. At inference, the student performs dementia screening using retinal images alone and can predict related brain atrophy volumes.

title: Cross-Modal Concept Transfer: From ECG Signals to Images for Explainable Disease Prediction
motivation: ECG data are often stored as report images while raw waveforms are not consistently retained, constraining deployment of signal-dependent models. Image models provide useful visual representations but struggle to capture quantitative waveform measurements, and common explanations are qualitative attention maps rather than clinically referenced values. A practical method should combine image availability with signal-derived, quantitatively interpretable concepts.
method: CMCT extends the Concept Bottleneck Model to cross-modal ECG learning by using signal-derived physiological measurements as intermediate concept labels. Image and signal encoders are trained so that image representations reflect these quantitative concepts, and the final disease prediction uses only the concept values. Because concepts can be obtained from images, signals, or stored measurements, inference and explanations remain modality-agnostic and quantitatively interpretable.

title: Cross-Modal Contrastive Learning of ECG and Angiography Representations for Severe Stenosis Classification
motivation: Severe coronary stenosis is usually diagnosed with invasive, resource-intensive X-ray angiography, which is generally reserved for patients already suspected of disease and can miss asymptomatic cases. ECG is inexpensive, non-invasive, and routinely acquired, but no reliable stenosis-specific signal has been established and severe stenosis may produce normal ECGs. A way to transfer angiographic stenosis information into ECG representations could enable earlier risk detection.
method: StenCE trains a transformer ECG encoder with multi-modal contrastive learning against a frozen, multi-view angiography encoder that is trained for coronary stenosis classification. The ECG representation is thereby aligned with stenosis-relevant angiographic features, after which the ECG model is fine-tuned for stenosis and other cardiac classification tasks. Inference uses ECG inputs alone, enabling non-invasive risk stratification.

title: Cross-Modal Prediction of DNA Methylation from Histology Images

categories.value: Multimodal Integration with Clinical / Genomic / Biomarkers

motivation: DNA methylation is clinically valuable for glioma classification and prognosis, but molecular profiling is costly, time-consuming, and difficult to access routinely. Existing histology-based predictors have mainly used MLP or conventional models and do not explicitly represent spatial relationships between tissue regions or establish whether inferred profiles capture clinically relevant phenotypes. A scalable image-based method should model WSI architecture while predicting continuous methylation signals with downstream clinical relevance.
method: GraphCpG converts each WSI into a spatial graph of tissue patches, using frozen CTransPath features as nodes and Delaunay-triangulated neighborhoods as edges. A multi-output Transformer Convolution GNN performs attention-weighted spatial aggregation and predicts continuous beta values for 10,000 CpG sites at both patch and slide levels, combining predictions across layers. The inferred methylation profiles are then used for survival stratification and mitotic and immune subtype prediction.

title: Cross-Surface Representation Learning for Accurate Gingiva Prediction in CBCT
motivation: Accurate gingival-margin delineation is important for periodontal assessment, but CBCT has low soft-tissue contrast and tissue adhesion makes the margin nearly indistinguishable from mucosa, cheeks, and tongue. IOS can provide surface contours but lacks internal periodontal structures and requires error-prone registration with CBCT, while voxel segmentation does not enforce the tooth-surface boundary. The task needs both an acquisition strategy that exposes the margin and a geometry-constrained representation for precise localization.
method: The work co-designs acquisition and modeling. A chair-side mouth retractor and impression tray isolate gingiva from adjacent mucosa, creating a continuous air interface that makes the margin visible in CBCT. Teeth are reconstructed as meshes and used as geometric priors; CSR samples radiodensity along vertex normals, while a band-aware Gaussian regression module predicts a continuous, topologically consistent gingival confidence field.

title: CrownFusion: 3D Dental Crown Generation Using Geometry Images and Latent Diffusion
motivation: Dental crown design must adapt to individual morphology and occlusion, yet remains labor-intensive and can have multiple clinically acceptable solutions. Point-cloud methods often require artifact-prone mesh reconstruction and smooth away high-curvature occlusal details, while single-view depth representations discard parts of the 3D anatomy relevant to contact. A generative representation should preserve complete surface geometry, support varied valid designs, and evaluate functional occlusal fit.
method: CrownFusion represents a crown surface as a high-resolution CrownImage, a 2D grid whose entries store 3D surface coordinates, preserving full geometry and fine occlusal details. A conditional latent diffusion model combining a SiT transformer and FLUX VAE generates CrownImages while cross-attending to embeddings of the surrounding dentition. Multiple candidates can be produced for a case, and an antagonist-proximity occlusal-fit metric evaluates functional alignment beyond Chamfer distance.

title: CSAM-HQ: A Multi-stage Refinement Framework for Surgical Instrument Segmentation based on SAM and Probabilistic Graphical Models
motivation: Accurate surgical instrument segmentation supports navigation, decision-making, simulation, and robotic control in minimally invasive surgery. Existing foundation-model adaptations can localize instruments but often produce ambiguous boundaries, fragmented masks, and inter-class false positives, especially for thin structures, because high-frequency geometry and structural consistency are lost.
method: CSAM-HQ uses a three-stage coarse-to-fine framework with a SAM image encoder and prototype-based class prompts for semantic localization. A learnable, prototype-conditioned HQ-Token and residual HQ branch recover high-frequency boundaries, while an IoU-aware calibration head suppresses ambiguous masks. A fully connected CRF then enforces pixel-level spatial and appearance consistency to reduce fragmentation and preserve thin instrument topology.

title: CSGE: Break the SSL Bottleneck in Medical Image Segmentation via Collaborative Semantic-Geometric Experts
motivation: Semi-supervised medical image segmentation is needed because dense annotations are costly, yet conventional teacher-student methods are limited by semantic-geometric misalignment, confirmation bias, and hard-threshold information loss. High-confidence interior predictions can coexist with poor boundaries, while erroneous teacher labels are recursively reinforced and uncertain edge pixels are discarded.
method: CSGE retains a teacher-student framework but replaces passive confidence filtering with collaborative semantic-geometric refinement. BiomedCLIP supplies category-level semantic anchoring, while SAM uses teacher-derived prompts and conflict-aware iterative resampling to refine boundaries. A spatial trust-aware soft weighting map preserves gradients in uncertain regions and combines global consistency with local boundary supervision.

title: CSWinUNETR: Segmentation of Thin Anatomical Structures in Medical Images
motivation: Thin anatomical structures such as retinal vessels and cerebrovascular branches occupy few pixels, have low contrast and interruptions, and follow tortuous anisotropic paths. Standard segmentation networks therefore produce fragmented masks or miss fine branches, while existing attention and dynamic convolution designs do not jointly provide robust long-range orientation reasoning and stable trajectory-aligned local aggregation across 2D and 3D data.
method: CSWinUNETR is a 2D/3D backbone that combines shifted cross-shaped stripe self-attention with detail-enhanced multi-scale self-attention. The stripe attention propagates long-range, orientation-aware context, while multi-resolution aggregation preserves subtle structures. Sparse-control dynamic snake convolution constructs dense curvilinear kernels from reliable control points, providing more stable trajectory-aligned local features than stepwise offset tracking.

title: CT2-DiT: Enabling Abdominal Non-contrast to Contrast-Enhanced CT Translation with Diffusion Transformers in the Low-Data Regime
motivation: CECT is important for characterizing focal liver lesions, but iodinated contrast agents, repeated radiation, and associated risks motivate synthesizing CECT from non-contrast CT. Although DiT can model global anatomical structure, it is data-hungry and paired NCCT-CECT data are scarce, making direct medical deployment prone to overfitting.
method: CT2-DiT applies a pure Diffusion Transformer to NCCT-to-CECT translation. It pre-trains the backbone to reconstruct images from public unlabeled CT data, injects manually synthesized CT-specific features, and uses spatial-intensity decoupled augmentation to improve generalization from scarce paired slices. Deep supervision is added to stabilize and improve data-efficient fine-tuning for conditional translation.

title: CT-Conditioned Diffusion Prior with Physics-Constrained Sampling for PET Super-Resolution
motivation: PET super-resolution is ill-posed because blur and noise depend on scanner physics, including PSF, detector geometry, and acquisition settings, while paired multi-resolution scans are rarely available. Purely supervised or image-domain generative restoration can over-smooth details or hallucinate structures and lacks guarantees that the output remains consistent with the measured PET data.
method: The method learns a CT-conditioned diffusion prior from high-quality PET/CT pairs using cross-attention for anatomical guidance, without requiring paired low- and high-resolution PET scans. During inference, a scanner-aware forward model explicitly includes PSF effects, and gradient-based measurement-domain data-consistency updates refine the iterative denoising samples. Progressive physics-constrained refinement activates these constraints late and moves from coarse to fine PSF modeling.

title: CTTok: Voxel-Abulary for Autoregressive 3D CT Volume Generation with Large Language Models
motivation: Text-conditioned 3D CT generation could provide privacy-preserving data augmentation and controllable simulation of rare pathology, but diffusion and flow methods require costly iterative sampling and may weakly align anatomy with text. Existing learned latent codebooks also couple neighboring regions through a decoder, limiting direct spatial correspondence between language and anatomy.
method: CTTok builds a frozen anatomical Voxel-abulary of 16×16×16 CT patches using random-hyperplane hashing in a pretrained vision-feature space. A fine-tuned Qwen-1.7B autoregressively predicts vision-token sequences interleaved with text, relying on causal attention rather than dedicated cross-attention. A single-pass 2.5D GAN removes residual patch-boundary artifacts without access to the original prompt.

title: Cubic Structure-Aware Neural Radiance Fields for Zero-Shot Super-Resolution of Susceptibility-Weighted Imaging
motivation: Routine SWI uses thick slices to keep scan times clinically acceptable, creating severe through-plane anisotropy that can obscure small cerebral microbleeds and break microvascular continuity. General SR methods may blur or distort SWI-specific susceptibility structures, while supervised approaches require paired HR scans that are difficult to acquire and are vulnerable to scanner-domain shifts.
method: CSANeRF performs zero-shot SWI super-resolution using only each patient’s LR volume as supervision. It replaces point-wise NeRF MLP modeling with cube-based spatial queries and a Cubeformer that applies structure-aware multi-head self-attention to local 3D neighborhoods. These explicit neighborhood priors are designed to preserve susceptibility-related structures and CMB continuity during continuous volume reconstruction.

title: CURA: Calibrated Uncertainty with Retrieval and Agents for Trustworthy Multimodal Medical Decision Support
motivation: Medical LLMs can behave as overconfident single-answer oracles, where errors may mislead triage while correct but underconfident answers trigger unnecessary testing. Retrieval, multi-agent deliberation, and uncertainty methods have largely been studied separately, leaving no unified mechanism that provides calibrated confidence together with abstention, set-valued predictions, and cost-aware escalation.
method: CURA grounds responses through a bidirectional LLM-knowledge-graph retrieval pipeline with probabilistic graph exploration and consults a heterogeneous clinical council. It fuses expert opinions with Bayesian belief aggregation to expose one calibrated posterior. Selective abstention, split conformal prediction sets, and an uncertainty-driven commit/continue policy turn this posterior into risk-, coverage-, and cost-aware actions.

title: Curia-2: Scaling Self-Supervised Learning for Radiology Foundation Models
motivation: Radiology foundation models need broad representations from large unlabeled CT and MRI collections, but natural-image self-supervised strategies do not fully account for radiological data characteristics. Although the original Curia demonstrated the value of scale, its training efficiency and the lack of a unified 2D/3D evaluation structure limited further scaling and comparison.
method: Curia-2 refines DINOv2-style self-supervised pre-training with radiology-specific data augmentations and objective functions. The resulting Curia-2 family scales from 86M to 1.3B parameters and supports multimodal CT and MRI representation learning. CuriaBench is reorganized into separate 2D slice-based and 3D volumetric tracks to evaluate slice and volume foundation models consistently.

title: Cut, Stitch, Adapt: Data-Efficient and Low-Calibration Speech BCIs
motivation: Speech iBCIs must cope with scarce labeled neural recordings and biological or mechanical drift that changes neural representations across days. Large cross-species pretraining and ensembles are costly, while day-specific normalization and calibration do not generalize reliably to future sessions. A practical system therefore needs data-efficient augmentation and explicit session-invariant adaptation.
method: Neural Cut-and-Stitch (NCS) uses forced phoneme alignments to isolate word-level neural segments, samples segments from a word dictionary to form new sentences, and applies normalization and crossfading for smooth reconstruction. An Adversarial Domain Adaptation Network (ADAN) aligns feature distributions across recording sessions to encourage a session-invariant neural manifold. The pipeline is designed around a lightweight recurrent decoder and reduced calibration requirements.

title: CW-B: Class Weighted Boosting Framework for Imbalance Resilient Multi Class Cardiac Phenotyping
motivation: Automated assignment of hospital discharge cardiac phenotypes supports risk stratification, treatment selection, follow-up, and referrals, but missed acute high-risk phenotypes can cause disproportionate clinical harm. Real-world records are heterogeneous and incomplete, while conventional models under skewed class distributions tend to favor prevalent classes and offer limited auditability. A practical method is therefore needed to model asymmetric clinical risk while remaining robust to missing data and interpretable for deployment.
method: CW-B is a class-weighted XGBoost pipeline for five-class cardiac discharge phenotyping. It uses fold-specific, clinically motivated instance weights to control the trade-off between overall discrimination and high-risk false negatives, together with leakage-free missingness-aware feature construction. The tree-based design retains efficient, interpretable split structures for auditing decisions and classwise errors.

title: Cycle-Verified Gentle Teaching and Confusion Correction for Label-Scarce Cross-Modal Single-Cell Annotation

categories.value: Multimodal Integration with Clinical / Genomic / Biomarkers

motivation: Annotating scATAC-seq cells from scRNA-seq references is difficult because the target modality is sparse, high-dimensional, and shifted, while labels are often extremely scarce. Under regimes with roughly one percent labeled source cells, early pseudo-label errors and noisy target supervision accumulate, collapsing boundaries between closely related cell states. A transfer method must therefore control supervision reliability and correct systematic confusions without requiring paired multi-omic measurements.
method: CADENCE is a semi-supervised cross-modality transfer framework that separates source-like target cells from ambiguous target-specific cells. It expands source supervision with curriculum optimal-transport pseudo-labeling and class-balanced selection, while a gentle teacher-assistant-student architecture confines noisy target supervision to an assistant and transfers robust representations to the student with EMA updates. A cycle-consistent bidirectional latent translator supplies reliability scores for gating and reweighting ambiguous cells, and prototype geometry dynamically corrects confusing class pairs and their soft labels.

title: D2C: Data-Efficient Skin Lesion Classification for Clinical Images by Representation Alignment Using Dermoscopic Resources
motivation: Skin-lesion diagnosis from ordinary clinical photographs is clinically accessible but hampered by lower image quality and greater imaging variability than dermoscopy. Existing deep-learning resources and datasets are concentrated in dermoscopic images, so clinical images often lack sufficient labels and diagnostic features. A data-efficient adaptation strategy is needed to transfer dermoscopic knowledge while accounting for cross-domain representation and pixel-level variation.
method: D2C formulates clinical-image skin-lesion classification as semi-supervised domain adaptation from abundant labeled dermoscopic images to sparsely labeled and largely unlabeled clinical images. It first trains on dermoscopy and builds class-aware dermoscopic feature vaults, then adapts the classifier using cluster-level and instance-level representation alignment with information retrieved from those vaults. The vaults provide broader diagnostic coverage than batch-only features and help address both feature-space and domain-specific imaging variation.

title: Data-Driven Optimization of Prostate Sectorization from MRI
motivation: PI-RADS sectors provide the clinical language for prostate lesion location and biopsy reporting, but their mapping to 3D MRI coordinates is not standardized. Rigid scripts use non-differentiable geometric assumptions and may omit anatomical partitions, whereas flexible methods can violate PI-RADS topology; consequently, sector-indexed biopsy records remain weakly spatially labeled and difficult to exploit. A differentiable, anatomically adaptable, and clinically compliant mapping is needed to turn these records into usable volumetric supervision.
method: The framework learns a global prostate sectorization template in a canonical coordinate system from lesion masks and expert sector labels. Learnable planes, longitudinal thresholds, and posterior lateral-central rays define a 24-sector map, while patient-specific zonal masks and soft sigmoid indicators preserve PI-RADS topology and enable gradient optimization. A latent-consensus objective maximizes lesion coverage and penalizes cross-sector spillover, producing an interpretable differentiable mapping that can also quantify sector-assignment adequacy.

title: DBT-Bleed: Dual-Branch Temporal Modeling with Key-Frame Selection for Surgical Bleeding Detection
motivation: Timely detection of intraoperative bleeding adverse events is important for surgical safety, but visible residual blood can look similar to unintended bleeding and requires temporal context to distinguish them. Existing methods often use frame-wise or short-clip processing and therefore struggle with multi-scale progression and long-video computation. The field also lacks broadly available IAE-annotated data, limiting development and cross-procedure evaluation.
method: DBT-Bleed uses a dual-branch representation to disentangle bleeding-IAE patterns from normal or residual-blood representations.
