Layer-wise multi-scale temporal adapters model short- and long-term bleeding progression, while HiRED hierarchically selects high-entropy, temporally informative frames and removes redundant segments from long videos. The framework is evaluated for cross-procedure transfer and is accompanied by the EndoPit-IAE neurosurgical IAE dataset.

title: DCLDs-RAG: Evidence-Grounded Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Diffuse Cystic Lung Diseases Diagnosis

categories.value: AI for Neglected Diseases & Limited-Resource Settings

motivation: DCLDs are rare diseases with subtle visual differences across classes, while limited clinical samples make conventional supervised deep models difficult to generalize. MLLMs can support low-resource diagnosis but lack specialized knowledge and reliable multimodal references, increasing hallucination risk; generic text retrieval often returns noisy, weakly grounded information. A retrieval framework must provide discriminative imaging evidence and structured clinical knowledge to support reliable reasoning.
method: DCLDs-RAG builds a disease-specific multimodal corpus of CT slices and expert-refined descriptions together with a structured DCLDs knowledge graph. A visual retriever learns angular-margin-aware embeddings to retrieve discriminative imaging evidence despite fine-grained inter-class overlap. A knowledge-clinical retriever extracts disease entities and relations as structured evidence, and an MLLM combines both evidence types with the query to produce the diagnosis and rationale.

title: DDecomp: Structured Uncertainty Decomposition Using Masked Autoencoders for Anomaly Detection in Diffusion MRI
motivation: Unsupervised anomaly detection in diffusion MRI could localize lesions without costly voxel-level labels, but acquisition noise, scanner differences, and protocol shifts can obscure subtle pathology. Masked-autoencoder reconstruction errors and conventional uncertainty estimates mix data noise with model mismatch, so high scores are not necessarily lesion-specific. A method is needed to isolate pathology-sensitive uncertainty and remain stable across heterogeneous protocols and lesion types.
method: DDecomp trains a masked autoencoder with heteroscedastic uncertainty modeling on healthy diffusion MRI data. During inference it jointly marginalizes stochastic mask patterns and dropout predictions to decompose uncertainty into aleatoric and epistemic components. The epistemic map, interpreted as model mismatch to out-of-distribution tissue, is used as the anomaly cue, improving lesion specificity under acquisition noise and protocol shifts within one model.

title: DD-INR: Dynamics-Driven Implicit Neural Representation for Accelerated Whole-Brain Functional MRI Reconstruction
motivation: Accelerated whole-brain fMRI requires strong k-space undersampling, making reconstruction ill-posed, while task-evoked BOLD changes are only a small fraction of the anatomical signal. Methods designed for anatomical accuracy or macroscopic motion can spend capacity on static structure, lose temporal fidelity, or hallucinate functional features; volumetric supervised training is also data- and memory-intensive. Reconstruction therefore needs a compact prior focused specifically on subtle, coherent dynamics.
method: DD-INR factorizes each accelerated fMRI sequence into a static anatomical background and a time-varying dynamic component. The background is reconstructed from samples pooled across time, while a subject-specific SIREN INR with separate spatial and temporal Fourier features represents only the dynamic signal. Spatial total-variation regularization, including a penalty on the temporal derivative, imposes coherent activation-related changes while the model is optimized directly against multi-coil k-space data.

title: DEC-Net: A Multi-Task Distillation Expert Collaboration Network for Glioma Grading and Molecular Subtyping Using Multimodal MRI
motivation: Non-invasive glioma grading and molecular subtyping from MRI could reduce reliance on invasive sampling, which is costly and vulnerable to heterogeneity-related sampling bias. Existing approaches often require accurate tumor segmentation and treat grading and molecular subtype prediction independently, overlooking shared biology and allowing task interference. A unified model must learn discriminative tumor regions, separate shared from task-specific information, and exploit dependencies between the outputs.
method: DEC-Net combines multimodal MRI with a Distillation ResModule whose anomaly-detection-guided teacher directs a ResNet student toward discriminative tumor-relevant regions. A Progressive Mixture-of-Experts module uses routing to hierarchically balance shared and task-specific experts, reducing interference between grading and molecular-subtyping tasks. A dependency loss explicitly models their biological correlation to encourage consistent joint predictions.

title: Decoding the Alzheimer’s Continuum: Interpretable Multi-gate Routing for Diagnosis and Transition Prediction
motivation: Alzheimer’s disease progresses continuously from normal cognition through MCI to dementia, but most deep models reduce it to separate static classification tasks and ignore stage transitions. Independent one-versus-one classifiers can produce conflicting probabilities and do not represent mutually exclusive clinical stages, while demographic and brain-volume priors are rarely integrated systematically. A unified, interpretable model is needed to jointly diagnose the current stage and estimate progression-related transitions from sMRI.
method: M3AD is a unified multi-task architecture built on enhanced Swin V2 with multi-gate mixture-of-experts blocks for diagnosis-stage classification and transition prediction. Specialized experts capture diagnosis-specific pathology while shared experts model common structural features, and adaptive attention fuses age, sex, and eTIV with image features. SimMIM pretraining initializes expert specialization, while the dual-gate routing provides interpretable activation signatures for stable versus progressive trajectories.

title: Decouple and Reason: Anatomically Guided Two-Stage Grounding of Lung Lesions in 3D Chest CT from Free-Text Reports

categories.value: Multimodal Integration with Clinical / Genomic / Biomarkers

motivation: Voxel-level grounding of lung lesions from free-text reports in 3D chest CT is needed for interpretable clinical analysis and CAD. Large volumetric spatial complexity and heterogeneous, descriptive findings make it difficult for one end-to-end model to learn precise localization and cross-modal reasoning simultaneously, so subtle lesions or their textual correspondences are often missed.
method: The DAGG framework decouples grounding into class-agnostic lesion segmentation followed by text-volume reasoning on candidate sub-volumes. The reasoning stage adds relative coordinates and lung-lobe priors for anatomical disambiguation, and uses independent pairwise alignment to avoid false-negative penalties from semantically overlapping reports and unlabeled false-positive candidates.

title: Decoupled Ordinal Refinement with Geometric Alignment for Chest X-ray Severity Scoring
motivation: Automated multi-region Brixia severity scoring on chest X-rays must handle extreme regional class imbalance, ordinal grades, and inter-rater subjectivity. The authors identify an interaction of Neural Collapse and Minority Collapse that collapses ordinal geometry and biases inter-ROI representations toward majority grades, rather than treating the problem as data scarcity alone.
method: DORGA constructs an Ordinal-Aligned Latent Space with learnable hyperspherical anchors fixed by polar and ordinal-separation constraints. It orthogonally separates each ROI embedding into severity and anatomical-structure components, then uses pattern-conditional Bayesian message passing with confidence-gated spherical interpolation to refine ambiguous severity embeddings while structure-aware attention selects inter-ROI neighbors.

title: Decoupled Single-Mask Annotation Noise Detection via Cross-Sectional Patch Self-consistency
motivation: Vascular CT datasets commonly contain only one segmentation mask per scan, yet thin, branching anatomy and contrast variation make localized annotation errors common. Multi-rater fusion is unavailable and training-coupled robust methods cannot explicitly show where or why a label is unreliable, creating a need for decoupled, auditable noise localization.
method: The method samples orthogonal cross-sectional patches along vessel centrelines using stable Bishop frames and retrieves intensity-similar neighbours across the dataset with scalable vector search. It estimates the conditional distribution of mask disagreement given image similarity, assigns residual-based pair scores, aggregates them into patch noise scores, and propagates these scores into scan-level quality maps for auditing or quality-weighted training.

title: Deep EM with Hierarchical Latent Label Modelling for Multi-Site Prostate Lesion Segmentation
motivation: Prostate lesion contours in multi-site mpMRI reflect institution-specific protocols and reader styles, so networks can overfit local labels and generalize poorly to unseen sites. Because each case often has only one biased annotation, test-site fine-tuning or multi-rater fusion is impractical and can reinforce the very labeling bias that limits deployment.
method: HierEM alternates an E-step that infers voxel-wise posteriors for a latent clean lesion mask with an M-step that trains a UNet using the posterior as a soft target. It jointly estimates site- and case-dependent sensitivity and specificity under logistic-normal hierarchical priors, decomposing global, site, and case effects to regularize annotation variation and learn site-invariant representations.

title: Deep Probabilistic Cerebrovascular Atlas
motivation: A high-fidelity population cerebrovascular atlas is needed to study vascular variation, aging, and pathology, but voxel and mesh representations discretize continuous vessels and can wash out fine structures or fail on variable topology. Standard coordinate-based networks also struggle to represent the full multi-scale tree because one parameter set must model both low-frequency major arteries and high-frequency distal branches.
method: VITAL represents cerebrovascular anatomy as a continuous implicit neural atlas conditioned on subject latent codes. A dynamically routed Mixture-of-Experts architecture separates scale-specific features, allowing the model to capture both major-artery geometry and distal-branch detail while supporting probabilistic demographic conditioning and anomaly-reference generation.

title: Deep-IMMA: an Interpretable Immune-Aware Multimodal Deep Representation Learning for Cancer Prognosis and Recurrence Prediction
motivation: Prognosis and biochemical recurrence prediction from histopathology needs to capture the spatial organization and interactions of tumor, stromal, and immune populations. Existing morphology-focused or loosely supervised vision-language models rarely encode this tumor–immune topology explicitly, limiting biological interpretability and risk discrimination without costly genomic or imaging inputs.
method: Deep-IMMA uses two stages: tile embeddings are first trained with joint supervision from structured captions, spatial cell-type maps, segmentation, cell abundance, immune phenotypes, and cross-modal consistency, then aggregated by spatially aware multiple-instance learning for recurrence prediction. The learned representations preserve neighborhood and immune topology while inference requires only histology images, and the framework produces textual and spatial risk explanations.

title: DEER: A Foundation Model with Dual-Branch CT-Enhanced Embeddings for Thoracoabdominal Radiographs

categories.value: AI for Neglected Diseases & Limited-Resource Settings
AI for Population Health, Public Health & Epidemiology

motivation: DR is central to screening but existing foundation-model research is heavily chest-focused, underrepresents abdominal disease, and image-only or weak labels do not capture the semantics in radiology reports. Because 2D DR offers limited disease information compared with 3D CT, CT localizers provide a potential bridge for transferring richer CT knowledge into generalizable DR representations.
method: DEER performs dual-branch contrastive multimodal pretraining that jointly uses DR images, CT localizers, and their radiology reports. CT-localizer and report information supplies richer disease semantics to thoracoabdominal DR representations, producing a unified foundation model trained on large-scale image-report pairs for downstream interpretation.

title: Defining Robust Ultrasound Quality Metrics via an Ultrasound Foundation Model
motivation: Ultrasound reconstruction quality is clinically important but common metrics such as PSNR, SSIM, and natural-image perceptual scores do not model speckle, shadowing, anisotropic sampling, or localized boundary-destroying artifacts. Existing no-reference methods are often tied to specific organs or protocols, motivating modality-aligned full- and no-reference metrics that relate image quality to task damage and clinician utility.
method: TinyUSFM-uLPIPS compares local token-relational and channel co-activation statistics across multiple TinyUSFM layers for full-reference perceptual distance. TinyUSFM-NRQ encodes overlapping patches, models organ-aware clean feature manifolds with Gaussian mixtures, and averages the worst-scoring regions for no-reference quality; the same token space is also used as a perceptual loss for super-resolution.

title: DeformTTA: Morphology-Aware Controllable Deformation for Test-Time Adaptation in Fetal Cardiac Ultrasound Image Segmentation
motivation: Fetal cardiac segmentation degrades across scanners, operators, and physiological states, while rapid motion and pathological deformation make target-domain anatomy especially difficult. Generic TTA based on entropy or consistency lacks explicit anatomical constraints and can follow noisy, low-contrast ultrasound textures, producing biologically implausible masks.
method: DeformTTA first predicts a target-domain mask, applies gated displacement fields to Gaussian-smoothed mask representations to simulate physiological cardiac motion, and uses a ControlNet-based generator to synthesize corresponding target-style images. Test-time optimization enforces consistency across motion-conditioned image-mask pairs while a Boundary Regularity shape prior monitors and preserves plausible morphology.

title: DeGenseGS: Geometrically and Semantically Decoupled Surgical Scene Understanding in 4D Gaussian Splatting
motivation: Autonomous surgical interaction requires 4D reconstructions that are both geometrically accurate and text-promptable, but dynamic Gaussian fields are usually semantically weak while 2D VLMs lack spatial grounding. Coupling semantic updates and geometric deformation is especially fragile under occlusion, tissue motion, and events such as cauterization, where appearance changes without corresponding physical displacement.
method: DeGenseGS uses a HexPlane encoder and shared kinematic latents that feed separate branches for geometric deformation and semantic evolution, preventing semantic changes from inducing spurious warping. Rasterization-native extraction analyzes continuous rendered feature maps with RGB guidance to correct local VLM inconsistencies and produce hole-free masks, while angularly aligned distillation respects the hyperspherical semantic space.

title: Demographic-Conditioned State Space Models for ECG-Based Age Estimation
motivation: Chronological age does not fully reflect individual physiological aging, whereas the gap between ECG-predicted age and actual age can serve as a cardiovascular risk biomarker. Existing CNN-based ECG-age models have limited receptive fields for subtle long-range waveform patterns and generally assume fixed-duration, complete 12-lead inputs. A more flexible model is needed to capture global physiology while incorporating demographic differences and handling real-world ECG quality and lead availability.
method: The method combines a convolutional stem with a shared-weight, bidirectional Mamba2 state-space backbone to model local ECG morphology and long-range temporal context across leads. Learnable lead embeddings retain lead-specific spatial context, while sex is injected through adaptive layer normalization throughout the backbone. Hierarchical temporal and channel attention pools informative time segments and leads, making the representation robust to varying signal duration and unavailable or noisy leads before age regression.

title: DenseTRF: Texture-Aware Unsupervised Representation Adaptation for Surgical Scene Dense Prediction
motivation: Surgical dense prediction, including tissue segmentation, instrument tracking, and surgical-zone prediction, is important for intraoperative guidance. Supervised models degrade across changes in anatomy, viewpoint, illumination, and procedure, while dense surgical annotations are costly and limited across institutions. Unsupervised target-distribution adaptation is needed, particularly one that can exploit texture-consistent yet geometrically variable surgical structures.
method: DenseTRF uses unsupervised slot attention to learn texture-aware, object-centric representations from target-domain surgical images through reconstruction. Its dense prediction head is conditioned on these slot representations, allowing adaptation to unlabeled target distributions. A periodic model-merging strategy balances target-domain specialization against retained generalization.

title: DentalPSAM: Lifting SAM to Dental Plaque Segmentation with Hybrid 2D-3D Knowledge Fusion
motivation: Dental plaque is a precursor to caries, gingivitis, and periodontitis, so accurate plaque segmentation from intraoral scans is clinically valuable. Labeled 3D plaque scans are scarce because staining and expert annotation are demanding, and neither geometry-only 3D methods nor appearance-focused rendered-image methods are sufficient alone. Plaque segmentation requires appearance cues such as color and texture together with 3D geometric context.
method: DentalPSAM processes an intraoral mesh and its rendered images in parallel with an interleaved 2D-3D dual-branch design built around SAM. The geometry-enhanced 2D branch encodes 3D coordinates as implicit prompts for SAM, while the appearance-enhanced 3D mesh branch fuses SAM appearance features with geometric tokens for direct mesh prediction. Lightweight bidirectional stitching adapters align the heterogeneous features so both branches refine one another, and their predictions are combined for the final segmentation.

title: DentMamba: An Anatomy-Aware Global-Local Hybrid Network for Large-Scale Multi-class Dental Disease Detection
motivation: Detecting multiple dental diseases in panoramic radiographs is challenged by tiny, inconspicuous lesions, large scale variation, class imbalance, and ambiguous boundaries. CNN detectors struggle to represent diverse lesion scales globally, whereas Transformer-style global attention is computationally expensive; existing methods also often ignore the vertical anisotropy of teeth. An efficient detector must combine local detail, global context, and dental anatomical priors.
method: DentMamba first localizes tooth regions to suppress irrelevant panoramic-image background, then performs fine-grained lesion detection within tooth ROIs. Its AnatoMamba block combines Mamba-based global modeling with anisotropic convolutions that encode vertical tooth-root priors, and MASAG uses bidirectional multi-scale spatial attention to improve feature fusion. A dynamic scale-aware hybrid loss changes the regression objective by lesion scale and aligns classification confidence with localization quality.

title: DeNuC: Decoupling Nuclei Detection and Classification in Histopathology
motivation: Nuclei detection and classification is central to computational pathology, but pathology foundation models have not shown their expected advantage on this task. Jointly optimizing coordinate regression and classification can degrade pretrained foundation-model representations, and detection converges much faster than classification. Treating both objectives as one shared-backbone task therefore wastes computation and weakens fine-grained nucleus representation.
method: DeNuC separates nuclei localization from nuclei type classification. A lightweight detector first predicts nucleus coordinates, after which a pathology foundation model encodes the image and its feature maps are queried at the detected locations to obtain nucleus-specific classification features. This prevents detection gradients from disrupting the foundation model's fine-grained pretrained representations and avoids using an unnecessarily heavy model for the easier detection task.

title: DepthPilot: From Controllability to Reliability in Colonoscopy Video Generation
motivation: Controllable colonoscopy video generators can synthesize specified lesions or classes, but visual controllability alone does not ensure clinical reliability. Generated videos may violate anatomical geometry or fail to reflect faithful mucosal and lesion characteristics, which undermines trustworthy synthesis and downstream 3D use. Reliable generation needs explicit physical grounding and stronger nonlinear modeling of irregular intestinal structure and rapid camera motion.
method: DepthPilot is a diffusion-based colonoscopy video generator with prior distribution alignment and adaptive spline denoising. Prior distribution alignment encodes a monocular depth sequence and aligns its latent features with the denoising backbone through parameter-efficient fine-tuning, providing geometric guidance without abruptly disturbing pretrained features. Adaptive spline denoising replaces fixed linear weights with learnable spline functions to model complex spatiotemporal dynamics under the depth constraints.

title: DermaFlux: Synthetic Skin Lesion Generation with Rectified Flows for Enhanced Image Classification
motivation: Skin lesion classifiers need large, diverse, well-annotated data to distinguish benign from malignant lesions, but clinical image collection and sharing are constrained by privacy, ethical, and legal requirements. Available data can be limited in skin tones, lesion morphology, and rare malignant subtypes, causing class imbalance and weak generalization. Existing diffusion generators also offer limited control and semantic alignment for clinically meaningful lesion attributes.
method: DermaFlux fine-tunes the rectified-flow model Flux.1 for text-conditioned skin lesion synthesis using parameter-efficient LoRA. It trains on curated public image-text pairs whose Llama 3.2-generated captions encode dermatologically meaningful attributes, including asymmetry, border irregularity, and color variation. Flux.1's CLIP and T5-XXL text encoders provide richer conditioning, while rectified flows learn a deterministic transport from noise to lesion-image latents.

title: DermAgent: A Multi-Tool Agentic System for Evidence-Grounded and Traceable Reasoning in Dermatology
motivation: Dermatological diagnosis requires subtle visual assessment, structured dermoscopic concepts, differential diagnosis, and verification against clinical knowledge. General MLLMs lack specialized dermatology perception and external evidence grounding, making them prone to hallucinations and unreliable when visually similar or rare conditions must be distinguished. An interactive system is needed that can integrate specialized tools, retrieve evidence, and expose auditable reasoning steps.
method: DermAgent uses an LLM controller to orchestrate seven specialized vision, language, and retrieval tools through an iterative Plan-Execute-Reflect loop. It combines complementary visual analyses with Case RAG over diagnosed images and Guideline RAG over clinical guidance to build a traceable evidence chain. A deterministic critic audits confidence, task coverage, and conflicts among sources, then triggers targeted tool calls and self-correction before synthesis.

title: DermDepth: Toward Monocular Metric Scale 3D Reconstruction Models for Dermatology
motivation: Dermatology relies on tracking lesion and wound size, morphology, and texture, yet these clinically important properties are inherently three-dimensional. Routine point-of-care capture is usually a single 2D image, which lacks depth and reliable metric scale, while purpose-built 3D systems require specialized hardware. Suitable real dermatological 3D datasets are also difficult to collect, leaving the generalization of monocular metric-depth models uncertain.
method: DermDepth introduces D-Synth, a rendered dermoscopy dataset with metric depth, surface normals, and camera intrinsics, to train and evaluate monocular dermatology 3D reconstruction. The approach fine-tunes affine-invariant 3D prediction models on synthetic data and a small amount of real clinical data to infer dense metric-scale depth and rich surface-normal texture from a single image. It evaluates the resulting geometry for lesion area, width, and volume measurement across dermoscopic and macroscopic settings.

title: Detail Consistent Stage-Wise Distillation for Efficient 3D MRI Segmentation
motivation: Accurate 3D MRI lesion segmentation is valuable for tumor and stroke assessment, but strong volumetric models are too memory- and latency-intensive for many deployment settings. When compact 3D U-Nets are repeatedly downsampled, they tend to retain coarse localization while losing small lesions and sharp boundaries. Conventional feature-matching distillation can oversmooth these vulnerable details and may also transfer noise or scanner-specific high-frequency artifacts.
method: DCD is a training-only, stage-wise knowledge-distillation method for compressing 3D encoder-decoder segmenters. At every encoder resolution, it applies a 3D discrete wavelet transform to teacher and student features, selectively reconstructs directional detail components with inverse DWT, and aligns these detail-focused representations. By leaving the low-frequency approximation comparatively unconstrained and excluding the most noise-prone extreme high-frequency band, it preserves global semantics while focusing supervision on clinically relevant boundaries and small structures.

title: Detecting Clinical Hallucinations in LVLMs via Counterfactual Visual Grounding Uncertainty
motivation: Clinical LVLMs can describe findings, anatomy, devices, or attributes that are unsupported by the image, creating safety and trust risks. Hidden-state detectors are unsuitable for black-box commercial models, while external verifiers often provide only binary conclusions without localizing visual evidence. A model-agnostic auditing method is therefore needed to both detect hallucinations and trace them to image regions.
method: The method audits an arbitrary black-box LVLM response by extracting visually verifiable medical entities and grounding each entity on the input image with a medical-domain-adapted Qwen-VL verifier. It constructs semantically related, spatially non-overlapping counterfactual entities and compares factual versus counterfactual grounding confidence and overlap to derive an entity-level uncertainty score for hallucination detection. This external, plug-and-play design also returns localized visual evidence for each decision.

title: Deterministic Hallucination Detection in Medical VQA via Confidence-Evidence Bayesian Gain
motivation: Medical VQA MLLMs may generate answers that misinterpret or contradict the image, with potential consequences including misdiagnosis and inappropriate treatment. Existing uncertainty-based detectors commonly require many stochastic generations and external NLI models for semantic clustering, making real-time deployment costly. Detection is needed that can expose answer-image inconsistency efficiently using self-contained model signals.
method: CEBaG performs deterministic answer-level hallucination detection from the model's own log-probabilities. It combines the standard deviation of token log-probabilities, representing inconsistent predictive confidence, with evidence magnitude, measured by per-token prediction shifts between image-present and text-only scoring. The parameter-free score requires one generation and two scoring passes, without sampling, external models, or task-specific tuning.

title: Det-Y: A Multi-center Dataset and Benchmark for Efficient Detection of Mycobacterium Tuberculosis in Sputum Smears
motivation: Microscopic sputum-smear examination is an affordable cornerstone of TB diagnosis, but manually finding sparse, slender bacilli is slow, labor-intensive, and prone to observer variation and false negatives. Deep learning adoption has been limited by the lack of public annotated data, while bacilli are small, elongated, variable in size, and often clustered. Practical screening additionally requires low computational cost for primary-care environments.
method: The work releases Det-Y, a two-center annotated sputum-smear dataset for Mycobacterium tuberculosis detection. It also introduces YOLO-Y, built on YOLOv11 and augmented with an Adaptive RoiStrip Block that uses horizontal and vertical strip convolutions to form directional spatial attention for slender bacilli. PANet provides multi-scale feature analysis while retaining a lightweight architecture suited to constrained settings.

title: Device-Constrained Real-Time EVD Catheter Segmentation
motivation: Freehand EVD placement in urgent bedside care has substantial catheter misplacement risk, whereas conventional navigation can be too costly and slow. AR guidance could offer a lower-cost alternative, but it requires real-time direct localization of a thin, low-contrast catheter under strict mobile/XR memory, latency, and power limits. Segmentation is further complicated by motion blur, reflections, occlusion, limited real data, and the large trajectory errors caused by local mask mistakes.
method: This work formulates marker-free EVD catheter segmentation from RGB video for mobile and standalone XR devices. It introduces a structure-aware loss that promotes consistency along the elongated catheter axis, and creates a session-partitioned bedside dataset supplemented by a 3D-driven synthetic generation pipeline. Lightweight backbones are evaluated under real-only, synthetic-only, and combined supervision to characterize cross-domain robustness and on-device accuracy-latency trade-offs.

title: DFuse: A Dual-Branch Adaptive Fusion Network for Multi-Channel MCG Denoising
motivation: MCG can provide non-invasive cardiac assessment with advantages over ECG, but clinical SQUID and OPM systems are expensive or operationally complex. Room-temperature TMR sensors are more accessible, yet their high, sensor-specific 1/f noise can obscure P-waves, T-waves, and fine QRS morphology. Existing denoising methods inadequately handle nonstationary TMR noise or neglect the spatial and inter-channel dependencies of multichannel recordings.
method: DFuse is a dual-branch adaptive fusion network for multichannel TMR-MCG denoising. One branch models long-range temporal context and the other preserves morphology-aware representations; their features are combined through time- and sample-varying fusion to accommodate heterogeneous channel-wise SNR. The study also builds simulated multichannel and real 24-channel TMR-MCG benchmarks for evaluation.

title: DGFMIL: Fuzzy Multi-instance Learning with Cross-Granularity Calibration and Soft Semantic Routing for Histopathological Image Staging
motivation: WSI pathological staging is important for diagnosis and treatment, but slide-level labels leave thousands of patches unlabeled. A patch may contain mixed or boundary-stage morphology, so assigning one pseudo-label discards clinically relevant heterogeneity and encourages overconfident errors. Conventional visual MIL features also lack alignment with the textual medical concepts used by pathologists.
method: DGFMIL combines multiple-instance learning with a differentiable interval type-2 fuzzification mechanism that assigns each WSI patch a stage-membership interval rather than a hard pseudo-label. Cross-granularity calibration and fuzzy-guided cross-attention refine fuzzy feature representation and fusion. A pathological concept text bank and Routing Soft Alignment Module constrain patch features to align with staging-related clinical concepts, yielding patch-level uncertainty and semantic explanations without patch annotations.

title: DiagMIL: Uncertainty-Gated Coarse-to-Fine Multi-resolution MIL for WSI Diagnosis
motivation: Multi-resolution MIL commonly processes high-magnification WSI evidence for every slide under the assumption that more detail is always helpful. Yet high-resolution patches may add noise and considerable computation when low-magnification context is already diagnostic. This differs from pathologists' coarse-to-fine workflow, in which magnification is increased chiefly for inconclusive cases.
method: DiagMIL performs multi-class WSI diagnosis in two stages. A low-resolution graph-based MIL screen produces independent class-wise sigmoid evidence, which is converted into Dirichlet belief and evaluated by a differentiable uncertainty-aware gate. Only inconclusive slides enter a high-resolution softmax stage; cross-resolution graph links and structure-level distillation enforce consistent representations and predictions.

title: Diagnose Like a Doctor: Misdiagnosis-Aware Structured Memory for Continual Learning of Medical Vision-Language Models
motivation: Medical VLMs must acquire new diseases and modalities over time without forgetting prior diagnostic knowledge. Medical images have high within-domain similarity but strong cross-domain differences, making fine-grained decision boundaries especially vulnerable during updates. Existing replay and RAG approaches emphasize positive matches and often fail to teach exclusion of visually similar mimics, leaving clinically hazardous misdiagnoses unresolved.
method: The proposed continual-learning framework integrates a hierarchical Pitfall Graph into RAG-guided fine-tuning. The graph links each medical entity with its definition, visually similar mimics, and explicit exclusion criteria, so retrieval supplies both positive knowledge and misdiagnosis-relevant hard negatives. A large offline multimodal database retrieves similar historical cases during training to support continual adaptation and reduce forgetting.

title: Diagnosing 3D Volumes from Camera Video: A Semantic-Robust Framework Without Direct DICOM Access
motivation: Most volumetric CAD systems require pristine DICOM CT or MRI volumes and direct PACS integration, creating infrastructure, cost, and workflow barriers, particularly in resource-limited hospitals. A camera recording slice scrolling severely degrades a 3D study through artifacts, blur, frame loss, and variable temporal sampling, so it is unknown whether diagnostic semantics remain usable. A robust method is needed to test camera video as a practical universal interface for volumetric diagnosis.
method: ScreenCAD diagnoses camera-captured slice-scrolling videos without reconstructing pristine DICOM data. It first localizes and perspective-rectifies the monitor with RTMDet, then uses a fine-tuned YOLOv5 detector to crop the imaging viewport. A frozen MedDINOv3 encoder produces frame embeddings that a Task-Token Mixture-of-Experts aggregator combines across the full variable-length video sequence for diagnosis.

title: Diagnostic Evidence-Based Prototype Learning via Dirichlet Process for Multimodal Bone Tumor Subtyping
motivation: Accurate primary bone tumor grading and histological subtyping require complementary CT and MRI information because individual modalities can be insufficient for overlapping tumor appearances. In practice, modalities are often missing, and available modalities may provide conflicting diagnostic signals. Existing deterministic fusion methods lack explicit reliability and uncertainty modeling, which can produce overconfident predictions under disagreement or incomplete inputs.
method: DPDEP projects CT and MRI features onto modality-specific, semantically aligned diagnostic prototypes to model heterogeneous tumor signatures. A Dirichlet Process stick-breaking evidential mechanism estimates prototype and modality reliability, then calibrates fusion to prioritize trustworthy evidence when modalities conflict. For incomplete inputs, DP-guided asymmetric evidential distillation transfers joint-modality reasoning by selectively dropping the more reliable modality during training, without imputing missing evidence.

title: DiCoP-SAM: Disagreement-Band Guided Corrective Prompting for Collaborative Semi-Supervised Medical Image Segmentation
motivation: Semi-supervised medical image segmentation must learn from few labeled and many unlabeled images, but fuzzy boundaries and complex anatomy make pseudo-labels noisy and prone to error amplification. Although SAM provides strong priors, its high-confidence semantic bias and sensitivity to prompt form can reinforce incorrect predictions when used in pseudo-supervision loops. An automatic way to generate error-aware corrective prompts without ground-truth masks or manual input is therefore needed.
method: DiCoP-SAM uses a two-stage CNN-SAM collaborative framework. TriGate-CPS combines foreground, background, and uncertainty gates to fuse pseudo-labels and identify high-risk disagreement bands. DiCoP converts these bands into corrective positive and negative point prompts for parameter-efficient SAM adaptation, then distills refined predictions back to the CNN in a predict-correct-relearn loop.

title: Differential Privacy Representation Geometry for Medical Image Analysis
motivation: Medical imaging models are trained on sensitive patient data, so differential privacy is important, but privacy-utility trade-offs are usually judged only by end-to-end AUROC or Dice. Such metrics do not reveal whether privacy noise damages linear separability, reshapes representation geometry, or mainly impairs task-head optimization, even though models may be transferred or used as frozen feature extractors. A diagnostic framework linking privacy-induced geometric changes to downstream utility is needed for informed privacy-model selection.
method: DP-RGMI treats differential privacy as a transformation of representation space and separates encoder geometry from task-head utilization. For each privacy budget, it measures embedding displacement from a shared pretrained initialization, spectral effective dimension of the embedding covariance, and the gap between frozen-encoder linear-probe utility and end-to-end private utility. The workflow uses DP-SGD for training and standard evaluation metrics to produce a diagnostic profile that is model- and dataset-agnostic.

title: Diff-SABR: Diffusion-Based Symmetry-Aware Reconstruction of Alveolar Bone Defects from CBCT
motivation: Accurate 3D reconstruction of alveolar bone defects from CBCT is important for implant surgery and graft planning, yet clinical assessment remains subjective and automated restoration is difficult. Low CBCT contrast, diverse and asymmetric resorption patterns, and the scarcity of paired clinical scans limit intensity-based methods and fully supervised learning. A reconstruction approach must therefore model realistic defects and exploit anatomical symmetry while requiring limited clinical annotation.
method: Diff-SABR is a symmetry-aware conditional diffusion framework trained with hybrid supervision. It generates anatomically principled defects using hyperbolic-paraboloid simulations and combines them with clinical data under a weakly supervised objective. AlignNet registers healthy mirrored anatomy to the defect site, while manifold-constrained latent alignment and diffusion reconstruction promote globally plausible ridge morphology.

title: Diffusion-Guided Anatomical Position Encoding for Dense Longitudinal CT Correspondence
motivation: Dense correspondence across longitudinal CT scans is needed for tracking disease and quantifying change, but scan pairs are scarce and temporally consistent annotations are expensive. Respiration, pathology, and acquisition differences create substantial appearance and deformation variation that can degrade explicit registration and limit generalization. The task therefore needs anatomically grounded representations that transfer across subjects without dense supervision or explicit alignment.
method: The framework distills anatomical priors from intermediate features of a pretrained CT generative diffusion model into voxel-wise position embeddings, enabling correspondence learning without spatial alignment or task-specific labels. Dual momentum contrastive dictionaries impose body-wide feature discrimination and global consistency. A coarse-to-fine refinement network then improves local matching to sub-voxel precision.

title: Digital Twin of the Lung from Wearable Biosignals for Real-Time Respiratory Monitoring
motivation: Respiratory rate is an early indicator of physiological deterioration, yet continuous measurement is largely confined to clinical equipment rather than home or wearable monitoring. Wearable ECG and PPG contain respiratory information, but existing approaches mainly estimate a scalar rate, while lung digital-twin models either require high-resolution inputs or are too complex for real-time use. A framework that converts wearable signals into continuous, patient-specific 3D lung motion is therefore needed.
method: The system first applies Pan-Tompkins QRS detection to wearable ECG, derives R-R intervals, interpolates them, and uses an optimized biquad bandpass filter to obtain an adaptive ECG-Derived Respiration waveform and respiratory rate. The continuous waveform drives vertex displacements on a CT-derived lung mesh, producing a synchronized 3D+t lung animation. This three-stage pipeline links signal extraction, rate estimation, and real-time digital-twin rendering.

title: Dino U-Net: Exploiting High-Fidelity Dense Features from Foundation Models for Medical Image Segmentation
motivation: Medical segmentation requires robust semantic and boundary representations, but transferring generic foundation-model features to domain-specific clinical tasks remains difficult. SAM-style models can be biased toward geometric contours and struggle with nuanced semantics, while dimensionality reduction of dense features can discard fine anatomical detail. A scalable architecture is needed to exploit DINOv3’s high-fidelity dense representations without losing information useful for segmentation.
method: Dino U-Net uses a frozen DINOv3 backbone as the encoder and a U-Net decoder, with a dual-branch DINO Adapter bridging foundation and medical feature domains. Its Fidelity-Aware Projection Module uses low-rank shared projection and dynamic feature modulation to reduce feature dimensionality while preserving fine-grained information. The design transfers dense semantic features to the decoder for regional and boundary-aware segmentation.

title: DINO-3DRA: Leveraging 2D Foundation Model Semantics for 3D Cerebral Aneurysm Segmentation
motivation: 3DRA aneurysm segmentation is difficult because aneurysms occupy very few voxels, resemble parent vessels, and vary across scanners, while large-scale 3D pretraining is unavailable. Although 2D foundation models such as DINOv3 provide dense structural priors, naïve slice-wise transfer fragments inter-slice continuity and can destabilize optimization under the natural-to-medical domain gap. Effective 2D-to-3D integration is therefore needed for stable volumetric segmentation.
method: DINO-3DRA combines a frozen DINOv3-Small path with a trainable 3D U-Net path for cross-dimensional semantic transfer. The Room-Lite spatial mixer uses depth-aware positional encoding and depthwise-separable convolutions to restore inter-slice volumetric coherence. Calibrated residual fusion with learnable scaling stabilizes the interaction between frozen foundation features and trainable volumetric features.

title: DINO-Med3D: Bridging Dimension and Domain Gaps in Volumetric Segmentation via Progressive Adaptation
motivation: Applying a 2D natural-image encoder directly to volumetric medical segmentation suffers from both a dimension gap and a domain gap. Slice-wise processing discards z-axis correlations, while DINOv3’s natural-image bias is poorly matched to subtle textures and low-contrast medical boundaries; simple projection or fine-tuning is therefore insufficient. A progressive strategy must align input dimensions and domains before adding volumetric reasoning and detail preservation.
method: DINO-Med3D progressively adapts a pretrained 2D DINOv3 encoder to volumetric medical segmentation. Stage I uses an Inter-slice Context Embedding module for pseudo-3D input context and a segmentation proxy task for domain alignment. Stage II freezes the aligned backbone, adds lightweight 3D adapters and LoRA for global inter-slice reasoning, and combines a parallel Detail-Recovery stream through Adaptive Gated Fusion to preserve high-frequency boundaries.

title: Di-PACT: Discrete Prognosis via Aligned Co-Topology of Pathways and Tumor Microenvironment

categories.value: Multimodal Integration with Clinical / Genomic / Biomarkers

motivation: Multimodal survival analysis combining WSIs and transcriptomics is vulnerable to overfitting because VFM features are high-dimensional and cohorts are limited. Simple pooling or random compression can remove rare prognostic tumor-microenvironment phenotypes, while unidirectional fusion underuses modality-specific context and can cause modality dominance. Cox-based proportional-hazards modeling may also miss nonlinear survival dynamics, motivating a more balanced and flexible framework.
method: Di-PACT compresses whole-slide VFM features using distance-aware stratified sampling and direct-bottleneck encoding while retaining tumor microenvironment diversity. Bidirectional pathway co-attention lets pathway and WSI representations inform each other, and three-branch residual fusion preserves WSI-specific, pathway-specific, and cross-modal prognostic signals. Survival is modeled as discrete-time classification to capture nonlinear dynamics and support multi-level pathway-morphology interpretation.

title: Directed Ordinal Diffusion Regularization for Progression-Aware Diabetic Retinopathy Grading
motivation: Diabetic retinopathy severity follows an irreversible, asymmetric trajectory, but most ordinal methods treat grades as static and symmetrically ordered ranks. Symmetric constraints can encourage implausible closeness between non-consecutive stages or reverse transitions, producing representations inconsistent with biological worsening. DR grading therefore needs supervision that explicitly respects the forward direction of disease progression.
method: D-ODR constructs a directed graph within each mini-batch, connecting feature-neighboring samples only when the destination has an equal or more advanced DR stage. Multi-scale diffusion on this graph propagates progression structure and penalizes predicted-score inversions along valid forward paths. The regularizer is used only during training, encouraging a progression-consistent representation without inference-time overhead.

title: Discovering Heterogeneous Neurodegenerative Disease Patterns From MRI Data for Improved Prediction
motivation: Neurodegenerative diseases show heterogeneous biomarker patterns, making diagnosis and progression prediction difficult. Conventional all-in-one predictors may be suboptimal, while unsupervised or semi-supervised subtyping can capture variability that is not relevant to diagnostic or prognostic tasks. A method that discovers subtypes under direct predictive guidance is therefore needed.
method: The framework is a mixture-of-experts model with a router that assigns each subject to specialized expert networks, whose assignments define disease subtypes. Each expert performs the prediction task, so routing is guided by predictive objectives rather than only feature similarity. This jointly discovers clinically informative subtypes and improves prediction from heterogeneous neuroimaging data.

title: Discriminative Directional Projection for Reverse Distillation in Breast Ultrasound Anomaly Detection
motivation: Breast ultrasound anomaly detection can be trained using only normal images because obtaining precise lesion annotations is costly. Existing reverse distillation methods optimize global feature cosine similarity but use pixel-wise discrepancies for testing, creating an objective mismatch, and direct cosine optimization can reach poor local optima. The framework needs a training objective that better matches detection and improves anomaly sensitivity.
method: DDP Loss projects teacher and student features into a channel-wise directional subspace generated by a learnable sampler, then enforces pixel-wise cosine consistency there. Alternating optimization updates the student and searches for directions with the largest teacher–student discrepancy, while an orthogonality regularizer preserves diverse directions. These choices align training with pixel-wise testing and strengthen anomaly-discriminative representations without extra architectures or pseudo anomalies.

title: Discriminative Synergistic Temporal Diffusion for Ultrasound Video Thyroid Nodule Segmentation
motivation: Thyroid-nodule ultrasound videos are difficult to segment because nodules are small, boundaries are blurred, and probe motion and tissue deformation create complex temporal variation. Although diffusion-based methods can reconstruct structures progressively, existing approaches treat heterogeneous lesion cues equally at every denoising stage. The varying contributions of motion and texture cues must therefore be modeled explicitly for reliable coarse localization and boundary refinement.
method: DSTD is a diffusion-based video segmentation framework with a Retentive Motion Perception module for temporally consistent motion cues and a Discriminative Texture Perception module for evaluating texture evidence around ambiguous boundaries. A Synergistic Controller adaptively balances motion and texture guidance at each denoising timestep, matching the coarse-to-fine behavior of diffusion reconstruction. The framework is supported by a pixel-level annotated dataset of 374 ultrasound thyroid-nodule videos.

title: Disease-Consistent Visual-Text Alignment and Fusion for Reliable Radiology Report Generation
motivation: Automatic radiology report generation could reduce radiologists’ workload, but clinically reliable generation remains difficult. Retrieval methods may select reports that are semantically similar yet diagnostically inconsistent, and standard cross-attention fuses all retrieved text without reflecting selective clinical reasoning. Disease semantics are also rarely embedded directly in visual representations, limiting sensitivity to diagnostic findings.
method: DCAF introduces a Disease-Consistent Retrieval Enhancer that uses multi-positive contrastive learning and an explicit disease-matching constraint to retrieve diagnostically consistent reports. Its Optimal Transport-Enhanced Cross-Modal Fusion selectively integrates clinically relevant text conditioned on visual evidence rather than treating all tokens equally. An auxiliary disease classification branch encodes diagnostic hypotheses into visual features for disease-aware reasoning.

title: Disentangling Clinic-Specific Acquisition Variability from Motion Dynamics in Intrapartum Ultrasound
motivation: Intrapartum ultrasound can reveal continuous fetal-head progression, but current single-frame analysis misses temporal motion information and is sensitive to noise. Multi-clinic videos introduce variability from hardware, probe motion, operators, and protocols that distorts latent temporal trajectories. Static harmonization methods cannot adequately remove these temporal acquisition effects, motivating explicit disentanglement of clinic variability from physiological motion.
method: The self-supervised framework combines temporal regularization, adversarial disentanglement, and a Hierarchical Cross-Attention encoder. It separates clinic-invariant motion representations from clinic-specific acquisition factors while modeling temporal structure, allowing the learned representation to preserve physiological dynamics and suppress protocol-related distortions. The framework is pretrained on videos collected under heterogeneous protocols from three clinics.

title: Disentangling Prompt Dependence to Evaluate Segmentation Reliability in Gynecological MRI
motivation: Promptable segmentation models can generalize across tasks, but small changes in user prompts may cause large mask changes, which threatens reliability in clinical workflows. Medical images often have low contrast and diffuse boundaries, increasing both inter-observer prompt ambiguity and sensitivity to imprecise interactions. Existing uncertainty or refinement methods conflate these distinct sources of prompt dependence, so an interpretable disentangled evaluation is needed.
method: The framework models the image-conditioned distribution of clinically plausible prompts with a Mixture Density Network; its dispersion quantifies prompt ambiguity and propagates to pixel-level uncertainty. A stability-margin predictor is trained from realistic perturbations around reference prompts to estimate the minimum change that causes a meaningful mask discrepancy, measuring local sensitivity. These two metrics separately characterize inter-user ambiguity and interaction imprecision.

title: Disentangling Uterine and Bladder Activity in Paired EHG-MRI Data Using Anatomy-Guided Multicluster Beamforming
motivation: EHG offers non-invasive monitoring of uterine electrical activity, but pelvic anatomy, low signal-to-noise ratio, and adjacent-organ motion make source isolation difficult. Prior paired EHG–MRI analyses often assumed an empty bladder, while uterine and bladder activity overlap in frequency, so frequency filtering alone is insufficient. An anatomy-guided approach is needed to separate the two sources with limited-channel recordings.
method: The method builds subject-specific volumetric lead-field and direction-of-arrival dictionaries from 3D MRI segmentations of the uterus, bladder, and electrodes. Spatially coherent organ-specific clusters define uterus-pass and bladder-null constraints in a multicluster LCMV beamformer, with Bayesian covariance shrinkage for robust estimation. Overlap-add reconstruction produces organ-resolved uterine and bladder time series from paired EHG and MRI.

title: Displacement Preserving Relational Distillation for Robust Medical Segmentation
motivation: Reliable 3D medical segmentation must handle anatomical variability and domain shifts while remaining efficient enough for deployment. Conventional knowledge distillation can be unstable across architectures, dilute supervision because 3D volumes are background-dominated, and transfer scanner-specific absolute activations. Distillation should instead preserve transferable anatomical structure through architecture-agnostic relational signals.
method: DPRD performs relational distillation on ROI-pooled, case-level embeddings from hierarchical encoder stages. It matches normalized pairwise displacement vectors between teacher and student representations, providing scale-invariant local relational supervision without direct activation matching or dense voxel relations. ROI masking reduces background-dominated supervision and supports distillation across heterogeneous architectures.

title: Distilling Photon-Counting CT Into Routine Chest CT Through Clinically Validated Degradation Modeling
motivation: Routine EICT is widely available but has more noise, lower spatial resolution, and artifacts that obscure small structures and subtle lesions, whereas PCCT offers better image quality but is scarce and expensive. Direct EICT-to-PCCT learning would require impractical paired scans and risks unrealistic structures or textures. A scalable, clinically controlled way to transfer PCCT quality to EICT is therefore needed.
method: MIRA uses a clinically validated degradation-to-restoration pipeline: realistic acquisition degradations transform PCCT into EICT-like images, and a latent diffusion model learns to invert them. A general CT autoencoder is pretrained on PCCT and large-scale EICT data to provide latent representations, while radiologist validation constrains the simulated degradation process. The resulting enhancement model can apply PCCT-like restoration to routine EICT without paired scans.

title: Distilling Temporal Coherence Into 2D Networks for Transrectal Ultrasound Prostate Video Segmentation
motivation: Real-time TRUS prostate segmentation is needed for image-guided interventions, but independent 2D models ignore temporal context and produce flickering masks. 3D or temporal-interaction networks improve coherence at the cost of latency and often require dense frame annotations. Moreover, unstable acoustic regions caused by motion and probe pressure can propagate misleading temporal supervision, so temporal learning must focus on reliable anatomy while preserving 2D efficiency.
method: The Temporally Consistent Learning Framework distills video coherence into a standard 2D student during training, retaining single-frame inference. Confidence-Weighted Temporal Consistency uses optical-flow warping residuals to downweight unstable regions, while Dual-scale Prototype Alignment contrastively aligns local boundary and global semantic features across neighboring frames. Geometric-equivariance pseudo-labeling and student–teacher distillation reduce the need for dense video annotations and preserve spatial priors.

title: Diverse Normal Prototypes-Guided Contrastive Reconstruction for Medical Anomaly Detection
motivation: Unsupervised medical anomaly detection must identify rare, weakly annotated abnormalities from normal training images, but reconstruction methods often miss fine local lesions. Frozen encoders transfer poorly from natural-image pretraining to medical domains, and coherence-based prototype learning can collapse to a dominant prototype. A domain-adaptive representation with diverse normal prototypes is therefore needed for reliable localization.
method: DNP-ConFormer uses a trainable student encoder and momentum-updated teacher for domain-adaptive contrastive reconstruction. A Prototype Extractor obtains Diverse Normal Prototypes from encoder features and injects them into decoding through cross-attention. A Diversity-Aware Alignment loss balances feature-to-prototype assignments and maintains prototype distinctiveness, while branch discrepancies produce anomaly maps.

title: DIVER-Surv: Diffusion and Virtual-Node Graph Fusion for Cross-Cohort Glioma Survival
motivation: Survival prediction for diffuse glioma must combine heterogeneous clinical variables with high-dimensional mpMRI across institutions. Discriminative imaging encoders can be sensitive to scanner and protocol shifts, clinical fields differ in naming and availability, and concatenation-based fusion misses important interactions. A cross-cohort method is needed that learns robust imaging features, accepts heterogeneous clinical information, and explicitly models modality dependencies.
method: DIVER-Surv learns acquisition-robust 3D mpMRI representations with a dual-branch diffusion denoising objective. Structured clinical variables are converted into patient-level text and encoded by a frozen biomedical language model, avoiding manual covariate harmonization. An attention-based modality graph with a learnable virtual node models cross-modal interactions, and joint Cox, denoising, and stop-gradient consistency losses train the framework.

title: DK-Net: Semi-supervised Wavelet-KAN Landmark Localization for Angle of Progression Measurement in Intrapartum Transperineal Ultrasound
motivation: Automated Angle of Progression measurement from transperineal ultrasound requires localizing pubic-symphysis and fetal-skull landmarks, but speckle, acoustic shadows, contrast variability, and scarce expert labels make this difficult. Generic semi-supervised learning does not explicitly address these ultrasound artifacts, and complex competition pipelines can hinder real-time deployment. An efficient single-model approach needs ultrasound-aware feature calibration and refinement.
method: DK-Net is a Mean Teacher semi-supervised landmark detector using weak-to-strong consistency and confidence-filtered pseudo-labels. A KAN-based channel recalibration module adapts features to acquisition-dependent contrast, while a wavelet-domain KAN refiner gates high-frequency subbands to suppress speckle and preserve landmark structures. A pubic-symphysis-guided interaction head stabilizes fetal-skull tangent localization under shadowing.

title: DLCE-MIL: Depth-aware Local Context Enhanced Multiple Instance Learning for Patient-Level IVCM Fungal Keratitis Classification
motivation: Fungal keratitis subtyping from IVCM is clinically important because Fusarium and Aspergillus differ in treatment sensitivity, yet their filamentous morphology can be difficult to distinguish. IVCM sequences are acquired along depth with clinician-guided, non-monotonic sampling, while standard MIL treats slices as unordered IID instances and ignores local continuity and absolute depth. A sequence-aware patient-level model is needed to exploit this acquisition structure.
method: DLCE-MIL extracts slice features with DINOv2 and integrates physical depth embeddings as conditional modulation signals. Its Local Instance Context Enhancement module uses lightweight 1D convolutions to model short-range relationships among neighboring slices in irregularly acquired sequences. These local features complement global multiple-instance aggregation for patient-level classification.

title: Do Not Break the Vessels: Structure-Preserving Mean Flow for Vascular Image Translation
motivation: Clinically accessible NIRII images have limited resolution and scattering, while 2PF microscopy provides detailed vascular topology but is impractical for routine use. Existing translation methods emphasize pixel fidelity or realism and constrain structure only at the output, allowing vessel breaks and spurious branches during generation. The training-time clean structures also differ from degraded inference vesselness, so a trajectory-level and gap-aware preservation mechanism is needed.
method: SPMF formulates vascular translation as a continuous Brownian-bridge diffusion flow constrained by structural invariance. It derives an orthogonality condition between flow velocity and structural gradients, implemented with time-weighted topology regularization that is stronger during coarse generation. Prototype-Guided Structural Refinement retrieves training vascular prototypes and optimizes degraded input vesselness toward a shared anatomical manifold.

title: DosePlug: Observation-Driven Dose Modeling for Robust Low-Dose Reconstruction and Segmentation
motivation: Low-dose CT and PET reduce radiation exposure but amplify noise, artifacts, and contrast loss that impair lesion segmentation. Many reconstruction models process all dose levels similarly, while metadata-based conditioning may be unavailable or poorly reflect task-relevant corruption. Explicitly estimating degradation from sinograms is needed for dose-adaptive restoration that preserves segmentation cues.
method: DosePlug estimates an observation-driven dose from sinogram periodicity degradation and mutual-information cues rather than relying on dose metadata. Periodicity-aware attention restores corrupted sinogram periodicity using a periodicity library, and dose-aware feature-wise polynomial modulation applies nonlinear conditioning to intermediate reconstruction features. The lightweight plug-in can be attached to reconstruction backbones to adapt restoration and segmentation to corruption severity.

title: DPMix-GAN: Dual-Domain Perception and Dynamic Patch-Wise Mixing GAN for 3D CT Synthesis in MR-only Radiotherapy

categories.value: Multimodal Integration with Clinical / Genomic / Biomarkers

motivation: MR offers superior soft-tissue contrast without radiation but lacks electron density required for radiotherapy dose calculation, motivating reliable MR-to-CT synthesis. Spatial-only GANs can overfit modality textures and oversmooth bone and tissue interfaces, while diffusion models are slower and may introduce stochastic anatomy. Moreover, image similarity alone does not establish dosimetric validity, so anatomy-focused synthesis requires clinical treatment-planning validation.
method: DPMix-GAN combines spatial and frequency-domain perception in a generator to capture complementary anatomy and high-frequency boundaries. Its 3D patch-wise feature dynamic mixing exchanges high-order statistics to suppress modality-specific textures and promote anatomy-oriented representations. The GAN design retains efficient deterministic inference while supporting image-level and radiotherapy dosimetric validation.

title: DreamReg: Belief-Driven World Model for 2D–3D Ultrasound Registration
motivation: Real-time registration of intraoperative 2D US slices to preoperative 3D volumes is difficult because slices are partial and speckle-corrupted, and future observations depend on probe actions. Existing one-shot or short-horizon methods cannot accumulate evidence or model how clinicians adjust motion using visual feedback. A sequential model should maintain uncertainty about alignment and exploit action-conditioned future observations.
method: DreamReg represents 2D–3D registration as sequential belief updating over rigid poses using a Dreamer-style latent world model. A recurrent belief combines stochastic latent observations, pose, actions, and volume context; training uses rendered trajectories with posterior inference and prior regularization. At inference, the model rolls out action-conditioned dynamics to imagine candidate probe motions and observations, then refines the pose without new observations or dense correspondences.

title: DRGFuse: Alignment-Guided Dual-Layer Reliability-Gated CT–WSI Fusion for Preoperative TRG0 Vs TRG1–3 Prediction in Esophageal Cancer

categories.value: AI for Population Health, Public Health & Epidemiology

motivation: Preoperative prediction of TRG0 versus TRG1–3 in esophageal cancer could guide treatment and surveillance, but TRG is defined from whole post-treatment specimens while CT and biopsy WSI provide partial, localized evidence. Cross-center variation and disagreement between morphology and histology make fixed-weight or concatenation fusion unreliable, especially when false TRG0 predictions are costly. A robust model must control cross-modal transfer and optimize performance in the low-FPR regime, including missing-modality settings.
method: DRGFuse segments CT to obtain stable tumor and peritumoral regions and uses a pathology foundation model to encode biopsy WSI tokens. Its dual reliability gates estimate cross-modal mismatch, constrain controlled interactions before fusion, and route reliable information with residual logit fusion as a fallback. Training adds alignment and co-teaching components with a low-FPR objective, while inference retains the compact encoders and fusion core.

title: DSCE-Net: Dual-Scale Conditioned Evolving Network with Balanced Optimization for All-in-One Medical Image Restoration
motivation: All-in-one medical image restoration seeks one model for multiple modalities and degradations, but shared representations suffer cross-task interference and unequal optimization difficulty. Existing conditioning often uses coarse cues and does not model both global degradation statistics and local variation, while loss or gradient balancing may ignore convergence status. A task-adaptive network with balanced optimization is needed for consistent restoration across heterogeneous tasks.
method: DSCE-Net uses frequency prompts and a learnable prototype-kernel bank to generate sample-, channel-, and spatially adaptive dynamic convolutions. This dual-scale conditioning captures globally consistent degradation statistics and locally heterogeneous textures within a shared restoration network. A progressive reweighting strategy jointly considers update strength and convergence pace to balance optimization across tasks.

title: DTI-Guided Volumetric Spherical Harmonics Regression for Single-to-Multi-shell dMRI Synthesis
motivation: Multi-shell diffusion MRI provides richer microstructural information than single-shell scans, but its longer and more motion-sensitive acquisition limits clinical and cohort-scale use. Predicting an unobserved shell from one shell is ill-posed because cross-b-value behavior is underdetermined, and image-domain methods are vulnerable to mismatched gradient directions and signal inconsistency that can harm diffusion measures.
method: DTI-SHNet represents source and target shell diffusion signals as real symmetric spherical-harmonic (SH) coefficients, reducing sensitivity to mismatched gradient directions. It estimates direction-agnostic DTI maps such as FA and MD plus a brain mask, and conditions a spatial 3D U-Net on these priors and source coefficients to regress target-shell coefficients using volumetric patches. A signal-consistency regularizer reconstructs signals on randomly sampled canonical directions and constrains them in the signal domain.

title: Dual Agreement Consistency Learning for Semi-supervised Fetal Ultrasound Segmentation
motivation: Fetal ultrasound segmentation supports objective fetal biometry, but manual delineation is operator-dependent and can introduce clinically consequential measurement errors. Pixel-level annotation requires substantial expert labor, while lightweight models are difficult to train reliably when only a small labeled set is available and conventional semi-supervised methods may propagate unstable pseudo-labels.
method: DACL jointly trains a lightweight CNN and a Transformer with labeled supervision and cross-pseudo supervision on unlabeled fetal ultrasound images. Its dual-agreement consistency loss combines pixel-wise probabilistic alignment through KL divergence with entropy-based confidence agreement, suppressing unreliable pseudo-labels across heterogeneous architectures. An EMA Transformer teacher and mixup-based interpolation consistency further stabilize learning from unlabeled data, while the Transformer is used only during training.

title: Dual-Adaptive SAM3: Hierarchical Routing over Low-Rank Expert Layers for Parameter-Efficient Medical Image Segmentation
motivation: Medical segmentation requires adapting general vision-language foundation models to heterogeneous modalities, anatomies, and pathologies. Full fine-tuning is parameter-inefficient and risks forgetting pretrained knowledge, while conventional mixture-of-experts designs add substantial parameter and memory costs; static PEFT also cannot provide input-conditioned hierarchical specialization.
method: DA-SAM3 adapts SAM3 through two complementary mechanisms. A Dynamic Expert Router jointly uses visual input and textual concept prompts to sparsely select relevant experts, while Decomposed Parameterized Experts represent each expert as a frozen SAM3 base plus a trainable low-rank delta. These components are arranged hierarchically so different network depths specialize in coarse alignment, semantic identification, and boundary refinement.

title: DualCaMIL: Dual-Level Causal Multi-instance Learning for Patient-Level Diagnosis in Reflectance Confocal Microscopy

categories.value: Multimodal Integration with Clinical / Genomic / Biomarkers

motivation: Reflectance confocal microscopy offers a non-invasive, near-cellular alternative to histopathology for basal cell carcinoma, but labels are available only per patient while multiple images form each patient bag. Instance-level artifacts and modality styles, together with patient-specific macro-patterns, can create spurious correlations, so enforcing invariance at only one level may suppress pathology or fail to generalize across patients.
method: DualCaMIL performs causal disentanglement at both levels of patient-level MIL. Its Cross-modal Microscopic Causal Disentanglement module uses histopathology as a structural reference to separate lesion-relevant content from instance-level imaging interference. The Patient-aware Macro-level Causal Module attenuates patient-shared, disease-irrelevant structure during aggregation, and counterfactual perturbations are used to stress-test reliance on non-causal factors.

title: Dual-Domain Cross-Modal Decoding for Clinical Text-Guided Medical Image Segmentation
motivation: Pulmonary infection segmentation remains difficult when abnormalities are diffuse, low-contrast, and bounded by subtle texture changes or acquisition noise. Clinical text can specify what should be delineated, but existing text-guided methods mainly align spatial semantics and underuse frequency information that governs texture and boundaries; full-resolution interaction is also computationally expensive.
method: DD-CMD separates language guidance into spatial and frequency roles within a coarse-to-fine decoder. Text-Guided Spatial Cross-Attention aligns multi-scale visual tokens with frozen PubMedBERT text embeddings and applies gated residual fusion, while Spectral-Text Adaptive Modulation uses DCT band-energy statistics to predict text-conditioned FiLM channel recalibration. Three decoder stages operate from 7×7 to 56×56, followed by lightweight refinement to recover 224×224 masks.

title: Dual-Domain Meta Conditioning Network for Fetal Head and Pubic Symphysis Segmentation in Ultrasound Images Analysis
motivation: Reliable segmentation of the fetal head and pubic symphysis is required for angle-of-progression estimation during labor. Intrapartum ultrasound contains speckle noise, shadowing, weak contrast, anatomical variation, rotation, and partial occlusion, while local CNNs may miss long-range dependencies and limited annotations constrain more powerful models.
method: DMC-Net introduces stage-specific Domain Meta Conditioning Modules to inject structural and spectral priors into an ultrasound segmentation network. An encoder-side Structural DMCM supplies anatomical cues, while Frequency-aware Cross-scale Attention models spatial-frequency interactions and produces refined frequency information for a second decoder-side DMCM. The Progressive Spectral Reconstruction Decoder then refines Fourier magnitude and phase components to restore fine boundaries.

title: DualGGR-MoME: A Mixture of Multimodal Experts with Dual-Branch Gating and Global-Guided Routing for Cancer Survival Prediction
motivation: Combining whole-slide images and genomics can capture complementary macro- and micro-level information for cancer survival prediction. However, sequencing errors, missing values, staining variation, and other real-world noise can directly distort input-conditioned expert weights in existing MoME models, causing misallocation and unstable predictions.
method: DualGGR-MoME uses four multimodal fusion experts with complementary strategies, including attention-based, bottleneck, additive, and unimodal pass-through fusion. Dual-Branch Gating derives multiple routing signals from pooled expert outputs rather than raw inputs. Global-Guided Routing combines those signals with a global representation of WSI and genomics modalities to compute robust expert weights, decoupling signal generation from weight computation.

title: Dual-Modality Neural Network Integrating Sequence and Structural Information for Drug-Target Interaction Prediction

categories.value: Multimodal Integration with Clinical / Genomic / Biomarkers

motivation: Drug-target interaction prediction can reduce the cost and time of experimental screening, but existing models often rely on a single modality or use shallow fusion of heterogeneous drug and protein information. They therefore struggle to capture complementary sequence and structural cues and the complex nonlinear relationships underlying interactions.
method: MGK-DTI has parallel sequence and structure branches for drugs and proteins. Its Mambaformer combines Mamba-based long-range modeling with multi-head attention for complementary temporal and global context, while a Hybrid Gated Graph Convolutional Network adaptively couples drug molecular topology with protein structural features and cross-modal injection. A Latent Alignment Module unifies the feature spaces before a Kolmogorov-Arnold Network models nonlinear interactions for prediction.

title: Dual-Registration Reciprocal Super-Resolution for Prior-Guided Real-Time 4D-MRI
motivation: Real-time 4D-MRI could support adaptive radiotherapy, but the aggressive undersampling needed for sub-300 ms acquisition causes severe aliasing and loss of anatomical detail. Super-resolution must reconstruct complex anatomy from corrupted frames, yet spatially aligned high-resolution ground truth is unavailable; motion-induced misalignment also limits the use of diagnostic or breath-hold scans as priors and supervision.
method: DuReg-SR uses a Hierarchically Recursive Mutual Network with separate encoders for undersampled 4D-MRI and a patient-specific T1w reference. Its coarse-to-fine decoder alternates super-resolution and deformable registration, recursively propagating deformation fields and reconstructed features so the reference anatomy is progressively aligned and infused. Anatomically-Constrained Mutual Training warps a static breath-hold HR scan to supervise dynamic frames while preserving temporal anatomical consistency, avoiding the need for aligned real-time ground truth.

title: Dual-Space Cold-Start Active Learning Guided by SAM3 for Medical Image Segmentation
motivation: Medical image segmentation depends on costly expert annotations, and cold-start active learning must select informative samples without an initial labeled set. Feature-only representative sampling is redundant, coverage sampling over-selects outliers, and coarse proxy masks may misestimate segmentation difficulty; SAM3 provides useful structural cues but its zero-shot masks can be unstable under medical domain shift.
method: The Dual-Space Active Sampling framework uses SAM3-generated pseudo-masks as task-aware priors while selecting samples in two complementary spaces. Centroid Affinity Scoring with a Cluster-Balanced Penalty favors typical image features without repeatedly querying dense cluster cores. In a pseudo-mask descriptor space, uncertainty-weighted morphological diversity promotes broad shape coverage and filters unreliable zero-shot structures, combining both criteria for cold-start queries.

title: Dual-Stage Course-to-Fine Tooth Alignment Framework with Decoupled Position, Orientation and Shape Features
motivation: Automated 3D tooth alignment is needed to support efficient, objective orthodontic planning. Existing approaches often entangle positional, rotational, and shape irregularities, and consequently struggle with severe malocclusions, missing teeth, and large extraction gaps.
