Practical methods also need richer tooth features without requiring restrictive multimodal inputs.
method: The framework separates tooth alignment into coarse positional correction and fine orientation/shape refinement. A lightweight bidirectional RNN first aligns tooth centroids using improved centroid sequencing, then a ViT-based diffusion model with long-range skip connections predicts quaternion rotations and translations. Statistical tooth shape models registered to oral scans provide explicit shape and orientation features for precise adjustment.

title: Dual-Stream Diffusion with Structure-Aware Fusion for Joint Synthesis of Coherent Medical Image-Mask Pairs
motivation: High-quality paired medical images and ROI masks are difficult to obtain because expert annotation is costly and data are privacy constrained. Existing joint generators can couple geometry with appearance, causing fragmented masks, boundary mismatch, and synthetic-to-real distribution shift. Many also depend on strong conditional inputs, limiting scalable unconditional pair generation.
method: DSD learns the joint image-mask distribution with separate transformer denoising streams for structure and appearance, reducing their optimization conflict. Time-Gated Fusion injects structure tokens into the appearance stream through cross-attention, with stronger guidance at earlier noisy steps. Structure-Aware Heads predict the mask and coarse-to-fine image components, including structure-conditioned high-frequency details, to improve boundary alignment.

title: Dual-Teacher Knowledge Distillation with SAM and Learnable Prototype Guidance for Semi-supervised 3D Medical Segmentation
motivation: 3D medical segmentation is essential for diagnosis and treatment planning but requires expensive voxel-level annotations. Mean Teacher semi-supervised methods can accumulate erroneous pseudo-labels through confirmation bias, especially in low-contrast regions. With few labels, they also lack the anatomical priors needed to segment small or variable structures reliably.
method: The method combines an EMA internal teacher with a frozen, prompt-driven SAM-Med3D external teacher for semi-supervised 3D segmentation. The external teacher distills anatomical shape and boundary priors, while a learnable decoder prototype module reconstructs semantic predictions and residually calibrates EMA pseudo-labels. An entropy-guided prototype calibration loss focuses feature constraints on uncertain voxels and fuzzy boundaries.

title: DUCX: Decomposing Unfairness in Tool-Using Chest X-Ray Agents
motivation: Tool-using chest X-ray agents orchestrate planners and specialized modules, creating fairness pathways beyond those of standalone medical models. Final-answer fairness metrics alone cannot reveal whether disparities arise from a tool, differential routing, or final reasoning and synthesis. Process-level attribution is therefore needed to diagnose and target inequity in clinical agentic systems.
method: DUCX audits MedRAX-style chest X-ray question-answering agents using observable execution trajectories. It measures end-to-end utility and fairness, then attributes subgroup disparities to tool-exposure bias, tool-transition bias, and LLM reasoning bias. The study evaluates multiple driver LLMs and uses CheXAgentBench together with the curated demographic-aware MIMIC-FairnessVQA benchmark.

title: Dynamic Collaborative Continual Test-Time Adaptation for 3D Vessel Segmentation
motivation: Vessel morphology is clinically informative, but domain shifts across centers, scanners, and populations degrade deployed 3D vessel segmentation models. Continual test-time adaptation can update models from unlabeled streams, yet self-supervision may reinforce errors and break vessel topology through disconnections or spurious branches. Fixed teacher-student schemes are also unreliable when the nominal teacher is worse on shifted, complex vessel data.
method: DyCo-CTA performs online unlabeled adaptation with two collaborating models whose teacher-student roles are dynamically assigned according to relative reliability. A pseudo-break transformation creates complementary inputs that encourage preservation of vessel structure. The framework also applies topological regularization to align critical topological points, complementing pixel-level consistency and protecting global connectivity.

title: Dynamic Spatial-Temporal Mapping for EEG-to-fMRI Synthesis via Gaussian-Guided Heterogeneous Graph Neural Network
motivation: EEG-to-fMRI synthesis could provide accessible brain monitoring with high spatial-temporal detail, but neurovascular coupling is nonlinear and ambiguous. Static or implicit regression approaches do not explicitly capture region- and subject-specific hemodynamic delays. They also struggle with the spatial mixing caused by volume conduction, in which scalp EEG is displaced from its cortical sources.
method: DSTP represents scalp electrodes and brain ROIs as distinct nodes in a Dynamic Heterogeneous Graph Neural Network with evolving directional relations. Learnable Gaussian masks gate EEG history during message passing to model ROI-specific hemodynamic delays and dispersions, while a Transformer integrates historical state evolution. A multi-objective loss jointly enforces reconstruction, temporal consistency, and brain topological consistency.

title: Dynamic Sub-domain Modeling for Robust Medical Image Segmentation
motivation: Medical images within one nominal dataset can still contain latent sub-domains caused by acquisition, reconstruction, anatomical, and pathological variation. A single shared segmentation model averages these heterogeneous distributions, weakening subtle cues and imposing a boundary-accuracy ceiling. Existing fine-grained, adaptation, and fixed-expert methods generally do not explicitly discover and model unknown or emerging intra-domain modes.
method: This framework treats single-domain segmentation as inference over latent sub-domains. A nonparametric prototype mechanism discovers distributional modes and adds prototypes only when novel modes appear; each prototype conditions a specialized expert through a hypernetwork. Soft routing with uncertainty-tempered calibration adapts sub-domain posteriors at test time without gradient or weight updates.

title: DynFS-MoE: Dynamic Functional-Structural Mixture-of-Experts for Post-Traumatic Epilepsy Diagnosis

categories.value: Multimodal Integration with Clinical / Genomic / Biomarkers

motivation: Post-traumatic epilepsy is a serious delayed complication of traumatic brain injury, and early identification is difficult because it involves heterogeneous structural and functional brain alterations. Unimodal approaches cannot jointly capture functional temporal dynamics and structural network information. Conventional multimodal fusion may lose modality-specific information, allow dominant modalities to overwhelm others, and apply uniform weights despite phenotype-dependent relevance.
method: DynFS-MoE first divides fMRI BOLD signals into temporal patches and injects dMRI-derived structural connectivity into each patch through gated cross-modal fusion. Modality-specific and cross-modal experts then learn complementary functional, structural, and interaction representations. A Modality-Class MoE router uses class-conditioned representations to select modality patches and weight experts for diagnosis.

title: EA-LDM: Explicit Alignment Latent Diffusion Model for Patient-Specific CT Reconstruction from Bi-planar X-Rays
motivation: Bi-planar X-ray-based CT reconstruction could reduce imaging dose and speed up image acquisition for adaptive radiotherapy compared with frequent CBCT. However, overlapping anatomy in 2D projections makes 3D reconstruction spatially ambiguous, while the ill-posed one-to-many mapping causes population models to oversmooth or hallucinate patient-specific details. A pre-treatment planning CT is informative but may be anatomically outdated during treatment.
method: EA-LDM aligns bi-planar X-ray features directly to a pre-trained 3D CT latent space, producing conditional embeddings that guide latent diffusion reconstruction. This Explicit Alignment uses volumetric CT semantic priors to disambiguate 3D structure from overlapping projections. Patient-Specific Optimization uses bi-level optimization to combine population-level reconstruction learning with priors from a patient's pre-treatment planning CT while accounting for anatomical changes during treatment.

title: ECFR: Entropy-Consistency Flow Rectification in Test-Time Adaptation for Medical Foundation Models
motivation: Medical foundation models can degrade under continuous shifts in devices, protocols, and patient populations, whereas test-time adaptation can update from unlabeled online data. Existing TTA commonly minimizes entropy or enforces consistency in one direction, which can make incorrect predictions overconfident or preserve flawed representations. Safer adaptation requires identifying unreliable samples and preventing their errors from accumulating into model collapse.
method: ECFR uses an EMA Mean Teacher to compute predictive entropy and teacher-student consistency for each streaming test sample. It partitions samples into entropy-consistency quadrants, minimizes losses to consolidate likely correct samples toward the high-consistency, low-entropy state, and maximizes objectives to sequester high-risk samples while stopping their erroneous gradient propagation. A dynamic memory bank calibrates the quadrant thresholds as the test distribution drifts.

title: ECG-CoCa: Physiology-Informed Contrastive and Generative Framework for ECG Interpretation
motivation: Automated ECG interpretation must jointly assess subtle waveform morphology and global rhythm, but expert reading is labor-intensive and variable. Existing image-based, global contrastive, or generative approaches can lose fine detail, underrepresent rare conditions, or generate reports that drift from physiological evidence. A unified raw-signal framework is needed for clinically faithful interpretation under these constraints.
method: ECG-CoCa directly interprets raw multi-channel ECGs through joint contrastive and generative learning. Its Physiology-Informed Dual-Granularity Encoder combines multi-scale convolutions and Transformer layers to disentangle local morphology and global rhythm for cross-modal alignment and report generation. Clinical-Concept Aware Reweighting upweights rare diagnostic concepts, while Diagnostic-Context Memory supplies global diagnostic anchors to the decoder to improve report consistency.

title: ECHO: Estimated Composite Hybrid Observation for Zero-Shot Self-Supervised MRI Reconstruction
motivation: Accelerated MRI reconstruction from undersampled k-space is ill-posed, while dataset-trained deep models can fail on unseen sampling trajectories, acceleration rates, contrasts, or anatomies. Zero-shot self-supervised methods reduce this domain-shift dependence, but their data splitting creates a training-inference acceleration mismatch and their large networks are costly and prone to overfitting under limited supervision. A more observation-consistent and compact zero-shot design is needed.
method: ECHO avoids splitting the acquired k-space data by constructing composite training inputs from intermediate reconstructions that are statistically consistent with inference-time observations. It uses an under-parameterized physics-informed network designed for zero-shot reconstruction, combining learned regularization with MRI data consistency. The framework also analyzes the role of randomized secondary masks in reconstruction.

title: Echo2ECG: Enhancing ECG Representations with Cardiac Morphology from Multi-view Echos

categories.value: Multimodal Integration with Clinical / Genomic / Biomarkers

motivation: ECG is inexpensive and ubiquitous for electrical abnormalities, but it cannot directly measure structural cardiac phenotypes such as LVEF, which usually require Echo. Supervised ECG prediction depends on Echo-derived labels, while prior multimodal self-supervision aligns ECG with a single local Echo view and often requires reports. This mismatch between global electrical signals and partial anatomy limits scalable learning of morphology-aware ECG features.
method: Echo2ECG is a multimodal self-supervised framework that aligns global ECGs with complete multi-view Echo studies rather than isolated Echo views. It leverages powerful unimodal encoders pretrained on large datasets to distill multi-view cardiac morphology into an ECG encoder, without paired text reports. The learned ECG representation is then intended for morphology-dependent classification and ECG-to-Echo retrieval.

title: Echo4DIR: 4D Implicit Heart Reconstruction from 2D Echocardiography Videos
motivation: Patient-specific 3D+t cardiac anatomy could support assessment of morphology, motion, and function using low-cost 2D echocardiography. Sparse 2D views leave unseen geometry ambiguous, and independently reconstructed frames lack dense correspondences, causing flicker, mesh drift, and non-physical deformation. Synthetic training priors also differ from clinical ultrasound, requiring adaptation without 3D ground truth.
method: Echo4DIR learns a conditional cardiac signed distance function from statistical shape-model priors, conditioned on multi-view echo-mask features fused by an Epipolar Mask Encoder with epipolar cross-attention. At test time, an SDF-tailored differentiable renderer and learnable transducer transformations self-supervise patient-specific adaptation from uncalibrated clinical masks. A velocity network and Radial SDF Alignment constrain temporal shape evolution to produce continuous 4D geometry.

title: EchoFID: A Multi-teacher Distilled Evaluation Network for Cardiac Ultrasound Image Generation
motivation: Cardiac ultrasound generation is useful for augmentation and representation learning, but reliable evaluation remains unresolved. Generic natural-image metrics and single-task medical backbones fail to capture the distinct anatomical, functional, diagnostic, and texture information in echocardiography. Directly averaging or strictly matching multiple expert features also obscures or conflicts with their different inductive biases.
method: EchoFID learns an evaluation-specific feature encoder by distilling an ensemble of pretrained expert networks for segmentation, diagnosis, and functional measurement. Rather than forcing teacher and student features to match directly, lightweight converters reconstruct each teacher feature space from the student embedding. Forward decodability preserves teacher-relevant information, and asymmetric gradient routing prevents competing teacher signals from destabilizing the shared encoder.

title: EchoLVFM: One-Step Video Generation via Latent Flow Matching for Echocardiogram Synthesis
motivation: Controllable echocardiogram video generation could enable augmentation, counterfactual analysis, and training around clinically important variables such as EF. Existing high-fidelity approaches commonly require many sampling steps and force heterogeneous videos to fixed temporal lengths through discarding, cropping, resampling, or interpolation. These choices reduce efficiency and can distort or lose clinically relevant temporal dynamics.
method: EchoLVFM performs controllable echocardiogram video synthesis with one-step latent flow matching. During training, it learns a conditional average velocity from temporally augmented latent videos, using partial observed frames and target EF as conditioning. A masked conditioning strategy identifies valid frames, allowing variable-length sequences and supporting reconstruction or EF-based counterfactual generation from partial videos.

title: EchoPilot: Training-Free Ultrasound Video Segmentation via Scale-Space Semantic Prompting and Reliability-Gated Memory
motivation: Ultrasound video segmentation is difficult because of speckle noise, artifacts, weak boundaries, and rapid anatomical deformation. A single point click and anatomical label often leave target scale and boundaries ambiguous, while greedy memory propagation turns initial mistakes into persistent temporal drift. Task-specific fine-tuning requires costly annotations and may not transfer across devices or settings.
method: EchoPilot is a training-free pipeline that combines a frozen medical VLM for category-grounded localization, a VFM for dense geometric features, and a promptable video segmentor for prediction and propagation. Scale-Space Semantic Prompting uses the parameter-free S.E.E.D. criterion to choose contextual scale and derives precise auxiliary point prompts from dense features after one click. Reliability-Gated Memory selectively freezes the propagation memory when predictions are uncertain.

title: Echo-SCAR: Temporal Feature Learning for Myocardial Scar Detection from Routine Echocardiography

categories.value: AI for Neglected Diseases & Limited-Resource Settings

motivation: Myocardial scar determines prognosis, arrhythmic risk, and treatment decisions, but LGE-CMR is too costly and inaccessible for population-level screening. Routine echocardiography is widely available but provides functional measures with limited sensitivity for segment-level scar and lacks direct tissue characterization. It remains unclear which temporal echocardiographic features can capture subtle scar-related changes across segments and etiologies.
method: Echo-SCAR uses paired Echo-CMR data to train view-specific nnU-Net models that segment myocardial regions across apical two-, three-, and four-chamber videos and map them to AHA segments. It extracts either temporal radiomic descriptors from segmented myocardium or global-average-pooled encoder bottleneck embeddings, then applies matched temporal summaries. Class-weighted random forest classifiers predict per-segment CMR hyperenhancement, with feature fusion also evaluated.

title: EchoTracker2: Enhancing Myocardial Point Tracking by Modeling Local Motion
motivation: Myocardial point tracking supports strain estimation, yet echocardiography contains speckle noise, low contrast, and view-dependent artifacts. Unlike natural-video motion, myocardial deformation is smooth, cyclic, spatially coherent, and locally confined by biomechanics. General-purpose and coarse-to-fine tracking designs may therefore devote unnecessary capacity to global motion instead of the pixel-level local accuracy needed for functional measurements.
method: EchoTracker2 uses a fine-stage-only architecture for full-cycle myocardial point tracking, omitting the coarse initialization used in common coarse-to-fine trackers. It augments pixel-precise features with local spatiotemporal context and combines them with long-range joint temporal reasoning over neighboring trajectories. The design searches for correspondence within a confined local neighborhood suited to physiologically constrained myocardial motion.

title: EchoVQA: Enabling Conversational Assistance for Point-of-Care Cardiac Ultrasound
motivation: Point-of-care echocardiography expands access to cardiac imaging, but acquisition and interpretation require expertise that is often unavailable. Existing echocardiography VQA data are small, limited to high-quality images and few views, and do not help novices improve probe positioning toward diagnostic A4C imaging for LVEF. Existing medical multimodal models can also require billions of trainable parameters, limiting practical deployment.
method: EchoVQA provides a large echocardiography VQA dataset spanning public and point-of-care images, varied views, image quality, and multi-turn questions on view, quality, visibility, LVEF feasibility, and acquisition guidance. Its human-in-the-loop pipeline uses expert category labels and templates, GPT-4o for image-specific QA expansion, and expert review for clinical grounding. The accompanying parameter-efficient multimodal method combines visual adaptation prompts, text prompt learning, and instance-level prompt optimization.

title: ECLIPSE: EHR-Constrained Localized Inference for Pan-Tumor Segmentation
motivation: Pan-tumor segmentation is needed for cancer staging, treatment planning, and prognosis, but voxel-level annotations are scarce and tumors vary markedly across organs. Existing imaging-only methods ignore structured EHR findings such as lesion count, size, and region, while manual prompts do not scale to routine or multifocal cases. These sparse clinical descriptors are spatially informative but cannot by themselves determine voxel-level tumor locations.
method: ECLIPSE first estimates a tumor-type-prompt-conditioned spatial response map in a pretrained decoder to produce dense, coarse localization hypotheses. Its Clinical-Constrained Hypothesis Generation module turns EHR lesion count, maximal diameter, and anatomical subregion into soft constraints on count, size, and regional coherence, yielding bounding boxes. These automatically inferred boxes are then encoded as spatial prompts for voxel-wise refinement.

title: EdgeCVS: Democratization of surgical AI with a Distilled Edge-Deployable Critical View of Safety (CVS) model
motivation: Critical View of Safety assessment during laparoscopic cholecystectomy helps prevent bile duct injury, but visual assessment by surgeons is subjective and ambiguous. High-performing AI systems often use very large backbones that require hardware and infrastructure unavailable in typical operating rooms. A compact model is needed to make consistent CVS assessment practical on accessible edge hardware.
method: EdgeCVS uses phase-gated distillation to transfer a high-capacity CVS teacher into a 5M-parameter student for edge deployment. It exploits the phase-specific, anatomically focused visual space of CVS and enriches student supervision with phase-gated pseudo-labels and anatomical spatial priors. This is intended to let the compact model recover the teacher's complex decision boundaries while supporting real-time CPU inference.

title: EEGRFusion: Uncertainty-Aware EEG-to-Image Evidence for Adjunct Bedside Assessment of CMD in Disorders of Consciousness
motivation: Behavior-based assessment of disorders of consciousness can be unreliable in cognitive motor dissociation, where patients may have covert neural responses despite absent or inconsistent behavior. Bedside EEG is more scalable than fMRI, but EEG-to-image decoding is difficult because EEG is noisy and variable, and CLIP-based conditioning can lose low-level perceptual evidence or cause structural drift. Clinician-reviewable and uncertainty-aware evidence of stimulus processing is therefore needed as an adjunct to bedside evaluation.
method: EEGRFusion maps EEG into a visual-semantic space for zero-shot image retrieval and EEG-conditioned image generation. Its MAMD encoder combines a temporal path with a montage-aware spatial path, including electrode geometry and regional priors, to create robust EEG embeddings aligned with frozen CLIP image embeddings. For generation, it models an EEG-to-CLIP conditional distribution with Rectified Flow and decodes it using a frozen diffusion backbone with an IP-Control Fusion Adapter; multi-sample uncertainty heatmaps expose variability.

title: Efficient Conformal Volumetry for Template-Based Segmentation
motivation: Template-based segmentation propagates labels through deformable registration and is commonly used to derive clinically meaningful volumes. Although conformal prediction can guarantee coverage for such scalar biomarkers, direct output-space calibration produces wide intervals, and feature-based approaches for deep segmentation models do not directly apply to registration pipelines. The deformation field itself contains geometric information that drives volumetric uncertainty and should be exploited for more efficient uncertainty quantification.
method: ConVOLT performs conformal prediction for volumetric biomarkers by conditioning calibration on features extracted from the registration deformation field. It trains a label-specific regressor to predict a multiplicative volumetric scaling factor, then conformalizes that factor using calibration data to form valid intervals. By using geometric cues such as local expansion, contraction, and heterogeneity, the method scales uncertainty with volume while avoiding purely output-space calibration.

title: Efficient Flow Matching for Sparse-View CT Reconstruction
motivation: Sparse-view CT reconstruction is ill-posed, and diffusion models provide strong image priors, but their stochastic SDE sampling can conflict with repeated physics-based data-consistency corrections. This interaction may require many iterations and neural network evaluations, which is unsuitable when CT images are needed quickly in emergency or interventional settings. A reconstruction prior with more coherent, efficient interaction with data consistency is needed.
method: FMCT formulates sparse-view CT reconstruction with a Flow Matching prior whose deterministic ODE trajectory is interleaved with data-consistency corrections. EFMCT further reuses velocity fields predicted at prior adjacent steps, based on their smooth temporal evolution, to reduce neural network function evaluations. The method analyzes the reuse error and uses explicit data consistency to keep the resulting integration error controlled.

title: Eigen-Directed Random Projection for Medical Image Class Incremental Learning
motivation: Medical imaging classifiers must learn newly emerging diseases or modalities over time without forgetting earlier conditions. Retaining historical patient data is often infeasible because of privacy and governance constraints, making replay-free CIL important. In fine-grained medical tasks, existing analytic classifier methods using random projection can leave similar classes poorly separated, so incremental updates erode decision margins.
method: EDRP is a training-free analytic CIL framework that builds a classifier from fixed pretrained features. It replaces structure-agnostic random projection with an eigen-directed, data-driven projection that expands margins along principal directions associated with class confusion while preserving complementary information. Its dual-view analytic design targets fine-grained class separability with low memory overhead.

title: EmERGE: A Multimodal LLM-Based Evidence-Mediated ECG Report Generation and Evaluation Approach
motivation: Automated ECG reports could improve the efficiency, consistency, and accessibility of cardiac care. Current multimodal language-model approaches often map ECG signals and images directly to text, which can generate conclusions driven by dataset bias or language priors rather than valid electrophysiological evidence. This causes hallucination and makes the clinical reasoning behind reports difficult to interpret or verify.
method: EmERGE reframes ECG report generation as evidence-mediated causal reasoning rather than direct signal-to-text prediction. It first infers six clinically established electrophysiological evidence dimensions, including rhythm and rate, P waves, P-R intervals, QRS complexes, ST segments, and T-wave/QT information, then conditions diagnosis generation on this structured evidence. A rule-guided counterfactual protocol perturbs relevant leads, waveform segments, or morphologies to test whether evidence and diagnostic outputs change selectively.

title: E-MRL: Cross-View Aligned Evidence-Driven Multimodal Reinforcement Learning for Reliable 3D Tumor Analysis
motivation: VLMs for 3D CT tumor analysis can produce clinically plausible but false reports because long volumes and sparse pathology make it hard to attend to critical visual cues. Standard SFT and text-oriented RL reward report fidelity without supervising whether the conclusion comes from the appropriate slice, allowing language priors or irrelevant visual regions to drive reasoning. Reliable tumor analysis requires verifiable correspondence between report content and local evidence in the volume.
method: E-MRL casts 3D CT report generation as a diagnosis-localization-verification Markov Decision Process. Besides producing a global report, the model selects a key evidence slice, which is independently re-queried locally; rewards combine diagnostic correctness with text and visual evidence grounding. A cross-view consistency reward encourages alignment between the global report, the selected local slice, and the reference report.

title: ENC-ODE: Event-level Neurodegenerative Modeling in Continuous Time with Neural ODEs
motivation: Predicting longitudinal biomarker evolution is important for early diagnosis and management of neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer's disease. Available biomarker measurements are sparse and irregular because imaging is costly and burdensome, while discrete-time sequence models are poorly suited to irregular gaps. Existing continuous and discrete approaches also commonly compress all multimodal history into one representation, obscuring which past events matter for a particular target time and modality.
method: ENC-ODE propagates every past modality-specific observation through diagnosis-conditioned neural ODE dynamics to predict its evolution at a target time. It then uses attention conditioned on the requested target time and modality to aggregate these event-level predictions. This avoids compressing the entire irregular multimodal history into one latent state and preserves target-relevant event information.

title: End2Reg: Learning Task-Specific Segmentation for Markerless Registration in Spine Surgery
motivation: Spine-surgery navigation requires millimeter-level registration accuracy, yet common approaches use radiation-intensive intraoperative imaging and invasive bone-anchored markers. Markerless RGB-D registration could avoid these burdens, but current pipelines depend on weak or noisy segmentation labels and sometimes manual overlap selection. Segmentation errors can propagate into registration, especially with heterogeneous point clouds, low overlap, soft-tissue occlusion, and surgical instruments.
method: End2Reg jointly learns task-specific segmentation and rigid registration between preoperative anatomy and intraoperative RGB-D point clouds. Segmentation masks are optimized solely through the registration objective, without explicit segmentation labels, using a Straight-Through Gumbel-Softmax estimator to support end-to-end optimization. This lets the system select anatomy useful for alignment while avoiding noisy weak labels and manual overlap selection.

title: EndoDA3: Unified Depth and Pose Estimation for Endoscopic Video
motivation: Monocular endoscopic 3D reconstruction can provide surgical depth cues for lesion sizing, navigation, and robotic automation, but deformable tissue, weak texture, and changing illumination make it difficult. Existing self-supervised and foundation-model adaptations often use multi-stage or separate pose-estimation networks and infer frames independently. This leaves error accumulation, inefficient model design, and insufficient temporal consistency in surgical videos.
method: EndoDA3 adapts Depth Anything 3 for self-supervised, continuous endoscopic reconstruction in a single shared network. Its Dual-Vector Modulated LoRA (DVM-LoRA) efficiently enables joint prediction of scale-consistent depth and camera pose without a separate pose network or ground-truth depth. An uncertainty-aware projection loss confidence-weights reprojection-depth signals to enforce temporal continuity while reducing the influence of instruments and non-rigid tissue motion.

title: EndoGSim: Physics-Aware 4D Dynamic Endoscopic Scene Simulations via MLLM-Guided Gaussian Splatting
motivation: Dynamic reconstruction and simulation of endoscopic scenes are important for surgical planning, spatial intelligence, and autonomous robotic control. Existing reconstruction methods largely model appearance but not object material properties, preventing physically credible simulation. Methods for physics-aware general scenes also do not adequately handle dynamic surgical video, informed material initialization, or distinct tissues and instruments.
method: EndoGSim represents deformable tissues and instruments from endoscopic video with 4D Gaussian Splatting, aided by depth estimation and segmentation. It introduces an object-wise material field whose parameters are initialized by an MLLM and refined in a differentiable Material Point Method. Rendering and optical-flow supervision jointly optimize the material parameters for visual and physical fidelity.

title: EndoVLM: An Endoscopy Vision-Language Pre-training Model via Anatomy-Guided Sparsity and Progressive Alignment
motivation: Endoscopy foundation models are mainly trained with unimodal visual self-supervision and therefore miss the anatomical, pathological, and procedural knowledge in clinical reports. A report usually describes an entire examination, whereas its many unannotated images or video frames lack explicit correspondence to report findings. This modality and granularity gap prevents precise vision-language alignment for endoscopic analysis.
method: EndoVLM is a vision-language foundation model pre-trained on paired endoscopic image collections and clinical reports. Anatomy-Guided Sparse Pooling uses report descriptions as queries to select and aggregate anatomy-relevant frames from redundant image sets. Progressive Semantic-Aware Alignment uses anatomy and pathology soft targets to move from patient-level to localized alignment, while Semantic-Concentrated Masked Autoencoding learns visual detail only from the selected semantic-rich frames.

title: EndoX: A GPU-Accelerated Endoscopic Perception Simulation Framework
motivation: Endoscopic depth estimation, reconstruction, and coverage analysis need geometric ground truth for rigorous training and evaluation, but such measurements cannot readily be obtained during clinical procedures. Existing datasets provide limited spatial annotations, diversity, or modalities, while existing simulators trade physical realism against scalable rendering speed. A system is needed to generate diverse, photorealistic endoscopic data with complete geometric supervision at scale.
method: EndoX is a GPU-accelerated synthetic-data and interactive simulation framework that automatically converts CT data into anatomically accurate 3D organ meshes. It uses physics-based rendering to generate co-registered RGB images and ground-truth depth, normals, optical flow, occlusion, camera coverage, and geometry. Sensor, lighting, material, and trajectory settings are customizable, and a containerized headless deployment supports scalable generation.

title: Enhancing Brain MRI Anomaly Detection and Reasoning with ROI Rethink and Synthetic Data
motivation: Brain MRI VLMs commonly make single-pass diagnoses without identifying the image regions that support their conclusions, so clinicians cannot audit their reasoning and models may hallucinate findings on normal scans. Open-ended anomaly detection is particularly difficult because rare neurological diseases create OOD cases, while prevalent benchmarks are largely closed-ended. Limited data also encourages overfitting to known distributions.
method: BrReMark uses a two-turn "Mark-and-Rethink" diagnostic trajectory: it first hypothesizes abnormalities and marks suspicious bounding boxes, then re-examines the marked regions to produce a grounded diagnosis. The model is trained with supervised reasoning trajectories followed by GRPO-based reinforcement learning using localization, semantic correctness, and clinical-safety rewards. Pathology synthesis based on domain randomization augments rare lesions and promotes OOD robustness.

title: Enhancing Pathological VLMs with Cross-scale Reasoning
motivation: Pathologists integrate global tissue architecture at low magnification with cellular morphology at high magnification, but most pathological VLMs and benchmarks treat images at a single scale. This mismatches clinical reasoning and limits tasks requiring verification across magnifications. Naively designed multi-image VQA can additionally admit text-only shortcuts, yielding apparent accuracy without genuine cross-scale visual reasoning.
method: The work introduces Scale-VQA, constructed through constraint-guided question design and adversarial text-only screening so answers require visual evidence across magnifications. It also presents ScaleReasoner-R1, trained with curated reinforcement-learning tasks for cross-scale VQA. The framework treats pathology interpretation as coordinated use of low-magnification architectural evidence and high-magnification cellular evidence.

title: Equity-Aware Self-supervised Multi-domain Connectome Representation Learning for Major Depressive Disorder Diagnosis
motivation: Functional-connectome models for Major Depressive Disorder often rely only on time-domain correlations, missing complementary frequency-dependent coherence information. Label-dependent learning is vulnerable to heterogeneous, site-dependent MDD diagnoses and limited annotations, reducing generalization across populations. Representation learning also seldom directly addresses demographic bias and unequal subgroup reliability.
method: RESOLVE uses separate graph encoders for correlation-based and coherence-based functional connectomes, with intra-domain contrastive learning and fusion into a unified embedding. A cross-domain consistency objective and topology-preserving reconstruction retain complementary connectivity information and network organization. Optimal Transport aligns demographic subgroup distributions in latent space to learn demographic-invariant representations before downstream MDD diagnosis.

title: ESRT: Endoscopic Stereo Reconstruction Transformer
motivation: Stereo endoscopic reconstruction is needed to recover depth for lesion assessment and surgical 3D visualization, yet specular reflections, illumination variation, and smooth tissue textures make correspondence estimation unstable. Unconstrained transformer matching creates ambiguity because stereo endoscope disparity is mainly horizontal. Endoscopic 3D labels are difficult to obtain, and conventional transformer reconstruction can be too computationally costly for real-time clinical use.
method: ESRT is a multi-scale encoder-decoder transformer for endoscopic stereo reconstruction. Its row-wise cross-attention confines cross-view correspondence search to the horizontal epipolar direction, excluding geometrically invalid regions. A distillation-based strategy transfers geometric knowledge from a pretrained teacher without requiring endoscopic 3D annotations, while the efficient architecture targets real-time use.

title: Estimated Age-Guided Cerebral Microbleed Segmentation

categories.value: Multimodal Integration with Clinical / Genomic / Biomarkers

motivation: Cerebral microbleed segmentation is hindered by low prevalence, severe class imbalance, and limited annotated data. CMB prevalence and lesion characteristics are positively associated with age, yet chronological age is unavailable in all datasets and prior clinical priors are not generally applicable to all CMB subtypes. Incorporating an accessible age-related biomarker could improve subject-specific segmentation and reduce annotation burden.
method: AgeCMBNet first estimates chronological age from T1-weighted MRI using a pretrained Meta-matching model. It uses a shared image encoder and selects one of two decoders according to whether estimated age is below or above the training-cohort median. This age-stratified design injects an aging prior while sharing imaging features and adding limited parameters.

title: Evidential Fusion Network for Multimodal Survival Prediction Under Missing Modalities

categories.value: Multimodal Integration with Clinical / Genomic / Biomarkers

motivation: Multimodal survival models can support precision oncology, but real clinical records often lack whole-slide images or transcriptomic measurements because of tissue, cost, and infrastructure constraints. Imputation methods can be computationally costly and may hallucinate absent biological signals, while simple masking approaches do not explicitly characterize information loss. Clinical survival prediction also needs calibrated distinction between data noise and ignorance caused by missing inputs.
method: EMMS learns multimodal survival representations and represents each modality's survival prediction as Dempster-Shafer evidence parameterized by Gaussian Random Fuzzy Numbers. Its fusion incorporates modality reliability together with aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty. Missing modalities are encoded as vacuous evidence with zero epistemic strength, allowing a closed-form aggregation in which only available modalities contribute and total evidence quantifies missingness-induced uncertainty.

title: Evidential Neural Networks for Uncertainty-Aware Alzheimer’s Disease Screening from Resting-State EEG
motivation: The task is accessible subject-level screening of Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias from resting-state EEG. EEG is inexpensive and portable, but clinical use requires reliable confidence in addition to discrimination, since neural models can be miscalibrated and overconfident on noisy or atypical recordings. Existing Bayesian approximations provide uncertainty at substantial inference cost, motivating a single-pass uncertainty method for safer selective screening.
method: The method replaces EEGNet’s softmax head with an evidential layer that predicts nonnegative evidence and a Dirichlet distribution, yielding class probabilities and vacuity-based epistemic uncertainty in one pass. Temperature scaling and the UMSE uncertainty regularizer encourage low vacuity for correctly learned samples while retaining uncertainty for ambiguous recordings. Evaluation uses subject-level, leakage-safe stratified group cross-validation and compares deterministic, MC Dropout, and ensemble baselines.

title: Evidential Perfusion Physics-Informed Neural Networks with Residual Uncertainty Quantification
motivation: CT perfusion analysis estimates cerebral blood flow, blood volume, and transit time through an ill-posed deconvolution problem needed for urgent stroke triage. Classical and data-driven methods can be unstable under noise or sparse sampling, while deterministic PINNs enforce tracer-kinetic constraints but provide only point estimates and cannot express uncertainty from imperfect physics consistency. Bayesian or ensemble alternatives are computationally costly for rapid per-case deployment, creating a need for efficient uncertainty-aware perfusion estimation.
method: EPPINN combines coordinate-based networks for arterial input, tissue concentration, and perfusion parameters with an evidential model of physics residuals. A Normal–Inverse–Gamma distribution represents voxel-wise aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty in tracer-kinetic consistency without Bayesian sampling or ensembles. Physiologically constrained parameterization, structured CBV–MTT modeling, progressive annealing, and stabilized per-case optimization improve robustness under noisy and sparse temporal sampling.

title: Evi-Steer: Learning to Steer Biomedical Vision-Language Models through Efficient and Generalizable Evidential Tuning
motivation: Biomedical VLM adaptation must handle scarce labels, subtle visual distinctions, and scanner or population domain shifts while remaining parameter-efficient. Existing prompt, adapter, or low-rank methods apply deterministic updates and do not account for uncertain image-text alignment; full fine-tuning is expensive and can erase pretrained knowledge. An efficient cross-modal method that adapts conservatively under weak or conflicting evidence is therefore needed.
method: Evi-Steer freezes BiomedCLIP and injects low-dimensional steering modules into intermediate vision and text representations, updating only 0.11% of parameters. Evidential modeling estimates latent epistemic confidence, which gates residual token updates so weak evidence produces conservative adaptation. Dempster–Shafer fusion combines visual and textual evidence, suppressing conflicting cross-modal updates during few-shot and domain-shift adaptation.

title: EvoMed: Self-Evolving Medical VLM via Training-free Continued Learning
motivation: Medical VQA requires fine-grained image interpretation and specialized clinical reasoning, yet general VLMs often miss subtle pathology and hallucinate confident diagnoses. Supervised fine-tuning is constrained by scarce labels and high compute, can require smaller backbones, and risks forgetting pretrained abilities. The work therefore seeks to add medical expertise without parameter updates or the associated computational and forgetting costs.
method: EvoMed keeps the VLM weights frozen and builds an external knowledge base through a closed loop of diverse reasoning, self-critique, contrastive summarization, and add/modify/delete/keep maintenance. At inference, a coarse semantic-triplet filter followed by vision-text cross-encoder reranking retrieves relevant clinical priors and injects them into the context. This retrieval-guided, training-free process grounds predictions while preserving generalist capabilities.

title: Evo-RAD: Navigating Rare Retinal Disease Diagnosis via Self-Evolving Agentic Retrieval

categories.value: AI for Neglected Diseases & Limited-Resource Settings

motivation: Rare retinal diseases are underrepresented and heterogeneous, so foundation models can confuse them with visually similar common conditions. Parameter-efficient fine-tuning may overfit scarce rare cases or be dominated by common classes, while static nearest-neighbor retrieval suffers from hubness and returns semantically wrong evidence. Diagnosis therefore needs iterative, context-aware evidence refinement rather than a fixed retrieval set.
method: Evo-RAD formulates retrieval as an MDP in which a graph-based agent sequentially DELETEs discordant references, INSERTs pathologically consistent cases, or TERMINATEs. Group Relative Policy Optimization trains this policy with a homogeneity-aware reward that favors diagnostically coherent support sets. The evolving reference set then supplies context for rare-disease diagnosis, reducing hubness-driven common-disease confusions.

title: Expert-like Bone Ultrasound Segmentation through Expert-in-the-loop Mask-conditioned Progressive Learning
motivation: Bone segmentation in ultrasound supports image-guided orthopedic workflows, but speckle, low contrast, and shadowing make precise manual contours slow and difficult. Existing interactive methods mainly use independent clicks or scribbles, do not model experts’ progressive brush-based behavior, and rarely adapt from approved corrections. A system that completes imperfect expert intent while reducing annotation time is needed.
method: ExiL treats annotation as a progressive trajectory: a signed-distance-field simulator generates partial expert-like brush masks, and a lightweight 7.8M-parameter U-Net completes and refines them conditioned on the current mask and ultrasound image. An expert mode updates the model from accepted corrections, enabling continual personalization to annotation behavior. The design explicitly models dense brush intent and evolving progress rather than isolated clicks or final-mask prediction.

title: Explainability in Multimodal Deep Transformation Models for Stroke Outcome Prediction

categories.value: Multimodal Integration with Clinical / Genomic / Biomarkers

motivation: Stroke outcome prediction must combine high-dimensional neuroimaging with structured clinical variables while remaining understandable for clinical decision support. Statistical models are interpretable but handle images poorly, whereas deep models extract image features effectively but leave their image branch opaque; explainability for probabilistic DTMs had not been established. Practical post-hoc explanations are therefore needed to inspect image evidence and generate clinical hypotheses.
method: The multimodal DTM models a conditional outcome distribution by combining a 3D CNN image transformation component with an interpretable linear tabular component. Grad-CAM is extended through gradients of the transformation-derived class probability, while 3D Occlusion masks image regions and measures probability changes. Using both maps enables complementary spatial explanations, similarity analysis, and error or hypothesis investigation without changing the model architecture.

title: Exploiting Interior Geometry for Intracranial Aneurysm Detection and Segmentation on 3D Point Clouds via GNNs
motivation: Accurate 3D detection and segmentation of intracranial aneurysms is important for rupture-risk assessment and intervention planning, but cerebral vessels have complex tubular topology. Conventional local point or graph features are easily confused by curvilinear anatomy, while GNNs can lose information through over-smoothing and over-squashing and remain difficult to interpret clinically. Explicit interior geometry and transparent graph reasoning are needed to resolve these ambiguities.
method: EXPIGEO probes the interior of a vascular surface point cloud with inward rays, estimates centerline and radius information, and derives a pruned skeleton. It computes physiology-aware geometric descriptors such as radius-gradient magnitude, constructs a feature-rich graph on the full surface, and trains a GNN for point-wise segmentation from which aneurysm instances are detected. Instance-level explainability identifies decision-driving subgraphs and structural error sources.

title: Exploiting Longitudinal Context in Clinician-Verified Interactive Lesion Tracking
motivation: Serial CT lesion tracking is required for treatment-response assessment, but manual retrieval and delineation are time-consuming and variable. Fully automatic trackers can silently follow the wrong structure, whereas registration-segmentation pipelines allow verification but discard baseline appearance and are sensitive to off-center prompts; other longitudinal models are not promptable. A clinically safe approach must combine baseline context, correction by a clinician, and robust segmentation.
method: The Verified Tracking workflow lets registration propose a follow-up lesion prompt that a clinician can verify or correct, after which the model uses it together with the baseline lesion. A shared-weight encoder performs early spatial prompt fusion, and a latent Difference Weighting Block emphasizes temporal changes before longitudinal segmentation. Large-scale synthetic longitudinal pretraining supplies multi-timepoint trajectories and simulated prompts so the model learns to use longitudinal context.

title: Exploring Efficient Weakly Supervised Ultrasound Video Object Segmentation with VLM-Guided Structure Advantage Learning
motivation: Breast-lesion segmentation in ultrasound videos is difficult because boundaries are blurred, motion artifacts occur, and appearance changes over time. Dense labels are expensive, while existing weak or box supervision still requires many coarse annotations and often cannot recover precise structures from simple visual constraints. The work seeks to reduce annotation effort by using medical VLM knowledge to guide fine-grained mask exploration.
method: The method uses a frozen medical VLM as a high-level supervisor and introduces a Guidance Conditional Dirichlet Diffusion Strategy to combine lesion cues for mask generation under weak supervision. Structure Advantage Learning compares the relative quality of candidate structural predictions, allowing the segmentation model to explore and refine boundary details without a full RL pipeline. The authors also provide a 433-video breast-lesion ultrasound dataset for training and evaluation.

title: Exploring Subnetwork Interactions in Heterogeneous Brain Network via Prior-Informed Graph Learning

categories.value: AI for Neglected Diseases & Limited-Resource Settings

motivation: Identifying disorder-related functional pathways from interactions among brain subnetworks is important for diagnosing disorders such as ASD, BD, and MDD. With limited medical samples, purely data-driven Transformer attention lacks knowledge of functional brain organization and can overfit spurious correlations, producing implausible and poorly generalizable interaction patterns. The task therefore needs prior-guided interaction modeling.
method: KD-Brain is a prior-informed graph learning framework that represents the brain as a heterogeneous network and models interactions among functional subnetworks. Its Semantic-Conditioned Interaction mechanism injects subnetwork functional identities into Transformer attention queries, while a Pathology-Consistent Constraint aligns learned attention distributions with clinical priors. Together, these dual priors guide interaction learning toward pathology-aware and interpretable functional pathways under limited data.

title: FA-Diff: Leveraging Frequency-Aware RWKV Diffusion for OCT to Correlation-Stability Map Translation
motivation: OCT provides micrometer-scale structural imaging for malignant biliary stricture assessment, but OCT B-scans alone have limited malignancy sensitivity. CS maps can characterize stiffness associated with cholangiocarcinoma, yet their intraoperative acquisition requires disruptive mechanical compression and hardware changes. Existing OCT-to-CS translation models insufficiently capture both global context and fine high-frequency deformation patterns needed for elastography.
method: FA-Diff is a frequency-aware RWKV diffusion framework for directly translating structural OCT B-scans into CS maps. It combines wavelet-guided stiffness interaction with FG-Shift, a spatial-frequency adaptive scanning strategy that strengthens RWKV modeling of vertical stiffness textures and global coarse-to-fine context. FASN adaptively modulates and fuses wavelet sub-band coefficients using inter-stage states, emphasizing elasticity-relevant frequency information.

title: Fair Curriculum Learning for Concept Bottleneck Models in Dermatology
motivation: Dermatology models often perform worse for darker skin types because of representation bias, biased feature extraction, and evaluation that obscures group-level disparities. CBMs improve interpretability through intermediate dermatological concepts, but standard CBMs have no explicit mechanism to ensure equitable performance. A training approach is needed that preserves concept-based reasoning while directly addressing skin-type fairness.
method: Fair Curriculum CBM trains a concept bottleneck model through four fairness-first phases: balanced foundation, demographic parity, equalized odds, and performance parity. It optimizes fairness losses and introduces adversarial debiasing progressively while jointly training all interpretable concepts. This embeds bias mitigation within concept learning rather than applying fairness only after training.

title: FairGE: Gated Expert Routing for Intersectional Fairness in Medical Foundation Models
motivation: Medical foundation models can produce unequal diagnostic performance across demographic groups, yet most fairness work considers one protected attribute at a time. Real clinical fairness risks can concentrate in sparse intersectional groups, where separate subgroup adaptation is unstable and prone to overfitting. Learned features may also leak demographic information and enable proxy discrimination, requiring multi-attribute fairness adaptation.
method: FairGE adapts frozen medical foundation-model visual encoders using two complementary modules. MA-dMoE inserts lightweight adapters with shared experts and separate routers for each sensitive attribute, then aggregates their routing distributions for intersectional adaptation without dedicated sparse-subgroup adapters. MAP applies a Purifier MLP and multiple gradient-reversal adversarial classifiers to suppress sensitive demographic information from the final visual representation before disease classification.

title: Fairness Beyond Demographics: Optimizing Performance Across Appearance-Based Hidden Cohorts in Medical Imaging
motivation: Medical imaging models may have larger performance gaps across visually coherent but unlabeled hidden cohorts than across visible demographic groups. Demographic-based fairness methods can miss these latent sources of error, require potentially unavailable metadata, and become data-sparse as multiple demographics are intersected. Fairness optimization therefore needs a scalable, label-free basis for identifying and mitigating underperforming subpopulations.
method: LHCF first clusters images into K appearance-based hidden cohorts using learned embeddings, then applies fairness optimization across those cohorts. By optimizing over latent, visually coherent subpopulations rather than predefined demographic groups, it can be used with existing fairness approaches and avoids the combinatorial sparsity of intersectional demographic partitions. The work also introduces HIDFairBench to assess hidden-cohort quality and fairness under increasingly complex demographic partitions.

title: FairPneum: Improving Fairness in Pneumonia Diagnosis and Lesion Segmentation
motivation: Pneumonia diagnosis and lesion segmentation can be biased because demographic characteristics, disease subtype, and image appearance are tightly coupled and unevenly represented in training data. Single-layer adversarial methods may leave sensitive signals at other feature levels, while fairness research for segmentation and continuous measures such as Dice remains limited. A medical-imaging-specific approach is needed to reduce disparity without discarding pathology-relevant information.
method: FairPneum uses hierarchical embedding disentanglement, with multi-level adversarial modules that progressively remove sensitive attributes such as age, sex, and subtype from representations across encoding stages. Its counterfactual re-entanglement strategy combines debiased and sensitive embeddings to encourage pathology-relevant, attribute-invariant features. It also introduces LPE and GPE for evaluating fairness in continuous outcomes such as Dice similarity, supporting both diagnosis and lesion segmentation.

title: Faithful, Interpretable Chest X-ray Diagnosis with Artifact-Free B-cos Networks
motivation: Clinical chest X-ray AI requires explanations that clinicians can understand and verify, whereas many conventional DNNs lack inherent interpretability and post-hoc heatmaps can be coarse or misleading. B-cos networks provide built-in, class-specific evidence maps, but standard versions produce severe grid aliasing artifacts. These artifacts make otherwise faithful explanations visually unreliable for clinical use.
method: The work modifies intrinsically interpretable B-cos networks with two anti-aliasing variants, B-cos_ASAP and B-cos_BP. ASAP or BlurPool replaces artifact-producing downsampling operations with an anti-aliased path, improving the clarity of built-in class-specific contribution maps. The framework is applied to chest X-ray disease detection in both multi-class and multi-label settings.

title: FARSIGHT: A Dynamic Multi Modal Medical Image Analysis Framework Powered by a Prior Knowledge Guided Vision Language Model
motivation: Retrospective medical image archives are often not model-ready: they lack fine-grained labels, have unreliable metadata and non-diagnostic overlays, and require costly expert curation. Studies also contain variable image counts, irrelevant frames, heterogeneous modalities, and missing or misaligned data, which makes patient-level multimodal prediction difficult. An auditable archive-to-prediction workflow is needed under offline privacy constraints.
method: FARSIGHT links archive curation and patient-level prediction through MAGOS and HMMIL. MAGOS is an offline, prior-knowledge-guided VLM-plus-rules agent that performs modality routing and rule-constrained ROI extraction with schema-checked structured outputs. HMMIL then aggregates evidence within and across modalities, accommodating variable study lengths and missing modalities without forced alignment.

title: Fast 3D Cell Volume Reconstruction from Multi-focus Images by Cross-modality Knowledge Distillation
motivation: Three-dimensional cell volumes provide richer structural information than 2D cell images and can support stable, reliable cytological diagnosis. Existing DIP-based reconstruction from multi-focus image sequences avoids requiring a large training dataset, but it relies on time-consuming per-sample optimization. Faster reconstruction is needed while retaining the structural quality of 3D volumes.
method: DeepCVR uses cross-modality knowledge distillation to reconstruct 3D cell volumes from multi-focus images in one forward pass. It first trains a U-Net-based variational autoencoder, CellVAE, on 3D cell volumes to learn a structural latent space. The trained CellVAE encoder serves as a teacher for MF-CellEncoder, which maps multi-focus images to the teacher's latent variables; pairing this student with the CellVAE decoder yields the reconstruction model.

title: Fast Few-Shot Embolization Simulations in Ischemic Stroke Using Equivariant Neural Fields
motivation: In acute ischemic stroke, embolization determines clot location, geometry, and mechanical state, which affect thrombectomy difficulty and patient outcome. High-fidelity FEM can simulate these patient-specific dynamics but is too computationally expensive for time-critical clinical use. Existing Lagrangian neural dynamics approaches also commonly require many high-fidelity simulations, motivating a fast and data-efficient surrogate.
method: The method is a meshless neural surrogate for Lagrangian embolization dynamics that predicts particle acceleration updates with SE(3)-equivariant neural fields. Rotation and translation equivariance encode the physical symmetry of clot-vessel interactions, enabling learning from sparsely sampled high-resolution FEM simulations and inference at full spatial resolution. This design targets generalization across patient-specific vascular geometries with few training simulations.

title: FDMMBone: Flow-Based Conditional Deformable Mesh Modeling for Accurate 3D Bone Defect Completion
motivation: Accurate 3D completion of bone defects is needed for personalized implant design and surgical planning, where anatomically plausible structure, precise boundaries, and smooth surfaces are all important. Existing voxel, point-cloud, implicit, symmetry-based, and other generative representations struggle to preserve topology and surface fidelity while remaining conditionally consistent, especially for complex or large defects.
method: FDMMBone represents bone shapes in a deformable tetrahedral (DMTet) parameter space and uses conditional flow matching with probability-flow ODE integration to generate anatomically valid mesh parameters. A geometry-constrained projection-correction step enforces boundary consistency during sampling. Subdivision-based deformation refinement then separates global shape generation from local surface refinement, improving smoothness and boundary continuity.

title: FDRAS: Failure Diagnosis and Repair for Airway Segmentation
motivation: Airway segmentation from chest CT supports bronchoscopy navigation and surgical planning, but domain shifts can cause disconnected distal branches, boundary leakage, and other structural failures that voxelwise overlap metrics may miss. Existing quality-control methods detect errors without repairing them, while refinement methods directly alter masks or use heuristic repairs without explicitly separating diagnosis from correction, limiting controllability under distribution shift.
method: FDRAS explicitly separates structural failure diagnosis from mask correction. A diagnosis network predicts an SDF-based boundary error map and a skeleton-derived tree connectivity error map from the CT volume and initial mask. These fields condition a mask-only refinement network through asymmetric and cross-attention mechanisms, focusing updates on localized defects while preserving reliable regions and avoiding topology drift.

title: Feature Space Guidance for Breast Cancer Classification in DCE-MRI
motivation: DCE-MRI classification of healthy, benign, and malignant breast cases is clinically valuable, but 4D high-dimensional inputs, tiny lesions, and protocol differences across centers make robust automation difficult. Fixed phase selection and maximum-intensity projections discard spatial or temporal information and remain vulnerable to protocol-specific biases, while case-level labels provide weak spatial supervision for lesion-focused learning.
method: The framework first localizes breast tissue and separates the breasts to reduce background uptake and compensate for deformable misalignment. It embeds each temporal DCE-MRI volume with a radiology foundation model, models relationships across phases, and adaptively selects informative latent features instead of using fixed phase selection. Large-scale supervised lesion-segmentation pretraining supplies anatomically discriminative representations before case-level classification fine-tuning.

title: FedAgree: Label-Free Performance Estimation Under Distribution Shift for Federated Medical Imaging Analysis
motivation: Federated medical models can suffer substantial performance loss at new hospitals because scanners, protocols, and patient populations differ, making OOD performance estimation important before deployment. Target-site labels are scarce or costly, while Agreement-on-the-Line requires multiple independently trained models, creating significant computational overhead. Federated learning already produces diverse client checkpoints that could provide this information more efficiently.
method: FedAgree reuses the diverse local and cross-client model checkpoints naturally produced during federated training for Agreement-on-the-Line-style OOD accuracy estimation. It defines five checkpoint-selection and combination strategies that progressively incorporate cross-client information, avoiding the need to train additional independent models. The approach is evaluated across multiple medical imaging modalities and both IID and non-IID federated settings.

title: FedCHDP: Federated Concept-Guided Dual-Modal Prompting for CHD Diagnosis
motivation: Early first-trimester CHD screening is clinically important, but fetal hearts are small and complex and ultrasound interpretation is subjective. Federated learning can enable privacy-preserving collaboration, yet generic CLIP prompt tuning faces semantic ambiguity, intra-class anatomical variation, and strong cross-hospital distribution shifts that cause local visual and textual prompts to overfit site-specific biases.
method: FedCHDP builds a federated medical concept library with fine-grained descriptors for chamber number, flow number, and flow pattern, and uses these concepts to construct instance-adaptive textual prompts alongside unconditional disease prompts. An uncertainty-aware gate fuses concept-conditioned and global-prior predictions. On the visual side, global-guided contrastive alignment pulls local visual embeddings toward shared disease prototypes and away from mismatched subtypes, reducing site-specific bias.

title: Federated Medical Image Segmentation under Modality Heterogeneity via Specialized Adapters
motivation: Federated medical segmentation often involves institutions using different modalities such as MRI and CT, and clients may be completely modality-disjoint. Aggregating modality-specific updates across such clients causes negative transfer and cross-modality interference, while existing federated segmentation methods generally assume homogeneous modality distributions and lack mechanisms for robust cross-modal generalization.
method: FedMoSA inserts modality-specialized and shared adapters into the SAM image encoder to separate modality-specific representations from modality-agnostic ones. It aggregates specialized adapters only among clients sharing a modality, while shared components use modality-balanced aggregation. Prototype-based alignment further encourages consistent shared-adapter representations across heterogeneous clients.

title: FedProIn: Mitigating Client Drift for Learnable Prototypes in Federated Medical Imaging

categories.value: AI for Neglected Diseases & Limited-Resource Settings

motivation: Statistical heterogeneity in federated medical imaging causes local models and representations to drift because scanners, protocols, populations, and disease prevalence differ. Parameter averaging and single mean prototypes may misalign high-dimensional semantics, inadequately represent multimodal class structure, and reduce inter-class separability. A method is needed to control both feature drift and prototype drift while aggregating informative prototypes.
method: FedProIn treats multiple learnable class prototypes as trainable global model parameters jointly optimized with a feature encoder. Feature divergence loss aligns local features with frozen global features, while prototype contrastive loss pulls local prototypes toward global prototypes and away from their previous local states. A normalized influence aggregation strategy weights client prototypes according to their contribution when forming the global multi-prototype representation.

title: FedSwitch: From Standard to Balanced Aggregation via Private Histogram Estimation in Federated Medical Image Classification
motivation: Medical federated classification often has strongly imbalanced label distributions across institutions, so FedAvg can favor prevalent conditions and underperform on rare pathologies. Distribution-aware aggregation needs global label statistics, but clients cannot safely disclose these counts; repeated differentially private releases under partial participation accumulate noise and privacy cost, making the estimate unusable.
method: FedSwitch privately estimates the global label histogram during a warm-up phase: clients bound their counts, add partial discrete Laplace noise, and secret-share the noisy values with Shamir’s scheme. A single reconstruction at an analytically selected switching round avoids repeated privacy composition. The recovered histogram then switches aggregation from FedAvg to inverse-frequency, distribution-aware weighting.

title: FermatSyn: SAM2-Enhanced Bidirectional Mamba with Isotropic Spiral Scanning for Multi-Modal Medical Image Synthesis

categories.value: AI for Neglected Diseases & Limited-Resource Settings

motivation: Multi-modal medical image synthesis can compensate for missing scans needed for clinical planning, but it must preserve both global anatomy and fine lesion texture. Existing GANs, diffusion models, ViT hybrids, and Mamba methods either distort long-range structure, incur high cost, lose high-frequency details during downsampling, or introduce directional artifacts through raster or rectangular-spiral scanning. Domain-aware anatomical priors and a more isotropic serialization strategy are therefore needed.
method: FermatSyn uses a frozen SAM2 Vision Transformer with LoRA+ fine-tuning to inject anatomical priors, together with a Hierarchical Residual Downsampling Module and Cross-scale Integration Network to preserve and fuse fine details with global features. Its Bidirectional Fermat Scan Mamba serializes feature maps along a continuity-constrained golden-angle Fermat spiral, using forward and backward state-space paths to provide near-isotropic long-range modeling and reduce directional artifacts.

title: FetalAgents: A Multi-Agent System for Fetal Ultrasound Image and Video Analysis
motivation: Fetal ultrasound is central to prenatal screening, but interpretation depends heavily on expert sonographers, and existing automated models are usually narrow, task-specific tools that fragment the clinical workflow. Real examinations also involve multiple anatomical planes and continuous video streams, while current systems provide limited coordination between classification, segmentation, biometry, and structured reporting. A comprehensive, workflow-aligned approach is needed to support end-to-end analysis.
method: FetalAgents uses a lightweight language-driven coordinator to interpret clinical intent, identify anatomical context, and dispatch tasks to specialized vision experts for diagnosis, measurement, and segmentation. For video examinations, an automatic keyframe module selects diagnostically relevant frames across anatomical planes; coordinated experts analyze them and combine the findings with patient metadata into a structured report. This creates an auditable workflow spanning static images and continuous ultrasound streams.

title: Fibers of Asymmetric Similarity: A Framework for Clinical and Imaging Data
motivation: Prenatal CHD screening must handle rare disease, variable ultrasound quality, incomplete risk factors, and uneven information across modalities. Standard symmetric distances and objectives do not reflect the greater cost of missing CHD or the directional nature of comparing rare pathology with normal cases. A similarity formulation that can explicitly balance missed and spurious findings is therefore needed.
method: The paper uses asymmetric Tversky prototype comparisons separately for structured clinical data and imaging rather than fusing modalities. For clinical variables, a composite objective combines prototype attraction, contrastive separation, and entropy-regularized soft assignment, with schema-aware and hypergraph encoders for independent and relational variables. For images, frozen encoder features are classified through asymmetric Tversky similarity fields against learned prototypes, allowing pretrained backbones to be used without fine-tuning.

title: Fine-Grained Cerebrovascular Parsing in DSA via Structurally-Grounded Semantic Disentanglement
motivation: DSA is essential for neurovascular diagnosis and intervention, where clinically meaningful decisions require distinguishing individual arterial segments rather than only extracting vessels. Existing automated approaches mainly perform binary segmentation, while 2D projection, vessel overlap, tortuous branching, and variable contrast make anatomical labels ambiguous. Automated topology-aware parsing is needed to reduce the manual, subjective identification of clinically distinct vessels.
method: AngioParse is a multi-expert framework for fine-grained DSA vessel parsing. Its dual-stream expert synergy combines a high-recall global binary vessel prior with fine-grained anatomical features. Structural grounding constrains the union of anatomical predictions to the binary vessel support, while decoupled orthogonal prediction branches reduce semantic confusion among vascular classes.

title: FlowReg: Reconstruction-Guided Flow Matching for Universal Spinal CT/X-Ray Registration
motivation: Spinal CT/X-ray registration for image-guided surgery requires both high accuracy and real-time speed. Optimization-based methods can be slow and depend on segmentation or landmarks, while direct learning-based pose regression is sensitive to initialization and local minima. Existing reconstruction-and-compare approaches are limited largely to single objects, leaving a need for a general framework that handles relative motion across multiple vertebrae and cross-modal differences.
method: FlowReg is an end-to-end CT/X-ray registration framework for both single- and multi-vertebra settings. A reconstruction branch recovers vertebral volume information from biplanar X-rays to provide a spatial prior, while a registration flow-matching branch learns deterministic SE(3)-aware pose gradients and shared inter-vertebral representations. Difference-Aware Feature Fusion aligns DRR and X-ray features, and the framework includes sim-to-real training.

title: FluxCut: Shifting from Global Reconstruction to Local Geometry for Unsupervised Small Lesion Segmentation
motivation: Small brain lesions are important for early diagnosis but are difficult to annotate and segment because they have weak contrast, subtle boundaries, and extreme voxel imbalance. Reconstruction-based unsupervised anomaly detection models global normality, so lesion residuals can be obscured by smoothing, misalignment noise, and domain shift. A method centered on local discriminative geometry is needed to preserve small-lesion signals without annotations.
method: FluxCut decomposes unsupervised small-lesion segmentation into localization and mask generation. A first-stage network learns boundary-aware representations with an adaptively weighted flux objective, producing a flux map that highlights lesion candidates. Frozen backbone features from flux-guided patches are then supplied to a graph-based segmentation head that optimizes an unsupervised correlation-clustering objective for boundary delineation.

title: FOCUS: Towards Fetal Obstetric Corrective UltraSound Guidance

categories.value: Multimodal Integration with Clinical / Genomic / Biomarkers

motivation: Obstetric ultrasound requires coordinated probe manipulation, machine settings, and adaptation to factors such as fetal motion and acoustic shadowing. Existing AI work commonly assesses image quality but does not identify when a trainee's technique is suboptimal or explain how to correct it. This limits its usefulness for training amid shortages of experienced sonographers and training resources.
method: FOCUS learns temporally grounded corrective guidance from trainee obstetric ultrasound videos and expert feedback. A dual-head visual framework separately models anatomical context and corrective instruction, producing semantic embeddings for feedback generation. Its lightweight transformer language module, CorLM, is conditioned on anatomy, corrective instruction, and visual embeddings to generate actionable comments.

title: Footprint-Guided Exemplar-Free Continual Histopathology Report Generation
motivation: WSI-based pathology report generation is usually trained in a static setting, although clinical deployment introduces new organs, institutions, and reporting conventions sequentially. Naive fine-tuning causes catastrophic forgetting, while storing slides, patch features, or growing domain-specific components can be costly or restricted by governance. A storage-efficient approach must retain both visual and linguistic knowledge while operating without reliable domain identifiers at inference.
method: The method performs exemplar-free continual WSI-to-report learning using compact per-domain footprints in a frozen patch-embedding space. Each footprint contains representative morphology tokens, slide-level co-occurrence summaries, and patch-count priors, which are used to synthesize pseudo-WSI representations for replay; an immediate teacher generates pseudo-reports for supervision. Per-domain report-style prototypes steer a lightweight style prefix, and the compatible footprint is inferred from slide content at test time.

title: Foundation Model-Driven Key Anatomy Frame Selection for Blind-Sweep Ultrasound Fetal Birth Weight Estimation

categories.value: AI for Neglected Diseases & Limited-Resource Settings

motivation: Accurate FBW estimation shortly before delivery is important for delivery planning and perinatal risk management, but conventional ultrasound estimation requires standardized planes and precise measurements by experienced operators.
