This dependence is especially problematic where sonography expertise is scarce. Blind-sweep ultrasound can reduce acquisition demands, but its noisy, redundant, unconstrained videos require identifying informative anatomical evidence for reliable regression.
method: This framework estimates FBW from blind-sweep ultrasound videos through hierarchical evidence selection and regression. Anatomy-Guided Frame Selection uses FetalCLIP image-text similarity and anatomical prompts to retain frames likely to contain relevant structures. Redundancy-Aware Feature Compression then refines selected frame representations, and a Prior-Guided Attention Regressor integrates them for birth-weight prediction.

title: FrameONE: Hierarchical Motion Modeling for Universal Multi-view Echocardiographic Keyframe Detection
motivation: ES and ED frames underpin echocardiographic measurements, but their visual anatomical definitions differ substantially across standard views, and manual identification is labor-intensive and variable. Existing deep-learning methods are largely view-specific, often require extra annotations, or use computationally intensive visual motion modeling. A unified model must exploit shared cardiac rhythm without confusing it with differing anatomy and motion directions across views.
method: FrameONE is a unified end-to-end model for ES and ED detection across multiple echocardiographic views. Its Hierarchical Motion Modeling first uses intra-view multi-task learning to disentangle motion from structural appearance within each view. Inter-view general motion learning then separates view-agnostic cardiac dynamics from view-specific motion patterns, enabling shared but flexible representations across views.

title: FreeBridge: Variational Schrödinger Bridges for Cellular Transition Dynamics
motivation: High-content imaging measures control and treated cells only as fixed endpoint populations, so individual cellular trajectories cannot be observed. Endpoint distribution alignment alone leaves intermediate dynamics underdetermined: multiple stochastic processes can connect the same marginals while passing through morphologies unsupported by data. Biologically interpretable perturbation modeling therefore needs explicit admissible cell states and geometry-constrained transitions.
method: FreeBridge represents segmented individual cells as atomic states in a fixed latent cellular manifold and models control-to-perturbation changes with a time-conditioned Schrödinger Bridge drift. An empirical latent-support regularizer constrains intermediate transport to regions supported by observed single-cell morphologies. This explicitly separates cellular state specification from stochastic transition learning under endpoint-only supervision.

title: Frequency and Geometry Guided Graph Clustering for Weakly Supervised Skin Lesion Segmentation
motivation: Pixel-level skin-lesion annotations are expensive and subjective, which restricts large-scale deployment of fully supervised segmentation. Image-level weak supervision reduces annotation burden, but CAM-based pseudo-masks tend to cover only discriminative lesion cores and miss complete structure. Local CNN constraints and downsampled graph propagation also inadequately capture global topology, spectral boundary cues, and fine lesion geometry.
method: FG3-Cluster reformulates weakly supervised skin-lesion segmentation as differentiable graph node clustering. Frequency-aware Feature Modulation injects local spectral priors into deep features, after which a semantic-spatial graph and GNN capture long-range structural dependencies. Tri-Source Refinement fuses graph clusters, CAM responses, and the input image using improved side-window mean filtering to align pseudo-masks with lesion boundaries.

title: Frequency-Aware Multi-Margin Loss for Imbalanced Medical Ordinal Classification
motivation: Medical ordinal classification models disease stages whose labels have an inherent progression order, but real medical datasets are often long-tailed. Fixed inter-stage margins assume uniform transitions and can compress representations of rare severe stages, while imbalance biases predictions toward head stages. An adaptive ordinal formulation and an evaluation metric sensitive to harmful tail-stage directional errors are therefore needed.
method: We propose Frequency-aware Multi-Margin Loss (FMML), which uses Boundary-Level Scaling to adapt inter-stage margins to transition sparsity and Anchor-Level Scaling to strengthen supervision for rare-stage anchors. These frequency-aware adjustments preserve global ordinal geometry while preventing compression of severe-stage representations. We also introduce Long-Tailed Rank Deviation (LTRD), a metric that measures rank errors together with class-frequency and directional bias.

title: Frequency-Aware Neural Architecture Search with Bidirectional Mamba for EEG Emotion Recognition
motivation: Cross-subject EEG emotion recognition is difficult because signals are noisy, non-stationary, and highly variable across subjects and frequency bands. Hand-designed backbones and shared architectures may not match the different temporal scales and information complexity of individual bands. Existing NAS methods also rarely search efficient long-sequence modules or node functionality together with topology, motivating a more flexible frequency-specific search framework.
method: We introduce a frequency-aware neural architecture search framework with cross-band fusion for cross-subject EEG emotion recognition. Each frequency band has an independently searchable directed acyclic graph, and the search space includes both graph topology and node-level temporal configurations. Bidirectional Mamba nodes model past and future context in offline EEG sequences, allowing band-specific architectures and efficient long-range temporal modeling.

title: Frequency-Aware Post-Training Quantization for Medical Image Denoising
motivation: Low-dose CT and X-ray imaging reduce radiation exposure but introduce noise and artifacts, while deep denoisers are often too computationally and memory intensive for constrained deployment. PTQ is practical because it avoids costly retraining, yet ultra-low precision causes substantial fidelity loss in medical denoising. Spatial-only calibration and architecture-specific statistical assumptions fail to address the concentration of errors in high-frequency subbands across diverse backbones.
method: We develop an architecture-agnostic dual-stage PTQ framework for medical image denoising using the stationary wavelet transform (SWT). Tensor-level calibration uses mixed-granularity initialization, while wavelet-guided output-level optimization explicitly penalizes quantization distortions in individual subbands, especially high-frequency components. The design targets ultra-low-bit deployment across CNN, ViT, and hybrid denoising backbones without retraining on full data.

title: Frequency-Aware Prototype Learning in VLM for Intracranial Aneurysm HR-VWI Segmentation
motivation: Intracranial aneurysm segmentation on HR-VWI is important for assessing wall enhancement and rupture risk, but aneurysms are small and their borders are obscured by weak contrast, imperfect blood suppression, and parent-vessel distraction. CNNs may blur fine boundaries under severe imbalance, while dense global attention can be dominated by background structures and frequency cues may be lost during aggregation. A method that preserves boundary frequencies and focuses interactions on lesion-relevant representations is needed.
method: We propose a frequency-aware VLM segmentation framework that applies discrete wavelet decomposition to multi-scale features and uses text-conditioned filtering to retain lesion-relevant high-frequency responses for query updates. Multi-scale features are summarized into foreground and context prototypes, enabling selective prototype-guided interactions that suppress parent-vessel and background distractions. Together, these components sharpen weak HR-VWI boundaries while handling extreme foreground sparsity.

title: From Baseline to Future CT: Large-Scale Diffusion Pretraining for Single-Scan IPF Progression Prediction
motivation: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis has heterogeneous progression, but routine longitudinal CT is sparse, irregular, and affected by acquisition differences and non-rigid deformation. Predicting a future scan from one baseline could support individualized trajectory analysis, yet existing progression methods may require multiple scans or generate at insufficient spatial resolution, and high-capacity 3D models are difficult to train on small IPF cohorts. Large thoracic screening repositories offer a way to learn a transferable prior before disease-specific adaptation.
method: We build a high-resolution 3D latent generative framework by first learning a detail-preserving patch-based autoencoding representation with overlap-average stitching. A covariate- and time-conditioned latent diffusion model with a longitudinal ControlNet is pretrained on more than 30,000 thoracic screening scans from over 12,000 patients, then adapted to IPF progression using lung-focused patch-decoded supervision. This separates a transferable thoracic generative/longitudinal prior from disease-specific adaptation while preserving volumetric lung detail.

title: From Exams to Trajectories: Neural Controlled Differential Equations for Longitudinal Mammography Vision-Language Pretraining
motivation: Longitudinal interpretation of mammography requires comparing irregularly timed multi-view exams and evolving reports to detect changes and assess risk. Most models analyze one exam at a time or use discrete temporal encodings, which are fragile to missing visits and long gaps, while vision-language methods generally ignore longitudinal context. A continuous-time multimodal approach is therefore needed to model patient trajectories and connect language with visual change.
method: Dynamo encodes each patient’s multi-view screening history as a continuous-time latent trajectory with a coarse-to-fine exam-level Neural CDE encoder, avoiding discrete positional assumptions for irregular visits. A Temporal Visual Question Answering loss performs query-driven masked-token prediction conditioned on this trajectory, aligning report language with evolving visual features. The framework jointly pretrains on mammograms and paired reports for temporally grounded downstream representations.

title: From Geometry to Clinic: A Physics-Aware Evaluation Framework and Benchmark for Automated Dental Crown Design
motivation: Automated dental crown design must produce restorations that function safely, yet current evaluations mainly use Chamfer or Hausdorff distance. Geometric similarity can miss occlusal interference, open proximal contacts, and poor marginal adaptation, creating a gap between model scores and clinical success. A physics-aware, clinically interpretable benchmark is needed to measure functional validity and reduce reliance on subjective inspection.
method: CrownBench reformulates automated crown evaluation around physical interactions with opposing and adjacent dentition rather than geometric resemblance alone. It defines clinically interpretable Feasibility Metrics for hard survival constraints and Quality Metrics, such as occlusal contact distribution, for personalized functional assessment. The benchmark compares state-of-the-art generators and validates metric rankings against blinded dentist judgments.

title: From Patches to Patients: A Study of the Tile-to-Slide Performance Transferability in Digital Pathology
motivation: Whole-slide image analysis requires extensive tissue tiling, feature extraction, and slide-level MIL training, making comparison of many foundation models costly. Tile-level benchmarks are efficient but may not reflect clinical slide performance, whereas slide-level benchmarks are closer to clinical use but computationally heavy. The study addresses whether tile-level rankings transfer reliably to slide-level outcomes and under what conditions.
method: The study benchmarks 19 pathology foundation models on 16 tile-level and 42 slide-level tasks. Tile representations are evaluated with linear probing, while slide predictions use Mean Pooling and ABMIL aggregators; Pearson, Spearman, and Kendall correlations quantify transferability. Sensitivity analyses examine cohort size and tiles per slide, and top-five overlap assesses whether tile results can shortlist encoders before expensive slide training.

title: From Perception to Anticipation: Forecasting Vessel–Instrument Interactions in Endoscopic Surgery under Unreliable Observations
motivation: Vessel injury during ESD can cause bleeding, but segmentation-based guidance only describes the current scene and cannot warn of an approaching interaction. Predicted masks are noisy, and a short observation window provides little temporal redundancy; moreover, touching and approaching depend on different portions of the sequence. A method must therefore estimate observation reliability separately from temporal reasoning and anticipate the next interaction state.
method: The framework first uses a cross-modal latent recovery module to enforce consistency between visual features and geometry derived from predicted vessel masks, forming a shared representation that limits noise propagation. A dual asynchronous memory separates transient recent dynamics from stable interaction prototypes through different admission and retrieval rules. Reliability-aware training supports category-specific temporal reasoning for heterogeneous interaction evidence.

title: From Point Estimates to Distributions: GMM Pooling for MIL in Preterm Birth Prediction
motivation: Preterm birth risk assessment commonly acquires multiple cervical ultrasound images, but image-based models often select only one image per patient. Standard MIL pooling further collapses the remaining instances into a point estimate, discarding view and acquisition variability that may contain predictive cues. A distribution-aware, permutation-invariant representation is needed to use all images under patient-level supervision.
method: The method treats each patient’s multiple TVUS images as a variable-sized MIL bag and extracts instance features with a shared encoder. GMM pooling estimates a joint feature distribution using soft component responsibilities and instance importance weights, then embeds it through log-density evaluations at learnable probe vectors. A U-Net backbone is jointly trained for cervical segmentation and bag-level prediction, providing anatomically informed features while the distributional pooling preserves within-patient variability.

title: From Scanning Guidelines to Action: A Robotic Ultrasound Agent with LLM-Based Reasoning
motivation: Free-hand ultrasound is operator dependent, while existing autonomous systems usually encode anatomy-specific rules or task-specific policies that transfer poorly across scanning objectives. Although LLMs could provide flexible high-level planning, prior robotic ultrasound work gives limited attention to the reasoning behind guideline execution and tool selection. A unified agent is needed to interpret diverse guidelines, adapt decisions to observations, and make its planning behavior more reliable.
method: The system uses an LLM agent to retrieve relevant steps from ultrasound handbooks, reason over observations and scan state, and dynamically call perception and control tools with parameters. This supports non-linear workflows such as repeating steps, changing strategies, or adjusting force according to image quality and anatomy instead of following fixed protocols. RL fine-tuning targets the agent’s reasoning and tool-selection behavior, with verbal tests on unseen guidelines and real robotic scans of the gallbladder, spine, and kidney.

title: From Sparsity to Geometry: Spatial Modeling for 3D Reconstruction from Biplanar Bone X-rays
motivation: Biplanar X-rays offer lower dose and cost than CT for 3D bone reconstruction, but the inverse problem is ill-posed and long-bone images contain large dark background regions. Existing work emphasizes larger datasets and stronger networks, with limited analysis of how spatial constraints affect sparse inputs; camera metadata can also be unavailable at inference. Explicit, consistent geometry is needed to stabilize reconstruction when planar structural cues are sparse.
method: ExpGS uses a fixed virtual AP/lateral biplanar configuration in normalized coordinates, removing the need for case-specific camera metadata at inference. Its non-degenerate rays define a consistent frustum-intersection volume that constrains reconstruction and suppresses background interference. The study compares explicit, canonical, and implicit spatial modeling under a shared training setup to isolate the effect of geometry, especially for sparse femur inputs.

title: From Trajectories to Phenotypes: Disease Progression as Structural Priors for Multi-organ Imaging Representation Learning

categories.value: AI for Neglected Diseases & Limited-Resource Settings
AI for Population Health, Public Health & Epidemiology

motivation: Imaging-derived phenotypes summarize multi-organ state but provide static snapshots, so IDP-only representations may miss temporal diagnosis patterns and comorbidity structure that characterize disease progression. Longitudinal EHRs contain such trajectories at population scale, while imaging cohorts may be limited. The work is motivated by using trajectory knowledge as a structural prior for more robust imaging representation learning and prediction.
method: A generative disease-trajectory Transformer trained on longitudinal diagnosis sequences produces subject-level embeddings that supervise an organ-wise IDP encoder through geometry-preserving representation alignment. The learned imaging representations can be combined with trajectory embeddings through cross-attention for downstream disease and time-to-onset prediction. This transfers population-scale progression structure into imaging features while retaining an optional multimodal fusion pathway.

title: FSE-Reg: Enhancing 3D Deformable Registration with Frozen Large-Scale Pre-trained Segmentation Encoders
motivation: Learning-based deformable registration needs robust correspondences but is vulnerable to limited training data, domain shifts, ambiguous intensities, and encoders trained from scratch. Segmentation-assisted methods can depend on label coverage and unreliable masks, while foundation features often require costly adaptation or iterative matching. A reusable anatomy-aware 3D feature space is needed to provide stable correspondence cues with lightweight feed-forward decoding.
method: FSE-Reg applies the same frozen, pretrained 3D segmentation encoder to moving and fixed images, producing shared multi-scale anatomy-aware pyramids for a coarse-to-fine residual deformation decoder. It adds a multi-scale cosine similarity constraint in frozen feature space, supplying correspondence cues without segmentation outputs or labels during registration. DPI-Fuse explicitly combines feature differences and products to refine flow updates while the frozen backbone improves data efficiency and cross-domain stability.

title: FunPiQ: A New Benchmark for Pixel-Level Quality Assessment in Fundus Images
motivation: Color fundus photographs often contain localized illumination, contrast, or visibility degradations, but existing FIQA datasets mainly provide image-level labels whose criteria vary by clinical task. Such labels are subjective and cannot quantitatively assess whether methods localize degraded regions, while post-hoc explanations are often imprecise. Pixel-level anatomical-visibility annotations and explainable-by-design learning are needed for task-agnostic, trustworthy quality assessment.
method: FunPiQ introduces a 300-image benchmark with expert pixel-level annotations describing local anatomical visibility and quality. EFIQA-CP uses a shallow CNN with a large receptive field to adapt features and trains with Non-Negative Positive-Unlabeled learning on anatomical-visibility quality pseudo-labels, reducing pseudo-label overfitting. The benchmark evaluates classification, anomaly detection, and explainable-by-design methods for both quality prediction and localization.

title: Fusion-E2Pulse: A Multimodal Event-RGB Fusion Network for Non-contact Pulse Wave Reconstruction
motivation: Non-contact pulse-wave reconstruction is needed for screening and monitoring when contact sensors are impractical, and waveform morphology provides information beyond heart rate, including vascular resistance and arterial stiffness. RGB cameras smooth subtle pulsations through their exposure integration, whereas event cameras are sensitive to these changes but vulnerable to motion-induced noise, leaving a gap between morphological fidelity and robustness.
method: Fusion-E2Pulse is a multimodal network that combines filtered RGB signals as stable structural priors with event streams that capture rapid intensity changes. RGB-guided fusion suppresses motion artifacts, while event information restores fine waveform morphology such as the dicrotic notch. The framework also uses time-frequency adversarial supervision with spectral and morphological objectives to promote faithful physiological reconstruction.

title: G3R: Gaussian-Based Geometry-Guided Reconstruction for Fetal Brain MRI
motivation: High-resolution 3D fetal brain MRI is important for prenatal diagnosis, but fetal motion, thick slices, inter-slice gaps, and limited orientation coverage make slice-to-volume reconstruction severely ill-posed. Existing implicit methods can be slow because of stochastic PSF sampling, while unconstrained 3D Gaussian Splatting may overfit projections by flattening or stretching primitives and produce distorted anatomy. An efficient reconstruction method therefore needs explicit structural guidance without sacrificing the speed advantage of Gaussian representations.
method: G3R first uses a pre-trained Density-Gated Prior Network (DGPN) with Density-Gated Refinement to construct a continuous geometric prior from motion-corrupted slices and inpaint acquisition gaps using a physics-derived density map. Gaussian primitives are initialized by fitting this prior, then refined against observed slices in a second stage. An annealed distillation constraint preserves the prior's global geometry while slice fitting recovers detailed anatomy, with Gaussian-PSF convolution evaluated through exact covariance addition.

title: Gabor Primitives for Accelerated Cardiac Cine MRI Reconstruction
motivation: Accelerated cardiac cine MRI must reconstruct high-resolution spatiotemporal images from undersampled k-space, where scan-time limits make the inverse problem ill-posed. Compressed sensing and learned models may rely on restrictive regularization, large training sets, or implicit parameters, while ordinary Gaussian primitives represent sharp boundaries inefficiently because their spectra remain near the k-space origin. A compact, interpretable representation that covers both low- and high-frequency anatomy is needed.
method: The method replaces each Gaussian with a complex-valued Gabor primitive whose complex-exponential modulation shifts its spectral support to an arbitrary k-space location, while zero frequency recovers the standard Gaussian. For cardiac cine dynamics, a two-component low-rank temporal model separates geometry changes from signal-intensity changes through dedicated bases. The primitives are rasterized, passed through a multicoil MRI forward model, and optimized directly against acquired k-space data.

title: GCM-Net: Anatomy-Aware Gaussian-Contrastive Multi-layer Fusion Network for Abdominal Ultrasound Standard Plane Classification
motivation: Standard-plane classification in abdominal ultrasound supports diagnosis and autonomous scanning, but low contrast, speckle noise, anatomical variation, and subtle differences between neighboring planes create substantial ambiguity and operator dependence. Existing models often have limited receptive fields, generic foundation-model features, or narrow single-organ coverage, so they may confuse morphologically similar planes. More anatomy-sensitive and discriminative representations are needed for comprehensive, reliable recognition.
method: GCM-Net adapts a pre-trained ViT with lightweight adapters and constructs a multi-scale feature pyramid. Its learnable multi-layer feature fusion module dynamically weights aligned hierarchical features, while adaptive anisotropic Gaussian refinement predicts a differentiable anatomical centroid and shape-specific spatial attention. A dual head jointly performs classification and memory-bank-based supervised contrastive learning, and temporal confidence refinement stabilizes predictions in ultrasound videos.

title: GeneRAG: A Retrieval-Augmented Framework for Spatially Resolved Gene Expression Prediction

categories.value: Multimodal Integration with Clinical / Genomic / Biomarkers

motivation: Predicting spatially resolved gene expression from H&E images could make molecular profiling more accessible, but cross-modal variability, sparse and noisy ST measurements, and black-box models limit reliability and clinical interpretability. Existing systems are often closed-set and cannot generalize to genes absent from training, while LLM and rigid retrieval approaches lack adequate morphological grounding. A flexible mechanism is needed to incorporate external reference knowledge and support unseen genes.
method: GeneRAG adds a model-agnostic retrieval stage around existing image-to-ST predictors. Its Dual-Constrained Retrieval module learns an Elastic Net sparse sampling matrix that balances morphological similarity and biological gene-expression constraints when selecting references from a pre-constructed bank. Final expression profiles are produced from weighted retrieved samples, decoupling stored knowledge from model parameters and enabling transparent rationales and prediction of unseen genes.

title: Generative Anchor-Guided Federated Domain Generalization for Heterogeneous Pan Cancer Image Analysis

categories.value: AI for Neglected Diseases & Limited-Resource Settings

motivation: Federated pathology learning preserves privacy across institutions, but standard methods assume a unified label space that is unrealistic when cancer centers use disjoint diagnostic categories. Aggregating gradients from conflicting local classifiers can cause negative transfer and overfit site-specific semantics, undermining generalization to unseen cancer domains. The challenge is to learn universal histomorphological geometry without shared class correspondences.
method: FedGMA performs federated domain generalization without requiring shared class labels. In generative anchor-based semantic decoupling, a shared hypernetwork maps semantic-agnostic latent prompts to client-specific geometric anchors, so feature alignment targets morphology rather than conflicting local label semantics. Geometric consistency regularization uses a memory bank of historical features as negatives to maintain compactness and separability when batches are small.

title: Gene-Selective Morphological Conditioning with Heteroscedastic Flow Matching for Spatial Transcriptomics
motivation: H&E-based spatial transcriptomics prediction must model how tissue morphology relates to expression, yet genes differ greatly in that coupling strength. Existing methods use one shared morphology representation, do not explicitly capture coordinated gene programs, and apply the same generation noise to all genes, even though tightly coupled genes should be more deterministic than variable ones. These gaps limit biological fidelity and calibrated generation.
method: The framework introduces gene binding modules that decompose image morphology into functional subspaces and let each gene selectively attend to relevant programs. Regulator tokens form a compact bottleneck that captures and redistributes coordinated information across genes. Heteroscedastic flow matching learns a separate uncertainty for each gene, emphasizing predictable genes during training and using near-deterministic or broader stochastic sampling according to that uncertainty at inference.

title: Genetically Aligned Patient Representations Improve Hematological Diagnosis

categories.value: Multimodal Integration with Clinical / Genomic / Biomarkers

motivation: Hematological diagnosis combines blood-cell morphology with cytogenetic and molecular findings, but most computational hematology models analyze morphology alone and therefore miss molecular heterogeneity. Single-cell blood-smear images are at the scale where morphology may reflect genetic alterations, yet paired multimodal datasets are scarce. A patient representation aligned with genetic information is needed to better match clinical diagnostic workflows.
method: GenBloom uses a two-stage patient-level training strategy. It first self-supervises a transformer aggregator with an iBOT head on single white blood cell images from more than 1,500 patients, then applies supervised contrastive learning on acute myeloid leukemia cases to align visual patient representations with karyotype abnormalities and targeted-panel mutations. The resulting encoder supports diagnostic prediction and retrieval of diseases or genetic alterations.

title: GeoCAN: Nonlinear Causal-Geometric Learning for Echocardiography Quality Assessment
motivation: Echocardiography quality assessment is affected by complex acquisition conditions and confounded degradations, so visual changes unrelated to quality can create spurious correlations. Moreover, aggregating relational interactions with local features entangles spatial-semantic structure and makes causal quality factors difficult to identify. Robust EQA requires explicit modeling of causal relationships and anatomical topology rather than relying on entangled Euclidean features.
method: GeoCAN introduces Causal-Geometric Learning to represent visual factors as nodes, estimate directed conditional interactions, and use hyperbolic geometry to separate quality-determining factors from confounding degradations. Nonlinear Relational Aggregation then integrates relational structure into quality features while explicitly disentangling it from local visual representations. Together these components model asymmetric causal dependencies and reduce spurious correlations and feature entanglement.

title: Geometric-to-Semantic Spherical Transfer Learning for Cortical Sulci Labeling
motivation: Exhaustive cortical sulci labeling is important for brain mapping and morphometry, but more than 60 nomenclature-dependent sulci per hemisphere exhibit strong inter-individual variability and include small, topologically ambiguous structures. Expert annotations are extremely scarce, while supervised surface models are data-hungry and often cover only a limited subset of sulci. The problem calls for transferring geometric knowledge from large unlabeled cohorts to the low-data semantic labeling task.
method: The framework pre-trains a spherical encoder on approximately 30,000 unlabeled UK Biobank subjects using locally optimized self-supervision on curvature and depth, encouraging sensitivity to intrinsic cortical topology. For sulcal labeling, extracted sulcal fundi are added as a semantic channel through a softly initialized Topological Prior Injector, which bridges the two-channel geometric pre-training input and the downstream semantic input while reducing catastrophic forgetting. A surface-native pipeline projects volumetric expert labels onto the spherical mesh for comprehensive labeling.

title: Geometry-Aware Manifold Trajectory Modeling for Task fMRI Activation Mapping
motivation: Task fMRI activation mapping localizes brain responses to controlled cognitive states. Conventional GLM analysis assumes a fixed, linear HRF, but BOLD responses can be nonlinear, state-dependent, and variable across regions and individuals; high-dimensional, noisy fMRI further complicates inference. Manifold trajectories may capture task dynamics more faithfully, yet their geometry has rarely been converted into a principled activation measure.
method: The framework embeds whole-brain fMRI frames on a learned low-dimensional manifold and models their temporal organization as a trajectory graph. It identifies a central baseline cluster, computes each frame's geodesic distance to that cluster, and uses the resulting task-engagement signal in the Manifold Geodesic-based Similarity (MGS) statistic to generate vertex-wise activation maps without HRF fitting.

title: Geometry-Aware Point-to-Voxel Fusion via Gaussian Splatting for Intracranial Aneurysm Segmentation
motivation: Accurate CTA segmentation of intracranial aneurysms is important because rupture can cause catastrophic subarachnoid hemorrhage. Small aneurysms often resemble normal tortuous vascular bends in intensity, so voxel-only models can produce false positives and lose fine boundaries, whereas point-based methods capture geometry but lack dense CTA context. A method is needed to combine explicit surface shape with spatially aligned image semantics.
method: GeoP2VNet extracts rotation-invariant surface descriptors from vessel point clouds with its Geometric Feature Extraction module. A differentiable Point-to-Voxel Gaussian splatting layer aligns and projects these sparse geometric cues into voxel features, and Dual-Gated Residual Fusion adaptively emphasizes useful geometric priors near anatomically important regions while suppressing them in normal vessel segments.

title: Geometry-Aware Self-supervised Learning for Whole-Heart 3D+t Representation
motivation: Whole-heart cine CMR contains complementary sparse SAX and LAX views over the cardiac cycle, but labels are scarce despite large unlabeled cohorts. Dense 3D+t self-supervision is costly, while simplified or concatenated multi-plane approaches discard information, rely on weak implicit alignment, and can solve reconstruction through local inpainting. Efficient representation learning must make cross-plane geometry explicit and learn coherent whole-heart structure from sparse views.
method: The method augments spatio-temporal cine-CMR tubelet tokens with DICOM-derived patient-space coordinates and encodes each sparse plane with a shared encoder. Voxel-query cross-attention aggregates plane features into a latent 3D volume, from which masked tubelets are reconstructed through coordinate-constrained trilinear reprojection. Hierarchical masking combines within-plane tubelet masking and whole-plane dropping to require cross-plane completion and encourage global 3D reasoning.

title: Geometry-Aware Superpixel Graph Transformer with Metadata for Skin Lesion Classification

categories.value: Multimodal Integration with Clinical / Genomic / Biomarkers

motivation: Dermoscopic lesion classification is difficult because lesions are heterogeneous and benign and malignant cases can differ only subtly. Global or patch-based CNN/ViT representations do not explicitly model lesion subregions and their spatial relations, while late metadata fusion cannot influence visual evidence aggregation. Spatially grounded region reasoning with integrated patient context is therefore needed.
method: GeoMeta-GT partitions deep CNN feature maps into SLIC superpixels and uses pooled frozen-CNN descriptors as graph node features. Region edges encode distance and orientation, while demographic and clinical metadata are projected into a dedicated context node connected to all regions. An edge-aware graph transformer, similarity-weighted refinement, and graph-level pooling perform geometry-grounded multimodal reasoning for benign-malignant classification.

title: GES-Net: A Gesture, Error, and Smoothness Aware Network for Surgical Skill Assessment
motivation: Automated RAS skill assessment is needed because expert video review and GEARS scoring are labor-intensive, inconsistent, and hard to scale. Existing video-based systems commonly predict only an opaque overall score, offering little actionable feedback and often lacking validation beyond simulation. Errors and motion smoothness are clinically relevant to skill but are insufficiently modeled in relation to scoring.
method: GES-Net jointly learns surgical gesture recognition, error detection, and skill assessment from RAS videos. It aligns visual features with gesture semantics through gated cross-attention and scheduled masked guidance, then uses multi-stage temporal reasoning to model gesture transitions. For assessment, soft error weighting focuses evaluation on error segments and jitter features quantify motion smoothness, enabling diagnostic feedback alongside skill scores.

title: GFR-MIL: Glance–Focus–Reflect Based Multiple Instance Learning for Multi-Scale Whole Slide Image Analysis
motivation: WSIs are gigapixel images with scarce pixel-level labels, making weakly supervised MIL necessary but computationally demanding. Efficient coarse-to-fine MIL selects high-resolution regions from low-resolution evidence, yet its one-way and often static Top-K selection cannot correct missed regions and discards information from unsampled tissue. WSI analysis needs bidirectional cross-scale reasoning that can revise global judgments using local diagnostic evidence.
method: GFR-MIL extracts low- and high-magnification WSI features and processes them through stacked Glance-Focus-Reflect blocks. Glance selects informative coarse regions, Focus examines corresponding high-resolution patches with spatial modeling, and Reflect feeds fine-grained evidence back to recalibrate global representations and later selections. A recycling token for unselected regions and memory masking preserve supervision and promote broader dynamic exploration.

title: GG-AE: Genetically-Guided Autoencoder for Disentangling Structural Networks of Brain Atrophy

categories.value: Multimodal Integration with Clinical / Genomic / Biomarkers

motivation: Neurodegenerative atrophy reflects overlapping effects of genetic susceptibility, environment, lifestyle, and other processes, so similar MRI patterns can have different causes. Unsupervised imaging models can entangle these sources, whereas association analyses miss network organization and symmetric multimodal fusion can obscure the biological genotype-to-phenotype pathway. A biologically constrained approach is needed to separate genetically driven atrophy from non-genetic variation.
method: GG-AE first trains a VAE to encode disease-associated SNP variation into a compact genetic latent representation. With that encoder fixed, a dual-latent imaging autoencoder separates voxel-wise MRI into a genetic-aligned subspace and a residual subspace, coupled by subject-level contrastive alignment. Its non-negative, softly orthogonal decoder produces additive, part-based spatial atrophy networks for interpretable decomposition.

title: GGFI-Net: Genomics-Guided Cross-Modal Imputation for Multimodal Survival Analysis with Missing Modality

categories.value: Multimodal Integration with Clinical / Genomic / Biomarkers

motivation: Multimodal survival prediction can capture complementary tumor phenotypes, but clinical datasets are often fragmented and lack one or more modalities. Heavy GAN or diffusion imputation is poorly suited to small, high-dimensional cohorts because it requires substantial data and can overfit. Missing-modality modeling therefore needs lightweight feature imputation that preserves prognostic information.
method: GGFI-Net trains a compact CT autoencoder and freezes its encoder to provide radiomic latent targets. Its Lightweight Cross-Modal Mapper maps genomics-derived pathway activity scores to CT-embedding-aligned auxiliary features for cases lacking CT. A genomics-only teacher transfers survival-relevant knowledge to the multimodal student through Genomics-Driven Survival Distillation, encouraging prognostic consistency of real and imputed radiomic representations.

title: Glasses: Adapter-Enhanced DINOv3 with Boundary-Aware Multi-Scale Representations for Medical Image Segmentation
motivation: Medical image segmentation must combine global semantic understanding with accurate local anatomy and boundaries, which are difficult in low-contrast images with blurred contours. ViTs and pretrained foundation models provide strong global semantics but often yield single-scale features with insufficient boundary-aware structural bias, especially when largely frozen to prevent overfitting. A stable adaptation mechanism is needed to add hierarchical local structure without disrupting pretrained representations.
method: Glasses keeps most of a pretrained DINOv3 backbone frozen and applies a Multi-Scale Deformable Attention Adapter to interact between convolutional structural priors and selected intermediate Transformer tokens. In parallel, an Edge-Aware Convolutional Encoder learns boundary-enriched multi-scale features under nested boundary supervision. A U-Net-style decoder progressively fuses both feature streams to produce high-resolution segmentation masks.

title: GLeVE: Graph-Guided Lesion Grounding with Proposal Verification in 3D CT
motivation: Grounding radiology report descriptions to lesions in 3D CT is needed for efficient, verifiable clinical interpretation, particularly when reports describe multiple organs and lesions. Existing global segmentation, report-supervised, and phrase-level grounding methods do not reliably establish one-to-one lesion correspondence or pixel-accurate localization, especially for small low-contrast lesions. The semantic-spatial gap between composite text descriptions and volumetric anatomy therefore remains a central challenge.
method: GLeVE represents each lesion description as an atomic semantic unit and applies relation-aware graph reasoning over organ attribution, lesion attributes, and inter-lesion relations to form lesion-wise queries. It combines these with organ-segmentation priors to generate anatomy-aware candidates, then verifies candidates at the region level to enforce one-to-one text-lesion correspondence. Octree-based autoregressive refinement progressively improves lesion boundaries for pixel-level grounding.

title: Global-Local Structure-Aware Alignment for Automated LGE MRI Report Generation
motivation: LGE MRI is the clinical standard for detecting myocardial scar and fibrosis, but slice-by-slice interpretation with cross-slice integration is time-consuming and operator-dependent. Existing volumetric report-generation methods mainly compress scans into global features and use global vision-language alignment, which can obscure subtle regional enhancement patterns and fail to capture structural continuity. Reliable automated reporting therefore requires structure-aware local and cross-slice reasoning.
method: GLSA-RG represents LGE volumes with structural graphs that model regional interactions within slices and continuity across slices, while organizing report descriptions as a standardized myocardial-segment graph. It jointly learns global volume-report alignment and fine-grained, graph-level cross-modal alignment, then optimizes these representations with report generation. This explicitly connects corresponding visual and textual structures while retaining global semantic context.

title: Good Enough? An Investigation on the Impact of Label Quality in Large-Scale Medical Datasets
motivation: Large medical segmentation datasets are increasingly built by refining automatically generated masks, but expert review remains costly and the resulting label quality is uncertain. Prior label-noise studies do not adequately reflect modern pseudo-labeling pipelines or distinguish direct deployment from pretraining. It is therefore necessary to determine when expensive label refinement materially affects segmentation performance.
method: The study creates realistic noisy-label variants of four abdominal segmentation datasets using predictions from nnU-Net, medical foundation models, and TotalSegmentator. It trains native 3D segmentation models on these pseudo-labeled datasets and evaluates both direct in-dataset use and pretraining followed by fine-tuning on an independent clean dataset. This isolates how pseudo-label quality affects the two common training workflows without changing the model architecture.

title: Graph Neural Networks for Morphometric Characterization of the Aortic Valve
motivation: Aortic-valve morphometry supports diagnosis and planning of procedures such as TAVR, but it commonly depends on localizing nadirs and commissures. Existing automated approaches primarily minimize landmark localization error, even though those errors propagate into clinically important distances and angles. Because morphometric measurements have anatomical and geometric dependencies, they need to be refined as related quantities rather than treated independently.
method: The method formulates 29 aortic-valve morphometric measurements as nodes in a graph, with edges encoding shared underlying anatomical landmarks and measurement dependencies. Measurements initially derived from landmark detection are used as node inputs to a GNN, which combines geometric features and structural context to refine them jointly. This directly optimizes anatomically consistent measurement values without modifying landmark detection.

title: Graph-of-Differences: Anatomy-Structured Difference Alignment for Medical Image Re-identification
motivation: Medical image re-identification supports longitudinal record linkage, cohort deduplication, and privacy auditing, but models can exploit shortcuts. Token-level feature differences may compare unrelated anatomy or imaging artifacts, while pixel saliency maps do not give stable, verifiable explanations in named anatomy. Clinically auditable re-identification requires identity comparisons grounded in homologous anatomical structures.
method: GoD represents each image as an anatomy graph whose named regional nodes are constructed with modality-specific parsers. For an image pair, it learns soft node correspondence, computes differences over matched regions, and aligns their graph-level difference with the global frozen-backbone difference. It provides explanations as attributions over named nodes and audits their faithfulness with node insertion and deletion tests.

title: Group Equivariant Diffusion for Anomaly Detection in Computational Cytology
motivation: In whole-slide cytology, diagnostically abnormal cells are rare, heterogeneous, and difficult to annotate, so anomaly detection trained on normal patches can help prioritize review. Unlike organ-centric images, single-cell diagnostic morphology is unchanged by rotations and flips, yet standard diffusion models treat transformed views differently. This produces orientation-dependent reconstructions and unstable anomaly rankings, which is problematic when only the top-K cells can be reviewed.
method: The proposed framework uses a D4-equivariant U-Net denoiser in a partial-diffusion anomaly detector, sharing parameters across rotated and reflected single-cell views. At inference, equivariant noise coupling and optional frame averaging encourage equivariant reconstruction trajectories and symmetrized pseudo-healthy reconstructions. Reconstruction-based anomaly scores are thereby made more consistent across D4 transformations.

title: Group-Conditioned Representation Modulation for Fair Skin Disease Diagnosis
motivation: Skin disease classifiers can exhibit persistent performance disparities across demographic groups such as skin type and sex. Conventional fairness methods often suppress sensitive-attribute signals, but skin type can encode clinically relevant disease prevalence and lesion morphology, so suppression may reduce diagnostic accuracy. Under a shared backbone, group objectives can also compete for representational capacity, motivating group-conditioned use of shared features.
method: GIM first analyzes a frozen pretrained shared backbone to compute group-conditional utility scores for convolutional channels from group-specific activation prototypes. It derives a binary mask for each group, then applies these masks during group-conditioned fine-tuning to suppress channels with weak or unstable group alignment. Backbone parameters and architecture remain shared, and the method adds no trainable parameters.

title: GTRE: A Physiological-Semantic Foundation Model for Generalizable EEG Analysis via Preference-Guided Alignment
motivation: EEG recordings differ across institutions in electrode configurations, hardware, annotation protocols, and patient populations, creating domain shifts that undermine single-source models. Existing self-supervised EEG methods often do not use the clinical narratives that encode diagnostic interpretation, and EEG-text alignment remains underexplored. Generalizable EEG analysis therefore needs representations that are both physiologically grounded and clinically semantically aligned.
method: GTRE uses graph-aware attention with 3D electrode topology and hierarchical temporal encoding of micro patches and macro windows to produce montage-agnostic EEG representations. In Stage 1, multi-domain grounding contrastively aligns EEG segments with clinical reports while using prototype-based regularization to reduce cross-dataset drift. In Stage 2, Masked-DPO trains on expert-validated preferred and less precise summaries, applying pathology-aware masking and a similarity-scaled margin to emphasize diagnostic content.

title: GU-SAM2: A Semi-supervised Medical Image Segmentation Framework via Gated Feature Fusion of MIM-Pretrained U-Net and SAM 2
motivation: Medical segmentation depends on scarce expert annotations, while conventional semi-supervised pseudo-labeling can reinforce errors in low-data settings. SAM 2 also has a natural-to-medical domain gap and treats 3D scans as video sequences, so its object-tracking behavior can cause semantic drift when an organ disappears across slices. A method is needed to exploit unlabeled medical data while adapting SAM 2 toward anatomically consistent segmentation without pseudo-label confirmation bias.
method: GU-SAM2 decouples data use into two stages. It first performs label-free masked image modeling on unlabeled medical images with a lightweight U-Net to learn medical texture and anatomical priors. Under labeled, prompt-guided supervision, a Gated Feature Fusion module then adaptively injects these features into SAM 2 to promote anatomy-based semantic matching across volumetric slices.

title: H2GT: Hub-enhanced Hierarchical Graph Transformer for Explainable Diagnosis of ASD with Functional Brain Networks
motivation: ASD diagnosis remains difficult because symptoms are heterogeneous and definitive biological markers are lacking. fMRI-derived functional brain networks can reveal altered connectivity, but GNNs tend to miss system-level module coordination and Transformers can overlook fine-grained intra-module topology. Existing methods also insufficiently exploit the established modular and hub organization needed for interpretable biological evidence.
method: H2GT incorporates functional-brain-network topology into a hierarchical Graph Transformer. A hub-prioritized attention mechanism encodes identified hub nodes as spatial attention biases, while dedicated components model within-module connectivity and coordination between modules. This multi-scale design yields node-, hub-, and module-level evidence for ASD diagnosis.

title: H2M-Net: Hierarchical Hyperbolic Memory Network for Pathological Report Generation
motivation: Pathology report generation from gigapixel WSIs must connect cellular morphology, regional histological patterns, and global diagnostic conclusions. Existing approaches generally model multi-scale features as flat Euclidean representations, which can distort tree-like hierarchical structure and weaken logical consistency across diagnostic levels. Report generation therefore needs a representation space and information flow that preserve local-to-global hierarchy.
method: H2M-Net embeds pathological image and report representations in the Lorentz hyperbolic space to model their hierarchical relations. A radial position loss and an entailment loss constrain parent-child geometric and semantic inclusion. Its bottom-up cascaded visual encoder, memory encoder, and text decoder progressively propagate information from local patches to global diagnostic text.

title: HadBalance: A Plug-and-Play Unified Global Geometric Prior Framework for Generalizable Biomedical Segmentation
motivation: Biomedical segmentation requires structurally consistent predictions, but existing boundary, shape, and topology priors are often task-specific and do not transfer well across organs or modalities. Many targets are globally near-convex, yet datasets also contain genuinely non-convex anatomy, so uniformly enforcing such a prior can erase valid concavities and fine details. A general geometric prior therefore needs conflict-aware integration with the segmentation objective.
method: HadBalance introduces Hadwiger Shape Priors, an interpretable global regularizer based on 2D area, perimeter, and Euler characteristic to encode near-convexity. Its Conflict-Aware Objective Balancing (CAOB) treats segmentation as the anchor, projects out only conflicting prior-gradient components, and adaptively balances the remaining contributions. This plug-and-play optimization preserves useful geometric constraints without suppressing genuine concavities.

title: Hallucination Detection and Correction in Medical VLMs via Counter-Evidence Verification
motivation: Medical VLMs can generate clinically inaccurate or fabricated descriptions unsupported by images, creating safety risks and reducing clinician trust. Existing detection methods emphasize text-reference consistency, uncertainty, or attention maps, but they do not rigorously test whether a specific assertion is grounded in its corresponding visual region. A traceable mechanism is needed to identify and mitigate visually ungrounded claims without retraining the VLM.
method: CoEV is a training-free, plug-and-play post-hoc framework that verifies generated claims against localized visual evidence. It selectively masks evidence regions as counterfactual probes and measures whether textual assertions change in a way consistent with visual support rather than linguistic priors. Bidirectional verification places statements in a Four-Quadrant Diagnostic Map, enabling hallucination detection and correction during inference.

title: HAM-BGT: Harmonic-Aware Multimodal Brain Graph Transformer for Brain Disease Diagnosis
motivation: Functional and structural brain networks provide complementary information for brain-disorder diagnosis, and structural connectivity constrains functional activity in the connectome-harmonic domain. Existing multimodal methods commonly concatenate features or fuse the two networks as independent graphs, overlooking this inherent coupling. Local message passing can also miss long-range interactions between brain regions.
method: HAM-BGT explicitly models structure-function coupling through connectome harmonics. A Spectral Graph Filtering-Based Harmonic Encoding injects structural-topology priors into functional connectivity representations, followed by multimodal graph Transformer layers for local and long-range regional interactions. A Harmonic-Aware Filter after each layer adaptively reorganizes regional features across frequency bands to extract coupling patterns relevant to diagnosis.

title: Harmless Copyright Protection for CT Dataset
motivation: Unauthorized use of medical datasets can expose sensitive patient information and infringe intellectual property. Backdoor watermarking can verify whether a model was trained on protected data, but conventional trigger-based verification deliberately causes abnormal outputs and thereby embeds a security vulnerability. Image-domain watermarks are also exposed after reconstruction and can be inspected, tampered with, or removed.
method: LMHBW learns a watermark mask in the CT measurement domain before reconstruction. Its optimization jointly enforces reconstruction consistency between clean and watermarked measurements and downstream verifiability through improved prediction accuracy on watermarked samples. The protected dataset is formed by injecting the learned watermark into a subset of training measurements, and ownership is verified from the accuracy difference between watermarked and clean samples.

title: HAR-MoE: Hierarchical Affinity-aware Routing Mixture-of-Experts for Unified Multi-Organ Ultrasound Analysis
motivation: Unified multi-organ ultrasound models must jointly handle dense pixel-level segmentation and sparse image-level classification, whose gradient dynamics differ substantially. In existing MoEs, dense segmentation gradients can dominate data-driven routing, causing expert dilution and negative transfer for classification. Flat routing also conflates task optimization requirements with organ-specific anatomical variation.
method: HAR-MoE replaces monolithic routing with a hierarchical two-stage MoE. A task-conditioned coarse router screens experts to separate dense-segmentation and sparse-classification optimization, then an organ-conditioned fine router specializes for anatomy. Learnable affinity priors stabilize routing and reserve expert capacity for sparse tasks while maintaining shared representations.

title: Harmonic Kernel Mixing for Interpretable Oculomotor Event Segmentation in Video-Nystagmography
motivation: Nystagmus slow-phase velocity (SPV) is essential for vestibular assessment, but extracting it requires reliable separation of slow phases, fast phases, and artifacts from VNG recordings. Manual and threshold-based pipelines are labor-intensive and sensitive to noise, drift, artifacts, and inter-subject variation, while many learning methods only output high-level labels. Oculomotor signals also contain non-stationary, cross-frequency structure that unconstrained or independently treated filters do not capture interpretably.
method: NyST-Net combines a Harmonic Kernel Mixing (HKM) spectral front-end with multi-scale temporal modeling to segment slow phase, fast phase, no nystagmus, and artifacts in VNG signals. HKM augments Sinc-parameterized band-pass filters with learnable coupling among harmonically related neighboring bands while retaining interpretable cutoff frequencies and coupling weights. Predicted slow-phase segments directly support continuous SPV reconstruction for downstream physiological assessment.

title: Harnessing Adversarial Distillation to Customise Debiased, Disease-Specific Pathology Foundation Models for Breast Cancer
motivation: General pathology foundation models are expensive to deploy and may retain site-specific acquisition signatures and disease-prevalence biases from pan-cancer, multi-centre pre-training. These confounders can drive shortcut learning and impair out-of-distribution generalization, while broad pre-training may underrepresent subtle breast-cancer morphology. Standard knowledge distillation compresses teachers but offers little control over transferring such bias into a disease-specific student.
method: SmartStu distils multiple large teacher PFMs into a lightweight breast-cancer-specific student backbone. It trains a noise model to predict nuisance, edge-dominated site-related cues and uses adversarial distillation to encourage the student to recognize but suppress features predictive of those nuisances. Multi-teacher ensemble distillation and an auxiliary self-supervised objective with artifact injection further improve robustness to acquisition variability.

title: HbO2 and HbR Spatiotemporal Heatmap Feature Fusion Network for ADHD Diagnosis in Children
motivation: Childhood ADHD involves nonlinear spatiotemporal hemodynamic abnormalities and persistent attentional instability, but existing fNIRS models often model space and time separately or only capture fragmented windows. Such approaches can miss transient localized anomalies and cumulative temporal deficits. They also commonly use single hemoglobin modalities or simple concatenation, neglecting the physiological HbO2-HbR coupling that may be disrupted in ADHD.
method: STHFFN converts discrete fNIRS channels into anatomically continuous spatiotemporal cortical heatmaps. Its parallel spatiotemporal attention jointly learns spatial co-activation and temporal hemodynamic evolution, while Bilateral Hemoglobin Complementarity uses cross-modal attention to model HbO2-HbR interactions. A memory pool aggregates long-range dynamics, and the resulting multimodal features are adaptively fused for ADHD prediction.

title: HD-TTA: Hypothesis-Driven Test-Time Adaptation for Safer Brain Tumor Segmentation
motivation: Brain tumor segmentation models can fail under scanner, protocol, or cohort shifts, producing missed tumors, false-positive islands, or boundary leakage. Standard TTA applies generic optimization broadly and can cause negative transfer by degrading already-correct masks or spilling tumor predictions into healthy tissue. Dice and recall can hide these safety-relevant errors, motivating selective adaptation focused on false positives and severe boundary deviations.
method: HD-TTA first produces a baseline mask and uses a Gatekeeper to skip refinement for confident cases. For selected cases, it generates parallel geometric hypotheses: compaction to remove noisy volumetric artifacts and inflation to recover potentially under-segmented tumor. An unsupervised representation-guided selector uses intrinsic texture consistency to choose the safest refined output, with the backbone frozen.

title: HeartFormer: Semantic-Aware Dual-Structure Transformers for 3D Four-Chamber Cardiac Point Cloud Reconstruction
motivation: Routine cine MRI provides sparse 2D slice observations, and inter-slice motion and misalignment limit accurate 3D reconstruction of cardiac anatomy. Existing methods largely focus on biventricular geometry and do not address coherent multi-class completion of atrial and ventricular structures. Four-chamber reconstruction must recover thin atrial walls, heterogeneous substructures, and tightly coupled spatial relationships from incomplete inputs.
method: HeartFormer is a semantic-aware dual-structure transformer for coarse-to-fine multi-class cardiac point-cloud completion. Semantic-Aware Global Structure Aggregation models overall cardiac topology, while Semantic-Aware Substructure Aggregation models chamber-specific priors; a two-stage refinement progressively improves geometric detail and anatomical consistency. It is embedded in an automated pipeline that converts segmented multi-view cine-MRI contours into sparse point clouds and reconstructs dense four-chamber surfaces.

title: HeartVolMesh: Cardiac Volumetric Mesh Reconstruction via Covariance-Guided Graph Deformation
motivation: Patient-specific tetrahedral cardiac meshes are needed for finite-element and computational-fluid-dynamics digital twins and scalable in-silico trials. Segmentation-then-meshing pipelines can blur thin-wall anatomy, require case-specific tetrahedralization, and produce inconsistent connectivity, while existing deformation methods usually reconstruct only surfaces and use deterministic Euclidean supervision. A method is needed that models local boundary uncertainty and directly yields topology-consistent volumetric meshes with cross-case correspondence.
method: HeartVolMesh represents each template surface vertex as an anisotropic Gaussian, predicting its displacement and a Cholesky-parameterized covariance with a 3D CNN-GNN. Covariance-aware negative log-likelihood supervision and lightweight mesh regularization model directional uncertainty while preserving graph-based topology. A fixed tetrahedral template is aligned, non-rigidly registered, and warped through a propagated deformation field, producing volumetric meshes with preserved connectivity and correspondence.

title: HEDS-Net: A Hybrid State-Space Architecture with Axial Bridge and Progressive Weighting for Medical Image Segmentation
motivation: Medical image segmentation must capture global context and precise local boundaries across lesions, polyps, and multi-organ CT structures. CNNs have limited long-range modeling, while global-context models can lose fine details; this tension is especially difficult for low-contrast, scale-varying, and anisotropic anatomy. A coordinated architecture is needed to balance semantic consistency, boundary preservation, cross-scale fusion, and stable optimization.
method: HEDS-Net is a U-shaped encoder-decoder whose HVST block combines a Visual State-Space branch for efficient long-range modeling with an ADCA branch for multi-scale local enhancement. Smooth progressive fusion shifts training from globally organized VSS features toward boundary-sensitive ADCA features. AXIS-Bridge performs decoder-conditioned and axis-wise skip refinement, while DS-Head supplies progressively weighted auxiliary supervision during training and uses only the main head at inference.

title: HemoPIC: A Physics-Informed Cerebral Hemodynamics Digital Twin for Brain Perfusion
motivation: Perfusion imaging is used to assess stroke and tumors, but routine CBF, CBV, and MTT quantification depends on manual arterial input function selection and deconvolution, which can introduce variability. Conventional pipelines produce static maps rather than an executable, mechanistic evolution of cerebral hemodynamics, limiting temporal prediction and intervention simulation. A routine-imaging-only approach is needed to infer physical states while directly producing clinically actionable indices.
method: HemoPIC formulates cerebral perfusion as a physics-informed inverse problem coupling tracer advection-diffusion with regional inflow-outflow dynamics and a two-element Windkessel model. It estimates patient-specific hemodynamic parameters and latent states directly from perfusion time series, using regional aggregation to avoid requiring subject-specific outlet conditions. The inferred dynamics generate CBF, CBV, and MTT maps while retaining an executable temporal digital twin.

title: Hepato-LLaVA: An Expert MLLM with Sparse Topo-Pack Attention for Hepatocellular Pathology Analysis on Whole Slide Images
motivation: HCC diagnosis relies on gigapixel WSIs whose heterogeneity makes manual interpretation labor-intensive and variable, especially for subtle lesions. Thumbnail processing loses patch-level details, while slide encoders may compress thousands of patches into redundant global tokens and usually lack multi-scale diagnostic capability. A pathology MLLM needs topology-aware, detail-preserving compression and clinically grounded supervision across resolutions.
method: Hepato-LLaVA is a pathology-specialized MLLM fine-tuned with LoRA through a unified multi-scale training pipeline. Sparse Topo-Pack Attention models 2D tissue topology, aggregates local diagnostic evidence into compact semantic tokens, and preserves global context while reducing redundancy; a lightweight connector bridges visual and language features. HepatoPathoVQA supplies expert-validated questions and answers at WSI, ROI, and patch scales to support hierarchical clinical reasoning.

title: HERO: Hypothesis-Driven Evidence Retrieval from Omics for Multi-task Breast Cancer Analysis

categories.value: Multimodal Integration with Clinical / Genomic / Biomarkers

motivation: Breast cancer analysis requires linking H&E WSI morphology with molecular biomarkers while providing an auditable trail of examined regions and supporting observations. MIL attention may select non-diagnostic areas under heterogeneity, VLM readers can favor visually salient regions, and multimodal fusion usually treats omics as parallel features rather than a retrieval constraint or completeness check. A method is needed to use observed omics as an explicit, testable hypothesis for endpoint-aware evidence retrieval.
method: HERO converts DNA methylation and miRNA through a sparse pathway-to-morphology prior into a K-dimensional intent vector and keyword set. TF-IDF retrieval over structured 10× captions selects endpoint-relevant WSI regions, and a cosine consistency gate compares the intent with retrieved visual evidence. When the gate detects a deficit, deterministic re-ranking performs one bounded repair round targeting under-supported morphology axes, making retrieval and verification lexically auditable.

title: Heterogeneity-Adaptive Diffusion Schrödinger Bridge for PET-Guided Whole-Body MRI Translation
motivation: Whole-body PET/MR acquisition is lengthy, motivating synthesis of time-consuming MR sequences from faster inputs. Whole-body anatomy has strongly heterogeneous, region-dependent distributions that challenge a single translation model, and lesions have complex cross-modality signals that can be biased toward dominant healthy tissue. Translation therefore needs explicit region conditioning and PET-guided mechanisms that preserve pathological fidelity.
method: HA-DSB models whole-body MR translation as stochastic transport between source and target distributions using a heterogeneity-adaptive Diffusion Schrödinger Bridge. Region context embeddings from body-location and organ descriptions condition the bridge dynamics, while a PET-guided noise modulation module spatially adapts forward corruption. During reverse denoising, multi-scale PET attention amplifies lesion-relevant structures, integrating metabolic prior information into pathological reconstruction.

title: HiEDL: Hierarchical Evidential Deep Learning for Uncertainty-Aware Tumor Segmentation from 3D CT via Boundary Regularization
motivation: Accurate CT tumor segmentation is difficult because lesions have low contrast and highly variable morphology, especially at organ-tumor boundaries. Deterministic Softmax models can be over-confident in these ambiguous regions, and flat classification ignores the anatomical containment relationship between tumors and organs. A reliable method should quantify uncertainty while using the hierarchy and local geometry to refine tumor boundaries.
method: HiEDL decouples tumor segmentation into a superordinate organ prediction and a subordinate tumor prediction, explicitly enforcing that tumors are contained within their organs. Evidential outputs represent predictive uncertainty in a single forward pass, while a hierarchical boundary loss based on signed distance maps regularizes ambiguous organ-tumor transitions. The combination targets both anatomical consistency and over-confident boundary errors.

title: Hierarchical Cautious Optimization for Semi-supervised Medical Image Segmentation
motivation: Semi-supervised volumetric segmentation uses abundant unlabeled images, but unlabeled gradients are noisy and less reliable than gradients from expert labels. Standard optimizers mix both sources symmetrically, which can amplify confirmation bias or destabilize the optimization trajectory. An optimizer should respect this reliability asymmetry while retaining the benefits of unlabeled supervision without changing the segmentation architecture.
method: HCO is an optimizer-level modification for momentum-based SSL training. It computes momentum solely from labeled gradients to establish a trusted descent direction, then admits unlabeled gradient components only when they align with that momentum. This source-aware gating lets unlabeled supervision reinforce labeled learning without allowing conflicting noisy updates, while remaining a drop-in method with negligible overhead.

title: Hierarchical Cross-Modal Fusion with Modality-Specific Training Paradigms for High-Precision Non-invasive Aging Assessment
motivation: Non-invasive aging assessment is clinically relevant, but unimodal imaging or behavior analysis cannot capture the interconnected structural and functional changes of aging. Existing cross-modal methods often concatenate features late and overlook hierarchical relationships and modality-specific characteristics, limiting complementary information. A clinically interpretable system needs coordinated ocular, behavioral, and gait signals with modality-aware training and progressive fusion.
method: The framework trains each modality with a specialized paradigm: progressive self-masked OCT/OCTA encoding, active-learning-enhanced behavioral syllable representation, and multi-stage gait quantization. Fusion proceeds from unimodal encoding to intra-ocular OCTA-OCT alignment and then inter-domain feature enhancement. An entropy-guided probabilistic weighting strategy combines peripheral structural features with central behavioral and gait outputs for aging prediction.

title: Hierarchical Disentangled Consistency Learning for Semi-supervised Multi-modal Medical Image Segmentation
motivation: Semi-supervised multi-modal segmentation must exploit unlabeled data despite heterogeneous modalities and unequal reliability. Existing methods impose prediction or representation consistency on entangled features, which can suppress modality-specific cues and prevent effective use of complementary information. A hierarchical strategy is needed to separate invariant and modality-specific semantics before applying consistency constraints at multiple levels.
method: HDCL first uses Disentangled Representation Learning to decompose each modality into shared and modality-specific features, aligning shared semantics while reducing shared-specific redundancy. Shared-Specific Dual-path Decoding generates predictions from shared, specific, and fused spaces through dual-path decoders. Multi-level Prediction Consistency Learning then imposes intra- and inter-space consistency on unlabeled data, exploiting complementary supervision without suppressing modality-specific cues.

title: Hierarchical Hyperbolic Self-Attention Network for Medical Image Segmentation
motivation: Medical image segmentation must preserve fine boundaries while modeling global anatomical context for disease monitoring and treatment planning. CNN-based U-Nets have limited global-context modeling, while many Transformer and Mamba variants operate in Euclidean space and use the same attention strategy at every depth. This can inadequately represent hierarchical anatomical patterns and the distinct local-versus-semantic roles of shallow and deep features.
method: H2SA-Net combines a wavelet-transform encoder with hyperbolic feature learning for medical image segmentation. Its depth-adaptive Hyperbolic Self-Attention applies pixel-wise attention to shallow features for local spatial refinement and channel-wise attention to deep features for global semantic recalibration, using the Einstein Midpoint for aggregation. A hyperbolic MLR head performs geometry-consistent per-pixel classification.

title: Hierarchical Memory for Radiology Report Generation with Rich Context
motivation: Radiology report generation benefits from both similar reports from other patients and a patient's longitudinal history. Cross-patient evidence can aid rare findings, whereas longitudinal evidence captures patient-specific changes but can encourage copying prior statements. Existing systems often concatenate these noisy, partially relevant sources into long prompts, leaving the decoder to perform unreliable implicit evidence selection.
method: HM-RRG organizes cross-patient retrieved reports and within-patient longitudinal reports as a hierarchical, image-conditioned memory instead of one flat prompt. It compresses each retrieved report into a compact memory vector, maintains chronological segment-level memories for prior reports, and hierarchically retrieves from both memory sources during segment-wise decoding. This selective evidence prompt is intended to prioritize relevant clinical information and suppress noisy or conflicting context.

title: Hierarchical Multi-Video Multiple Instance Learning: AI-Interpreted Point-of-Care Ultrasound for TB Detection

categories.value: AI for Neglected Diseases & Limited-Resource Settings
AI for Population Health, Public Health & Epidemiology

motivation: TB imposes a major burden in low-resource settings, where sputum tests, NAATs, and chest radiography have sensitivity, infrastructure, or cost limitations. Portable POCUS could support frontline screening, but TB evidence in raw lung ultrasound is sparse and distributed across frames and bilateral lung zones. Existing AI systems commonly assess individual videos or curated keyframes, which does not match routine multi-video acquisition or yield patient-level integration.
method: HMV-MIL formulates TB detection from routine multi-site lung ultrasound as hierarchical multi-video multiple-instance learning. Attention pooling first identifies informative frames within each video, then gated MIL aggregates site-level video embeddings into a patient-level representation. Auxiliary supervision from human-interpretable pulmonary pathology findings regularizes the learned features toward recognizable ultrasound patterns.

title: Hierarchical Region-Aware Multi-Granularity Mamba for White Matter Lesion Segmentation
motivation: WMH and MS lesions on FLAIR MRI are small, scattered, low-contrast, and often have indistinct boundaries, making accurate delineation difficult. Medical SAM variants can lose fine local detail because of large tokens, while attention-based fusion is costly and may not propagate subtle contextual cues. Existing SAM-Mamba approaches also use causal scan orders that are poorly aligned with non-causal image structure and weaken distant clinically related cues.
method: HiRAM is integrated into a SAM-CNN hybrid decoder for WM lesion segmentation. A region-tailored prior generator decomposes fused features into interior, boundary, and background representations, and multi-granularity Mamba performs region-specific confidence-driven, non-causal state-space propagation before holistic context propagation. Region-Awareness Enhancement blocks retain SAM token-feature interactions while refining complementary CNN and SAM features with HiRAM.

title: Hierarchical Text-Guided Brain Tumor Segmentation via Sub-Region-Aware Prompts
motivation: Brain tumor sub-regions WT, TC, and ET often have ambiguous visual boundaries, although radiology text provides clinically relevant cues about edema, necrosis, and enhancement. Current multimodal methods commonly use one global report embedding and one shared output head. This overlooks sub-region-specific language and the anatomical nesting relation ET⊂TC⊂WT, potentially producing inconsistent masks.
method: TextSCP uses a text-modulated soft cascade decoder that predicts WT, then TC, then ET, with coarser soft spatial priors guiding finer sub-region predictions. Distinct learnable soft prompts steer a shared LoRA-adapted BioBERT encoder to create specialized text representations for each sub-region. Text-semantic channel modulators convert those representations into squeeze-and-excitation-style channel refinements in their corresponding decoder branches.

title: HiFi-Rep: Leveraging High-Resolution Vision Foundation Models with Tri-Planar Slice Context for CT Report Generation
motivation: Generating radiology reports from 3D CT requires both whole-volume understanding and retention of subtle findings across hundreds of slices.
