Native 3D encoders are computationally expensive, while existing 3D and slice-based methods often downsample images or omit views to control memory and sequence length. Such compression can remove fine diagnostic anatomy and leave generic language models insufficiently grounded in clinical terminology.
method: HiFi-Rep extracts dense features from native 512×512 axial, coronal, and sagittal CT slices with a frozen DINOv3 backbone. Its parameter-free HiFi-S2D module applies inter-slice mean pooling followed by Space-to-Depth transformation, condensing volumetric tokens while retaining in-plane spatial detail in channels. A specialized medical LLM, MedGemma, generates reports from the tri-planar features with interleaved textual instructions for multi-view spatial alignment.

title: Hi-FL: Hierarchical Federated Learning Adaptation of Vision-Language Models for Multi-Institutional Surgical Phase Recognition
motivation: Surgical phase recognition supports context-aware intraoperative assistance, but privacy regulations prevent centralized use of heterogeneous surgical video data. Institutions differ in hardware, instruments, platforms, and workflows, creating domain shifts. Existing surgical VLM adaptation and standard federated optimization treat phases as flat categories and mix universal procedural semantics with center-specific noise, leading to semantic drift.
method: Hi-FL adapts surgical VLMs in federated settings through a Hierarchical Adaptation wrapper that separates procedure-level global context, phase-level dynamics, and action-level frame cues. It also introduces class-conditional Targeted Alignment and Repulsion loss to align local representations with global class semantics while repelling cross-institutional interference. The framework is designed to retain shared procedural logic while adapting to center-specific variation without centralizing data.

title: High-Capacity Robust Medical Image Exfiltration via Neural Network Weight Replacement
motivation: Collaborative medical AI platforms may prohibit raw-image export but allow validated trained models to leave the secure environment, creating an insider exfiltration channel through model weights. Lightweight sanitization such as fine-tuning, pruning, and quantization may preserve model utility while providing limited auditing. Prior task-based and bit-level hiding attacks respectively lack robustness or are highly sensitive to small weight perturbations, limiting compatible high-capacity image leakage.
method: The work presents a continuous neural-steganography attack that compresses medical images into 512-dimensional latent codes using a StyleGAN2-based adversarial autoencoder. The codes are trained with noise injection for perturbation robustness and distributional regularization to match Kaiming initialization statistics, then replace selected high-variance weights in a conventional medical model before normal task training. After export and possible mitigation, the attacker extracts the weight segments and reconstructs images with the pretrained generator.

title: High-Frequency Guided Feature Refinement for Semi-supervised Ultrasound Image Segmentation
motivation: Semi-supervised ultrasound segmentation has limited labels and must balance semantic localization against accurate boundaries under speckle noise and low tissue contrast. DINOv3 provides strong global semantics but abstracts away fine spatial detail, degrading pseudo-label boundaries. Existing feature-agnostic upsampling can use noisy raw images as guidance, leading to over-smoothed predictions and unreliable pseudo-labels.
method: HG-SemiSeg combines a frozen DINOv3 encoder with AnyUp and a High-Frequency Component Enhancement module for semi-supervised ultrasound segmentation. HFCE uses DWT spectral decomposition to isolate high-frequency components, then adaptively amplifies structurally meaningful edge detail while suppressing non-semantic noise. These refined cues guide feature upsampling so the teacher produces more boundary-consistent pseudo-labels for student supervision.

title: HiLoGraph: Hierarchical-Longitudinal Brain Network Representation Learning

categories.value: AI for Neglected Diseases & Limited-Resource Settings

motivation: Longitudinal brain MRI can reveal within-subject aging change and provide a healthy reference for detecting pathological deviations. Classical normative models often treat voxels or regions independently, while graph methods preserve connectivity but usually use only cross-sectional, single-scale data. Existing longitudinal self-supervised methods operate on image volumes and may train on mixed healthy and diseased cohorts, which can obscure normative aging patterns.
method: HiLoGraph constructs atlas-level ROI and fine-grained 3HG brain graphs from morphological features and structural connectivity. A hierarchical graph encoder fuses both scales through cross-scale message passing into a shared latent space, while a top-down decoder reconstructs ROI features to enforce cross-scale consistency. Trajectory-smoothness and contrastive-ordering losses constrain repeated healthy-subject visits, yielding a normative latent reference whose subject-level deviations can support clinical classification.

title: HiPath: Hierarchical Vision-Language Alignment for Structured Pathology Report Prediction
motivation: Pathology reports combine primary diagnosis, histological grade, and immunohistochemistry findings across anatomical sites, but existing pathology VLMs generally produce flat labels or unconstrained text. These formats do not ensure slot consistency or expose safety-critical field-specific errors, and most models are trained only on English data despite demand for structured Chinese reporting. A model explicitly trained and evaluated for structured, slot-level diagnosis prediction is therefore needed.
method: HiPath uses frozen UNI2 and Qwen3 backbones with three trainable modules totaling 15M parameters. The Hierarchical Patch Aggregator combines evidence from multiple images, Hierarchical Contrastive Learning aligns image and text at segment and case levels using optimal transport, and Slot-based Masked Diagnosis Prediction generates typed diagnostic slots from a closed vocabulary. Free-text reports supervise training, while inference uses visual features and frozen vocabulary embeddings.

title: HiProS: A Hierarchical Prompt Selection for Stage-wise Vision–Language Alignment in Medical Image Segmentation

categories.value: Multimodal Integration with Clinical / Genomic / Biomarkers

motivation: Medical image segmentation benefits from diagnostic text, but existing vision-language methods usually propagate the same textual representation through every decoder stage. This ignores the hierarchy from fine-grained morphological Findings to global Impressions, causing local and global semantics to be misaligned, especially for diffuse lesions. Manual clinical reports are also difficult to obtain at scale, motivating stage-specific alignment with automatically generated text.
method: HiProS generates structured Findings and Impressions text automatically with a VLM and encodes the two report components as token embeddings. At each decoder stage, a Stage-wise Prompt Selector assigns the appropriate component and uses a learnable threshold to select relevant tokens while suppressing others. A Fusion Alignment Module then integrates the selected tokens with multi-scale visual features for progressive mask prediction.

title: HK-Fuse: Hilbert-Interleaved Kimi Delta Attention for Incomplete-Modality Brain Tumor Segmentation
motivation: Multimodal MRI provides complementary information for brain tumor subregions, yet clinical scans often lack one or more sequences. Existing incomplete-modality fusion methods flatten 3D features into 1D sequences, weakening spatial structure, and commonly use zero tokens for missing modalities, making fused representations information-sparse. These issues particularly harm small subregion segmentation and call for spatially preserving, selective fusion.
method: HK-Fuse arranges multimodal 3D features with a fixed-slot, modality-interleaved order produced by 3D Hilbert scanning, preserving spatial locality during long-range interaction. Its Hilbert-Interleaved Kimi fusion block applies bidirectional Kimi Delta Attention to selectively aggregate cross-modal context while reducing the influence of zero-filled missing modalities. Key-Voxel Routing further selects top informative voxels in high-resolution skip features for sparse cross-modal interaction.

title: HomoSeg: A Weak-Label-Guided Semi-supervised Framework for Tumor Microenvironment Segmentation

categories.value: AI for Neglected Diseases & Limited-Resource Settings

motivation: Tumor microenvironment segmentation is important for cancer diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment, but pixel-level labeling of gigapixel slides is expensive and requires specialized expertise. Weakly supervised CAM methods often localize only the most discriminative regions and produce imprecise boundaries, whereas semi-supervised segmentation usually still requires pixel annotations. A framework that retains stronger boundary supervision while using only weak labels is needed.
method: HomoSeg uses histological spatial homogeneity to identify single-label samples and applies superpixel segmentation to synthesize samples with dense, reliable pixel labels. A multi-task Siamese network jointly performs classification, segmentation, and CAM prediction, while weak-to-strong consistency transfers supervision from synthetic samples to unlabeled data. Offline distillation then removes noise from synthetic supervision and produces a lighter model.

title: HoughSAM: Geometry-Guided Zero-Shot Segmentation of Main Incision in Cataract Surgery Using SAM2 for Skill Assessment
motivation: The geometry of the main cataract incision is a clinically meaningful, context-specific indicator of surgical skill, but existing skill assessment is often global or indirect. The incision is a transient, irregular tool-tissue interaction that is difficult to segment under changing viewpoints and lighting, and no public pixel-level wound dataset is available for supervised training. An interpretable, annotation-efficient method is therefore needed to measure wound geometry directly from surgical video.
method: HoughSAM processes cataract video frames with edge detection and the Hough transform to detect circular pupil and limbus structures. Points sampled from these regions prompt SAM2 to segment the anatomical masks; because the incision disrupts these masks, convex completion and mask subtraction isolate the transient wound region. Geometry features from the wound mask are then used to estimate incision architecture and size without task-specific training or finetuning.

title: How Good Are Foundation Models in Longitudinal MRI Disease Progression Reasoning?
motivation: Longitudinal MRI interpretation requires comparing multiple anatomical views across time, locating interval changes, and judging disease progression. Existing vision-language benchmarks largely analyze isolated single-timepoint images and lack structured localization guidance, while models show failures in temporal change direction and spatial precision. A benchmark that evaluates integrated temporal-spatial reasoning across clinical follow-up scans is needed.
method: The Time-Aware Multi-View MRI Benchmark harmonizes longitudinal scans from seven clinical cohorts and provides multi-sequence images across axial, coronal, and sagittal views with temporal metadata. It defines open-ended, multiple-choice, and binary questions covering temporal reasoning, progression, sequence ordering, change localization, and structured guidance about boundaries, imaging features, and confounders. Expert-guided question generation and verification support systematic evaluation of 17 VLMs on integrated temporal-spatial reasoning.

title: Human-AI Collaboration for 2D/3D Registration Quality Assurance
motivation: 2D/3D registration supports image-guided surgery, but millimeter-scale misalignments can cause serious navigation and implant-placement errors. Visual inspection alone is insufficient for reliably detecting such failures, and increasingly automated systems require human operators to understand and verify algorithmic outputs. Decision support with explainability is needed to improve safety-critical quality assurance and user understanding.
method: The study integrates a learning-based 2D/3D registration quality-assessment model into a human decision workflow and provides optional explainable-AI evidence for its predictions. Eighteen participants reviewed registration correctness under Human-only, Human+AI, and Human+XAI conditions. Objective measures and subjective workload, trust, and understanding were compared across these collaboration settings.

title: Human-In-The-Loop Multi-agent Ventilator Decision Support with Contextual Bandit Preference Learning
motivation: Ventilator management requires repeated adjustments as physiology and disease trajectories evolve, while clinicians differ in risk tolerance and tuning preferences. Fixed rules do not generalize well to heterogeneous, nonstationary ICU states, and end-to-end reinforcement learning or single-model systems are difficult to control, audit, and integrate into workflow. Clinicians therefore need decision support that is safe, traceable, personalized, and able to adapt through repeated interaction.
method: VDSS decomposes ventilator titration into role-specific agents for detection, phase-goal inference, hold/adjust gating, strategy and mode selection, parameter planning, safety checking, and feedback-driven revision. Contract-governed structured interfaces, layered short- and long-term memory, and deterministic compatibility checks provide traceable multi-round recommendations. A contextual bandit updates clinician-specific preferences from each accepted decision, while structured rejection feedback directs targeted replanning.

title: Hybrid Transformer-Mamba for Weakly Supervised Volumetric Medical Segmentation
motivation: Volumetric CT and MRI segmentation normally needs costly voxel labels, so weakly supervised methods use slice-level labels but lack localization information. Most such methods rely on 2D encoders and overlook relationships across neighboring planes, while direct cross-plane self-attention is computationally quadratic in the number of planes. Efficient modeling of cross-plane context is needed to improve localization without losing tractable complexity.
method: TranSamba inserts a Cross-Plane Mamba block before a Transformer block at every encoder layer. Patch tokens from neighboring planes are reshaped into one sequence for linear-time Mamba interaction, then restored to per-plane sequences for parallel in-plane self-attention and class-to-patch attention maps. The resulting hybrid architecture transfers volumetric context to localization while keeping time complexity linear and batch space complexity constant in volume depth.

title: Hyperbolic Contrastive Learning with Entailment for Spatial Transcriptomics
motivation: Spatial transcriptomics provides spatially resolved gene expression but is costly, equipment-intensive, and sensitive to experimental noise, motivating prediction from histopathology images. Existing image-based methods often produce over-smoothed, overly uniform expression and mainly use Euclidean representations, which do not explicitly capture hierarchical and asymmetric relationships between gene regulation and tissue morphology. A biologically structured representation is needed to improve multimodal alignment and expression prediction.
method: HyCLoST encodes histopathology patches and paired gene-expression vectors with pretrained UNI2-h and Geneformer, then projects both modalities into a shared hyperbolic space. Hyperbolic contrastive learning models hierarchical relationships, while a directional gene-to-image entailment loss reflects the asymmetric link in which molecular profiles give rise to tissue morphology. At inference, image embeddings retrieve nearby gene embeddings to predict expression, and evaluation is standardized across the SpaRED benchmark.

title: Hyperbolic Vision-Language Interaction for Semi-supervised Medical Image Segmentation
motivation: Semi-supervised medical image segmentation seeks to exploit abundant unlabeled data while reducing the burden of expert pixel annotations, but existing pseudo-labeling and consistency methods rely mainly on visual cues. Vision-language segmentation methods add textual guidance yet usually operate in Euclidean space, which distorts the tree-like hierarchical structure of anatomical concepts. A geometry-aware framework is therefore needed to represent anatomical hierarchies and use textual information without amplifying pseudo-label errors.
method: HyperSemi projects visual features and text embeddings into the Poincaré ball through a Hyperbolic Semantic Embedding module to align cross-modal representations with anatomical hierarchies. A Geometry-aware Semantic Integration module uses hyperbolic distance weighting and tangent-space aggregation to inject textual semantics into encoder features. An Uncertainty-aware Region Mixing strategy identifies high-uncertainty regions from dual-network discrepancies and applies mixed supervision to reduce pseudo-label confirmation bias.

title: HyperVLP: Enhancing Hierarchical Surgical Video-Language Pre-training in Hyperbolic Space
motivation: Surgical phase recognition must interpret procedural progression, but supervised systems require dense labels and often generalize poorly across institutions and unseen procedures. Existing surgical video-language pre-training embeds phases, steps, and actions in flat Euclidean spaces, weakening parent-child dependencies, while treating all nonmatching pairs as negatives can push clinically related segments apart. A representation and training objective that preserve workflow hierarchy and avoid these structural false negatives is needed.
method: HyperVLP maps video and text representations into a shared Lorentz hyperbolic manifold to encode hierarchical containment in surgical workflows. Its geometry-aware contrastive loss downweights semantically related samples within the same procedural context, reducing structural false negatives. A cone-based hyperbolic entailment objective enforces parent-child relations across and within modalities, while progressive two-stage optimization first learns alignment and then refines hierarchical containment.

title: HypOProto: Hyperbolic Ordinal Prototypes for Left Ventricular Filling Pressure Classification
motivation: LVFP is an important marker for cardiac disease, but the usual Doppler-derived E/e’ measurement is operator-dependent and may be unavailable in resource-limited settings, motivating inference from accessible B-mode echocardiography. Existing deep learning approaches for echo are largely black boxes, and interpretable prototype methods have not targeted LVFP. Because LVFP is ordinal with ambiguous cases around the clinical threshold, a transparent model that represents this ordered uncertainty is needed.
method: HypOProto uses a frozen, explainable patch-based foundation-model backbone and maps representations into hyperbolic space for prototype classification. Prototypes are ordered along the physiological E/e’ scale: borderline cases near the diagnostic threshold are placed near the hyperboloid root, while more certain cases lie farther outward. The Hyperbolic Prototype Angular Separation loss encourages discriminative prototype directions and supports interpretable case-based predictions.

title: I²-Med: Interpretable Medical Inference Through Visual-Guided Dynamic Logits Calibration

categories.value: Multimodal Integration with Clinical / Genomic / Biomarkers
AI for Neglected Diseases & Limited-Resource Settings

motivation: Medical vision-language models can describe images and reason in language, but their explanations may lack transparent grounding and contain visual hallucinations that are dangerous in clinical use. Supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning can improve terminology or textual reasoning structure, yet they do not explicitly verify each generated token against the medical image. Inference therefore needs a mechanism that enforces visual faithfulness while preserving the model’s reasoning ability without costly retraining.
method: I²-Med combines GRPO-based structured reasoning with a training-free inference mechanism called MedCalib-IF. During decoding, BiomedCLIP evaluates image-text consistency for candidate tokens, and Dynamic Logits Calibration modulates their scores to favor visually supported words and suppress hallucinated details. The approach changes generation behavior without updating the large model parameters.

title: IAVS: A Multi-center Dataset and Applicability Evaluation System for Computational Fluid Dynamics-Oriented Intracranial Aneurysm Segmentation
motivation: Accurate segmentation of intracranial aneurysms and parent vessels is needed for CFD-based hemodynamic and rupture-risk analysis, but manual delineation is laborious. Existing datasets and evaluation metrics emphasize voxel overlap and often lack refined vessel annotations, geometric validation, and CFD records; Dice can miss adhesions or surface defects that break mesh generation or distort flow. A multi-center resource and application-oriented evaluation are needed to connect segmentation quality with downstream CFD usability.
method: IAVS curates a multi-center dataset of 3D MRA scans with expert aneurysm and parent-vessel annotations, together with STL geometries, centerlines, meshes, and CFD outcomes. Its standardized pipeline checks topology, preprocesses morphology, converts masks into geometric and mesh models, and performs CFD computation. The CFD-Applicability Score summarizes whether a segmentation can support clinically usable hemodynamic simulation, complementing overlap metrics.

title: ICH-DIANet: A Modality-Disentangled and Attention-Expert Interaction Network for Brain Injury Assessment in Intracerebral Hemorrhage
motivation: Rapid and objective assessment of brain injury severity in intracerebral hemorrhage is important for treatment planning, yet the Glasgow Coma Scale depends on subjective behavioral responses and can be unreliable under sedation or altered consciousness. Unimodal imaging or simple multimodal fusion cannot fully capture complementary relationships between CT findings and clinical reports. Existing fusion strategies also retain intra-modal redundancy and use fixed interactions despite substantial patient-to-patient variation, motivating disentangled and adaptive multimodal modeling.
method: ICH-DIANet applies a Modality Disentanglement Module that uses orthogonality constraints to separate 3D CT and clinical-text features into shared and modality-specific subspaces. An Attention-Based Mixture-of-Experts module dynamically gates expert outputs according to patient characteristics and uses attention for deeper cross-modal alignment. These components jointly reduce redundancy and adapt fusion to heterogeneous inter-patient information.

title: ICHOR: A Robust Representation Learning Approach for ASL CBF Maps with Self-supervised Masked Autoencoders
motivation: ASL perfusion MRI provides noninvasive regional CBF measurements useful for neurological disease assessment, but low signal, protocol and vendor variation, and inter-site heterogeneity produce inconsistent image quality. The limited availability of labeled ASL data makes it difficult to train models that transfer across cohorts. Existing large neuroimaging pre-trained models focus mainly on structural or multi-contrast MRI and do not provide a dedicated backbone for physiological ASL CBF maps.
method: ICHOR pre-trains a 3D Vision Transformer masked autoencoder on ASL-derived CBF maps by reconstructing randomly masked volumetric patches. The pre-training corpus combines 11,405 scans from 14 studies with varied sites and acquisition protocols, producing a general-purpose ASL encoder. The encoder can then be adapted to diagnostic classification and CBF map quality prediction with limited labels.

title: IgG4-QPC: Quantitative Pathology-Consistent Virtual Staining from H&E to IgG4
motivation: IgG4 IHC diagnosis depends on the density and spatial distribution of sparse IgG4-positive plasma cells, whereas virtual-staining methods often optimize global appearance or continuous tissue regions. Real IHC slides also contain non-specific staining artifacts that can resemble positive cells, while existing methods usually assume clean supervision or filter such samples out. A method is needed that preserves cell-level quantitative pathology and explicitly handles noisy staining supervision.
method: IgG4-QPC introduces Segmentation-Guided Instance-Level Alignment, using a positive-cell segmentation prior to align generator features with plasma-cell semantics and enforce spatial density consistency. Its Noise-Aware Adversarial Learning identifies non-specific staining artifacts and applies spatially adaptive mask weights so background noise contributes less to optimization. Together, the modules target discrete cell-instance generation while making training robust to noisy IHC supervision.

title: Image-mediated fMRI-to-caption generation with visual pathway tokens and hyperbolic alignment
motivation: Generating precise captions from fMRI is difficult because neural activity and language occupy very different representational modalities. Direct language decoding often recovers only coarse semantics, while regional averaging discards fine-grained visual information; Euclidean alignment may also inadequately represent the non-uniform similarity structure of brain and semantic representations. An intermediate image space with geometry-aware alignment and richer visual-cortex features is needed to improve brain-to-language decoding.
method: The framework first trains an image-to-caption pathway with a frozen image encoder, an image perceiver, and LLaMA3. It then encodes whole-brain fMRI responses and fine-grained visual-cortex vertices through separate pathways, predicts image embeddings, and aligns them to target embeddings in the Poincaré ball. Token Probability Distribution Alignment distills next-token distributions from the image-conditioned branch, while visual pathway tokenization supplies detailed cortical information beyond regional averages.

title: Imbalance-Aware Distributional Alignment of Heterogeneous Modalities for HER2 Status Prediction

categories.value: Multimodal Integration with Clinical / Genomic / Biomarkers

motivation: HER2 status prediction can benefit from combining microscopic WSI information with macroscopic MRI, but the modalities differ greatly in perspective, density, and dimensionality, making direct feature interactions ambiguous. WSI is much information-richer and can dominate optimization, causing the model to underuse MRI and sometimes perform worse than a unimodal model. The task therefore needs alignment that tolerates heterogeneous correspondence and optimization that explicitly addresses modality imbalance.
method: IADA represents WSI and MRI features as latent distributions and aligns their overlap to promote semantic consistency without requiring ambiguous local correspondences. A dynamic gradient modulation module estimates each modality’s contribution from unimodal prediction scores and adaptively suppresses updates from the dominant modality. This encourages the fusion model to learn complementary information from both microscopic WSI and macroscopic MRI inputs.

title: ImPartial: Multi-channel Whole-Cell Segmentation Using Partial Annotations
motivation: Cell segmentation is fundamental to biomedical image analysis, but dense pixel-wise labels are costly, especially for noisy microscopy and multiplexed imaging with variable channel configurations. Existing methods commonly require reliable masks and fixed or consistent input channels, and are less suitable for extremely sparse annotations, structured noise, and domain shifts. A method is needed to obtain robust instance segmentation from limited partial supervision.
method: ImPartial is a weakly supervised cell instance-segmentation framework trained from a small number of user scribbles. It combines scribble supervision with blind-spot, self-supervised multi-channel quantized imputation, modeling foreground and background through limited unimodal intensity distributions. This auxiliary objective promotes noise-robust foreground-background separation, while the scribbles resolve touching-instance ambiguity; the design accepts variable channel counts and is scale-agnostic.

title: Improved Vascular Segmentation via Binary Flow Matching with Straight-Path Regularization
motivation: Thin-vessel segmentation is difficult because catheters, guidewires, motion artifacts, and other background structures can resemble vessels in both intensity and shape. Single-pass models cannot revisit uncertain regions, often yielding false positives and disconnected vessels. Diffusion-based iterative methods permit refinement but inject stochastic noise and optimize noise reconstruction rather than segmentation-oriented objectives.
method: Binary Flow Matching (BFM) formulates vessel-mask refinement as deterministic probability transport in Bernoulli parameter space. At each step, it conditions on a Bernoulli-sampled binary state and uses an x1-parameterized model to predict the final clean mask directly, allowing segmentation-specific supervision. A straight-path regularizer encourages locally linear probability trajectories, stabilizing topology evolution and reducing the required refinement steps.

title: Improving Factuality of 3D Brain MRI Report Generation with Paired Image-domain Retrieval and Text-domain Augmentation
motivation: Acute ischemic stroke requires rapid and factually reliable interpretation of DWI and ADC MRI findings to support treatment decisions. Generating radiology reports from 3D MRI is challenging because volumetric image evidence must be translated into clinical language, while pretrained 3D encoders are scarce and robust image-text alignment is difficult. Existing supervised or segmentation-based pipelines also limit scalability and cross-institutional generalization.
method: PIRTA is a retrieval-augmented report-generation framework that retrieves clinically similar 3D DWI/ADC volumes with a pretrained 3D vision encoder. It uses the paired clinician-authored reports of retrieved cases as textual evidence to ground LLM-based generation, avoiding explicit image-text alignment. The retrieval encoder is a 3D Vision Transformer pretrained with MAE self-supervision on large-scale unlabeled MRI.

title: Inception-Powered Unrolling Reconstruction for Accelerated Dynamic Cardiac Late Gadolinium Enhancement MRI
motivation: LGE is essential for myocardial scar assessment, but conventional static acquisition at a single cardiac frame is vulnerable to respiratory and cardiac motion and does not retain dynamic information. Distributing sequential k-space data across frames can improve motion robustness without longer scans, but makes every frame severely undersampled. Existing compressed-sensing and standard deep-unrolling approaches leave artifacts or have limited receptive fields for complex dynamic correlations under extreme acceleration.
method: IPUR-LGE reformulates sequential segmented PSIR-LGE acquisition as highly accelerated dynamic multi-frame reconstruction without extending scan time. It uses a physics-guided unrolled reconstruction network whose iterations contain multi-branch inception operators to provide diverse receptive fields and multi-scale modeling for aliasing and myocardial detail. A parameter-shared fixed-point formulation lowers memory demand and improves scalability for dynamic reconstruction.

title: Induce to Empower: Improving Lightweight Baselines via Foundation Model Induction for Generalized Polyp Segmentation
motivation: Polyp segmentation can support colorectal cancer prevention, yet polyps show substantial appearance variation, ambiguous boundaries, and cross-dataset domain shifts. Lightweight models are suited to real-time use but have limited representation capacity and generalization, whereas direct use or joint adaptation of foundation models is computationally expensive and lacks sufficient domain-specific labels. A practical method must transfer complementary foundation-model knowledge without undermining lightweight deployment.
method: Lite-PolypInductor (Lite-pi) augments lightweight U-Net, U-Net++, or PraNet baselines with a Unified Foundation Model Inductor. From the lightweight encoder's latent features, the module generates FM-specific prototype embeddings and aligns them through reconstruction supervision to structural priors extracted from SAM, DINOv2, and OneFormer. Transformer-based fusion then emphasizes polyp-relevant and boundary information while retaining complementary semantic cues for the decoder.

title: Inflated Performance in fMRI-Based ASD Diagnosis: A Reproducibility Study of Data Leakage in Feature Selection Pipelines
motivation: rs-fMRI machine-learning studies for ASD diagnosis have reported very high accuracies that are often interpreted as evidence of clinical readiness. However, high-dimensional connectivity features require feature selection, and applying label-informed selection before cross-validation can leak test information and inflate performance estimates. Reproducible auditing is needed to determine whether reported accuracy reflects genuine generalization.
method: This work reproduces MADE-for-ASD and XAI-for-ASD on ABIDE I, identifies their feature-selection leakage, corrects the implementations, and re-evaluates them under cross-validation. The corrections move supervised F-score selection and SVM-RFE inside the appropriate training folds, and the study also addresses numerical-stability issues. It provides corrected public code forks, practical implementation safeguards, and assesses LLM-assisted code review as an initial diagnostic aid subject to expert validation.

title: Information Maximization for Long-Tailed Semi-Supervised Domain Generalization
motivation: Domain generalization seeks models that remain reliable on unseen domains, while SSDG reduces labeling burden by using only a few labels alongside abundant unlabeled samples across source domains. Existing SSDG methods commonly assume uniform class distributions, an assumption that fails in practical long-tailed settings such as rare-disease data. Class imbalance substantially degrades these methods, creating a need for an SSDG objective that does not impose class-balance bias.
method: IMaX is a plug-in information-maximization objective for long-tailed semi-supervised domain generalization. It maximizes mutual information between learned features and latent labels while constraining learning with labeled samples. To reduce the class-balance bias of the standard marginal-entropy term, it replaces that term with an alpha-entropic objective derived from Tsallis divergences, allowing existing SSL and SSDG methods to better accommodate arbitrary class distributions.

title: Injecting a Low-Rank Background Prior: A Plugin for Medical Image Segmentation
motivation: Pathological anomalies such as polyps, nodules, and lesions vary greatly in appearance and may be camouflaged by complex anatomy, artifacts, or occlusion. Purely discriminative CNN and Transformer segmentation models can lack an explicit representation of background regularity, making anomaly-background separation and boundary delineation unreliable in noisy cases. The clinical search-by-subtraction process suggests modeling normal background patterns and identifying deviations from them.
method: The Low-Rank Background Prior (LRBP) Plugin models bottleneck background features with a compact PCA subspace learned from a global dynamic memory bank. It uses projection residual energy as an anomaly cue and injects this residual into an encoder-decoder segmentation model, while hard-example mining and redundancy-based replacement maintain challenging but diverse background prototypes. A lightweight gate learns, from a ground-truth-derived separability target during training, when residual injection is reliable; at inference the memory bank and basis are frozen.

title: InSPIRE: Multiparameter Inversion for Ultrasound Computed Tomography via Sequential Position-Based Implicit Representation
motivation: USCT can provide quantitative breast maps of sound speed and acoustic impedance, which respectively reflect tissue properties and sharp diagnostic boundaries. Simultaneous recovery is severely ill-posed: limited low-frequency data causes cycle-skipping, and velocity-density coupling causes parameter crosstalk. Supervised reconstruction lacks in-vivo ground truth, while standard CNN priors over-smooth impedance details and existing coordinate methods do not adequately address multiparameter crosstalk or spatially varying illumination.
method: InSPIRE performs unsupervised joint inversion of sound speed and acoustic impedance by representing both properties as continuous coordinate-conditioned functions within an INR and U-Net architecture. Its geometry-aware positional encoding uses radially modulated Fourier features to impose spatially adaptive spectral bias, particularly for central regions with restricted ring-array illumination. Dual branches with frequency-adaptive coordinate attention separate the two parameters, while sequential frequency-progressive optimization updates the reference state with implicit noise regularization across bandwidth transitions.

title: INST-Align: Implicit Neural Alignment for Spatial Transcriptomics via Canonical Expression Fields
motivation: Multi-slice spatial transcriptomics analysis requires aligning serial tissue sections to recover coherent 3D context, but sample preparation introduces large non-rigid distortions and arbitrary rotations. Alignment is unsupervised because biological ground-truth correspondences are generally unavailable, and raw expression also contains inter-slice batch effects. Existing methods treat alignment and expression integration separately, which can either weaken biological diversity through over-correction or lack expression-level feedback for registration.
method: INST-Align jointly learns a coordinate-based non-rigid deformation network and a shared Canonical Expression Field, an INR that maps spatial coordinates to expression embeddings. Training first establishes a stable canonical embedding space, then jointly optimizes deformations and spatial-feature matching. A unified loss combines geometric proximity with canonical-field feature similarity using adaptive soft assignments, and sharing the canonical field across slices regularizes ambiguous correspondences while absorbing batch variation.

title: Interaction-Aware Contrastive Multi-task Learning for Joint Segmentation and Malignancy Classification in Thyroid Ultrasound
motivation: Thyroid ultrasound assessment requires both nodule delineation and malignancy diagnosis, but staged segmentation-then-classification workflows can propagate boundary errors into diagnosis. Existing joint models often rely on shared parameters or prediction-level cues, leaving limited feature-level exchange and causing attention-boundary mismatch. A tighter, clinically consistent coupling is needed because morphology-based malignancy cues depend on accurate delineation.
method: IC-MTL uses a shared encoder with segmentation and malignancy-classification heads. A bidirectional Cross-task Interaction module passes boundary-sensitive cues to classification and malignancy-related semantics to segmentation through gated residual updates. Supervised Contrastive Multi-task Regularization is applied after interaction at image level for benign/malignant separation and pixel level for foreground/background separation.

title: Interactive MWA Planning via Probabilistic Inverse Inference
motivation: MWA is a curative option for unresectable tumors, but planning based on manufacturer power-duration charts neglects patient-specific perfusion, vasculature, and coupled electromagnetic-thermal effects. Physics-based bioheat simulation can model these factors but is too expensive for interactive use, while iterative planning approaches do not scale well to MWA's expanded parameter space. Patient-specific, safety-aware planning therefore requires direct real-time parameter inference.
method: The framework combines a forward surrogate and an inverse planning model trained on high-fidelity FEM-generated data. Given a tumor mask, perfusion map, and clinician-proposed trajectory, the inverse model assesses trajectory feasibility and directly infers generator power, ablation duration, and axial depth adjustment. The surrogate predicts ablation outcomes in real time, while sequential optimization supports interactive multi-antenna planning.

title: Interpretable Local-to-Global Estimation of Brain Aging Speed From Morphological Changes Using Longitudinal Structural MRI Data
motivation: Cross-sectional brain age delta captures accumulated deviation at one time point and may reflect a stable baseline shift rather than an ongoing aging rate. Longitudinal methods estimate scan-pair age differences, but commonly depend on intensity or texture changes that are sensitive to artifacts and scanner variation. Their single global estimates also obscure the spatially heterogeneous morphology of normal and disease-related brain aging.
method: The method derives longitudinal morphology from diffeomorphic registration between two structural MRI scans and computes Jacobian determinant maps of voxel-wise expansion or contraction. It partitions each map into non-overlapping patches and uses dedicated local regressors to estimate regional age differences. Learned patch relevance scores aggregate these local estimates into a global age-difference prediction, from which aging speed is obtained using the scan interval.

title: Interpretable Longitudinal Disease Forecasting with Graph-Based Multimodal Encoding and Population-Aware Language Generation
motivation: Accurate and interpretable longitudinal forecasting of Alzheimer's disease progression is important for early intervention and clinical workflow. Real-world multimodal records are irregular and incomplete, while existing approaches provide limited clinical explanation and often overlook population-level disease trajectories. Language-model approaches also generally lack longitudinal, hierarchically structured priors for explanation generation.
method: ENIGMA encodes incomplete heterogeneous longitudinal records with a multimodal bipartite graph module to produce semantically aligned representations. A multimodal language model is trained with longitudinal language tuning based on generated hierarchical interpretations, jointly forecasting future disease status and producing structured explanations. Its Dual Population Memory retrieves multimodal disease-evolution patterns and textual impressions to inform population-aware generation.

title: Interpretable Medical Image Diagnosis via VLM-based Concept Alignment and Graph Reasoning
motivation: Clinical image diagnosis needs predictions grounded in findings that physicians can inspect and correct, whereas saliency maps identify locations without stating what was found. Conventional Concept Bottleneck Models treat signs as independent scalar scores and can lose diagnostic information outside a fixed, incomplete concept set. Fine-grained alignment between modality-specific visual signs and clinical semantics is also difficult for general-purpose VLMs.
method: ConceptAlignE-G builds on BiomedCLIP and uses a concept-aware perception module to extract a dedicated sign-specific feature for each clinical imaging sign. These features are aligned with expert-defined concept text embeddings to produce sign probabilities. The probabilities form edge weights in a dynamic sign-image relational graph, and a GCN fuses image semantics, sign information, and text knowledge for classification while retaining sign-level intervention points.

title: Interpretable Probabilistic Medical Image Segmentation via Gaussian Process with Explicit Modelling of Annotation Bias and Variability
motivation: Medical segmentation annotations contain systematic bias and variability even among expert raters, and these imperfections propagate into trained models. Existing multi-rater probabilistic methods can emulate rater-specific delineations, but usually encode annotator effects implicitly through nonlinear latent representations. An explicit account is needed to distinguish image ambiguity from annotation-induced uncertainty and to analyze how rater behavior affects predictions.
method: The framework encodes an image with a U-Net and applies an SVGP in latent-feature logit space to estimate an image-dependent reference logit distribution. It models each annotator's labels as additive perturbations with explicit annotator-specific bias and variance. This produces closed-form rater-conditioned predictive probabilities, enabling direct sensitivity analysis of how annotation behavior affects segmentation uncertainty and outputs.

title: Interpretable Structure-Function Coupling via State-Space Models for Brain Connectome Analysis

categories.value: Multimodal Integration with Clinical / Genomic / Biomarkers

motivation: Structural connectivity provides an anatomical basis for functional connectivity, yet common connectome models enforce one-to-one coupling between corresponding regions. This conflicts with evidence that functional interactions arise through distributed, often polysynaptic, structural pathways across multiple regions. Existing graph convolutions and pairwise attention mechanisms do not adequately represent this long-range many-to-many coupling or modular brain organization.
method: SSFuse separately encodes SC and FC graphs, interleaves their regional tokens, and processes the sequence with a graph state-space model so that hidden states accumulate prior cross-modal information. This realizes distributed many-to-many SC-FC coupling without explicitly enumerating all region pairs. The hierarchical GM-SSFuse-H variant performs within-module fusion before cross-module integration, and interaction metrics quantify the learned distributed coupling.

title: Intraoperative Fluoroscopy-Volume Registration Using Virtual-Supervision Skeleton Attention
motivation: During ERCP, registering intraoperative 2D fluoroscopy to preoperative CT or MR volumes could improve navigation, but X-ray lacks depth and soft-tissue visibility. Landmark approaches require expert 2D annotations and are sensitive to instrument occlusion, while intensity- and learning-based methods remain vulnerable to occlusion and virtual-to-real domain shift. A robust annotation-free registration strategy is therefore needed for challenging intraoperative images.
method: The method generates differentiable virtual fluoroscopic images and skeleton bone masks from preoperative CT to train virtual-supervision pose regression networks. Its dual ResNet-18 branches use skeleton-guided spatial attention, gated image-mask fusion, and an auxiliary bone-mask decoder to estimate an initial pose. A subsequent differentiable optimization refines the pose using bone-proportion-weighted local normalized cross-correlation and bone-mask Dice similarity.

title: Intraoperative X-Ray-Guided Tumor Tracking via Dynamic 3D/2D Registration with Task-Driven 3D Gaussian Priors
motivation: Intraoperative X-ray is real-time and workflow-compatible for liver intervention, but weak soft-tissue contrast, structural overlap, and missing depth make stable 3D tumor localization difficult. Single-view dynamic reconstruction is highly ill-posed, while existing registration approaches often emphasize organ surfaces, skeletal anatomy, or patient-specific optimization. Tumor-relevant dynamic 3D/2D registration needs a representation that preserves internal target structure and uses limited X-ray motion cues effectively.
method: The proposed two-stage framework first constructs a static label-aware 3D Gaussian liver-tumor prior from preoperative CT, using tumor-focused non-uniform sampling and constrained initialization. It then extracts inter-frame 2D X-ray motion and maps it to Gaussian deformation through a sparse 3D control-point lattice. The motion is decomposed into rigid-like sliding and residual deformation and trained in a closed registration loop with joint 2D and 3D supervision.

title: IntraStyler: Intra-Domain Style Synthesis for Cross-Modality MRI Domain Adaptation
motivation: Segmenting vestibular schwannoma and cochlea on T2 MRI is clinically important, but T2 annotation is expensive, motivating adaptation from labeled contrast-enhanced T1 MRI. Image-level domain adaptation often treats the target domain as homogeneous, despite substantial within-T2 variation caused by scanners, field strengths, and acquisition protocols. Methods that synthesize diverse styles generally require predefined sub-domains, which may be unavailable or too coarse to capture fine-grained variation.
method: IntraStyler is a 3D unpaired ceT1-to-T2 image translation method conditioned on a per-image target style reference. A jointly trained 3D style encoder uses a contrastive objective in which positive samples share style but differ in anatomy, while negatives share anatomy but differ in style. The resulting anatomy-disentangled style embedding conditions the synthesis backbone, enabling fine-grained target-style generation without predefined sub-domain labels.

title: InvDetect: Unsupervised Medical Anomaly Detection in the Noise Latent Space of DDIM
motivation: Unsupervised medical anomaly detection is needed because abnormal-region annotations are costly and synthetic anomalies may not match real pathology. Reconstruction methods suffer from pseudo-normal image pixel mismatches, whereas embedding methods may not adequately separate normal and abnormal samples.
method: InvDetect trains a DDIM only on normal image patches, then applies DDIM inversion to map patches into a noise latent space. It fits a lightweight one-class SVM to normal noise latents, aggregates patch anomaly scores into a pixel-wise map, and applies spatial contiguity refinement to suppress isolated errors.

title: Inverse Protocol Prediction from Spheroid Microscopy Imaging via Morphology-Aware Structured Learning
motivation: 3D spheroid imaging is widely used, but images are rarely used to verify whether observed morphology agrees with recorded culture protocols. Protocol inconsistencies can undermine reproducibility, while morphology is ambiguous across conditions, acquisition settings introduce confounders, and richly annotated 3D microscopy datasets are limited.
method: The framework casts inverse protocol prediction as structured multi-label prediction from a single bright-field spheroid image. It extracts morphometric descriptors from automated segmentation, fuses them with deep visual embeddings, and uses a Hierarchical Multi-Task Transformer that conditions predictions on preceding protocol attributes. Domain-adversarial supervision and morphology-preserving augmentation are used to reduce acquisition bias and support cross-dataset generalization.

title: Inversion from ECG Foundation Model
motivation: Cloud ECG foundation models return embeddings for downstream use, but leaked embeddings may reveal immutable biometric and clinical information. ECG embedding inversion is underexplored, and existing inversion strategies from vision and language are unsuitable because ECG lacks established pretrained decoders and realistic cloud query budgets are limited.
method: SHINE first learns an ECG mapper from a limited number of direct query-response pairs to approximate a victim ECG foundation model's embedding space. The mapper synthesizes pseudo query-response pairs, which train an ECG inverter from scratch. The trained inverter reconstructs ECG signals directly from exposed victim embeddings without relying on a pretrained ECG decoder.

title: IOSVLM: A 3D Vision-Language Model for Unified Dental Diagnosis from Intraoral Scans
motivation: Intraoral scans preserve detailed 3D tooth-gingiva geometry, yet existing dental VLMs use 2D images or rendered multi-view scans and can lose spatial and geometric cues. Direct 3D diagnosis must handle heterogeneous scan forms, co-occurring and morphologically subtle diseases, class imbalance, and scarce paired IOS-text data.
method: IOSVLM represents native IOS scans as point clouds in a 3D encoder-projector-LLM architecture for unified multi-disease diagnosis and generative VQA. It introduces a geometry-to-chromatic proxy to mitigate the gap between color-free IOS data and color-dependent point-cloud pretraining. A two-stage curriculum first learns perception and geometry-language alignment from larger, noisier supervision, then fine-tunes on higher-quality supervision.

title: IRIS: An Intelligent Vision-Language System for Ocular Surface Diseases via Topic Tree and Scene-Driven VQA Generation
motivation: Ocular surface diseases are common and can cause preventable blindness, but expert diagnosis often requires specialized stationary equipment. Existing foundation models and VLMs underrepresent external eye photography and may hallucinate or lack precise anatomical grounding; flat image-caption data also fails to teach anatomy-to-sign clinical reasoning.
method: IRIS curates IRIS-120K and trains a compact 4B VLM using a clinically driven VQA data engine. Its Topic Finding Tree hierarchically connects visual findings to ocular regions and pathology concepts, while scene-driven generation creates role-adaptive dialogues across clinical scenarios. Source-specific preprocessing and quality-aware sampling improve the fidelity of the external-eye image supervision.

title: JANUS: Anatomy-Conditioned Gating for Robust CT Triage Under Distribution Shift

categories.value: Multimodal Integration with Clinical / Genomic / Biomarkers

motivation: CT triage must reliably detect clinically important findings across institutions, including conditions defined by size, attenuation, or other quantitative biomarkers. Visual foundation models lack explicit mechanisms for such measurement cues and can rely on spurious appearance correlations under scanner or reconstruction shifts; simple additive fusion does not explicitly resolve conflicts with quantitative priors.
method: JANUS combines a visual CT stream with macro-radiomic scalar priors derived from anatomy-aware measurements. Organ-Masked Attention Pooling produces label-specific visual features, while Anatomically Guided Gating projects and sigmoid-bounds the priors to multiplicatively modulate those features before label-specific prediction. It also defines Physiological Veto Rate to quantify selective suppression of high-confidence false positives.

title: Joint Biomarker and Survival Prediction via Concept-Conditioned Multimodal Slot Factorization

categories.value: Multimodal Integration with Clinical / Genomic / Biomarkers

motivation: Biomarker prediction and survival estimation are correlated oncology tasks, but they require different evidence: localized fine-grained tumor morphology versus global tissue and patient-level context. Existing joint methods are often unimodal and lack explicit mechanisms to reconcile this task-granularity heterogeneity, limiting use of pathology-report context for survival modeling.
method: PathoSlot competitively reweights fused WSI and pathology-report features, then softly factorizes them into task-aligned multimodal slots. Biomarker-oriented slots support local diagnostic morphology prediction, while a survival-oriented slot models global prognostic patterns; a context-gated residual selectively updates the survival slot with global context. Concept conditioning anchors each slot to its clinical prior to stabilize slot-task alignment and limit inter-task interference.

title: Joint Decomposition and Learned Deformation for Part-to-Whole MRI to Histology Registration
motivation: MRI-to-histology registration is needed to validate neuroimaging biomarkers at the cellular level, but a single histology section must be aligned to a 3D MRI volume despite resolution, dimensionality, and contrast gaps. Fragmented tissue, nonlinear and out-of-plane deformation, and uncertain slice localization compound the part-to-whole problem. Existing sequential approaches address only subsets of these challenges and can accumulate errors.
method: The framework uses three coordinated SIREN-based implicit neural representations: a support network for shared anatomy, a residual network for stain-specific appearance, and a deformation network for tissue displacement. A first optimization phase jointly learns image decomposition and global affine alignment, followed by a phase that freezes affine parameters and estimates local non-rigid and 3D deformation. This jointly handles slice localization, fragmented tissue, cross-modal appearance differences, and deformation from a single MRI-histology pair.

title: Joint Imaging–ROI Representation Learning via Cross-View Contrastive Alignment for Brain Disorder Classification
motivation: Brain-disorder classification commonly uses either full 3D volumes for global anatomy or ROI graphs for localized inter-regional relationships. Their respective and complementary contributions remain unclear because prior fusion systems are task-specific and confound representation benefits with architectural and training differences.
method: The method uses modular encoders to derive a global volumetric imaging embedding and a local ROI-graph embedding for each subject. Projection heads map both views into a shared latent space, where a bidirectional InfoNCE objective pulls same-subject pairs together and separates different subjects. The aligned embeddings can then be fused for classification, while branch-specific attribution analyses assess complementary patterns.

title: Joint Multi-modal Learning for Susceptibility-Induced Distortion Correction in Diffusion MRI
motivation: Susceptibility-induced geometric and intensity distortions in dMRI impair the study of brain pathways, especially near tissue-cavity boundaries such as the brainstem. B0-based methods can lack local information, while FOD-based methods use cumbersome two-step pipelines and do not exploit the complementary information in B0 and FOD images.
method: MMDC-Net formulates distortion correction as a one-step unsupervised multimodal optimization that uses one shared deformation field to reduce discrepancies between opposite phase-encoding B0 and FOD images. Its Modality-Aware Attention Module extracts correction-relevant features from each modality, a differentiable unit corrects B0 intensity bias, and PCGrad mitigates conflicts between multimodal similarity-loss gradients.

title: Joint Segmentation and Graph-Based Skeletal Representation Learning with Geometric Priors
motivation: Skeletal representations (s-reps) characterize anatomical interior geometry, including local width and boundary curvature, which is valuable for structures such as the hippocampus and for disease analysis. Classical evolutionary s-rep fitting is slow, and existing learning-based approaches often depend on masks or surface meshes rather than producing s-reps directly from images. An end-to-end image-based approach is needed to make skeletal modeling faster, more scalable, and compatible with segmentation workflows.
method: The method uses a 3D U-Net to jointly predict a foreground probability map and support s-rep generation from the original image. A variational encoder combines global anatomical context with cues from differentiable skeletonization, while learnable node-position queries use cross-attention and a topology-aware spectral graph decoder to predict the fixed-topology s-rep. Spoke-direction and boundary-orthogonality losses impose explicit geometric consistency.

title: Joint-Level Motor Imagery Decoding in fNIRS via a Unified Pairwise Machine Learning Framework
motivation: Motor-imagery BCIs could support stroke rehabilitation by decoding intended movements without physical execution. Fine-grained decoding from fNIRS is difficult because imagined movement produces weak, delayed hemodynamic responses, while prior work largely considers coarse classes or only a limited set of joints. A unified assessment of how separable all upper-limb joint tasks are is needed for interpretable and clinically meaningful decoding.
method: TSCIML-MI casts the eight upper-limb motor-imagery classes as all 28 pairwise binary fNIRS decoding tasks within one subject-wise pipeline. It converts signals to HbO/HbR concentration changes, filters and epochs them, then extracts temporal/statistical, spectral, and coupling features. Correlated features are removed, ANOVA selects training-fold features, and multiple linear and nonlinear classifiers are evaluated with nested cross-validation and hyperparameter optimization.

title: Just 32 Tokens: Medical Referring Image Segmentation via Next-Token Mask Prediction
motivation: MRIS segments a target region from a free-form clinical description, but conventional approaches often require complex fusion modules, multi-stage decoders, or external segmentation models. Although MLLMs offer unified image-text reasoning through next-token prediction, long mask-token sequences make inference inefficient, and compact tokenizations can lose fine boundaries and spatial coherence. A dedicated autoregressive formulation is needed to retain accurate mask generation under a very small token budget.
method: 32TokenMRISeg reformulates MRIS as autoregressive next-token mask prediction by a multimodal LLM. Each mask is encoded with only 32 discrete tokens from a 1024-entry codebook to reduce decoding length. Mask-level supervision refines decoded boundaries, chain-of-thought prompting organizes language-derived spatial cues, and token-order prediction provides an auxiliary signal that stabilizes autoregressive generation.

title: KAN-AINet: Kolmogorov-Arnold Network with Adaptive Illumination Modulation for Generalizable Polyp Segmentation
motivation: Automated polyp segmentation can assist early colorectal cancer detection, but manual delineation is time-consuming and subjective. Performance commonly degrades across clinical centers because endoscopic illumination varies with systems and protocols, producing highlights and shadows. Existing operations and edge filters are largely fixed and input-agnostic, limiting adaptation to local imaging conditions and true polyp margins.
method: KAN-AINet is a ConvNeXt-U-Net augmented with Kolmogorov-Arnold Network modules. Its KAN-based Illumination Modulation Module learns per-channel feature scaling conditioned on brightness patterns in the encoder, and its KAN-based Boundary Attention Module combines multiscale edge cues with adaptive nonlinear discrimination in the decoder. These learnable nonlinear responses target illumination-dependent feature degradation and unreliable polyp boundaries.

title: KANEx: Translating Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks’ Interpretability to Medical Explainability
motivation: Clinical AI systems need transparent and accountable decision processes, yet high-performing image classifiers are typically opaque. Post-hoc methods such as Grad-CAM approximate feature importance, while VLM-generated explanations can hallucinate and have opaque reasoning. The work investigates whether the mathematically interpretable spline units of KANs can ground more faithful visual attribution and trustworthy language explanations for chest X-rays.
method: KANEx combines KAN-based chest X-ray classification with visual and textual explanation. It derives KAN-Map from forward activations of KAN spline functions to quantify spatial-patch contributions without gradient backpropagation, producing interpretability-grounded heatmaps. The framework supplies these grounded contexts to a downstream VLM to generate context-aided clinical explanations.

title: KANResDiff: Learning Local Residual Diffusion via Kolmogorov-Arnold Network for Ambiguous Medical Image Segmentation
motivation: Ambiguous medical image segmentation must generate diverse yet anatomically plausible segmentations that reflect annotation uncertainty and inter-observer variability. Existing cVAE, logit-distribution, and diffusion methods use fixed stochastic formulations, which do not establish a progressive, stage-aware ambiguity model. Residual diffusion is promising, but MLP time embeddings couple inference stages and fixed residual interactions cannot adjust deterministic and stochastic contributions to their different roles across stages.
method: KANResDiff learns local residual diffusion for AMIS with two KAN-based components. Independent Time Encoding represents time using locally supported spline-based functions, reducing interference between timesteps and enabling stage-specific ambiguity roles. Residual Schroedinger Bridge learns step-specific deterministic residual weights by constructing local bridges across timesteps, allowing the balance between deterministic structure and stochastic diversity to vary over inference.

title: KEPIL: Knowledge-Enhanced Prompt-Image Learning for Prompt-Robust Disease Detection
motivation: Radiological findings are long-tailed, so rare conditions often lack enough annotations for supervised learning and require reliable zero-shot VLM inference. Current CLIP-style medical VLMs can be highly sensitive to minor prompt changes, while knowledge generated solely by LLMs may be hallucinated or inconsistent. Clinically deployable systems need prompt-robust representations grounded in dependable external medical knowledge.
method: KEPIL grounds a CLIP-style VLM in curated resources such as medical ontologies, using an LLM only to draft and normalize ontology-constrained text. Dynamic prompt enrichment produces diverse clinically grounded descriptions, semantic-aware contrastive learning aligns equivalent prompt variants while separating different meanings, and entity-centric report standardization creates ontology-aligned representations. Together, these components aim to stabilize zero-shot and fine-tuned image-text reasoning under linguistic variation.

title: Keypoint Correspondence Learning for CBCT–IOS Registration
motivation: CBCT-IOS registration is essential for 3D dental modeling, diagnosis, and implant planning, but it remains labor-intensive when performed manually. The large gap between CBCT volume intensity and IOS surface geometry makes direct correspondence uncertain. Segmentation-based pipelines are vulnerable to unstable segmentation, metal artifacts, outliers, and distance-based alignment that does not explicitly ensure reliable matches.
method: The framework learns modality-aligned CBCT and IOS feature embeddings and directly estimates cross-modal keypoint correspondences. It selects registration-relevant keypoints using intra-modality saliency and the sharpness of each cross-modal matching distribution, then jointly predicts inlier existence and pairwise match correctness. At inference, iterative SVD estimates the rigid transform while the matching criterion is annealed from feature similarity toward geometric consistency.

title: KGT-Reg: Knowledge-Guided Multimodal Framework for Medical Image Registration
motivation: Deformable medical image registration establishes dense correspondence for longitudinal analysis, navigation, and multimodal diagnosis. Although deep networks accelerate registration, they mostly optimize voxel intensities and local gradients, which can generalize poorly under anatomical variability and produce smooth but anatomically implausible deformations. Text embeddings alone do not encode inter-organ relations, motivating integration of structured anatomical knowledge into registration.
method: KGT-Reg integrates paired-volume visual features with text embeddings of organ descriptions and graph neural encodings of an anatomical knowledge graph. Text-guided semantic alignment adds localized structural context, while the graph pathway represents organ adjacency, hierarchy, and spatial topology. A graph-enhanced fusion module conditions and dynamically modulates deformation-field decoding to promote anatomically consistent registration.

title: KIDA: Kinematic-Intent Dual-path Alignment for Surgical Error Detection
motivation: Automated surgical error detection is needed for intraoperative safety and objective skill assessment in robotic-assisted surgery. Subtle errors caused by degraded control, ineffective attempts, or unstable manipulation can resemble valid maneuvers but may accumulate into serious complications. Existing appearance-driven classifiers enrich observed features but lack an explicit reference for correct execution, leaving this visual and motion ambiguity unresolved.
method: KIDA reframes surgical error detection as comparison between observed execution and clinically defined intended behavior. Its Kinematic Execution Branch adds lightweight motion dynamics to represent fine-grained execution, while the Clinically-Guided Intent Branch uses clinical textual descriptions to query motion-aware visual features. Intent-Execution Alignment regularizes normal maneuvers toward consistency and decouples subtle errors from the normative semantic space to enlarge their feature margin.

title: KiD-Seg: Kinetic-Disentangled Contrastive Learning with Anchor Guidance for Incomplete Multi-Modal Liver Tumor Segmentation

categories.value: AI for Neglected Diseases & Limited-Resource Settings

motivation: Accurate liver tumor delineation requires complementary multi-modal MRI information, but clinical protocols commonly produce structured group-wise modality absence. Existing incomplete-modality methods can contaminate reliable T2WI anatomy through symmetric alignment, ignore discriminative DCE kinetic evolution, and simulate clinically implausible independent modality dropout. A method is needed that remains robust across realistic incomplete MRI combinations while preserving anatomy and exploiting enhancement dynamics.
method: KiD-Seg treats T2WI as a permanent anatomical anchor and organizes the remaining sequences into clinically meaningful atomic groups. Its asymmetric anchor-guided contrastive learning aligns auxiliary features to the preserved T2WI representation, while differential kinetic disentanglement derives phase-to-pre-contrast maps and contrastively separates tumor from background. Hierarchical atomic-group fusion uses structured group-wise dropout and completeness-aware self-distillation to keep predictions consistent from T2WI-only to complete inputs.

title: KiMoCo-Net: Dual-Domain Learning for MRI Motion Artifact Correction
motivation: Patient motion disrupts MRI k-space consistency, causing structured ghosting and blurring that reduce diagnostic quality and may require rescanning. Image-domain deep models discard or do not explicitly correct acquisition-level phase and frequency distortions, while k-space-aware methods often use k-space only for detection or consistency supervision. Motion correction should directly address corruption in the domain where it arises.
method: KiMoCo-Net uses two cascaded correction stages trained end to end. A frequency-domain network first operates on complex-valued k-space to restore phase and magnitude consistency before inverse Fourier reconstruction; a spatial-domain network then refines anatomy and suppresses residual artifacts. A hybrid objective jointly enforces k-space fidelity and image-domain structural similarity.

title: Kinetics-Informed Neural Representation for Dual-Tracer Dynamic PET Separation
motivation: Simultaneous dual-tracer PET can capture complementary physiology in one scan, but indistinguishable annihilation photons make separation from mixed dynamic measurements severely ill posed. Voxel-wise kinetic fitting amplifies noise, produces spatially inconsistent maps, and becomes difficult with many dual-tracer parameters. Supervised deep approaches also depend on paired data that are rarely available clinically and may lack explicit kinetic interpretability.
method: The framework represents each tracer's kinetic parameters as continuous functions of spatial coordinates rather than independently fitting them voxel by voxel. Hash-encoded coordinates are mapped by an MLP to physiologically constrained parameters, which are passed through compartmental kinetic models to reconstruct separated tracer dynamics. The shared coordinate-based representation spatially couples estimation and is fitted to the measured mixed dual-tracer TACs without paired training data.

title: KJD-25K: A 3D Multi-modal Dataset and Benchmark for Knee Joint Diagnosis

categories.value: Multimodal Integration with Clinical / Genomic / Biomarkers

motivation: Knee MRI interpretation and reporting require time-intensive specialist reasoning about imaging findings, severity, and clinical diagnosis, with increasing data scale and inter-observer variability. Although MLLMs could assist this workflow, available knee datasets largely target classification, segmentation, or localization and do not adequately capture expert-aligned diagnostic reasoning. A large, clinically grounded 3D multimodal benchmark is needed to develop and assess reliable knee diagnostic models.
method: KJD-25K is a 3D multi-modal knee MRI benchmark containing 25,000 volume-report pairs from four standard sequences, expert-curated Chinese radiology reports, and structured diagnostic and severity annotations. It was built through expert case selection, report structuring and verification, AI-assisted label generation with clinician review, and final quality/privacy compliance review. The work also proposes clinically aware and linguistic metrics and benchmarks eight MLLMs for knee diagnostic reporting.

title: K-MaT: Knowledge-Anchored Manifold Transport for Cross-Modal Prompt Learning in Medical Imaging
motivation: Medical VLMs adapted on high-end modalities such as CT often fail on accessible low-end modalities such as radiography, despite shared pathologies. Standard prompt learning can overfit source-domain and seen-class statistics, causing catastrophic forgetting and modality-specific decision shortcuts. Zero-shot transfer needs to preserve diagnostic semantics without target-domain visual supervision.
method: K-MaT builds on BiomedCLIP and factorizes learnable prompts for strict asymmetric transfer from high-end to low-end modalities. LLM-generated clinical descriptions serve as semantic anchors that constrain prompts against loss of clinically meaningful knowledge. It then uses Fused Gromov-Wasserstein optimal transport to align the low-end prompt manifold with the relational structure of the visually grounded high-end manifold, requiring no low-end training images.

title: KMP-MIL: Knowledge Memory Pool Multiple Instance Learning with Foundation Model for Continual Whole Slide Image Classification
motivation: Continual WSI classification must learn sequential organ-specific tasks while retaining earlier diagnostic knowledge, but gigapixel slides, sparse cues, and cross-organ shifts intensify catastrophic forgetting. Existing continual pathology methods commonly rehearse stored slides or sample embeddings, which can conflict with clinical privacy and governance constraints. A rehearsal-free method is needed that supports both known-task and task-agnostic inference.
method: KMP-MIL couples a frozen pathology foundation model with a growing pool of compact task-specific parameterized memory units, avoiding storage or replay of historical WSIs. For each slide, a WSI-level query retrieves Top-K memory units, which drive prototype-conditioned feature calibration before MIL aggregation and textual calibration using class text prototypes in a shared vision-language space. It supports task-aware retrieval for task-CL and a universal memory pool for task-agnostic class-CL inference.

title: Knowledge Distillation-Driven Quality Transfer with Importance-Guided Supervision for Fundus Image Enhancement
motivation: Real-world low-quality fundus images caused by illumination, blur, and motion can obscure lesions and vessels, undermining diabetic retinopathy diagnosis and automated grading. Paired real low- and high-quality images are difficult to obtain, while unpaired approaches may introduce structural or color artifacts. Existing enhancement also commonly supervises all pixels uniformly despite the unequal clinical importance of retinal structures.
method: The proposed semi-supervised framework combines unpaired quality transfer with supervised enhancement on synthetically degraded pairs. Its quality-transfer branch freezes CNNs learned on high- and low-quality domains and uses knowledge-distillation alignment of their classifier outputs to guide a generator toward the high-quality domain without paired real images. A pixel-level importance decoder adaptively increases reconstruction supervision for clinically important structures such as the optic disc, vessels, and lesions.

title: Knowledge-Enhanced Representation Learning with Retrieval-Augmented Multimodal Fusion for Survival Prediction
motivation: WSI and transcriptomics provide complementary information for cancer survival prediction, but both contain substantial disease-irrelevant redundancy. Sparse malignant regions, rare molecular abnormalities, and intratumoral heterogeneity also make discriminative representations unstable, especially with limited medical datasets. Methods focused mainly on cross-modal interaction lack explicit mechanisms to suppress redundancy and stabilize clinically meaningful signals.
method: KERA uses two stages: ARPnet first pretrains on pan-cancer data to align WSI and transcriptomic modalities while retaining cancer-type-relevant information under cancer-type supervision. The pretrained network then supports RAFnet, which retrieves contextually similar intra- and inter-modality features from a precomputed multimodal database and fuses them with patient representations. This combines redundancy-aware representation learning with retrieval-based contextual enrichment to stabilize prognostic signals.

title: KOAL: Knowledge-Driven Prostate Cancer Grading with Ordinal-Aware Learning
motivation: Non-invasive lesion-level Gleason Grade Group prediction from mpMRI could improve prostate cancer risk assessment and reduce unnecessary biopsy, but image-pathology relationships are subtle and heterogeneous. Existing methods often ignore age, PSA, and expertise encoded in radiology reports. They also model GGG as a flat class or a single ordinal label, overlooking its composition from primary and secondary Gleason patterns.
method: KOAL integrates mpMRI with clinical variables and report-derived population-level knowledge through three modules. Clinical-Context Modulation uses age and PSA to condition cross-attention and adaptively recalibrate image features; Knowledge-Guided Prototype Alignment contrastively aligns lesion representations to offline LLM-derived grade-specific semantic anchors. Hierarchical Ordinal-aware Constraints separately predict primary and secondary Gleason patterns, then use a Differentiable Bio-logic Mapping Layer based on ISUP rules to produce a grading-consistent GGG.
