title: KS-SAM: Kolmogorov-Arnold-driven Shape Alignment for Single-Domain Generalization in 3D Medical Image Segmentation
motivation: Single-domain generalization for 3D medical segmentation is difficult because modality, scanner, and protocol shifts can entangle domain-specific texture with anatomical semantics. SAM and naive fine-tuning can overfit source appearance statistics, while conventional LoRA may not capture nonlinear shifts and distillation can propagate texture bias. Robust unseen-domain segmentation requires adaptation based on domain-invariant anatomical geometry.
method: KS-SAM combines a domain-expert 3D network with SAM adaptation to anchor segmentation in 3D geometry. Its uncertainty-aware feature fusion performs multiple noisy-input passes and fuses consensus segmentation/SDF predictions into uncertainty-filtered shape priors; KPSSD injects these priors into SAM through bidirectional geometric-semantic distillation while limiting texture leakage. KAN-LoRA replaces linear low-rank projections with localized spline-based activations to model nonlinear modality shifts and reduce forgetting.

title: LAD: Learnable Anisotropic Deformation for 3D Medical Image Analysis
motivation: Three-dimensional medical images have non-uniform slice spacing and acquisition-dependent spatial biases, whereas standard 3D Transformers assume isotropic voxel grids. Fixed resampling can distort native anatomy and fine details, and static or isotropic positional encodings cannot adapt to instance-specific spacing or semantic distortions. A model that adapts its internal geometry to each volume is therefore needed.
method: LAD is an instance-adaptive geometry framework inserted into 3D Transformers. An instance-aware anisotropy learner regresses axis-specific spatial scales from intermediate image features, then uses them to modulate rotation frequencies in anisotropic RoPE and to gate feature channels through adaptive anisotropic feature modulation. This dual pathway calibrates both spatial attention coordinates and semantic responses to native volumetric geometry without explicit spacing metadata.

title: LaGuadia: Language-Guided Adaptive Distillation from Pathology Foundation Models
motivation: Pathology foundation models provide rich whole-slide image representations but their large parameter counts make deployment computationally expensive. Multi-teacher distillation can transfer complementary expertise, yet uniform or vision-only weighting ignores tissue and clinical semantic heterogeneity, so the most appropriate teacher may vary by region. Clinical language offers a more objective reference for selecting expertise during distillation.
method: LaGuadia builds a compact pathology image encoder through language-guided multi-teacher distillation. It extracts visually observable clinical keywords from pathology reports, uses MedSigLIP as a vision-language meta-teacher to align patch features with those keywords, and weights multiple PFM teachers according to their semantic alignment with the clinical narrative. The resulting adaptive distillation transfers context-specific expertise while retaining a lightweight student.

title: Landmark-Free Assessment of Lower-Limb Alignment with Implicit Neural Shape Functions from Knee Radiographs
motivation: Lower-limb alignment is clinically important for knee osteoarthritis treatment and arthroplasty outcomes, but conventional radiographic measurements are manual and time-consuming. Recent automated methods predict a predefined set of anatomical landmarks, requiring dense annotations and tying the system to fixed clinical definitions. A flexible representation that can measure alignment without explicit landmarks is needed.
method: The workflow first aligns knee radiographs using tibial-plateau reference points and uses a CNN/U-Net pipeline to predict two-channel signed distance functions for femur and tibia. An implicit neural shape auto-decoder embeds the predicted anatomy in a compact latent space, with only the latent code optimized at test time. A four-layer MLP then directly regresses alignment angles from the latent representation, avoiding a fixed landmark coordinate output.

title: LangOR: 3D Language Field Reconstruction for Operating Room
motivation: Semantic understanding of operating rooms is needed for navigation, transcription, and resource management, but existing approaches rely on dense 2D annotations and provide limited spatial reasoning. Open-vocabulary 3D language-field methods also struggle with operating-room-specific entities and sparse, occluded views. An annotation-free method that combines domain-aware semantic extraction with reliable 3D reconstruction is needed.
method: LangOR first uses a robust VLM-based OR Perceptor with domain-constrained prompts and multi-round mask refinement to produce zero-shot 2D entity masks and semantics. It reconstructs an instance field in 3D Gaussian Splatting using geometric constraints and mask-aware contrastive learning from sparse views. A cross-view pixel-level lifting strategy and instance-mask-Gaussian matching associate 2D semantics with consistent 3D instances.

title: Large-Scale Distributed GPU-Accelerated Respiratory Motion-Resolved Reconstruction of 3D Non-cartesian mGRE MRI
motivation: Respiratory motion-resolved reconstruction of 3D non-Cartesian multi-echo MRI can provide quantitative abdominal maps for free-breathing exams, but the non-separable 3D encoding operator makes reconstruction computationally demanding. Repeated nuFFT operations over coils, echoes, and motion states, enlarged fields of view, and single-node memory limits hinder just-in-time use. A scalable multi-node, multi-GPU design is needed to handle this tightly coupled optimization.
method: The framework distributes the coupled reconstruction problem over a two-dimensional process grid spanning motion states and echoes, while partitioning coil computations across GPUs within each node. Coil reductions remain intra-node over NVLink/NCCL, whereas inter-node communication uses structured nearest-neighbor halo exchanges. An asynchronous distributed PDHG implementation overlaps communication with local 3D nuFFT work, and partition-aware I/O reduces per-GPU memory use for enlarged fields of view.

title: Large-Small Model Collaboration for Zero-Shot Surgical Phase Recognition
motivation: Lightweight surgical phase models capture temporal dynamics but often fail under domain shift, while surgical foundation models transfer broadly yet produce temporally inconsistent and clinically imprecise zero-shot predictions. Adapting to unseen procedures usually requires manual annotations, and directly distilling noisy foundation-model outputs can accumulate errors. A label-free collaboration that combines foundation-model generalization with temporal refinement is needed.
method: LaST uses a surgical foundation model to generate initial frame-level phase pseudo-labels for an unlabeled target domain. Two lightweight temporal models are warmed up on these labels, then iteratively refined using class-wise Gaussian Mixture Model loss filtering and cross-training on peer-selected reliable samples to reduce confirmation bias. A cycle-replay loop feeds the refined predictions back as improved supervision for subsequent iterations.

title: Latent Lessons from Histopathology: A Registration-Free Cross-Modal Supervision Framework for mpMRI-Based ISUP Grading
motivation: Exact ISUP grading from mpMRI could improve prostate-cancer management, but current models require large amounts of expert-labeled MRI data. Histopathology directly determines ISUP grade and could provide useful supervision, yet existing cross-modal approaches require coarse MRI–whole-slide registration and task-specific designs, limiting scalability. A registration-free way to transfer histopathology information into an MRI encoder is needed.
method: The framework jointly pretrains an mpMRI encoder with two objectives: a 3D-adapted SimCLR branch learns general representations from augmented prostate MRI studies, while a multimodal contrastive branch aligns those embeddings with patient-matched prostatectomy embeddings produced by the PRISM histopathology foundation model. A projection head places both modalities in a shared latent space, and the losses are combined during pretraining despite incomplete pairing. The pretrained MRI encoder is then fine-tuned for downstream grading without requiring spatial registration.

title: Latent Motion Spectral Regularity for Congenital Heart Defect Screening in Fetal Echocardiography
motivation: Congenital heart defects are a major cause of fetal morbidity and mortality, and automated screening could support care where specialist resources are limited. Most four-chamber-view methods use static frames or appearance reconstruction, overlooking periodic cardiac dynamics and requiring labeled abnormal cases or labor-intensive supervision. A normal-only, motion-aware detector that is robust to fetal variability and site differences is needed.
method: The method learns a one-dimensional latent motion trajectory from normal 4CV fetal echocardiography videos, representing cardiac phase progression over time. It defines a cycle-adaptive spectral regularity score as the ratio of high-frequency to total trajectory power within sliding windows covering a fixed number of cardiac cycles, then robustly aggregates scores across videos of varying length. Elevated high-frequency fluctuations serve as the anomaly signal for CHD screening.

title: Latent Pathology–Age Decoupling in Functional Connectivity Graphs for Multi-task Schizophrenia Assessment
motivation: Functional connectivity could support prediction of schizophrenia symptoms and cognitive deficits, but age-related brain changes overlap with disease pathology. Models may therefore exploit age-correlated shortcuts, while completely removing age can discard information needed for aging-sensitive cognitive tasks. The latent representation needs to separate pathological and age variation while retaining age as controlled context.
method: LPAD uses a dual-stream graph encoder to produce pathology-oriented and age-oriented representations from functional-connectivity graphs. Orthogonal decoupling and supervised contrastive regularization reduce shared age information in the pathology stream while preserving a separate age stream. Clinically informed gated modulation then reintroduces age only as a subordinate contextual signal before task-specific pooling and prediction.

title: Latent-CURE: Interpretable Breast Cancer Diagnosis via Dual-Asymmetric Chain-of-Thought
motivation: Breast-ultrasound diagnosis requires structured assessment of BI-RADS morphology, but current multimodal large-model systems often map visual features directly to labels through opaque correlations. Severe benign–malignant imbalance encourages shortcut learning, causing rare but decisive malignant indicators to be ignored. A transparent reasoning process and an objective that protects minority malignant features are needed.
method: Latent-CURE reformulates multimodal breast-ultrasound diagnosis as deterministic metric retrieval in a normalized latent space with predefined clinical anchors. Its implicit feature-aware chain of thought sequentially retrieves BI-RADS descriptors in the order margin, calcification, orientation, and final diagnosis, conditioning each step on the preceding semantic history. A dual-asymmetric loss dynamically adjusts margins and weights so rare, high-specificity malignant descriptors are not dominated by common benign patterns.

title: Latent-to-Latent Flow for Volumetric Stochastic Segmentation
motivation: Medical image segmentation must represent inter-observer variability because ambiguous organ and tissue boundaries affect treatment planning, but deterministic models cannot capture this aleatoric uncertainty. Existing stochastic segmentation research is dominated by 2D data, while volumetric settings face scarce multiple annotations, high computational cost, and difficult deployment in time-sensitive applications. A scalable method for modeling clinically meaningful uncertainty in 3D volumes is therefore needed.
method: The method introduces Latent-to-Latent Flow (L2L-Flow), which performs stochastic segmentation by applying flow matching between encoded image and label representations. It also develops a time-shifted noise schedule to stabilize volumetric Flow-SSN training at high resolution. Operating in latent space provides a controllable efficiency-performance trade-off for radiotherapy uncertainty delineation and multi-organ segmentation.

title: Learnable Gaussian Prototype Guided Ordinal Learning for Fine-Grained WSI Grading
motivation: Whole-slide grading is important for pancreatic cancer diagnosis, but cytological and histopathological severity progresses gradually, with subtle boundaries and sparse malignant regions. Conventional MIL methods treat grades as independent categories, ignoring inter-grade proximity and the strong heterogeneity of instances within a slide, which can destabilize predictions near ambiguous boundaries. The gap is an interpretable representation that explicitly models disease progression while aggregating weakly supervised WSI evidence.
method: GPO-MIL constructs a global space of learnable Gaussian prototypes and reorders the prototypes according to their correlation with slide grades, creating an interpretable benign-to-severe progression axis. Prototype responsibilities guide attention when aggregating heterogeneous WSI instances, emphasizing grade-defining regions. An ordinal-aware objective combines prototype separation, monotonicity constraints, and hierarchical supervision to stabilize progression structure and grading.

title: Learnable In-Context Templates for Medical Image Segmentation via In-Context Learning
motivation: In-context learning enables medical segmentation models to adapt from annotated support examples, but retrieve-and-prompt methods repeatedly load raw images. Raw medical images are noisy and heterogeneous, so nearest-neighbor retrieval can introduce irrelevant backgrounds or ambiguous boundaries, while searching large pools creates substantial latency. A compact, representative support mechanism is needed for efficient and reliable clinical deployment.
method: Learnable In-Context Templates replaces query-specific retrieval of raw image-mask examples with a compact set of trainable semantic templates. In-Context Template Distillation progressively optimizes these templates to retain representative lesion morphologies while suppressing background noise and spurious correlations. The templates act as a cleaner support set for foundation-model segmentation, eliminating database retrieval during inference.

title: Learning Beyond Pixels: Structured Knowledge Topology Consistency for Semi-supervised 2D/3D Medical Image Segmentation
motivation: Semi-supervised segmentation is needed because expert pixel-level annotations are expensive and privacy-constrained, yet most consistency methods only align final probability maps. Pixel-level agreement does not explicitly preserve salient landmarks, global sample relationships, or coherent transitions from low-level to semantic features, leaving models vulnerable to blurred boundaries and topological fragmentation in low-label regimes. A method that regularizes these higher-order diagnostic structures is needed.
method: SKTC-Net uses a dual-student semi-supervised architecture and augments conventional supervised and output-consistency losses with three structural constraints. Spatial Attention Consistency aligns salient anatomical regions, Relational Structure Consistency aligns batch-wise similarity topology, and Evolutionary Flow Consistency aligns inter-layer Gram-matrix transitions. Together these constraints transfer clinical-style spatial, comparative, and hierarchical reasoning to intermediate representations.

title: Learning Class Difficulty via Dynamic Focal Attention for Histopathology Segmentation
motivation: Histopathology segmentation must handle clinically important classes that may be difficult because of morphological variability, ambiguous boundaries, and contextual similarity. Existing data- and loss-level reweighting largely treats class rarity as a proxy for difficulty and only changes gradients after class-specific representations have been formed, while standard query attention weights classes uniformly. A representation-level, class-specific difficulty mechanism is needed.
method: Dynamic Focal Attention (DFA) adds a learnable scalar bias for each class to the cross-attention logits of a query-based mask decoder, changing class-conditioned feature aggregation before prediction. The biases start from a centered log-frequency prior to avoid early gradient starvation and are then optimized with the segmentation objective, allowing them to reflect emerging class difficulty. The framework also defines static frequency-based and hard-class variants within the same focal-attention formulation.

title: Learning Directional Semantic Transitions for Longitudinal Chest X-Ray Analysis
motivation: Longitudinal CXR interpretation requires comparing studies to detect subtle disease progression, but existing temporal fusion and discrepancy models often fail to isolate progression cues from invariant anatomy and acquisition-related pseudo-changes. They also generally detect change without representing whether the trajectory is improving or worsening. A report-grounded representation that explicitly models directional semantic transitions is needed.
method: ProTrans formulates progression between paired CXRs as a learnable directional transition in semantic space rather than simple feature fusion or subtraction. State contrastive alignment grounds each study in report-derived disease states, while transition contrastive alignment links the progression representation to report-described changes. Reversed temporal modeling and bidirectional reconstruction consistency jointly enforce directionality and coherent forward and backward trajectories.

title: Learning Diverse and Realistic Polyp Data via Style-Fused Diffusion Models
motivation: Accurate polyp segmentation supports colorectal cancer screening, but annotated endoscopic data are scarce and cover limited morphology. Existing synthesis methods often reuse public masks, inheriting structural bias, and may produce images with unrealistic or inconsistent color and texture. A generator must expand plausible lesion shapes while preserving mask semantics and endoscopic style realism.
method: SFD-Polyp is a mask-conditioned diffusion framework that uses a Style Integration Module to inject appearance cues from real endoscopic images during denoising while preserving mask-aligned lesion semantics. Morphology-Preserving Mask Synthesis creates anatomically constrained mask variants through controlled contour and sub-region perturbations, which are used at inference to generate structurally diverse image-mask pairs. The resulting synthesis combines varied morphology with more consistent color and texture realism.

title: Learning Dual Prior Presentation for Opportunistic Screening of Visceral Artery Aneurysms on Non-Contrast CT
motivation: Opportunistic VAA screening on non-contrast CT could detect potentially fatal aneurysms without additional imaging, but weak vessel-tissue contrast, complex branching, and tiny lesion support make direct segmentation unreliable. Aneurysmal dilation is a continuous deformation rather than a discrete object, and normal bifurcations or curved vessels can mimic lesions. The task needs representations that separate dilation-sensitive evidence from anatomy-induced ambiguity.
method: DeepVAA augments a multi-label vascular segmentation backbone with two continuous prior branches. A geometric confidence prior represents aneurysmal dilation as a smooth response along the vessel wall, while an anatomical reliability prior models ambiguity from bifurcations and high-curvature segments. During inference, structured prior projection uses reliability to suppress geometry-induced activations and calibrate the lesion confidence map.

title: Learning from Good Neighbors: Slice-wise Quality-aware CT-to-Diffusion MRI Synthesis
motivation: CT-to-MRI synthesis could provide MRI-like soft-tissue information when MRI acquisition is costly or impractical, but the large modality gap makes this direction challenging. Generated quality also varies across slices, while many methods neither estimate slice quality nor exploit the 3D anatomical continuity of adjacent slices. A quality-aware, context-guided framework is needed for consistent volumetric synthesis.
method: LGN first uses a Latent Diffusion Model to generate draft DWI from CT. An LPIPS-based teacher-student Quality Predictor estimates quality for each generated slice, and a 3D context-aware Cross-Attention Refiner selectively improves low-quality slices by attending to high-quality neighboring slices. This quality-guided refinement exploits anatomical continuity to reduce artifacts and slice-to-slice inconsistency.

title: Learning Geometry-Aware Bundles with Spectral Heat Kernel Diffusion for fMRI-based Brain Disease Diagnosis
motivation: fMRI-based diagnosis is difficult because functional connectivity is noisy and different brain regions may lie on heterogeneous local manifolds. Conventional GNNs aggregate all ROIs in one shared Euclidean space, causing geometric misalignment, while random edge or node dropping for contrastive learning can destroy the brain network topology. A geometry-aware representation must coordinate local regional spaces and generate topology-preserving perturbations.
method: VB-GCL lifts the fMRI connectivity graph into a vector bundle by assigning each ROI a learnable orthogonal local subspace. A Bundle Laplacian coordinates message passing across these heterogeneous geometries and supports multi-hop geometric diffusion for classification. A parallel contrastive stream uses heat-kernel spectral perturbations at different diffusion scales to create topology-preserving views and improve noise robustness.

title: Learning Hierarchical Anatomy-Grounded Representation for Cross-Modal Registration
motivation: Cross-modal deformable registration must align complementary MRI and CT anatomy despite large appearance differences, acquisition variability, and deformation. Pointwise contrastive methods often treat voxels independently and fail to model hierarchical anatomical context and topology, making correspondence disambiguation and plausible deformation difficult. A representation that explicitly captures global-to-local anatomical structure is therefore needed.
method: HAGR augments contrastive learning with cross-view feature reconstruction, using similarity-based reconstruction as a structured proxy for anatomy-aware representations. It learns a hierarchical feature space in a coarse-to-fine architecture: a matchability-aware coarse stage provides global anatomical context, while a coarse-guided fine stage performs implicit hard-sample mining for difficult local correspondences. Registration is then performed in the learned hierarchical feature space.

title: Learning Invariant Anatomical Representations from Multi-Sequence MRI for Brain Segmentation
motivation: Brain segmentation from MRI requires costly voxel-level annotations, while multi-sequence data are often incomplete and structurally correlated across sequences. Existing self-supervised methods may treat sequences independently, rely on complete sequence sets or static healthy templates, and remain insensitive to pathological heterogeneity. A unified pretraining approach should learn sequence-invariant anatomy while representing pathology-aware variations.
method: TeInL disentangles each multi-sequence MRI representation into sequence-invariant anatomical content and sequence-specific style. Cross-sequence reconstruction with dynamic style prototypes and anatomical consistency learning forces the content representation to preserve shared structure while style prototypes provide sequence intensity information. A semantic alignment module aligns visual features with pathology-aware anatomical text from a Structures Description Repository, and style alignment links sequence prototypes to text descriptions.

title: Learning Modality-Invariant Structure and Distribution Alignment for Multimodal Medical Image Registration
motivation: Multimodal registration must align anatomy despite large modality-dependent intensity discrepancies. Existing feature-level methods may require pre-aligned supervision and be decoupled from deformation estimation, while image translation and interaction modules can underuse modality-invariant structure. A unified unsupervised method is needed to strengthen shared anatomy and reduce intensity discrepancies during registration.
method: The framework introduces a shared Structure-Aware Frequency Enhancement (SAFE) module that decomposes features into frequency components and selectively amplifies structure-sensitive high-frequency responses; shared parameters encourage modality-invariant structural encoding. Registration-guided Multimodal Contrastive Alignment (RMCA) constructs positive pairs between warped moving features and corresponding fixed features using the predicted deformation field. Contrastive feature alignment and deformation estimation are therefore optimized jointly without pre-aligned supervision.

title: Learning Prototypes for Unsupervised Joint Generation of Conditional Templates and Atlases
motivation: Conditional brain templates and atlases should jointly represent cohort-specific anatomy and regional organization, but they are usually constructed independently, weakening their correspondence. Atlas construction also commonly requires individual parcellation labels that are rarely available, while simply warping a public atlas is intensity-driven and can create regional misalignment or topological artifacts. A unified unsupervised approach using only a public template-atlas pair is needed.
method: LatentAtlas learns conditional prototypes in a shared latent space and decodes each prototype through task-specific heads into a template, an atlas parcellation, and deformation fields. A multi-decoder VAE first establishes the latent distribution and decoders, after which a conditional generator is optimized using cohort conditions such as age in both latent and volumetric spaces. A public template-atlas pair is propagated to individual subjects to create pseudo labelmaps, which supervise parcellation and provide population-based regularization against registration errors and topological artifacts.

title: Learning Quantitative Calibration of Computed Tomography for Bone Mineral Density Estimation Using Multi-Center Data
motivation: Opportunistic osteoporosis screening from routine CT could estimate bone mineral density without extra scans, but converting Hounsfield Units to physical density normally requires a calibration phantom. Scanner- and center-dependent calibration variation makes single-center calibration unreliable, especially at out-of-distribution centers. A spatially dense, multi-center method is needed to produce robust QCT maps and generalizable vBMD estimates.
method: The method uses supervised 3D image-to-image translation to generate voxel-wise QCT density maps of the proximal femur directly from routine CT. Volumetric BMD is then computed within a femur mask, preserving spatial density distributions rather than predicting only a scalar value. Training and evaluation use leave-one-center-out multi-center data so the learned mapping can handle center-specific calibration shifts, including out-of-distribution centers.

title: Learning Robust Medical Image Segmentation Under Mixed-Quality Annotations
motivation: Medical segmentation datasets often mix accurate and corrupted masks because of inter-observer variability and ambiguous boundaries. Label-correction methods may refine all samples uniformly, while supervision-selection methods discard uncertain regions and fail to recover useful structure. Robust learning therefore needs to estimate reliability and adaptively correct annotations while limiting confirmation bias.
method: RGSS trains two segmentation networks in parallel and uses peer-network per-sample losses with a two-component GMM to estimate annotation reliability. Clean annotations are used directly, whereas noisy masks are refined by a pretrained diffusion-based mask refiner whose strength is adjusted to the estimated noise severity. The refined masks are blended with peer-model predictions using an epoch-dependent schedule, and the networks are iteratively updated with these reconstructed targets.

title: Learning Role-Conditioned Alignment for Medical Image Referring Segmentation
motivation: Referring segmentation of pulmonary infection must resolve lesion morphology, quantity, and location, while diseased regions often overlap healthy tissue with fuzzy boundaries. Existing medical referring segmentation systems usually treat reports as a monolithic global feature, missing token-level roles and producing diffuse guidance. More granular role-aware alignment and explicit boundary modeling are needed for precise grounding.
method: RCA extracts visual and linguistic features and aligns them through a global text interaction plus three role-conditioned attention mechanisms. A coordinate scoring function uses location tokens for spatial grounding, energy-based modeling captures lesion semantics such as infection type, and a text-gated lesion query incorporates quantity priors. A Boundary Refinement Module adds edge-aware information before the segmentation head to sharpen lesion boundaries against healthy tissue.

title: Learning Task-Specific Anatomical Priors via Context Distillation for In-Context Medical Image Segmentation
motivation: Visual in-context segmentation depends strongly on the composition of its context set, but growing clinical repositories make selecting a few representative demonstrations computationally expensive and vulnerable to redundancy or noise. Existing context selection and matching methods assume a manageable candidate pool and do not directly learn compact anatomical priors for segmentation. A task-specific distilled context is needed to stabilize performance and reduce inference cost.
method: CD-MIM treats context demonstrations as learnable templates rather than a fixed subset of raw samples. A curriculum-driven masking scheduler progressively hides image regions, and a meta-learning-based optimization process trains templates to reconstruct them, encouraging encoded structural dependencies and cross-patient anatomical variation. The distilled templates can replace or complement raw demonstrations for frozen visual in-context segmentation models.

title: Learning the Hierarchical Organization in Brain Network for Brain Disorder Diagnosis
motivation: Functional brain-network diagnosis is often based on predefined atlases that impose strict sub-network boundaries. These boundaries can miss strong cross-network correlations and obscure disorder-related interactions, reducing classification accuracy and interpretability. A learnable hierarchical organization is needed to capture intrinsic subgraph dependencies without fixed functional labels.
method: BrainHO uses learnable subgraph tokens and hierarchical attention to aggregate brain-network nodes according to feature affinity rather than fixed atlas labels. An orthogonality constraint encourages diverse and complementary organizations, while hierarchical consistency uses high-level graph semantics to refine node-level features. The resulting hierarchical subgraphs support disorder classification and localization of disease-related network biomarkers.

title: Learning to Distort: Weakly-Supervised Image Quality Transfer for Prostate DWI Correction
motivation: Single-shot prostate DWI is susceptible to geometric distortions that disrupt correspondence with anatomical images and can impair diagnosis, yet paired distorted-undistorted clinical scans are rarely available. Acquisition-based correction requires extra scans, while unpaired methods may be unstable, slow, or hallucinate anatomy. A weakly supervised strategy is needed to learn correction from image-level quality labels by first generating realistic distortions.
method: The framework first pretrains an image-quality assessment encoder and learns latent prototypes for distorted and undistorted DWI distributions. A weakly supervised prototype flow-matching model is guided toward the distorted prototype manifold to synthesize clinically realistic susceptibility artifacts from undistorted images. These synthetic distorted-undistorted pairs then supervise a second IQT model trained in the forward correction direction, avoiding direct unpaired correction and its risk of anatomical hallucination.

title: Learning to Optimize Radiotherapy Plans via Fluence Maps Diffusion Model Generation and LSTM-Based Optimization
motivation: VMAT planning is a high-dimensional inverse problem that jointly optimizes MLC apertures, monitor units, and dose objectives while enforcing machine-dose consistency. Repeated optimization for different treatment configurations is time-consuming, and existing gradient, reinforcement-learning, and supervised planners can suffer from difficult loss landscapes, limited search coverage, or poor adaptability.
method: The method uses a distribution-matching distilled diffusion model to generate clinically feasible VMAT fluence maps in one shot. An LSTM-based learning-to-optimize module updates the latent variables and monitor-unit scale using dose-gradient history from a differentiable dose engine, refining the generated map toward prescribed objectives. Diffusion and dose components remain frozen during optimization and inference, while machine-constrained fluence maps are validated for deliverability.

title: Learning to Read Where to Look: Disease-Aware Vision–Language Pretraining for 3D CT
motivation: 3D CT vision-language models usually align an entire volume with an entire report, providing only coarse global supervision, while organ-level methods require external segmentation and curated regional text. Radiologists often mention specific slices in reports, but this local signal is largely unused for locating findings within a scan.
method: RadFinder pretrains a 3D CT vision-language model with SigLIP-style contrastive alignment of volumes and reports, while adding disease labels as prompt text in the shared embedding space. The authors mine report references to series and image numbers to create snippet-slice pairs and train an intra-scan localization objective that predicts the axial depth associated with a text snippet. Global retrieval, disease classification, and local grounding are optimized in one unified model.

title: Learning to Segment Burns with Limited Labels: A Dual-Path Cascaded Network with Uncertainty-Guided Teacher Diffusion Exposure
motivation: Burn segmentation from color images is needed for burn-area estimation, treatment decisions, and monitoring, but heterogeneous tissue, irregular diffuse margins, and illumination variation make pixel boundaries ambiguous. Pixel-level burn annotations are laborious and scarce, while contextual models may lose boundary precision and pseudo-labels become unreliable in low-label settings.
method: UADA-MSPCNet combines a high-resolution spatial path with a cascaded atrous contextual path to model irregular burn boundaries and heterogeneous tissue at complementary scales. An exponential-moving-average teacher-student framework uses uncertainty-weighted consistency and cross-scale pseudo-label supervision on unlabeled real images. Diffusion-generated burn images are supplied only to the teacher, enriching pseudo-label formation without directly biasing student optimization.

title: Learning to Trim: End-to-End Causal Graph Pruning with Dynamic Anatomical Feature Banks for Medical VQA
motivation: Medical VQA models can exploit dataset-specific anatomical and linguistic shortcuts instead of diagnostic evidence, causing poor out-of-distribution generalization. Static confounder dictionaries cannot track dynamic anatomical priors, and test-time pruning adds cost without improving the model’s intrinsic representations.
method: LCT encodes the image and question, maintains a momentum-updated Dynamic Anatomical Feature Bank as a proxy for dataset-level confounders, and compares regional visual features with its prototypes. A differentiable Causal Trimming module converts these similarities into soft masks that suppress confounder-correlated regions while preserving instance-specific evidence. The trimmed visual representation is fused with the question embedding and trained end to end with a joint objective.

title: Learning to Unify Deformable Shape and Texture Representations for Cardiac Video Classification
motivation: Cardiac MR video classification models often rely mainly on intensity texture and miss myocardial deformation patterns that reveal pathological motion. Existing multimodal approaches simply concatenate or add shape and texture features and apply uniform temporal weighting, ignoring cross-modal interactions and phase-dependent diagnostic importance.
method: ShapeFuse projects deformable shape and image-texture features into a shared latent space and applies bidirectional cross-attention to model their mutual spatiotemporal dependencies. An adaptive fusion gate dynamically weights the two modalities at each cardiac phase, and learned temporal pooling emphasizes diagnostically informative timepoints. The resulting integrated representation supports cardiac video classification while exposing modality and phase attention.

title: Learning What Can Move: Patient-Specific Motion Subspaces from a Single Scan
motivation: Deformable registration learns motion from image pairs, entangling the representation with fixed and moving domains and making changes in modality or dimensionality require specialized adaptations. Although anatomical structure constrains plausible motion, existing approaches generally generate motion instances rather than a reusable patient-specific subspace inferred from one scan.
method: The asymmetric network uses only a fixed image to predict patient-specific scalar motion modes that span a plausible deformation subspace. Given a new observation, motion is instantiated by solving a small set of mode coefficients in closed form, rather than relearning a pairwise displacement field. A ModeNorm layer removes the signed-scale ambiguity between modes and coefficients, enabling the same modes to handle 3D images, 2D images, 2D masks, and surface points.

title: Learning Where to Look: A Reinforcement Learning Framework for Robust Micro-ultrasound Prostate Cancer Detection

categories.value: Multimodal Integration with Clinical / Genomic / Biomarkers

motivation: Micro-ultrasound prostate cancer detection is difficult because suspicious tissue is subtle and interpretation varies with clinical experience. Training is further limited by core-level pathology labels without pixel annotations, missed small tumors, sparse supervision, and severe benign-tissue imbalance, while holistic models may attend to spurious regions instead of learning where to look.
method: Prost-RL inserts a lightweight reinforcement-learning policy before a foundation-model encoder-decoder to produce spatial attention maps that serve as soft prompts for lesion heatmaps and core-level classification. Adaptive Policy Optimization coordinates supervised and policy learning, while symmetric cross-entropy with negative-entropy regularization addresses sparse, noisy weak labels and encourages sharp localization. The policy is trained end to end with the prediction modules.

title: Learning Where to Look: Pathologist-Inspired Multi-field-of-View Evidence Retrieval for Cell Type Classification in H&E
motivation: Cell typing in H&E whole-slide images requires evidence ranging from intrinsic morphology to neighborhood and tissue context, but most models use a fixed field of view. Enlarging that view can dilute local evidence, while a small view can miss decisive out-of-view cues; pathologists instead navigate multiple magnifications selectively.
method: TRACE uses three nested, cell-centered experts for a polygon-masked local cell view, a neighborhood view, and a broader tissue-context view. Pretrained ViT token features are queried by the target cell through attention pooling, allowing local and context experts to retrieve discriminative regions rather than average each view. An uncertainty-aware router mixes expert predictions, and a responsibility-driven objective aligns routing weights with each expert’s ground-truth support to encourage complementary specialization.

title: LEGEND: A Language-Aligned EEG Foundation Model with Flow Matching Latent Denoising
motivation: EEG foundation models often lack semantic alignment, so they depend on task-specific fine-tuning and generalize poorly to unseen datasets. Their prevalent masked reconstruction objectives focus on pointwise waveform or spectral details and may neglect global, invariant neural structure, limiting robustness.
method: LEGEND combines a Mamba2 signal backbone with Flow Matching Latent Denoising, which perturbs latent embeddings between a Gaussian prior and encoded signals and learns a vector field to recover globally consistent structure. Its Signal-Language Alignment module reformulates EEG tasks as instruction-following generation, conditioning autoregressive answers on the signal and a natural-language prompt. A weighted sum of language cross-entropy and flow-matching losses jointly trains semantic alignment and structural regularization.

title: LeGend: Lesion-Guided Longitudinal CXR Generation via Gaussian-Biased Causal Attention
motivation: Longitudinal follow-up CXR generation must depict subtle, spatially localized disease progression, yet autoregressive models often rely on implicit attention and over-attend to peripheral non-lesional reference regions. This structural corner/edge bias reduces lesion overlap and can produce disease-inconsistent follow-up images.
method: LeGend first uses an offline vision-language model to predict sparse lesion coordinates from multimodal inputs and converts them into a normalized 2D Gaussian salience prior. Gaussian-Biased Causal Attention adds this sample-specific prior to causal self-attention logits during autoregressive decoding, steering token interactions toward lesion-relevant regions while preserving causality. The plug-and-play bias is injected at selected middle layers to balance lesion guidance with image reconstruction.

title: Lesion-Centric Structured Report Generation for 3D CT with Multimodal Large Language Models via Hierarchical Evidence Tokens
motivation: Structured 3D CT reporting requires attribute-level reasoning over volumetric scans, but clinically decisive evidence is localized to lesions. Unfolding volumes into long visual sequences causes relevant cues to be overwhelmed by background tokens, while available lesion masks are often used only as input hints. These problems are particularly harmful for multi-task prediction with limited and imbalanced data.
method: The method builds a lightweight 3D-to-MLLM interface that represents a CT volume as a fixed-length set of image tokens. A lesion-guided attention loss regularizes cross-modal attention toward lesion-relevant tokens during training. Global Evidence Slots summarize the long visual sequence through learnable-query cross-attention pooling and are injected with fine-grained tokens as a hierarchical evidence interface.

title: Leuko, I Am Your Prototype: A Prototypical Detection Framework for Fine-Grained Laryngeal Lesion Stratification
motivation: NBI endoscopy is central to laryngeal lesion screening, and accurate stratification is needed because lesion risk determines follow-up and treatment. Fine-grained classification is difficult because SCC, leukoplakia, and low-risk lesions share visual characteristics, vary in size and appearance, and appear amid dominant healthy-mucosa context. Standard single-stage detectors optimize boxes and cross-entropy without explicitly organizing lesion-centered representations, leaving ambiguous and underrepresented classes vulnerable to contextual bias.
method: The framework augments YOLO11n with a multi-scale feature fusion module and an auxiliary prototypical branch. RoIAlign extracts localized lesion features, which are L2-normalized and trained to cluster around learnable SCC, LEUKO, and LR prototypes using a temperature-scaled prototype loss jointly with detection loss. Training first bootstraps the detector alone, then initializes prototypes from class embeddings and updates them with an exponential moving average.

title: Leveraging Pathology Co-occurrence for Test-Time Adaptation in Chest X-Ray Diagnosis
motivation: Chest X-ray classifiers can deteriorate after deployment at sites with different equipment, protocols, and patient populations. Source-free test-time adaptation is practical in such settings, but conventional entropy-based TTA was developed for single-label tasks and treats samples and labels independently. In multi-label radiology, pathologies have structured, domain-dependent co-occurrence patterns, so individually confident yet implausible predictions can introduce harmful adaptation gradients.
method: CoWA is a source-free TTA method for multi-label chest X-ray classification. It estimates a pathology co-occurrence matrix from incoming model predictions and uses agreement between each predicted label configuration and this emerging target structure as a reliability signal. Adaptation gives greater weight to structurally consistent samples and downweights inconsistent ones, reducing noisy entropy-minimization updates without target labels or source data.

title: LinGuinE: Longitudinal Guidance Estimation for Volumetric Tumour Segmentation
motivation: Volumetric tumour segmentation and lesion correspondence across time are important for radiotherapy planning, treatment-response assessment, and disease-progression analysis. Most segmentation systems produce semantic masks for individual timepoints, while existing tracking approaches may omit masks, limit radiologist control, require longitudinal labels, or address only narrow modality and cancer settings. A practical method is needed to follow a radiologist-selected lesion throughout a study without relying on difficult-to-obtain tracked longitudinal training data.
method: LinGuinE combines image registration with promptable semi-automatic segmentation to track and segment a selected lesion across every scan in a longitudinal study from one prompt at any timepoint. Registration propagates the guidance between scans, and the framework can pair arbitrary registration algorithms with semi-automatic segmenters. Its modular design requires no longitudinal training data and supports temporally direction-agnostic use.

title: LiSAD: A Label-Efficient Implicit Model with Spatially Adaptive Directional Total Variation for Spatial Transcriptomics

categories.value: Multimodal Integration with Clinical / Genomic / Biomarkers

motivation: Spatial domain identification partitions tissue into functional regions from gene expression and spatial coordinates, forming a basis for downstream spatial transcriptomics analysis. Methods based on fixed adjacency can be misleading in heterogeneous tissue, and approaches that directly model discrete grids struggle to represent subtle continuous variation and blurred domain transitions. Although full annotation is costly, existing methods rarely exploit the representative spot labels that pathologists can provide.
method: LiSAD combines implicit neural representations with hypergraph learning to convert discrete spatial transcriptomics observations into continuous spatial representations while modeling high-order spot relationships. It introduces spatially adaptive directional total variation regularization, which adapts to local spatial variation to preserve relevant high-frequency detail and delineate boundaries. A label-efficient optimization strategy uses a small amount of expert spot annotation to refine domain representations and predictions.

title: LLM-Bootstrapped Targeted Finding Guidance for Factual MLLM-based Medical Report Generation
motivation: MLLM-based medical report generation can omit important findings or hallucinate inaccurate information, which prevents reliable clinical use. End-to-end models couple visual recognition and medical language organization, so reports are generated directly from image features without an explicit factual basis. Large image datasets with exhaustive finding labels are scarce, particularly for disease-focused applications, because manual annotation is expensive.
method: Fact-Flow decouples report generation into clinical finding identification followed by finding-guided MLLM report generation. It conditions the MLLM on explicit multi-label findings so report composition has a factual basis. To avoid manual finding annotation, an LLM bootstraps a labeled image--multi-label dataset from existing image-report pairs.

title: LLM-Steered Clinical Knowledge Discovery for CVD Outcome Modeling

categories.value: Multimodal Integration with Clinical / Genomic / Biomarkers
AI for Population Health, Public Health & Epidemiology

motivation: CVD outcome models can predict accurately but often remain black boxes, whereas clinical use also requires reproducible factors and stable interactions that form reusable knowledge. Performance-driven high-dimensional learning can exploit cohort-specific proxies and unstable correlations, especially when subgroup uncertainty is high. A discovery process is needed that records auditable evidence rather than merely selecting one high-scoring model, while using clinical semantics to direct limited exploration.
method: EGL samples clinical variable subsets from an Ising-style distribution over binary inclusion masks, whose node biases and pairwise couplings represent marginal and co-inclusion structure. Candidate subsets are repeatedly cross-validated under a fixed budget; a REINFORCE update favors high-reward subsets, while an online evidence ledger accumulates reproducible node and edge evidence. EGL-LLM adds an interpretable LLM control plane with a semantic agenda to steer which subsets and interaction neighborhoods are probed, without changing the evidence definitions or evaluation budget.

title: Localization-Grounded Supervision: Revisiting Vanilla SFT of Large Vision-Language Models for Medical Image Analysis
motivation: Although LVLMs are strongly pretrained, their advantages do not reliably transfer through vanilla SFT to fine-grained medical image analysis, where zero-shot performance is also insufficient. Analyses indicate that SFT leaves attention diffuse and fails to establish fine-grained vision-language semantic alignment with task-relevant regions. In 3D imaging, limited volumetric pretraining further means that LVLMs lack intrinsic 3D spatial alignment.
method: The work first uses attention visualization and DePass-VL, a region-level contribution analysis adapted for LVLMs, to characterize failures of vanilla SFT. Localization-Grounded Supervision adds explicit localization signals to task data during SFT, using pretrained 2D spatial alignment to foster fine-grained semantic alignment. For 3D tasks, it jointly learns semantic objectives and 3D anatomical localization through multi-task training to build volumetric spatial alignment.

title: LoFi: Location-Aware Fine-Grained Representation Learning for Chest X-Ray
motivation: Chest X-ray retrieval and phrase grounding require fine-grained representations because clinically relevant findings are often spatially confined. Contrastive models rely on implicit local image-text alignment without explicit region supervision, while LVLM representations may not generalize well under external validation. Training autoregressive medical models from scratch on image-text-box triples is also difficult because region-level annotations are scarce.
method: LoFi uses a lightweight LLM and a region-level pretrained encoder to jointly optimize sigmoid, captioning, and location-aware captioning losses. The location-aware objective supplies region-level supervision through grounding and dense-captioning tasks, while captioning learns from long-form reports. The learned fine-grained encoder is then integrated into retrieval-based in-context learning to retrieve more suitable demonstrations for chest X-ray grounding.

title: LoHi-Net: A Low-to-High Hierarchical Wavelet Network for Laparoscopic Surgical Smoke Removal
motivation: Electrocautery and similar energy devices produce surgical smoke during laparoscopy, degrading visibility and potentially compromising surgical safety. Existing de-smoking methods generally process spectral components holistically or use frequency information only as auxiliary guidance, overlooking the different behaviors of global smoke and local detail. This creates a trade-off in which removing heavy smoke can damage high-frequency surgical textures and structures.
method: LoHi-Net performs wavelet-based restoration in a low-to-high hierarchy. It first restores low-frequency components to suppress global smoke, then uses the resulting cleaner structural features as priors to guide high-frequency texture refinement through a Low-to-High structural guidance block. Specialized hierarchical Visual Mamba variants model the distinct characteristics of frequency bands while keeping the network compact.

title: Longitudinal Multi-view Modeling for Breast Cancer Risk Prediction
motivation: Breast cancer risk prediction from screening mammography is needed to support personalized screening and earlier detection, particularly for women with dense breasts. Existing longitudinal methods either align only one view or combine multiple views without explicit temporal spatial correspondence, leaving complementary CC/MLO and longitudinal cues underused.
method: LMV-Net explicitly aligns current and prior mammographic feature maps separately for the CC and MLO views using image-based deformation fields. It then applies a breast-wise dual-stream attention block with parallel self-attention and cross-attention to refine longitudinal features and fuse complementary cross-view temporal evidence.

title: Longitudinal Reliability of Cross-Sectional Normative Models Under Measurement Error
motivation: Longitudinal neuroimaging is essential for studying brain aging and disease progression, but common analyses track raw change without population-norm context. When cross-sectional normative models are applied repeatedly, measurement variability from scanners, protocols, and preprocessing can be mistaken for biological deviation, while the reliability of such longitudinal interpretation is largely unquantified.
method: The work introduces the Longitudinal Deviation Index (LDI), defined as the ratio between true inter-individual residual-slope variance and variance expected from measurement error. It derives theoretical LDI values from test-retest data using a pretrained cross-sectional normative model and validates the index against longitudinal data from cognitively normal adults, providing a noise-aware basis for interpreting deviations.

title: LongMedBench: Benchmarking Medical Agents for Long-Horizon Clinical Decision-Making
motivation: Clinical decisions require integrating evolving evidence across many visits, tests, treatments, and outcomes rather than retrieving facts from an isolated encounter. Existing medical-agent benchmarks mainly assess short-horizon QA, tools, simulated encounters, or static temporal questions, and therefore do not systematically test long-horizon EHR reasoning and decision use.
method: LongMedBench converts MIMIC-IV structured records and clinical notes into ordered multi-visit event streams with patient-, visit-, and event-level representations. It supplies note, event, and interaction-context memory modules and evaluates agents through progressively harder factual QA, temporal reasoning, and long-horizon decision-making suites under controlled memory settings.

title: Lost in the Folds: When Cross-Validation Is Not a Deep Ensemble for Uncertainty Estimation
motivation: Ensemble disagreement is often used to estimate epistemic uncertainty for medical image segmentation and trigger reliability-oriented actions such as referral or failure detection. However, K-fold CV models are frequently called deep ensembles even though their differing training subsets mix seed variability with data-exposure effects, making the meaning and suitability of their uncertainty unclear.
method: The study audits terminology in segmentation-uncertainty literature and performs a controlled comparison between five-fold CV ensembles and five-member deep ensembles using otherwise matched configurations. It evaluates their disagreement for calibration, failure detection, annotation ambiguity, and distribution-shift robustness, and adds a lightweight nnU-Net modification for training true same-data, different-seed deep ensembles.

title: Lost in Volume: The CT-SpatialVQA Benchmark for Evaluating Semantic-Spatial Understanding of 3D Medical Vision–Language Models

categories.value: Multimodal Integration with Clinical / Genomic / Biomarkers

motivation: Spatial understanding across CT slices is central to diagnosis and procedural planning, requiring localization and consistent 3D anatomical relationships. Although 3D medical VLMs can produce fluent descriptions, existing benchmarks emphasize descriptive or measurement questions and do not systematically determine whether models ground semantic-spatial reasoning in volumetric evidence rather than priors or language correlations.
method: CT-SpatialVQA builds clinically grounded spatial QA pairs from CT-RATE radiology reports and paired 3D CT volumes through LLM generation, independent LLM validation, and human auditing. Its questions target localization, laterality, directional relations, containment or adjacency, and spatial extent; a standardized protocol evaluates 3D medical VLM answers using both LLM-based and conventional text assessment.

title: LOT-Bridge: A Latent Optimal Transport Bridge Based on Signed Distance Fields for Automatic Skull Defect Reconstruction
motivation: Skull defects require personalized implants, but manual design is costly and time-consuming. Existing SDF latent diffusion approaches accelerate design but require many stochastic noise-to-sample iterations, can introduce incorrect geometry, and may accumulate errors by separately training the decoder and latent generator.
method: LOT-Bridge represents complete and defective skulls as SDFs and formulates reconstruction as optimal transport in both latent and data spaces. An ODE-based latent bridge learns a transport vector field from defective to complete representations for deterministic reverse sampling, while joint optimization of the bridge and decoder combines flow-matching, reconstruction, adversarial, and implant losses. Its decoder includes an Adaptive Morphological Block that adaptively performs feature erosion or dilation during upsampling to refine reconstructed surfaces.

title: Low-Rank Text-Guided Spectral Learning for Semi-supervised MHSI Segmentation
motivation: MHSI can expose subtle tissue biochemical changes, but its highly correlated bands create redundancy and pixel-level pathology annotations are expensive to obtain. Visual-only semi-supervised methods can produce biased pseudo-labels when spatial contrast is weak, while they rarely exploit stable spectral signatures, low-rank structure, or textual clinical knowledge.
method: LoTS-Net uses text-guided spectral channel selection to identify discriminative, low-rank spectral representations while incorporating text semantics into channel selection. It also builds a spectral feature container that stores and retrieves correlated spectral prototypes, guiding spectral-spatial fusion and more reliable pseudo-label generation from labeled and unlabeled samples. The work further extends public MHSI datasets with text prompts to form a microscopic hyperspectral vision-language benchmark.

title: Low-Rank Velocity Fields as a Structural Prior for Unsupervised 4D Medical Image Interpolation
motivation: Endpoint-only unsupervised 4D medical image interpolation must synthesize intermediate volumes from two endpoint scans, despite having little direct supervision for motion. Voxel-wise high-dimensional motion models can fit locally inconsistent high-frequency deformations under this setting, causing unstable boundaries, non-physiological warping, and reduced usefulness for downstream analysis.
method: The framework parameterizes deformation velocity fields with a Tucker low-rank representation comprising globally shared spatial bases and a compact sample-specific core. It estimates these fields across multiple resolutions for coarse-to-fine motion refinement, composes scale-wise deformations at inference, and performs bidirectional continuous-time interpolation to synthesize arbitrary intermediate volumes. The method also relates bounded low-rank parameters to control of velocity-field smoothness energy.

title: Low-Rank-Modulated Functa: Exploring the Latent Space of Implicit Neural Representations for Interpretable Ultrasound Video Analysis
motivation: Ultrasound videos contain clinically important temporal dynamics, and accurate ED and ES identification is required for cardiac functional measures such as ejection fraction. Existing Functa-based INR video representations support reconstruction but leave their latent-space structure and interpretability largely unexplored, despite video size, noise, and temporal redundancy.
method: LRM-Functa builds on time-resolved VidFuncta modulation vectors and constrains them to a learned low-rank subspace. A shared INR remains conditioned on video-level and temporally structured modulation codes, producing compact reconstructions while making latent temporal trajectories visualizable. The structured trajectories can be traversed to synthesize smooth cardiac-cycle frames and directly identify ED and ES indices without additional task-specific training.

title: Low-Resource Cross-Modality Nucleus Detection via One-Sided Domain Adaptation
motivation: Nucleus detection models often fail to generalize across microscopy modalities because of domain shift. GAN- and diffusion-based unsupervised adaptation usually assume abundant unlabelled target images, but in low-resource target domains they degrade, while bidirectional GAN alternatives are computationally costly and can depend on unreliable pseudo-labels.
method: The proposed one-sided UDA framework translates labeled source microscopy images into target style with a single GAN and trains a target-domain nucleus detector on the translated images. Its masked contrastive learning module aligns corresponding source and translated patch features, sampling positives from nucleus regions and negatives from background, while the detector jointly augments discriminator supervision to preserve detection semantics. Differentiable augmentation of scarce target and translated images is used to reduce discriminator overfitting.

title: LRMIL: Efficient Low-Resolution Multiple Instance Learning via High-Resolution Knowledge Distillation for Whole Slide Image Classification
motivation: Whole slide image classification must handle extremely large images with limited patch-level annotation, making multiple instance learning useful for slide-level prediction. Existing methods extensively encode high-resolution patches, which is computationally expensive and misses global tissue architecture and spatial context visible at lower magnification. A method is needed that preserves HR semantic information while enabling efficient LR-only inference.
method: LRMIL transfers high-resolution (HR) semantic knowledge to low-resolution (LR) representations through two distillation stages. Patch-level cross-resolution distillation aligns HR patch embeddings with spatially corresponding LR token regions, after which slide-level distillation trains an LR student MIL model using bag supervision and guidance from an HR teacher. Inference uses only LR patches and the distilled student, reducing preprocessing and feature-extraction cost.

title: L-TGVN: Leveraging Longitudinal Priors for Personalized Rapid MRI
motivation: MRI is slow, motivating undersampling, but aggressive undersampling makes the linear inverse problem ill-posed and leaves many reconstructions compatible with the measurements. Population-trained reconstruction priors become insufficient at high accelerations, while longitudinal scans provide useful patient-specific context. Temporal changes, misalignment, and protocol drift make naive prior reuse unsafe because it can suppress real pathology or introduce incorrect structures.
method: L-TGVN is a longitudinal trust-guided variational network that uses the latest prior scan as subject-specific side information for reconstructing a heavily undersampled current MRI. It constrains the prior's influence to remain consistent with acquired k-space measurements, helping preserve interval changes rather than blindly copying the prior. The design avoids explicit preregistration and tolerates protocol differences across visits.

title: LumiState: Retinex-inspired Illumination Decoupling in 4D Gaussian Splatting for Endoscopic Reconstruction
motivation: Dynamic endoscopic reconstruction is important for surgical navigation, but near-field coaxial lighting, wet-tissue specularities, exposure changes, and shadows violate the photometric consistency assumed by 3D/4D Gaussian Splatting. These variations become entangled with Gaussian attributes, causing artifacts and degraded geometry and appearance. Existing physically based methods assume unsuitable distant lighting or static scenes, while learned corrections lack physically meaningful reflectance-illumination separation.
method: LumiState incorporates Retinex-inspired decomposition into 4D Gaussian Splatting by modeling each frame as view-independent tissue reflectance multiplied by a varying illumination map. A lightweight UNet estimates the illumination from a bright-channel projection and provides an illumination embedding; a fusion network then modulates per-Gaussian spherical-harmonic coefficients using this embedding and Gaussian position. Two-stage training and a bright-channel prior regularize the ill-posed decomposition and support controllable illumination editing.

title: M3D-QAdapter: 3D Medical VQA with Lesion-Level Finding-Segmentation Alignment and Query-Driven Adaptive Token Reduction
motivation: 3D medical VQA on CT must represent volumetric context, but a volume can produce thousands of visual tokens, creating high memory and latency costs. Lesions are sparse and severe negative-positive imbalance can overwhelm diagnostic signals and bias models toward no-finding answers. Existing slice, pooling, or organ-level compression loses 3D detail and generally reduces tokens without using the question context; lesion-level alignment is also hindered by incomplete annotations.
method: M3D-QAdapter first trains a 3D vision encoder with image-report alignment enhanced by lesion-level finding-segmentation correspondences. Its safe negative mining heuristic excludes likely unannotated findings from the alignment loss, reducing harmful negatives under incomplete annotations and severe imbalance. During VQA, a question-dependent planner selects anatomical regions, invokes text-prompted 3D segmentation, and applies geometry-semantic farthest point sampling to retain representative tokens for the LLM.

title: MAGE: Color-Invariant and Spatial Knowledge Distillation for Gastric Neoplasm Classification

categories.value: AI for Neglected Diseases & Limited-Resource Settings

motivation: Differentiating gastric adenoma from carcinoma is clinically important but difficult because the classes look highly similar and have ambiguous boundaries. ROI-based pipelines propagate localization errors and lose surrounding context, whereas full-image classifiers may dilute subtle lesion patterns and often exploit background or color artifacts. The work is needed to make models focus on intrinsic morphology while remaining deployable without masks.
method: MAGE trains an auxiliary local expert on images that retain the neoplasm inside the ground-truth mask in grayscale while zeroing the background. This expert learns color-invariant morphological cues and transfers classification logits and spatial attention maps to a deployable full-image branch through dual-objective distillation. The inference model therefore needs no annotated mask while receiving spatial guidance toward lesion structure and retaining useful color information.

title: MAGEFormer: Learning Metric-Consistent Representations for Anisotropic CT Segmentation
motivation: Clinical CT is often anisotropic, with much coarser through-plane spacing than in-plane spacing, whereas ViT-based segmentation commonly assumes an isotropic voxel lattice. This metric mismatch makes voxel-index neighborhoods inconsistent with physical anatomy and can harm boundaries of small or low-contrast structures; isotropic resampling can further degrade accuracy. A representation-level solution is needed to enforce physical metric consistency beyond index-based positional encodings or localized thickness adaptations.
method: MAGEFormer embeds physical voxel spacing into representation learning through three components. Metric-Adaptive Spatial Embedding calibrates positional frequencies by spacing, Geometry-Constrained Attention adds metric-aware biases to suppress physically implausible correlations, and Geometric View Voting aggregates deterministic subvoxel views at inference to reduce discretization bias. Together they calibrate encoding, feature interaction, and prediction for anisotropic CT.

title: Making HE Histopathological Images More Colorful by Conditional Flow Matching
motivation: HES staining adds saffron to highlight collagen, which can aid diagnosis, but it is more expensive than HE staining and limits access to HES-based analysis. Converting HES to HE is straightforward by removing the saffron component, whereas generating realistic saffron from HE is difficult. Existing stain-translation methods, including UNet and GAN approaches, do not fully exploit a physically meaningful concentration representation for this inverse task.
method: The method first separates an HE image into hematoxylin and eosin concentration maps using stain separation in optical-density space. A conditional Flow Matching model generates the missing saffron concentration conditioned on these maps, and the HES RGB image is reconstructed with the Beer-Lambert law. Operating in concentration space makes stain composition approximately linear and supports efficient high-resolution synthesis.

title: MamaDino: Mammography-Aware Multi-view Attentional DINO for 3-Year Breast Cancer Risk Prediction

categories.value: AI for Population Health, Public Health & Epidemiology

motivation: Screening programs use largely uniform intervals despite substantial heterogeneity in individual breast cancer risk, motivating image-based personalized prediction. Leading models often use high-resolution inputs, CNN backbones, and limited explicit contralateral reasoning, which increases computational cost and may underuse complementary bilateral information. The work investigates whether a lower-resolution hybrid model with explicit left-right fusion can retain strong 3-year risk prediction.
method: MamaDino combines frozen self-supervised DINOv3 ViT-S features with a trainable CNN encoder on 512×512 mammograms. A BilateralMixer explicitly aggregates information between left and right breasts to produce a 3-year risk score, combining transformer global representations, CNN texture cues, and contralateral reasoning. The model is designed to test whether structured multiview fusion can offset the reduced input resolution.

title: Mamba Based Anisotropic Diffusion Model for Speckle Noise Reduction in Ultrasound Images
motivation: Ultrasound speckle is signal-dependent and can obscure fine anatomy, reducing diagnostic and automated-analysis quality. Classical filters and PDE diffusion offer interpretability but depend on manually tuned functions and parameters and can oversmooth or fail in textured regions, while purely deep models lack physical grounding. A hybrid approach is needed to combine adaptive restoration with the structure and interpretability of diffusion dynamics.
method: The method embeds a hyperbolic-parabolic diffusion model into a learnable iterative denoising system. Two Mamba-based networks estimate the gray-level indicator and edge detector at each iteration, whose product forms the diffusion function used in the PDE update. End-to-end training with paired noisy-clean images preserves the PDE structure while adapting smoothing to local intensity, edges, and broader context.

title: MammoFlow: Multiview Mammogram Synthesis with Anatomically Consistent Flow Matching
motivation: Clinical mammography relies on paired CC and MLO projections whose complementary views help localize abnormalities, but high-quality paired datasets are scarce, privacy-sensitive, and cancer cases are imbalanced. Existing synthesis methods mainly generate single views, require a reference view, or ignore explicit 3D anatomical relationships, leading to cross-view artifacts. A method is needed to generate realistic paired mammograms with anatomically consistent projections for data augmentation and downstream learning.
method: MammoFlow augments a pretrained rectified-flow model with an alignment module that searches a 2D affine subspace to establish correspondence between CC and MLO anatomy. It applies a differentiable Earth Mover’s Distance loss to match the aligned one-dimensional anteroposterior tissue-intensity distributions of the generated views. A temporal loss scheduler reduces the constraint when denoised images are still blurry, allowing paired synthesis with an implicit 3D consistency prior.

title: MAP-Diff: Multi-anchor Guided Diffusion for Progressive 3D Whole-Body Low-Dose PET Denoising
motivation: Low-dose PET lowers radiation exposure but introduces severe noise and quantitative degradation, threatening diagnostic reliability. Existing diffusion denoisers mainly supervise the final full-dose reconstruction, leaving their intermediate reverse states unconstrained. This neglects the physically progressive, dose-dependent structure of PET acquisition and can yield dose-inconsistent trajectories.
method: MAP-Diff constrains a 3D PET diffusion model with clinically acquired intermediate-dose images used as trajectory anchors. It calibrates anchor timesteps by matching simulated diffusion degradation to real multi-dose PET degradation and applies a timestep-weighted anchor loss. This extends supervision across the reverse trajectory, enabling dose-consistent intermediate restoration from an ultra-low-dose input.

title: MARBLE: Lightweight EEG-to-fMRI Translation via Mamba-Attention and ROI-Conditioned Decoding
motivation: fMRI provides spatially resolved whole-brain BOLD measurements but is costly, non-portable, and restrictive to acquire, whereas EEG is inexpensive and temporally precise. Existing whole-brain EEG-to-fMRI methods commonly use Transformer encoders without an inductive bias for HRF-driven delayed dynamics. Their ROI conditioning also offers limited transparency about how EEG features produce regional predictions.
method: MARBLE uses a hybrid Mamba-Transformer encoder for end-to-end whole-brain EEG-to-fMRI translation. Selective state-space modeling supplies an inductive bias for HRF-related causal and delayed temporal structure, while attention refines the shared latent representation. ROI-specific decoders use cross-attention on this representation to predict regional BOLD series and expose region-specific electrode contributions.

title: Marginal Constrained Morphological Prototype Learning for Patch Search in Whole Slide Images
motivation: WSIs are gigapixel images in which diagnostically decisive morphology may occupy only a small subset of thousands of patches. Conventional fixed-encoder MIL pipelines either process all patches at high cost or use heuristic sampling that can miss rare critical evidence. Independently learned prototypes may also represent frequent but non-discriminative morphology rather than slide-level diagnostic signals.
method: MMPL formulates WSI diagnosis as task-aware retrieval of a compact set of informative patches. It learns global morphological prototypes through a Sinkhorn-Knopp assignment objective against a momentum-stabilized feature queue, encouraging balanced and diverse prototype use. Prototype-guided top-k selection then couples patch retrieval, slide-level prediction, and encoder optimization in one end-to-end objective.

title: MaRS: Robust Out-of-Distribution Detection via Mahalanobis Residual Scoring
motivation: Medical imaging models can fail silently under shifts in patients, scanners, protocols, or artifacts, making reliable OOD detection essential for safe deployment. Confidence and feature-distance methods can be unreliable in medical settings or high-dimensional embeddings. Latent reconstruction methods often use L2 residual norms, which discard anisotropic residual structure and can hide informative OOD deviations.
method: MaRS is a lightweight, label-free post-hoc OOD detector operating on frozen foundation-model features. A lightweight autoencoder learns the in-distribution feature manifold, and MaRS computes reconstruction residuals. It scores those residuals with a Mahalanobis distance using their covariance, emphasizing deviations in low-variance residual directions rather than uniformly aggregating them with L2.

title: Mask to Concept: Auto-Promptable SAM3 via Efficient Test-Time Concept Embedding Search for Few-Shot Annotation
motivation: Pixel-level medical segmentation annotations are expensive, while prompt-based SAM tools require manual geometric input for every image and do not scale well. Existing training-free automatic annotators add external matchers or auxiliary networks and often remain inconsistent across instances. Although SAM3 supports reusable text concepts, vague descriptions and limited fine-grained clinical knowledge hinder direct use in medical imaging.
method: M2C adapts frozen SAM3 for few-shot medical annotation by replacing manually written concepts with a learnable concept embedding. Given labeled masks, the embedding prompts SAM3 and is updated through segmentation-error gradients, allowing visual concepts to be refined without external modules or parameter retraining. Its HUE module combines prediction entropy with concept-to-box prompting inconsistency to route uncertain cases for correction; corrected masks further update the embedding in an active annotation loop.

title: Mask-Guided Attention Regulation for Anatomically Consistent Counterfactual CXR Synthesis
motivation: Counterfactual CXR generation should alter a pathology while preserving patient-specific anatomy, supporting controlled analysis and data augmentation.
