Diffusion editing can propagate stable anatomical semantics globally through self-attention, causing non-target structural distortion. Subtle localized pathologies also create weak, noisy conditioning signals, making lesion position and extent unstable; retraining control branches adds deployment burden.
method: The framework regulates attention during conditional diffusion sampling without retraining. Anatomy-aware organ masks gate self-attention to confine structural interactions to valid anatomical ROIs. A pathology-guided module reweights pathology-token cross-attention within target regions early in denoising and applies lightweight latent corrections based on an attention-concentration energy to control lesion location and extent.

title: MASurv: Risk-Conditional Martingale Adversarial Training for Calibrated Multi-slide Survival Prediction in Whole-Slide Histopathology Images
motivation: WSI survival MIL methods are usually optimized for discrimination metrics such as C-index, which do not assess the absolute accuracy of predicted risks. Poor calibration can systematically misestimate risk for clinical subgroups and create inequitable treatment guidance. Global post-hoc recalibration cannot enforce conditional calibration under censoring and requires target-domain data that may be unavailable during cross-institution deployment.
method: MASurv augments discrete-time WSI survival MIL training with an Adversarial Conditional Moment Test (ACMT). ACMT adversarially enforces time-local conditional moment orthogonality of counting-process martingale residual increments within matched risk strata, directly targeting calibration under censoring. A second ACMT task regularizes prediction consistency among multiple slides from the same patient.

title: Maximizing Domain Generalization in Automated Fetal Brain Biometry
motivation: Fetal brain biometry from MRI supports prenatal neurodevelopment assessment and diagnosis, but manual landmark-based measurement is labor-intensive and variable between raters. Automated models can degrade substantially in new clinical environments because scanners, protocols, reconstruction methods, gestational ages, and abnormalities vary. Domain generalization for fetal biometry remains underexplored, and adaptation should work without target labels or source-data access.
method: BioTTA is a backbone-agnostic, source-free unsupervised test-time adaptation framework for fetal brain biometry. Starting from a source-pretrained model that predicts landmark heatmaps and biometric scalars, it adapts each unlabeled target sample using length-consistency, entropy-minimization, and boundary-gradient objectives. Atlas-guided anatomical priors constrain these self-supervised objectives, using consistency between heatmap landmarks and scalar measurements as adaptation supervision.

title: MBFAD: Benchmarking Balance Function Assessment with Environmental Perturbation and Synergistic Tasks
motivation: Balance assessment is important for functional independence and fall prevention, but clinical scales are subjective snapshot measures. Kinematic and plantar-pressure data are complementary, yet existing data and methods rarely synchronize both modalities under genuine instability or use activity context to identify stability states. Many approaches separate activity recognition from fall detection, limiting pre-emptive assessment in complex activities.
method: MBFAD provides synchronized whole-body kinematics and plantar-pressure data for static, dynamic, and reactive balance activities, including environmentally induced imbalance states. The proposed M^2-Balance model jointly performs activity recognition and balance-function assessment, treating activity semantics as a prior for stability analysis. HSConv recursively extracts multi-scale semantic features, while CSConv uses an expected channel damage matrix to reduce redundancy and identify stability-sensitive channels.

title: MDL-DA Track: Self-supervised Sperm Motility Direction Learning and Density-Adaptive Association for Sperm Tracking
motivation: Accurate sperm tracking is needed for CASA to derive clinically relevant motion parameters. Sperm are small and visually homogeneous, move nonlinearly, and can shift between sparse and crowded distributions, so appearance-only or motion-only association is unreliable. Direction labels are also difficult to obtain, while existing trackers do not adequately model local density and sperm-specific orientation.
method: MDL-DA Track combines self-supervised Sperm Motility Direction Learning (SMDL) with Density-Adaptive Object Association (DOA). SMDL uses short-term temporal bounding-box displacement as pseudo-supervision for a direction branch jointly trained with YOLOX detection, yielding geometric orientation cues without direction labels. DOA estimates local density, using motion-dominant matching in sparse regions and adaptively combining motion, appearance, and learned direction features in dense regions.

title: MDPNet: A Multi-Scale Deformable Prototype Network for Accurate and Interpretable Medical Image Classification
motivation: Medical image classifiers need both accurate diagnoses and rationales that clinicians can inspect. Post-hoc saliency explanations can be unstable and do not expose decision logic, while conventional prototype models use rigid, single-scale contiguous patches. This can miss distributed diagnostic evidence and the joint local-detail/global-context information needed in clinical images.
method: MDPNet combines a Multi-Scale Feature Extraction Module (MSFEM) with deformable prototype learning for interpretable medical image classification. MSFEM captures fine morphological details and global context, while independently movable prototype subparts align a prototype with spatially variable or non-adjacent evidence. A logit-adjusted loss calibrates decision boundaries under class imbalance.

title: MEASURE: Multi-Task Slice Selection and Regression for Neonatal Brain Biometry
motivation: Neonatal MRI biometry provides objective markers of brain growth and injury in preterm-born infants, but manual Kidokoro-protocol measurements are slow and variable between raters. Existing automation commonly depends on dense segmentation or landmark annotations, which are expensive and vulnerable to domain shifts. A direct, annotation-efficient way to identify standard planes and estimate measurements is therefore needed.
method: MEASURE follows the clinical workflow in two stages without voxel-level supervision. A ViT-based multi-task selector identifies the optimal measurement plane for each biometric, then a multi-task regression network jointly predicts the measurements using measurement-specific spatial attention. This explicit plane selection and shared prediction design target efficient, anatomy-aware neonatal biometry.

title: Measuring Prediction Uncertainty in Neural Cellular Automata
motivation: Medical segmentation systems can fail silently under unusual anatomy, poor image quality, or distribution shifts, so they must indicate when a mask is unreliable. Neural cellular automata generate predictions iteratively, but common uncertainty methods were designed for one-pass feed-forward models and may overlook instability in inference dynamics. A native uncertainty measure is needed for NCA-based segmentation.
method: The work introduces resilience, a training-free uncertainty score for NCA segmentation. It perturbs the final latent automaton state slightly, evolves the NCA for additional steps, and measures whether the resulting segmentation recovers the original solution. This directly tests the stability of the learned dynamics and attractor-like behavior without architectural changes or retraining.

title: Measuring What VLMs Don’t Say: Validation Metrics Hide Clinical Terminology Erasure in Radiology Report Generation

categories.value: Multimodal Integration with Clinical / Genomic / Biomarkers

motivation: Radiology report generation should preserve clinically useful and equitable information, yet standard text-overlap metrics can reward generic normal-finding templates. Such template collapse can omit patient-specific clinical terminology while retaining high aggregate scores, and conventional metrics do not reveal demographic terminology redistribution. Evaluation must therefore measure both missing clinical language and shifts in group-associated vocabulary.
method: The paper proposes Clinical Association Displacement (CAD), which compares demographic word associations in human reference reports and generated reports at the vocabulary level. Its summary metric, Weighted Association Erasure (WAE), quantifies overall displacement and loss of clinically informative terminology across groups. The framework is used to audit how deterministic and stochastic decoding affect specificity and demographic associations beyond standard overlap scores.

title: MEC: A Multi-expert Consultation Framework for Synergizing Frozen Foundation Models in Whole Slide Image Analysis
motivation: Whole-slide image analysis commonly uses a frozen Pathology Foundation Model followed by MIL, but different PFMs have distinct biases and no single model is consistently best across tasks. Model selection discards complementary expertise, feature alignment can be resource-intensive and task-agnostic, and naive ensembles may dilute useful signals. A framework is needed to exploit complementary, task-specific diagnostic evidence from multiple PFMs.
method: MEC treats heterogeneous frozen Pathology Foundation Models as independent digital experts within a weight-based MIL aggregator. Each expert localizes task-specific discriminative regions in its own feature space; Stochastic Evidence Masking suppresses top-ranked features to expose complementary cues. MEC then aggregates the collective consultation evidence and individual expert opinions into a robust multi-view decision.

title: MEC: Medical Evidence Capsules for Retrieval-Augmented Generation in Medical Multimodal Question Answering
motivation: RAG is used in medical multimodal QA to improve accuracy and reduce hallucinations, but existing methods often retrieve heterogeneous sources separately and simply concatenate them. Textual, structured, model-based, and imaging evidence differ in representation and granularity, making reliable alignment between conclusions and traceable evidence difficult. Medical QA therefore needs explicit, controllable evidence-use relationships rather than more loosely assembled context.
method: Medical Evidence Capsules (MEC) normalize heterogeneous evidence into compact units containing a medical assertion, retrieval cue, and citable evidence snippet. These capsules provide a unified interface through which text, structured knowledge, model-encoded experience, and image/report evidence can be jointly retrieved and invoked during generation. The work also constructs a multimodal retrieval corpus to support this evidence organization.

title: Med3D-R1: Mitigating Narrative Bias and Enhancing Reasoning Consistency in 3D Medical Vision-Language Models
motivation: 3D CT VLMs face unstable alignment between high-dimensional volumetric features and textual embeddings. Standardized radiology reports can also induce a positional narrative bias, with normal findings early and abnormalities later, reducing abnormality sensitivity during autoregressive training. Final-answer-oriented supervision further leaves intermediate clinical reasoning insufficiently constrained by report evidence.
method: Med3D-R1 first fine-tunes a 3D CT VLM with a Residual Alignment Mechanism (RAM) and Abnormality Re-Weighting (ARW). RAM anchors volumetric tokens to a reference embedding to stabilize 3D-text projection, while ARW reweights abnormality tokens to counter positional narrative priors. A subsequent reasoning-aware reinforcement-learning stage applies a consistency reward that aligns generated reasoning traces with report-supported evidence and penalizes unsupported statements.

title: Med-CAP: Counterfactual Evidence and Adaptive Prior Suppression for Robust Medical Visual Question Answering
motivation: Med-VQA is trained with limited and imbalanced medical data, allowing models to rely on frequent answer distributions and question-template language rather than pathology in the image. These imbalance and modality-shortcut biases especially harm rare, clinically important cases and out-of-distribution generalization. Robust Med-VQA needs both visually grounded reasoning and calibration against sample-specific language priors.
method: Med-CAP combines Counterfactual Evidence Modeling (CEM) and Adaptive Prior Suppression (APS). CEM uses feature-gradient attribution to form evidence-preserving and evidence-dropping counterfactual inputs, then applies sufficiency-and-necessity constraints to make decisions visually grounded. APS dynamically subtracts a question-only language prior from fused logits according to prior confidence and counterfactual evidence strength.

title: MedCenterDet: A Center-Based Object Detection Framework for 3D Medical Image
motivation: Precise 3D target localization is clinically important, but voxel-level segmentation is costly to annotate and lesion boundaries can be ambiguous. Bounding-box detection is more efficient, yet anchor-based 3D methods require substantial tuning and expand computation across a large search space; existing anchor-free alternatives can be difficult to optimize or rely on rigid priors. A flexible detector is needed that localizes diverse targets without predefined anchors.
method: MedCenterDet is an anchor-free, center-based 3D detector that predicts object-center heatmaps and analytically decodes bounding-box geometry. Its anisotropic Gaussian targets encode object-specific extents, while a Counterfactual Attention Learning module contrasts factual attention with random-noise interventions to optimize attention toward target structures. A second refinement stage uses multi-scale features to improve proposal confidence and 3D box precision.

title: MedConcept: Unsupervised Concept Discovery for Interpretability in Medical VLMs

categories.value: Multimodal Integration with Clinical / Genomic / Biomarkers

motivation: Medical VLMs can perform strongly but their latent representations remain opaque, limiting trust in high-stakes clinical use. Gradient- and attention-based explanations are usually task-specific and do not reveal reusable concept-level structure in pretrained multimodal representations. Moreover, concept-discovery work lacks scalable quantitative evidence that its inferred concepts agree with clinical semantics.
method: MedConcept applies a sparse autoencoder to global representations from a pretrained medical VLM, decomposing polysemantic embeddings into sparse latent concept activations. It names these units by similarity matching with embeddings of a clinically curated concept vocabulary and generates patient-level pseudo-report-style concept summaries. For post-hoc evaluation only, an independently pretrained frozen medical LLM compares predicted concepts with paired radiology reports using Aligned, Unaligned, and Uncertain scores.

title: MedEnv: Scaling Multimodal Virtual Medical Environments for Long-Horizon Diagnosis
motivation: Clinical diagnosis requires long-horizon, multi-turn evidence gathering and decision-making, whereas static medical VQA does not train or assess these capabilities. Existing EHR-driven simulators are limited by missing or noisy records and weak interaction logic, while synthetic settings can be unrealistic or inconsistent. A scalable environment with reliable multimodal evidence and feedback for long-horizon policy learning is therefore needed.
method: MedEnv builds DiagWorld, an EHR-grounded multimodal simulator that converts longitudinal MIMIC-IV records into over 496K interactive diagnostic trajectories. It augments incomplete patient-specific evidence with a disease-level knowledge base and constraint validation, and provides workflow-aligned tools for retrieval, tests, EHR fragments, and chest X-ray analysis. Within this environment, Diagnosis-R1 uses supervised initialization followed by reinforcement learning with terminal correctness and dense confidence-increase rewards after each action.

title: MedExpMem: Adapting Experience Memory for Differential Diagnosis
motivation: Experienced clinicians accumulate comparative insights that distinguish easily confused diseases, but VLMs are stateless across diagnostic encounters. Fine-tuning is often impractical for continual clinical adaptation because of privacy, cost, and catastrophic-forgetting concerns. Standard RAG and agent memory also emphasize disease descriptions, facts, or histories rather than persistent, structured differential reasoning.
method: MedExpMem is a persistent, parameter-free experience memory for VLM diagnostic agents. It converts the agent's own errors into structured notes for diagnosis pairs, containing discriminative features, actionable decision rules, and reasoning-error patterns. Memory is built through zero-shot error discovery followed by reflective re-diagnosis and refinement, then retrieved with anatomical scope to guide future differential diagnosis.

title: MedFM-Robust: Benchmarking Robustness of Medical Foundation Models
motivation: Medical foundation models may perform well on clean benchmarks but encounter acquisition artifacts, patient-related variation, and modality-specific degradations in practice. Generic corruption tests do not capture effects such as CT beam hardening, MRI ghosting, or pathology stain variation. The field also lacks a unified robustness evaluation spanning vision-language tasks, segmentation, and fine-tuning choices.
method: MedFM-Robust provides a unified robustness benchmark for medical VLMs and SAM-based segmentation models. It applies modality-adaptive base and medical-specific perturbations across eight modalities, calibrated into five severity levels, and evaluates VQA, captioning, visual grounding, and segmentation. The benchmark also compares fine-tuning strategies to characterize their robustness implications in clinical adaptation.

title: MedFuse-Seg: Multi-level Visual and Semantic Context Fusion for Segmentation-Based Medical Reasoning
motivation: Language-driven medical segmentation could reduce reliance on manually placed spatial prompts, but current systems are sensitive to prompt wording and often lack diverse, reasoning-rich training data. Approaches that separately process semantic understanding and localization can lose fine boundary detail when visual information is compressed. Complex clinical queries require both robust semantic interpretation and precise anatomical delineation.
method: MedFuse-Seg constructs Med-ReasonSeg, a 539,383-pair image-mask-Q&A dataset spanning nine modalities, with referring and semantic prompts generated and verified through a hierarchical LLM pipeline. Its architecture combines MedSigLIP, MedGemma, and MedSAM: MedGemma-guided reasoning supports mask decoding, while a Multi-Level Context Fusion block injects hierarchical MedSigLIP features into the MedSAM encoder. This couples clinical semantic reasoning with multi-scale spatial detail for prompt-based segmentation.

title: Medical Image Spatial Grounding with Semantic Sampling
motivation: Medical VLM research has focused largely on report generation, VQA, and disease identification, leaving the practical reliability of spatially grounded reasoning unclear. Three-dimensional medical images introduce distinct challenges involving slice views, coordinate systems, and anatomical, directional, and relational language. Existing grounding studies do not systematically isolate these factors or provide a controlled evaluation of 3D grounding failures.
method: The work introduces MIS-Ground, a controlled benchmark for 3D anatomical spatial grounding that varies modality, slice direction, coordinate convention, visual prompts, terminology, and question types. It evaluates whether VLMs can identify, localize, and distinguish structures across serialized medical volumes. It also proposes MIS-SemSam, a low-cost, inference-time, model-agnostic method that samples groups of semantically similar tokens to improve spatial reasoning.

title: Medical Knowledge-Guided Fusion of Holistic Hospital Data for Tumor Survival Analysis
motivation: Tumor survival depends on complementary pathology, genomic, clinical, and treatment information, so unimodal models cannot capture all prognostic determinants. Existing multimodal approaches often support fixed modality combinations or learn cross-modal interactions purely from limited cohorts, making them prone to spurious correlations. Medical knowledge is needed to explicitly guide scalable fusion across heterogeneous hospital data rather than merely serving as an auxiliary input.
method: MKGSurv organizes holistic hospital data into pathology, genomics, clinical, and treatment disciplines, and uses LLMs to derive pairwise relevance scores, relationship descriptions, and survival-oriented insights. A Correlation-Aware Graph Attention Network uses the knowledge-derived descriptions to guide cross-disciplinary message passing. A Correlation-Guided Alignment loss further aligns learned latent correlations with the quantified relevance scores.

title: MedObvious: Exposing the Medical Moravec’s Paradox in VLMs via Clinical Triage

categories.value: Multimodal Integration with Clinical / Genomic / Biomarkers

motivation: Fluent diagnostic narratives from VLMs do not ensure that they have verified whether an image is valid and coherent to interpret. Clinicians perform pre-diagnostic checks of modality, anatomy, view, orientation, and integrity, particularly when reasoning over image sets, slices, or series. Existing medical VLM benchmarks largely assume these checks are solved and can therefore overlook a safety-critical failure mode.
method: MedObvious is a 1,880-task benchmark for pre-diagnostic visual sanity checking over 2x2 and 3x3 medical image grids. It uses five progressive tiers and five evaluation formats to test outlier detection or identification, covering clinical safety failures, synthetic visual inconsistencies, and negative controls with no outlier. The benchmark evaluates set-level coherence before diagnosis, including modality, anatomy, viewpoint, orientation, and image-integrity checks.

title: MedPro: Dual-View Propagation and Prototypical Assessment for Training-Free Few-Shot Medical Segmentation
motivation: Few-shot medical segmentation is limited by the high cost of expert pixel-level annotations, motivating agile training-free use of foundation models. SAM2 can propagate support masks directly, but cross-subject intensity shifts, low contrast, and similar adjacent structures can cause unstable propagation and spatial drift. Its limited high-level semantic discrimination also makes it difficult to verify that a propagated mask remains anatomically correct.
method: MedPro is a training-free few-shot segmentation framework built around SAM2 propagation. It first applies histogram matching to align support and query intensity distributions, then forms global and focus-zoomed local pseudo-video sequences for bidirectional propagation. Candidate masks are finally assessed against DINOv2-derived support prototypes using semantic similarity, selecting the mask with stronger anatomical consistency.

title: MedPruner: Training-Free Hierarchical Token Pruning for Efficient 3D Medical Image Understanding in Vision-Language Models
motivation: Processing high-resolution CT or MRI volumes in VLMs creates a large visual-token burden that hinders practical clinical inference and consumes context needed for other information. Directly concatenating consecutive 2D slices introduces major redundancy because neighboring slices are highly similar. Fixed pruning ratios also fail to account for heterogeneous information density and different visual-backbone attention patterns.
method: MedPruner is a training-free, model-agnostic hierarchical pruning framework for 3D medical VLM inputs. Its Inter-slice Anchor-based Filtering removes redundant slices, and Dynamic Information Nucleus Selection adaptively retains visual tokens according to cumulative attention weights. The two-stage design compresses slices and tokens according to their information content while preserving diagnostically relevant signals.

title: MedQ-Engine: A Closed-Loop Data Engine for Evolving MLLMs in Medical Image Quality Assessment
motivation: Med-IQA is necessary for reliable diagnosis and clinical AI deployment, but MLLMs remain weaker than experts, especially for descriptive assessments with clinical reasoning. Descriptive expert annotations are expensive, while simple scores provide limited learning signal. One-time data collection also cannot target the model's changing, concentrated failure patterns after each update.
method: MedQ-Engine iteratively improves MLLMs for Med-IQA through evaluating, exploring, and evolving phases. It clusters development-set failures into prototypes, uses them as retrieval anchors over a large image pool, and combines AI pre-annotation with progressive human verification. Entropy-guided routing triages annotations to control cost, while quality-assured data are used for fine-tuning and subsequent re-evaluation.

title: MedRAG-SCA: A Retrieval-Augmented Self-correcting Agent for Clinically Compliant Cross-Modality MRI Synthesis

categories.value: AI for Neglected Diseases & Limited-Resource Settings

motivation: Brain MRI acquisitions are often incomplete because of contraindications, motion, or time constraints, although neuro-oncology workflows require multiple complementary modalities. Existing synthesis models can appear visually realistic while violating imaging protocols such as CSF suppression, so pixel-level quality does not guarantee clinical validity. A method is needed that grounds synthesis in measurable guidelines, verifies outputs clinically, and corrects violations without erasing pathology.
method: MedRAG-SCA uses a Retrieve–Verify–Refine agentic loop for clinically compliant cross-modality MRI synthesis. A protocol-aware RAG consultant converts ACR guidance into quantitative pixel-space criteria, while an Anatomist–Radiologist–Diagnostician committee verifies geometry, modality fidelity, and pathology preservation. A targeted refinement controller inpaints only violating regions, and a geometric fail-safe relaxes intensity constraints in complex edema cases to protect anatomy.

title: MedTri: Structured Medical Report Normalization for Enhanced Vision–Language Pretraining
motivation: Medical vision–language pretraining uses reports as supervision, but raw reports vary in style, length, and structure and often include image-irrelevant clinical content. This heterogeneity weakens fine-grained image–text alignment, while existing entity-based or cloud LLM normalization either discards imaging detail or raises computational and privacy concerns. A lightweight, anatomically expressive, locally deployable normalization method is needed.
method: MedTri normalizes free-text reports into [Anatomical Entity: Radiologic Description + Diagnosis Category] triplets. The anatomy-grounded structure retains morphological and spatial information while removing stylistic and image-irrelevant content, providing consistent local supervision for vision–language pretraining. Its modular interface also supports knowledge enrichment and anatomy-grounded counterfactual text augmentation.

title: MedTriage-LM: Anatomically Grounded Visual Phenotype Synthesis for Interpretable ED Triage

categories.value: Multimodal Integration with Clinical / Genomic / Biomarkers

motivation: Emergency department triage is time-critical and depends on subjective judgments that can produce inconsistent severity assessment and resource allocation. Existing automated systems based on MIMIC-IV-ED mainly use tabular and textual data, while the cohort lacks bedside visual records even though clinicians rely on visual distress cues. A practical approach is needed to inject anatomically grounded visual information and produce actionable triage instructions rather than only numerical risk scores.
method: MedTriage-LM generates synthetic Visual Phenotype Maps by projecting clinical evidence onto a canonical human template with a weakly supervised Gaussian field generator. Cross-attention integrates these spatial maps with structured triage variables and clinical text in a Transformer architecture using clinical and vision encoders. The model predicts actionable three-class triage instructions and generates spatially grounded textual rationales.

title: MedTriFlow: Efficient Resolution-Agnostic 3D Medical Image Generation with Implicit Triplane Representation
motivation: 3D medical image generation is expensive because voxel-based models scale cubically with resolution and tie their latent grids to a fixed output size. Consequently, they cannot flexibly generate the same anatomy at different resolutions without retraining, despite heterogeneous clinical imaging requirements. Existing triplane methods either require costly instance optimization or remain constrained by voxel-grid supervision, motivating an efficient resolution-agnostic approach.
method: MedTriFlow uses a triplane autoencoder with 3D-aware projection to compress volumes into a compact discrete latent space and models a continuous anatomical field with an implicit neural representation. Flow matching generates samples in the triplane space, reducing the cost of volumetric generation, while continuous decoding reconstructs anatomy at arbitrary resolutions. A structure-guided adaptation mechanism supports conditional reconstruction tasks.

title: MedTSC-Net: Bridging Semantic and Scale Gaps in Text-Guided Medical Image Segmentation
motivation: Medical segmentation depends on large annotated datasets, but privacy constraints and annotation costs create data scarcity, especially for ambiguous lesion boundaries. Diagnostic reports can provide spatial and clinical guidance, yet existing text–image interaction is often shallow, attention mechanisms overlook channel semantics, and encoder–decoder receptive fields are mismatched. A framework is needed to close these semantic and scale gaps for precise, few-shot segmentation.
method: MedTSC-Net introduces a Visual-Linguistic Harmonizer that projects image and report features into a shared latent space during encoding. A Channel-Spatial Attention module models complementary text-guided dependencies across channel and spatial dimensions, and Receptive Field Alignment recalibrates decoder feature scales for boundary localization. Together these components form a harmonized encoding–decoding framework for text-guided lesion segmentation.

title: MedTS-TTT: Test-Time Training for Medical Time Series Classification
motivation: EEG, ECG, and other medical time series show strong subject-level heterogeneity, so a fixed model can generalize poorly to unseen individuals. Domain adaptation methods often require extra modules, target batches, or stable target statistics that are difficult to maintain for sequential clinical signals. Test-time training is suitable for unlabeled online adaptation, but many existing methods incur high latency through iterative optimization.
method: MedTS-TTT introduces Closed-Loop Self-Alignment TTT, which builds a token-level self-supervised target and performs a single-step fast-weight update for intra-layer alignment on each test sample. Its Gated Convolutional Backbone fuses the adapted token representation with a gated convolutional branch to model local dynamics while controlling information flow. This design enables online sample-wise adaptation without iterative inner-loop optimization.

title: MedVol-R1: Reward-Driven Evidence Grounding for Volumetric Reasoning Segmentation
motivation: Volumetric reasoning segmentation must resolve implicit clinical references and produce spatially coherent voxel masks from free-form queries. Segmentation-token approaches hide this decision process in latent representations, offering little verifiable evidence and often generalizing poorly beyond familiar wording. An interpretable framework is needed that grounds the referent explicitly and links evidence to reliable 3D delineation without costly chain-of-thought annotations.
method: MedVol-R1 explicitly separates evidence grounding from 3D delineation: an LVLM selects a key axial slice and 2D bounding boxes, which a frozen MedSAM2 propagates into a coherent volumetric mask. After cold-start supervised fine-tuning, GRPO optimizes the model with rewards for valid formatting, informative evidence selection, 2D localization, and cross-slice consistency. The framework therefore develops structured reasoning without requiring annotated chain-of-thought sequences.

title: MedXEdit-GRPO: Reasoning-Aware Online RL for Counterfactual Medical Image Generation
motivation: Counterfactual medical image editing supports controlled what-if analysis, but existing supervised methods mainly match pixel distributions and may fail to align abstract instructions with precise pathological edits. Reinforcement learning could optimize these clinical goals directly, yet handcrafted pixel metrics and isolated proxy rewards are unstable, reductionist, and vulnerable to reward hacking. A unified reasoning-aware reward is needed to provide stable, clinically meaningful feedback.
method: MedXEdit-GRPO curates a 30,000-sample MedXEdit-Reward dataset containing source and edited images, instructions, expert rationales, and comprehensive scores. MedXEdit-Score follows a reasoning-before-scoring procedure to provide semantically grounded, multidimensional feedback. GRPO then optimizes the editing policy with a unified signal that balances instruction compliance and anatomical consistency.

title: Memory-Guided Random-Direction Feature Disentanglement Model for Multi-phase MRI Translation
motivation: Complete high-quality multi-phase CE-MRI is often unavailable because of scan time, patient tolerance, repeated-examination concerns, and contrast-agent exposure. Existing translation models can be computationally heavy and opaque, while disentanglement methods often use multiple encoders or discriminators and treat content and style as uncoupled variables. A parameter-efficient and interpretable model is needed to preserve anatomy while controlling phase-specific appearance.
method: MG-RDFD uses a shared VAE encoder to map paired phases into Gaussian posteriors and applies Flip Distribution Alignment before selecting latent points along a random one-dimensional direction. Density criteria identify a shared content anchor and phase-preferred style anchors within the same geometry, explicitly coupling structure and appearance without multiple encoders or content discriminators. A segmentation-guided style memory bank retrieves region-specific prototypes for organs and lesions.

title: MERIT: Multi-scale Mamba with Enhanced Information Retention for Treatment Response Prediction from Whole Slide Images
motivation: Whole slide images are enormous, multi-resolution, and spatially organized, making treatment-response prediction a long-sequence problem with limited training samples. Transformers incur quadratic costs, while existing Mamba designs are unidirectional, prone to long-range information forgetting, and insufficiently multi-scale for pathology images. A model is needed that preserves spatial continuity, integrates hierarchical features, and retains distant contextual information efficiently.
method: MERIT uses a hierarchical multi-scale Mamba architecture for WSI treatment-response prediction. A dual-branch topology-preserving scan maintains spatial continuity across magnifications, while serial Mamba fuses features from multiple multi-scale foundation models with progressive information inheritance. A retentive information-transfer mechanism preserves message tokens and propagates residuals to reduce long-range forgetting.

title: Merlin Plus: A Large-Scale, Multi-cancer, Image-Mask-Report Dataset
motivation: Early tumor detection in CT can improve outcomes, and segmentation offers accurate and interpretable assistance to radiologists. However, public CT datasets contain tumor masks for only a few organs, leaving many high-mortality cancers without adequate supervision and limiting multi-cancer segmentation. A scalable way to obtain high-quality masks across organs is therefore needed.
method: Merlin Plus extends the Merlin CT-report collection with 1,153 per-voxel tumor masks spanning nine organs and adds longitudinal patient and scan metadata. A report-based active-learning pipeline first trains the R-Super segmentation model from radiology reports, then uses its masks as radiologist-editable proposals and retrains it through successive cycles. The resulting dataset supports multi-organ tumor detection and segmentation as well as temporal cancer-progression modeling.

title: MetaFormer: Efficient Metadata-Guided Transformer for Patient-Aware 12-Lead Electrocardiogram Reconstruction
motivation: Wearable devices enable long-term monitoring of transient cardiac events but usually record only one lead, which is insufficient for the diagnostic requirements of a clinical 12-lead ECG. Existing single-lead reconstruction methods treat the ill-posed cross-lead mapping as generic regression, ignoring individual anatomical and physiological differences and consequently producing ambiguous or population-average waveforms. Patient-specific constraints are needed for clinically precise reconstruction.
method: MetaFormer reconstructs a complete 12-lead ECG from a single reference lead while conditioning the solution on patient metadata. A meta tokenizer converts heterogeneous demographic attributes into semantic tokens, and a metadata-guided Transformer integrates these tokens through cross-attention to align reconstructed representations with individualized physiological baselines. This patient-aware conditioning is designed to resolve cross-lead spatial ambiguity and avoid regression toward population-average waveforms.

title: MetaVFM: Meta-Learned Efficient Adaptation of Vision Foundation Models for Medical Imaging
motivation: Vision foundation models need adaptation for specialized medical tasks, but full fine-tuning is costly while PEFT methods still require many optimization steps and are highly sensitive to adapter placement, rank, and initialization. The best configuration varies across heterogeneous datasets, making per-task search expensive and limiting reliable deployment. A unified approach should jointly select configuration and initialization while improving convergence efficiency.
method: MetaVFM meta-learns a joint representation of datasets and adapter configurations so that placement, rank, and initialization can be selected for an unseen task without per-dataset hyperparameter search. It first builds an AdapterZoo with a weight-sharing Multi-Rank LoRA Super-Adapter that efficiently explores insertion positions and nested ranks across many datasets. A performance-aligned dataset–adapter meta-space then retrieves both an adapter structure and initialization, followed by lightweight fine-tuning.

title: Microglia-RTS: Instance Segmentation of Microglia in Hypoxic Ischemic Fetal Sheep Brain Histology

categories.value: AI for Neglected Diseases & Limited-Resource Settings

motivation: Microglia activation and morphology are important indicators of inflammatory injury and treatment response in hypoxic–ischemic encephalopathy, including in fetal sheep models. Their counting and morphological classification in histology are largely manual, time-consuming, and prone to observer variability, limiting scalable drug screening and mechanistic analysis. Automated, reproducible instance segmentation is needed for high-throughput phenotyping.
method: Microglia-RTS is a two-stage pipeline for high-resolution microglia instance segmentation. A modified RT-DETR with a pretrained DINOv3 ConvNeXt backbone uses adaptive query selection to adjust the number of queries to local cell density, while a fine-tuned SAM2 generates masks from detector proposals. Overlapping patches are processed and stitched with overlap awareness to preserve cellular detail in whole histology images.

title: MicroscopyCLIP: A Domain-Specific Vision-Language Model for Optical Microscopy
motivation: Microscopy images contain fine-grained cellular morphology needed for biomedical research and diagnosis, but existing CLIP and medical vision-language models are mainly trained on natural images, radiology, or general medical text. Microscopy annotations are often subjective, coarse, and not standardized, so these models lack effective image–text alignment and transfer poorly across microscopy datasets. Domain-specific paired supervision is needed to support microscopy zero-shot understanding.
method: MicroscopyCLIP adapts a pretrained CLIP model to optical microscopy by constructing a large image–text corpus of fluorescence microscopy images paired with expert-reviewed descriptions. The model is fully fine-tuned so that its shared embedding space captures fine-grained cellular morphology rather than natural-image or radiology semantics. It is then used for prompt-based zero-shot classification and linear probing on in-domain and external microscopy datasets.

title: MiGAD: Gut Microbiota-informed Genetic Surrogates for Multimodal Alzheimer’s Disease Diagnosis
motivation: Alzheimer’s pathology can precede symptoms by years, making early diagnosis from imaging alone uncertain, while gut microbiome profiles provide potentially relevant gut–brain signals but are heterogeneous and temporally unstable. Stable microbiota-related genetic evidence could provide transferable peripheral information, yet existing models rarely use such representations and often require unavailable multimodal inputs at deployment. A framework is needed that exploits this evidence while retaining practical MRI-only screening.
method: MiGAD first selects microbiota-informed candidate variants by integrating multi-cohort microbiome and AD genetic evidence with Mendelian randomization and colocalization, then derives subject-level genotype representations. MRI, clinical variables, and genetic information are encoded as modality tokens and fused with a cross-modally aligned hierarchical Transformer for three-class AD staging. Knowledge from this multimodal teacher is distilled into an MRI-only student so screening remains usable when peripheral inputs are unavailable.

title: MIL-PF: Multiple Instance Learning on Precomputed Features for Mammography Classification
motivation: Mammography classification involves very high-resolution, multi-view images but usually only breast-level labels, making end-to-end adaptation of large foundation models computationally expensive and difficult under weak supervision. Rich pixel-level or textual annotations are generally unavailable, and standard CLIP-style or encoder-focused approaches are poorly suited to this setting. An efficient method is needed to exploit strong frozen representations and aggregate sparse lesion evidence across views.
method: MIL-PF freezes foundation encoders such as DINOv2 and MedSigLIP, precomputes their representations for mammography images, and trains only a roughly 40k-parameter MIL head. The head aggregates instances hierarchically across the multiple views of a breast, using attention to capture global tissue context and sparse local lesion evidence. This separates costly encoder computation from lightweight task adaptation while retaining visual explainability.

title: MINT: Molecularly Informed Training with Spatial Transcriptomics Supervision for Pathology Foundation Models
motivation: Pathology foundation models learn morphology from large whole-slide image collections but do not explicitly encode the tissue’s molecular state. Spatial transcriptomics provides spatially resolved gene expression that can supervise this missing information, yet using it for foundation-model enhancement risks catastrophic forgetting of pretrained morphology. A method must incorporate molecular supervision while preserving transferable visual features.
method: MINT fine-tunes pretrained pathology Vision Transformers by appending a learnable spatial-transcriptomics token, keeping molecular information separate from the morphological CLS token. DINO self-distillation and explicit feature anchoring to the frozen pretrained encoder preserve visual representations during molecularly supervised adaptation. Gene-expression regression at both Visium spot and Xenium patch resolutions supplies complementary supervision across spatial scales.

title: Missing Modality-Aware Calibration for Trustworthy Brain Tumor Segmentation
motivation: Brain tumor segmentation typically combines complementary MRI modalities, but protocols, scan failures, and patient factors often lead to missing inputs. Existing methods may preserve segmentation accuracy in these settings while producing miscalibrated confidence, and common calibration assumptions overlook that difficulty depends on which modalities are absent and varies spatially. Reliable combination-specific confidence estimates are needed for clinical intervention and trust.
method: MMA-LTS is a post-hoc voxel-wise calibration module for multimodal brain tumor segmentation under incomplete MRI inputs. It predicts a spatially adaptive temperature field conditioned on a learnable modality-availability token and a voxel-wise difficulty score, allowing calibration strength to depend on the specific missing-modality combination and local region. The module can be attached without retraining the segmentation model, targeting confidence correction while preserving its predictions.

title: Missingness-Aware Multimodal Learning for Four-Class Adrenal Tumor Classification
motivation: Distinguishing hormonally active adrenal tumors from non-functioning adenomas is clinically important, but current workflows often require multi-step endocrine testing and contrast-enhanced CT, which add burden, radiation, or contrast-related risks. A four-class model using non-contrast CT and routine clinical variables is underdeveloped, and real-world clinical fields are frequently missing while tumor classes are imbalanced. The method must therefore fuse modalities according to input reliability and improve minority-class discrimination.
method: The proposed missingness-aware multimodal model combines non-contrast CT with non-hormonal clinical variables while explicitly encoding which clinical fields are absent. Structured embeddings modulate imaging features through feature-wise affine transformation, and a reliability descriptor derived from missingness patterns predicts sample-specific weights for imaging, clinical, and interaction representations. A distribution-aware prototype regularization objective further shapes the fused embedding to compact classes and improve separation under imbalance.

title: Mitigating Grade Boundary Conflicts for Disease Severity Grading with Ambiguous Labels
motivation: Disease severity grading supports tasks such as lung-nodule malignancy and diabetic-retinopathy assessment, but expert labels are often ambiguous. Adjacent grades have unclear boundaries and annotators may apply inconsistent standards, degrading robustness and generalization. Existing proxy-label, sample-selection, and ordinal-prior approaches do not directly resolve these boundary conflicts.
method: HDU first warms up a backbone and forms per-grade feature prototypes within each batch. Its Grade Boundaries Harmonizing module re-estimates probabilistic labels from sample-prototype similarity, then calibrates the original labels. Unimodal Projection maps these calibrated labels to ordinally valid unimodal distributions, while early-learning regularization limits later overfitting to ambiguous supervision.

title: MLLM-Enhanced Region-Aware Bidirectional Evidence-Based Model for Tongue Diagnosis
motivation: Tongue diagnosis offers a rapid, noninvasive means of early health screening in TCM, where tongue signs relate to syndrome patterns and organ states. Current systems commonly treat these two predictions independently and insufficiently combine regional signs with whole-tongue appearance. They also make limited use of clinical and TCM knowledge, reducing clinically grounded reasoning and interpretability.
method: The method uses Augmented Global-Local Feature Fusion (AGLFF) to mutually refine whole-tongue and region-specific token representations through cross-attention and gated patch fusion. An Uncertainty-Weighted Bidirectional Mixture-of-Experts module routes and propagates evidence between syndrome and organ branches in both directions, with consistency regularization. It also adaptively fuses MLLM-derived semantic priors with visual features for joint inference.

title: MMIC-EndoDepth: Self-Supervised Endoscopic Depth Estimation with Multi-Mechanism Illumination Correction
motivation: Monocular endoscopic depth is needed for surgical navigation, 3D reconstruction, and augmented-reality applications, but real colonoscopy lacks practical ground-truth depth acquisition. Self-supervised methods therefore rely on photometric reconstruction, whose brightness-constancy assumption fails under specular reflections, dynamic illumination, and interreflections. This creates unreliable depth estimates in endoscopic scenes.
method: MMIC-EndoDepth is a self-supervised monocular endoscopic depth framework with an Illumination-Aware Photometric Correction module before geometric reconstruction. The module decomposes photometric distortion into pixel-wise specular highlights, patch-level exposure variation, and depth-guided global lighting attenuation. A spatially adaptive MoE selects the appropriate correction per region, while entropy, load-balancing, and warmup mechanisms stabilize expert use.

title: MM-UNet: Meta Mamba UNet for Volumetric Medical Image Segmentation
motivation: Medical image segmentation requires both local detail and long-range spatial dependencies. CNNs have limited receptive fields, whereas attention-based ViTs are computationally expensive; SSMs offer linear-complexity sequence modeling but were designed for 1D data. Directly flattening 3D images causes spatial discontinuities, and SSMs also struggle with the high-variance features common in medical imaging.
method: MM-UNet is a unified U-shaped encoder-decoder with replaceable meta-blocks across the encoder, bottleneck, and decoder. Its selected hybrid block places SSMs after sequential CNNs and within residual connections, supplying lower-variance inputs that SSMs can model more effectively. A bi-directional scan order further reduces discontinuities created when volumetric spatial features are flattened into sequences.

title: MoCaf-Mamba: Modality Completion and Alignment in Feature Space for Missing-Modality Segmentation
motivation: Multimodal imaging provides complementary evidence for segmentation, yet modalities are often unavailable at inference because of protocol constraints, artifacts, or cost. Static filling and content-agnostic placeholders lose modality-specific semantics, while pixel-level synthesis is costly and may not target segmentation-relevant information. Residual geometric misalignment between modalities also degrades their fusion.
method: MoCaf-Mamba completes missing modality representations in feature space using MCFS, conditioned on available modalities and supervised by reconstruction constraints. Hierarchical DFA predicts bounded dense displacement fields and warps features through differentiable sampling before fusion. STM then combines the completed, aligned multi-scale features using local convolutional cues, global token context, and a consensus token for decoding under arbitrary missing patterns.

title: Modality-Agnostic Domain Generalizable Medical Image Segmentation via Self-Coordinated Focusing
motivation: Automated medical image segmentation can reduce the labor and observer variability of manual delineation, including for early tumors. However, limited datasets and substantial cross-domain appearance shifts break the assumption that training and test data have the same distribution. Existing static perception and feature-extraction mechanisms do not adapt sufficiently to diverse unseen clinical inputs.
method: SCFNet combines Dynamic Focusing Convolution and Interactive Attention Fusion Decoding for modality-agnostic domain-generalizable segmentation. DFC pre-perceives target type and spatial scale distribution to adapt convolutional aggregation weights and receptive fields to each input. IAFD decomposes low-level semantic information with wavelet transformation and uses cross-level interactive attention to fuse salient information during decoding.

title: Modeling Clinical Workflow for SYNTAX Scoring from Coronary Angiography Videos
motivation: SYNTAX scoring guides coronary artery disease treatment by integrating lesion complexity across anatomically defined coronary segments and views. Most automated approaches instead regress directly from angiography videos to a patient-level score, collapsing vessel identity, lesion attribution, and hierarchical clinical reasoning. This limits interpretability, robustness, and generalization on heterogeneous multi-view data.
method: The framework preserves coronary vessel-segment identity across video frames and angiographic views, estimates segment-level stenosis severity, and hierarchically aggregates evidence according to coronary anatomy. A segment-aware decision field embeds discrete stenosis assessments in a continuous topology-aware representation, maintaining spatial coherence and correspondence. The work also integrates and completes public angiography data with vessel segmentation and derived structural annotations to support model training.

title: MORI-Seg: Learning Morphological Geometry for Instance Segmentation Without Instance Annotations
motivation: Instance-level kidney-unit quantification is necessary for morphometric analysis, but public pathology datasets usually contain only semantic masks that merge adjacent objects of the same class. Heuristic splitting is sensitive to variable crowded morphology, while supervised instance segmentation requires expensive individual-instance masks. Semantic-to-instance methods also often lack explicit geometry tailored to heterogeneous kidney structures.
method: MORI-Seg learns instance-separating geometric representations from semantic masks alone in an end-to-end framework. It jointly models object-centric distance fields for interior structure and boundary-band representations for contact interfaces. A class-conditioned feature-disentanglement module promotes coherence within each instance and separation between adjacent instances.

title: MoSE: Mixture-of-Scale-Experts for Medical Image Restoration
motivation: Medical images acquired under constrained conditions exhibit diverse degradations, including blur, noise, and low resolution, yet subtle anatomical texture distortions can affect diagnosis. Unified restoration models may use redundant computation because their shared architecture cannot specialize across these conditions. Conventional MoE reduces computation sparsely, but homogeneous experts still inadequately adapt to different anatomical context scales and may lose structure or texture.
method: MoSE routes each restoration input to heterogeneous experts with progressively different receptive fields. Shallow-wide experts target local edges and fine textures, whereas deep-narrow experts model long-range anatomical context; a scale-aware load-balancing loss encourages their balanced use. An Orientation-Contrast Guided filter provides wavelet-based directional and local-contrast guidance for high-frequency reconstruction, and ATLS evaluates patch-level anatomical texture fidelity.

title: Motion-Conditioned Multi-view Fusion for Myocardial Infarction Localization from Echocardiography
motivation: Myocardial infarction causes regional wall-motion abnormalities, and echocardiography is routinely used to assess them across complementary apical views. Motion-only approaches often require dense anatomical supervision or are sensitive to noise, while foundation-model approaches generally use a single view and remain unreliable for segment-level localization under view-dependent ambiguity. A scalable method must combine motion and visual evidence without extensive labeling.
method: MCF-Net uses the pretrained EchoPrime foundation model as a shared visual encoder for A4C and A2C views. It transfers a single annotated template frame to initialize point tracking across videos, producing sparse-supervision motion trajectories and segment-aware Gaussian soft masks. Motion embeddings gate visual features, and cross-view attention fuses complementary evidence while retaining strong appearance cues.

title: MPFlow: Multi-modal Posterior-Guided Flow Matching for Zero-Shot MRI Reconstruction
motivation: Zero-shot MRI reconstruction from undersampled or low-quality measurements is severely ill-posed, so unconditional single-modality generative priors can create anatomically plausible but incorrect intrinsic or measurement-consistent extrinsic hallucinations. Complementary MRI sequences are commonly acquired clinically, yet existing methods do not provide a principled way to use them at inference while retaining an unconditional prior. A mechanism is therefore needed to use cross-modal anatomical evidence to resolve reconstruction ambiguity and improve reliability efficiently.
method: MPFlow keeps an unconditional rectified-flow MRI prior fixed and injects auxiliary MRI information only at inference. It first trains PAMRI self-supervisedly to align target and auxiliary modalities in a shared patch-level representation space, using an adaptive InfoNCE temperature based on normalized mutual information. During sampling, data consistency and PAMRI cross-modal feature alignment jointly guide posterior updates, with noise optimization used to improve trajectory initialization.

title: MRI2Rep: Autoregressive Structured Report Generation for 3D Liver MRI
motivation: Manual interpretation and reporting of 3D liver MRI are time-consuming, while end-to-end generation of clinically structured, guideline-conformant reports remains underexplored. Small 3D MRI cohorts provide noisy report-level supervision with variable terminology and negation, and volumetric inputs require modeling cross-sequence cues and long-range spatial structure under limited computation. An approach is needed that can derive reliable structured supervision from routine reports and generate liver MRI reports without costly lesion-level annotations.
method: MRI2Rep converts noisy free-text reports into auditable, closed-vocabulary diagnostic sequences through its LI-RADS-guided Report-to-Label Canonicalization module, resolving negation, uncertainty, and wording variation. An encoder-decoder then autoregressively predicts these structured sequences from multi-phase 3D liver MRI volumes. Deterministic templates render the predicted sequences as standardized professional reports, without requiring lesion-level boxes or masks.

title: MRSeg3D: A Perturbation-Resilient Model for 3D Medical Reasoning Segmentation
motivation: 3D reasoning-based segmentation lets users specify targets through natural-language instructions, but performance on curated prompts does not establish robustness to the varied and ambiguous instructions encountered clinically. Existing systems can lose visual grounding as reasoning and decoding proceed, causing semantic drift and a mismatch between generated reasoning and segmentation masks under instruction perturbations. Robust systems need tighter visual-semantic coupling and a systematic evaluation of instruction-level robustness and reasoning-segmentation alignment.
method: MRSeg3D uses a single-encoder reasoning-segmentation architecture that persistently couples visual evidence to language reasoning and mask decoding. Two cascaded vision injectors insert multi-level visual features into intermediate reasoning layers to anchor interpretation to invariant image cues under ambiguous instructions. A Seg-Local Projector works with the mask prompt encoder to enrich text-visual cues and improve execution of the [SEG] token for final mask generation.

title: MS-GDUN: Multi-scale Graph Deep Unfolding Network with Gradient-Threshold Learning for FMT Reconstruction
motivation: FMT can support early tumor detection but reconstructing fluorescence distributions is severely ill-posed because of photon scattering, sparse sources, and limited surface measurements. Classical sparse iterative methods depend on approximate physics, hand-tuned parameters, and fixed global thresholds, which impair stability under noise and scattering. Fully data-driven methods may generalize poorly and underuse the finite-element topology, motivating an interpretable approach that learns reconstruction updates while exploiting graph structure.
method: MS-GDUN unfolds the Sparse Graph Manifold Learning reconstruction process into a learnable, physics-guided layered network. It constructs graphs constrained by finite-element mesh photon-transport distances and uses Graph Convolutional Blocks to capture multi-hop diffusion correlations. Iteration-specific gradient update directions and node-adaptive sparsity thresholds are learned end to end, while multi-scale graph cross-attention fuses local and global features across four scales.

title: MSHF-Net: Multimodal Breast Cancer Molecular Subtype Prediction via Segmentation-Guided Hierarchical Fusion Network

categories.value: Multimodal Integration with Clinical / Genomic / Biomarkers

motivation: Breast cancer molecular subtype guides therapy and prognosis, but invasive biopsy and postoperative pathology can miss tumor heterogeneity because they sample only limited tissue. Imaging-based prediction could offer a non-invasive preoperative alternative, yet single modalities provide incomplete evidence and existing multimodal approaches do not adequately model scale differences or complementarity among mammography, ultrasound, and clinical data. Small lesion regions and Luminal/Non-luminal imbalance further allow background distraction and reduce reliability for minority subtypes.
method: MSHF-Net predicts Luminal versus Non-luminal breast cancer by jointly using mammography, ultrasound, and clinical features. Its Hierarchical Tri-modal Fusion module exchanges and integrates complementary information from the three modalities at multiple levels. Segmentation-Guided Aggregation combines whole-image context with lesion-focused features, and Class-Balanced Focal Loss increases emphasis on under-represented subtypes.

title: mSpecFusion-Net: Intelligent Multimodal Smartphone Imaging for Mobile Differential Diagnosis of Psoriasis and Dermatitis and Deep Learning
motivation: Psoriasis and seborrheic dermatitis share signs such as erythema and scaling, creating diagnostic ambiguity that can delay appropriate management, especially in primary care and teledermatology. Mobile RGB images are vulnerable to variable distance, angle, illumination, specular reflection, and tissue scattering, which obscure subtle distinctions. Multiple optical contrasts can be complementary, but naive multimodal fusion may underuse modality-specific cues or amplify artifacts, so robust mobile integration is needed.
method: DermaSpecFusion combines a smartphone multimodal dermascope with mSpecFusion-Net for psoriasis-versus-seborrheic-dermatitis diagnosis. The system acquires co-polarized and cross-polarized multispectral reflectance plus UV-excited autofluorescence, calibrates the modalities with an embedded white reference, and applies PCA to reduce spectral redundancy. mSpecFusion-Net encodes each modality in parallel and uses an iterative-fusion Transformer to repeatedly exchange and refine cross-modal evidence into a unified diagnostic representation.

title: MSQG-3DNet: Multi-scale Token Selection with Query-Decoder and Gated Fusion for 3D Breast Tumor Classification
motivation: Lesion-level benign-malignant classification in 3D ABUS can improve downstream CAD decisions, but variable voxel spacing, anisotropic artifacts, and weak malignancy cues dispersed through the volume make the task difficult. CNNs preserve local texture and morphology but can dilute subtle cues and do not explicitly capture long-range dependencies, whereas direct 3D Transformer use is computationally costly and can include many redundant background tokens. A model is needed to retain multi-scale lesion details while efficiently aggregating task-focused global volumetric evidence.
method: MSQG-3DNet standardizes intensity-normalized lesion-centered ABUS ROIs onto a fixed 48 x 48 x 48 lattice before processing them with an SE-enhanced dilated 3D residual encoder. It tokenizes multi-scale features at two scales and adds coordinate-based, sinusoidal, and scale embeddings to preserve spatial and scale information. LayerScale-stabilized Transformers model long-range dependencies; token selection removes redundant background tokens, a cross-attention Query-Decoder extracts task-relevant global evidence, and gated fusion combines global descriptors for classification.

title: MSS-Net: Learning Hierarchical Multi-scale and Multimodal Representations for Complex Cardiac Disease Classification
motivation: Complex cardiovascular and comorbid conditions require ECG interpretation of both subtle local morphology and global heartbeat rhythm. Existing parallel or single-scale approaches often fragment these representations, leaving local and global evidence semantically inconsistent and insufficiently interactive; global features may also overshadow subtle pathological fluctuations. ECG alone has limited representation capacity, while clinical text lacks precise localization, motivating a way to coordinate multi-scale signal features and clinical context.
method: MSS-Net combines spectral-temporal multi-scale ECG learning with clinical-text prior guidance. Adaptive Gated Spectral Injection rebalances global features and modulates them in the frequency domain to capture long-range rhythm dependencies, while Dual Cross-scale Interaction selectively fuses these global features with local morphology. Prior-Guided Feature Aggregation aligns latent ECG representations with clinical-context information during training to calibrate pathological features for prediction.

title: MuellerPT: Decomposition Driven Pre-training for Dense Learning in Mueller Polarimetry
motivation: Mueller matrix polarimetry provides tissue contrasts related to scattering, absorption anisotropy, and microstructure, but dense labels are scarce and acquisition settings can shift substantially across specimens and systems. Models trained from scratch or with generic initializations therefore struggle to learn clinically transferable representations under noise, calibration drift, and domain shift. Lu-Chipman decomposition maps are physically interpretable and available without manual annotation, creating an opportunity for a task-agnostic physics-grounded pretraining signal.
method: MuellerPT pretrains separate encoders for normalized Mueller matrices and the intensity-only m(0,0) channel on MAP-Org data, then fine-tunes them for dense segmentation or classification. Its self-supervised pretext task predicts per-pixel Lu-Chipman decomposition quantities: depolarization, retardance, and diattenuation. Physics-informed Mueller-element dropout simulates hardware choices and encourages transfer across systems, while a refinement block fuses the polarimetric and intensity streams.

title: Multi-agent Test-Time Adaptation for Robust Medical Image-to-Image Translation
motivation: Medical image-to-image translation can degrade under scanner, protocol, and population shifts, even though preservation of fine spatial and intensity relationships is critical for synthesis and denoising. Existing test-time adaptation methods are generally tied to a task model and use fixed strategies without explicitly measuring each sample's shift or deciding whether adaptation is warranted. Heterogeneous test samples therefore require a modular mechanism for selective, sample-specific adaptation in image-to-image translation.
method: The proposed framework formulates test-time adaptation as four coordinated agents: a predictor for translation, a monitor for distribution shift, a selector for adaptation decisions, and an adaptation agent for model updates. The agents communicate through a shared space, separating adaptation control from the pretrained image-to-image translation model. This design enables sample-specific decisions about whether and how much to adapt and is evaluated with both GAN- and flow-matching-based translation models.

title: Multi-Annotation Adaption: A Label-Informed Dynamic Framework for Medical Segmentation and Localization
motivation: Lesion segmentation and localization are important for diagnosis, treatment planning, and monitoring, but dense mask annotation is costly. Existing weakly supervised methods use lighter annotations such as points or boxes, often by converting them into error-prone pseudo-masks. A unified method is needed to exploit mixed annotation types while reducing reliance on precise masks.
method: MALFOY is a plug-and-play label-informed framework that trains from masks, noisy masks, points, bounding boxes, and other annotation styles within one model. It encodes annotation type through label weights linked to annotation-specific losses, then searches training records or a validation set for weights that yield the desired segmentation or detection objective. The design supports both 2D and 3D lesion tasks and can extend to multi-expert annotations.

title: Multi-camera AR Guidance System for Surgical Instrument Handling and Assembly: Investigating Workload and Efficiency
motivation: Scrub nurses must handle and assemble complex, manufacturer-specific instruments under time pressure, including unfamiliar instruments when experienced staff are unavailable. Paper or PDF manuals are often not available at the point of use and can prolong surgical interruptions. Context-aware AR guidance requires reliable, marker-free pose estimation for a realistic operating-room workflow.
method: The system couples marker-free multi-camera 6D instrument pose estimation with head-mounted AR guidance. Pose estimation and consecutive camera calibration use known objects, while the pose model is trained entirely on synthetic data. Based on estimated poses, the AR display presents in-situ localization cues and step-wise assembly animations, with gaze selection and a foot pedal used to navigate steps.

title: Multi-depth Rubidium PET Graph Neural Network for Major Adverse Cardiac Event Prediction
motivation: Early prediction of major adverse cardiac events can support personalized monitoring and management, while established non-imaging risk factors do not explain all cardiovascular risk. Rubidium PET myocardial perfusion imaging provides predictive MBF measurements, but routine polar-map representations flatten the left ventricle and discard its native geometry and depth-specific perfusion. A method is needed to capture subtle, localized multi-depth perfusion patterns in 3D.
method: The work uses an automated 3D 82Rb PET processing pipeline to build tissue-depth-specific GNNs for MACE prediction. Graph models operate in native 3D PET space and incorporate epicardial, centerline, and endocardial perfusion-related signals, including MBF, uptake, and activity. The approach is compared with centerline-derived intensity features and CNNs using flattened polar maps to assess the value of preserved geometry and multi-depth information.

title: Multi-Disease Diagnosis in Retinal Images via Patch-Level Reasoning and Selective Aggregation
motivation: Retinal images are used to diagnose multiple co-occurring diseases, but image-level supervision can cause lesion-disease mismatching. Models may associate lesions of a frequently co-occurring disease with another disease and still fit the training labels. This produces incorrect spatial reasoning and poor generalization when diseases occur independently.
method: MD-PRSA uses a patch-based transformer decoder with learned disease queries to produce disease-specific predictions for each retinal patch. A multiple-instance-learning aggregation module selectively combines only patches with strong evidence for each disease. This spatial attribution constraint promotes implicit disease localization and suppresses patches whose lesions are spuriously associated with co-occurring diseases.

title: Multi-Expert Representation Learning with Dynamic Routing for Brain Captioning
motivation: Brain captioning seeks to translate neural activity into natural-language descriptions, but existing methods usually align brain signals to a single static textual or visual representation. This ignores the hierarchical organization of visual cortex and variability across cortical regions and subjects. Noisy neural signals and inter-subject variation further make stable brain-vision alignment difficult.
method: MERPA aligns brain activity with structured visual tokens extracted by multiple frozen, task-specialized vision experts spanning geometric and semantic abstraction levels. A brain-conditioned dynamic routing module predicts expert weights to adapt the contribution of each expert to neural activity. Its progressive alignment objective first applies optimal transport for global distribution matching and then robust regression for feature-level refinement; a frozen captioning decoder generates text from predicted brain tokens at inference.

title: Multi-frame Restoration for 10 Hz Lissajous Confocal Laser Endomicroscopy
motivation: Lissajous CLE enables high-speed handheld optical biopsy, but at 10 Hz each frame samples only pixels along a resonant trajectory and leaves many structured holes. Aggregating frames can increase coverage, yet motion and sparse observations make dense correspondence unreliable and can reintroduce motion artifacts. The task also lacked paired data with temporally aligned high-quality references for supervised restoration.
method: The authors introduce MaLissa, a paired benchmark in which high-quality targets are matched from mosaics stitched from slow-scan frames. Their MIRA recurrent restoration model reconstructs each high-quality frame from the current low-quality Lissajous frame and preceding frames. MIRA caches and reuses encoded features across time, then uses lightweight flow-free global displacement alignment to combine temporally mismatched sparse observations with low latency.

title: Multi-Kernel Gated Decoder Adapters for Robust Multi-Task Thyroid Ultrasound under Cross-Center Shift
motivation: Thyroid ultrasound systems must segment nodules using global geometric reasoning and assess malignancy using local texture cues. Scanner, acquisition, operator, and overlay differences across centers shift these cues asymmetrically, undermining clinical generalization. A single shared multi-task encoder can therefore cause negative transfer between contouring and risk assessment.
method: The unified framework shares either a ResNet34 or MedSAM backbone and jointly predicts nodule segmentation, TI-RADS malignancy, and anatomical position. Its MKGA decoder adapter refines skip features with parallel standard and dilated convolutions, gates them using deeper semantic context, and fuses the gated features through residual refinement. ResMKGA additionally applies residual channel recalibration at the bottleneck, while PCGrad can be used to reduce conflicting multi-task gradients.

title: Multilayer Modularity-Aware Graph Autoencoder for Detecting Subpopulation Community Structure in Dynamic Brain Networks
motivation: Dynamic fMRI network analysis must distinguish temporal reconfiguration of brain communities from intrinsic differences between subjects. Existing multilayer and deep graph methods commonly focus on individual subjects or assume a homogeneous population and a common community partition. This overlooks latent subpopulations with distinct baseline node-level community structures and can confound analysis of dynamic brain states.
method: MMGAE-WSBM uses a two-stage hierarchical pipeline. It first clusters WSBM parameters derived from shared prior node communities to infer latent subject subpopulations. These labels guide contrastive coupling in a multilayer modularity-aware graph autoencoder, preserving within-community topology while separating subgroups in embedding space; a Markov-switching WSBM then derives time-resolved brain states from the learned community partitions.

title: Multimodal Contrastive Regression for Organ-Resolved Biological Age Prediction

categories.value: Multimodal Integration with Clinical / Genomic / Biomarkers
AI for Population Health, Public Health & Epidemiology

motivation: Chronological age does not represent the genetic, environmental, lifestyle, and organ-specific factors that drive heterogeneous aging. Existing biological-age models often use a single organ or limited biomarkers, providing only a partial assessment of distributed aging. Robust organ-resolved estimation requires integrating structural imaging with functional, physiological, and clinical information.
method: The proposed framework jointly learns from organ MRI and complementary structured clinical variables to estimate biological age for six organ systems. It uses a contrastive regression loss to organize the shared latent space according to continuous age differences within and across modalities. Training on healthy participants uses chronological age to model normative aging patterns, enabling organ-specific age estimates and age gaps in mixed populations.

title: Multimodal Large Language Model-Driven Self-Verification Reasoning for Interpretable Diagnosis of Diffuse Cystic Lung Diseases

categories.value: AI for Neglected Diseases & Limited-Resource Settings

motivation: Diffuse cystic lung diseases are rare disorders whose subtypes have overlapping cystic CT appearances, making differential diagnosis difficult. Reliable diagnosis requires both whole-lung 3D distribution analysis and local slice-level morphology assessment, but an entire CT volume exceeds typical MLLM context limits. Naive slice sampling loses spatial information and can lead to unstable, hallucinated, and poorly interpretable predictions.
method: The framework follows a clinical global-to-local reasoning workflow. Global Spatial Perception obtains lung and cyst masks, renders their 3D distribution into a compact coronal visualization with a slice-index navigation axis, and uses it with clinical metadata to form an initial MLLM diagnostic hypothesis. Multistep Self-Verification Reasoning then iteratively retrieves representative axial slices, checks discriminative morphology and distribution evidence, and refines diagnostic probabilities until reaching confidence or reporting uncertainty.

title: Multimodal-Conditioned Flow Matching for Pathology Nuclei Data Augmentation
motivation: Nuclei segmentation and classification are fundamental for computational pathology, but supervised models are limited by the scarcity of large, accurately annotated datasets.
