Existing generative augmentation methods are inefficient, perform poorly with small annotated sets, and often lack sufficient control over tissue-specific texture and morphology.
method: The framework uses optimal-transport flow matching with synchronous multimodal conditioning to generate aligned nuclei masks and pathology images in an end-to-end model with few-step sampling. Cell center points and text descriptions guide mask layout, while self-supervised features from computational pathology foundation models provide morphological and textural guidance for image synthesis.

title: Multi-parametric MRI for Contrast Agent Free Breast DCE-MRI Synthesis
motivation: Breast DCE-MRI is important for cancer detection and diagnosis, but gadolinium contrast agents introduce adverse-reaction risks, cost, and additional examination time. Prior synthesis methods often rely on a single structural MRI sequence, while the diagnostic information in DWI and ADC has been underused; diffusion-based alternatives can also be too slow for clinical workflows.
method: A conditional GAN takes T1w MRI, multi-b-value DWI, and ADC maps as multi-parametric input and synthesizes several post-contrast DCE-MRI phases simultaneously. A multi-scale enhancement consistency loss enforces agreement of predicted enhancement maps across resolutions, improving structural detail while avoiding the long inference times of diffusion models.

title: Multi-probe Trait–State Latent Modeling for Cross-Context Clinical Motor Assessment
motivation: Clinical motor tasks provide observations shaped by instructions, effort, fatigue, and environment, whereas clinicians seek motor capacity that remains stable across contexts. Existing motion models are largely context-bound and treat observed task performance as ability, making cross-context and cross-center assessment qualitative and difficult to reproduce.
method: The model represents each standardized task as a partial probe, using a shared subject-level latent for stable motor traits and probe-specific latents for transient execution effects. It aggregates probe evidence with precision weighting, and generates resting-state gait from the shared trait alone so that cross-context consistency can be assessed.

title: Multi-regional CT Radiomics Fusion to Quantify Pathology-Derived Pollutant Burden in Lung Cancer

categories.value: Multimodal Integration with Clinical / Genomic / Biomarkers

motivation: Anthracotic carbon deposition is a biological measure of cumulative particulate exposure, but it is visible only in invasive histopathology and therefore unsuitable for scalable screening or longitudinal monitoring. Self-reported and geospatial exposure proxies are qualitative, while CT may contain exposure-related phenotypes distributed differently across anatomical regions.
method: The method extracts standardized radiomic and habitat features from six anatomical compartments, including tumor, lung parenchyma, and peritumoral rings. Region-specific classifiers use cross-validated stability feature selection, and their predictions are combined through weighted late fusion to estimate a pathology-derived Lung Pollutant Index from CT.

title: Multi-scale Dual-domain Fusion-Based Spatio-Temporal Graph Learning for fNIRS Signal Classification
motivation: fNIRS multi-class decoding is hindered by physiological artifacts, the sluggish hemodynamic response function, scale-dependent spatio-temporal heterogeneity, and large inter-subject variation. Existing models often use single-hemoglobin time-domain correlations or isolated single-scale processing, so they miss phase-oppositional coupling and transient neural dynamics needed for robust cross-subject decoding.
method: MsDFSTGL builds a noise-resilient graph from dual-domain HbO2-HbR neurovascular coupling using a Time-Frequency Global Correlation module and GCNs. Parallel multi-scale branches apply scale-adaptive TFGC and Multi-Stage Differential Encoding to separate transient triggers from slow hemodynamics, then Multi-Scale Multi-Head Cross-Attention and a Cross-Scale Mixture-of-Experts aggregate inter-scale information adaptively.

title: Multi-Stage Dilated Convolution-Mamba Network for Surgical Action Triplet Recognition
motivation: Surgical action triplet recognition must capture both subtle local motions and long procedural dynamics while modeling dependencies among instrument, verb, and target. Existing convolutional or attention methods have limited temporal coverage or high cost, often treat triplet components independently, and struggle with long-tailed surgical classes.
method: DCM-Net stacks Dilated Convolutional Mamba blocks, with a State Space Model branch for long-range dependencies and parallel dilated-convolution branches for multi-scale local temporal patterns. Its Task-aware Graph Fusion module forms nodes for Instrument, Verb, Target, and Triplet across feature scales, using intra-scale and cross-scale edges to propagate semantic relationships.

title: Multi-stage NeRF for Efficient 3D Coronary Artery Reconstruction from Two Narrow-Angle Angiographic Projections
motivation: Coronary angiography provides high-quality 2D projections but leaves the underlying 3D vessels ambiguous because of overlap and foreshortening. Existing learning-based reconstruction commonly assumes multiple or widely separated views or requires paired 3D ground truth, whereas routine procedures may provide only two projections with a narrow angle and highly sparse 3D support.
method: NeCA++ performs self-supervised reconstruction in stages: a low-resolution representation first estimates a coarse vascular structure and defines an active region, after which optimization is restricted to that region while higher-resolution hash levels are progressively activated. A ray-aligned geometry constraint and a bimodal density penalty reduce projection ambiguity and encourage early separation of vessels from background.

title: Multi-view Consistency-Based Adaptation of SAM2 for 3D ABUS Tumor Segmentation
motivation: 3D ABUS can support breast cancer detection, but tumor segmentation is difficult because tumors vary in size, shape, and boundary appearance and high-quality volumetric labels are scarce. Foundation models such as SAM2 suffer from medical domain gaps, while existing adaptations often require expensive full pixel annotations and are not designed for unseen 3D ABUS domains.
method: The approach adapts SAM2 with separate adapters for slices along the three orthogonal axes and uses point annotations as prompts for volumetric propagation. Pseudo-labels from the other axes provide multi-axis consistency regularization, while a learnable detection token estimates tumor presence in each slice to improve pseudo-label quality.

title: Mutual Distillation of Dual-Foundation Models for Semi-supervised PET/CT Segmentation
motivation: Whole-body PET/CT organ segmentation requires both anatomical CT information and metabolic PET information, but accurate 3D annotations are expensive and the two modalities have blurred or mismatched boundaries. Conventional semi-supervised methods can reinforce erroneous pseudo-labels, and existing foundation-model distillation approaches are mainly single-modality and do not exploit cross-modal complementarity.
method: MuDuo uses a lightweight student with two foundation-model pathways: student predictions prompt SAM-Med3D on CT and a prompt generator supplies point prompts to SegAnyPET on PET. The resulting pseudo-labels are fused and filtered by an IoU-based consensus rule, then used in consistency regularization to mutually distill structural and functional knowledge without manual prompts.

title: Mutually Promoted Medical Image Segmentation and Classification via Prompt-Driven Interaction
motivation: Fine-tuned SAM can segment medical images but is class agnostic, so it cannot reliably identify the predicted anatomy and may select implausible masks when boundaries are ambiguous. Treating segmentation and classification as separate stages limits feature interaction, propagates errors, and reduces robustness across organs, lesions, and imaging modalities.
method: BiMI couples a fine-tuned SAM segmentation branch with hierarchical classification through a Coarse2Fine Matrix and Global2local Feature Enhancement. A frozen language model expands coarse and fine predictions into a structured description, whose text embedding weights anatomical structural descriptors to rank SAM’s candidate masks within the box prompt using Structure-Aware Candidate Selection.

title: MUX-USCT: A Noise-Robust Neural Network for Ultrasound Computed Tomography
motivation: Ultrasound computed tomography (USCT) reconstructs quantitative tissue maps for applications such as breast and prostate imaging, but full-waveform inversion is computationally demanding. Existing DNN reconstructions perform well on clean data yet treat all waveform channels equally, so transducer faults and changing clinical noise distributions can cause severe degradation and provide no indication of which channels are unreliable. A model that can adapt to unknown inference-time noise while retaining clean-data performance and exposing degraded transducers is therefore needed.
method: MUX-USCT is an encoder-decoder DNN that incorporates the acoustic acquisition geometry through an adaptive learned multiplexer. Its encoder uses attention to assess transducer signal content, identify and filter corrupted paths, and compress multi-path waveforms, while a position-aware decoder selectively routes relevant path information to each output pixel. The architecture is parameterized by the number of paths and transducers and requires no noise-augmented training.

title: MVDA-Net: Multi-View Dual-Alignment Network for 3D Carotid Artery Segmentation
motivation: Accurate CTA segmentation of the carotid vessel wall, lumen, and calcification supports assessment of atherosclerotic disease and treatment planning. Generic 3D segmentation methods struggle with discontinuous lesions, extreme foreground scarcity, low-contrast double-edge vessel walls, irregular calcifications, and weak spatial-semantic complementarity during encoder-decoder alignment. These characteristics motivate a method that preserves small-structure context, progressively refines boundaries, and adaptively aligns complementary features.
method: MVDA-Net introduces three modules for multi-structure carotid CTA segmentation. Spatially-Aware Orthogonal Projection performs multi-view projection with spatial attention to propagate context across discontinuous lesions while preserving localization. Hierarchical Inverted Attention Refinement transfers boundary-enhancing attention from deep to shallow layers, and Synergistic Feature Alignment uses feature differences and summation to suppress redundancy and model complementary spatial-semantic information.

title: N6-TreeMamba: Radiology Knowledge-Guided 6-Neighborhood Tree Scanning for 3D MRI-Based Stroke Complication Prediction

categories.value: Multimodal Integration with Clinical / Genomic / Biomarkers

motivation: Early prediction of stroke-associated pneumonia (SAP) and hemorrhagic transformation (HT) from multi-sequence brain MRI could support timely intervention, but informative signals are subtle, spatially diffuse, and distributed across sequences. CNNs have limited long-range modeling, whereas Transformers are computationally expensive for 3D volumes. State-space models offer linear scaling, yet their performance depends on a scan order that should preserve 3D anatomy and incorporate clinically meaningful regions.
method: N6-TreeMamba replaces naive rasterization with a 6-neighborhood tree scanning strategy that builds an input-dependent token order over 3D MRI, preserving volumetric locality while enabling efficient long-context Mamba processing. Its radiology knowledge-guided anchoring module uses WMH segmentation to sample anchors from WMH and nearby background regions, prioritizing clinically relevant pathology while maintaining whole-brain coverage. Reordered tokens are processed by TreeMamba blocks for stroke-complication prediction.

title: NASD-Diff: A Noise-Assisted Structural Difference Diffusion Model for CT Angiography Generation from NCCT
motivation: CTA provides important vascular information but requires iodinated contrast agents that pose risks for patients with allergy, renal impairment, or repeated-exposure concerns, while NCCT is safer but shows vessels poorly. Although diffusion models have advanced modality translation, most use global random noise and do not explicitly model the regional structural changes caused by contrast injection, especially in vessels. A generation process that prioritizes vascular differences while preserving image texture is needed for contrast-free CTA-like imaging.
method: NASD-Diff introduces a noise-assisted structural-difference degradation operator that models contrast-induced attenuation of vascular signals during the forward diffusion process while adding controllable noise for high-frequency texture modeling. Its DeST-Net dual decoder separately predicts vascular structural differences and texture-related noise, and uses adjacent-slice conditional embeddings to incorporate context. A global perceptual refinement objective further regulates contrast, semantic consistency, and texture quality.

title: NEARL: Interacted Query Adaptation with Orthogonal Regularization for Medical Vision-Language Understanding
motivation: Medical image analysis needs models that can generalize across modalities and support diagnosis, but CLIP-like VLMs are pretrained on natural image-text data and exhibit a substantial medical domain gap. Prompt learning adapts only text, while unidirectional interaction fails to exploit CLIP’s dual-modality structure and can propagate errors between modalities. A parameter-efficient approach is needed to achieve bidirectional alignment while preserving the generalization of the pretrained encoders.
method: NEARL adapts a frozen CLIP image-text model through two parameter-efficient components. USEformer uses shared low-dimensional projections and learnable image/text queries to perform bidirectional cross-attention, producing mutually enriched visual and textual representations. OCA injects these cross-modal residuals through Gram-Schmidt-based orthogonal decomposition, separating novel domain information from incremental updates and reducing interference with pretrained knowledge.

title: NeRD: Neuro-Symbolic Rule Distillation for Efficient Ontology-Grounded Chain-of-Thought in Medical Image Diagnosis
motivation: Trustworthy medical image diagnosis requires explanations that map visual evidence to established diagnostic criteria, but opaque deep models limit clinical adoption. Concept Bottleneck Models score every predefined concept, creating inference and intervention burden, while generative rationales may select statistically discriminative but ontology-inconsistent concepts and lack validated intervention mechanisms. A method is needed to produce concise, ontology-grounded reasoning without extensive expert-authored rationales or exhaustive concept scoring.
method: NeRD first induces explicit logical diagnostic rules over clinical concepts from data, avoiding manual rule engineering. It then selects activated rules, simplifies their logic, and grounds the remaining concepts to distill compact, case-specific reasoning chains into multimodal chain-of-thought (MCoT) explanations. This rule-based distillation links concept-level interpretability with generative reasoning and supports concept interventions during diagnosis.

title: NetCorr: A Resection-Induced Network Perturbation Framework for Predicting Seizure Freedom in Drug-Resistant Epilepsy
motivation: For drug-resistant epilepsy, clinicians need to estimate seizure freedom after a planned or completed resection, but the epileptogenic zone is latent and must be inferred from imperfect intracranial EEG biomarkers. Channel-level events such as spkHFOs and network-level connectivity each provide partial information and have largely been studied independently. A framework that links these scales and quantifies how resection disrupts epileptogenic network dynamics could improve outcome prediction.
method: NetCorr constructs ripple-band synchronization networks from interictal iEEG and detects channel-level spkHFOs. It fits per-channel regressions from network participation features to smoothed spkHFO rates, using the resulting R² values as network-spkHFO coupling scores. Resection is then modeled as a perturbation of preserved-channel coupling, and a two-dimensional signature summarizes changes in coupling statistics for outcome prediction.

title: Network-Aware Bilinear Tokenization for Brain Functional Connectivity Representation Learning
motivation: Resting-state FC supports analysis of individual differences in brain organization, behavior, and mental health, but its high dimensionality, noise, and subject variability make compact predictive representations difficult. MAE methods require meaningful token units, yet region-centric and graph-based schemes treat FC as homogeneous and overlook modular network organization; network-pair blocks are also heterogeneous and cannot share a simple patch encoder. A tokenizer should therefore reflect functional networks while handling variable block sizes efficiently.
method: NERVE partitions FC matrices into heterogeneous blocks defined by pairs of large-scale functional networks and applies a structured bilinear tokenizer. Learnable network-specific region embeddings interact bilinearly to encode each intra- or inter-network block, preserving network identity while reducing parameter growth from quadratic to linear in the number of networks. These tokens are used in a masked autoencoder for self-supervised representation learning.

title: NeuroAlign: A Unified Plug-and-Play Enhancer for Visual and Linguistic Brain Decoding
motivation: Non-invasive brain decoding seeks to reconstruct visual stimuli and decode linguistic captions from fMRI, but noisy neural signals are poorly aligned with structured latent spaces of generative models. Pointwise objectives can fracture neural geometry, pooling can erase fine spatial detail, and unconstrained projections cause semantic ambiguity and drift, harming both visual fidelity and text decoding. A universal enhancer is needed to preserve topology, maintain multi-scale information, and anchor semantics without modality-specific retraining.
method: NeuroAlign is a plug-and-play enhancer that aligns arbitrary fMRI encoders with pretrained generative decoders through three modules. Hierarchical Dynamic Transport uses Sinkhorn-regularized optimal transport to preserve fine-grained feature topology, while Concept Memory Injection retrieves semantic prototypes under a concept-distribution alignment objective. Cross-Attention Fusion combines these spatial and semantic signals with asymmetric gated attention before projection into the generative prior.

title: NeuroFlow: Manifold-Aware Topological Flow Matching for EEG Decoding
motivation: EEG offers high temporal resolution and portability for visual brain-computer interfaces, but reconstructing images from it is ill-posed because neural signals are noisy, non-stationary, and semantically ambiguous. Channel-wise or static models miss transient functional connectivity, while graph aggregation can cause over-smoothing and dimensional collapse; diffusion-based generation further introduces stochastic semantic drift and high latency. A method is needed to preserve dynamic topology, compactly anchor semantics, and generate images along a stable, efficient trajectory.
method: NeuroFlow uses a two-stage EEG-to-vision pipeline. DynamicResGNN infers sample-specific functional connectivity and combines graph aggregation with residual fusion, while a Barlow Twins orthogonality constraint limits over-smoothing and dimensional collapse; a Prototype Refinement Layer retrieves visual memory prototypes to rectify semantic ambiguity. Conditional Flow Matching then learns a deterministic optimal-transport path from the rectified EEG representation to image embeddings, which are decoded by a frozen SDXL backbone with an IP-Adapter.

title: NeuroSonic: Conditional Flow Matching for EEG-to-Speech Reconstruction
motivation: Reconstructing natural continuous speech from scalp EEG is difficult because weak, spatially diffuse, artifact-prone neural measurements must be mapped to acoustically coherent speech trajectories. Direct waveform regression and existing GAN or diffusion approaches can be unstable under heterogeneous EEG conditioning; multi-step stochastic sampling can accumulate artifact- and subject-related errors. A trajectory-aware and robust generative formulation is therefore needed.
method: NeuroSonic formulates EEG-to-speech reconstruction as conditional flow matching, learning a deterministic probability-flow velocity field that transports noise-corrupted acoustic states toward clean speech. It embeds patch-level EEG and audio tokens in a shared space and uses a time-conditioned gated Transformer to parameterize the transport ODE. This explicitly models acoustic trajectories while avoiding stochastic iterative denoising, aiming to remain stable under artifacts and cross-subject variation.

title: NeuroSymb-MRG: Differentiable Abductive Reasoning with Active Uncertainty Minimization for Radiology Report Generation
motivation: Automated radiology reporting could reduce reporting workload and improve documentation consistency. However, encoder-decoder and retrieval-based systems may produce fluent but biased or hallucinated text, lack explicit clause-level multi-hop reasoning, and poorly cover rare conditions in imbalanced, noisy datasets. Interpretable reasoning with quantified uncertainty is needed to improve factual reliability and data efficiency.
method: NeuroSymb-MRG maps image features to probabilistic clinical concepts, composes them into differentiable multi-hop abductive logic chains, and decodes the chains into templated report clauses. Retrieval evidence and constrained language-model editing refine the draft, while a verifier identifies high-risk contradictions. Its active loop uses rule-level uncertainty and diversity to select informative cases and refine training and prompts.

title: NoiBox: Safeguard Frontier via Reverse Adversarial Diffusion for Noisy-Box-Supervised 3D Tumor Segmentation
motivation: Voxel-wise 3D tumor annotations are clinically valuable but expensive and difficult to scale, whereas a single coarse 3D bounding box can be supplied quickly. Loose clinical boxes contain normal tissue near their inner boundaries and can omit tumor outside the box. Hard box constraints, rigid pseudo-labels, and one-way propagation can reinforce boundary errors and confirmation bias, motivating soft supervision that represents coupled inner and outer uncertainty.
method: NoiBox partitions the volume into a far-field safe-background region and box-centered inner and outer uncertainty bands. It mines reliable foreground-core and safe-background seeds, then uses reverse adversarial diffusion to generate a detached soft safeguard-frontier target from outward foreground and inward background evidence. Training combines distance-decayed safe-background supervision with adversarial diffusion consistency, and can be applied to 3D segmentation backbones.

title: Noise-Aware Importance–Uncertainty Disentangled Multimodal Learning for Robust Cancer Survival Prediction

categories.value: Multimodal Integration with Clinical / Genomic / Biomarkers

motivation: Accurate cancer survival prediction is needed for personalized treatment because tumor staging alone cannot fully capture biological heterogeneity. WSIs offer technically stable but weak prognostic cues, whereas mRNA has stronger prognostic signal but substantial technical variability. Existing fusion methods commonly combine features directly and do not explicitly model this importance-uncertainty asymmetry or separate shared from modality-specific information, producing fragile multimodal predictions.
method: NADMSurv uses an importance-uncertainty dual-track module to preselect WSI patches and mRNA genes while quantifying modality- and patient-level noise. A noise-aware mechanism disentangles shared multimodal representations from modality-specific ones. Hypergraph neural networks model higher-order patient relations, and subjective logic with cross-attention and consensus operators performs uncertainty-aware evidence-level fusion.

title: Non-intrusive Body Composition Assessment from Full-Body mmWave Scans
motivation: Body composition assessment provides more clinically informative measures than BMI or weight, but CT and MRI are unsuitable for frequent population-level monitoring. mmWave radar can rapidly and privately reconstruct clothed body surfaces, but paired mmWave and internal body-composition data are scarce. MRI/CT posture differs from standing mmWave acquisition, so a method must address both missing paired labels and the domain gap.
method: The method trains one point-cloud encoder with multiple regression heads using synthetic mmWave-like point clouds from segmented MRI/CT, parametric SMPL human meshes, and mmWave data. The heads learn body-composition volumes, height, and body circumferences from anterior and posterior surface observations. This multi-task design exploits the complementary labels and geometry available from each source to bridge posture and modality gaps for VAT and BFP estimation.

title: Non-linear INR-Based Motion Modeling for 4D Radiotherapy
motivation: Respiratory motion complicates radiotherapy for lung and liver tumors because treatment requires a patient-specific relationship between an external surrogate and internal deformation. Conventional pipelines first perform deformable registration and then fit a linear surrogate-to-motion model. Such models cannot adequately represent localized hysteresis and spatially heterogeneous nonlinear motion, while existing dynamic INRs do not explicitly use an external control signal.
method: The proposed patient-specific INR motion model uses a SIREN to represent a continuous deformation vector field as a function of spatial coordinates and an external respiratory surrogate. It jointly optimizes image registration and surrogate-to-motion regression, eliminating prior pairwise registration. Separate forward and backward models are trained with cyclic consistency and spatial-temporal smoothness, while anisotropic frequency scaling accommodates different spatial and temporal dynamics.

title: Non-parametric Prototypes Enable Semantic Graph Learning for Whole-Slide Pathology
motivation: Placental WSI classification supports pathological assessment and clinical diagnosis, but WSIs exhibit substantial dataset-level visual diversity that per-slide patch selection often ignores. Fine-grained textual descriptions can add context, yet commonly treat attributes independently and fail to capture their hierarchy. Existing vision-language fusion also inadequately integrates complex visual-semantic relations, limiting generalization.
method: ProtoSG-Net first creates non-parametric dataset-level prototypes from WSIs and coarse pathological attributes to guide selection of informative patches. It then builds a prototype-guided semantic graph that models relationships among key patches and fine-grained attributes. Prototype-based calibration refines the hierarchy and visual-textual alignment of semantic features before graph learning performs global WSI classification.

title: Non-Stationary Spectral State-Space Networks with Region-Wise Frequency Routing for Robust Fundus Vessel Segmentation
motivation: Fundus vessel segmentation and artery/vein separation are important for vascular biomarker analysis but degrade under shifts in illumination, contrast, pathology, and acquisition domain. Thin capillaries depend on subtle high-frequency edge evidence, whereas lesions and appearance changes can resemble vessels. Uniform feature processing and generic regularization can therefore miss fine vessels or amplify artifacts, especially when annotated data are limited.
method: NS3Net combines a Mamba-based state-space backbone with NS3MoE, which routes frequency-plane regions to specialized experts. The module refines high-frequency Fourier magnitudes while preserving phase to emphasize vessel edges and capillaries, and retains low-frequency appearance through a residual path. Supervised two-view routing consistency aligns routing distributions for original and photometrically perturbed labeled images, regularizing the model without target-domain adaptation.

title: NR-Align: Non-rigid Alignment for Non-simultaneous Two-View 3D Coronary Reconstruction in Complex Cardiac Interventions
motivation: Two non-simultaneous DSA views can be sufficient for 3D coronary reconstruction, but cardiac pulsation and respiration cause non-rigid inter-view motion. This violates rigid-geometry assumptions and produces cross-view misregistration, vessel discontinuities, ghosting, and topology errors. Existing sparse-view approaches often use simplified rigid motion in synthetic training, creating a need for physiologically plausible deformation data and explicit alignment before reconstruction.
method: NR-Align uses physiology-driven synthesis to generate supervised paired coronary volumes with respiratory translation and cardiac torsion under asynchronous dual-view acquisition. Given union and overlap occupancy maps from dual-view backprojection, a 3D encoder-decoder predicts corrected vessel support and the cross-view-consistent region through separate heads. The aligned outputs are then combined for downstream 3D reconstruction, explicitly compensating mismatch before reconstruction.

title: NutriDiff: Phenotype-Consistent Diffusion Augmentation for Malnutrition Screening

categories.value: AI for Population Health, Public Health & Epidemiology

motivation: Elderly malnutrition requires early screening, but conventional quantitative measures require specialized instruments and visual bedside assessment depends on evaluator experience. Facial morphology may reflect loss of muscle and adipose tissue, yet clinical facial data are limited and practical acquisition constraints restrict existing methods. Standard diffusion augmentation cannot reliably control subtle malnutrition-related facial traits, so label-inconsistent synthetic images can introduce noise into screening models.
method: NutriDiff fine-tunes Stable Diffusion with view- and nutrition-class-conditioned LoRA adapters to generate candidate multi-view facial images. It detects facial keypoints and extracts features from the temporal, periorbital, malar, and jawline regions. Candidate images whose morphology deviates from the corresponding real-class distribution according to Mahalanobis distance are filtered out, and the retained images augment training of the screening model.

title: Occlusion-aware Disparity Estimation via Depth Prior Embedded Cost Volume for Stereo Endoscopic Images
motivation: Stereo disparity estimation is needed to reconstruct depth for 3D navigation in laparoscopic surgery, but occlusion and camera baseline differences create unmatched pixels with no valid correspondence. Conventional cost volumes therefore contain ambiguous or leaked costs, which destabilize aggregation and degrade disparity predictions. A method that can infer reliable disparities in these regions is needed for robust surgical vision.
method: DEDENet first predicts a coarse disparity prior by affine-transforming a monocular depth map in its Coarse Disparity Estimation module. Its Depth Prior Embedded Cost Volume converts this prior into a disparity probability distribution and iteratively fuses it with a conventional correlation volume through cross-attention. This depth-guided volume design supplies information where stereo correspondences are missing and improves robustness to occlusion.

title: OCS-MAMBA: Object-Centric, Logic-Guided Approach for Surgical Action Understanding
motivation: Real-time surgical action planning and adverse-event anticipation require long procedural context, explicit tool-tissue interactions, and adherence to safety rules. Existing self-attention models cannot efficiently retain the history of lengthy procedures, pixel-token representations lack object-centric structure, and static retrieval or text summaries lose evolving, fine-grained state. A system is needed that combines efficient long-range modeling with explicit semantic and surgical logic constraints.
method: OCS-Mamba decomposes dense DINOv2-reg features into sparse, trackable object slots using Adaptive Slot Attention and Gumbel-Softmax presence gating. A graph-factored Mamba state-space model propagates long-range temporal information over interaction graphs with linear complexity. A differentiable logic-constrained loss penalizes invalid instrument affordances and unsafe tool-tissue interactions, while a retrieval-augmented safety head provides guideline-based Stop/Proceed guidance.

title: Oculo: A Multilabel Dataset for the Identification of Ocular Abnormalities from Ultrasound Images
motivation: Ocular ultrasound is important for diagnosing vitreoretinal disease when optical media are opaque, but interpretation requires specialized expertise and has substantial inter-rater variability. Prior deep-learning studies generally use private datasets or single-pathology annotations, limiting reproducibility and objective comparison. A public, multi-label benchmark is needed to support standardized automated analysis across ophthalmic abnormalities.
method: Oculo releases 1,630 B-scan images from 1,242 patients with annotations for multiple ophthalmic abnormalities, enabling multi-label evaluation beyond retinal detachment alone. The study benchmarks EfficientNet-B0, ResNet50, VGG-19-BN, ViT-B-16, and ophthalmic or ultrasound foundation models under single-task and multi-task settings. It also compares full fine-tuning, linear probing, and LP-to-FT training strategies to establish reproducible baselines.

title: Omni-Sleep: A Sleep Foundation Model via Hierarchical Contrastive Learning of CNS–ANS Dynamics
motivation: Sleep physiology reflects coordinated but distinct dynamics of the central and autonomic nervous systems across EEG, EOG, EMG, ECG, and respiration. Existing sleep foundation models often fuse these signals in a topology-agnostic space, ignoring their physiological organization and becoming vulnerable to domain shifts and missing modalities. A representation learner that preserves within-system structure and brain-body synchronization is needed for generalizable sleep staging and disease assessment.
method: Omni-Sleep partitions PSG modalities into CNS signals (EEG, EOG, EMG) and ANS signals (ECG and respiration), then encodes each modality with convolutional patch encoders and RoFormer sequence encoders. Hierarchical contrastive learning enforces within-system consistency and aligns pooled CNS and ANS representations to capture brain-body coupling. Latent-space masked temporal modeling captures long-horizon sleep dynamics, supporting pretraining on large multimodal PSG collections and use with missing channels.

title: On the Behavior of Calibration Error Under Rater Disagreement
motivation: Medical imaging labels often contain legitimate disagreement among raters, yet calibration is commonly computed against a majority-vote label. Because majority voting nonlinearly changes the target distribution, even predictions of the true underlying probabilities can appear miscalibrated, undermining the oracle guarantee. A principled calibration target is needed so calibration error remains meaningful under subjective labeling.
method: The work formalizes each exam's latent positive-label probability and analyzes how majority voting transforms that distribution. It proposes evaluating calibration directly against individual rater labels with MR-ECE, or retaining consensus labels while analytically adjusting predictions with AdjustedECE. Theoretical analysis shows both protocols restore the oracle guarantee, and controlled sensitivity studies plus a breast-density case study test the resulting behavior.

title: On the Robustness of Temporal Vision-Language Models for Surgical Endoscopy Videos
motivation: Temporal vision-language models provide reusable prompt-based interfaces for surgical video understanding, but endoscopy routinely contains defocus, haze, blur, noise, cautery smoke, compression, and packet loss. These structured shifts can disrupt video-text alignment, and existing evaluations do not provide a reproducible endoscopy-specific protocol that separates artifact effects from dataset or procedure shifts. Robustness characterization and low-supervision adaptation are therefore needed for reliable clinical deployment.
method: The study defines Endo-C6, a fixed-severity benchmark of six endoscopy-realistic frame corruptions, and evaluates prompt-based temporal video-text classifiers on GI and laparoscopic datasets under clean and corrupted conditions. It standardizes clip length, stride coverage, prompts, and mean versus worst-case reporting to isolate artifact-driven failures. RobustEndoCLIP adapts a pretrained temporal CLIP with few-shot, parameter-efficient VeRA tuning on clean clips while keeping the prompt interface and backbone encoders frozen.

title: One Sequence to Segment Them All: Efficient Data Augmentation for CT and MRI Cross-Domain 3D Spine Segmentation
motivation: Automatic spine segmentation models are usually trained for a specific modality or contrast and can fail when deployment involves different CT/MRI sequences, scanners, or protocols. Although augmentation is widely used for generalization, its effect on cross-modality 3D transfer has rarely been isolated, and many advanced methods are computationally costly or difficult to adopt. A practical augmentation strategy is needed to improve out-of-domain robustness without sacrificing in-domain performance or training efficiency.
method: The study trains nnUNet-based 3D spine segmentation models on single-sequence datasets and tests them across CT and MRI domains with different contrasts, scanners, and fields of view. It augments standard geometric and intensity operations with GPU-based transformations such as intensity inversion, Scharr filtering, segmentation-driven redistribution, random convolutions, histogram equalization, bias fields, unsharp masking, and nonlinear functions to mimic modality and protocol variation. The GPU trainer integrates with nnUNet and MONAI while preserving efficient training.

title: Oneclass4ASD: Autism Spectrum Disorder Screening via One-class Classifier
motivation: Eye tracking could provide an objective signal for early ASD screening, but binary classifiers require ASD and healthy data even though ASD gaze patterns are difficult to collect and highly variable across individuals. This variability and limited data reliability can disrupt models trained to distinguish two fixed groups. A screening approach that learns normal gaze behavior and detects deviations is needed to reduce dependence on ASD samples.
method: Oneclass4ASD reframes ASD screening as one-class anomaly detection, training only on healthy participants' eye-tracking fixation patterns and treating ASD patterns as abnormalities at test time. It computes an uncertainty-aware weight for each image stimulus from the similarity of healthy fixation maps, giving more reliable and discriminative stimuli greater influence during feature fusion. The same uncertainty scores select a high-performing subset of stimuli for training.

title: One-Shot Data Selection for Medical Image Classification via Graph Coverage
motivation: Medical image classification often has limited annotation or computation budgets, making it important to choose a representative labeled subset before training. Active learning requires repeated oracle access and retraining, while one-shot facility-location methods use flat pairwise distances that overlook local manifold structure. A training-free selection method that captures neighborhood coverage and respects class balance is needed.
method: The method freezes foundation-model embeddings, constructs a global k-nearest-neighbor graph over all labeled training samples, and forms a sparse two-term coverage kernel from the normalized adjacency and its square. Greedy facility-location selection with class-budget constraints then chooses a representative subset that covers direct and two-hop manifold neighborhoods. This local graph approximation preserves the selection behavior of a full heat diffusion kernel while avoiding model training and expensive spectral computation.

title: On-Manifold Variational Learning with Heat-Kernel Priors
motivation: Unsupervised medical-image representation learning is needed when diagnostic labels are noisy, subjective, or fail to reflect morphological heterogeneity. Standard latent-variable models estimate prototypes by Euclidean averaging, which can place them in low-density regions off the data manifold and cause component overlap or degeneration as sub-populations multiply. A generative framework should learn label-free structure while keeping prototypes anatomically plausible and quantifying ambiguous groups.
method: The framework combines a variational latent model with a geometry-aware EM algorithm whose M-step selects each sub-population prototype as a graph medoid with maximal diffusion centrality on a heat-kernel-weighted latent graph. A Dirichlet energy regularizer preserves smooth intrinsic geometry and supports coherent transitions between sub-populations. Per-sub-population uncertainty scores provide label-free quality assessment, while the general manifold-anchored EM can extend to other latent-variable models.

title: Ontology-Grounded Structured Prediction for Dental CBCT Reporting
motivation: Dental CBCT supports assessment of teeth, jawbones, canals, and pathology, but routine reporting must jointly state what is present, where it is located, and how it is characterized. Existing benchmarks mainly address segmentation, while free-text metrics do not reliably measure clinical correctness such as omissions, hallucinations, or incorrect tooth localization. A standardized structured representation and evaluation framework is therefore needed to move from segmentation toward clinically grounded reporting.
method: The work releases 893 clinical reports for 529 ToothFairy3 CBCT volumes and converts them into validated RDF/Turtle instances based on a clinician-designed OWL ontology with 13 finding types and qualifier axes. CBCT reporting is formulated as three linked prediction stages: finding presence, anatomical slot allocation, and property prediction. A baseline combines frozen multi-scale VoxTell features, a structure-indexed encoder, and ontology-driven heads, with hierarchical metrics separating detection, localization, and characterization.

title: Open World MRI Reconstruction with Bias-Calibrated Adaptation
motivation: MRI reconstruction models are expected to operate across unseen centers, anatomies, protocols, and scanner conditions, where distribution shifts can severely degrade performance. The degradation reflects both a generative image prior that is misaligned with the target domain and training-tuned hyperparameters that no longer fit the test data. Adaptation is needed that uses only single-image supervision while preserving transferable knowledge and avoiding costly retraining.
method: BiasRecon treats open-world adaptation as alternating optimization of a calibrated generative prior, score-based denoising, and adaptive regularization. Frequency-guided prior calibration introduces layer-wise variables that selectively modulate frequency-specific features using self-supervised k-space signals, while score-based denoising uses the calibrated prior for reconstruction. Stein’s Unbiased Risk Estimator adjusts the prior-measurement trade-off to test-time noise without ground truth, requiring fewer than 100 tunable parameters.

title: Open-PMC-18M: A High-Fidelity Large Scale Medical Dataset for Multimodal Representation Learning

categories.value: Multimodal Integration with Clinical / Genomic / Biomarkers

motivation: Biomedical VLMs are highly sensitive to image-text alignment, yet literature-derived datasets often pair compound figures with short, symbolic, or context-dependent captions. Such coarse pairings mix heterogeneous panels and encourage reliance on superficial textual cues, limiting cross-modal representation quality and downstream transfer. Existing subfigure extraction work is limited in scale and contextual enrichment is largely absent, motivating a high-fidelity large-scale resource.
method: Open-PMC-18M applies a scalable curation pipeline with metadata filtering, transformer-based subfigure detection, subcaption extraction, and summaries of in-text references. A DAB-DETR detector is trained on 500,000 synthetically composed compound figures with diverse layouts and medical modalities, while language models generate subcaptions and contextual summaries. The resulting 18-million-pair dataset is used to train VLMs and evaluate retrieval and zero-shot classification across radiology, microscopy, and visible light photography.

title: OpenRC: An Open-Source Robotic Colonoscopy Framework for Multimodal Data Acquisition and Autonomy Research
motivation: Colonoscopy is clinically important but remains affected by occlusion, blur, operator variability, and ergonomic constraints. Existing efforts typically study robotic hardware or video-based perception separately, and available datasets rarely synchronize operator actions with actuation state and pose. This lack of integrated, open hardware and multimodal data blocks reproducible research on control-aware perception and autonomy.
method: OpenRC is a modular, low-cost retrofit for conventional colonoscopes that preserves the clinical workflow while synchronizing video, operator commands, actuation state, and electromagnetic-tracked distal-tip pose. The framework validates motion consistency and cross-modal latency, then provides a dataset of 1,894 teleoperated episodes covering navigation, failures, and recovery across ten task variations. Its open hardware, software, and aligned recordings support reproducible multimodal learning and closed-loop autonomy research.

title: OPGAgent: An Agent for Auditable Dental Panoramic X-ray Interpretation
motivation: OPGs support full-arch dental screening, but clinicians often need separate specialized models for tasks such as detection, segmentation, and pathology assessment. General dental and medical VLMs provide multitask flexibility yet underperform task-specific models on local spatial cues, while existing medical agents lack dental mechanisms such as FDI notation and dynamic ROI cropping. Current VQA benchmarks also miss unasked findings and cannot quantify hallucinations, so a domain-specific auditable system and workflow-aligned evaluation are needed.
method: OPGAgent is a training-free ReAct-style planner that coordinates hierarchical evidence gathering, a specialized toolbox, and a consensus subagent. It analyzes global dentition, quadrants, and tooth-level regions, using dynamic crops and stored FDI-based coordinates to invoke spatial, detection, utility, and expert tools. The consensus component combines tool evidence and resolves conflicts with anatomical constraints before committing supported findings. OPG-Bench represents clinical reports as Location-Field-Value triples to evaluate comprehensive findings and hallucinations.

title: OphthFlowBench: A Unified Ophthalmology Multimodal Benchmark with Workflow-Aligned Evaluation
motivation: Ophthalmology MLLM benchmarks are fragmented between image VQA and text-only questions, use restricted formats, and evaluate queries in isolation. This does not reflect clinical practice, which integrates multiple information types through a continuous sequence from perception to management, making practical utility and capability deficits difficult to identify. A unified benchmark and domain-specific model are therefore needed for workflow-level assessment.
method: OphthFlowBench combines multimodal VQA and text-only clinical questions in both open-ended and closed-form formats, and evaluates them across four sequential workflow stages: visual perception, clinical interpretation, disease diagnosis, and clinical management. The benchmark contains ophthalmic questions and images from high-quality sources and supports granular stage-wise analysis. Oph-RL is built on Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct and trained with supervised fine-tuning followed by difficulty-aware GRPO to specialize the model for ophthalmic workflows.

title: Opportunistic Cardiac Health Assessment: Estimating Phenotypes from Localizer MRI Through Multi-modal Representations

categories.value: Multimodal Integration with Clinical / Genomic / Biomarkers

motivation: Cardiac phenotypes such as ejection fraction and ventricular volumes are usually derived from cine CMR, which requires dedicated, high-resolution, ECG-gated acquisition and is costly. Localizer MRI is rapid and routinely acquired but coarse, static, and not intended for diagnosis, while ECG and patient metadata provide complementary temporal and contextual information. A method is needed to exploit these inexpensive modalities for opportunistic phenotype estimation without requiring CMR at inference.
method: C-TRIP aligns localizer MRI, ECG, and tabular metadata in a shared latent space while reserving inference for localizer MRI alone. Separate modality encoders are first pretrained, then fused through contrastive alignment that pulls together data from the same subject and separates different subjects. A final regression head predicts cardiac phenotypes from the enriched representation, combining spatial information from localizers, temporal information from ECG, and patient context during training.

title: OPS: One-Shot Point Prompted Semantics-Aware Learning for Medical Image Registration
motivation: Unsupervised registration avoids expensive annotations but typically optimizes global intensity similarity without distinguishing anatomical structures from background. Weakly supervised alternatives improve semantic alignment but require labor-intensive segmentations or landmarks, and SAM-based substitutes may need image-specific prompts and generalize poorly to unseen anatomy. A method is needed to inject semantic guidance with extremely sparse supervision across an unlabeled cohort.
method: OPS uses frozen DINOv3 features to turn one manually placed point per organ on a single reference slice into global semantic anchors. Feature-similarity matching propagates these anchors across all unlabeled volumes and produces dense semantic similarity maps. The maps guide registration through semantic feature embedding and semantics-aware loss optimization, which modulates representations and reweights similarity losses toward anatomically meaningful regions.

title: Optimal Steps for Fast Diffeomorphic Shape Registration
motivation: Clinical shape registration must scale to large cohorts while remaining fast, automated, and topology preserving. Learning-based methods require costly training and may be brittle to atypical anatomy, whereas volumetric processing is memory intensive and fast surface methods can tear meshes or invert triangles. A practical approach is needed that combines point-based efficiency with the topological guarantees of diffeomorphic registration.
method: The proposed learning-free pipeline alternates feature-aware matching with a conjugate-gradient quadratic solver and a diffeomorphic shooting step. A Majorize-Minimize/Demons-inspired scheme separates matching from regularization, while a closed-form 3x3 block-Jacobi preconditioner and early CG termination reduce the inner iterations. The method operates directly on point clouds, curves, or surface meshes and retains diffeomorphic topology guarantees without landmarks or training.

title: OPVD: On-Policy Chain-of-Visual-Thought Distillation for Medical Reasoning
motivation: Medical VLMs need step-by-step reasoning that links visual evidence to clinical conclusions, but rule-based RL methods usually provide rewards only for final-answer correctness and require extensive sampling. Sparse feedback leaves intermediate reasoning weakly supervised, while repeated policy exploration is computationally expensive and can be unstable. An efficient training framework is needed to provide dense multimodal reasoning supervision without external teachers or costly exploration.
method: OPVD constructs interleaved vision-language Chain-of-Visual-Thought trajectories using a shared policy model in teacher and student roles. The teacher receives the ground-truth answer as a prior, identifies informative regions, applies crop-and-zoom operations, and produces a detailed reasoning trajectory; the student processes the original input without that prior. Token-level on-policy distillation aligns the student’s reasoning with the teacher’s dense trajectory using only two sampling rounds, replacing sparse answer-level RL rewards and extensive exploration.

title: OR-Action: Multi-Role Video Understanding with Fine-Grained Actions
motivation: Operating rooms are cluttered, occluded, safety-critical environments where multiple clinicians interact with tools and devices over time, yet external OR video understanding remains underexplored. Scene graphs provide interpretable frame-wise relations, but converting these snapshots into temporally extended, fine-grained, multi-role actions is brittle, especially for long-tailed relations and state changes. A dense action benchmark and temporal modeling approach are therefore needed for workflow-aware assistance, documentation, and training.
method: The work introduces OR-Action, an action-centric benchmark with a fine-grained, role-specific taxonomy and dense temporal segments generated by rule-based distillation from scene-graph state changes. It evaluates scene-graph pipelines for temporal action recognition and presents a vision-only temporal pooling and multi-person classification model using a frozen video foundation model. A multi-view teacher to single-view student feature-alignment strategy distills cross-view context to improve recognition when only one egocentric stream is available.

title: Ordinal Diffusion Models for Color Fundus Images
motivation: Diabetic retinopathy progresses continuously, but color fundus datasets usually provide only five coarse ordinal stages. Treating these stages as independent categories in conditional generative models ignores their ordering and limits realistic synthesis, especially for underrepresented disease stages and populations. A model that captures the disease continuum is needed to generate clinically consistent training images.
method: The proposed ordinal latent diffusion model conditions generation on a scalar representation of diabetic retinopathy severity rather than independent categorical labels. It uses dual conditioning to separate retinal anatomical structure from disease-specific pathology, with a learned structural embedding guiding reconstruction. This design supports smooth interpolation between adjacent severity stages while preserving visual realism and clinically ordered disease consistency.

title: Ordinal Priors for Colonoscopy Temporal Segmentation
motivation: Accurate localization of colon anatomical segments in withdrawal videos supports automated reporting, coverage assessment, and disease-extent evaluation. Existing temporal models treat segments as unordered classes, causing temporally inconsistent predictions and anatomically impossible jumps despite the fixed proximal-to-distal sequence. Incorporating anatomical ordinality is needed for clinically coherent segmentation and better generalization.
method: The framework adds a distance-weighted ordinal regression objective to the temporal segmentation model, so errors between anatomically distant colon segments are penalized more strongly. At inference, an ordinal-constrained decoder refines raw predictions by enforcing anatomically plausible transitions along the colon. Together, training and decoding priors reduce flickering and non-adjacent jumps while supporting cross-dataset use without target-domain fine-tuning.

title: Organ-Invariant Tumor Representation Learning via Disentangled Adversarial MAE for Multi-organ Ultrasound Imaging
motivation: Multi-organ ultrasound varies substantially in organ appearance, speckle, contrast, and tumor type, making it difficult to learn tumor features that transfer across organs. Existing masked autoencoders entangle tumor abnormalities with organ-specific anatomy and generally lack explicit textual organ guidance during reconstruction. Disentangling shared tumor information from anatomical confounders is needed for robust multi-organ tumor classification and segmentation.
method: DA-MAE splits the encoder into tumor and organ branches and uses an orthogonal objective to decorrelate their features. Gradient-reversal adversarial organ classification suppresses organ-specific information in the tumor branch, while BiomedCLIP-derived organ text prompts guide the decoder toward organ-aware reconstruction. The shared pretraining scheme transfers the organ-invariant tumor encoder to downstream classification and segmentation across organs.

title: OrthoFlow: Decoupled Landmark Prediction and Image Synthesis for Orthodontic Treatment Outcome Visualization
motivation: Visualizing post-treatment facial profiles from lateral cephalograms is valuable for orthodontic planning and patient communication, but outcomes depend nonlinearly on skeletal, dental, and soft-tissue changes and on the chosen treatment plan. Conventional indices or landmark predictors provide limited visual information, while direct image translation can ignore anatomical geometry and suffer from alignment and domain-shift issues. A plan-conditioned method that predicts structure and appearance coherently is needed.
method: OrthoFlow decomposes prediction into geometry and appearance. A text-conditioned Flow Matching model with a Graph-Transformer backbone predicts post-treatment landmark displacements from the treatment plan, modeling local topology and global structure interactions. A second conditional Flow Matching model synthesizes the post-treatment cephalogram from the predicted anatomical contour and the pretreatment image, allowing image generation to focus on appearance while respecting explicit geometry.

title: OrthoMorphNet: Alignment-Guided Hierarchical Morphological Synthesis of Post-orthodontic Dentition and Gingiva
motivation: Digital orthodontic planning needs accurate post-treatment tooth arrangement and surrounding gingival morphology from pretreatment scans. Existing learning-based alignment methods mainly predict rigid tooth motions, leaving nonlinear gingival deformation unknown, while stochastic diffusion outputs are less suitable for deterministic clinical setup refinement. Joint, anatomically plausible prediction of dentition and gingiva is therefore needed for faithful simulation and appliance planning.
method: OrthoMorphNet first predicts per-tooth translations and unit-quaternion rotations by combining local tooth geometry with global spatial context through cross-attention. Its composite objective imposes geometric regularization, collision avoidance, and arch continuity for deterministic, physically plausible alignment. The predicted dentition then conditions a Swin-transformer 3D encoder-decoder that synthesizes gingiva in volumetric indicator-grid space, with Marching Cubes extracting the final surface.

title: OSCAR: Occupancy-Based Shape Completion via Acoustic Neural Implicit Representations
motivation: Ultrasound-guided spine intervention requires complete 3D vertebral geometry, but acoustic shadowing and reverberation expose only fragments of hard-tissue surfaces and vary across viewpoints. Existing shape completion methods often use annotated point clouds and treat shadows as missing data, ignoring ultrasound image formation and view-dependent acoustic effects. A physics-informed, label-free completion method is needed to reconstruct occluded anatomy robustly from partial B-mode observations.
method: OSCAR uses a coupled latent space that represents both ultrasound appearance and vertebral shape, together with a Neural Implicit Representation modeling spatial occupancy and acoustic interactions. Ray-traced acoustic parameters let the model account for view-dependent signal transmission and infer unseen regions without explicit shadow labels or labels at inference. The coupled representation supports label-free surface extraction, multi-view completion, and acoustic image synthesis from a known shape.

title: OsteoFlow: Lyapunov-Guided Flow Distillation for Predicting Bone Remodeling after Mandibular Reconstruction
motivation: Long-term mandibular remodeling after segmental reconstruction affects graft-host union, yet nonunion remains common and local interface geometry is an important determinant of healing. Physics-based simulations are costly and case-dependent, while standard generative models and one-step distillation do not enforce biologically plausible, trajectory-level evolution from early to late postoperative scans. A data-driven method that preserves longitudinal transport consistency and interface anatomy is needed, particularly in low-data settings.
method: OsteoFlow formulates remodeling as conditional flow transport from Day-5 to Year-1 CT regions of interest and predicts a time-dependent image-space velocity field. A registration-derived stationary velocity-field teacher provides a continuous trajectory, which is distilled through Lyapunov-guided supervision rather than only one-step matching. Rectified-flow supervision and a resection-aware, bone-focused image loss jointly improve rollout stability, anatomical correspondence, and endpoint fidelity near the graft-host interface.

title: OTCHA: Optimal Transport-Driven Confidence-Aware Latent Hub Alignment for Multi-view Medical Image Classification
motivation: Multiple 2D medical views provide complementary projections, but they are often unregistered and contain view-specific artifacts, background, and varying coverage. Directly fusing dense per-view tokens allows unreliable content to contaminate shared representations and reduces robustness across view configurations. A general mechanism for partial cross-view matching and token reliability is needed to preserve diagnostically informative correspondences.
method: OTCHA inserts learnable latent hub tokens between per-view patch embedding and fusion. For each view, an entropic optimal-transport plan matches patches to hubs using feature similarity and geometry, while token-conditional dustbins permit partial matching and rejection of irrelevant content. Transport confidence gates hub-mediated message passing and weights an optimal-transport representation-alignment loss, producing refined tokens for robust multi-view classification.

title: OT-Coupled Flow: Towards Realistic TEE Simulation via Unpaired Cross-Modality Translation with Anatomical Consistency
motivation: Realistic CT-based TEE simulation could support procedural training and robotic navigation, but existing simulators often rely on segmented anatomy and lack the acoustic texture and visual complexity of clinical TEE. Paired CT-TEE data and expert annotations are impractical because CT is static 3D whereas TEE is dynamic, operator-dependent 2D imaging with different physics and tissue deformation. An unpaired method must therefore match the real TEE appearance while preserving CT-consistent anatomy without masks.
method: OTC-Flow first pretrains an adversarial VQ-VAE on unlabeled TEE frames to establish a modality-consistent latent prior. Its Optimal Transport Coupled Flow Matching constructs pseudo-correspondences between CT-conditioned features and real TEE latent codes, enabling unpaired conditional flow regression toward the real TEE manifold. A pseudo-supervised anatomical consistency loop uses CT-derived geometry to constrain spatial alignment without TEE masks or paired CT-TEE data.

title: OTFusion: Optimal Transport-Driven 3D Multi-modal Medical Image Fusion for Enhanced Cross-Modality Representation
motivation: Multi-modal medical image fusion must combine complementary MRI and CT information while preserving anatomical structure and modality-specific semantics. Existing methods mainly use heuristic or implicit feature aggregation, making cross-modal distribution discrepancies difficult to control and potentially causing structural distortion or semantic loss. A principled distribution-alignment mechanism is therefore needed for stable, coherent fusion.
method: OTFusion reformulates fusion as optimal-transport alignment between source modality distributions and an ideal fused distribution, using Kantorovich dual potentials for regularization. Its collaborative dual-network design combines a U-Net mapping network with a latent potential network, while the Cross-Dimensional Interaction Module captures dependencies across spatial and feature dimensions. An adaptive constraint promotes modality complementarity while preserving feature consistency.

title: P2R-Net: Physics-to-Reality SM Calibration Network with Sparse Measurement Guidance for High-Precision MPI Reconstruction
motivation: High-fidelity MPI system matrices require exhaustive voxel-by-voxel calibration, which is time-consuming and must be repeated when acquisition conditions change. Physics-only simulations have a domain gap from real measurements, while sparse-recovery methods may inadequately model spatial coupling, anisotropy, and response scaling. An efficient calibration method is needed that combines physical priors with sparse, system-specific measurements.
method: P2R-Net uses a dual-branch encoder-decoder to map a dense physics-derived system matrix (SM) toward the measurement domain using sparse measured SM guidance. Multi-scale cross-attention injects measurement characteristics into physics representations, while the SC-Block models spatial coupling and the AFD module stabilizes and corrects physics-derived features. The design preserves physical plausibility and quantitative response information during calibration.

title: PALETTE: Pathology-Aware Latent Embedding for Targeted Tissue Expression
motivation: Virtual IHC staining could reduce the cost and labor of chemical staining, but morphology-to-expression mapping is complex and paired H&E-IHC slides are often spatially misaligned. Reconstruction-oriented encoders trained from scratch compress high-resolution tissue into low-capacity latents, risking loss of long-range context and semantically important structures. A representation-decoupled approach is needed to support coherent molecular synthesis despite these bottlenecks.
method: PALETTE separates semantic encoding from molecular image synthesis. A frozen pathology foundation model extracts high-capacity multi-scale continuous representations from H&E images, while a modality-specific VQGAN represents IHC images as hierarchical discrete tokens. A conditional Visual Autoregressive Transformer predicts these tokens coarse-to-fine using dual-pathway conditioning, preserving morphology while generating molecular texture.

title: PancCADx: A Multimodal Framework for Pancreatic Cancer Diagnosis

categories.value: Multimodal Integration with Clinical / Genomic / Biomarkers

motivation: Pancreatic cancer diagnosis from EUS is highly operator-dependent, and subtle early-stage findings create substantial inter-observer variability. Conventional CNNs provide limited semantic rationale, while general multimodal models face scarce specialty data and can hallucinate when trained with SFT alone. A clinically aligned system must combine visual evidence with expert-like, transparent reasoning.
method: PancCADx adapts the Qwen3-VL-8B-Thinking multimodal model to pancreatic EUS diagnosis with explicit Chain-of-Thought reasoning. It uses expert reasoning paths for Supervised Fine-Tuning and then Direct Preference Optimization to prefer clinically verified outputs over flawed ones, with LoRA enabling efficient adaptation. The resulting model combines EUS images with clinical information and is trained to provide evidence-based, less hallucinatory reasoning.

title: PANet: Probability-Anchored Network for Ultrasound Bone Segmentation
motivation: Ultrasound bone surface segmentation supports orthopedic analysis and navigation, but ambiguous boundaries, appearance variability, artifacts, and bone-like soft tissues make predictions unstable. Hand-crafted physical priors are sensitive to devices and imaging conditions, while other networks lack explicit confidence regulation and can produce false positives. Robust segmentation therefore requires controllable probability modeling that generalizes across clinical settings.
method: PANet inserts an explicit probability space between U-Net features and segmentation outputs, representing confidence in bone versus surrounding soft tissue. Global linear bias, local probability exchange, and global attention activate and discriminate bone responses, while progressive decoder exchanges refine boundaries and suppress false-positive propagation. A unified segmentation head supervises probability estimation across stages and aligns feature learning with the evolving segmentation.

title: Parameter-Efficient Self-Supervised Adaptation for EEG-FM under Fixed Computational Budgets
motivation: EEG foundation models can learn transferable representations from abundant unlabeled recordings, but clinical deployment faces distribution shifts across hardware, montages, and sampling rates. Full fine-tuning is computationally impractical, and it remains unclear how much unlabeled target-domain data is needed for reliable adaptation. A systematic, compute-constrained study is needed to establish efficient adaptation and data requirements.
method: The study performs parameter-efficient self-supervised adaptation by updating only the final encoder layer of pretrained EEG-FMs while retaining each model's original SSL objective. It evaluates both contrastive BIOT and masked-reconstruction CBraMod under a normalized fixed-compute protocol, then assesses the adapted representations with frozen-encoder linear probing. The analysis varies unlabeled-data quantity and patient/window composition across in-distribution and out-of-distribution clinical tasks.

title: Patch-to-Global: Random Patch Diffusion for Globally Consistent Megapixel Artifact Inpainting in Whole Slide Images
motivation: Bubbles, folds, and other artifacts in whole-slide images can conceal morphology and cause confident but incorrect computational pathology predictions. Detect-and-discard quality control may remove sparse but diagnostically essential lesions, while existing diffusion restorers generally operate only on small patches and lack global alignment. A megapixel-scale method is needed to reconstruct artifacts coherently with surrounding healthy tissue.
method: RestorePath uses a pathology-foundation-model-conditioned Latent Diffusion Model for megapixel artifact inpainting. Large Kernel Attention captures long-range histological dependencies, while random patch diffusion extends reconstruction beyond individual patches. Distance-Weighted Interpolation supplies conditioning from nearby healthy tissue, and an Adaptive Guidance Scale adjusts diffusion guidance to local content and complexity for globally aligned restoration.

title: Pathologist Attention–Aligned Report Generation for Prostate Histopathology
motivation: Pathologists selectively inspect diagnostically relevant regions of WSIs, and these attention patterns can provide visual evidence for report generation. Existing pathology report and VQA models rarely use human attention, relying instead on predicted semantic cues or manually specified regions that may not reflect actual expert viewing. Incorporating real pathologist attention could improve grounding, report quality, and interpretability without adding inference inputs.
method: The authors collect multi-scale viewport trajectories and synchronized verbal descriptions from pathologists examining prostate WSIs, convert them into component-specific saliency maps, and use them as training supervision. An auxiliary attention-alignment loss regularizes the report-generation model's image-token attention toward the corresponding pathologist attention distribution. The plug-and-play loss is evaluated with models using cross-attention and self-attention, while attention supervision is required only during training.

title: PathoMamba: Piecewise-Diffeomorphic Registration via Stiffness-Modulated State Space Dynamics
motivation: Longitudinal glioma MRI registration must align scans while preserving healthy-brain topology and accommodating tumor growth, shrinkage, and mass effect. Homogeneous smoothness regularization creates a conflict: strong regularization prevents folding but suppresses tumor deformation, whereas weak regularization permits pathology changes but can produce unrealistic folding. A registration model needs spatially varying dynamics that encode heterogeneous biomechanical behavior efficiently in 3D.
method: PathoMamba is a dual-stream registration framework that injects a tumor Signed Distance Function into Mamba state dynamics as a stiffness-modulating prior. Its six-direction isotropic scans address the causal bias of 1D SSMs, with the discretization step acting as numerical inertia: small values preserve healthy-tissue memory and large values permit rapid tumor updates. The network predicts a Stationary Velocity Field integrated by scaling-and-squaring, and trains with a Therapy-Aware Biomechanical Loss that constrains deformation according to tumor growth or shrinkage trends.

title: Patient-Conditioned Vision–Language Priors with Stable Mixture-of-Experts for Label-Efficient Alzheimer’s MRI Staging
motivation: Structural MRI-based Alzheimer’s staging is valuable, but reliable multi-class training is limited by scarce, inconsistent labels. The CN, MCI, and AD stages are ordinal, and a two-stage CN-AD error is clinically more serious than an adjacent-stage mistake, which standard accuracy objectives do not reflect. A label-efficient method is needed that uses transferable semantic priors, remains stable under small imbalanced batches, and explicitly models clinical risk.
method: The framework builds a frozen patient-conditioned VLM prior by prompting a CLIP text encoder with demographic information and aligning it with CLIP embeddings from representative MRI slices. A scale-preserving, norm-stabilized mixture-of-experts classifier uses this prior while avoiding expert collapse and logit-scale drift in small, imbalanced batches. An EMA teacher provides semi-supervised consistency, and the training and evaluation explicitly account for ordinal staging and clinically weighted errors.

title: PAVL: Enhancing Feature Prototype Alignment with Vision–Language Model for Semi-supervised Medical Image Segmentation
motivation: Semi-supervised medical image segmentation seeks to reduce the burden of voxel-level annotation by using unlabeled data, but existing methods can overlook voxel-wise uncertainty and subtle boundary features. Weak inter-class discrimination makes visually similar anatomical categories and their boundaries difficult to separate, while CLIP-based approaches often lack fine spatial and structural detail. A method is therefore needed that combines reliable local features with richer semantic guidance.
method: PAVL introduces unified representation matching (URM) to align teacher and student spatial features and voxel logits, improving consistency in uncertain and boundary regions. Its prototype alignment (PA) module selects uncertainty-reliable voxel features to construct robust class prototypes. Embedding fusion CLIP (EFCLIP) combines CLIP text embeddings with voxel-level visual features, joining global semantic priors with local structure to distinguish similar categories.

title: PCRP: Progressive Coarse-to-Fine Refinement for Pathology Grounding
motivation: Pathology visual grounding must localize tissue regions from specialized language, but targets are often tiny, low-contrast, blurred, or surrounded by similar background textures. Short medical descriptions can also drift toward irrelevant context, and box-only supervision provides insufficient boundary information. Robust grounding therefore requires stronger fine-grained visual cues and explicit boundary refinement.
method: PCRP uses separate visual and text branches and introduces Visual-Word Fusion (VWF), which retrieves word-specific visual evidence through text-to-vision cross-attention and injects it into text features with a learnable gate. Its two-stage Coarse-to-Fine Boundary-Aware Regression (C2F-BAR) first predicts a stable coarse box, then uses pixel-level masks from teacher SAM3 as boundary priors. A curriculum shifts refinement prompts from ground-truth boxes to predicted boxes.

title: PC-Seg: Progressive Cross-View Consistency for 3D OCT Segmentation from Sparse 2D Annotations
motivation: OCT volumetric segmentation is clinically useful but normally requires labor-intensive voxel annotations, while sparse labels are usually available only on standard B-scans. Existing semi-supervised methods mainly process slices independently and fail to exploit 3D context, and conventional multi-view or multi-network schemes require extra orthogonal annotations or are prone to overfitting under extreme sparsity. An annotation- and computation-efficient way to lift sparse 2D labels into 3D is needed.
method: PC-Seg begins with one 2D model that learns consistency between standard B-scans and orthogonal views, progressively producing reliable volumetric pseudo-labels despite OCT anisotropy. These pseudo-labels supervise a 3D model, after which 2D and 3D models co-train and mutually refine predictions through ensemble pseudo-labeling. The staged curriculum avoids the early confirmation bias and computational burden of training multiple networks from scratch.

title: PC-VLG: Position-Correlated Vision–Language Graph Alignment for Semi-supervised Medical Image Segmentation
motivation: Semi-supervised segmentation must achieve anatomically consistent predictions with few pixel-level labels, but visual-only consistency methods can be unstable in complex regions. Existing vision–language methods usually assume spatially agnostic pixel–text or mask–text correspondence, so adjacent or visually similar organs may share ambiguous textual matches and blurred boundaries. Explicit object-level positional relations are needed to disambiguate cross-modal anatomy.
method: PC-VLG builds a Vision–Language Graph Alignment Network in which anatomical structures are represented as graph nodes carrying visual, textual, and positional cues. Position-Correlated Cross-Modal Graph modules encode geometry-aware relations between objects, enabling structured alignment beyond pixel–text or mask–text matching. The framework combines coarse segmentation with visual and textual anatomical prior branches for semi-supervised learning.

title: Peeling an Onion: Layer-Wise Doppler-Backprojected Ultrasound Microvascular Vector Flow Imaging
