motivation: Complete vector flow fields are important for quantitative microvascular hemodynamics, but least-squares VFI is intrinsically unstable when only a limited range of transmit and receive angles is available. Alternative microbubble or erythrocyte super-resolution approaches require long acquisitions and do not directly provide instantaneous blood-cell flow. A method that exploits vessel morphology and local flow continuity is needed for accurate instantaneous microvascular vectors.
method: The method first uses microvascular morphology and angular Doppler velocities to estimate a vessel-aligned direction vector field. A layer-wise peeling strategy traverses the vascular network through complementary centripetal edges and centrifugal centerlines, while a Hessian-based direction estimator supplies candidate directions and Doppler data resolves their ambiguity. A weighted global optimization then backprojects angular Doppler velocities onto the direction field to recover the vector flow.

title: Percept-Aware Surgical Planning for Visual Cortical Prostheses with Vascular Avoidance
motivation: Cortical visual prostheses require electrode placement in folded and variable V1 anatomy, where placement determines the resulting phosphene map. Existing strategies emphasize visual-field coverage, anatomical landmarks, and vascular avoidance but do not directly optimize predicted task-relevant perceptual fidelity. A unified planning approach is needed to optimize perceptual outcomes together with surgical safety and anatomical feasibility.
method: The framework treats cortical electrode coordinates as learnable variables and optimizes them end-to-end through a differentiable model of prosthetic vision. Its objective minimizes task-level perceptual error while enforcing vascular avoidance and gray-matter feasibility on realistic folded cortex. The formulation also supports joint optimization of multi-electrode thread configurations under a fixed insertion budget.

title: Perfusion Aware Infarct Core and Penumbra Segmentation on NCCT with Region Constraints
motivation: Joint infarct-core and penumbra segmentation from NCCT could support rapid acute ischemic stroke decisions, but the penumbra is poorly visualized on NCCT and has been largely underexplored. Handcrafted hemispheric-symmetry priors are fragile to anatomical variation, chronic lesions, and positioning, while generic pretrained features are not inherently aligned with lesion physiology. The task needs structural and perfusion-aware guidance without requiring perfusion imaging at inference.
method: CoMPASS-Net uses a pretrained DINOv3-ViT encoder with a lightweight ResUNet decoder to jointly predict infarct core and total ischemic tissue, from which penumbra is derived as their difference. A mismatch-ratio classification head imposes a clinically meaningful regional relationship between the two masks without assuming hemispheric symmetry. A segmentation-guided conditional diffusion branch, supervised by perfusion maps such as Tmax, learns a physiology-aware intermediate representation that highlights perfusion abnormalities.

title: PET-Adapter: Test-Time Domain Adaptation for Full and Limited-Angle PET Image Reconstruction
motivation: PET reconstruction is degraded by Poisson noise and physical effects, with limited-angle acquisitions making the problem harder. Deep models often generalize poorly to unseen scanners, tracers, and anatomies, while practical adaptation data may lack paired reference images. An efficient adaptation strategy is needed that preserves measurement-informed reconstruction quality across full- and limited-angle settings.
method: PET-Adapter performs dataset-wide unsupervised test-time domain adaptation of a generative reconstruction model pretrained only on phantom data. It introduces layer-wise low-rank anatomical conditioning, including MR guidance, to adapt across anatomies, tracers, and scanners without paired ground truth. Ordered Subset Expectation Maximization reconstructions provide a physics-informed warm start through diffusion inversion, reducing sampling from 50 steps to 2.

title: PETFlux: Taming Natural Foundation Models for Accurate MRI-to-PET Synthesis
motivation: MRI-to-PET synthesis could provide functional biomarkers without radiation, but anatomy does not uniquely determine metabolism, making the mapping ill-posed. Limited paired molecular-imaging data can cause medical generative models to overfit, oversmooth, or create misleading textures, and natural-image foundation models have a substantial domain and semantic mismatch. The problem requires domain adaptation, patient-specific metabolic guidance, and explicit preservation of functional detail.
method: PETFlux adapts the pretrained Flux.1 Kontext backbone to MRI-to-PET synthesis using Low-Rank Adaptation within a rectified flow-matching framework. Patient metadata is converted into soft tokens and combined with LLM-generated metabolic descriptions grounded in a curated clinical knowledge base, supplying patient-specific semantic guidance. A log-scale focal frequency loss emphasizes clinically important high-frequency metabolic detail while penalizing artificial textures.

title: PhaseAT: Fourier Phase Adversarial Training for Medical Image Domain Generalization
motivation: Medical imaging models face distribution shifts from scanners, protocols, reconstruction pipelines, and patient populations, while access to target domains is often limited. Existing domain-generalization methods commonly diversify style or intensity but can remain dependent on unstable texture correlations, and pixel-space perturbations may emphasize irrelevant high-frequency noise. Since Fourier phase preserves spatial organization more than appearance, a phase-focused robustness objective is needed to discourage shortcut learning.
method: PhaseAT generates adversarial training views by perturbing only the Fourier phase of the luminance channel in YCbCr space while preserving the amplitude spectrum. A phase-saliency mask focuses bounded updates on frequencies whose phase changes most affect the loss. The model is optimized with a weighted combination of losses on clean and phase-perturbed images, encouraging robustness to geometry-focused shifts in both single-source and multi-source DG.

title: PhaseGen: A Diffusion-Based Approach for Complex-Valued MRI Data Generation
motivation: MRI raw k-space contains phase as well as magnitude information, but most clinical AI methods use magnitude-domain images and discard phase. Public magnitude-only datasets are abundant, whereas complex-valued k-space datasets and diagnostic labels are scarce. A way to derive plausible complex data from magnitude images is therefore needed to make phase-informed downstream learning more accessible.
method: PhaseGen is a magnitude-conditioned diffusion framework that generates MRI phase while keeping the supplied magnitude fixed, yielding synthetic complex-valued images that can be Fourier-transformed to k-space. It uses complex-valued diffusion noise and a complex-valued residual U-Net, with magnitude supplied as a constant conditioning channel throughout denoising. The synthetic raw data is intended for pretraining downstream k-space models and subsequent fine-tuning with limited real phase data.

title: PhaseMamba: Two-Stage Learning from Short Clips to Full Procedures for Online Surgical Phase Recognition
motivation: Online surgical phase recognition must label long videos using only past frames, despite redundant content, noisy frames, ambiguous visual differences, and abrupt transitions. Transformer temporal models can be costly for long real-time sequences, while existing Mamba methods do not adequately address variable phase duration and unstable transitions. Efficient causal modeling that preserves both local transition cues and long-range procedure context is needed.
method: PhaseMamba learns surgical phases progressively in two stages. A bidirectional Mamba local learner is pretrained on short clips with joint phase-classification and transition-detection heads to produce transition-aware features. A forward-only Mamba then fuses these local features with frame features for causal full-procedure inference, followed by a phase-order refinement that suppresses implausible low-confidence transitions using training-derived priors.

title: PhyDiCT: Plug-and-Play CT Reconstruction from Sparse X-Rays via Differentiable Rendering and Strong Priors
motivation: Reconstructing a 3D lung CT volume from only a few X-ray views is severely ill-posed because much volumetric information is absent. Conventional approaches generally need many projections, while fully trained learning methods require costly paired 2D-3D data and may generalize poorly to unseen pathology. Existing plug-and-play diffusion approaches also often use weak, unconditional natural-image priors and rewards that do not model physical projection formation.
method: PhyDiCT is a training-free plug-and-play method that steers a pretrained text-conditioned 3D CT diffusion model during inference. Its differentiable reward renders candidate volumes into X-ray projections using the Beer-Lambert law, enforcing 3D-to-2D observation fidelity. Split Gibbs sampling alternates reward-guided likelihood optimization with denoising under the CT prior, and an extra-compute refinement step targets artifacts and anatomical coherence.

title: PhyRadGS: Physics-Aware Radiative Gaussian Splatting for Fly-Scanning CBCT Reconstruction
motivation: In fly-scanning CBCT, the gantry rotates continuously while flat-panel detector rows are read out at different times. Static, instantaneous-geometry reconstruction assumptions therefore cause angular motion blur, row-dependent geometric distortion, and loss of fine structures. Explicit temporal modeling is needed, but conventional temporal supersampling is too expensive for time-sensitive use.
method: PhyRadGS represents the attenuation field using learnable 3D Gaussians and incorporates known fly-scan kinematics into the X-ray acquisition model. It partitions detector rows into strips to model rolling-shutter timing and subdivides each exposure into temporal micro-states to approximate motion blur. A multi-pose batch-rendering kernel parallelizes these micro-view renderings before assembling the final projection.

title: Physical-Driven Unified Implicit Regularization Network with Scan Parameter Prompts for Accelerated Multi-parametric MR Imaging
motivation: Multi-parametric MRI provides clinically useful tissue maps but requires multiple contrast acquisitions and consequently long scan times. Two-step accelerated pipelines propagate reconstruction artifacts into quantitative fitting, whereas direct one-step approaches can have misaligned reconstruction and quantification objectives. A physically consistent formulation that tightly couples both tasks is needed for stable, interpretable accelerated imaging.
method: PDUIR-Net unrolls an implicit-regularization solver for a unified objective that jointly estimates multi-contrast images and quantitative maps under acquisition, signal-physics, image-prior, and map-prior constraints. Its reconstruction module uses scan parameters as prompts to separate shared from contrast-specific information across contrasts. A proximal quantitative-mapping module learns data-driven priors on cross-contrast signal ratios, enabling progressive end-to-end joint estimation.

title: Physics-Based iOCT Sonification for Real-Time Interaction Awareness in Subretinal Injection
motivation: Subretinal injection requires precise cannula depth control in a very thin retinal region while avoiding the poorly regenerative RPE beneath the target. En face microscopy lacks direct depth information, while interpreting iOCT cross-sections alongside the microscope view increases visual attention demands and cognitive load. Auditory feedback must convey not only needle position but also interaction-induced retinal deformation during injection.
method: The proposed framework converts segmented retinal layers from streaming iOCT B-scans into structured auditory feedback through a physics-inspired acoustic model. Needle motion and injection-induced retinal-layer displacement act as excitation inputs, allowing the sound to encode retinal entry, proximity to the RPE safety boundary, and subretinal bleb formation. The real-time design is intended as a complementary guidance channel during interactive surgery.

title: Physics-Driven Cold Diffusion with Severity-Aware Sampling and Adaptive Degradation Estimation for MRI Motion Artifact Removal
motivation: Patient motion during MRI acquisition produces k-space phase inconsistencies that obscure anatomy and can compromise diagnosis or require repeat scans. Paired clean/corrupted data are scarce, unpaired translation can confuse acquisition style with artifacts, and standard diffusion adds Gaussian noise that does not reflect motion corruption. Stochastic reverse sampling can also introduce variability and risk hallucinated anatomy.
method: This method formulates MRI motion artifact removal as noise-free cold diffusion trained only on motion-free images. Its deterministic forward degradation operator uses acquisition-consistent k-space masking and Dirichlet-weighted motion-state assignment to simulate motion corruption and align diffusion time with artifact severity. Severity-aware sampling and adaptive degradation estimation then guide a deterministic restoration trajectory for varied motion patterns and severities.

title: Physics-Grounded Weakly Supervised Histopathological Tissue Segmentation via Frozen Tri-Domain Prototypes

categories.value: AI for Neglected Diseases & Limited-Resource Settings

motivation: Pixel-level annotation for whole-slide histopathology is prohibitively costly, making weakly supervised semantic segmentation important. Yet large intra-class morphological variation produces fragmented pseudo-label seeds, and recursive pseudo-label noise progressively drifts the learned semantics. Spatial appearance is also sensitive to staining and pleomorphism, motivating stable physical references that capture structural and spectral invariants.
method: PhysPro stabilizes weakly supervised histopathology segmentation with offline, frozen prototypes in semantic, Fourier phase-morphological, and spectral-energy domains. A physics-semantics mixture of experts uses tri-scale fusion and sub-band amplitude calibration to separate spatial morphology from spectral energy into complementary representations. Its discrepancy supervisor compares the three prototype domains per pixel to distinguish reliable regions, boundary ambiguity, and label noise, then applies adaptive soft-label supervision and spectral recalibration.

title: Physics-Informed Surrogate Model Using Graph Neural Network for Cardiac Electrophysiology
motivation: High-fidelity cardiac electrophysiology simulation is important for understanding heart disease but solving coupled PDE-ODE models on cardiac meshes is too slow for real-time digital twins. Existing neural surrogates are often tied to idealized grids or lack explicit EP constraints and realistic anatomical anisotropy. A surrogate must account for varying 3D geometry and fiber architecture while preserving interpretable wave-propagation physics.
method: The method represents biventricular meshes as graphs whose node and edge features encode EP state, mesh geometry, fiber-sheet-normal orientations, and direction-dependent effective conductivity. An encoder-processor-decoder GNN with graph attention and an LSTM autoregressively predicts transmembrane-potential and recovery-variable increments from a window of prior graph states. Training incorporates monodomain and Aliev-Panfilov reaction-diffusion constraints to promote biophysical consistency.

title: Physics-Inspired Continuous Transformer for Fast QDSA Reconstruction
motivation: Intra-operative treatment of intracranial aneurysms would benefit from rapid hemodynamic assessment, but alternatives such as 4D Flow MRI, CTP, and CFD are impractical during intervention. Routine DSA can support API through time-density curves, yet irregular frame rates and dose-reduction gaps make conventional per-pixel Gamma-variate fitting slow and unstable. Physiologically implausible temporal reconstructions can also distort timing measures and downstream velocity estimates.
method: PIC-Former reconstructs a continuous DSA time-density curve from irregularly sampled frames using a causal transformer conditioned on inter-frame time gaps. Physics-inspired contrast-kinetic regularization encourages plausible contrast arrival, peak, and washout behavior without imposing PDE residuals. The reconstructed curves serve as the fitting engine for full-field API maps and for QDSA velocity estimation through shifted least squares.

title: Physio-Anatomical Prior-Guided Probabilistic Field Learning for Ultrasound-Based Neuro-Fascial Interface Landmark Localization
motivation: Ultrasound localization of acupuncture-related Deqi response zones is clinically important for safe and standardized treatment, but these neuro-fascial targets are visually ambiguous and vary substantially across anatomical sites and subjects. Deterministic landmark detectors that rely on texture or rigid templates cannot represent the depth-dependent, inherently probabilistic stimulation region and may produce overconfident, physiologically implausible points.
method: PAPF-Net reformulates acupoint localization as uncertainty-aware probability-field learning rather than deterministic coordinate regression. Its Category-Conditional Anatomical Prototype module selects site-specific learnable templates and deformably aligns them to each ultrasound input, injecting geometric priors for anatomical heterogeneity. A dual-head uncertainty decoder predicts the field mean and variance, with distribution-aware Sinkhorn supervision to model depth-dependent acoustic ambiguity and attenuation.

title: Physiologically Consistent Missing Channel Reconstruction and Cascaded MoE for Impairment Categorization from Visual Electrophysiological Signals
motivation: Visual electrophysiology offers an objective basis for visual impairment categorization, but real recordings frequently lose channels because of sensor failures, motion artifacts, or environmental interference. Existing imputation methods generally optimize generic signal similarity without enforcing electrophysiological plausibility, so synthesized structures can obscure clinically relevant patterns and degrade categorization.
method: The framework treats missing-channel completion as physiology-constrained generation followed by impairment categorization. A GAN uses a sequence-to-sequence Transformer generator and 1D CNN discriminator, trained with a loss that emphasizes stimulus-related waveform regions, multi-scale temporal structure, and evoked-response amplitude statistics. Reconstructed signals are then processed by a cascaded mixture-of-experts that performs mode-wise and binocular inter-channel gating before EfficientNet classification, suppressing unreliable or hallucinated structures.

title: Physiology and Anatomy Aware Inverse Inference of Myocardial Infarction for Cardiac Digital Twin
motivation: Accurate myocardial infarction localization is needed for risk stratification, but LGE-MRI is costly and resource-intensive, while ECG alone cannot quantify detailed infarct location, size, extent, or transmurality. Existing inverse-inference digital-twin methods often use unrealistic scar morphologies, model mainly depolarization while omitting repolarization, and have limited ability to capture subtle ECG changes or explain the inferred infarct.
method: The method builds a cardiac digital-twin pipeline with anatomy-aware stochastic infarct synthesis, generating irregular scars with border zones across locations, sizes, extents, and transmuralities. It simulates a virtual cohort of full QRS-T ECG waveforms so that both ventricular depolarization and repolarization are represented. PAA-Net jointly encodes 3D myocardial geometry and multi-lead ECG signals to infer infarct regions and improve interpretability of the ECG–infarct relationship.

title: Physiology-Aligned Hierarchical Network for Heart Murmur Detection
motivation: Automated heart murmur detection can identify abnormal recordings, but most methods operate at the recording level and do not indicate the cardiac phase or auscultation site driving a decision. They also struggle to integrate multiple site recordings into the patient-level diagnosis used clinically, limiting robustness and interpretability without fine-grained annotations.
method: PHANet follows the physiological hierarchy of auscultation, encoding phase-level Mel-spectrogram features, fusing phases within each cycle, modeling cycle sequences with a temporal convolutional network, and aggregating evidence across sites. Its phase-aware fusion combines a murmur classification guide with contextual feature saliency, while site-aware prediction fusion confidence-weights site-specific logits. Patient-level supervision trains these intermediate cues without requiring fine-grained phase or site labels.

title: Physiology-Guided Cross-View Spatial-Temporal Aligning for Early Prediction of pCR in Breast Cancer from Longitudinal Multimodal MRI
motivation: Early prediction of pathological complete response during neoadjuvant chemotherapy could enable timely treatment adaptation, but tumors often show little morphological change after only the first cycles. Existing longitudinal models depend on later time points, and conventional multimodal attention is not sufficiently sensitive to subtle early signals or discrepancies in acquisition views and resolution.
method: CALM fuses early longitudinal multimodal MRI using a multimodal Transformer with Physical-distance-weighted Cross-view Inter-modal Attention, correlating axial and sagittal features without resampling that could blur tumor texture. A Physiology-Gated Guidance Module uses the high tumor-signal saliency of DWI to guide cross-modal fusion and suppress background enhancement. Trajectory Margin Contrastive Loss constrains latent feature distances and directions to represent longitudinal pathological response trajectories.

title: PhysioSplat: Physics-Informed Dynamic Gaussian Splatting for Surgical Scene Reconstruction
motivation: Dense dynamic reconstruction from monocular endoscopic video is needed for navigation, augmented reality, and robotic assistance, but surgical scenes combine non-rigid tissue deformation, tool occlusion, and wet-surface reflections. Current 4D Gaussian Splatting methods generally optimize visual appearance with a single deformation field, lacking separate tool kinematics, biomechanical constraints, and optical modeling; this can cause interface shearing, implausible tissue motion, and highlight artifacts.
method: PhysioSplat extends dynamic Gaussian Splatting with three coupled physical components. It separates rigid or articulated tool Gaussians from deformable tissue Gaussians using semantic supervision, enabling tool removal and temporally consistent recovery of occluded anatomy. A differentiable biomechanical regularizer predicts stiffness and enforces deformation-energy, volume, and collision-repulsion constraints, while a specular-aware radiance model decomposes diffuse and view-dependent components under co-located endoscopic lighting.

title: PhysOCT: Physics-Guided Retinal Modeling for OCT Image Synthesis
motivation: OCT is valuable for retinal diagnosis and monitoring, but limited expert annotations constrain learning-based analysis and motivate conditional synthesis. Existing lesion- or segmentation-conditioned generators can produce visually plausible scans while allowing lesion evolution that is inconsistent with deformation of surrounding retinal layers, because they lack a practical physical model of lesion-induced forces.
method: PhysOCT is a plug-in conditioner for longitudinal OCT generators. Given consecutive lesion masks, a force prediction network estimates lesion-induced forces, and a differentiable meshfree solver based on enhanced Generalized Moving Least Squares with a stabilized Lagrangian update propagates retinal-layer geometry to produce a next-step structural prior. This prior and a deformation-aligned sketch of the previous scan condition a diffusion generator, coupling lesion evolution with anatomically consistent layer deformation.

title: PICA: Physics-Guided Implicit Neural Fields with Boundary Conditioning for Intracranial Aneurysm Hemodynamics
motivation: Patient-specific aneurysm hemodynamics support rupture-risk stratification, but conventional CFD requires segmentation, meshing, and iterative solving that are too slow for routine or emergency use. Learning surrogates are faster yet often oversmooth velocity fields, losing near-wall gradients and fine vortices that determine clinically relevant biomarkers; voxel models also have fixed resolution and operator models lack adequate local fidelity and boundary coupling.
method: PICA represents aneurysm hemodynamics as a boundary-conditioned implicit neural field over SDF-enriched voxel geometry. A multi-scale 3D U-Net extracts geometric features, FiLM injects patient-specific inlet centroid, normal, and flow-rate parameters, and a Fourier-encoded coordinate decoder predicts velocity at arbitrary 3D locations without meshing. Physics-guided divergence and momentum/vorticity regularization, together with progressive two-stage training, promotes physically consistent fields and cross-anatomy generalization.

title: Piecewise Dynamic Diffusion Regularization for Reconstruction of Cardiac Cine MRI
motivation: Real-time free-breathing cine MRI provides efficient imaging of true cardiac physiology, but each frame has very few measurements and motion makes reconstruction severely ill-posed. Strong spatiotemporal priors are needed, yet existing diffusion reconstruction methods are computationally demanding and generally limited to short gated acquisitions, preventing practical use on long real-time sequences.
method: PDDR embeds a spatiotemporal diffusion model as a prior within a variational cine-MRI reconstruction framework. Dedicated spatial layers learn cardiac anatomy, while temporal layers learn motion from gated cine data. The learned dynamic prior is applied piecewise across long sequences, allowing reconstruction of hundreds of free-breathing frames while controlling the computational burden of full spatiotemporal diffusion sampling.

title: PiMoE: Physics-Informed Mixture-of-Experts for Accelerated MRI Reconstruction
motivation: Accelerated MRI reconstruction is a heterogeneous inverse problem: spatial difficulty varies with acquisition-induced aliasing and encoding stability as well as anatomical complexity. Existing unrolling and adaptive methods allocate uniform capacity or route mainly from latent image features, making them vulnerable to distribution shifts and unable to reflect acquisition physics when assigning reconstruction resources.
method: PiMoE replaces a monolithic unrolled prior with specialized experts selected by dual routing. It derives aliasing susceptibility, phase alignment, and magnitude imbalance from the undersampling mask and coil sensitivities, combines them into a local difficulty score, and uses that score to balance physics-based and feature-based routing. Physics routing gains authority in highly ill-posed regions, while feature routing dominates well-conditioned areas, enabling token-wise adaptation without image ground truth for the descriptors.

title: PINet: A Multimodal Network for Pontine Infarction Segmentation and Early Neurological Deterioration Prediction

categories.value: Multimodal Integration with Clinical / Genomic / Biomarkers

motivation: Pontine infarction can cause severe disability or death, and reliable lesion segmentation together with early neurological deterioration (END) prediction is important for treatment planning. Manual assessment is time-consuming and variable, while existing methods usually separate segmentation and prediction or use uniform multimodal fusion, preventing lesion evidence from informing risk prediction and prognostic signals from guiding segmentation. An integrated model is therefore needed to exploit complementary imaging and clinical information.
method: PINet is a multimodal multi-task network that jointly segments pontine infarcts and predicts END with explicit cross-task interaction. It replaces pooling and upsampling with invertible DWT/IWT operations to preserve high-frequency boundaries, uses a Dual-Task Guided Fusion Module to produce task-specific combinations of MRI and clinical features, and applies a Mamba-based global aggregator for slice continuity and long-range dependencies. A second-order multimodal classifier models imaging–clinical correlations for END prediction.

title: PINNOCHIO: Physics-Informed Neural Network for Coupled Hyperelastic Interface-Volume Simulation in Orthognathic Surgery

categories.value: AI for Population Health, Public Health & Epidemiology

motivation: Patient-specific facial soft-tissue simulation is needed for iterative orthognathic surgery planning, but high-fidelity FEM is too slow and requires extensive parameter tuning. Pure deep networks are fast yet lack physical constraints and can produce invalid internal deformation, while a unified PINN is unstable because interface sliding and volumetric hyperelastic deformation follow different mechanics. Clinical data also supervise mainly the outer facial surface, leaving internal motion unobserved.
method: PINNOCHIO uses a hybrid sequential decomposition that first predicts discontinuous bone–soft-tissue interface motion and then propagates it through the tissue volume with hyperelastic physics constraints. The framework is trained with synthetic FEM supervision and adapted to clinical cases using only postoperative outer-surface supervision, enforcing internal biomechanical consistency without volumetric ground truth. This design separates heterogeneous mechanical regimes while retaining an efficient neural simulator.

title: Pix2Rep-v2: Data-Efficient Representation Learning for Dense Medical Imaging Applications
motivation: Dense medical imaging tasks such as segmentation require pixel-level annotations, whose scarcity limits development across new modalities, anatomies, and scanners. Existing dense contrastive SSL methods require sufficient crop overlap and incur high computation from many local negatives, while foundation models can demand massive data or annotation resources. A scalable, data-efficient approach should learn useful local semantics and support few-shot or annotation-free use.
method: Pix2Rep-v2 learns pixel- and voxel-level representations with a non-contrastive redundancy-reduction objective and an equivariance formulation based on a single spatial augmentation. Its multiscale design is intended to scale to 3D and wide-field data without the many negatives and restricted overlap required by dense contrastive methods. Besides linear probing and fine-tuning, it provides a training-free in-context variant that matches images to dense prototypes.

title: PlaneCycle: Training-Free 2D-to-3D Lifting of Foundation Models Without Adapters
motivation: Medical CT, MRI, and OCT are volumetric, but large 2D foundation models are usually applied slice by slice, which misses cross-slice dependencies. Converting them to 3D or adding adapters generally requires retraining and does not provide intrinsic 3D capability beforehand, while dedicated 3D pretraining has less accessible data. A training-free, architecture-agnostic way to reuse costly 2D representations is needed.
method: PlaneCycle is a parameter-free, architecture-agnostic operator that reuses a pretrained 2D backbone for volumetric data. It cyclically applies spatial aggregation over the HW, DW, and DH planes through network depth, using shared layers and plane-specific positional encoding to progressively integrate 3D context while preserving the original parameters. The lifted model can be used without training and remains compatible with linear probing or full fine-tuning.

title: Plane-Wise Retrieval Memory and Structural Evidence Fusion for Tetralogy of Fallot Video Diagnosis
motivation: TOF screening in fetal echocardiography videos depends on transient, view-specific findings acquired during probe motion, while real examinations often omit recommended planes. Generic frame or clip classifiers can miss flash-by cues, pool evidence without view-aware reasoning, and degrade under multi-center domain shifts. VLMs could provide protocol-based reasoning, but their tendency to over-interpret weak evidence requires explicit handling of non-assessable views and complementary retrieval evidence.
method: The proposed plane-aware VLM treats plane-labeled frames as keyframes and expands them with local neighborhoods to capture transient findings. It asks a clinically structured checklist only in view-appropriate planes, explicitly distinguishing findings that are not assessable from findings that are absent. A plane-wise memory bank retrieves normal and TOF prototypes through similarity log-likelihood ratios, and case-level predictions combine retrieval evidence with checklist cues modulated by plane coverage.

title: Planning the Perfect Burn: Multi-objective PSO for Multi-needle Thermal Ablation
motivation: Multi-needle thermal ablation of hepatic tumors requires balancing coverage, efficiency, safety, and insertion depth, yet planning is mostly manual and becomes combinatorially difficult as targets and needle numbers grow. Prior approaches often optimize only trajectories, place needles sequentially, fix ablation geometry or needle count, or use computationally expensive thermal simulation, so they cannot provide comprehensive Pareto planning at intraoperative speed. A joint, adaptive, safety-aware optimizer is needed.
method: The pipeline jointly optimizes all needle trajectories, ablation parameters, safety constraints, and per-needle activation using a decomposition-based four-objective MOEA/D-PSO. The objectives cover tumor coverage, efficiency, safety distance from critical structures, and insertion depth, while activation variables determine needle count and support pullback ablations. CUDA fitness evaluation and Vulkan safety-map rendering make Pareto planning fast enough for intraoperative use.

title: PoCoLT: Position-Aware Cross-Modal Learning with LLM-Decoupled Hierarchical Reports for TMD Diagnosis
motivation: TMD diagnosis requires comparing open- and closed-mouth MRI from each TMJ, but conventional single-image models do not capture inter-position interactions. Segmentation-guided methods require costly 3D pixel annotations, and existing image-only models ignore raw reports that contain useful holistic diagnostic information. Because reports mix position-specific details and are unavailable during practical inference, their semantics must be decomposed and aligned without making inference report-dependent.
method: PoCoLT introduces a TMD-tailored Position-Modal paradigm with Position-aware Intra-modal Construction and Position-aware Cross-modal Alignment. A Cross-position Visual Fusion module combines open- and closed-mouth MRI features while emphasizing globally informative channels, and an LLM-guided Textual Decomposition converts holistic reports into two position-specific and one cross-position subreports. Supervised hierarchical alignment first organizes the textual space and then aligns matching visual and textual levels, allowing report guidance during training but report-free inference.

title: PolypSteer: Counterfactual Endoscopic Synthesis via Training-Free Activation Steering
motivation: Endoscopic detectors should respond to pathology rather than confounding anatomy, motivating anatomy-matched diseased and healthy training pairs. Re-prompting diffusion models rerolls the whole trajectory and changes unrelated structure, while inversion-based editing introduces reconstruction drift and may require masks. A method is needed to alter only the target clinical concept while preserving all other image content exactly.
method: PolypSteer extracts a pathology vector from each contrastive prompt pair in the cross-attention layers of a frozen diffusion transformer. During generation, per-token cosine-similarity gates remove or add the concept-aligned activation while a shared noise seed keeps both counterfactual images on the same trajectory. This produces anatomy-matched pairs without inversion, fine-tuning, source images, or annotations, with an interpretable indication of where steering occurs.

title: PoseBridgeNet: Learning a Pose-Evolving Schrödinger Bridge for Multi-Organs Segmentation in Prenatal Volumetric Ultrasound
motivation: Mid-trimester fetal volumetric ultrasound can support prenatal screening, but multi-organ segmentation is difficult because of low contrast, low resolution, and indistinct boundaries. Variation in fetal pose changes organ arrangement, morphology, occlusion, and feature distributions, causing inconsistent performance across scans. Existing pose normalization or estimation methods are not integrated with segmentation to directly correct these pose-induced shifts.
method: PoseBridgeNet inserts a Pose-Evolving Schrödinger Bridge into a U-Net bottleneck to model pose-induced feature distribution shifts as entropy-regularized optimal transport with a learnable stochastic differential equation. Its Mixture-of-Experts decoder combines one shared expert for cross-pose anatomical commonalities with specialized experts for organ- and pose-specific variations. Joint optimization integrates stochastic pose alignment with multi-organ segmentation.

title: Positive Semi-definite Group-Aware Instance Disentangled Learning for WSI Representation
motivation: MIL is widely used for gigapixel WSI classification, but instance representations and decisions are entangled spatially, semantically, and at the aggregation level. Attention scores mainly reflect correlation with bag predictions, making it difficult to distinguish pathological factors, understand local contributions, or relate weights to true causal relevance. An interpretable framework should disentangle these factors and provide explicit effect-based decision weighting.
method: PG-CIDL learns WSI representations through three disentangling phases. Positive semi-definite latent factor grouping maps instances into a low-rank latent subspace and partitions them into groups to reduce spatial entanglement; cluster-reasoning instance disentangling uses probability-based counterfactual inference to estimate instance effects and separate tumor, microenvironment, and background semantics. Finally, a generalized linear weighted aggregation reweights features by these effects to make the bag-level decision more transparent.

title: Posterior-Aware Motor Phenotyping with Multimodal Imaging Validation in Parkinson’s Disease

categories.value: Multimodal Integration with Clinical / Genomic / Biomarkers

motivation: Parkinson's disease has heterogeneous motor profiles that can obscure trial stratification and precision treatment, even among patients with similar total severity. Existing data-driven subtyping is sensitive to hyperparameters, usually gives hard labels without uncertainty, treats different cluster granularities as conflicting, and lacks systematic multimodal imaging validation. A reproducible representation of motor presentations therefore needs uncertainty-aware modeling and validation beyond a single clustering choice.
method: The work uses Bayesian Gaussian mixture models to derive visit-level Parkinson's motor states from longitudinal MDS-UPDRS-III assessments, sweeping predefined model configurations and using patient-block bootstrap to assess occupancy stability. Posterior vectors support a three-tier confidence triage for clear versus boundary assignments, while Cramer's V reconciles partitions at different granularities. The fixed preprocessing and model are also applied without refitting to an external cohort, and states are examined against longitudinal motor relations plus DaTSCAN and structural MRI measures.

title: POT-SAM3: Prompt-Only Tuning for One-Shot Electron Microscopy Segmentation
motivation: Serial-section EM segmentation is needed to quantify cellular ultrastructure, but expert pixel-level annotation is costly and imaging or preparation differences create substantial domain shifts. Adjacent sections offer continuity for propagation, yet limited-annotation methods often require retraining or frequent per-slice corrections. Although SAM3 fits a detection-and-propagation workflow, it does not reliably recognize EM concepts and requires interactive prompts, including for newly appearing targets.
method: POT-SAM3 freezes SAM3 and learns only a small set of EM-target concept prompt tokens from one annotated reference section. Tokens are initialized from encoded instance boxes and optimized with segmentation supervision under two-view augmentations, then replace conventional point, box, and text prompts at inference. SAM3 performs prompt-free detection and tracking across sections, while detector candidates are added to account for newly appearing instances.

title: PRA-PoE: Robust Multimodal Alzheimer’s Disease Classification under Arbitrary Modality Missingness
motivation: AD classification benefits from complementary sMRI, PET, and clinical evidence, but real clinical cohorts have non-random and highly imbalanced missing modality patterns. Training and deployment may contain different modality subsets, causing context-dependent representation shift, especially for rare combinations. Existing imputation methods often treat synthesized features as fully observed, allowing uncertain estimates to produce overconfident and harmful fusion.
method: PRA-PoE combines Prototype-anchored Representation Alignment with uncertainty-aware Product of Experts fusion. Learnable global prototypes and availability-conditioned missing-aware tokens encode which modalities are observed, align representations across modality subsets, synthesize missing features, and refine observed representations. Each modality is represented as a Gaussian expert; closed-form PoE fusion automatically lowers the contribution of uncertain experts through lower precision.

title: Precision Recall Controllable Radiology Report Generation via Hybrid Natural Language and Clinical Reward Learning

categories.value: Multimodal Integration with Clinical / Genomic / Biomarkers

motivation: Radiology report generation could reduce the workload of clinical reporting, but conventional maximum-likelihood and language-metric optimization mainly favors fluent text. Such reports can remain clinically incorrect, incomplete, or mismatched to a clinical scenario. Different uses require different precision-recall trade-offs, such as recall-oriented screening and precision-oriented diagnosis, yet existing generators offer little explicit control.
method: The method trains a chest X-ray report generator with reinforcement learning and a continuous control parameter that adjusts the clinical precision-recall balance during inference. A clinical reward supervises the presence and absence of clinically relevant findings, complementing language-based objectives. Group-relative reward normalization is used within training groups to reduce reward variance and stabilize policy optimization.

title: Predicting Radiologist Expertise from 3D Gaze Patterns During CT Interpretation
motivation: Objective assessment of radiology expertise is important for training, and experts and novices show differing visual-search behavior. Handcrafted gaze measures may miss the complexity of this behavior, while most deep gaze-based skill assessment methods operate on 2D images or videos rather than volumetric CT. A model that incorporates attention behavior within 3D image context could support process-based assessment from an interpretation session.
method: The framework uses a DINOv2 vision transformer to classify radiologist expertise from thoracic CT reading sessions with synchronized eye tracking. Per-patch fixation signals are injected as a learnable log-space self-attention bias and used for gaze-weighted pooling of patch embeddings. These complementary mechanisms allow volumetric features to capture both CT content and the regions receiving reader attention.

title: Preoperative Simulation of Personalized Breast Reconstruction via Implant Prior Controllable Diffusion
motivation: After mastectomy, implant selection and placement for breast reconstruction are often based on coarse measurements and repeated intraoperative adjustments. Discrete implant shapes may not fit individual anatomy, contributing to asymmetry and suboptimal aesthetic outcomes. Existing outcome simulations either focus on assessment after surgery or prioritize visual plausibility without explicitly modeling surgical variables and anatomically faithful reconstruction planning.
method: The proposed pipeline generates postoperative chest CT within the surgical breast ROI using conditional 3D latent-diffusion inpainting, preserving anatomy outside the region. It builds a canonical implant-template library from postoperative implant masks, then scales and anatomically aligns a selected template to construct a patient-specific spatial implant prior. A ControlNet-style branch encodes this prior and injects multiscale features into the diffusion U-Net while the pretrained backbone is frozen, enforcing implant-related geometry during generation.

title: Pressure-Tuned Auditor for Sycophancy-Resistant Breast Ultrasound VLM Diagnosis
motivation: Breast-ultrasound BI-RADS decisions determine observation, follow-up, or biopsy, so prompt-induced diagnostic errors can be clinically consequential. Medical VLMs may exhibit sycophancy, abandoning a correct assessment to agree with a biased clinician suggestion and potentially reinforcing confirmation bias. Existing defenses are largely text-only, lack clinically motivated medical-imaging evaluation, and do not provide post-hoc correction of a sycophantic output.
method: PTA establishes a breast-ultrasound sycophancy benchmark using clean and clinically misleading prompts, then applies multimodal Pressure-Tune training to an auditing agent. Training combines adversarial rationale supervision with visual grounding so the agent can identify localizable ultrasound evidence. In a two-agent pipeline, the independently trained auditor reviews and corrects the initial VLM output after a potential prompt-induced diagnostic flip.

title: PriLoRA: Prior-Conditioned Low-Rank Adapters for Medical Vision Models
motivation: Medical imaging foundation models are costly to fully fine-tune because curated data and dense expert annotations are limited. LoRA reduces the update cost but its purely linear low-rank updates can have limited expressivity. Sinusoidal adapters can increase capacity, but their fixed frequency is sensitive and difficult to transfer across medical modalities and tasks.
method: PriLoRA retains frozen backbones and LoRA factors, but applies an input-conditioned sinusoidal transformation to the low-rank update. A lightweight modulator extracts input-derived prior features and predicts amplitude, effective frequency, phase, and additive-shift parameters for each block and sample. This makes adapter expressivity adaptive while retaining LoRA-style modularity and parameter efficiency without a task-specific fixed-frequency search.

title: Prior-Anchored Debiasing for Long-Tailed Multi-Organ Pathology Report Generation
motivation: Pathology report generation from WSIs has mostly been developed for single organs, whereas clinical practice involves multiple organs with long-tailed sample distributions. In this setting, visual encoders can favor head-organ morphologies and miss tail-organ cues, while decoders can overfit head-class report language. Fluent reports for underrepresented organs may therefore be diagnostically unreliable, and long-tail classification remedies do not directly solve free-text generation.
method: PriOrGen uses two prior-anchored components for multi-organ WSI report generation. The Visual-Prototype Anchored Bottleneck applies the information bottleneck principle with learnable anchors to retain diagnostically relevant patches while filtering redundant, head-biased visual information. The Meta-Report Anchored Bank distills organ-specific representative report templates and retrieves relevant textual priors to guide the decoder toward organ-faithful narratives.

title: Prior-Guided Hierarchical Vector Quantized-VAE for Digital Subtraction Angiography Generation
motivation: DSA is essential for vascular visualization during interventions, but movement between pre-contrast and live frames creates artifacts that can obscure vessels and require repeat procedures. Registration can be expensive and unreliable in complex anatomy, while existing deep models may use only the live frame and continuous latent representations. Without the mask-image anatomical prior and robust separation of noise, reconstructions can be fragmented, particularly with low contrast or severe motion.
method: PH-VQVAE uses a dual-branch hierarchical VQ-VAE encoder to extract multiscale features from the pre-contrast mask and contrast live image. At each scale, window-based cross-attention fuses the anatomical prior with local contrast differences, implementing feature-space soft subtraction that tolerates local misalignment. Hierarchical discrete codebooks represent large and small vessels while filtering motion inconsistencies and background noise that lack compact discrete representations.

title: PRISM: Differentiable Analysis-by-Synthesis for Fixel Recovery in Diffusion MRI
motivation: Diffusion MRI microstructure fitting is highly nonconvex, and conventional voxelwise processing discards spatial coherence, making recovery of multiple fibers in narrow crossings unreliable. Bias fields, per-measurement intensity variation, and Rician magnitude noise further destabilize such recovery when handled in separate preprocessing steps. A jointly optimized, spatially aware inverse model is therefore needed for robust fixel estimation.
method: PRISM performs differentiable analysis-by-synthesis over spatial patches using an explicit multi-compartment model with CSF, gray matter, up to K white-matter fiber compartments, and a restricted compartment. It jointly optimizes tissue parameters and nuisance calibration, with repulsion and sparsity priors providing soft fiber model selection and spatial coherence. The framework supports either fast MSE fitting or Rician NLL fitting that self-supervises the noise level.

title: Privacy-Preserving Video-Based Facial Palsy Recognition via Dynamic Facial Action Modeling

categories.value: AI for Population Health, Public Health & Epidemiology

motivation: Facial palsy is an early, visible stroke indicator that could support rapid screening when CT, MRI, or neurological expertise is unavailable. Single-frame methods miss movement dynamics, while existing video methods often rely on privacy-sensitive raw facial appearance and non-public data. A reproducible approach must capture temporal asymmetry while reducing dependence on identifiable appearance information.
method: DP-Face is a video-based deep learning framework that replaces raw RGB appearance with privacy-preserving structural cues from facial landmarks and wrinkle patterns. It models temporal muscle dynamics through facial Action Units and combines these representations for palsy recognition. The work also introduces Palsy-330, a publicly available 330-subject video dataset, and evaluates the framework with patient-independent splitting.

title: Proactive Domain Unification for Robust Echocardiography Segmentation
motivation: Left-ventricle segmentation is needed for automated cardiac function assessment, yet echocardiography varies substantially across centers and vendors because of acquisition settings, speckle statistics, and proprietary processing. Passive domain generalization may fail when target appearance is far from the source, while unconstrained generative translation can hallucinate boundaries or distort anatomy. The challenge is to proactively normalize appearance while preserving clinically important structure.
method: PDU is an inference-time preprocessor that maps heterogeneous echocardiography images into a fixed, source-aligned appearance domain without target labels or test-time model updates. A boundary-conditioned generative unifier, guided by LV cues from an HED model, normalizes vendor-specific appearance while constraining geometric drift. Reliability-guided frequency fusion preserves low-frequency anatomy from the raw image and injects unified high-frequency style residuals with adaptive strength, making the module plug-and-play for different segmenters.

title: Probabilistic Multi-rater Segmentation via Style-Aware Boundary Conditioning
motivation: Multi-rater segmentation contains meaningful differences in how experts delineate ambiguous boundaries, so consensus labels can discard clinically relevant uncertainty and personalization cues. Existing probabilistic or personalized methods often smooth fine boundary behavior or adapt only through separate heads, limiting sensitivity to local contour shifts. A model is needed that preserves shared anatomy while representing rater-specific boundary preferences and concentrating uncertainty where experts disagree.
method: The framework disentangles a shared content representation from a rater-specific style factor and conditions intermediate encoder features on that style to generate personalized segmentations without duplicating decoders. Style-Conditioned Personalization allows fine-grained boundary preferences to influence decoding while maintaining common anatomical content. A Disagreement-Aware Boundary Loss concentrates supervision within a controllable band around inter-rater divergence and remains stable where raters agree.

title: Probe-EM: Targeted Neuron Tracing via Training-Free Semantic Verification
motivation: Petabyte-scale EM connectomics still suffers from over-segmentation, and completing neuronal morphologies requires manual proofreading measured in person-years. Existing validation methods usually scan globally between discrete segments and depend on large labeled datasets, making them inefficient for tracing specific neurons and difficult to transfer to new volumes. A targeted, training-free tracing and verification workflow is needed to reduce this bottleneck.
method: Probe-EM uses a skeleton-guided Heuristic Spatial Search to grow a neurite from a user-selected seed through an iterative probing and verification cycle, exploiting geometric priors for local-to-global reconstruction. Its Dimension-Aware Semantic Verification module uses NeuroSAM 2 with Planar Ensemble Consensus for intra-slice splits and Axial Spatio-Temporal Propagation for inter-slice splits. The workflow is integrated into Neuroglancer for interactive human-in-the-loop proofreading.

title: Progressive Self-supervised Learning with Individualized Community Assignment for Brain Network Analysis
motivation: Functional brain communities vary across individuals and can reorganize in neurological conditions, but common SSL masking policies are generic and do not explicitly model this heterogeneity. High dimensionality, limited samples, and inter-subject variability further make supervised representations prone to overfitting and weak generalization. Brain network analysis therefore needs self-supervision that respects individualized modular structure and makes reorganization interpretable.
method: BrainPICM models subject-specific ROI-to-community assignments with progressive unbalanced optimal transport, producing soft memberships and ROI confidence scores while allowing outlier regions through a virtual community. These confidences drive curriculum-style masking that gradually introduces low-confidence, potentially pathological ROIs into self-supervised reconstruction. A deviation-aware aggregation module summarizes redistribution relative to a population template and fuses community-level deviations with ROI connectivity features for prediction.

title: ProMoE-FL: Prototype-conditioned Mixture of Experts for Multimodal Federated Learning with Missing Modalities
motivation: Multimodal clinical data are fragmented across institutions, and real-world sites often lack some modalities because of equipment, protocol, or data-management differences. Existing federated methods may require representative public multimodal data, assume stable cross-client relationships, or replace every missing modality with an identical class prototype, losing instance diversity. Missing-modality synthesis must therefore be privacy-preserving, client-aware, and able to capture complementary and heterogeneous information.
method: ProMoE-FL maintains a global client-aware prototype bank that summarizes modality distributions across institutions and conditions a shared Mixture-of-Experts on prototypes and modality indices. Direction-aware routing synthesizes missing-modality features from available modalities while reusing experts across modality combinations, avoiding combinatorial parameter growth. Client-specific prototypes provide latent priors that account for non-IID cross-site variation without requiring external public data.

title: Prompt and Probe: Data-Efficient Adaptation of Black-Box Foundation Models via Unified Active Visual Prompting
motivation: Clinical deployment of foundation models is constrained by expensive expert annotation and by API-served models whose weights, gradients, logits, and internal features are inaccessible. Existing black-box prompt adaptation generally assumes fixed labeled data, while active learning methods often require gradients or calibrated probabilities, and they rarely unify classification and segmentation. A query-only framework is needed that adapts frozen models while selecting informative samples under limited annotation budgets.
method: Prompt and Probe uses a lightweight Visual Prompt Decoder that maps shared image and anatomical embeddings to global additive prompts for classification and spatial channel-concatenated prompts for segmentation. The decoder is trained against a frozen black-box foundation model with SPSA zeroth-order updates using only input-output queries. After training, multi-scale perturbations produce image-level and pixel-level prediction instability scores, which are normalized and fused to rank unlabeled samples for annotation across tasks.

title: Prompt Group-Aware Training for Robust Text-Guided Nuclei Segmentation
motivation: Text-guided segmentation models can produce inconsistent masks for semantically equivalent prompts, which undermines reliable use in pathology and clinical workflows. Existing methods usually assume a one-to-one prompt-to-region mapping and treat prompt variation as noise, so supervised training rarely learns structured equivalence among valid descriptions. Robust nuclei segmentation requires prompt-invariant behavior without changing the inference interface.
method: The framework groups semantically related prompts that share an image mask and trains the segmentation model to behave consistently within each group. A quality-guided group regularization uses segmentation loss as an implicit ranking signal for relative prompt reliability. A stop-gradient logit-level consistency loss aligns predictions across prompts without architectural changes or additional supervision, while inference remains unchanged.

title: PromptGate: Client-Adaptive Vision–Language Gating for Open-Set Federated Active Learning
motivation: Medical image pools in hospitals are open-set and contain artifacts, background tissue, and unrelated pathologies alongside target classes, so standard active learning can waste annotation budgets on OOD samples. Existing open-set methods are mostly centralized or use fixed global notions of OOD, while federated sites have heterogeneous scanners and protocols and cannot share raw data. An adaptive federated gate is needed to purify candidate pools before any acquisition strategy operates.
method: PromptGate adapts a frozen BiomedCLIP with class-specific learnable prompts split into globally shared and locally personalized tokens, aggregated across clients with FedAvg. The prompted VLM classifies each unlabeled image as an in-distribution target class or non-target category, and only predicted ID images enter the downstream acquisition strategy. Oracle labels from queried samples update both prompt components over rounds, progressively refining the client-adaptive ID/OOD gate while remaining strategy-agnostic.

title: PromptMedCT: A Training-Free LLM-Guided Framework for Volumetric CT Data Realization with Quantifiable Disease Manifestations and Multi-Tier Annotations
motivation: Radiology foundation models need clinically structured image-text data, including descriptions, lesion masks, and bounding boxes, to learn grounded diagnostic and temporal reasoning. Such annotations are expensive and privacy-constrained to collect, while existing generators either require large supervised training or omit multi-tier annotations. A controllable, scalable method for realizing lung CT data with these annotations is therefore needed.
method: PromptMedCT is a training-free, LLM-guided diffusion framework that couples clinical semantic prompts with anatomical constraints for lung CT synthesis. It supports a prompt mode for high-fidelity, domain-specific generation and a parametric mode for scalable control of disease characteristics. The parametric mode produces CT scans together with descriptive prompts, infection/lobar masks, and bounding boxes, providing structured multi-tier supervision.

title: Propagating Structural Guidance: Synthesizing Fluorescein Angiography from Fundus Images and Sparse OCT Scans
motivation: FFA reveals vascular perfusion, leakage, and microcirculation but requires invasive dye injection, whereas CFP is non-invasive and widely available. CFP-only synthesis is limited because surface appearance lacks depth-resolved tissue properties and functional vascular information, which can lead to implausible fluorescence patterns. Additional structural guidance is needed to make synthesized FFA more anatomically grounded and clinically useful.
method: The framework builds a tri-modal dataset of paired CFP, FFA, and OCT eyes and uses OCT as complementary structural guidance for FFA synthesis. Its Spatially Aligned Cross-Modal Fusion module projects depth-resolved OCT features onto the fundus plane and injects them into the CFP encoder through adaptive layer normalization. Token-wise Cross-Modality Alignment further applies token-level contrastive learning to align CFP and FFA representations at corresponding spatial positions.

title: ProSMA-UNet: Decoder Conditioning for Proximal-Sparse Skip Feature Selection
motivation: U-Net skip connections preserve spatial detail but also pass low-level textures, background clutter, and acquisition noise directly to the decoder, especially harming low-contrast segmentation. Conventional attention gates mainly apply dense sigmoid reweighting, which attenuates but rarely removes incompatible activations. Explicit, context-aware sparse selection is needed to filter irrelevant skip responses.
method: ProSMA-UNet reformulates skip gating as decoder-conditioned sparse feature selection within a U-Net. It constructs a multi-scale compatibility field with lightweight depthwise dilated convolutions, then applies an ℓ1 proximal operator with learnable per-channel thresholds to perform closed-form soft-thresholding and set irrelevant activations to zero. A decoder-conditioned channel gate driven by global decoder context further suppresses semantically inconsistent channels.

title: ProSyn-Net: A Reliable Prototypical Synergy Network for Imbalanced Dermatologic Multimodal Ultrasound Diagnosis
motivation: Multimodal ultrasound combines morphology from B-mode with hemodynamics from color Doppler, but modality quality can vary greatly and Doppler may be mostly noise. Incidence-driven class imbalance compresses minority lesion manifolds, while deterministic models can be unjustifiably over-confident on ambiguous cases. A diagnostic framework must adaptively filter modalities, model non-convex minority structure, and quantify uncertainty.
method: ProSyn-Net first uses dynamic cross-attention to exchange B-mode and color Doppler information, with sample-adaptive weights that reduce interference from an uninformative modality. It maps the fused feature to distances from learnable lesion prototypes and decodes the distance profile through a nonlinear MLP, trained with focal, compactness, and prototype-separation losses. An uncertainty-aware manifold ensemble combines models across data partitions and supports selective deferral of high-uncertainty cases.

title: Proto-CAP: Prototype Memory Fusion and Curriculum-Adaptive Loss for Pediatric Myopia Visual Question Answering
motivation: Pediatric myopia requires joint interpretation of CFP and OCT, but existing Med-VQA datasets focus on general radiology and lack fine-grained ophthalmic annotations. Limited domain-specific data makes deep models prone to overfitting, while static or costly reweighting losses do not adapt well to changing training difficulty. A dedicated dataset and adaptive prior-guided training method are needed.
method: The authors introduce PM-VQA, an expert-verified multimodal dataset for pediatric myopia containing CFP and OCT images with question-answer pairs. Proto-CAP uses Question-Guided Prototype Fusion, where a learnable memory bank supplies medical concepts to visual representations according to the question. Its Curriculum-Adaptive Poly-2 Loss changes training difficulty dynamically to balance gradient boosting and hard-example mining on small data.

title: Protocol-Manifold Coverage Learning (PMCL): Source-Free Active Adaptation for Multi-Center Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma MRI Segmentation
motivation: Accurate primary GTV delineation on CE-T1 MRI is essential for NPC radiotherapy, but scanner and acquisition protocol mixtures cause cross-center domain shifts and boundary drift that may be hidden by stable Dice scores. Existing source-free active adaptation methods emphasize representativeness or uncertainty without explicitly covering under-sampled protocols or measuring protocol-induced boundary instability. Boundary-focused, coverage-constrained querying is therefore needed.
method: PMCL performs source-free active adaptation by representing each target volume with a compact protocol signature. It applies protocol-aware perturbations to measure boundary-band Protocol Disagreement, then selects queries under a Group Prior Coverage constraint so that a limited annotation budget spans protocol modes. The procedure requires neither source data nor pseudo-labels.

title: PROTON: Prototype-Based Test-Time Online OOD Detection for Medical VLMs
motivation: Medical VLMs can classify images zero-shot but may silently accept OOD inputs at deployment. Static softmax-based scores work inconsistently across far, semantic, and covariate shifts because covariate-shifted samples can look similar in softmax space while occupying different embedding regions. A training-free detector must exploit this geometric signal and adapt its scoring to the incoming stream.
method: PROTON is a post-hoc module on a frozen medical VLM that maintains per-class prototype queues from high-confidence test predictions. It computes cosine distance to the nearest online prototype and adaptively fuses this score with the VLM’s Maximum Concept Matching score using running variance estimated by Welford’s algorithm. A confidence gate limits contamination of the prototype bank, requiring no model modification, training data, or prompt engineering.

title: ProtoReg: Prototype Guidance and Dual-Level Uncertainty-Weighted Consistency for Semi-supervised Pulmonary Perfusion Regression
motivation: Pulmonary perfusion maps are useful for regional lung-function assessment, but paired CT-perfusion acquisitions are costly and scarce. In semi-supervised dense regression, continuous pseudo-labels lack direct confidence estimates, so consistency training can reinforce teacher errors and fragmented spatial noise. A method is needed to estimate reliability and regulate consistency at both voxel and regional levels.
method: ProtoReg uses an EMA teacher to produce continuous pseudo-targets from weakly perturbed CT and trains a student with strong-consistency objectives. A learnable functional prototype bank converts prototype-induced entropy into reliability estimates for continuous regression targets. Dual-level Uncertainty-weighted Consistency Loss applies these weights at voxel and lung sub-unit levels, while external unlabeled CT volumes expand the available training data.

title: Prototype Instance-Semantic Disentanglement with Low-Rank Regularized Subspace Clustering for WSIs Explainable Recognition
motivation: In WSIs, tumor patches are sparse and precancerous tissue can closely resemble tumor tissue, creating both instance-level and semantic entanglement in MIL. Redundant non-tumor instances can dominate aggregation, while ambiguous tumor semantics make instance explanations unreliable. A framework must isolate informative subspaces and establish clearer prototype-based semantic boundaries.
method: PID-LRSC uses two-phase coarse-to-fine low-rank regularized subspace clustering to reduce redundancy from non-tumor instances and expose discriminative tumor subspaces. It then applies prototype instance-semantic disentanglement with enhanced contrastive learning to separate tumor from morphologically similar precancerous tissue. The two components are optimized end to end for more interpretable MIL representations and decisions.

title: Prototype Learning for Visual Field Estimation from Fundus Photography in High Myopia
motivation: Standard automated perimetry for high myopia is subjective, time-consuming, and affected by test-retest variability, motivating imaging-based functional estimation. Existing models often regress 52 sensitivities independently, ignoring structured defect patterns, while VF labels are noisy and paired fundus-VF data are limited. A compact structural prior could improve robustness and interpretability under these conditions.
method: ProtoVF first derives a compact set of representative visual-field prototypes from training VF maps through unsupervised decomposition. A model predicts combination coefficients for these prototypes from fundus photography, then reconstructs the complete 52-point sensitivity map. This constrains predictions to plausible VF patterns and provides clinically interpretable prototype components instead of unconstrained pointwise outputs.

title: Prototype Memory-Guided Training-Free Anomaly Classification and Localization in Prenatal Ultrasound

categories.value: AI for Neglected Diseases & Limited-Resource Settings

motivation: Prenatal ultrasound anomaly classification and localization are important for fetal health and pregnancy management, but rare and heterogeneous anomalies are difficult to identify reliably. Existing learning-based and few-shot methods require large same-modality annotated datasets or fine-tuning for new categories, which is impractical when data and clinical resources are limited.
method: The proposed training-free framework uses a DINOv3 vision foundation encoder and only a few bounding-box-annotated reference ultrasound images per class. It builds a memory bank of class-wise global prototypes and anomaly-related fine-grained prototypes, uses prototype-driven soft merging to aggregate discriminative anomaly features for localization, and applies class-aware prototype consistency to refine predictions.

title: Prototype-based Physiological Transfer Enables NCCT-only Hyperacute Stroke Tissue-Window Segmentation Under Missing Perfusion

categories.value: AI for Neglected Diseases & Limited-Resource Settings

motivation: Accurate ischemic-core and penumbra delineation is needed for tissue-window-based reperfusion decisions in acute ischemic stroke. CTP provides the necessary hemodynamic information but is often unavailable, while NCCT is widely accessible yet contains only subtle static appearance cues. Direct NCCT models generalize poorly, and reconstructing CTP from NCCT is an underdetermined process that can hallucinate hemodynamics.
method: ProPhyT transfers physiological semantics from CTP rather than attempting to synthesize missing perfusion maps. A self-supervised CTP encoder defines a hemodynamic embedding space whose clustered features form a prototype bank; an NCCT encoder is aligned to this space to retrieve relevant prototypes from NCCT alone. Similarity-weighted retrieved prototypes are converted into spatially varying dense prompts that parameter-efficiently condition a medical foundation segmentation model for core and penumbra delineation.

title: Prototype-Driven Robust Domain Generalization in Corneal Endothelial Cell Segmentation
motivation: CEC morphology quantification supports diagnosis and management of corneal disease, but manual or semi-automated analysis is laborious and subjective. Deep segmentation models trained on small, homogeneous datasets often overfit to domain-specific biases and fail on unseen centers, devices, diseases, or species. Robust extraction of anatomical cellular features is therefore needed for clinically reliable deployment.
method: ProtoCEC learns prototype-based representations intended to separate invariant CEC morphology from domain-specific artifacts. Its prototype collector performs difficulty-aware mining from correct, under-segmented, and over-segmented regions to build cell and error prototype pools. A contrastive prototype enhancer improves prototype discrimination, while a prototype allocator dynamically matches and bidirectionally rectifies input features during mask generation.

title: Proxy-CAC: Learning Coronary Calcium Segmentation from Volume-Level Scores
motivation: CAC and its Agatston score are important for cardiovascular risk assessment, but obtaining CAC segmentations requires lesion-level analysis of cardiac CT. Real-world clinical databases commonly retain the final volume-level score without voxel-wise masks, leaving substantial data unusable for conventional segmentation training. Direct score regression lacks the interpretable lesion maps clinicians need.
method: Proxy-CAC is an end-to-end 3D U-Net that predicts voxel-wise CAC probability maps while being trained primarily from volume-level Agatston scores. It incorporates a differentiable Agatston Scoring layer that replaces the metric's non-differentiable operations with smooth sigmoid-based relaxations. Training first initializes the network on a small expert-mask dataset, then uses a larger score-labeled CT dataset with hybrid anatomical and score-based supervision.

title: PseudoRET: A General Retinal Segmentation Framework with Multi-target Pseudo Embeddings
motivation: Retinal structure and lesion segmentation supports diagnosis, monitoring, and risk assessment, but fundus datasets are fragmented by target and annotation protocol. Directly combining these datasets creates missing-label bias, while diffuse, small, or numerous targets also make manual SAM prompting impractical. A unified multi-target approach must exploit disjoint annotations while preventing pseudo-label errors from accumulating.
method: PseudoRET trains a single SAM-style retinal segmentation model with a task-agnostic semi-supervised scheme for disjoint vessel, lesion, and optic disc/cup annotations. A pseudo embedding memory stores and propagates pseudo supervision across tasks for the same image alongside available ground truth. Its confidence-aware pseudo loss dynamically weights stored pseudo labels using spatial reliability and prediction stability, reducing the impact of noisy labels.

title: PSP: Harnessing Position and Shape Priors for Cross-Domain Few-Shot Medical Image Segmentation
motivation: Few-shot medical image segmentation reduces annotation requirements, but suffers a major performance collapse when support and query images come from different modalities such as CT and MRI. Existing cross-domain methods often rely on frequency or local texture alignment, which remains vulnerable to modality-specific appearance changes. Organ position and geometric shape are more stable across modalities and offer useful invariants for robust segmentation.
method: PSP explicitly incorporates cross-modal anatomical position and shape invariants into few-shot segmentation. Position Coordinate Embedding injects relative polar coordinates and uses self-attention to give support and query features spatial awareness; Shape Prototype Modulation combines signed-distance statistics and Fourier shape descriptors to produce shape-aware support prototypes. Hybrid-Prototype Prediction then adaptively calibrates these prototypes to the query feature distribution before cosine-similarity segmentation.

title: Pulmonary Embolism Risk Stratification from CTPA and Medical Records: Vascular Graphs Are Not All You Need

categories.value: Multimodal Integration with Clinical / Genomic / Biomarkers

motivation: PE risk stratification guides decisions such as intensive care, thrombolysis, and anticoagulation, but standard guidelines combine medical records, CTPA assessment, and blood tests that are frequently unavailable at initial diagnosis. CTPA-derived vascular burden may contain relevant information, yet manual assessment of thrombus locations is too time-consuming for routine care. It is therefore unclear whether automated vascular biomarkers or vascular graphs improve routine-data risk stratification beyond simpler clinical predictors.
method: This work benchmarks automatic PE guideline risk stratification from structured medical records and CTPA-derived biomarkers when blood tests are unavailable. It compares tabular models augmented with global vascular biomarkers against GNNs operating on patient-specific pulmonary vascular graphs, including approaches for integrating global clinical features into GNNs. The investigation also analyzes why vascular information may not improve prediction beyond medical records and cardiac biomarkers.

title: QCAgent: An Agentic Framework for Quality-Controllable Pathology Report Generation from Whole Slide Image
motivation: Clinical pathology reports must cover diagnostic context, microscopic morphology, and critical predictors, rather than merely state a slide-level diagnosis. Existing single-pass WSI-to-text methods compress many patches into global representations, which can lose sparse decisive findings and encourage LLMs to hallucinate generic details without slide-specific evidence. Report generation therefore needs user-controllable requirements and a mechanism to revisit localized evidence for verification.
method: QCAgent frames WSI report generation as an iterative audit-retrieve-revise process. It first uses PRISM global features and cluster-sampled patches with Patho-R1 to draft a report, then applies a checklist-guided quality-control module to detect missing or non-compliant details.
