Feedback is converted into morphology-oriented text queries for semantic patch retrieval, and retrieved evidence drives successive revisions until the report meets the specified criteria; only evidence-supported claims are retained.

title: QG-MIL: A Gated Transformer Aggregator for Domain-Agnostic Multiple Instance Learning in Medical Imaging
motivation: Attention-based MIL is useful when only slide- or patient-level labels are available, but its attention can collapse onto a few instances. This concentration produces overconfident, unstable predictions and weakens generalization across cohorts and imaging sources. Existing remedies often require masking, auxiliary losses, pretraining, or multi-stage procedures, motivating an aggregation design that addresses the issue intrinsically across different MIL scales.
method: QG-MIL is a drop-in gated transformer MIL aggregator designed to discourage attention concentration through architecture rather than auxiliary training objectives. It combines RMSNorm pre-normalization, per-head query-key normalization, learnable fine-grained gates on attention outputs, and SwiGLU feed-forward modules, before using gated attention pooling for bag classification. The same aggregator design is applied across whole-slide pathology and cell-level hematology MIL settings.

title: Quality-Guided Semi-supervised Learning for Medical Image Segmentation
motivation: Dense medical-image segmentation labels are expensive to obtain, making SSL important for using unlabeled data. However, SSL commonly trusts all pseudolabels or filters them using model confidence and uncertainty, which are self-referential and may miss systematic segmentation errors. A learned assessment grounded in the compatibility of an image and its predicted mask is needed to guide use of unreliable pseudolabels.
method: The framework trains a dedicated quality predictor on image-mask pairs to estimate segmentation quality independently of the segmentation network's confidence. Its training masks include synthetic corruptions and outputs from partially trained segmenters, so the predictor learns realistic error patterns. Predicted quality is integrated into existing SSL methods through a differentiable quality-aware regularization loss and quality-based reweighting of pseudolabel samples.

title: Quantification of 3D Musculoskeletal CT Image-Based Biomarkers in the Lumbar Spine: Application in Metastatic Prostate Cancer

categories.value: AI for Neglected Diseases & Limited-Resource Settings

motivation: Osteosarcopenia in prostate cancer contributes to frailty, fractures, and mortality, but its progressive bone and muscle deterioration is difficult to monitor at scale. Manual 2D single-slice measurements are impractical longitudinally and are sensitive to slice selection and patient positioning, limiting detection of subtle changes.
method: The study develops an automated pipeline for serial CT that combines deep-learning vertebral detection with 3D segmentation of lumbar vertebral bodies and psoas muscles. It derives vertebral bone density plus psoas volume and density as volumetric biomarkers, enabling longitudinal analysis of musculoskeletal decline and its association with metastatic burden.

title: Quantification of Uncertainty with Adversarial Models in Medical Image Segmentation
motivation: Clinical segmentation requires reliable pixel-level uncertainty, particularly for longitudinal monitoring and decisions at subtle pathological boundaries. Standard segmentation networks can be overconfident, while stochastic uncertainty methods may sample only limited posterior regions and inadequately expose potential failure modes.
method: QUAM-SM is a post-hoc segmentation uncertainty framework that performs targeted adversarial search to find pixels whose predicted class can be readily flipped. These adversarially fragile pixels form a sensitive uncertainty map, and the framework separately characterizes epistemic and aleatoric uncertainty.

title: Quantify, Collect, and Correct: Evidence-Driven Multi-agent Framework for Critical Evidence Refinement in Emergency Rooms
motivation: Emergency-room reasoning must reach decisions under time pressure with incomplete and rapidly changing evidence. Existing multi-agent dialogues often end before obtaining critical cues, and unweighted coverage measures can miss the importance of a small number of decision-critical items.
method: QCC is a closed-loop multi-agent framework with Quantify, Collect, and Correct stages. It uses the Weighted Evidence Convergent Index (WECI) to importance-weight acquired evidence, an Evidence-Driven Planning Module to prioritize missing evidence using current dialogue and retrieval-augmented knowledge, and a verifier to cross-check evidence against diagnosis and revise inconsistent conclusions.

title: Question-Driven Decision Tree via Knowledge Distillation for Interpretable Prediction
motivation: High-stakes medical image recognition needs verifiable decision processes, but black-box deep models are opaque and post-hoc explanations may be unstable or unfaithful. Interpretable-by-design concept models expose reasoning but use flat concepts that poorly reflect conditional clinical reasoning and can sacrifice predictive performance.
method: QDT represents prediction as a hierarchical decision tree of clinically meaningful sequential sub-questions, yielding an auditable question-level path. A high-capacity teacher transfers visual reasoning to the logic-constrained student through knowledge distillation and intermediate-representation alignment, preserving useful feature interactions under the tree constraints.

title: R2P-SAM: Root-to-Prompt Hair Instance Segmentation with Geometric Priors under Point Supervision
motivation: Individual hair-strand segmentation is needed for quantitative trichological assessment, but thin, curved, entangled strands are difficult to separate. Dense labels are costly, bounding boxes are geometrically ambiguous, and naïve root prompts leave SAM without sufficient local or global structural guidance, causing over- or fragmented segmentation.
method: R2P-SAM reformulates hair instance segmentation as root-to-prompt generation while keeping the SAM backbone frozen. A root detector and geometric-prior module infer orientation and centrality fields from sparse root annotations, converting roots into skeleton-aligned prompt trajectories that guide SAM toward continuous, separated strand masks.

title: RACA: Rule-Aligned Collaborative Agents for Evidence-Grounded Breast Ultrasound Classification
motivation: BUS interpretation is complicated by speckle noise and artifacts, while clinical diagnosis depends on BI-RADS-style rule-governed aggregation of imaging descriptors. Most image-to-label classifiers optimize accuracy without anchoring predictions in these rules, and current agent systems are not designed to enforce diagnostic criteria or traceable case-based refinement.
method: RACA organizes BUS classification into three rule-driven stages. Perception agents convert lesion morphology and semantics into structured evidence; a risk-modeling agent applies explicit clinical constraints to estimate malignancy risk and form an initial decision; a critic-guided calibration agent retrieves prior cases to refine conflicts or unstable evidence.

title: RADAR: A Multimodal Benchmark for 3D Image-Based Radiology Report Review

categories.value: Multimodal Integration with Clinical / Genomic / Biomarkers
AI for Neglected Diseases & Limited-Resource Settings

motivation: Radiology-report discrepancies can affect patient safety, especially when preliminary emergency interpretations inform care before final review. Existing discrepancy resources are often text-only or synthetically corrupted and do not test whether a proposed report edit is supported by volumetric imaging in the real preliminary-to-final workflow.
method: RADAR provides a multimodal benchmark built from real preliminary-to-attending abdominal CT report revisions. Given a 3D CT study, preliminary report, and candidate edit, models must assess image support, clinical severity, and whether the edit is a correction, addition, or clarification under standardized evaluation protocols.

title: RadHiera: Semantic Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning for Medical Report Generation
motivation: Radiology reports have a clinical hierarchy: Findings record observations and Impression synthesizes conclusions. Existing report generators often treat reports as flat text or optimize only report-level quality, which can yield missed critical findings, overstated diagnoses, and unsupported or inconsistent impressions.
method: RadHiera uses semantic hierarchical reinforcement learning to optimize report generation at the whole-report, Impression, and Findings-Impression consistency levels. Its reward design combines linguistic and factual report quality, severity-aware weighting of clinically critical Impression errors, and CheXbert-derived label-set constraints with hallucination penalties to keep conclusions supported by findings.

title: RADIANT-PET: Reasoning-Augmented PET/CT Lesion Segmentation with Large Language Models and Reinforcement Learning
motivation: PET/CT lesion segmentation is essential for oncologic tumor-burden assessment, but physiological uptake, inflammation, infection, post-treatment changes, and artifacts can mimic malignancy. Image-only segmenters lack the explicit lesion-level clinical reasoning used by radiologists to distinguish these sources of uptake, causing false positives and unreliable measurements.
method: RADIANT-PET first uses a permissive high-sensitivity segmenter to propose uptake regions and splits them into lesion candidates. It converts each candidate into a structured description of uptake, morphology, and anatomical context, then uses a local LLM, optimized with GRPO reinforcement learning, to reject false positives; radiology reports can be incorporated as additional context.

title: Radiogenomics-Driven Hierarchical Multimodal Stacking for Non-invasive Triage of High-Risk PKD1-Truncating Genotypes in ADPKD

categories.value: Multimodal Integration with Clinical / Genomic / Biomarkers

motivation: ADPKD severity differs substantially by genotype, and PKD1-truncating mutations carry particularly high risk, making early genotype-specific triage clinically important. Yet htTKV and routine MRI show extensive phenotype overlap across PKD1-T and milder genotypes, while prior imaging models largely do not address this difficult intra-PKD1 discrimination problem.
method: The proposed two-stage hierarchical stacking framework extracts handcrafted 3D radiomic features from automatically segmented total kidney volume on T2-weighted MRI. Multiple base classifiers produce out-of-fold probabilistic radiomic representations under nested cross-validation, which a meta-learner fuses with age and htTKV to model nonlinear imaging-clinical interactions without data leakage.

title: RaD-Seg: Region-Aware Disentangled Learning for Plan-Guided Longitudinal Tumor Segmentation in Head-and-Neck Adaptive Radiotherapy

categories.value: AI for Population Health, Public Health & Epidemiology

motivation: Head-and-neck adaptive radiotherapy requires reliable longitudinal segmentation of primary and nodal gross tumor volumes on pre-treatment and mid-treatment scans. Existing methods often separate the time points or enforce global temporal consistency, under-modeling the asymmetric evolution of stable anatomy, regressing GTVp, and subtly changing GTVn, which can cause clinically important contour errors.
method: RaD-Seg uses paired preRT–midRT scans and integrates three modules: Region-Aware Dual-Stream Contrastive Learning separates stable anatomical anchors from response-sensitive target features using region prototypes. Temporal-Difference Response Encoding represents treatment effects as a preRT–midRT residual code that modulates midRT anatomy representations. Plan-Guided Asymmetric Regularization anchors midRT semantics to the preRT plan in stable regions while allowing plausible, target-specific evolution.

title: RadSLDP: Selective Local Differential Privacy for Radiology Vision-Language Models

categories.value: Multimodal Integration with Clinical / Genomic / Biomarkers

motivation: Radiology VLM fine-tuning is often outsourced because hospitals lack the computational infrastructure, requiring sensitive clinical text to leave a trusted environment. Standard differential privacy assumes trusted access to raw data, while uniform local perturbation protects untrusted training at a severe utility cost; privacy protection therefore needs to focus on the non-image-inferable clinical context.
method: RadSLDP defines a policy that identifies non-visual clinical context (NVCC) tokens, combining demographic rules with an expert-validated taxonomy. It clips and perturbs only the embeddings of these sensitive tokens with calibrated Gaussian noise to provide per-token (ε, δ)-local differential privacy, while transmitting image-inferable token embeddings unchanged. The mechanism is model-agnostic and operates before data are sent to an untrusted trainer.

title: RaLMPH: Reliability-Aware Learning for Multi-Pathologist Harmonization in Whole-Slide Image Classification
motivation: Whole-slide image MIL commonly assumes one unambiguous gold label, but clinical slides often receive divergent judgments from pathologists. Existing methods typically assume single-instance data or globally reliable or unreliable annotators, making them poorly suited to gigapixel slides where disagreement can vary across localized diagnostic contexts.
method: RaLMPH builds a reliability field by jointly modeling local neighborhood structure in WSI feature space and annotator uncertainty measured by label entropy. It uses this field to rank pathologists separately for each sample or slide, selecting locally trustworthy opinions rather than assigning global expert reliabilities. An adaptive gating mechanism then fuses the multiple labels according to local reliability before MIL training.

title: RAM-Missing: Retrieval-Augmented Missing-Aware Fusion for Robust Lung Cancer Subtyping

categories.value: Multimodal Integration with Clinical / Genomic / Biomarkers

motivation: Real-world multimodal lung cancer data can have severe structured missingness, with most patients in the described cohort lacking CT scans. Methods that assume complete modalities or use naive imputation can collapse when deployed on incomplete data, motivating fusion that explicitly represents missing modalities and the reliability of their surrogates.
method: RAM-Missing uses a Retrieval-Augmented Proxy Generator to query a historical memory bank and construct proxy embeddings for missing CT modalities. A Retrieval Uncertainty Quantifier estimates retrieval entropy, and an Uncertainty-Guided Conditional Router allocates fusion experts according to the modality mask and uncertainty. This design limits reliance on low-quality proxies while supporting tri-modal lung cancer subtyping under severe missingness.

title: RAPO: Risk-Aware Anatomical Prior Optimization via Reinforcement Learning for CAC Detection in Rheumatoid Arthritis
motivation: Rheumatoid arthritis substantially elevates cardiovascular risk, making coronary artery calcification an important biomarker for early risk stratification and opportunistic screening on routine chest CT. In RA cohorts, calcifications can be minute and low-contrast, while motion and non-gated acquisition artifacts make detection difficult; standard IoU-focused models also do not account for the asymmetric cost of false negatives.
method: RAPO uses a coarse-to-fine reinforcement-learning pipeline that first applies Direct Preference Optimization to establish discrimination and then trains with Risk-aware GRPO. Its rewards include a Chan–Vese anatomical prior that encourages compact CAC geometry and an intrinsic risk penalty derived from uncertainty to discourage false negatives in ambiguous regions. The framework is designed for localization of minute CAC lesions on routine chest CT.

title: RareGCD: Toward Rare Disease Discovery via Generalized Category Discovery
motivation: Generalized Category Discovery must recognize known diseases while discovering unseen categories without exhaustive annotation, but medical datasets are often long-tailed and novel categories may be rare diseases. Existing medical GCD methods are commonly evaluated in balanced settings and use separate objectives for labeled and unlabeled data, leaving rare novel categories with weak supervision and unreliable discovery.
method: RareGCD first uses labeled known-category samples as prototypes to guide associations among labeled and unlabeled instances, with constraints that prevent samples from different known classes from being merged. It then applies prototypical contrastive learning with density-aware, instance-wise temperature scaling to strengthen supervision for reliable samples and temper updates for boundary samples. A parametric classification head is added in a subsequent joint-optimization stage to establish explicit decision boundaries.

title: RASP: Bridging the Long-Tail Gap in Surgical Video Understanding via Retrieval-Augmented Perception
motivation: Unified surgical video understanding must support phase recognition, CVS assessment, and fine-grained action-triplet recognition despite highly long-tailed category distributions. VLMs encode category knowledge parametrically, so frequent classes dominate learning, rare clinically important triplets are underrepresented, and limited examples also make visual-text alignment fragile.
method: RASP stores visual-semantic training entries in an external memory bank to provide non-parametric category priors. Its Contextual Representation and Semantic Retrieval module compresses temporal windows, retrieves coarse semantic priors, and gates them with current-frame features. The Multi-Context Feature Representation module performs evidence-aware cross-attention for fine-grained prior selection and uses an evidence gate to fall back to local features when retrieval is uninformative.

title: RatSeizure: A Benchmark and Saliency-Context Transformer for Rat Seizure Localization
motivation: Rat models are important for studying epileptogenesis and treatment response, but automated seizure-behavior research lacks a public benchmark with dense temporal annotations and standardized evaluation. Existing animal datasets emphasize generic behaviors or coarse labels, while pathology-specific resources are often inaccessible or insufficiently granular for precise seizure-event localization.
method: RatSeizure introduces long-form recordings segmented into 10-second clips with dense seizure-related action-unit labels and precise temporal boundaries, together with standardized splits and evaluation protocols. It also proposes RaSeformer, a saliency-context Transformer for temporal action localization that emphasizes behavior-relevant temporal context while suppressing redundant cues. The benchmark supports both behavior classification and temporal localization.

title: RDE-Seg: Role-Disentangled Experts with Residual Routing and Anatomy Constraints for DSA Guidewire Segmentation
motivation: Accurate guidewire segmentation is essential for navigation in fluoroscopy-guided interventions, yet DSA images contain class imbalance, motion blur, and low signal-to-noise ratios. Existing methods generally segment guidewires independently and overlook their strong dependence on vascular anatomy, so pixel accuracy alone can produce structurally implausible or discontinuous outputs.
method: RDE-Seg adapts SAM with LoRA-based domain specialization, role-disentangled experts for anatomical and instrumental structures, and conservative residual routing in the decoder. It jointly predicts vessels and guidewires so vessel masks can constrain guidewire outputs. A lightweight anatomy-constrained refinement projects predictions into a vessel tolerance band and repairs small discontinuities with morphology-aware operations.

title: Really Need Recursion? Revisiting One-Pass Registration with Multi-Level Multi-Space Contextual Guidance
motivation: Deformable registration methods often use recursion to refine alignment, but repeated passes increase computational cost and slow inference. One-pass pyramid methods are faster yet can lack contextual cues describing the remaining distance to the target alignment, leaving unclear whether recursion is genuinely necessary for high-performance registration.
method: M2CG is a one-pass progressive pyramid registration network that supplies each step with contextual guidance from previous, current, and subsequent levels. It gathers cues in four spaces: image, image-feature, segmentation, and segmentation-feature space, allowing the network to characterize the remaining alignment distance without repeated passes. The framework supports both unsupervised registration and semi-supervised training when segmentation labels are available for part of the data.

title: Real-Time 6D Ultrasound Probe Pose Tracking in Freehand Scanning
motivation: Ultrasound image quality and systems for training, skill assessment, and probe guidance depend on accurate 6D probe pose estimation during freehand scanning. Existing electromagnetic, optical, or inertial trackers add cost and hardware complexity, while markerless methods can become unstable under hand occlusion and dynamic motion. A robust trackerless approach is therefore needed for realistic unconstrained scanning.
method: UPTrack uses a single RGB-D camera and a two-stage pipeline that first detects probe keypoints and then performs keypoint-guided 6D pose estimation. A pose-estimation foundation model supports tracking, while an automated self-training strategy reduces manual annotation for the keypoint detector. The design targets robustness to hand occlusion and rapid probe motion while retaining real-time operation.

title: Real-Time Hardware-Free HIFU Interference Suppression via Teacher-Student Diffusion Framework
motivation: Continuous HIFU sonication interferes with ultrasound imaging, degrading guidance and forcing stop-and-shoot protocols that can prolong treatment and leave periods without monitoring. Existing suppression methods commonly require proprietary raw RF data, hardware synchronization, or costly iterative computation, limiting clinical deployment and real-time use. A hardware-free solution on routine B-mode images is needed for concurrent guidance during therapy.
method: mHC-Diff operates directly on standard B-mode images and uses an mHC-UNet with manifold-constrained Hyper-Connections to increase capacity while separating acoustic artifacts from anatomy. It first trains a multi-step diffusion Teacher to learn an anatomy-aware restoration prior, then distills that prior into a one-step Student for efficient inference. This hardware-free image-domain design avoids proprietary RF access and synchronization requirements.

title: Real-Time Prediction of Impending Severe Fetal Distress Using Deep Learning on Fetal Heart Rate Monitoring
motivation: Severe fetal distress, including Category III fetal heart rate status, can indicate acidemia and requires rapid intervention, but current care generally reacts only after the pattern appears. Events are relatively rare, manual interpretation varies between observers, and existing automated alerts may be late or generate excessive false alarms. Predicting onset several minutes earlier could create a window for preventative action.
method: The study trains a deep learning model on fetal heart rate and uterine contraction signals to predict impending severe fetal distress five minutes before its onset. It is designed for continuous monitoring windows and is developed with multicenter data, internal validation, and independent external validation to assess generalizability. The combined signal formulation provides an actionable early-warning output for clinical decision-making.

title: Reasoning Text-to-Video Retrieval for Operating Room Clips via Action-Driven Digital Twins
motivation: Operating-room video retrieval must locate short clips for safety, training, and quality review, but important queries are often implicit and require reasoning about temporal relations such as the step before an action. Existing global embedding methods do not reason over such queries, and visually similar clips from the same procedure can differ only in actions and state transitions. A representation and retrieval strategy that captures temporal action dynamics is needed.
method: OR3 converts each operating-room clip into an action-driven digital twin composed of concurrent subject-action-object triplets grouped within non-overlapping temporal intervals. An LLM imagines a hypothetical ActDT from the text query, allowing retrieval through intra-modal matching with a single encoder trained using ActDT-specific hard negatives. Evidence-grounded refinement updates the imagined representation using discrepancies with top retrieved candidates and procedure-specific patterns.

title: Reasoning Trace Divergence: An Empirical Signal for Trustworthy Black-Box MLLMs in Histopathology Classification
motivation: MLLMs can produce plausible but ungrounded explanations in medical diagnosis, and black-box access prevents inspection of internal probabilities or representations. Existing uncertainty measures based mainly on label consistency can miss systematic overconfidence, especially when few-shot prompting yields coherent but fabricated reasoning in histopathology classification. A signal that audits the stability of reasoning itself is needed to expose these grounding failures.
method: Reasoning Trace Divergence (RTD) evaluates the stability of an MLLM's generated reasoning under semantic-preserving visual perturbations, using the D4 rotations and reflections of histopathology patches. A secondary LLM maps free-form justifications into structured feature states, allowing divergence of logical paths to be measured separately from final-label consistency. Predictions with high reasoning stability are then used to define a safer operating region for black-box classification.

title: Reconstructing Isotropic 3D Cervical MRI from Anisotropic Clinical Scans via Anatomy-Style Decoupled INRs
motivation: Clinical cervical MRI commonly uses orthogonal anisotropic slices with large gaps, causing through-plane information loss that can obscure lesions and limit 3D diagnosis or downstream CAD. Reconstruction is further complicated by heterogeneous intensities, patient motion, and partially mismatched fields of view between scan orientations. A multi-view super-resolution method without paired isotropic ground truth is needed to produce coherent 3D volumes.
method: The method registers orthogonal cervical MRI scans in a unified coordinate system and reconstructs a continuous volume with a hybrid implicit neural representation. A pre-trained single-view super-resolution module and a shared 3D Residual Dense Network provide anatomical features, while stochastic view dropout trains the model to handle partially missing fields of view. Learnable style embeddings and anatomy codes decouple shared geometry from view-specific intensity, with sparse coordinate supervision guiding reconstruction.

title: Recover Semantics First, Generate Better: Improved Latent Modeling for 3D MRI Reconstruction and Cross-Contrast Synthesis
motivation: Multi-contrast MRI offers complementary diagnostic information, but acquiring all sequences is expensive and motivates 3D cross-contrast synthesis. Latent compression makes volumetric generation feasible, yet existing compressors can lose long-range anatomical coherence and contrast-specific semantics while pixel-wise objectives over-smooth small lesions and boundaries. Better latent representations are needed before generative synthesis can be reliable.
method: The framework introduces a Latent Harmonization Encoder that combines convolutional features with slice-wise ViT context, aligns their statistics, and discretizes the fused representation so long-range anatomy is retained. A Semantic Recovery Block aligns latent embeddings with features from a frozen self-supervised DINO teacher to restore contrast-specific semantic separability. An Anatomy-aware Frequency Loss uses anatomy-semantic attention to preserve diagnostically important high-frequency structures during reconstruction.

title: ReDIVE: A Two-Stage Hybrid Network for Keratitis Diagnosis via Retinex-based Enhancement and Depth-Informed Vertical Embedding
motivation: Infectious keratitis diagnosis with IVCM is often treated as single-frame classification, ignoring the corneal depth distribution that distinguishes pathogens and can cause misdiagnosis. Sequential approaches may use continuity without explicitly modeling anatomical depth, while low signal-to-noise ratio and non-uniform illumination further degrade images. A sequence-level method that combines image enhancement with depth-aware modeling is needed.
method: ReDIVE first applies a customized differentiable multi-scale Retinex module that estimates illumination and adaptively enhances degraded IVCM frames. A ConvNeXt encoder extracts frame-level visual features, which are combined with sinusoidal absolute-depth and relative-depth embeddings. A ViT decoder then models inter-frame correlations over the resulting sequence tokens for pathogen classification.

title: Reducing Expert Annotation Effort for CTA Vessel Delineation with Synthetic Pretraining
motivation: CTA vessel analysis requires accurate delineation of both the lumen and outer vessel wall, but routine contouring is manual, time-consuming, and variable between readers. Fully supervised deep models generally need large private annotated datasets, while heuristic unsupervised methods can depend on brittle assumptions about vessel appearance. A label-efficient strategy is needed to scale reproducible delineation with limited expert correction.
method: The pipeline pre-trains a U-Net on a large collection of automatically generated lumen and vessel-wall contour annotations, without manual labeling. It then fine-tunes the network on a small set of manually corrected contours, using cross-sectional vessel representations and evaluating model-reader disagreement against inter-reader variability. This staged design transfers synthetic supervision while adapting predictions to reader delineations.

title: Reference-Guided Gradient Balancing Loss for Long-Tailed Multi-label Medical Image Classification
motivation: Medical multi-label classification is strongly long-tailed: frequent categories and abundant negative labels can overwhelm gradients from rare diseases. Existing ranking losses may uniformly suppress negative logits without modeling class-specific distributions, leaving hard false positives and poor tail-class decision boundaries. A loss that adaptively balances negative and positive gradients is needed for reliable recognition of low-prevalence conditions.
method: RGB combines an adaptive negative suppression loss with a positive enhancement loss for long-tailed multi-label classification. When true and false predictions coexist in a batch, correct predictions provide class-specific references for correcting hard false-positive logits; otherwise, negative gradients are reduced according to prediction confidence. The positive term weights samples by difficulty and class frequency to strengthen learning for rare diseases and improve class-wise logit separation.

title: Refining 3D Medical Segmentation with Verbal Instruction
motivation: Accurate 3D anatomical segmentation supports diagnosis, measurement, and intervention planning, but predictions often contain shape errors caused by domain variation, limited or imbalanced data, and inaccurate annotations. Radiologists can recognize and verbalize these discrepancies, yet medical datasets pairing erroneous shapes with corrective language are unavailable, preventing language-driven refinement. A benchmark and model are therefore needed to connect clinician instructions with geometric corrections.
method: The authors introduce CoWTalk, a benchmark of arterial 3D shapes with controllable morphological errors paired with corrective instructions. Their iterative refinement model encodes shapes as vector sets, fuses them with text features, and decodes updated shapes progressively according to clinician instructions. This provides an end-to-end vision-language mechanism for human-in-the-loop multi-class vascular segmentation refinement.

title: Reformulating Chest X-Ray Report Generation as Fine-Grained Visual Question Answering with Structured Clinical Report Templates
motivation: Automated chest X-ray reporting could reduce radiologists’ workload, but manual interpretation is labor-intensive and existing VLMs are commonly trained with concise holistic reports. Such reports omit many observations and encourage linguistic priors, leading to incomplete understanding and factual hallucinations. A structured, fine-grained supervision strategy is needed to reflect radiologists’ stepwise examination of anatomy and improve clinical reliability.
method: TGST builds a radiology textbook-aligned tree template whose nodes decompose pulmonary findings into anatomical entities, lesions, and actionable attributes. A two-stage pipeline maps free-text reports to this structure and uses a medical VLM to fill missing observations, producing dense, semantically targeted supervision. The VLM is then trained as a sequence of localized clinical VQA tasks rather than solely on holistic report text, encouraging precise image-text alignment.

title: RefTr: Recurrent Refinement of Confluent Trajectories for 3D Tubular Tree Centerlines
motivation: Centerline graphs of vessels and airways are important for diagnosis, planning, navigation, and morphometry, and missing small branches can create clinical risk. Segmentation-based approaches require costly voxel labels, graph predictors may violate tree topology, and sequential trackers have low recall and cannot repair early mistakes. A compact end-to-end method is needed that can refine complete branches, preserve valid topology, and retain high recall.
method: RefTr is a Transformer-based 3D image-to-graph model with a Producer that predicts candidate trajectories and a shared Refiner that recurrently aligns them to target branches. It uses a discrete confluent trajectory representation in which branches share prefixes and split at divergence points, allowing whole-branch refinement while preserving topology. Many-to-one matching increases recall, while patch-level duplicate suppression and Tree Non-Maximum Suppression merge redundant branches; radius-aware metrics provide more robust evaluation.

title: Reliability-Aware Cross-Prompt Aggregation for Propagation-Based Segmentation of Arbitrary 3D Medical Objects
motivation: Volumetric segmentation must maintain spatial and semantic consistency despite inter-slice appearance changes, diverse anatomies, modalities, and disease patterns, while 3D annotations are scarce. Propagation-based SAM methods offer annotation-efficient 3D prediction but accumulate early errors and typically refresh prompts with fixed distance heuristics that ignore anatomical variability and local reliability. An adaptive strategy is needed to combine stable global guidance with changing local cues.
method: The framework propagates segmentation from two complementary prompts at every slice: the initial prompted slice for stable global semantics and the dynamically propagated front slice for local appearance. It estimates prompt reliability without labels using cycle consistency and cross-prompt agreement, then combines predictions with spatial-distance and reliability-aware weights. This training-free fusion replaces rigid refresh intervals and down-weights unreliable guidance to limit error accumulation.

title: ReLiF-3D: Prior-Guided Semi-supervised 3D MRI Segmentation via Robust Bias-Consistent Paired Views

categories.value: AI for Neglected Diseases & Limited-Resource Settings

motivation: Dense 3D MRI annotation is expensive, motivating semi-supervised learning, but noisy pseudo-labels and drifting teacher targets can amplify errors when only a few labeled volumes are available. Scanner-dependent MRI bias fields create intensity shifts that distort lesion appearance and cause further distribution-shift failures, especially for small or low-contrast lesions. A robust framework should retain stable anatomical priors while learning consistency under realistic bias variation and uncertain predictions.
method: ReLiF-3D trains a lightweight 3D U-Net under a frozen SAM-Med3D prior, avoiding EMA teacher drift while retaining spatial and lesion-aware guidance. Its Smooth Orthogonal Bias Field generator creates paired clean and scanner-shifted MRI views using orthogonal smooth multiplicative and additive fields with a progressive schedule. Confidence-Gated Co-Regularization enforces voxel consistency only for reliable agreements, while Lesion-Aware Representation Consistency aligns lesion-focused embeddings and foundation-model semantics.

title: ReMeDI: Refined Memory for Disambiguation of Identities with SAM3 in Surgical Segmentation
motivation: Surgical instrument segmentation supports tracking and intraoperative guidance, but occlusions, rapid motion, re-entry, and viewpoint changes make long-term temporal consistency and identity preservation difficult. SAM3’s reliability-agnostic FIFO memory can write poor predictions, while stricter filtering may discard low-visibility frames needed for identity recovery; its fixed temporal encoding also limits long-horizon memory. The task needs selective memory, scalable temporal context, and explicit post-occlusion identity verification.
method: ReMeDI-SAM3 partitions memory into a relevance-aware bank that stores high-reliability frames and an occlusion-aware bank populated with identity-critical pre-occlusion frames from an unconditional buffer. Piecewise interpolation of temporal positional encodings expands effective memory capacity for long procedures without retraining. A multi-scale feature-based re-identification module with temporal voting verifies or corrects identities when instruments reappear after occlusion.

title: Remixing Embeddings for Patient Augmentation in Data Scarce Multiple Instance Learning
motivation: Medical MIL relies on bag-level labels while instance annotations are impractical, and its performance is constrained by scarce patients in rare diseases or expensive modalities. Standard augmentation changes individual instances but does not create realistic patient-level bags, and many bag-mixing methods require examples from every class. A patient-level augmentation method should generate plausible bags from pooled representations and remain usable when a class is missing or only a few patients exist.
method: RECIPE pools instance embeddings from patients and fits Gaussian mixture models to discover unsupervised clusters. Disease-level distributions over these clusters act as patient “recipes”; new bags are generated offline by sampling instances according to the relevant recipe, even when a target class is absent from the current dataset. Generated patients are selected with uncertainty quantification before being used to augment MIL training.

title: ReMiX-Seg: Latent Modality Completion Meets Expert Routing for Robust Glioma Segmentation
motivation: Glioma segmentation benefits from complementary FLAIR, T1, T1c, and T2 MRI, but clinical acquisitions often contain arbitrary missing modalities and span pre- and post-treatment distributions. Specialist models scale poorly, fusion-only methods cannot restore absent cues, and reconstruction methods may suffer representation mismatch and error propagation. A practical model should complete missing information in a compact latent space and adapt fusion to each available subset across domain shifts.
method: ReMiX-Seg uses a single network combining lightweight latent completion with subset-adaptive expert routing. A modality-specific encoder and Shift-Gated Token Refiner stabilize tokens, while a Context-Gated Imputer reconstructs missing modalities directly in task-driven latent space. Serialized Mamba Mixture-of-Experts Fusion performs mask-aware multi-scale fusion for each observed subset, and Expert-wise Consistency Alignment reduces distribution gaps between reconstructed and observed features.

title: RePCM: Region-Specific and Phenotype-Adaptive Bi-ventricular Cardiac Motion Synthesis
motivation: Cardiac motion across the cycle is needed for regional functional assessment, but densely sampled mesh sequences are difficult to obtain and disease populations exhibit strongly different regional dynamics. Global generative models can oversmooth these differences, while existing representations may lack explicit vertex correspondence or fine-grained regional controls. A method is needed to infer a coherent full-cycle bi-ventricular sequence from one end-diastolic mesh while preserving regional and disease-specific motion.
method: RePCM first learns vertex-wise motion descriptors from mesh sequences and clusters them into a data-driven functional partition. In a conditional VAE, its Region-Specific Injection Module performs masked, synchronized exchange within regions to preserve localized dynamics and limit inappropriate cross-region mixing. A phenotype-adaptive mixture-of-experts prior conditioned on the end-diastolic shape models disease-dependent latent motion trends while exploiting the coupling between anatomy and motion.

title: ReportX: The BraTS Clinical Report Dataset

categories.value: Multimodal Integration with Clinical / Genomic / Biomarkers

motivation: BraTS provides multiparametric MRI and tumor masks but lacks the richer clinical semantics found in radiology reports, such as enhancement, ventricular involvement, and midline shift. Existing BraTS report resources are limited, synthetic, automatically generated, or coarse, leaving incomplete supervision for 3D vision-language learning. A clinician-curated, structured report dataset is needed both to capture clinically relevant findings and to test whether report semantics can improve volumetric segmentation.
method: ReportX pairs 257 BraTS-GLI-2023 subjects with clinician-written qualitative reports and atlas- and mask-derived quantitative descriptors. The reports are evaluated for ontology coverage, template adherence, and inter-clinician consistency, providing structured semantic supervision beyond voxel masks. For segmentation, biomedical language models encode the reports, and a 3D U-Net uses these embeddings as auxiliary training-time vision-text guidance while inference remains image-only.

title: Representation Learning with Distance-Residualized Functional Connectivity for Cortical Parcellation from rs-fMRI
motivation: Functional parcellation from rs-fMRI is needed to define meaningful cortical units for brain-network and brain-behavior analyses while reducing data dimensionality. Existing methods largely depend on predefined similarities and linear compression, which cannot adequately model high-dimensional, nonlinear connectivity or disentangle it from spatial proximity. A self-supervised whole-cortex representation-learning approach is therefore needed for robust group-level parcellation.
method: The framework first residualizes vertex-wise functional connectivity against geodesic distance, then uses a variational autoencoder to learn compact, uncertainty-aware nonlinear representations. A neighborhood contrastive objective promotes local functional coherence, while Laplacian positional encoding reintroduces controlled spatial continuity before clustering into group-level cortical parcels.

title: ReScan-IA: A Spatially-Adaptive Diffusion Framework for Controllable 3D Intracranial Aneurysm Inpainting
motivation: Intracranial aneurysms vary widely in size, morphology, and location, while annotated CTA data are limited, imbalanced, and affected by center-specific shifts. Conventional augmentation cannot create new morphologies, 2D GAN synthesis lacks precise spatial control, and existing 3D diffusion inpainting may violate vascular anatomy. A controllable, anatomically consistent 3D synthesis method is needed to improve downstream detection and segmentation training.
method: ReScan-IA formulates aneurysm insertion as a virtual re-scan and uses a spatially adaptive 3D diffusion model to control placement and morphology. Dual conditioning combines a binary vessel prior for vascular continuity with Circle of Willis labels that select anatomically corresponding territories, insertion sites, and templates. Decoder-level spatial modulation provides explicit spatial control while preserving surrounding anatomy for synthetic augmentation.

title: Research Design Considerations for Empirical User Studies in MICCAI
motivation: Technical accuracy alone cannot establish that medical imaging and computer-assisted intervention technologies will work safely and effectively in clinical workflows. Conventional evaluations often omit how representative users interact with systems, despite those interactions affecting decisions, behavior, and outcomes. Standardized, rigorous empirical user studies are needed to provide reproducible evidence of human impact and support translation from technical development to bedside use.
method: The paper provides practical guidance for formulating, planning, and executing controlled empirical user studies in MIC and computer-assisted intervention. It emphasizes specifying hypotheses and outcomes, managing confounding factors and the trade-off between internal validity and ecological realism, and selecting an appropriate system fidelity from mock-ups to fully functioning systems. The framework also considers implementation, intervention validation, and evidence needed to assess human impact and clinical relevance.

title: Residual Diffusion Bridge in Wavelet Space for Medical Image Translation
motivation: Missing MRI contrasts hinder tumor management, registration, and downstream analysis, while acquiring all sequences increases scan time and motion risk; MRI-to-CT synthesis is also useful for MRI-only radiotherapy planning. Adversarial methods can be unstable and hallucinate structures, and pixel-space diffusion bridges entangle global contrast transport with local texture generation. Frequency-specific, paired translation with inspectable structure and texture controls is therefore needed.
method: Wavelet Residual Bridge (WRB) decomposes paired images with a three-level dual-tree complex wavelet transform. It deterministically maps low-pass coefficients for structure alignment and samples modality-specific high-frequency residuals through Gaussian diffusion bridges in compact texture subspaces. A Dirichlet constraint preserves non-texture source regions, while gradient-isolated, stage-wise training keeps structure mapping, residual synthesis, and image refinement separately interpretable.

title: Residual-Aware Structured Pruning with Dual-Stream Alignment for Adapter-Tuned SAM
motivation: Adapter-tuned SAM models offer strong medical segmentation but remain too computationally heavy for real-time clinical deployment, with adapters sometimes adding substantial overhead. Uniform compression overlooks that backbone pruning damages performance much more than adapter pruning because shared backbone representations are fragile while adapters are more redundant. An adapter-aware, residual-safe pruning and recovery strategy is needed to reduce compute without sacrificing segmentation quality.
method: RASP-SAM defines dependency-safe structured pruning units across attention, FFN, adapters, and residual couplings, treating the frozen backbone and trainable adapters asymmetrically. Orthogonal Residual Scoring ranks units using downstream gradient components that remain non-substitutable relative to merged pretraining and downstream subspaces, with cross-fitting. Dual-Stream Compensation then distills adapter and backbone information in two stages to recover accuracy from a small calibration set.

title: Resolution-Conditioned Representation Learning for Unified Brain MRI Modeling
motivation: Brain MRI protocols differ substantially in slice thickness, and fast thick-slice scans are common clinically but contain less through-plane detail. Models trained mostly on thin-slice data therefore face resolution-induced distribution shifts and often degrade on real clinical scans, while task-specific models do not provide a unified solution. A representation that explicitly conditions on resolution and acquisition context is needed for robust segmentation and diagnosis across settings.
method: The framework pretrains a shared brain-MRI encoder with self-supervised reconstruction on scans spanning many cohorts and slice thicknesses. It then aligns the image representation with acquisition parameters and demographic metadata to create a resolution-aware, acquisition-informed embedding. The resulting backbone supports both fine-grained tissue segmentation and mental-disorder diagnosis across heterogeneous resolutions.

title: Response-Aware Multimodal Learning for Post-treatment Visual Acuity Forecasting

categories.value: Multimodal Integration with Clinical / Genomic / Biomarkers

motivation: Long-term visual-acuity forecasting after anti-VEGF treatment is important for counseling and follow-up, but early data provide only limited and noisy information about heterogeneous response trajectories. Prior methods often predict a single endpoint or short-term response and compress OCT into global descriptors, missing localized microstructural cues that constrain vision. A multi-horizon model that explicitly captures early treatment response from paired visits is needed.
method: ReVA adapts a foundation-pretrained OCT transformer with LoRA and applies multi-head spatial attention to retain localized prognostic patch patterns. A dependency-aware tabular encoder represents OCT biomarkers and clinical variables, and cross-attention fuses the two modalities separately for baseline and month-1 visits. Temporal aggregation combines baseline status with early response, and temporal convolutional networks produce visual-acuity predictions at multiple future horizons.

title: Rest2Visual: Predicting Visually Evoked fMRI from Resting-State Scans
motivation: Visually evoked fMRI reveals stimulus-driven neural responses but is costly, requires synchronized protocols and sustained participation, and is difficult to scale. Resting-state fMRI is easier to acquire and contains subject-specific intrinsic organization, yet lacks an explicit stimulus link, while existing models generally do not combine resting priors with stimulus conditioning for individualized voxel-wise synthesis. A resting-conditioned model could reduce dependence on task-based acquisition while preserving stimulus information.
method: Rest2Visual computes a subject-specific intrinsic functional map from resting-state connectivity and combines it with a visual stimulus image. A 3D encoder extracts hierarchical volumetric features from the resting prior, while a conditional decoder injects frozen ResNet-50 stimulus embeddings at the bottleneck and through adaptive group normalization to generate voxel-wise evoked maps. Training uses voxel-wise MSE against trial-level beta volumes, enabling stimulus-aligned synthesis while retaining subject-specific structure.

title: Rethinking RAG: Mitigating Text-Driven Hallucinations via Feature-Level Retrieval Integration in Medical LVLMs

categories.value: Multimodal Integration with Clinical / Genomic / Biomarkers

motivation: Medical LVLMs can generate plausible statements that contradict image evidence, creating diagnostic risk. Text-only RAG may amplify language bias and encourage copying retrieved reports, while CLIP retrieval can treat negated and non-negated but clinically contradictory sentences as similar. Retrieval should therefore improve visual grounding at the feature level and filter inconsistent evidence before fusion.
method: The framework retrieves image-report pairs with a negation-aware strategy that filters clinically contradictory cases. A gated cross-attention module injects retrieved visual-textual features into upper vision-encoder layers of the query, enhancing visual representations rather than appending reports as language prompts. An attention grounding loss regularizes the fusion so it does not collapse onto a few tokens or references, encouraging balanced, clinically faithful evidence use.

title: Rethinking the Adaptation of Vision Foundation Models for Efficient Cell Segmentation
motivation: Cell segmentation is essential for computational pathology but must handle diverse modalities, contrasts, and morphologies, while pixel-level annotations are labor-intensive. Adapting vision foundation models usually fine-tunes heavy encoders or adds auxiliary prompt models, creating high computation and annotation demands. Since pretrained VFMs already encode general saliency, boundaries, and spatial continuity, an efficient method should realign these structural priors without retraining the encoder.
method: EffiCell-Seg keeps the VFM encoder fully frozen and builds a Cell Structure Prompt Encoder from its complementary representations. CLS-to-spatial-token cosine similarity supplies semantic saliency, PCA of spatial tokens supplies morphological features, and their gated fusion forms structural prior maps. A Synergistic Mask Decoder jointly predicts geometric distance fields and semantic maps with mutual cross-guidance to enforce contextual consistency.

title: Retinopathy of Prematurity Staging via Prototype-Evidential Learning
motivation: Accurate staging of retinopathy of prematurity (ROP) is needed for timely intervention, but early stages have subtle, localized signs and highly similar appearances. These overlapping boundaries make rigid classifiers unstable, while deterministic black-box predictions provide little information about whether the available evidence is sufficient. A method is therefore needed that can represent both inter-stage ambiguity and decision reliability in an interpretable way.
method: ProtoEvi-ROP uses two parallel pathways: a prototype branch learns stage-specific geometric references from spatially masked fundus images, while an evidential branch models the sufficiency of visual evidence. Prototype similarity and evidential beliefs are aligned with a coordination consistency loss and fused using reduced Dempster–Shafer fusion. Region-focused regularization stabilizes prototype geometry and limits feature drift.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Anatomical Guidance for Text-to-CT Generation
motivation: Text-to-CT generation offers semantic control from radiology reports, but reports underspecify spatial structure and can yield anatomically ambiguous or inconsistent volumes. Structure-conditioned methods provide stronger anatomical control but require target-volume annotations that are unavailable when the volume must be synthesized. A realistic approach is needed to obtain anatomical guidance without observing or segmenting the target scan.
method: The method retrieves a semantically related clinical case for each radiology report using a pretrained 3D vision-language encoder. The retrieved case’s anatomical annotation is used as a coarse structural proxy and injected through a ControlNet branch into a text-conditioned latent diffusion model. This provides spatial scaffolding while allowing the diffusion model to preserve report-driven semantic variability.

title: Retrieval-Based Mixture-of-Experts for Patient-Specific Cancer Survival Prediction with Incomplete Multimodal Data

categories.value: Multimodal Integration with Clinical / Genomic / Biomarkers

motivation: Cancer survival prediction benefits from complementary WSI and gene-expression information, but clinical workflows often leave one modality missing. Existing imputation and shared-representation methods mainly capture population-level modality information, overlooking patient-specific cross-modal dependencies, and their single prediction pathway cannot adapt to varied missingness patterns. A robust predictor should retrieve individualized complementary evidence and adjust its decision process to its reliability.
method: RMoE performs bidirectional cross-modal retrieval from a multimodal memory bank, using the available WSI or genomic representation to find phenotypically similar patients and aggregate their missing-modality representations. Risk-aware projection heads learn a shared retrieval space aligned with survival risk, while the original modality representations remain available for prediction. A reliability-aware mixture-of-experts router weights unimodal and multimodal experts according to retrieval confidence and modality availability.

title: Retrieval-Guided Semi-supervised Federated Learning for Medical Image Segmentation
motivation: Semi-supervised federated segmentation can use abundant unlabeled client data while preserving privacy, but the labels-for-public setting leaves clients without local annotations. Existing methods compress public samples into global parameters or pseudo-labels, losing the fine-grained semantics that could guide individual unlabeled images and handle client heterogeneity. Sample-level use of public references is needed for more adaptive local segmentation.
method: R2S2Fed retrieves semantically relevant labeled public samples for each unlabeled local image using feature similarity. Their representations condition a dynamic weight generator that produces query-specific segmentation parameters, giving each client sample adaptive guidance. Local training combines consistency learning on augmented unlabeled views with supervised learning on retrieved references, followed by federated aggregation.

title: REVEAL++: Differentiable Phenotypic Grouping for Vision–Language Retinal Modeling of Alzheimer’s Disease Risk

categories.value: Multimodal Integration with Clinical / Genomic / Biomarkers

motivation: The retina and structured clinical risk factors offer scalable, noninvasive signals for early Alzheimer’s disease risk modeling. Existing group-aware vision–language learning uses hard thresholds to assign phenotypic groups, imposing artificial boundaries on biologically continuous and overlapping risk profiles and preventing grouping from adapting during representation learning. A graded, learnable treatment of phenotypic similarity is needed.
method: REVEAL++ replaces hard phenotypic group assignments with continuous weights computed from similarities between retinal-image embeddings and clinical risk-profile embeddings. A soft aggregation operator converts these weights into graded multi-positive relationships, and a soft-target contrastive objective jointly learns cross-modal alignment and phenotypic structure end to end. This preserves the retinal–narrative VLM setting while allowing similarity to vary continuously.

title: Revisiting Integration of Image and Metadata for DICOM Series Classification: Cross-Attention and Dictionary Learning

categories.value: Multimodal Integration with Clinical / Genomic / Biomarkers

motivation: Automated DICOM series classification is needed for reliable analysis and protocol management, but series contain heterogeneous slices and variable lengths, while metadata may be missing, inconsistent, or unreliable. Image-only models struggle with volumetric context and scanner variation, whereas metadata pipelines often require error-prone imputation and separate-stage fusion. An end-to-end model must jointly exploit both sources while respecting metadata sparsity and slice variability.
method: The framework encodes image slices with a flexible 2.5D visual pathway and encodes observed metadata index–value pairs with a sparse missingness-aware dictionary and FiLM-based modulation, without imputing absent fields. A bidirectional cross-modal attention module contextualizes image and metadata embeddings across modalities and slices, followed by learnable pooling into a series representation. Equidistant slice sampling addresses variable series length and image dimensions.

title: Reward-Guided Distillation: A Progressive Pseudo-Bag Purification Framework for WSI Multiple Instance Learning
motivation: Four-class metastasis grading in WSIs must distinguish Normal, ITC, Micro, and Macro disease from weak slide-level labels. Random or indiscriminate pseudo-bag aggregation introduces semantic dilution and label noise, especially when sparse ITC or Micro signals are overwhelmed by irrelevant patches. The task needs a way to rank diagnostically useful instances and remove class-irrelevant pseudo-bags before final aggregation.
method: The framework first ranks WSI patches with a Progressive Shapley-based module and groups them into ordered pseudo-bags, with relabeling to reduce conflicts with slide-level supervision. A Reward-Guided Selection Module uses a generator–rewarder architecture to estimate pseudo-bag quality and produces a mask based on cosine-similarity rewards to discard irrelevant bags. The remaining purified features are aggregated by a second-tier MIL head for metastasis grading.

title: Riemannian Batch Normalization on Correlation Manifolds for EEG Decoding
motivation: Correlation matrices provide scale-invariant EEG representations, but their unit-diagonal constraint defines a geometry different from the general SPD manifold. Existing batch or Lie-group normalization methods do not respect this correlation-manifold structure and can move matrices off the valid space. A geometry-consistent normalization layer is needed to stabilize and accelerate deep EEG decoding.
method: CorBN computes the Fréchet mean of a batch under the Off-Log Metric, centers each correlation matrix by Lie-group translation, and scales centered tangent vectors according to their batch dispersion. A learnable manifold-valued bias then shifts the normalized matrices through group composition, while running geometric statistics support inference. All operations preserve the unit-diagonal correlation manifold and have closed-form expressions.

title: Right Answer, Wrong Evidence: Revealing Visual Confabulation in Multi-Image Medical VLMs with the Evidence Attribution Score
motivation: Medical VLMs can answer multi-image questions correctly while relying on irrelevant images or text shortcuts, a failure that accuracy alone cannot expose. Such visual confabulation is clinically risky because the model may fail when the visual evidence changes, even though its output appears correct. An annotation-free, model-agnostic measure is needed to test whether claimed evidence matches the evidence behaviorally required for the answer.
method: EAS separates behavioral and claimed evidence for a multi-image question. Behavioral Evidence Sets are obtained by leave-one-out image ablation, while Claimed Evidence Sets retain images consistently identified across repeated prompts. EAS is the Jaccard overlap between these sets, assigning zero to correctly answered cases with no observable visual dependence and enabling model-agnostic auditing.

title: R-MSA: Rhythm-Conditioned Surgical Video Skill Assessment via Morphology Synchronization and Uncertainty Calibration
motivation: Automated surgical skill assessment must compare fine-grained action quality across surgeons, but execution rhythm varies substantially: experts are often smooth and efficient whereas novices are slower and irregular. Most temporal models emphasize which actions occur and under-model how morphology unfolds with rhythm, causing distribution shifts across performers and durations. A rhythm-aware method is needed for fair, interpretable assessment with reliable confidence.
method: R-MSA uses a Rhythm Morphology Encoder to condition temporal representations on execution duration and produce rhythm-adaptive features. A morphology-synchronous decoder with learnable queries extracts shared procedural primitives after rhythm normalization, while a Surgical Sequence Alignment Module adds a Gaussian temporal prior to co-attention for localized correspondence. An uncertainty-calibrated interpretable tree performs reparameterized skill-score prediction with calibrated uncertainty.

title: Robotic Ultrasound Makes CBCT Alive
motivation: Intraoperative CBCT provides reliable high-resolution 3D context, but it is a static snapshot and cannot track soft-tissue deformation caused by respiration, probe pressure, or surgical manipulation. Robotic ultrasound offers dynamic soft-tissue information, yet limited acoustic coverage and artifacts make deformation-aware multimodal updating difficult, motivating a real-time integration method.
method: The framework aligns robotic ultrasound with CBCT using calibration initialization and LC2-based rigid refinement, then estimates motion from ultrasound streams with USCorUNet, a lightweight bidirectional correlation network trained with optical-flow-guided supervision. The estimated dense deformation is spatially regularized and transferred to the CBCT reference to update slices in real time without repeated radiation exposure.

title: Robust automatic brain vessel segmentation in 3D CTA scans using dynamic 4D-CTA data
motivation: Brain vessel segmentation datasets for CTA are small and largely limited to major vessels, leaving peripheral arteries and veins underrepresented. Manual annotation is difficult because bone, soft tissue, and variable vascular enhancement obscure vessels, creating a data bottleneck for robust single-phase CTA segmentation.
method: DynaVessel uses dynamic 4D-CTA to select arterial and venous phases, subtract bone and soft tissue, and generate vessel-separated volumes for semi-automatic annotation and expert validation. The resulting multi-phase artery and vein labels are used to train nnUNet on multiple CTA contrasts, enabling robust segmentation from single-phase scans.

title: Robust Colonoscopy Video Polyp Segmentation via Quality-Aware Memory and Prototype Alignment
motivation: Reliable polyp segmentation in colonoscopy videos requires temporal information, but motion blur, reflections, occlusions, and large displacement make individual frames incomplete or unreliable. Existing methods often build cross-frame queries from the degraded current frame and are further affected by appearance drift, causing erroneous retrieval and noise propagation.
method: The query-enhanced cascaded memory framework maintains a compact sensory memory of quality-filtered foreground and background states, gating updates by observation reliability and state consistency. It fuses this memory with current features to form stable queries that retrieve long-term appearance prototypes, while Prototype Alignment anchors appearance and limits drift during cross-frame association.

title: Robust Mitigation of Age-Dependent Confounding Effects via Sample-Difficulty Decorrelation

categories.value: AI for Population Health, Public Health & Epidemiology

motivation: Age can confound medical image classification by linking imaging morphology with disease prevalence, producing age-dependent false- and true-positive disparities that worsen when train and test age distributions shift. Enforcing strict age invariance can remove clinically meaningful age information, so mitigation must reduce harmful confounding without discarding useful signals.
method: After a warm-up stage, the method estimates label-conditioned, age-dependent trends in model-perceived difficulty and decorrelates age from these dominant trends. Robust Huber-weighted affinity weights attenuate shortcut correlations while preserving nonlinear age information, and an Age Coverage Score scales the penalty according to mini-batch age variance for stable optimization.

title: Robust Tooth Segmentation Under Orthodontic CBCT: A Metal Artifact-Aware Approach
motivation: Tooth instance segmentation in orthodontic CBCT supports diagnosis and treatment planning, but brackets and wires create severe metal artifacts that corrupt tooth structure and blur boundaries. Because two-stage pipelines depend on accurate bounding boxes, artifact-induced localization errors can crop out teeth or include neighbors and destabilize downstream segmentation.
method: The two-stage framework uses an artifact-aware localization loss that matches the intensity-weighted center of mass of predicted and ground-truth tooth patches, treating metal artifacts as informative localization cues. A 3D U-Net then segments each detected crop while jointly regressing a normalized distance map that de-emphasizes artifact-contaminated boundary responses and reduces false positives.

title: ROTE: Routing–Timescale Framework for Balanced Expert Allocation in MoE-Based Continual Segmentation
motivation: Continual clinical segmentation must adapt to new scanners, centers, and anatomical targets without replaying private historical data or forgetting prior tasks. In MoE-augmented SAM, conventional gating can collapse routing onto a few experts, leaving capacity underused and worsening catastrophic forgetting over long task sequences.
method: ROTE freezes the SAM backbone, adds MoE experts in the decoder, and uses continuously weighted soft routing to retain gradient access and expert recoverability. Locally-Regularized Soft Routing based on KAN constrains nonlinear gating to balance expert allocation, while Hierarchical Temporal Learning updates experts rapidly and routing slowly to separate adaptation timescales and reduce forgetting.

title: RPG-SAM: Reliability-Weighted Prototypes and Geometric Adaptive Threshold Selection for Training-Free One-Shot Polyp Segmentation
motivation: Training-free one-shot polyp segmentation can transfer knowledge from one labeled support image, but existing pipelines treat support regions and query response intensities as homogeneous. Reflections or mucus can make some support features unreliable, background cues are underused as negative references, and fixed thresholds fail when query heatmap intensities vary across clinical images.
method: RPG-SAM extracts DINOv2 features and uses SLIC superpixels to mine foreground and background prototypes from the support image. Reliability-Weighted Prototype Mining scores foreground prototypes by contrast and reverse purity, Geometric Adaptive Selection chooses query-specific thresholds from morphological consensus, and Prior-guided Iterative Refinement uses SAM2 to polish boundaries.

title: RT-Super: Learning Tumor Segmentation from Longitudinal Images and Reports
motivation: Multi-tumor segmentation is limited by the high cost and scarcity of pixel-level tumor masks, especially for tumor types poorly represented in public datasets. Hospitals nevertheless collect longitudinal and multi-phase images and radiology reports that contain complementary information, so a method is needed to use these sources during training while requiring only a single image at inference.
method: RT-Super is a self-distillation teacher-student architecture in which the teacher receives longitudinal and multi-phase images plus report-derived tumor information, while the student receives only one image. A report-aware transformer generates convolutional refinements for student features, and consistency losses enforce tumor location consistency across scans; teacher masks supervise the student for inference without reports or additional scans.

title: S2DLight: Single Step Diffusion Network via Degradation-Aware Adaptation for Surgical Endoscopic Image Low-Light Enhancement
motivation: Surgical endoscopy often suffers from limited illumination, scattering, noise, and low contrast that obscure fine anatomical structures. Although diffusion restoration can improve fidelity, medical datasets are small and directly using large pretrained text-to-image models causes anatomical-domain mismatch and costly multi-step inference.
method: S2DLight adapts a Stable Diffusion 2.1 backbone for endoscopic restoration through a contrastively trained degradation estimator that injects image-specific low-light representations. It reformulates diffusion sampling as a single-step latent prediction, adds latent structural augmentation with VAE skip connections, and uses training-time semantic alignment so a fixed enhancement prompt can provide useful conditioning at inference.

title: S2GAIN: Spatio-Spectral Guided Affinity Imputation Network for Alzheimer’s Disease Diagnosis with Incomplete Modality
motivation: Multimodal MRI and PET provide complementary structural and metabolic evidence for early Alzheimer’s disease diagnosis, but PET is often unavailable because of cost, infrastructure, and radiation concerns. Image-domain synthesis can introduce artifacts, while feature-level methods may align only spatial information or force unreliable PET components to match MRI, injecting noise into classification.
method: S²GAIN uses a cascaded dual-stream cross-modal backbone with lightweight imputers that infer missing PET features progressively from available MRI representations. Spatio-spectral joint alignment applies contrastive constraints to spatial features and Fourier magnitude spectra, while affinity-guided reliability weighting emphasizes predictable cross-modal components and suppresses uninferable noise; image-domain reconstruction regularization further maintains PET consistency.

title: S3H-Net: Injecting Hybrid Semantic-Spatial Guidance via Superpixel Hypergraphs for Medical Image Segmentation
motivation: Medical image segmentation is needed for diagnosis, treatment planning, and monitoring, but complex anatomy and blurred boundaries make fine delineation difficult. Patch-based graph and hypergraph nodes can mix foreground and background across anatomical boundaries, contaminating topological reasoning. Moreover, reasoning limited to bottlenecks or skip connections does not adequately guide fine multi-scale boundary recovery.
method: S3H-Net integrates superpixel-based semantic-spatial hypergraphs into a U-shaped segmentation network. Boundary-aware SLIC constructs contour-aligned nodes, while HSSH blocks in a parallel semantic encoder form spatial- and feature-similarity hyperedges to reason over multi-scale high-order correlations. A Cross-Covariance Semantic Injection module maps the reasoned hypergraph features back to pixel space and injects global context into local convolutional features.

title: SA-CFM: Structure-Aware Continuous Flow Matching for Normative Modeling of EEG Microstate
motivation: Parkinson's disease has heterogeneous cognitive trajectories, so group-level case-control analysis provides limited individualized characterization. EEG microstate statistics reflect rapid network coordination, yet existing EEG normative models treat them as independent variables and discard multivariate structure. Stochastic generative models also yield non-unique deviation scores across inference runs, undermining clinical reproducibility.
method: SA-CFM learns an age-conditioned, invertible continuous flow for EEG microstate normative modeling. It tokenizes microstate statistics as interacting physiological units and uses a Transformer velocity field with self-attention and shared age modulation to capture their dependencies. Deterministic flow inversion provides a unique subject-level deviation representation without disease labels.

title: SAFE-Diff: Scale-Aware Attention and Feature-Dispersive Diffusion with Uncertainty Estimation for Contrast-Enhanced Breast MRI Synthesis
motivation: DCE-MRI is highly sensitive for breast cancer detection and characterization, but gadolinium contrast increases scan burden, cost, and safety concerns. Non-contrast T1-weighted imaging and DWI offer anatomical and tissue-property cues for virtual enhancement, yet lesion textures and enhancement patterns are heterogeneous. GAN-based synthesis can compromise fine structural fidelity, motivating a robust high-fidelity alternative.
method: SAFE-Diff is a direct x0-prediction diffusion framework conditioned on non-contrast breast MRI, with convolutional extraction and complementary multi-scale attention for hierarchical anatomy. A shifted-window self-attention bottleneck captures longer-range context. It jointly predicts the synthesized image and pixel-wise variance for uncertainty-weighted reconstruction, and applies feature-dispersive regularization to intermediate representations to reduce redundancy and retain diagnostic detail.

title: SAFE-Diff: Structurally Anchored Diffusion for Anatomically Faithful CT Image Super-Resolution
motivation: CT super-resolution must improve perceptual clarity while preserving anatomy for reliable diagnostic measurement. Diffusion models are powerful for super-resolution but can sacrifice structural fidelity, produce inconsistencies, and incur high computation. A method is needed to explicitly balance perceptual detail with anatomically faithful reconstruction.
method: This SAFE-Diff uses a two-stage CT super-resolution pipeline followed by stationary wavelet fusion. A residual-prediction network with Squeeze-and-Excitation blocks produces an anatomically grounded coarse HR image from bicubic-upsampled LR input. A conditional U-Net with residual and Swin Transformer blocks performs truncated diffusion refinement, and a two-level SWT combines stable low-frequency structure from Stage 1 with high-frequency detail from Stage 2.

title: SAGEAgent: A Self-evolving Agent for Cost-Aware Modality Acquisition in Multimodal Survival Prediction

categories.value: Multimodal Integration with Clinical / Genomic / Biomarkers

motivation: Multimodal survival prediction can benefit from demographic, imaging, pathology, and genomic information, but these tests impose progressively greater clinical burden and follow a mandated order. Existing methods either assume complete data or passively accommodate missing modalities, without deciding whether a further test is justified for a particular patient. Adaptive acquisition also needs clinical transparency rather than opaque decision policies.
method: SAGEAgent formulates modality acquisition as sequential decisions along the clinical order from demographics to radiology, pathology, and genomics. At each stage, a frozen predictor supplies embedding, risk, and calibrated uncertainty, which clinical tools translate into text for a frozen LLM. The agent combines these signals with episodic retrieval of similar cases and semantic memory of rules periodically updated through self-reflection, then decides whether to acquire the next modality or stop without gradient updates.

title: SAM2 as a Key Bridge Between 2D Slices and 3D Volumes for Sparsely-supervised Medical Image Segmentation
motivation: Dense voxel-wise annotation for 3D medical segmentation is expensive, whereas annotating three orthogonal central slices is clinically practical. This sparse supervision provides too little constraint to recover complete, topologically coherent 3D anatomy, especially far from labeled slices. Existing cross-view methods can reinforce unreliable predictions, while registration cannot exploit unlabeled volumes to create new labels.
method: The framework uses SAM2 to propagate three orthogonal central-slice annotations through each 3D volume, with cross-case stacked slices serving as view-specific morphological anchors.
