A cross-view consensus mechanism estimates slice reliability from the other views and adaptively fuses predictions to limit propagation drift and single-view bias. Dense pseudo-labels are then refined by a 3D teacher-student module that dynamically balances 2D priors and volumetric predictions, followed by confidence-weighted fusion.

title: SAM-Cluster and SAM-LP: Structure-Aware Evaluation Metrics for Selecting WSI Feature Extractors Without MIL Training
motivation: WSI-based computational pathology relies on feature extractors and MIL aggregators, but the best feature extractor varies by dataset. Selecting one conventionally requires many costly MIL training runs. Standard representation metrics assume single images or naively pool patches, so they miss the bag structure, sparse signals, spatial heterogeneity, and histological organization of WSIs.
method: The authors introduce SAM-Cluster and SAM-LP, WSI-aware pre-evaluation metrics that rank feature extractors without training MIL models. SAM zero-shot segmentation identifies meaningful regions, allowing the metrics to assess intra-region consistency and inter-region separability at the bag level. SAM-Cluster adapts unsupervised clustering evaluation, while SAM-LP adapts label-based linear probing to the region-aware WSI setting.

title: SAMoCo: A Learning-Initialized and Physics-Refined Framework for Sampling-Agnostic Motion Correction in MRI
motivation: Patient motion during MRI acquisition causes artifacts that reduce image quality and diagnostic reliability. End-to-end deep learning correction can hallucinate structures and generalizes poorly across contrasts, while purely model-based methods can be slow, locally trapped, and restricted to specific sampling patterns. Motion-corrupted, undersampled acquisitions may also invalidate assumed coil sensitivity maps.
method: SAMoCo combines learning-based motion initialization with physics-driven instance-wise refinement. A pre-trained CNN-GRU processes undersampled k-space together with its sampling pattern to estimate motion parameters across varying shots and phase-encoding lines. An autofocusing and model-based reconstruction stage jointly refines those parameters, updates coil sensitivity maps, and reconstructs the corrected image.

title: SANT-CBM: Structurally-Aware and Noise-Tolerant Semi-supervised Concept Bottleneck Models
motivation: Concept Bottleneck Models make medical predictions interpretable through human-understandable concepts, but dense expert concept labels are scarce and expensive. Semi-supervised CBMs can use unlabeled images, yet heuristic pseudo-labels propagate noise and cause confirmation bias. They also often ignore pathological dependencies among concepts, permitting biologically implausible combinations.
method: SANT-CBM is a semi-supervised concept bottleneck framework that explicitly addresses pseudo-label reliability and concept structure. Its GMM-based dynamic weighting models the unlabeled-sample loss distribution to probabilistically down-weight noisy pseudo-supervision. A Structural Consistency Loss aligns predicted concept correlations on unlabeled data with clinically derived reference correlations, encouraging plausible concept combinations.

title: SAR-Net: Sample-Agnostic Retrieval Network for Robust Brain Tumor Segmentation with Missing Modalities
motivation: Multimodal MRI provides complementary information for brain tumor segmentation, but complete T1, T1ce, T2, and FLAIR acquisitions are often unavailable in practice. Synthesizing missing modalities can hallucinate anatomy, and implicit modality-invariant representations may remain entangled and poorly discriminative. A compensation strategy is needed that retains reliable structural boundaries under diverse missing-modality settings.
method: SAR-Net adopts a disentangle-contrast-retrieve design for missing-modality brain tumor segmentation. It separates modality-agnostic structural content from sample-agnostic styles, and uses momentum contrastive learning to organize discriminative style prototypes in a dynamic memory bank. Global Consensus Voting retrieves compatible styles for absent modalities, and adaptive modulation fuses them with content to preserve structure.

title: SAVer: Structure-Aware Validation of Standard Fetal Head Planes via Clinically Grounded Anatomical Completeness
motivation: Identifying standard fetal head ultrasound planes is essential for biometric measurement and detecting neurodevelopmental abnormalities. Existing image-level classifiers can be affected by pose and acquisition variability and may rely on global appearance rather than the anatomical landmarks that clinically define each plane. A clinically reliable system therefore needs explicit anatomical validation within plane recognition.
method: SAVer jointly performs fetal brain structure segmentation and head-plane classification using a perception backbone, a Plane Classification Module, and an Anatomical Reasoning Engine. The reasoning engine checks the presence, completeness, and spatial consistency of clinically relevant landmarks, while the Adapter Feature Alignment Module aligns segmentation representations with classification features without full encoder retraining.

title: SAW: Toward a Surgical Action World Model via Controllable and Scalable Video Generation
motivation: Controllable surgical video generation could alleviate data scarcity, synthesize rare actions, and support realistic surgical simulation. Existing methods often require expensive dense annotations or difficult structured intermediates at inference, while others provide insufficient control, realism, or temporal consistency in laparoscopic scenes. A scalable world model needs interpretable action inputs that can drive coherent tool-tissue interaction videos.
method: SAW fine-tunes an LTX-Video latent diffusion backbone with IC-LoRA to synthesize surgical action videos from four lightweight conditions: a language prompt, reference scene, tissue affordance mask, and 2D tool-tip trajectory. It encodes spatial conditions as VAE inputs to reformulate the task as video-to-video diffusion, and adds a depth consistency loss that reconstructs masked depth latents from denoised RGB tokens during training. This encourages geometrically plausible tool-tissue interactions without requiring depth input at inference.

title: Scalable Training of Spatially Grounded 2D Vision–Language Models for Radiology
motivation: Radiology VLMs can generate medical text but often cannot tie their outputs to specific image regions, limiting verification and clinical trust. Large-scale spatially grounded training data for clinical CT and MRI are scarce, and prior 2D slice datasets have remained limited in scale. A scalable approach is needed to learn language and spatial grounding jointly without manual spatial annotation.
method: The work builds RefRad2D, a bilingual clinical corpus of CT/MRI slice-text pairs with VQA and automatically derived spatial-grounding subsets. RadGrounder is a PaliGemma 2-based multitask VLM trained to perform report generation, VQA, and localization through token-based bounding-box prediction or segmentation. Its training combines routine-report supervision with LLM-based curation and automated segmentation-derived spatial labels.

title: S-CEReBrO: Breaking the Memory Barrier in Continuous EEG Monitoring
motivation: Continuous EEG monitoring, including seizure monitoring, produces signals whose temporal length grows indefinitely. Transformer-based EEG foundation models retain key-value states over the full history, so memory increases with duration and can exceed wearable or real-world hardware limits. Efficient long-context processing must preserve EEG's two-dimensional spatiotemporal structure while avoiding this memory overflow.
method: S-CEReBrO uses masked autoencoding pre-training with spatiotemporal EEG tokenization and a Windowed Alternating Attention mechanism. Windowed temporal and spatial attention restrict interactions to fixed local neighborhoods, evict stale tokens, and use layer-specific temporal dilation and shifts to expand context. This yields linear computation over channels and time with a constant resident KV-cache footprint for streaming inference.

title: SCISSR: Scribble-Conditioned Interactive Surgical Segmentation and Refinement
motivation: Pixel-level surgical scene segmentation is costly because anatomy and instruments are deformable, thin, reflective, and frequently occluded. In such scenes, point prompts are too sparse and boxes often include extensive background, making precise multiround correction inefficient. Scribbles can provide denser target cues but are not well integrated into surgical prompt-driven segmentation systems.
method: SCISSR augments a frozen SAM 2 backbone with a lightweight Scribble Encoder, Spatial Gated Fusion, and LoRA adapters. It converts all accumulated freehand scribbles into dense prompt embeddings for the mask decoder, while injecting the latest corrective stroke into the memory-attention query for iterative refinement. The trainable modules communicate with the backbone through standard embedding interfaces, supporting an architecture-agnostic prompt integration design.

title: SCKAN: Structural Consensus-Based KAN Prototype Learning for Semi-supervised Pancreas Segmentation
motivation: Accurate pancreas segmentation supports early cancer diagnosis, but dense labels are limited and pancreas morphology varies substantially across patients. Existing semi-supervised consistency and prototype methods mainly lack effective cross-sample structural knowledge, causing supervision bias and poor generalization such as under- or over-segmentation. Shared anatomical semantics across pancreatic subregions need to be modeled despite complex nonlinear sample relationships.
method: SCKAN learns cross-sample structural consensus through Structure-constrained Prototype Consistency Learning and Consensus-based Kolmogorov-Arnold Fusion. SPCL uses structure-aware spatial decomposition to form anatomy-guided subregion prototypes, then applies position-weighted contrastive optimization and positional decorrelation to align them across samples. CKaF uses KAN adaptive B-spline nonlinearities to aggregate stable consensus and filter morphology-specific noise.

title: ScribbleDose: Scribble-Guided Dose Prediction in Radiotherapy
motivation: Radiotherapy dose prediction requires target coverage while limiting dose to organs at risk, and most models rely on fully delineated anatomical masks for geometric guidance. Creating these masks is labor-intensive, whereas mask-free approaches may lose fine-grained structural constraints and two-stage mask-generation pipelines separate structure extraction from dose modeling. Sparse scribbles offer a lower-burden source of structural information that must be converted into clinically useful guidance jointly with dose prediction.
method: ScribbleDose provides an end-to-end scribble-mask-dose pipeline. Its Scribble Completion Module propagates sparse structure labels to semantically correlated voxels and uses supervoxel-based regularization to preserve boundary consistency, producing dense anatomical priors. The Structure-Guided Dose Generation Module incorporates these completed masks through mask-guided attention, and dose losses jointly optimize both completion and dose generation.

title: SD-SAM: Synergizing SAM and DINOv3 for Parameter-Efficient Polyp Segmentation and a Challenging Benchmark Dataset
motivation: Polyp segmentation is important for early colorectal cancer detection, but SAM needs spatial prompts and automatic prompt generation often depends on heavy, error-prone lesion-parsing networks. Medical adaptation of SAM also faces a parameter-versus-accuracy trade-off. Existing benchmarks are biased toward centrally located large polyps, leaving tiny and spatially dispersed lesions insufficiently represented.
method: SD-SAM uses a two-stage parameter-efficient design that couples DINOv3 and SAM. A lightweight decoder regresses Gaussian heatmaps of polyp centers from multiscale DINOv3 features to provide automatic high-confidence prompts, avoiding full lesion parsing. For segmentation, it applies DINOv3-guided hierarchical adaptation: shallow SAM layers receive cosine-similarity boundary distillation, while deep layers use QKV-based feature fusion for semantic priors.

title: Seamless Whole Slide Label-Free Virtual Staining
motivation: Label-free virtual staining could avoid destructive chemical staining, but gigapixel whole-slide images cannot usually be processed holistically because of memory limits. Patchwise inference disrupts tissue continuity and produces visible seams and color shifts that hinder pathological review. Existing consistency methods do not adequately provide both spatial and channel consistency for heterogeneous label-free source signals under stable BN-based generation.
method: COMB performs patch-based label-free virtual staining with a Consistency Memory Bank that stores and dynamically retrieves adjacent-tile feature representations separately from computation. Its retrieval-based context integration combines local padding for spatial continuity with neighbor-aware channel attention for stable cross-tile statistics. A sliding-window schedule limits memory overhead while maintaining contextual consistency across the whole slide.

title: SeedPro: Place Brachytherapy Seeds Like Expert Clinicians via Hierarchical Reinforcement Agents
motivation: Brachytherapy requires a preoperative plan that specifies seed placement to achieve tumor dose coverage while protecting organs at risk. Manual iterative planning is labor-intensive, variable between clinicians, and can yield suboptimal or mechanically impractical arrangements. Prior automated and reinforcement-learning approaches often prioritize dosimetry alone, potentially producing excessive punctures that do not reflect expert implantation practice.
method: SeedPro formulates brachytherapy preoperative planning as fine-grained seed-placement optimization by hierarchical reinforcement-learning agents. The agents plan seed number, injection trajectories, and individual seed positions and orientations while accounting for dose objectives and procedural practicality. This hierarchical approach is intended to produce reproducible expert-like plans with lower computational cost and fewer unnecessary punctures.

title: Seeing Through Multiple Views: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning via Selective Neurons for Consistent Radiology Report Generation
motivation: Multi-view radiology report generation is needed because individual X-ray projections provide incomplete anatomical information, while radiologists interpret each view before integrating findings. Existing fusion-based models can produce contradictory findings across frontal and lateral views because they overlook intrinsic view differences. Such inconsistency can undermine diagnostic reliability, especially when only a non-frontal view is available.
method: View-PNDF analyzes a radiology report generator at the neuron level to identify a compact set of neurons responsive to particular X-ray views. Its detection and verification modules identify these pattern neurons and quantify their contribution by selective deactivation. Fine-tuning is then restricted to the detected neurons, preserving view-agnostic representations; LLMs consolidate the resulting per-view reports into an integrated report.

title: Seeing Through Smoke: Surgical Desmoking for Improved Visual Perception
motivation: Electrocautery and vessel-sealing instruments generate smoke that obscures tissue detail in minimally invasive and robot-assisted surgery. This degradation can impair intraoperative decisions and vision-based functions such as instrument segmentation, tracking, and 3D reconstruction. Reliable learning-based desmoking is difficult because smoke is spatially variable and paired smoky-to-clean surgical data are scarce.
method: The method uses a ViT backbone and DPT decoder to extract and decode multi-scale endoscopic features. A physics-inspired head jointly predicts a smoke-free image and a smoke map by regressing parameters derived from an atmospheric scattering formulation. Training uses a large synthetic paired dataset produced by blending diverse artificial smoke maps with clean endoscopic images, while a paired da Vinci dataset supports evaluation of reconstruction and downstream perception tasks.

title: SegDINO: Introducing Multi-Scale Structure into DINO for Efficient Medical Image Segmentation
motivation: Medical image segmentation under limited data and varying imaging protocols requires representations that generalize well. Although DINO models offer transferable features, their features lack an explicit multi-scale hierarchy, making subtle targets such as small lesions difficult to segment with simple decoders. Existing remedies often use computationally expensive multi-scale fusion or upsampling decoders.
method: SegDINO adapts DINOv3 features for segmentation through lightweight scale modeling rather than a heavy decoder. Token Pyramid Adaptation reorganizes features from different DINO depths into a pseudo multi-scale pyramid. Scale-Aware Decoding then performs intra-scale refinement and top-down cross-scale propagation to recover detailed segmentation structure efficiently.

title: Segment Anything Model with Symmetric Spectral Uncertainty Gating for Generalizable Medical Image Segmentation
motivation: Medical segmentation models trained on one clinical center often fail on unseen centers because scanners, manufacturers, and protocols induce domain shifts. Single-domain generalization is practical when multi-institutional data cannot be shared, but conventional augmentation and style randomization have limited ability to learn robust anatomical priors. PEFT can adapt SAM with limited labels, yet it can also overfit the model to source-domain imaging styles.
method: SSUG augments PEFT-adapted SAM with a closed-loop design for single-domain generalization. Spectral Manifold Extrapolation actively simulates potential source-spectrum style shifts, and Uncertainty-aware Symmetric Channel Gating uses response divergence to calibrate style-sensitive channels. Hierarchical Decoupled Consistency further enforces anatomical consistency across multiple feature granularities.

title: Selective Confidence Fusion for Specular Highlight Detection in Medical Images
motivation: Specular highlights caused by directed illumination on moist tissue create saturated regions in endoscopic and other intraoperative images. They can obscure critical anatomy and corrupt the edge, color, and texture cues used by localization, segmentation, registration, and restoration systems. Existing methods and learning-based fusion often treat heterogeneous cues as equally reliable, making them fragile under complex illumination, saturation, fluids, and limited annotations.
method: The proposed framework combines edge, chromatic, background, and prediction-reliability cues through a Selective Confidence Fusion Module. It estimates spatial confidence for every cue and applies per-pixel soft weighting, softmax normalization, and residual attention reweighting. This selectively preserves reliable evidence while suppressing misleading cues from saturation, mirror-like gradients, altered color, or coarse-prediction errors.

title: Selective Rank-1 Orthogonality Regularization: Rethinking Stability-Plasticity Balance in Continual Medical Image Classification
motivation: Continual medical classification must acquire knowledge about emerging diseases while retaining prior diagnostic knowledge when prior data are unavailable. PTM-based methods with LoRA face a stability-plasticity dilemma: task-specific updates can interfere with old knowledge, whereas full-space orthogonality exhausts capacity for new tasks. A uniform treatment of the whole adaptation space cannot determine which parts should be protected versus reused.
method: SR1OR decomposes each task's LoRA adaptation space into unit rank-1 subspaces and uses Rank-1 Subspace Orientation Theory to characterize their stability or plasticity roles through local curvature and task-level sharpness. Progressive Subspace Identification selects stability-oriented subspaces, prioritizing high-curvature subspaces in sharp task landscapes. A Selective Orthogonality Constraint then regularizes new-task updates only against those selected subspaces while leaving the remaining subspaces free for adaptation.

title: Self-auditing Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning for Few-Shot 3D Medical Image Segmentation
motivation: Foundation models require site-specific adaptation for 3D medical segmentation because clinical sites differ in acquisition protocols, reconstruction, and patient populations. Few-shot volumetric annotation and 3D training are resource-intensive, while many clinical groups lack AI engineers to manually choose adapter topology, placement, and rank. Existing automated PEFT searches require multiple full fine-tuning runs and are impractical in this setting.
method: SEA-PEFT treats adapter type, placement, and rank selection as an online budgeted allocation problem during fine-tuning of a frozen foundation-model backbone. Its search-audit-allocate loop trains active adapters, estimates each adapter's Dice-per-cost utility by temporarily disabling it, and greedily reselects the active set under a parameter budget. EMA and IQR utility smoothing plus a finite-state ranking controller stabilize selection under noisy few-shot validation feedback; the final chosen configuration is fine-tuned from scratch.

title: Self-Supervised Implicit CEST Reconstruction via Physics-Informed Lorentz Encoding
motivation: Multi-pool CEST MRI can quantify metabolic effects such as APT, NOE, and MT, but dense Z-spectrum sampling causes long acquisitions that limit clinical use. Sparse sampling accelerates acquisition but makes high-resolution Z-spectrum reconstruction ill-posed. Conventional fitting can be unstable, and generic INRs lack spectral physical constraints, allowing noise overfitting and physically invalid oscillations.
method: Lorentz Encoding is a self-supervised INR framework that learns a continuous mapping from spatial-spectral coordinates to CEST signal intensity. It decouples spatial and spectral modeling: Hash Encoding represents high-frequency spatial texture, while learnable combinations of Lorentzian profiles encode the physically governed spectral dimension. Embedding these spectral priors in the encoding layer constrains reconstruction to plausible biological signals and suppresses non-physical spectral fluctuations.

title: Self-supervised Learning on Lingual Ultrasound Video Encodes Clinically Meaningful Articulatory Structure of Rhotic Production in Residual Speech Sound Disorder
motivation: Residual speech sound disorder can persist in children and is associated with long-term academic, social, and mental-health consequences. Lingual ultrasound can support rhotic treatment, but expert analysis of complex tongue motion is labor-intensive, and distinct tongue configurations can produce perceptually equivalent American English rhotics. Existing SSL methods focus mainly on phoneme-level classification, do not adequately control inter-speaker variability, and may emphasize pixel reconstruction over clinically meaningful articulatory structure.
method: BYOL-VS applies a non-contrastive joint-embedding SSL framework with a ViViT spatiotemporal encoder to lingual ultrasound video. It adds speaker-adversarial regularization to suppress speaker-specific variation while retaining articulatory structure in the embeddings. The learned representations are intended to capture both perceptual rhotic accuracy and within-phoneme tongue configurations without task-specific fine-tuning.

title: Self-supervised Longitudinal Neuroimaging Augmentation for Continuous Staging of Alzheimer’s Disease
motivation: Alzheimer's disease progression is biologically continuous, but standard diagnostic categories provide only coarse stages and can conceal substantial heterogeneity. Continuous neuroimaging staging is more suitable for monitoring subtle progression and treatment effects, yet approaches such as SLOPE depend heavily on longitudinal follow-up data. Typical cohorts contain many baseline-only subjects, leaving longitudinal supervision too sparse for robust staging.
method: The framework uses a residual GAN to synthesize plausible near-future amyloid PET visits for subjects with only baseline scans. A monotonic brain-change constraint encodes the biological prior of irreversible amyloid accumulation and guides the generator without explicit longitudinal supervision. These synthesized visits augment real longitudinal observations when training a continuous staging model, with directional agreement against real follow-up used for assessment.

title: Self-supervised Spline Autoencoder for Smooth Latent Dynamics in Echocardiography
motivation: Identifying end-diastole and end-systole in echocardiography is important for measuring chamber size, ejection fraction, and myocardial function. Existing automatic methods often require extensive annotations or impose rigid assumptions such as periodic, constant-frequency phase evolution, creating a gap between smooth interpretable dynamics and precise event localization.
method: The Spline Autoencoder learns temporally smooth, consistent latent trajectories that represent cardiac motion as low-rank dynamics without phase labels or predefined periodicity. A label-agnostic spectral embedding of normalized latent trajectory velocities recovers a cardiac phase variable and supports precise ED/ES localization, with lightweight label-informed assignment for semantic event names.

title: Self-supervised Temporal Regularization for Landmark-Based Cardiac Segmentation with Automatic AHA Regional Mapping
motivation: Frame-independent cardiac segmentation can produce temporal discontinuities, artificial jitter, and unreliable ejection-fraction or wall-motion measurements. Although graph-based landmark models provide topological guarantees and anatomical correspondences, they generally do not exploit temporal coherence, while existing temporal postprocessing is disconnected from the learned anatomical structure and requires no clinically interpretable regional mapping.
method: Starting from a landmark-based segmentation model with implicit anatomical correspondences, the method performs post-training self-supervised refinement on ultrasound sequences. It penalizes velocity and acceleration discontinuities of corresponding landmarks across frames, using temporal behavior rather than per-frame labels as supervision. The learned correspondences are also mapped automatically to the AHA 17-segment standard for regional wall-motion analysis.

title: Semantic Feature Modulation for Mammographic Lesion Classification
motivation: Mammographic lesion classifiers commonly predict benignity or malignancy from images alone, whereas radiologists reason with structured BI-RADS descriptors such as density, shape, margins, and calcification patterns. Descriptor effects are context-dependent, categorical labels can obscure mixtures of neighboring attributes, and existing descriptor predictors lack a transparent way to support what-if analysis or second-reader use.
method: The framework replaces selected Layer Normalization affine parameters with sample-specific parameters predicted by dedicated modulation networks for BI-RADS descriptors. Descriptor embeddings are injected at feature stages matched to their spatial semantics, allowing multiple attributes to modulate image features jointly and context-dependently. Continuous descriptor embeddings also support interpolation between categorical attributes and can accept probabilistic descriptor outputs for post-detection decision support.

title: Semantically Consistent Whole-Body PET/CT Report Generation with Local Lesion-Level Guidance
motivation: Whole-body PET/CT report generation must cover a large volume containing sparse, localized abnormalities, often summarizing multiple lesions in one statement. Full-volume models can dilute lesion-specific cues, while local captioning does not produce complete reports; conventional one-to-one contrastive alignment and template-heavy free-text supervision further limit semantic learning.
method: A SetTransformer-based aggregation module compresses a variable number of PET/CT lesion candidates into a fixed-length entity set, enabling many-to-one lesion-to-description alignment. Pretraining combines local entity alignment with global relation alignment to preserve paired semantics without assuming all other batch pairs are unrelated. Report generation is trained in two stages, first on structured positive findings and then on free-text reports to emphasize lesions and reduce template bias.

title: Semantic-Aware Organ-Level Esophageal Tumor Synthesis via Latent Rectified Flow

categories.value: AI for Population Health, Public Health & Epidemiology

motivation: Robust esophageal cancer models need large annotated datasets, but early-stage lesions are subtle and difficult to annotate at scale. Existing 3D CT synthesis usually inpaints texture inside a fixed lesion mask and scales lesion size, whereas esophageal cancer staging depends on invasion depth and involves organ-level wall thickening and mass effects that invalidate static masks.
method: SOFT uses a semantic-aware Latent Rectified Flow model to synthesize esophageal tumors while deforming the organ and preserving surrounding anatomy. Structured clinical attributes such as T-stage and tumor location control the generated invasion pattern. A synchronously trained segmentation head dynamically delineates the deformed anatomy, producing image-label pairs whose masks remain aligned with the synthesized structure.

title: Semantic-Consistent Dual-Image Vision-Language Alignment via Modality Routing for 3D PET/CT
motivation: PET/CT combines CT anatomy with PET metabolism, but existing vision-language methods often treat the pair as one input and favor CT-dominant or coarse representations. They can miss modality-specific information, suffer false negatives when semantically similar reports are contrasted, and overlook fine-grained links between organs and text.
method: PETCT-DiVLA uses separate 3D Vision Transformer branches for PET and CT together with a text encoder containing a token-level modality router. The router identifies PET-specific, CT-specific, and shared tokens, while a semantic-consistency-guided SigLIP loss uses organ abnormality labels to form more reliable positive and negative pairs. Global whole-report/whole-body and local sentence/organ alignments are learned jointly, with mask-free inference.

title: Sequence-Conditioned Flow-Based Models for Digital Phantom Generation in MRI
motivation: MRI analysis and phantom-based data generation require many high-quality images, but real data are limited by acquisition cost and patient confidentiality. Existing generative approaches may produce only one quantitative map, require unavailable ground-truth maps, yield physically implausible values, or ignore pulse-sequence parameters, threatening anatomical fidelity and cross-contrast robustness.
method: The self-supervised flow-based model takes T1-, T2-, and PD-weighted brain MR images together with their TR, TE, and ES parameters and predicts all three quantitative maps. These maps are passed to an MR signal model to synthesize weighted images, allowing the generated data to respect acquisition physics. Training combines synthetic and real Turbo Spin Echo data across sequence settings without requiring ground-truth quantitative maps.

title: Set-Based Groupwise Registration for Variable-Length, Variable-Contrast Cardiac MRI
motivation: Quantitative cardiac MRI requires motion correction because cardiac and respiratory motion causes blurring and biased parameter estimates. Existing deep groupwise registration networks encode sequences as fixed-length, ordered channel stacks, tying them to one protocol and failing on variable lengths, sampling orders, or markedly different contrast dynamics.
method: Any2Reg represents a quantitative cardiac MRI sequence as an unordered set and applies a shared encoder to each image. Correlation-guided feature aggregation builds a permutation-invariant canonical reference, while the deformation mapping is permutation-equivariant across set elements. Contrast-insensitive features from a foundation model are optionally fused to handle strong contrast changes, enabling registration across sequence lengths and protocols.

title: Set-Inclusive Uncertainty Modeling for Robust Brain Tumor Segmentation
motivation: Brain tumor segmentation depends on complementary T1, T1c, T2, and FLAIR evidence, yet acquiring all modalities is often impractical. Missing-modality methods commonly use deterministic embeddings that conceal information loss, allowing predictions to rely on plausible but unsupported features instead of expressing intrinsic uncertainty.
method: The framework represents each available-modality configuration as a Gaussian embedding whose mean carries task information and whose variance represents uncertainty from missing evidence. Means from partial configurations are regularized toward the full-modality mean, while variance is scaled by their aligned-mean discrepancy. A set-inclusive hierarchy further enforces larger uncertainty for modality subsets than for their supersets, preserving consistent uncertainty ordering.

title: SF-DINO: Spatial-Frequency Adapted Foundation Model for Multiple Myeloma Diagnosis

categories.value: AI for Population Health, Public Health & Epidemiology

motivation: Bone-marrow smear interpretation is central to multiple myeloma screening but is labor-intensive, subjective, and complicated by heterogeneous cell morphology and inter-class visual similarity. Existing automated studies often use binary or limited-lineage classification, while natural-image foundation models lack the domain-specific sensitivity needed for subtle nuclear and cellular textures.
method: SF-DINO adapts a DINOv3 backbone for fine-grained six-class bone-marrow cell diagnosis using parameter-efficient modules. A parallel spatial-morphology adapter injects high-frequency local cues while preserving pretrained semantics. Frequency-selective hashing attention uses spectral clustering to capture efficient global and long-range dependencies.

title: S-GRPO: Structural Group Relative Policy Optimization for Medical Image Segmentation
motivation: Medical image segmentation must achieve pixel-level accuracy as well as anatomically plausible global structure for diagnosis, planning, and navigation. Standard supervised losses mainly fit pixel-wise distributions, can settle in suboptimal minima, and cannot directly optimize non-differentiable structural criteria such as boundary distance or connectivity. Existing RL alternatives are unstable or too computationally slow for high-resolution dense prediction.
method: S-GRPO reformulates GRPO for dense segmentation through structural parallel sampling: a multi-head segmentation architecture produces diverse candidate masks in one forward pass. A Selector Network identifies an expert head and estimates group-relative advantages without an auxiliary critic. Advantage-Aware Distillation and conditional EMA reference updates stabilize optimization while balancing exploration and exploitation, and the framework can be attached to CNN, Transformer, or State Space Model backbones.

title: Shape-Adaptive Guidance Signal for Interactive Cortical Sulcal Labeling
motivation: Small, shallow LPFC sulci are relevant to studies of cognitive development and function, but their variable locations, shapes, and adjacency make automatic labeling unreliable. Expert manual labeling and correction are labor-intensive, limiting study scale. Interactive surface segmentation needs guidance signals that reflect detailed anatomy, because simple spatial-proximity encodings can refine these fine structures poorly.
method: The framework uses a spherical CNN for interactive LPFC sulcal labeling, combining surface geometry, the current prediction, and separately encoded positive and negative clicks. Its shape-adaptive guidance signal is obtained by solving the eikonal equation with a mean-curvature-based isotropic speed function. This makes the signal propagate rapidly along sulci and slowly across gyri, allowing clicks to guide anatomically informed iterative refinement.

title: Shape-Aware Registration Without Pretraining: CT-Ultrasound Bone Surface Alignment via Instance-Level Shape Completion
motivation: Orthopedic surgical plans derived from preoperative CT or MRI require accurate intraoperative registration, and US is attractive because it is real-time and radiation-free. Yet bone shadowing and restricted surgical scanning yield incomplete US bone surfaces, reducing registration robustness, particularly for long or symmetric bones. Paired CT-US data are scarce, limiting conventional learning-based completion and registration methods.
method: ComReg is an end-to-end CT-US bone surface registration framework that jointly learns patient-specific completion of partial US bone surfaces and cross-modal registration. During preoperative training, patient-specific CT bone models are used to simulate US point clouds, providing self-supervised supervision without cross-instance CT-US datasets. The learned completion prior and registration modules are then applied to real intraoperative US surfaces.

title: ShapeEFM: A Shape-Based Pretrained Foundation Model on ECG Morphology Comprehension
motivation: Mass ECG screening can detect asymptomatic cardiovascular abnormalities early, so robust representations from abundant unlabeled ECG data are important. Existing eSSL methods emphasize rhythm or high-level heartbeat semantics and may leave clinically important sub-beat morphology changes, such as QRS widening and ST deviation, insufficiently explicit. This limits morphology comprehension and interpretability for ECG-based assessment.
method: ShapeEFM is a transformer-based ECG foundation model pretrained with a generative eSSL objective. It discretizes temporal trend shifts into symbolic tokens, treats P, Q, R, S, and T waveform components as Cardio-Morphemes, and concatenates them into Cardio-Sentences. A Cardio-Morpheme Transformer uses temporal encoding, spatial and temporal embeddings, cardiac-cycle RoPE, and patch-wise attention to model morphology-level dependencies and support interpretable outputs.

title: Shape-Scale Aware Diffusion Models for Weakly Supervised Medical Image Anomaly Detection
motivation: Weakly supervised anomaly detection seeks pixel-level lesion localization from cost-effective image-level labels. Diffusion approaches often retain standard U-Net backbones whose isotropic convolutions inadequately represent complex directional and multi-scale anatomy, while ungated skips can transfer anomalies into healthy reconstructions. Their heavy iterative denoising also creates substantial inference latency.
method: The proposed direction-guided shape-scale-aware diffusion model replaces a standard diffusion U-Net backbone with a lightweight morphology-scale-aware design. Its Direction-Guided Multi-Scale residual module uses dual-branch dilated convolutions and hierarchical SE attention to learn direction-decoupled, multi-scale anatomical features. Anomaly-Sensitive Skip Fusion gates skip features from high-frequency boundary cues to limit anomaly leakage, while PDS-Conv reduces iterative diffusion cost.

title: ShapKO: Shapley-Adaptive Modality Knockout for Robust Multimodal Learning

categories.value: Multimodal Integration with Clinical / Genomic / Biomarkers

motivation: Clinical multimodal inputs are frequently missing because of acquisition failures, cost, triage, or site-specific protocols, causing all-modality models to degrade. Training can also over-rely on one highly predictive modality and undertrain complementary sources, leaving models fragile when that modality is unavailable. Static modality masking cannot adapt to changing modality utility or explicitly account for performance across the many possible availability subsets.
method: ShapKO is an architecture-agnostic training strategy that periodically evaluates validation utility across modality subsets and estimates each modality's marginal contribution with Shapley values. It converts these values into bounded, modality-specific knockout probabilities, masking above-average influential modalities more often. Models train under the current sampled knockout distribution with fixed placeholders for absent embeddings, then update the rates to promote complementary representations.

title: Shared Gaussian Geometry for Brain MRI Spatial Resolution Harmonization Without External Training
motivation: Clinical multi-contrast brain MRI commonly combines high-resolution isotropic structural scans with disease-targeted sequences that have anisotropic slices and modality-specific resolutions. This spatial heterogeneity impairs cross-contrast visualization, comparison, measurement, and arbitrary-view reconstruction. Interpolation oversmooths structures, whereas externally trained super-resolution models are difficult to generalize across heterogeneous, retrospective clinical protocols.
method: The method first fits an explicit subject-specific Gaussian scaffold from an isotropic T1-weighted structural scan using Gaussian Splatting. It then fixes this shared geometry and optimizes modality-specific appearance parameters from sparse target-modality slices for zero-shot continuous rendering and through-plane super-resolution. Topology-aware Gaussian densification, latent appearance regularization, and low-resolution modality consistency improve structural stability and contrast fidelity.

title: SHINE: An Entropy-Guided Digital Twin Framework for 3D Myocardial Scar Reconstruction from Sparse CMR
motivation: Ventricular tachycardia ablation planning requires accurate recovery of heterogeneous myocardial scar and narrow conducting isthmuses. Sparse, highly anisotropic LGE MRI leaves much of the myocardium unobserved, making topology-preserving 3D reconstruction ill posed. Discrete interpolation creates staircase discontinuities, conventional CNNs tend to smooth high-frequency channels, and deterministic neural fields cannot indicate reliability in unobserved regions.
method: SHINE represents scar probability as a continuous neural field on a patient-specific myocardial manifold. It builds this anatomical prior from automated Cine MRI segmentation and Statistical Shape Model fitting, spatially co-registering sparse LGE observations without voxel resampling. A Bayesian SIREN captures high-frequency scar geometry and estimates epistemic uncertainty; an Entropy-Weighted Dirichlet Energy loss smooths uncertain sparse regions while retaining observed fine topology.

title: SHOT-CCR: Biologically Guided Adversarial Training for Test-Time Adaptation in Cellular Morphology
motivation: High-content Cell Painting screens support drug discovery and perturbation analysis, but technical batch effects can obscure true cellular morphology and prevent generalization to unseen batches. Larger datasets require more batches, compounding this problem across cell types. General batch correction can remove useful signal, while cell-count differences are a biologically important confounder that models may overuse.
method: SHOT-CCR extends test-time adaptation for Cell Painting by combining entropy minimization, diversity regularization, and pseudo-labeling with biologically guided adversarial training. A cell-invariant gradient-reversal mechanism discourages encoder reliance on cell-count differences across batches and cell types. Rather than removing all batch information, it selectively down-weights cell-count-driven confounding while retaining batch-specific structure predictive of perturbations.

title: SIGMA-VAE: Sketched Isotropic Gaussian Multi-View Autoencoder for Normative Modeling
motivation: Normative modeling quantifies an individual's deviation from healthy brain variation and can characterize heterogeneous neurological or psychiatric pathology. Standard VAE latent spaces can contain poorly organized regions that make distance-based anomaly scores unreliable, and their dense entangled factors limit biological interpretation. Image ambiguity, scanner variation, and nonlinear healthy demographic trajectories further risk false-positive or confounded deviations.
method: SIGMA-VAE is a multi-view VAE for normative modeling that combines Sketched Isotropic Gaussian Regularization, L0-induced learnable sparsity, and an uncertainty-aware W-score. SIGReg uses characteristic-function matching to impose compact, hole-free latent geometry suitable for Euclidean deviation scoring. The sparsity term selects a minimal set of interpretable latent factors, while the W-score weights deviations by posterior variance to reduce ambiguity- and scanner-related false positives.

title: Single-Stage Hierarchical Rectification for Weakly Supervised Histopathology Segmentation
motivation: Weakly supervised histopathology segmentation aims to avoid costly pixel-level annotations by learning from image-level labels, but common CAM-based pipelines require classification, offline pseudo-mask refinement, and separate segmentation retraining. Local texture biases in shallow and intermediate features can create false positives that propagate through these stages, while repeated training increases computational cost. A single-stage method that corrects representations before CAM formation is therefore needed.
method: SSHR performs feature rectification during the forward pass, generating refined CAMs within one training loop instead of using offline pseudo-mask refinement and retraining. Its Hierarchical Feature Rectification Module combines Global Semantic Rectification, which uses deep classification-supervised context to reweight CAM-producing channels, with Contextual Homogenization, which aggregates local neighborhoods to suppress isolated spatial responses. A zero-initialized residual formulation integrates these corrections into the backbone while preserving stable optimization.

title: Single-Subject Multi-view MRI Super-Resolution via Implicit Neural Representations
motivation: Clinical MRI often has high in-plane but low through-plane resolution, with multiple orientations acquired to provide complementary anatomy. Registration followed by interpolation can blur fine structures, while supervised super-resolution depends on large, cohort-specific datasets; existing self-supervised methods often ignore multi-view data or assume pre-aligned scans. A single-subject method that integrates misaligned multi-view scans without external training data or prior registration is needed.
method: SIMS-MRI is a self-supervised, single-subject pipeline that models one anisotropic view with a multi-resolution hash-encoded implicit representation. It applies implicit deformable image registration to align another view without assuming pre-registration, then fuses the views to refine the representation and reconstruct an isotropic volume. The design uses complementary multi-view information while avoiding external paired training data and registration preprocessing.

title: SIRA: Reasoning-Aware Surgical Instrument Segmentation via Query-Anchored Alignment
motivation: Surgical instrument segmentation supports navigation, robotic assistance, workflow analysis, and skill assessment, but most methods treat it as category-driven localization dominated by visual appearance. Such formulations do not explicitly represent procedural roles or task-dependent context, even though surgeons identify instruments according to their function in a workflow. A query-conditioned formulation and benchmark are needed for context-dependent, semantically grounded segmentation.
method: SIRA formulates surgical instrument segmentation as query-conditioned inference under procedural context. It introduces the SurgRS dataset, pairing instance masks with structured query-answer supervision, and uses a multimodal architecture that separates target-level from query-level semantics. Query-anchored dual alignment aligns query meaning with visual features and segmentation prompts to improve semantic consistency in mask prediction.

title: Situational context embedding and knowledge-based grounding for LLMs in surgical training assistance
motivation: Simulation-based surgical training enables scalable practice, but trainees still lack timely clarification, contextual explanations, and individualized feedback without an instructor. LLMs could provide conversational guidance, yet generic systems may hallucinate, give nonspecific recommendations, and fail to use the simulator’s current phase and spatial state. A tutor grounded in both live simulator context and curated surgical knowledge is needed for safer, more relevant assistance.
method: The tutoring system derives structured situational context from serialized simulator states, including workflow phase, procedural targets, and spatial relations, and converts it into anatomically meaningful descriptions. It combines this context with simulator documentation and curated THA textbook knowledge through retrieval-augmented generation. An evidence-first policy with calibrated abstention limits unsupported answers, and the system is compared with a general LLM and expert references in a blinded surgeon study.

title: SkepticalNet: A Safety-Aware Interactive Segmentation Framework for Neuro-Oncology
motivation: Brain-lesion segmentation must generalize across tumor types, ages, and treatment conditions, but specialist automated models do not cover these domain shifts. Interactive foundation models offer broader applicability yet often process single modalities and exhibit trigger-happy behavior, hallucinating structures whenever a prompt is placed on healthy tissue. Neuro-oncology therefore needs a multimodal 3D interactive model with an explicit safety prior that can reject invalid guidance.
method: SkepticalNet extends nnInteractive with a native 3D residual U-Net that accepts four MRI modalities together with interaction maps. Its training dynamically samples atomic or composite lesion targets and alternates valid foreground supervision with a background branch whose target is an empty mask, teaching the model to reject prompts on healthy tissue while correcting boundary errors. The protocol also uses topology-aware interaction simulation and negative reinforcement near lesions.

title: Skill-Evolving Grounded Reasoning for Free-Text Promptable 3D Medical Image Segmentation
motivation: Free-text promptable 3D segmentation could match the unstructured language used in imaging orders and reports, but small differences in abbreviations, synonyms, or institutional phrasing can produce unstable masks. Larger vocabularies or stronger fusion do not ensure that ambiguous language is aligned with patient-specific anatomy, and purely linguistic reasoning is insufficient without visual evidence. The task needs an explicit reasoning process that grounds intent in images and can adapt to new linguistic variations.
method: SEER first builds the SEER-Trace dataset with diverse clinical requests, image-grounded evidence, rationales, executable target representations, and explicit skills such as synonym normalization and spatial reasoning. At inference, a vision-language model decomposes each request into evidence, rationale, and an answer that specifies the target for a frozen segmentation system. SEER-Loop retrieves and distills high-reward grounded reasoning episodes into reusable artifacts in SEER-Bank, enabling progressive self-refinement against linguistic variation.

title: Skin2Mind: A Multimodal Framework for Mental Health Risk Screening via Facial Images and Structured Skin Reports

categories.value: Multimodal Integration with Clinical / Genomic / Biomarkers

motivation: Mental-health screening mainly depends on self-report and interviews, which can be affected by recall bias, social desirability, and limited insight. Although the skin-brain axis suggests that psychological states may produce measurable facial skin phenotypes, existing dermatology studies do not directly link quantitative features to individual-level, standardized psychiatric risk labels. A multimodal framework is needed to model this relationship while handling redundancy among co-acquired images and reports.
method: Skin2Mind encodes multispectral facial images with a dermatology foundation model and structured skin reports with an LLM. Its Hierarchical Anchor Residual Fusion uses UV imagery as the stable anchor, injects white-light and cross-polarized cues through gated residual pathways, and then adds text features to the unified image representation through another gated fusion. A semantic Leave-One-Feature-Out analysis examines whether the learned decisions correspond to skin-brain-axis phenotypes.

title: SLICE-MIL: Counterfactual Semantic Anchoring of Disentangled Evidence for Child-Pugh Grading
motivation: Child-Pugh grading reflects hepatic reserve through heterogeneous biochemical and clinical factors whose manifestations on CECT are distributed across intra-hepatic remodeling and extra-hepatic sequelae. Slice-level labeling introduces noise, while conventional MIL can entangle regional signals and learn stage-correlated shortcuts without representing cumulative progression. A weakly supervised framework must therefore disentangle anatomical sources and explicitly anchor stage-specific evidence.
method: SLICE-MIL treats each CECT scan as a bag of slices and first applies Anatomy-Driven Dual-Query Attention to separate intra-hepatic and extra-hepatic signals using anatomical masks. Orthogonal filtration and residual routing decompose instance features into a compensated CP-A basis and incremental evidence pools associated with CP-A-to-B and CP-B-to-C progression. Representation-level counterfactual ablations impose a dominance order on these components, anchoring the ordinal staging logic and discouraging shortcut features.

title: SlideGuard: WSI Artifact Detection Benchmark
motivation: Physical processing, staining, scanning, and stitching can introduce many artifacts into whole-slide images, impairing both pathologist review and downstream algorithms. Although numerous QC tools exist, their comparative performance and cross-domain generalization have not been independently evaluated on a common, diverse dataset. A standardized benchmark spanning artifact, tissue, species, and source variation is needed to assess deployable WSI artifact detection.
method: SlideGuard assembles a cross-species, multi-source benchmark covering 11 artifact categories, six tissue types, and two species. It evaluates both pixel-level segmentation and patch-level classification methods after normalizing their outputs, comparing them with expert-annotated whole-slide images using Dice, accuracy, precision, and recall within tissue regions. The benchmark and standardized evaluation expose variation across artifact and tissue subgroups and support reproducible comparison of QC tools.

title: Slim nnU-Net: Revisiting nnU-Net Self Configuration from an Optimization Angle
motivation: nnU-Net is a strong medical-image segmentation baseline, but its over-parameterized 2D and 3D architectures require substantial memory and computation, limiting deployment on constrained hardware. Existing pruning methods typically rely on heuristic importance or redundancy measures and often require iterative pruning and retraining, without convergence or optimality guarantees. A training-integrated approach is needed to obtain hardware-efficient structured sparsity while retaining segmentation quality.
method: Slim nnU-Net reformulates nnU-Net training as proximal optimization with mixed L1 and group-L2 regularization. The individual term promotes weight sparsity, while the group term drives complete filters or channels to zero, allowing structural removal after a single integrated training process. This extends nnU-Net’s self-configuration principle to optimization and exposes a direct sparsity-accuracy control without heuristic pruning or retraining cycles.

title: SMART-KNEE: Sparse-Morphology Based Anatomical Reconstruction Using Topology-Aware Networks for Imageless Total Knee Arthroplasty
motivation: Imageless total knee arthroplasty must reconstruct patient-specific knee anatomy and align anatomical axes from sparse intraoperative landmarks without preoperative CT or MRI. Existing shape assumptions, statistical models, and imaging-dependent approaches can produce inaccurate morphology and axis estimates, compromising implant planning, sizing, and soft-tissue balance. A unified method is needed to complete landmarks and recover full femoral and tibial surfaces from minimal intraoperative data.
method: SMART-KNEE uses a cascaded anatomy-aware framework with two stages. A topology-aware E(3)-equivariant graph neural network completes the full femoral and tibial landmark sets from four intraoperative anchors, using Kabsch–Umeyama initialization, geometric message passing, and losses for positional and inter-landmark consistency. An anatomy-aware GAN then fuses the predicted landmarks with partial intraoperative point clouds to reconstruct complete patient-specific bone surfaces.

title: Smartphone-Based ASD Screening via Instance-Adaptive Cross-Modal Fusion and Contrastive Learning
motivation: Smartphone-based ASD screening could make assessment more scalable and affordable than conventional clinical procedures. However, mobile gaze data are corrupted by illumination, motion, calibration errors, and head movement, while ASD behaviors vary substantially across children; unimodal methods and static fusion therefore cannot reliably capture complementary cues. A robust approach must adapt modality contributions for each instance and learn from heterogeneous, limited medical data.
method: AMF-Net encodes eye behavior with two CNN branches that process fixation heatmaps and scanpath maps, while a temporal convolutional network represents yaw, pitch, and roll head-pose sequences. A Joint Representation Gating module models cross-modal interactions and assigns instance-specific weights so unreliable signals are downweighted. Cross-entropy is jointly optimized with supervised contrastive learning to improve class structure and generalization.

title: SONIC: Sonographer-Inspired Conceptual Explanation for Neural Networks
motivation: Automated fetal standard-plane identification can reduce the workload of ultrasound examination, but conventional DNNs rely on pixel patterns rather than the anatomical reasoning used by sonographers. Their black-box decisions provide little clinical transparency and may silently rely on implausible anatomy, limiting trust and deployment. An intrinsically interpretable framework is needed to ground predictions in clinically defined structures and support failure detection.
method: SONIC first discovers expert-validated anatomical landmarks with a prototype-based pipeline. It represents these concepts as graph nodes and their spatial dependencies as edges, then uses a graph convolutional network for fetal standard-plane classification. Graph attribution quantifies the importance of structures, while prediction–explanation consistency exposes anatomically implausible evidence as a failure signal.

title: SonoCLIP: Mask-Guided Region-Aware Vision–Language Pretraining for Fetal Ultrasound Analysis
motivation: Fetal ultrasound is essential for monitoring development, yet speckle noise, view-dependent artifacts, and operator dependence create substantial inter-observer variability, especially for subtle structures and in resource-limited settings. Existing vision–language models mainly perform global image–text alignment and often lack fetal-specific knowledge or sensitivity to clinically decisive local anatomy. A controllable foundation model is needed to align text with both overall views and localized structures.
method: SonoCLIP adds segmentation masks as an extra visual channel to the image encoder, allowing representations to retain global context while receiving explicit region prompts. It jointly learns global and region-level image–text alignment with a sigmoid pairwise contrastive loss that is less dependent on batch composition than softmax objectives. The model is pretrained on a curated 1.44M-image dataset covering 24 fetal ultrasound planes.

title: Source-Free Domain Adaptation for Medical Image Segmentation via LLM-Agent Collaboration
motivation: Source-free domain adaptation is needed to adapt medical segmentation models across institutions without sharing private source images. Existing methods can update too few parameters, rely on source-model pseudo-labels that accumulate errors under domain shift, or use a single SAM without semantic verification or reliability estimation. The adaptation loop therefore needs external semantic checking, multi-model correction, and mechanisms that suppress unreliable pseudo-labels.
method: RaMA uses a multimodal LLM as a cognitive meta-controller that checks segmentation semantics and produces spatial constraints such as points and boxes. These constraints guide a heterogeneous team of SAM3, MedSAM2, and SAM-Med2D agents, whose consensus corrections provide pseudo-labels instead of relying on one model. An LLM-derived reliability score, combined with agent agreement, weights self-training to limit propagation of noisy corrections.

title: Sparse Autoencoders for Interpretable Medical Image Representation Learning
motivation: Medical vision foundation models perform well but encode information in opaque representations that clinicians cannot directly inspect or verify. Existing SAE evidence is limited by single-modality or text-supervised settings, leaving unclear whether self-supervised models across CT and MRI naturally contain anatomy-aligned, interpretable concepts. A method is needed to expose such structure while preserving useful representation and retrieval capabilities.
method: The study trains Matryoshka Sparse Autoencoders with BatchTopK sparsification on frozen embeddings from BiomedParse and DINOv3, using a random-weight baseline to separate learned structure from architecture effects. Sparse features are evaluated for embedding reconstruction, downstream task retention, retrieval, and language-based interpretation. VLM- and segmentation-derived concept labels are grounded against a null baseline, enabling assessment of monosemanticity and zero-shot language-driven retrieval.

title: Sparse Local Latents for Explainable Zero-Shot Reasoning in Medical Vision-Language Models
motivation: Medical VLMs support zero-shot tasks but usually rely on global dense representations, making the evidence for predictions difficult to localize and interpret. Saliency and other attribution methods operate on entangled features and can be noisy or unstable, while integrating local sparse structure without damaging text alignment remains unresolved. A framework is needed to provide clinically meaningful local explanations and use them to guide predictions.
method: The framework obtains local, text-aligned image features from frozen MedSigLIP through both patch-based distillation and token alignment. A TopK sparse autoencoder decomposes these local embeddings into sparse latents that can be mined and interpreted using MedSigLIP text embeddings. Relevant latents are selectively recombined in the teacher embedding space to form classification probes that preserve zero-shot alignment while emphasizing localized evidence.

title: Sparsely Supervised Surgical Video Segmentation with Reliable Asymmetric Dual Memory
motivation: Surgical video segmentation spans long sequences where dense annotation is impractical, and sparse supervision leaves large gaps that promote error accumulation and temporal drift. Conventional VOS assumptions, per-frame models, and memory-coupled foundation encoders either miss multi-class semantic relationships, require dense labels, or limit adaptation under domain shift. A method must separately maintain short-term continuity and long-term semantic stability with limited labels.
method: D-GEM uses a DINOv3-based encoder with memory decoupled from feature extraction, enabling adaptation under surgical domain shift. A reliability-gated transient memory models short-term temporal continuity, while a bounded evolving anchor memory accumulates long-term class semantics and can discover classes absent from the first labeled frame. The asymmetric memories jointly support propagation and semantic stability under sparse supervision.

title: Spatially-Aware Graph Geometric Representation for Lung Nodules Detection
motivation: Pulmonary nodules are small, heterogeneous, and often resemble vessels or other normal structures, making early detection difficult and contributing to reader variability. Conventional convolutional and transformer detectors use fixed grids, receptive fields, or patch tokens and do not explicitly model irregular anatomical context, often requiring complex false-positive post-processing. A detector should represent non-local relationships among lung regions in a way that reflects radiologists’ structural reasoning.
method: The method represents lung parenchyma as a graph of anatomically meaningful superpixels and propagates information through non-local, non-rigid relationships. Each node uses a second-order embedding to capture local inter-feature covariance, and differentiable graph pooling learns a soft grouping into nodule and background representations. Orthogonality regularization encourages the two grouping embeddings to remain distinct, while a 2.5D setup tests the contribution of whole-slice context.

title: Spatiotemporal Modeling of Longitudinal MRI with Causal Graph Reasoning for Breast Cancer pCR Prediction
motivation: Early noninvasive prediction of pathological complete response to neoadjuvant chemotherapy could guide personalized breast cancer treatment, but longitudinal MRI dynamics are difficult to model in small cohorts. Many methods concatenate or difference time points, while 2D foundation models lose 3D continuity and correlation-based learning may confound treatment effects. A framework is needed to capture multi-scale spatiotemporal morphology and reason about causal relationships among imaging, biomarkers, and response.
method: The framework combines a biomedical foundation model with a Spatiotemporal-aware Attention mechanism. Multi-scale Adaptive Spatial-aware Attention captures volumetric tumor morphology across MRI slices, while Temporal-aware Attention models treatment-induced changes across longitudinal scans. A causal graph links imaging dynamics, clinical biomarkers, and pCR to support pathway discovery, counterfactual reasoning, and treatment-effect estimation.

title: Spatiotemporal Modeling of Tumor Dynamics via Optimal Transport for Enhanced Longitudinal Analysis
motivation: Longitudinal CT is important for monitoring tumor progression and treatment response, but patient follow-ups are sparse and irregular. Conventional augmentation and temporally conditioned generators can create realistic individual images while failing to explicitly constrain the trajectory of tumor shape change. A geometry-aware approach is therefore needed to generate anatomically plausible intermediate scans for trajectory-based analysis.
method: OxFlow first interpolates adjacent tumor masks along optimal-transport Wasserstein geodesics, creating mass-preserving, non-crossing intermediate shapes. It then conditions a ControlNet-augmented U-Net flow-matching model on each interpolated mask and a masked background, separating tumor geometry from appearance. The x-prediction flow-matching objective and tumor-region weighting support coherent CT synthesis along the trajectory.

title: SPEAR: Error-Guided Sparse Refinement for Scalable Deformable Medical Image Registration
motivation: Deformable registration establishes voxel-wise anatomical correspondence for longitudinal analysis, atlas construction, and image-guided intervention. Dense convolutional or attention-based models, including coarse-to-fine approaches, require substantial computation and memory on high-resolution 3D volumes and may require downsampling that weakens fine alignment. Selective refinement is needed to focus resources on anatomically misaligned regions.
method: SPEAR replaces dense multi-scale registration pyramids with progressive, region-wise sparse refinement. Segmentation-derived anatomical discrepancy signals drive Top-r routing toward misaligned regions, where structured sparse features update the deformation. A non-redundant routing constraint makes refinement stages explore complementary regions rather than repeatedly processing the same areas.

title: SpecF2M: A Spectral-Aware Multi-task Network Estimating Axial Length and Refractive Error from Pediatric Fundus Photographs
motivation: AL and SER are essential indicators for pediatric myopia screening and progression risk, but obtaining them requires dedicated biometry and cycloplegic refraction. Fundus photography is more accessible and reveals myopia-related posterior-pole changes, yet these cues are low-contrast, diffuse, multi-scale, and not identically related to AL, SPH, and CYL. Better component-aware and spectral-aware modeling is needed for screening-oriented estimation.
method: SpecF2M formulates AL, SPH, and CYL estimation as a component-level multi-task problem, using expert routing to combine shared and task-specific representations. It applies deterministic anatomy-guided enhancement to emphasize optic-disc/peripapillary, tessellation, and vessel-related cues. Its hybrid backbone combines multi-resolution wavelet modeling with Fourier-domain propagation to capture local and global spectral patterns.

title: Spectral-Semantic Consensus for Few-Shot Whole Slide Image Classification
motivation: Few-shot WSI classification has only slide-level labels despite gigapixel images, and diagnostically relevant regions can occupy less than 5% of a slide. Text-guided VLM retrieval can inject pathological knowledge, but averaging prompts loses semantic diversity and rigid image-text similarity can miss atypical disease patterns or select background. Patch selection must be both comprehensive and resistant to unreliable semantic matching.
method: SSC selects informative WSI patches through two parallel VLM-guided routes. DBPC distributes the patch-selection budget across shared learnable prompts and aggregates their consensus, increasing coverage of heterogeneous diagnostic evidence. SKP ranks patches by projection onto a principal subspace derived from textual priors, and uncertainty-guided fusion balances the two selections before cross-modal attention produces slide predictions.

title: Spectral-Temporal State Space Modeling on Functional Brain Networks
motivation: rs-fMRI functional networks can help characterize neurodegenerative and neurodevelopmental disorders by representing spatio-temporal brain activity. Static methods discard transient neural dynamics, while many spatio-temporal models separate topology from temporal processing or depend on heuristic sliding windows. A model is needed in which graph structure directly modulates multi-scale temporal dynamics without window selection.
method: SpecT-Mamba projects ROI BOLD signals onto low-frequency graph-Laplacian eigenvectors to form graph spectral coefficients. A learnable spectral-temporal kernel then jointly controls each spectral component's amplitude and frequency-conditioned temporal decay through mixtures of exponential memory scales. The resulting causal filter is expressed as a state-space model, enabling window-free, topology-guided temporal classification and interpretation.

title: Speech-Guided Multimodal Learning for Vocal Tract Segmentation in Real-Time MRI
motivation: Vocal tract segmentation in rtMRI supports phonetic research and clinical applications, but is difficult because of low contrast, rapid articulation, and limited spatial resolution. Synchronized speech can provide complementary information, yet prior multimodal methods do not explicitly align visual and acoustic representations and require audio at inference. This is impractical when MRI-compatible audio is unavailable or patients cannot provide reliable speech.
method: The framework uses phonological descriptors to construct subject-specific bounding-box priors for articulator localization. It pretrains visual and acoustic encoders with global and local cross-modal contrastive objectives, then fuses aligned features in a cross-attention decoder during training. Multimodal knowledge is transferred into the learned weights, so deployment requires only the rtMRI image.

title: SPHARM-Mamba: Rotation-Invariant Multiscale Modeling for Brain Age Prediction
motivation: Brain age prediction from cortical morphology requires modeling both local detail and long-range, spatially distributed age-related changes. Surface Transformers and Mamba models typically use patches, which add cost, create boundary and ordering issues, discard fine geometric information, and remain sensitive to rotation. A registration-free multiscale surface representation is needed.
method: SPHARM-Mamba projects dense genus-zero surface signals into spherical harmonics and applies spectral-domain convolution to integrate features within harmonic degrees. Degree-wise power aggregation converts the coefficients into compact rotation-invariant descriptors ordered naturally from global to local scales. Mamba blocks model dependencies across these degree-ordered tokens, followed by pooled age regression.

title: Spherical Clinical Embedding with Adaptive Multi-expert Fusion for AAA Rupture Classification
motivation: AAA rupture is clinically catastrophic, and its risk reflects complex geometry, tissue and texture heterogeneity, and patient clinical factors rather than maximum diameter alone. Single-modality or static fusion methods do not adequately represent these interactions and can degrade when clinical information is incomplete. A robust case-specific multimodal classifier is needed without relying on difficult biomechanical simulation.
method: XMoE combines a structured expert for geometric and region-based radiomics descriptors, a deep semantic expert for softly mask-modulated CTA slices, and a clinical expert. The clinical module jointly embeds feature values and missingness masks, reconstructs missing entries, and constrains the latent representation to a unit-norm spherical space. A unified cross-modal expert and confidence-driven, temperature-scaled routing dynamically combine expert logits for each case.

title: SpikeEEGformer: A Spike-Driven Transformer for Generalized EEG Recognition
motivation: EEG recognition is important for BCI, cognitive assessment, and clinical monitoring, but dense ANN computation is energy intensive and difficult to interpret. Although SNNs offer sparse binary processing and interpretable firing behavior, their spike-only feature extraction is limited, causing many systems to retain floating-point ANN-SNN components. EEG also requires robust joint channel-temporal modeling under temporal noise and sparse dynamics.
method: SpikeEEGformer is a spike-driven Transformer designed to avoid floating-point matrix multiplications in EEG feature extraction. Spike EEG Self-Attention jointly models channel and temporal relationships, while the Spatio-Temporal Spike Block links adjacent spiking states to reduce information decay. Latent Token Spike Attention provides multi-timestep, spike-friendly representation learning; firing behaviors and channel saliency are used for interpretation.

title: SpikeMamba: Spike-Driven State Space Models for Energy-Efficient Biomedical Sequence Modeling
motivation: Biomedical sequences such as ECG and EEG require expressive temporal models that can run continuously on resource-constrained edge, wearable, or implantable devices. Mamba-based SSMs scale linearly with sequence length but still perform dense full-precision recurrent MAC operations, creating substantial energy cost. A sparse event-driven implementation is needed while retaining temporal dependencies for predictive tasks.
method: SpikeMamba reformulates selective SSM recurrence as event-driven state transitions in the spike domain. It instantiates recurrent evolution with Leaky Integrate-and-Fire membrane dynamics, replacing dense MAC-heavy updates with binary accumulations emitted only on spikes. A state-dependent gate uses firing activity and membrane-potential variance to suppress redundant updates in inactive temporal segments.

title: Spinverse: Differentiable Physics for Permeability-Aware Microstructure Reconstruction from Diffusion MRI
motivation: dMRI can probe micron-scale diffusion barriers, but measured signals only indirectly reflect sub-voxel geometry. Existing compartment models provide voxel-level biomarkers without explicit interfaces and usually neglect permeability, while prior differentiable mesh inversion assumes a fixed topology. A permeability-aware method is needed to recover microstructural boundaries whose topology can emerge from the data.
method: Spinverse formulates boundary reconstruction as inversion of a face-wise permeability field on a fixed tetrahedral grid. A fully differentiable Bloch-Torrey simulator enables backpropagation from a signal-matching loss, with low-permeability faces recovered as interfaces by thresholding. Mesh-based spatial priors and a staged multi-sequence optimization curriculum regularize the ill-posed inverse problem and reduce local-minimum solutions.

title: SRMA-Mamba: Spatial Reverse Mamba Attention Network for Pathological Liver Segmentation in MRI Volumes
motivation: Cirrhosis assessment is important for prognosis and intervention, but biopsy is invasive and manual MRI delineation is labor-intensive and variable across observers. Pathological liver tissue has irregular, anisotropic anatomy, and existing volumetric methods insufficiently use intrinsic 3D spatial context. Linearizing a volume for Mamba processing can disrupt its topology and produce fragmented or poorly defined boundaries.
method: SRMA-Mamba is an encoder-decoder Mamba network for 3D pathological liver segmentation. Its SABMamba module rearranges volume features into sagittal, coronal, and axial planes, then uses anatomy-based selective scans and S6 processing to capture global spatial context efficiently. A Spatial Reverse Mamba Attention module progressively refines coarse maps using hierarchical encoder features, particularly improving boundary detail.

title: SRPAN: Implicit Neural Slice-to-Volume Reconstruction for Super-Resolution Pancreatic MRI
motivation: Pancreatic MRI surveillance is important for early PDAC detection, but routine acquisitions have high in-plane and poor through-plane resolution, limiting 3D assessment of small lesions. Existing SVR methods were developed for redundant multi-stack fetal MRI and rely on slice-level outlier rejection. Clinical pancreatic MRI commonly provides only two orthogonal stacks, where every slice is needed and local cross-view disagreement must be handled differently.
