method: SRPAN is an implicit neural slice-to-volume reconstruction framework tailored to two orthogonal pancreatic MRI stacks. It jointly optimizes per-slice rigid registration and a PSF-aware continuous image representation under heteroscedastic uncertainty. Cross-view gating assigns pixel-wise reliability weights, so localized inconsistencies are suppressed without discarding essential slices.

title: SS-IoSR: Self-supervised Intraoral Scans Repair
motivation: Raw intraoral meshes often contain holes, non-manifold edges, and disconnected components caused by reflective surfaces, limited access, and scanner limitations. These artifacts can require manual correction or rescanning, while generic point-cloud completion methods are poorly suited to nonuniform dental sampling and clinically important fine anatomy. Repair must preserve structures such as interdental and occlusal regions without hallucinating unsafe geometry.
method: SS-IoSR repairs localized intraoral scan defects with a self-supervised, patch-based hybrid completion framework. It learns geometric representations through masked autoencoding and uses a clinician-selected seed point to target the defective region. Explicit local geometric modeling is combined with implicit surface reconstruction, followed by differentiable Poisson-based refinement for continuous, faithful surfaces.

title: SSPT: Spiking Serialized Point Transformer for Couinaud Segmentation in 3D Medical Data
motivation: Couinaud liver segments are essential for anatomical liver resection planning, yet their virtual boundaries are defined by sparse vascular topology rather than visible organ contours. Fixed-grid volume models waste computation on sparse information, and point-based approaches often depend on hand-designed dense sampling or vessel rebalancing. Such manual manipulation can introduce bias and reduce robustness on raw clinical data.
method: SSPT is a spiking point-transformer architecture centered on Spiking Serialized Transformer Blocks. A Temporal Scanning Dispatcher maps unordered 3D points into locality-preserving space-filling-curve sequences and dispatches them into temporal spike steps; LIF neurons process this spatiotemporal flow. Spiking conditional positional encoding restores spatial information, while pulse-driven serialized attention replaces dense dot-product aggregation for efficient anatomy-aware segmentation.

title: Stabilizing Temporal Inference Dynamics for Online Surgical Phase Recognition
motivation: Online surgical phase recognition supports intraoperative monitoring and workflow assistance, but high frame-wise accuracy can still yield fragmented, unstable phase trajectories. Early errors can corrupt temporal states and cascade forward, while instantaneous decisions are vulnerable to transient confidence fluctuations despite transitions requiring accumulated evidence. Existing stabilization methods are often architecture-specific, and common metrics do not adequately measure within-segment instability.
method: The work introduces a model-agnostic Train-Inference-Evaluation framework for online SPR. During training, TEC reweights the onset of consecutive error runs to discourage temporal state corruption and forward error cascades. At inference, EGTP allows a phase transition only after sufficient accumulated evidence supports an alternative state; TFI evaluates instability-induced temporal fragmentation beyond frame-wise accuracy and token-based Edit Score.

title: Stage-Aware Adaptive Reaction–Diffusion Framework for Modeling Alzheimer’s Disease Progression with Tau and Amyloid-β PET Scans
motivation: Longitudinal tau- and amyloid-beta PET can quantify regional Alzheimer’s pathology, but sparse irregular follow-up and heterogeneous disease stage and pace make long-horizon forecasting difficult. Classical mechanistic models are interpretable but rigid, often assuming global diffusion and a single local reaction process. Pure neural ODE models better accommodate irregular observations but can sacrifice mechanistic transparency and stability.
method: STARD uses a stage-aware neural ODE that combines a connectome-constrained reaction-diffusion backbone with a structured local residual. It jointly learns subject-specific affine alignment from chronological to latent disease time, state-dependent ROI-wise diffusion modulation on a fixed connectome, and local negative-feedback and bounded logistic-gain dynamics. A lightweight gate conditioned on latent time and global burden balances mechanistic and local components.

title: STAMP: Subtype-Aware Spatio-Temporal Atlases for Personalized Prediction of Longitudinal Alzheimer’s Disease Progression
motivation: Alzheimer’s disease progression is heterogeneous, so discovering progression subtypes is important for clinical stratification and trial enrichment. Existing subtyping methods use low-dimensional scalar biomarkers and lose detailed spatial patterns, whereas image-based continuous-time models usually learn one shared trajectory without interpretable subtypes. A unified image-space model is needed to identify subtype structure and forecast personalized anatomical progression jointly.
method: STAMP learns a mixture of continuous-time spatio-temporal atlas trajectories directly from longitudinal 3D T1 MRI. It jointly estimates subtype weights, subtype-specific neural-ODE regional progression functions, subject-specific time shifts, and dense deformation fields conditioned on the mixed regional progression signal. A gating network uses baseline anatomy and clinical information for probabilistic subtype assignment, while regularization promotes stable, separated subtype usage.

title: Steer the Sampling, Not the Kernel Grid: Geometry-Guided Sampling Operator for Volumetric Segmentation
motivation: Volumetric segmentation requires accurate boundaries for lesion assessment and clinical planning, but thin, elongated, and anisotropic structures are especially vulnerable to small errors. Fixed-grid convolution and repeated downsampling can blur or alias fine detail, weaken orientation information, and propagate mistakes across scales. Existing approaches generally act on already sampled features or lack a unified, boundary-aligned treatment of refinement and downsampling.
method: GeoSample is a plug-in local operator that replaces both stride-1 refinement and stride-greater-than-1 downsampling in volumetric encoder-decoder networks. For each voxel, it predicts an SO(3) local frame and bounded step sizes, samples features symmetrically along the resulting directions, and converts paired samples into normalized directional and curvature-like cues with lightweight mixing. A rotation-consistent Consensus Field fuses encoder and decoder geometry fields at skip connections to align cross-scale features.

title: StrokeTimer: Robust Representation Learning for Ischemic Stroke Onset-Time Estimation from Non-Contrast CT
motivation: Acute ischemic stroke treatment eligibility depends on onset time, but onset is often unwitnessed and imaging must serve as a tissue-age surrogate. NCCT is routinely available but early ischemic changes are subtle, while real-world data are highly imbalanced and vary across centers, scanners, and protocols. Existing computational approaches often require manual lesion masks and methods addressing imbalance or domain variation separately are insufficient for this setting.
method: StrokeTimer is a fully automated NCCT onset-time classifier for three clinically relevant time windows. It combines reconstruction-based self-supervised disentanglement with independent semantic and style branches to learn pathology-sensitive features under scanner and acquisition variability. Energy-guided contrastive learning further refines representations for the long-tailed onset-time distribution without requiring manual lesion masks.

title: Structural Congruence Matters: Biological Pretraining for Vascular Graph Extraction
motivation: Vascular graph extraction provides connectivity and branching information needed to study hemodynamics, remodeling, and disease. However, expert graph annotation is expensive, and commonly used infrastructure pretraining supplies large but structurally mismatched priors. A biologically aligned source domain is therefore needed to reduce annotation demands while preserving vascular topology.
method: The method pretrains image-to-graph models on annotated botanical branching networks, whose growth and transport structure is more congruent with vasculature than infrastructure networks. It uses geometry-preserving graph representations, including border-aware edge clipping and degree-2 node retention, to retain local curvature and connectivity. The resulting biological priors are transferred to vascular graph extraction and evaluated across heterogeneous 2D and 3D domains.

title: Structural-Semantic Aware Information Reduction for Asymmetric EEG-Visual Alignment
motivation: EEG-visual alignment must match sparse, noisy neural signals with dense images whose backgrounds can dominate the semantic content. Existing data-driven compression lacks explicit structural guidance and can overfit superficial visual details, weakening generalization to unseen subjects and domains. The task needs modality reduction and alignment that reflect both visual structure and neural information granularity.
method: SAIR explicitly reduces visual information using Canny edges, monocular depth maps, and foveal blurring to emphasize structural and subject-relevant content while suppressing texture and background redundancy. Parallel encoders process EEG features at multiple granularities, and a structure-guided semantic modulation mechanism fuses them with the reduced visual representations. A hierarchical contrastive objective then aligns the two modalities for zero-shot retrieval.

title: Structure-Adaptive Sparse Diffusion in Voxel Space for 3D Medical Image Enhancement
motivation: 3D CT, PET, and MRI enhancement is clinically important, but high-resolution diffusion over volumetric data is computationally expensive. Latent, wavelet, or downsampled representations improve efficiency at the cost of high-frequency anatomical detail, while dense schedules contain redundant steps in conditional enhancement. A voxel-space method is needed that preserves detail while reducing training and sampling cost and adapting to heterogeneous anatomy.
method: The framework performs conditional diffusion directly in 3D voxel space on overlapping patches, predicting clean data x0 while using velocity-space supervision for stable gradients. It uniformly subsamples timesteps to form a sparse denoising trajectory, removing redundant steps enabled by the on-manifold target. A Structure-aware Trajectory Modulation module extracts local anatomical cues from the degraded input and recalibrates time embeddings at each U-Net block, adapting denoising to regional complexity.

title: Structure-Aware Sensorless 3D Ultrasound and Photoacoustic Reconstruction
motivation: Sensorless freehand 3D US and PA reconstruction could provide flexible volumetric imaging without external trackers, but long sequences suffer severe drift. Speckle decorrelation, acoustic clutter, probe compression, and out-of-plane motion destabilize feature matching, while coarse features miss useful microscopic motion cues. Robust tracking therefore requires separating unstable acoustic patterns and modeling reliable adjacent-frame structure.
method: SCC-Net combines a structure-aware channel decoupling module with bidirectional channel and cross-attention. Global spatial statistics guide adaptive filtering of modality-specific speckle and acoustic-clutter noise, while cross-attention establishes geometric correspondences between adjacent frames for stable tracking. Progressive training uses a motion-modulated MAE to emphasize dynamic regions, and bidirectional sequence consistency regularizes long-range reconstruction.

title: Structure-Contrast Disentangled INRs for Accelerated Multi-contrast MRI Reconstruction
motivation: MRI acquisition is slow, and supervised accelerated reconstruction requires large training collections that introduce data, field-strength, and domain-shift biases. Patient-specific INRs avoid external training data but generally lag supervised methods, and straightforward multi-contrast extensions fail to exploit shared anatomy efficiently. A reconstruction model is needed that uses complementary contrasts while remaining patient-specific and flexible to arbitrary contrast sets.
method: DISINR uses an encoder-decoder INR in which a SIREN-based encoder maps coordinates to a shared structure latent and a contrast embedding specifies the image contrast. These representations are combined through a bottleneck and decoded into contrast images, allowing complementary information to be shared across contrasts. Random masking of structure features during training encourages the network to learn a disentangled, reusable structural representation and support mixed acceleration protocols.

title: Subject- and Task-Aware EEG Foundation Model
motivation: EEG foundation models commonly use self-supervised pretraining but ignore available subject identities and task labels. Inter-subject neurophysiological variability and task heterogeneity can therefore produce unstructured representations that adapt poorly to new subjects and downstream tasks. Pretraining should exploit semantic labels to separate these sources of variation and improve transferability.
method: STEM combines self-supervised contrastive learning with supervised metric-based meta-learning in a shared EEG encoder. A decomposer separates encoded signals into subject-aware and task-aware features, with dedicated decoders supporting the corresponding learning objectives. This explicitly structures the latent space so task-relevant features are subject-invariant while subject-specific neurophysiological variation is modeled separately.

title: Subject-Specific Low-Field MRI Synthesis via a Neural Operator
motivation: Low-field MRI improves accessibility and cost but has lower SNR, resolution, and tissue contrast, limiting clinical utility. Large prospective cohorts are slow to assemble, while existing simulators based on noise and smoothing cannot represent nonlinear, tissue-specific contrast changes or realistic LF textures. A subject-specific simulator is needed to learn these degradations from limited paired HF-LF data for device evaluation and algorithm development.
method: H2LO formulates HF-to-LF synthesis as an end-to-end operator-learning problem over the continuous spatial MR signal. Its coordinate-image decoupled branch-trunk neural operator is tailored to preserve high-frequency 3D structure while modeling field-strength-dependent intensity and texture degradation. Pointwise intensity fidelity and gradient regularization train the operator from a small set of paired HF-LF scans, and synthesized data can augment LF enhancement training.

title: Sub-Resolution Monocyte Detection in Time-Lapse MRI: A Benchmark
motivation: Time-lapse MRI with iron-oxide labeling enables non-invasive study of individual immune-cell behavior, but manual detection is slow and error-prone. Monocytes occupy only 2–6 pixels, have variable appearance, and can resemble blood, air, or other artifacts, making conventional small-object detectors unreliable. The field also lacks a public dataset and standardized benchmark for reproducible comparison and design analysis.
method: The work introduces a publicly available 4D time-lapse MRI dataset with monocyte annotations, a fixed volume-level benchmark split, and an evaluation metric designed for 2–6 pixel targets. It establishes baselines using modern object detectors and systematically prunes YOLO detection heads, feature-pyramid levels, and loss terms. The analysis identifies which design components remain useful in the sub-resolution regime and under domain shift.

title: Sulcus-Aware Hippocampal Surface Modeling with Training-Time Sulcus-Guided Learning
motivation: The hippocampal sulcus is a thin internal indentation relevant to localized aging and Alzheimer’s morphology, but it is easily lost through partial-volume effects, mask-based extraction, and smoothing. Existing deformation methods can introduce invalid geometry, while reliable sulcus annotation is labor-intensive. A surface model is needed that preserves the sulcus, maintains fixed topology and correspondence, and avoids requiring sulcus masks at inference.
method: The framework builds a sulcus-preserving template and learns a dense, topology-consistent template-to-subject diffeomorphic deformation that is applied jointly to volumes and meshes. Sulcus masks, including a pseudo-sulcus cue, provide an auxiliary training-time signal to encourage alignment, while regularization limits geometric failures such as self-intersections. At inference, only the structural volume and hippocampus mask are required; the subject sulcus is obtained by propagating the template sulcus through the learned deformation.

title: SuRe-Flow: Surface-to-CT Synthesis via Retrieval-Augmented Rectified Flow for CT-Free Superficial Radiotherapy
motivation: Superficial radiotherapy still uses CT to obtain electron-density maps, adding workflow burden and ionizing exposure for often young patients. Generating CT from an optical surface is a fundamentally ill-posed 1-to-N problem because identical external topology can correspond to different internal anatomies, and standard rectified-flow training can average these possibilities. The method must constrain the internal solution while preserving the shallow interfaces that determine dose deposition.
method: SuRe-Flow encodes optical surfaces into a contrastive latent space and retrieves a topologically matched anatomical prior from a patient database. A ControlNet-conditioned rectified-flow backbone injects the retrieved prior to constrain the ambiguous surface-to-density mapping, while a dose-aware frequency loss preserves sharp superficial tissue interfaces important for electron dosimetry. This converts unconstrained synthesis into retrieval-augmented generation focused on the anatomy relevant to superficial treatment.

title: SurfMark3D: Surface-Based Graph Convolution Framework for Distal Femoral Landmark Localisation in Total Knee Arthroplasty
motivation: Accurate distal-femoral landmark localization is needed for morphometric measurements and implant planning in total knee arthroplasty. Manual annotation is slow and variable, while classical and volumetric or multi-view deep methods can be inaccurate, computationally costly, latency-limited, or modality-dependent. Coordinate regression and fixed isotropic heatmaps also fail to represent structural context and landmark-specific anisotropy and uncertainty.
method: SurfMark3D represents segmented distal-femur surfaces as point clouds and formulates landmark localization as dense probabilistic heatmap regression with learnable, landmark-specific Gaussian spreads. Its hybrid graph backbone combines Low-Rank Adaptive Graph Convolution for efficient local features with Bi-level Routing Point Attention for selective global context. Adaptive Wing and PointSTAR losses, with uncertainty-based multitask weighting, address localization ambiguity and anisotropic surface distributions.

title: Surgical Anatomy Recognition with Context Learning using Foundation Representations
motivation: Recognizing anatomical structures is essential for safe navigation and guidance in minimally invasive surgery, where limited viewpoints and no tactile feedback make perception difficult. Progress is constrained by the shortage of large, diverse, richly annotated surgical datasets, and existing anatomy datasets often have limited procedures, videos, or class coverage. Methods focused on tracking or other scene tasks do not adequately model procedure- and phase-dependent anatomical context.
method: The work introduces ATLAS-120k, a clip-level anatomy segmentation dataset with annotations from diverse procedures, modalities, and videos produced through expert labeling, propagation, refinement, and surgeon verification. The ATLAS video segmentation model combines surgical foundation-model embeddings with lightweight temporal and tracking components. It uses procedure type, surgical phase, and short-term visual memory as context to produce temporally consistent predictions while remaining suitable for real-time operation.

title: Surgical Video Temporal Grounding
motivation: Temporal grounding can support surgical reporting, complication review, and retrieval of training segments, but clinicians currently spend substantial time manually navigating long videos. General-domain grounding methods do not fit surgical workflows, which have a phase-to-action hierarchy and fine-grained semantics. Chunked processing improves scalability yet isolates chunks, losing continuity needed to distinguish continuing actions from new events.
method: The paper defines SurgVTG and the hierarchical multi-segment HMS-SurgVTG benchmark with nested grounding levels for phases, instruments, and action triplets. Its Memory-Augmented VLM processes long videos in scalable chunks while maintaining an explicit read-write memory loop. Lightweight heads dynamically update and inject structured procedural memories, preserving cross-chunk context for temporal grounding.

title: SurgLQA: Scalable Long-Horizon Surgical Video Question Answering
motivation: Surgical VideoQA should reason over procedures lasting tens of minutes or hours, where sparse critical events and causal relationships span multiple stages. Existing benchmarks mostly use images or short clips, while fixed uniform or sparse sampling can miss brief, clinically important cues and is costly for long videos. A scalable approach therefore needs precise temporal modeling, event localization, and query-conditioned reasoning under limited computation.
method: SurgLQA first applies Faithful Temporal Consolidation, using temporal-aware 3D convolutions, interleaved timestamp tokens, and an auxiliary retrieval objective to compress long videos while retaining temporal cues. Temporally-Grounded Multi-Policy Scaling then identifies query-relevant intervals and selects an adaptive sampling policy for each interval. The resulting query-conditioned sequence is passed to a vision-language model for answer generation.

title: SurgMark: Structure-Aware Watermarking for 4D Gaussian Splatting in Surgical Scenes
motivation: 4D Gaussian Splatting provides dynamic surgical scene representations useful for navigation, simulation, and training, making their authenticity and ownership important to protect. Watermarking methods for images, videos, and static 3D scenes do not directly handle continuously deforming anatomy and articulated instruments; naive parameter changes can create temporal inconsistencies. Perturbations can also damage segmentation features used for downstream surgical analysis and assistance.
method: SurgMark embeds watermarks in 4DGS while constraining changes with temporal coherence regularization that follows learned Gaussian motion trajectories. A motion-aware gradient weighting strategy adjusts watermark strength according to each Gaussian's motion magnitude. A segmentation feature consistency loss based on foundation segmentation models preserves semantic features for anatomical regions and instruments during embedding.

title: SurgOnAir: Hierarchy-Aware Real-Time Surgical Video Commentary
motivation: Real-time surgical understanding is needed for robotic systems and assistance because important decisions depend on subtle instrument and tissue changes. Most existing surgical video methods work offline or at coarse temporal scales, so they cannot react immediately as events unfold. Flat streaming descriptions also overlook the inherent phase-step-action hierarchy that provides contextual grounding and reduces ambiguity.
method: SurgOnAir is a streaming vision-language model that processes frames sequentially without future access and progressively emits narration tokens. It is trained with the hierarchical SurgOnAir-11k dataset, which provides temporally aligned action-, step-, and phase-level supervision. Interleaved multimodal tokens and explicit transition tokens let the model generate multi-level narration and signal workflow state changes online.

title: SurgRFO: Foundation Model Based Compositional Synthesis of Critical Retained Foreign Objects in Intraoperative Chest X-Rays

categories.value: AI for Neglected Diseases & Limited-Resource Settings

motivation: Critical retained foreign objects in intraoperative chest radiographs are rare, high-risk events whose subtle and occluded appearance makes reliable detection difficult. Positive cases are scarce, and standard or physics-based synthesis often leaves a domain gap from cluttered surgical radiographs or produces implausible combined images. More realistic synthetic examples are needed to train sensitive detectors and improve generalization.
method: SurgRFO uses two-stage synthesis. A surgical-domain fine-tuned Roentgen chest X-ray foundation model generates realistic RFO-free intraoperative backgrounds, while a lightweight U-Net learns localized RFO appearances from limited positive patches. Conditional Poisson fusion composites sampled RFOs at plausible locations and sizes, preserving photometric consistency for detector augmentation.

title: SurgVLA-Bench: Towards Evaluating Vision-Language-Action Models for Laparoscopic Surgical Robotics
motivation: VLA models could help surgical robots understand instructions and execute precise interventions, but existing models and benchmarks are designed for general robotics. Surgical deployment additionally requires domain-specific object discrimination, millimeter-level precision, and safety, while prior surgical datasets mainly assess perception rather than closed-loop action generation. A standardized benchmark is needed to evaluate the full visual-language-action pipeline and identify its surgical limitations.
method: SurgVLA-Bench is built in the SurRoL simulator with a hierarchical taxonomy from atomic actions to composite procedures and standardized multimodal trajectories. Its evaluation measures action precision, target discrimination and instruction following, as well as multi-step planning and spatial localization. The benchmark compares autoregressive and flow-matching VLAs, exposing capability differences and surgical bottlenecks such as restricted views and occlusions.

title: SurgZSD: Zero-Shot Surgical Action Triplet Detection via Attribute Composition and Clinical Feasibility Inference
motivation: Surgical action triplet detection provides structured instrument-verb-target semantics, but closed-set models fail when new instruments, anatomy, or actions appear across procedures. Existing zero-shot surgical approaches often provide labels without spatial localization, and general open-set detectors degrade because of the surgical domain gap. Clinical knowledge offers compositional visual attributes that can support recognition of unseen entities and clinically coherent triplets.
method: SurgZSD first fine-tunes Grounding DINO to spatially ground surgical instruments. Its Medical Knowledge-Guided Attribute Composition module uses a pretrained VLM to convert localized regions into structured medical attributes and compose unseen instruments, targets, and verbs. Clinical Feasibility-Constrained Joint Inference then optimizes Top-K triplets by combining visual parsing scores with medical compatibility penalties.

title: SurvTTA: Order-Aware Test-Time Adaptation for Heterogeneous Domain Shifts in Multi-modal Survival Analysis
motivation: Multimodal survival analysis supports oncological risk stratification, but cross-site deployment is harmed by equipment- and protocol-driven shifts that differ by modality. Survival predictions are ordinal, so matching absolute scores is inappropriate, and source data or target labels are often unavailable for adaptation. Existing test-time methods largely target classification, use modality-unified updates, or are unstable under noisy and conflicting guidance.
method: SurvTTA adapts pretrained multimodal survival models at test time using unlabeled target data while preserving invariant risk ordering. An order-aware regularization maintains topological consistency of relative survival risk, and modality-decoupled alignment balances adaptation across modalities with different shifts. Uncertainty-aware gradient correction suppresses unreliable samples and conflicting objectives to stabilize update magnitude and direction.

title: SutureFormer: Learning Surgical Trajectories via Goal-Conditioned Offline RL in Pixel Space
motivation: Predicting needle trajectories from endoscopic video could support anticipatory planning and safer robot-assisted suturing. Existing methods commonly require robot kinematics that are unavailable in many recordings and do not transfer across platforms, while dense frame-level trajectory annotations are costly. A pixel-based approach using sparse supervision is therefore needed to make trajectory prediction more transferable and practical.
method: SutureFormer reformulates surgical trajectory prediction as goal-conditioned visual navigation in pixel space, using only endoscopic image sequences and sparse keyframe waypoints. A Spatial CNN and Transformer encode spatial cues and long-range temporal context, while an autoregressive policy predicts waypoint directions and continuous step magnitudes. Offline Conservative Q-Learning with confidence-weighted rewards, behavioral-cloning regularization, and magnitude supervision enables stable learning from expert demonstrations without kinematics or dense labels.

title: SwallowReg: SAM-Assisted Deformable Registration with Adaptive Global-Local Features for Cine-MRI Swallowing Function Quantification
motivation: Quantifying tongue motion is important for evaluating postoperative swallowing function in tongue-cancer patients, and cine-MRI offers radiation-free, high-spatiotemporal-resolution imaging. Manual contouring is slow and observer-dependent, while automatic registration can fail under large deformation and intensity-similar neighboring tissues because it lacks tongue-specific semantics. The task requires registration that preserves both fine tongue boundaries and globally coordinated motion.
method: SwallowReg is an end-to-end joint segmentation-registration framework that uses SAM-derived semantic priors to guide tongue deformation estimation in cine-MRI. A SAM Feature Adaptor combines a frozen SAM image encoder, learnable CNN adaptation, U-Net multi-scale reconstruction, and deep supervision to produce hierarchical anatomical features. The registration network uses parallel DCNv3 and Swin Transformer branches with bidirectional coordinate-attention fusion, while an EdgeWeightedIoU loss emphasizes anatomical boundaries and joint losses couple segmentation with registration.

title: SWoMo: Neuro-Symbolic World Model for Cataract Surgery Simulation
motivation: Realistic cataract-surgery simulation is needed for novice training and interactive autonomous-agent development. Existing surgical world models often trade off visual realism, physically grounded tool-tissue interactions, and generalization to unseen geometries or workflows; video generators also lack fine-grained action control. A model that explicitly represents dynamics while preserving realistic appearance is needed for clinically useful simulation.
method: SWoMo decouples surgical interaction dynamics from visual appearance through a neuro-symbolic world model. A rule-based simulator and scene graphs represent tool-tissue motion, geometry, and constraints, while a diffusion model synthesizes realistic textures and tissue deformation. An inverse pairing procedure replays motions extracted from real videos in the simulator to create paired data for training video-to-video sim-to-real translation, with optional initial-frame or style conditioning.

title: SymmDiff: Symmetry-Guided Diffusion for Fracture Localization in Pelvic Radiographs
motivation: Pelvic-fracture localization on radiographs is difficult because anatomy overlaps, acquisition varies, and fracture cues may be subtle and asymmetric. Unsupervised anomaly detection can avoid extensive abnormal annotations, but generic reconstruction methods confuse normal anatomical variability with pathology and may miss microfractures. Because radiologists use bilateral comparison, contralateral consistency should be built into the diffusion correction process rather than applied only after reconstruction.
method: SymmDiff is a symmetry-aware latent diffusion framework that pairs anatomically corresponding left and right pelvic regions and injects contralateral information into every reverse-diffusion transition. It generates a patient-specific pseudo-healthy reconstruction by suppressing fracture-related asymmetries while preserving global anatomy. ROI-guided updates and contralateral latent-swap initialization focus denoising on regions with elevated bilateral discrepancy, and fractures are localized from input-reconstruction residuals.

title: Synergistic Information Disentanglement for Omni-Modal Slide Representation Learning in Computational Pathology

categories.value: Multimodal Integration with Clinical / Genomic / Biomarkers

motivation: Whole-slide representation learning could benefit from combining histology with genomic profiles and clinical reports, but many methods underuse reports and force modalities into a shared contrastive space. This alignment favors redundant information and can discard synergistic diagnostic signals that emerge only from joint observation. A task-agnostic objective is needed to preserve complementary cross-modal interactions for generalizable slide representations.
method: Φ-OMNI encodes histology, genomics, and clinical reports with domain-specific encoders and integrates them through a Synergistic Information Bottleneck. Its ΦID objective, implemented with a Gaussian Canonical Projector, suppresses shared redundancy while maximizing irreducible cross-modal synergy in the latent space. The resulting omni-modal representation is distilled into a slide encoder for robust unimodal few-shot use.

title: Synergistic Perception-Reasoning Governance: Grounding Medical MLLMs with Verifiable Anatomical Evidence
motivation: Medical MLLMs can produce fluent VQA answers or reports that conflict with imaging evidence, making hallucinations a barrier to trustworthy clinical use. Existing inference-time mitigations mainly calibrate internal statistics or require extra training, retrieval, or multi-stage verification, and they lack explicit anatomical grounding across tasks. A lightweight method is needed to anchor both visual perception and language reasoning to verifiable image evidence.
method: SPRG is a training-free inference framework that injects verifiable anatomical evidence on both perception and reasoning sides of medical MLLMs. ROI priors from MedSAM modulate visual activations, while anatomical coordinates are converted into discrete semantic tokens that serve as external memory for textual reasoning. A task-aware dynamic router selects modality-specific interventions according to task semantics to balance grounding and language fluency.

title: SynHydro: Biomechanics-Driven Domain Randomization for Hydrocephalus-Agnostic, Generalizable Tissue-Ventricle Segmentation Across Age, Modality, and Resolution
motivation: Pediatric hydrocephalus requires joint segmentation of ventricles and brain tissues for diagnosis and longitudinal monitoring. Severe deformation, evolving myelination, and heterogeneous MRI modalities and resolutions make existing models, which are often ventricle-only and protocol-specific, poorly generalizable. Labor-intensive pathological annotations are scarce, motivating synthetic training data that cover diverse anatomies and acquisition conditions.
method: SynHydro first applies a biomechanics-driven deformation module to healthy tissue labels to synthesize hydrocephalus anatomies with varied severity. A domain-randomized image synthesizer then generates multi-contrast MRI with varied contrast, noise, resolution, and artifacts, producing paired tissue-ventricle labels and images. A standard nnU-Net trained only on this synthetic cohort learns a single segmentation model intended to generalize across age, modality, resolution, and disease severity.

title: SynMamba: Synergizing Visual Mamba with Synthesized Clinical Semantics for Boundary-Aware Segmentation
motivation: Medical segmentation can improve by integrating images with clinical text, but high-quality image-text pairs are scarce. Existing backbones also have complementary weaknesses: CNNs miss global context, Transformers are costly, and Mamba-based models may lose fine local details. A model is needed that combines efficient global and precise local modeling while retaining semantic guidance when text prompts are absent.
method: SynMamba uses a dual-branch backbone that combines Visual Mamba for efficient global modeling with CNN features for fine local and boundary details, connected through a semantic interaction bottleneck. A rule-based modality-synthesis framework converts target masks into hallucination-free clinical narratives, injecting clinical semantics during training even when valid text is unavailable at inference. Boundary-aware supervision further emphasizes accurate lesion and tissue edges.

title: SYNPRED: A Synergistic Approach to Multimodal Learning for Clinical Prediction

categories.value: Multimodal Integration with Clinical / Genomic / Biomarkers

motivation: Imaging and molecular data describe complementary aspects of disease, but alignment-based multimodal methods mainly capture shared information and underrepresent modality-specific signals that may be predictive. They also provide limited support for missing modalities. A structured generative model is needed to separate shared, complementary, and irrelevant variation so multimodal synergy can improve both multimodal and unimodal prediction.
method: SYNPRED is a synergistic multimodal VAE that factorizes each modality into shared task-relevant, modality-specific task-relevant, and task-irrelevant instance-specific latent components. Shared task-relevant posteriors are combined with a mixture-of-experts, while reconstruction and task-conditioned KL objectives structure the latent factors; prediction combines embeddings with a product-of-experts. This design explicitly preserves complementary signals and supports prediction when one or more modalities are missing at test time.

title: TAIR: Text-Guided Adaptive Prompt Refinement for Coarse-to-Fine all-in-One Medical Image Restoration
motivation: Medical images suffer from diverse degradations across MRI, CT, and PET, motivating one model that can handle multiple restoration tasks. Existing all-in-one methods infer task information only from low-quality visual features and usually perform a single-step mapping, which can confuse heterogeneous degradations and miss the balance between global structure and fine detail. Text can provide explicit task and process guidance, but text-guided all-in-one medical restoration remains largely unexplored.
method: TAIR performs all-in-one restoration in two stages using dual-level textual prompts: a task-level prompt specifies what to restore, and coarse or fine instructions specify how to restore it. In the coarse phase, a composite prompt combines task text, a coarse instruction, and degradation-related visual cues to recover global structure; the resulting intermediate image helps form a fine composite prompt for texture refinement. An adaptive multi-prompt interaction module weights prompt contributions, and a text-driven quality-aware loss aligns outputs with high-quality descriptions while suppressing low-quality associations.

title: Task-Performance Routing for Multi-teacher Distillation in CT Medical Image Segmentation
motivation: CT organ segmentation benefits from large pretrained models, but different teachers excel at different organs and spatial regions because of their training objectives and data. Existing multi-teacher distillation usually uses global or instance-level weights and does not model the spatial heterogeneity of CT volumes, including changing contrast, boundary ambiguity, and morphology. A region-aware method is therefore needed to fuse complementary teacher knowledge without increasing inference cost.
method: Task-Performance Routing (TPR) distills multiple independently pretrained CT teachers by routing each spatial region according to observed prediction errors. It uses fine-grained routing in shallow layers for boundary detail and coarse routing in deep layers for semantic coherence, selecting stronger teachers in difficult regions while promoting complementary fusion in easier ones. The routing is parameter-free and integrated into hierarchical distillation without adding inference overhead.

title: TAVR-VLM: Risk-Conditioned Causal Grounding for Hallucination-Resistant Report Generation
motivation: TAVR planning requires linking global procedural risk to precise anatomical findings in 3D CT, echocardiography, and clinical data because small assessment errors can cause severe complications. Medical multimodal language models often generate plausible but unsupported findings, since dense visual attention does not ensure that each clinical statement is anchored to risk-relevant evidence. A causal, anatomically grounded generation mechanism is needed to reduce hallucinations and support reliable reports.
method: TAVR-VLM introduces Risk-Conditioned Causal Grounding Attention (R-CGA), a three-stage Risk→Region→Word pathway for multimodal report generation. A joint embedding predicts a procedural risk distribution and forms a causal risk bottleneck, which attends to CT tokens to produce a global risk mask and activated visual features. During autoregressive decoding, token-level attention for salient clinical entities is projected onto the risk-defined support, with a causal consistency objective penalizing attention outside that support.

title: TCCT: Trajectory-Conditioned CBCT Reconstruction for Sinusoidal Non-circular Orbits with a Fourier Neural Operator
motivation: Robotic CBCT can use non-circular trajectories to improve coverage and reduce artifacts, but conventional FBP assumes circular geometry and cannot model view-dependent redundancy. Iterative reconstruction supports arbitrary trajectories but is too computationally expensive for real-time use, while prior learned operators require retraining for each trajectory. A trajectory-conditioned, efficient reconstruction method is needed for varying robotic acquisitions.
method: TCCT conditions a spectral neural operator on sinusoidal source trajectories to predict view- and detector-dependent redundancy weights as continuous functions of geometry. The predicted weights are refined by a lightweight CNN and inserted into a differentiable shift-variant FBP pipeline. End-to-end reconstruction-driven training on simulated volumes learns the weighting without ground-truth redundancy labels, allowing one model to handle trajectories within the target orbit family.

title: TCFD-Net: Temporal-Calibrated Feature Disentanglement Network for Dual-Timepoint CT-Based Immunotherapy Response Prediction in Advanced Non-small Cell Lung Cancer
motivation: Early immunotherapy response prediction in advanced non-small cell lung cancer requires longitudinal CT because baseline images alone cannot capture evolving tumor changes. Existing shared-feature approaches entangle stable anatomy with treatment-induced dynamics, allowing dominant static signals to suppress subtle predictive changes. Irregular clinical scan intervals add further timing-related confounding, motivating explicit disentanglement and interval-aware calibration.
method: TCFD-Net explicitly factorizes longitudinal CT representations into temporal-invariant and temporal-variant subspaces using a Temporal Invariant-Variant Disentanglement Module. Cross-time MSE consistency, batch distance, and subspace orthogonality losses supervise the separation and encourage discriminative treatment-induced signals. A Time-Gating Mechanism then calibrates variant features according to inter-scan intervals, reducing confounding from irregular follow-up timing before response prediction.

title: TC-SSA: Token Compression via Semantic Slot Aggregation for Gigapixel Pathology Reasoning

categories.value: Multimodal Integration with Clinical / Genomic / Biomarkers

motivation: Gigapixel whole-slide images contain more than 10^5 patches, making direct processing by standard Transformer-based vision-language models exceed memory and context limits. Spatial sampling can discard rare but diagnostically important regions, whereas retaining broad evidence with sparse attention is expensive. The task therefore needs a fixed-budget compression strategy that preserves global diagnostic context while reducing visual token count.
method: TC-SSA compresses all WSI patch features into a fixed set of learnable semantic slots before vision-language reasoning. A gating network assigns each patch to at most two slots through sparse Top-2 routing, and weighted pooling aggregates routed patches into slot embeddings that are refined by independent MLPs. Soft load balancing, entropy, and z-loss regularization stabilize slot usage and prevent collapse while retaining global slide coverage under a strict token budget.

title: TEDi: Temporal Memory-Enhanced and Denoising Transformer for Surgical Instrument Segmentation
motivation: Accurate surgical instrument segmentation supports tracking, pose estimation, and other computer-assisted surgery tasks. Query-based models often localize instruments well but make category errors, including confusion between similar instruments and inconsistent labels for the same instance across adjacent frames. Predominantly frame-wise supervision fails to use temporal cues as stable semantic priors, motivating explicit cross-frame memory and consistency modeling.
method: TEDi adds temporal memory and denoising to query-based surgical instrument segmentation. A query-level memory bank and memory-search encoder retrieve discriminative representations from historical frames to enrich current queries. A window-based Temporal Consistency Denoising decoder builds an identity-aligned, temporally stable reference and corrects unreliable query representations across frames.

title: TeDyS: Temporal Dynamics with Spatial Context for Longitudinal Progression Prediction
motivation: Longitudinal progression prediction must detect subtle disease changes despite scan variability and irregular visit timing. Pairwise or difference-based methods fragment multi-visit evolution and are sensitive to spatial mismatch, while sequence aggregators often entangle short-term changes with long-term trends and acquisition variation. A unified framework is needed to model both temporal context and meaningful change across heterogeneous follow-up intervals.
method: TeDyS represents each visit with spatial slot tokens and updates a compact set of temporal queries using explicitly decomposed dynamics. Short-term dynamics are aligned residual changes between adjacent visits, while long-term dynamics are baseline-referenced deviations conditioned on elapsed time. Fused dynamics and visit-specific spatial context guide query updates, enabling evidence accumulation across irregular follow-up without mixing short- and long-range signals implicitly.

title: Temporal Phase-Difference Guided Spatiotemporal Learning for DSA Vessel Segmentation
motivation: DSA vessel segmentation is important for intraoperative visualization and quantitative endovascular assessment, but thin branches and residual soft-tissue or bone structures make segmentation difficult. Although existing methods model temporal sequences, they usually treat temporal information implicitly and do not explicitly represent contrast-agent propagation, which is the main source of vessel visibility. A method that combines interpretable flow dynamics with spatial vessel structure is needed, especially for distal and low-contrast vessels.
method: The framework forms a forward phase-difference projection that converts contrast-induced temporal intensity changes into a spatial prior, enhancing vessels and suppressing stable background and bone signals. A Mamba-based temporal encoder models long-range contrast-flow dependencies with linear complexity, while MinIP supplies complementary coarse vessel structure. A lightweight domain-aware fusion module combines these priors with temporal features before decoding the segmentation.

title: Testable Concept Bottlenecks for Pretreatment pCR Prediction in Breast DCE-MRI: Faithfulness and Reliability
motivation: Pretreatment pCR prediction from breast DCE-MRI can inform neoadjuvant treatment decisions, but the pretreatment-only setting must infer response from baseline phenotypes without early treatment changes. Common post-hoc heatmaps are difficult to validate through controlled interventions and may be unstable under perturbations, while medical concept labels are scarce. A predictor is needed that offers radiologist-readable evidence with testable faithfulness and case-level reliability.
method: The method freezes a 3D ResNet feature extractor and learns a lightweight projection-based concept bottleneck into a biomedical text-embedding space. Thirteen BI-RADS-style concepts are encoded with a frozen PMC-CLIP text encoder, and cosine similarities between projected image features and concept embeddings provide concept scores for a pCR prediction head. Faithfulness is tested by zeroing top-ranked concepts against random controls, while reliability is measured by concept stability under test-time augmentation and coverage–performance subset analysis.

title: Test-Time Adaptation for ECG Classification via SQI-Gated Self-training and Beat-Rhythm Consistency
motivation: ECG classifiers can degrade when acquisition devices and patient populations differ between training and deployment, while retraining for every target domain is impractical. Generic test-time adaptation may update on artifact-corrupted signals, causing drift, and often ignores the hierarchical beat morphology and rhythm structure underlying diagnosis. ECG-specific adaptation therefore needs reliability gating and physiologically structured consistency constraints.
method: BeatRhythm-TTA adapts a fixed ECG classifier online using unlabeled target signals through two components. SQI-gated self-training uses beat-wise signal quality and teacher confidence to block or scale updates on noisy segments, with an EMA teacher providing more stable pseudo-labels. Dual-level consistency enforces agreement between clean and augmented views at both beat morphology and rhythm scales, preserving ECG semantics during adaptation.

title: Test-Time Adaptation for Rare Surgical Phase Recognition: Bridging the Coverage-Gap Paradox
motivation: Automated surgical phase recognition performs poorly on rare phases occupying less than 5% of training frames, even when more rare-phase videos are added. Prototype dilution from diverse contexts and dominant common phases creates a coverage-gap paradox that class balancing, oversampling, and long-tail methods cannot resolve when class coverage is near zero. A source-free test-time strategy is therefore needed to adapt rare-phase representations during deployment.
method: The lightweight source-free TTA framework predicts with cosine similarity, applies confidence-weighted temporal smoothing, and updates rare-phase prototypes using an adaptive q-percentile pseudo-label threshold that avoids empty pools. It adds auto-guided frame selection with minimal annotation (B=5) while retaining compact prototypes under 20K parameters.

title: Test-Time Adaptation in Optical Coherence Tomography Using Trajectory-Aligned Time-Independent Flow
motivation: OCT analysis is sensitive to image-quality shifts from low-cost scanners, whose noise characteristics are rarely represented in training data. Existing test-time adaptation methods often rely on task-specific losses or pseudo-labels and are inconsistent for segmentation, while diffusion or flow approaches assume synthetic noise trajectories and can blur small lesions through downsampling. A method must align real-device noise with a usable generative trajectory without losing fine pathology.
method: TTA-Flow matches each incoming OCT image histogram to histograms sampled from synthetic reference flow trajectories before applying a flow-matching network. The flow network omits time conditioning so it can handle deviations between real-device noise and reference trajectory noise, producing higher-quality surrogates for downstream AMD biomarker segmentation.

title: Test-time Adaptation of Pelvic Bone Segmentation Models via Dynamic Reliability-Guided
motivation: Pelvic bone segmentation from CT is needed for robot-assisted pelvic trauma surgery, but cross-center imaging and population shifts degrade source-trained models. Online source-free adaptation is attractive because source data may be unavailable, yet existing methods accumulate boundary errors, neglect anatomical consistency, and are dominated by background voxels. Reliable pseudo-label assessment and target-specific supervision are required for robust adaptation.
method: ReGA estimates pseudo-label reliability with SICE, combining dropout-ensemble region consistency and boundary deviation, calibrated by confidence. Its trust-weighted feature refinement retrieves high-SICE features from a memory bank, while region-level contrastive learning enforces anatomical consistency; a teacher-student scheme supplies target-specific supervision under voxel imbalance.

title: Text as a Compass: Semantic-Navigated 3D Bone Collapse Prediction via Orthogonal Micro-volume Primitives

categories.value: Multimodal Integration with Clinical / Genomic / Biomarkers

motivation: Early femoral-head collapse prediction depends on subtle microstructural signs such as sclerotic-rim morphology and integrity rather than necrotic volume alone. Standard 3D CNNs dilute sparse pathological signals through isotropic aggregation, and existing vision-language models neglect clinical report priors or can form spurious text-image associations. A method is needed to retrieve fine-grained evidence while grounding it causally.
method: COMPASS represents local neighborhoods as tri-planar Orthogonal Micro-Volume Primitives, preserving sparse structural singularities such as sclerotic rims instead of averaging them volumetrically. A dual-stage optimization first aligns visual and report semantics to navigate from macro-regions to candidate micro-lesions, then uses counterfactual texts and hybrid supervision to verify causal lesion evidence and suppress spurious alignments.

title: Text as Illumination: Spatial Contrastive Retinex Learning for Language-Guided Medical Image Segmentation
motivation: Language-guided medical image segmentation can use clinical reports to reduce dependence on expensive pixel annotations, but existing methods either interact with text and vision implicitly or provide only coarse alignment supervision. These designs do not enforce fine-grained semantic consistency, so text guidance can fail to focus on the correct foreground and segmentation output. Explicit region-level alignment and background control are needed.
method: TIRNet treats text embeddings as semantic illumination at every decoder stage. Its Retinex-inspired Text Modulation Block produces positive and negative illumination maps to amplify text-relevant foregrounds and suppress background, while the Consistent Detail Compensation Block selectively restores high-frequency details using an illumination-reliability gate. Multi-Scale Illumination Supervision combines region-grounded contrastive and pixel-level background-suppression losses for explicit alignment.

title: Text as the Sieve: Information Bottleneck Guided Prototype Sieving for Text-Guided Medical Image Segmentation

categories.value: Multimodal Integration with Clinical / Genomic / Biomarkers

motivation: Pulmonary lesion segmentation benefits from diagnostic reports, but images contain far more redundant background than concise text. Existing pruning often removes textual tokens instead of visual redundancy, and late fusion lets background noise propagate through the encoder before language can intervene. Early visual information sieving with stable semantic reconstruction is therefore needed.
method: TeSi first compresses multi-scale visual features into axial prototypes and aligns them with report embeddings through Semantic Prototype Interaction. Its early IB-Sieve ranks prototypes by maximal text similarity and hard-selects informative visual tokens, routing discarded background information to a residual token. An asymmetric decoder with adaptive text fusion then refines boundaries while avoiding renewed visual noise and semantic drift.

title: Text Guidance and Distance Gating Improve Detection and Segmentation of Focal Cortical Dysplasia
motivation: Focal cortical dysplasia is subtle, heterogeneous, and often lacks clear MRI boundaries, so automated detection sensitivity remains limited even with surface-based graph models. Clinical workflows commonly provide suspected seizure-onset localization, but existing approaches do not use this prior to narrow the lesion search. False-positive clusters also limit specificity, motivating language guidance and distance-based filtering.
method: The model uses a pretrained MELD surface graph encoder and a language encoder, fusing cortical features with hemisphere- or lobe-level localization text through text-guided attention. At inference, a cluster-wise distance gate reuses MELD’s per-vertex distance regression to suppress false-positive lesion clusters. The framework also compares how different localization descriptions affect segmentation.

title: Text-Deficient Multimodal Stroke Segmentation with Lesion-Grounded Self-Retrieval-Augmented Generation
motivation: Acute ischemic stroke decisions require rapid infarct-core delineation on DWI and ADC, while preliminary reports provide useful lesion location and extent semantics. These reports are often missing or inconsistently archived in retrospective cohorts, limiting report-conditioned segmentation. A solution must recover clinically grounded text and use it alongside strong 3D image representations.
method: LeG-RAG normalizes lesion masks to an atlas, retrieves spatially concordant reports with a coarse-to-fine mask-driven strategy, and uses a multimodal LLM to synthesize missing preliminary reports without extra training. LLMSwin combines each report with learnable prompts for a frozen Llama-3-8B-Instruct text encoder, then fuses the text with multi-scale SwinUNETR features through two-way transformers for volumetric segmentation.

title: Text-Guided Multi-frequency Latent Diffusion for Medical Image Segmentation
motivation: Medical targets often have low contrast, ambiguous boundaries, and complex anatomy, making image-only segmentation unstable. Although latent diffusion provides generative priors, existing conditioning usually lacks explicit semantic and structural guidance, limiting boundary precision and global anatomical consistency. Text-aware frequency modeling is needed to provide complementary task semantics and structural detail.
method: TMF-Seg fuses image and text conditions with an Image–Text Conditional Fusion cross-attention module. A Text-Guided Multi-Frequency Enhancement module decomposes the fused representation into high-, mid-, and low-frequency components and reweights them according to textual context. The enhanced condition guides a latent diffusion U-Net for single-step segmentation, while the segmentation autoencoder and diffusion backbone remain frozen.

title: TGBD-Net: Tumor-Guided Bridging Distillation for Joint EGFR Mutation and Survival Prediction in Lung Cancer from CT Imaging
motivation: EGFR mutation and progression-free survival prediction from chest CT are clinically related tasks, but real cohorts often lack tumor annotations and do not provide both task labels for every patient. Shared-backbone multi-task models can therefore learn inconsistent representations across differently supervised subsets, while existing distillation methods mainly use fully labeled samples. A unified approach is needed to exploit partial labels and stabilize representation learning.
method: TGBD-Net uses a Swin-based Tumor-Guided Feature Extraction module to form a shared representation, aligning its tumor-guided feature with cropped tumor features when bounding-box annotations are available while retaining one path for unannotated patients. Bridging Distillation maintains EGFR- and survival-related attributes in shared anchors and transfers them to label-missing samples as similarity-weighted soft labels. The two mechanisms stabilize joint learning across heterogeneous supervision.

title: TGH-DB: Template-Guided Heteroscedastic Diffusion Bridge for Brain MRI-to-PET Synthesis
motivation: Amyloid PET supports early diagnosis and staging of neurodegenerative disease, but its cost, radiation exposure, and limited availability motivate synthesis from routinely acquired structural MRI. MRI-to-PET translation is ill-posed because MRI anatomy and amyloid accumulation are only indirectly related, while conventional diffusion processes discard spatial pathology priors by converging to isotropic Gaussian noise. A method is therefore needed that incorporates plausible population-level amyloid organization and regional variability.
method: TGH-DB builds a population-level amyloid PET template from voxel-wise cohort means and standard deviations, then uses a template-directed diffusion bridge with spatially heteroscedastic noise to model regional uptake variability. Its Time-Aware Evolutionary Denoiser uses parallel encoders, time-aware fusion, and time-modulated decoding to adaptively combine multiple MRI modalities during denoising. This design preserves stable pathology patterns while allowing uncertainty where uptake varies across subjects.

title: TG-OT: Topology-Guided CCTA-IVUS Registration via Optimal Transport Matching
motivation: Registering CCTA with IVUS could combine 3D coronary geometry and high-resolution plaque morphology, but differences in geometry, resolution, and artifacts make fusion difficult. Existing pipelines rely on precomputed lumen or vessel-wall segmentations, which are unreliable when IVUS acoustic shadowing from calcifications obscures boundaries. An automatic registration approach that can use robust topological cues without prior segmentation is needed.
method: TG-OT trains lightweight CNN detectors for calcifications, bifurcations, and lumen radii directly on the artery's (theta, z) cylindrical representation, avoiding explicit lumen or wall segmentation. Registration optimizes centerline warping using an unbalanced Sinkhorn optimal-transport loss with cylindrical spatial costs, supplemented by a lumen-matching term. The transport objective supplies informative gradients even when cross-modal detections are spatially disjoint and tolerates differences in feature mass.

title: The Learnability Gap in Medical Latent Diffusion
motivation: Long-tailed medical datasets leave rare but important conditions underrepresented, motivating latent-diffusion augmentation that can generate additional training data. Existing work emphasizes perceptual fidelity or domain-specific autoencoder tuning, assuming that faithful latents are easy for classifiers and diffusion models to learn. The paper investigates the resulting learnability gap, where discriminative information is preserved but organized in a way that impedes learning and weakens synthetic-data utility.
method: The study evaluates five autoencoder families across four medical benchmarks, comparing image-, reconstruction-, and latent-space classification to isolate latent learnability from reconstruction fidelity. It introduces noise-conditioned latent classifiers with FiLM layers and image-space teacher distillation as diagnostic probes and partial mitigations. These tools characterize how fine-tuning, distillation, and noise conditioning affect the gap while remaining efficient for filtering generated samples.

title: The Neuro-Developing Engine: a Surrogate Longitudinal Model for Infant Brain Dynamics Via Causal Distillation
motivation: Infant brain function changes rapidly and individually, yet most data-driven rs-fMRI methods describe static connectivity or predict longitudinal connectivity without mechanistic interpretation. Existing Neural Perturbational Inference models capture subject-specific dynamics only at a single scan time and cannot represent continuous developmental transitions or support intervention analysis. A longitudinal surrogate is needed to model age-driven evolution and identify region-specific influences on development.
method: NDE starts from individualized Neural Perturbational Inference surrogate models and learns age-dependent residual transitions between a younger and an older surrogate brain. A FiLM-conditioned generator embeds subject identity and age, while causal distillation, Jacobian-spectrum regularization, and soft-label contrastive learning encourage causal, age-sensitive residual representations. Region-level counterfactual developmental knobs then enable inverse-control simulations of how localized modulation changes future functional connectivity.

title: The Paper Has a GitHub, the GitHub Has a README, the README Has Nothing: Reproducibility Signals for Review Support
motivation: Medical-imaging papers increasingly depend on complex software, yet linked artifacts may be inaccessible, empty, incomplete, or promised only after acceptance. Reviewers cannot realistically execute arbitrary code, resolve all dependencies, acquire data, or reproduce GPU-heavy training, making reproducibility compliance difficult to assess under review-time constraints. A transparent tool is needed to perform objective artifact checks and distinguish verifiable evidence from missing or human-dependent judgments.
method: Paper-snitch parses manuscripts, resolves linked repositories, performs bounded accessibility and content checks, and applies policy-aware reproducibility checklists. It reports an interpretable verifiability score with sub-scores, criterion-linked excerpts, and inspectable artifacts covering items such as code, licenses, environments, weights, data instructions, and evaluation protocols. The workflow deliberately avoids executing untrusted code or GPU-intensive reproduction and presents results as reviewer decision support.

title: Think Global, Look Focal: Dual-Stream Retrieval-Augmented Pathology Report Generation for Whole Slide Images
motivation: Pathology report generation from gigapixel WSIs could reduce workload, but diagnostically important cellular details occupy tiny regions and are diluted when slides are represented as a single patch sequence. Retrieval-augmented methods also draw from redundant raw corpora and may indiscriminately fuse low-confidence evidence, causing morphology-inconsistent hallucinations. The task needs perception that preserves both slide context and focal lesions, together with confidence-aware medical knowledge retrieval.
method: DR-Gen separates WSI perception into a global stream for tissue architecture and a focal stream for diagnostic regions, then uses a Visual Priming Adapter to turn these features into slide-specific anchors for generation. It builds a CAP-protocol-guided diagnostic knowledge bank and applies Adaptive Confidence Gating to reweight retrieved evidence according to semantic confidence. Together, these components align report generation with morphology while suppressing low-confidence, non-diagnostic retrieval noise.

title: Through the Schrödinger Bridge: Benchmarking Antemortem Image Restoration from Postmortem Autolysis to Enhance Forensic Diagnostics
motivation: Postmortem autolysis irreversibly and stochastically dissolves nuclei, blurs boundaries, and disrupts tissue organization, reducing the objectivity of forensic histopathological diagnosis. Pixel-aligned fresh/postmortem pairs are practically unavailable, and the morphological changes violate assumptions of supervised, cycle-consistent, or appearance-only translation methods. Moreover, generic image metrics such as FID may not correspond to diagnostic plausibility, motivating a dedicated task, dataset, and clinically grounded evaluation.
method: AutoPath is constructed from adjacent liver tissue blocks, with one processed promptly and the homologous block exposed to induce autolysis, yielding nearly ten thousand unpaired patches across 69 cases. The work formulates restoration as a Schrödinger Bridge between autolyzed and non-autolyzed image distributions, allowing stochastic transport through large morphological changes without pixelwise pairs. It evaluates restoration with slide-level diagnostic distribution consistency, complementing image metrics that may not reflect forensic usefulness.

title: Through-Plane Attention for Anisotropic CT Super-Resolution Improves Quantitative Lung Cancer Analysis
motivation: Routine thick-slice CT has severe through-plane anisotropy that breaks airway and lobar continuity and can impair lung-cancer AI analysis. Thick-to-thin reconstruction is ill-posed because slice averaging irreversibly removes anatomy, while paired multi-scanner LR/HR data are scarce and better image metrics do not guarantee better downstream measurements. A robust super-resolution method must model inter-slice structure and be validated on clinically relevant quantitative tasks.
method: TVSRN-V2 extends volumetric CT super-resolution with an anisotropy-aware Through-Plane Attention Block that applies sagittal and coronal self-attention and learned channel-wise fusion to model inter-slice dependencies. Its hybrid training curriculum combines real paired LR/HR scans with synthetically degraded pseudo-LR volumes to cover heterogeneous scanner and protocol degradations. The framework is assessed not only by reconstruction quality but also through lobe and bronchi segmentation, histology classification, and survival modeling.

title: Time Matters: Rethinking Diffusion and Flow Models in One-Step Medical Image Translation
motivation: Medical image translation prioritizes fidelity and quantitative correctness, whereas the usual diffusion narrative emphasizes diverse sampling and iterative denoising. Multi-step stochastic sampling can introduce hallucinations or acquisition noise, and diffusion models may not outperform simple one-step regression in accuracy while still overfitting. The work asks whether the time-conditioned formulation itself provides useful regularization for reliable deterministic translation.
method: JiR retains the time-conditioned predictor from diffusion or flow modeling but removes stochastic noise injection, iterative denoising, and other unnecessary components, yielding a deterministic one-step translator. It redesigns the forward interpolant and prediction space for each task and adds a time-consistency loss that aligns predictions at intermediate times with the endpoint target. This treats the time variable as a trajectory-coupling regularizer and supports architecture-agnostic medical image translation.

title: Time-Grounded Clinical Prediction from Longitudinal Multimodal Patient Histories

categories.value: Multimodal Integration with Clinical / Genomic / Biomarkers

motivation: Chest X-ray VLMs are usually trained on isolated visits or short prior-current pairs, while real clinical interpretation requires integrating irregular, multi-visit histories. Non-monotonic courses such as relapse and remission make single images insufficient, and existing datasets rarely combine sequential imaging with reports, tests, and treatment decisions. A longitudinal benchmark is needed to measure time grounding, multi-event evidence aggregation, and decision-relevant prediction.
method: MIMIC-MTE organizes each patient trajectory into 3 to 10 timestamped events, pairing CXR images and untruncated reports with routine tests and explicit treatment plans. It defines next-event forecasting, interval-specific longitudinal question answering, and treatment-plan inference using temporally bracketing evidence. The paper benchmarks medical and general VLMs in zero-shot and supervised fine-tuning settings to establish baselines for time-grounded reasoning.

title: TinyH2GNet: Exploring Lightweight Models for Gene Expression Prediction from H&E Images

categories.value: AI for Neglected Diseases & Limited-Resource Settings

motivation: Spatial transcriptomics measures gene expression with spatial context but is costly, time-consuming, and dependent on specialized equipment. H&E images are routinely available and can reflect molecular tissue states, motivating image-based gene-expression prediction. Existing approaches use models ranging from small CNNs to large transformer and graph hybrids, leaving unclear whether greater complexity improves prediction or whether lightweight models can work in resource-constrained settings.
method: The study benchmarks representative CNN, transformer, and graph-based image-to-gene models under identical protocols, then constructs pruned variants of a compact CNN baseline. TinyH2GNet reduces model capacity to sub-million parameter networks while retaining the prediction pipeline, enabling CPU-oriented inference with much lower memory and computation. The design uses systematic capacity and efficiency analysis to examine whether architectural complexity is necessary for spatial transcriptomics prediction.

title: TissueCodePilot: A Code-Action Agent for AI-Assisted Spatial Tissue Analysis
motivation: Spatial tissue analysis is needed to quantify cellular microenvironments and tissue architecture, but most software exposes only fixed, predefined features. Missing analyses often require computational experts, creating delays, while combining image processing and machine learning makes custom feature extraction technically demanding. A system that can perform flexible analyses from minimal natural-language input and recover through execution feedback could make on-demand analysis more accessible.
method: TissueCodePilot is an environment-aware ReAct-style coding agent that iteratively interprets observations, updates a short-horizon plan, calls domain tools, executes Python, and uses interpreter feedback to revise subsequent actions. Its workspace exposes tools such as cell segmentation and classification, while intermediate artifacts and outputs remain available for later steps. The system is evaluated against one-shot and retry-on-error prompt-based coding agents using an expert-annotated benchmark of spatial analysis questions.

title: TOF-GR: Unsupervised PET Reconstruction via Time-of-Flight Gaussian Representation and Kernel-Based Prior Modeling
motivation: Low-dose PET reconstruction is highly ill-posed because photon starvation produces extremely low-SNR projection data, making small lesions difficult to restore. Supervised deep models require paired high-quality data that are costly to obtain and may generalize poorly, while self-supervised INRs suffer spectral bias and can amplify noise or blur lesion boundaries. An unsupervised representation is therefore needed that can recover local high-frequency structure while controlling noise and preserving anatomy.
method: TOF-GR represents the PET activity volume explicitly as controllable anisotropic 3D Gaussian primitives and incorporates the PET system matrix into differentiable Gaussian voxelization. A kernel matrix derived from MRI priors is integrated during voxelization to constrain the representation toward anatomically plausible structure. The reconstruction objective combines Poisson likelihood, kernel-based anatomical regularization, and a TV penalty for physics-consistent optimization under low-count data.

title: TOFlow: Learning-Based Isotropic Reconstruction and Flow Mapping from Multi-orientation TOF-MRA
motivation: TOF-MRA is widely used for non-contrast cerebral vascular imaging, but anisotropic resolution and orientation-dependent signal loss can obscure small, in-plane, or slow-flow vessels. 4D Flow MRI provides hemodynamic information but requires long, gated, low-resolution acquisitions that limit routine neurovascular use. A method that fuses multi-orientation TOF-MRA could improve isotropic structural depiction while estimating flow information without dedicated flow imaging.
method: TOFlow extends the NeSVoR implicit neural representation with multi-resolution hash-grid encoding, acquisition-specific uncertainty weighting, and task-specific output heads. It learns orientation-dependent magnitude components for isotropic reconstruction and signed magnitude-direction components for flow mapping, synthesizing each TOF-MRA observation by projection onto its slice normal. A streamline-consistency loss traces predicted vectors through vessel masks, penalizing directional changes and premature vessel exits to resolve sign ambiguity and encourage coherent flow.

title: Tooth Alignment via Virtual Trajectories with Clinical Constraints
motivation: Orthodontic tooth alignment is a prolonged process involving repeated evaluation and fine adjustments under patient-specific biomechanical conditions, not merely prediction of a final state. Most automated methods regress one rigid transformation per tooth in a single step and apply clinical constraints only to the final configuration, providing no supervision or assessment for intermediate movements. This can make complex multi-tooth alignment unreliable and inconsistent, especially when only pre- and post-treatment data are available.
method: The framework reformulates alignment as prediction of K incremental 6-DoF rigid transformations whose accumulation forms a virtual treatment trajectory. PointNet++ encodes tooth point clouds and an SSM-based sequential predictor estimates stage-wise SE(3) updates. Trajectory stabilization suppresses excessive displacement and collapse, intermediate-state re-learning supplies denser supervision, and clinical constraints are enforced at every stage for progressive refinement.

title: ToothFairy3: Scaling CBCT Maxillofacial Segmentation to 77 Classes with U-Mamba2
motivation: CBCT segmentation is essential for dental planning but manual voxel annotation is laborious and error-prone for thin, low-contrast, and variable structures. Public datasets remain fragmented, with limited dense labels, incomplete tooth and canal coverage, and insufficient representation of maxillary anatomy, hindering fair comparison and generalization. In addition, heavy 3D models and sliding-window inference create substantial latency for multiclass clinical workflows, so both coverage and efficiency must improve.
method: ToothFairy3 extends the public CBCT benchmark with 102 fully annotated scans and a 77-class taxonomy covering maxillofacial structures, tooth pulp cavities, and small neurovascular anatomy, while reserving a server-evaluated held-out set. U-Mamba2 uses a U-Net-style encoder-decoder with a Mamba2 state-space block at the bottleneck to capture long-range context with lower computational scaling.
