Domain-informed training incorporates dental knowledge to support multiclass segmentation across the expanded field of view.

title: Topology-Driven Transferability Estimation of Medical Foundation Models for Segmentation
motivation: Medical vision foundation models trained with SSL form a large model zoo, but the best encoder varies by downstream segmentation task. Exhaustive fine-tuning of every candidate is computationally expensive, motivating training-free transferability estimation. Existing classification-oriented metrics emphasize global statistical overlap or linear separability and may miss the local geometric and boundary structure that determines dense segmentation quality.
method: The framework estimates transferability without gradient updates by comparing feature and label manifold structure. Global Representation Topology Divergence constructs feature and semantic Minimum Spanning Trees to measure overall structural alignment, while Local Boundary-Aware Topological Consistency evaluates separability around anatomical boundaries. A task-adaptive fusion mechanism weights global and local scores according to target topological complexity to produce a model-ranking proxy.

title: TopoOR: A Unified Topological Scene Representation for the Operating Room
motivation: Operating-room reasoning involves irreducibly polyadic interactions among surgeons, robots, instruments, patients, and monitors, but surgical scene graphs mainly encode pairwise relations and therefore fragment joint spatial and kinematic constraints. OR data also span distinct manifolds, including 3D motion, robot kinematics, audio, and RGB features; tokenizing them into a shared latent space can discard this structure. A representation that preserves higher-order relations and multimodal geometry is needed for safety-critical surgical understanding.
method: TopoOR represents the operating room as a multimodal combinatorial complex whose cells encode entities and higher-order group relations, preserving relationships beyond dyadic edges. Its Higher-Order Attention Network propagates messages across boundary and co-boundary incidence neighborhoods with rank-aware attention, retaining modality-specific geometry instead of forcing all inputs into one latent space. The pooled representation supports joint downstream tasks such as next-action anticipation, robot-phase prediction, and rule-based sterility assessment.

title: TotalFM: An Organ-Separated 3D-CT Foundation Model Leveraging Large-Scale Routine Clinical Radiology Data
motivation: Building robust 3D-CT foundation models from routine clinical archives is hindered by unstructured reports, multiple heterogeneous series per examination, and unreliable whole-volume report correspondence. High-resolution 3D inputs also reduce batch size because of memory demands, while whole-report and whole-volume embeddings may lose fine-grained contextual and geometric information. A scalable strategy is needed to align clinical findings with anatomically meaningful CT regions while balancing resolution, batch size, and representation reliability.
method: TotalFM automatically converts routine CT studies and reports into organ-level volume–finding pairs by separating whole examinations into anatomically meaningful units. This granularity enables high-resolution 3D encoding with practical batch sizes and produces more specific image–finding correspondence for contrastive learning. The resulting foundation model is trained on a large collection of clinical CT series and organ-level pairs for zero-shot organ and finding analysis.

title: Toward Markerless Video-Based Tremor Analysis: Objective Quantification of Pathological Tremor in Mouse Preclinical Models
motivation: Objective tremor quantification in mouse models is important for studying Parkinson’s disease mechanisms and treatment effects, but visual scoring is subjective and contact-based sensors or motion-capture systems are invasive, costly, or restrictive. RGB cameras offer a non-invasive alternative, yet existing video approaches may miss subtle oscillations and tremors along the anti-gravity direction, especially from top-down views. A markerless method using ordinary cameras is needed to measure tremor severity during natural movement.
method: The pipeline processes side-view RGB videos with segmentation-based preprocessing and pose-derived body-part coordinates to isolate the mouse from background motion. A Move Detection Module separates voluntary locomotion from involuntary oscillations, while a Tremor Score Estimation Module sensitively quantifies subtle vertical vibrations into a severity score. The method is evaluated using videos synchronized with accelerometer measurements from unrestrained mice.

title: Toward Synergistic Learning for Liver Vessel and Couinaud Segmentations
motivation: Accurate liver-vessel and Couinaud-segment segmentation is needed for planning and navigating liver cancer resection. Existing methods usually treat the tasks independently or require manual vessel masks, even though Couinaud boundaries are determined by vascular topology and vessels are small, branching, and anatomically variable. An automated method must therefore model vascular geometry and use it to infer functional segments.
method: The framework jointly segments liver vessels and Couinaud segments in an anatomy-driven, one-way pipeline. Tri-directional Convolution uses isotropic and orthogonal anisotropic branches to model elongated vascular morphology, while VAST combines channel-spatial attention with boundary and topology constraints to preserve connectivity and branching. Skeleton-Aware Sampling uses the predicted vascular representations as geometric priors for Couinaud boundary localization, avoiding dependence on manually supplied vessel masks.

title: Toward Thyroid Cancer BRAF V600E Mutation Prediction via Multimodal Large Language Model: Dataset and Model Development

categories.value: Multimodal Integration with Clinical / Genomic / Biomarkers

motivation: BRAF V600E status is important for prognosis, recurrence risk, and treatment planning in papillary thyroid carcinoma, but its standard sequencing-based detection is invasive and costly. Ultrasound contains mutation-associated phenotypes, yet prior approaches are largely single-modal and struggle to relate subtle, localized tumor cues to clinical narratives. A multimodal model and dataset are needed to support less invasive, integrated prediction.
method: BRAF-MLLM combines ultrasound images, reports, and clinicopathological records in a multimodal large language model. Its Tumor-centric Multimodal Dual-scale Alignment module separates intra-tumoral and extra-tumoral visual features and aligns them with fine-grained clinical semantics, suppressing ultrasound background noise and emphasizing localized mutation-related cues. The aligned representations are fused for MLLM reasoning and efficiently adapted to thyroid oncology with LoRA; the work also introduces the MM-BRAF dataset and a benchmark.

title: Towards Class-Aware Semantic Decoupling in Multi-modal Disease Diagnosis with Missing Modalities

categories.value: Multimodal Integration with Clinical / Genomic / Biomarkers

motivation: Multimodal diagnosis can exploit complementary images, text, and tabular records, but clinical data often lack one or more modalities, causing unstable predictions. Existing imputation, distillation, prompt, and disentanglement methods may introduce noise, require complete training data, or focus on global alignment while overlooking class-specific disease semantics. Robust diagnosis therefore requires class-level shared-specific representations that remain useful with arbitrary available modalities.
method: The Class-aware Semantic Decoupling framework organizes multimodal representations around disease classes rather than a global feature space. Class-aware Shared-Specific Modeling uses learnable class queries to extract class-related shared and modality-specific components, while Semantic-guided Decoupling Learning performs class-wise redundancy control and relevance-weighted cross-modal alignment. Class-aware Shared-Specific Fusion then adaptively combines these components so predictions remain discriminative when modalities are missing.

title: Towards Direction-Equilibrated Segmentation in 3D Medical Images
motivation: 3D medical images have anisotropic resolution and complex boundaries, especially along the low-resolution axis, where gradual intensity changes blur anatomical edges. CNNs have limited receptive fields, Transformers are costly without explicit anisotropy modeling, and fixed one-dimensional Mamba scanning can disrupt spatial continuity; existing wavelet methods are often 2D and use fixed bases. A learnable 3D directional framework is needed for accurate structure and boundary perception.
method: DEM-Mamba follows a direction decoupling, equilibrium modeling, and adaptive aggregation pipeline for 3D segmentation. Its Orientation-Aware Module uses learnable 3D Riesz wavelets to separate directional high-frequency boundary features, Bidirectional Balanced Mamba models long-range anisotropic dependencies through complementary scans and adaptive normalization, and Orientation-Conflict Fusion weights multidirectional features by their correlations. Together these components address directional imbalance, preserve fuzzy boundaries, and maintain spatially coherent fusion.

title: Towards the Digital Dental Models: High-Fidelity CBCT-to-IOS Fusion via Anatomy-Aware Geometric Transformers
motivation: Fusing CBCT internal anatomy with high-resolution IOS surfaces is essential for accurate digital dental models and safe procedures, but current workflows are manual or sensitive to initialization, density differences, occlusion, and metal artifacts. Generic registration networks tend to emphasize low-frequency semantics and smooth away the high-frequency curvature and topology that distinguish teeth. An automated method must explicitly exploit dental geometric priors while handling cross-source discrepancies.
method: AAGT formulates CBCT-IOS fusion as end-to-end point-cloud registration with anatomy-aware feature extraction, matching, and transformation estimation. The Equivariant Saliency Weighting Module derives saliency from surface information, Anatomy-Aware Embedding encodes dental topological priors, and the Anatomy-Aware Transformer fuses these priors with spatial context to emphasize discriminative landmarks. This design preserves high-frequency dental geometry and improves robustness to metal artifacts and cross-source resolution differences.

title: Towards Unified Image–Video Modeling Across B-Mode and Contrast-Enhanced Ultrasound for Multi-task Analysis
motivation: Ultrasound practice produces heterogeneous images and videos across organs, B-mode, and CEUS, yet most deep models are designed for one organ, task, or temporal format. Image and video pipelines are usually separate, limiting parameter sharing, scalability, and cross-domain generalization. A unified multi-task architecture is needed to learn consistent representations while modeling temporal information for video analysis.
method: UIV-US uses shared parameters to jointly model B-mode and CEUS images and videos for segmentation and classification. Structured Semantic Conditioning Prompt supplies five structural and spatial attributes to condition shared features across clinical settings. For video reasoning, Memory-Reinforced Temporal Attention maintains segmentation consistency through memory and cross-attention, while segmentation-aware Feature-Level Attention aggregates frames for classification.

title: Towards Unified Surgical Scene Understanding: Bridging Reasoning and Grounding via MLLMs
motivation: Reliable computer-assisted surgery requires recognizing workflow phase, reasoning about instrument-tissue interactions, and grounding those semantics in precise image regions. Existing methods address phase recognition, triplet recognition, and segmentation mostly in isolation; recent coupled methods often omit phases or target grounding and lack temporal consistency. A unified model is needed to connect temporal, relational, and spatial understanding for interpretable assistance.
method: SurgMLLM fine-tunes an MLLM to reason jointly about surgical phases, instrument-verb-target triplets, and triplet entities. Dedicated segmentation tokens are temporally aggregated and passed as language-conditioned prompts to a SAM2-based segmentation network, linking high-level semantics to pixel masks for instruments and targets. End-to-end training couples language reasoning supervision with grounding losses, supported by the CholecT45-Scene dataset with aligned frame-level masks and triplet labels.

title: Towards Versatile and Safe Multi-electrode Path Planning for SEEG Implantation
motivation: SEEG planning must place multiple electrodes to sample epileptogenic networks while avoiding vessels, sulci, and other critical anatomy. Current planning is largely manual, and existing automated methods often separate target selection from trajectory optimization or use soft penalties that can leave violations when electrodes interact. A coupled, coverage-aware and constraint-satisfying planner is needed for versatile and safe implantation.
method: The method formulates multi-electrode SEEG planning as patient-level reinforcement learning with one action per rigid electrode. Each action jointly refines a target and insertion direction, while a capsule-based coverage model represents continuous recording sensitivity around the trajectory and promotes ROI coverage. Deterministic projection and fixed checks enforce anatomical collision, sulcal, and inter-electrode spacing constraints, making later decisions account for already accepted electrodes without manual penalty tuning.

title: TraceCXR: Verifiable Chest X-ray Reports via Evidence-Addressable Graph Prompting
motivation: Chest X-ray report generation must describe subtle abnormalities under long-tailed disease distributions, but vision-language models can hallucinate unsupported findings and attention maps are difficult to audit as evidence. Existing clinical structures or grounding methods often lack a patient-specific retrieval-to-localization loop and can be noisy or brittle. Reports therefore need explicit links from each clinical statement to localized, inspectable radiographic evidence.
method: TraceCXR builds ProtoGraph, linking clinical concepts to disease-aware visual prototypes so retrieved concepts can be traced to candidate image evidence. EviLoop Prompting performs image-conditioned graph retrieval and prototype-guided localization, while confidence-gated residual injection suppresses unreliable prompts. Process-Supervised Node Planning regularizes clinically relevant node selection and concentrated evidence attribution, complemented by symmetric image-text contrastive learning with negation-aware hard negatives.

title: TRACE-PSG: Traceable Sleep Diagnosis Support with Pointer-Grounded Evidence
motivation: Clinicians must integrate dense multi-page PSG plots, indices, and annotations with free-text CC/HPI, while multimodal LLMs can miss document structure, hallucinate claims, and provide outputs that are hard to audit. Syntax-constrained generation alone does not ensure factual grounding, and numeric extraction may lose chart topology and provenance. Sleep decision support therefore needs explicit pointers to report or narrative evidence and reliable abstention under indeterminate findings.
method: TRACE-PSG uses a two-stage constrained pipeline for structured, auditable sleep decision support. Stage 1 trains report metric extraction with rule-scored reinforcement learning using GRPO; Stage 2 starts from that checkpoint and fine-tunes generation of clinical JSON containing diagnosis, evidence atoms, notes, and treatment fields. A restricted Pointer Bank and bounded evidence-atom budget provide deterministic provenance checks and support abstention when evidence is missing or indeterminate.

title: TracerAD: Training-Free Few-Shot 3D Anomaly Detection for Novel PET Tracers
motivation: Novel PET tracers and established tracers introduced at new or resource-limited sites often lack sufficient healthy-control scans and diagnostic labels, forcing clinicians to rely on a few subjective references. Existing anomaly detectors commonly require large training cohorts or analyze only 2D slices, losing volumetric context needed for small, deep neurodegenerative structures. A few-shot method that reasons directly in 3D and provides interpretable maps is therefore needed for cold-start deployment.
method: TracerAD is a training-free few-shot framework that uses frozen vision foundation-model features from MNI-registered 3D brain PET volumes and only a handful of healthy-control scans. It detects deviations at three scales: coordinate-level Spatially-Anchored Focal Detection, Region-Constrained Semantic Matching within anatomical regions, and Topology-Aware Metabolic Reasoning over a sparse brain graph. Their combination produces an interpretable 3D anomaly heatmap without task-specific model training.

title: Tracer-Adaptive Expert Learning for Generalizable PET Lesion Segmentation

categories.value: Multimodal Integration with Clinical / Genomic / Biomarkers

motivation: PET/CT lesion segmentation must distinguish pathological lesions from physiological uptake, although both appear as high-intensity hot spots whose meaning depends on anatomy and tracer type. Conventional mixture-of-experts models route primarily by visual features, so conflicting physiological patterns can be sent to the same expert and produce competing gradients. Segmentation therefore needs routing and feature refinement guided by explicit anatomical and tracer-specific priors, including for unseen tracers.
method: ProMoE is a prototype-driven mixture-of-experts framework that embeds each PET/CT patch using anatomical occupancy and tracer-specific physiological expectations from a fixed atlas. Expert routing is determined by similarity between this embedding and learnable expert prototypes, combining anatomical overlap with physiological consistency. A dual-stage modulation module then applies anatomy-aware FiLM modulation followed by prototype-driven physiology-aware modulation, with a frozen CT stream providing anatomical grounding for PET segmentation.

title: Track2Map: Online Deformable SLAM with Motion-Aware Pose Optimization in Robotic Surgery
motivation: Stable metric 3D reconstruction of deformable tissue is needed for guidance tasks in robot-assisted minimally invasive surgery, but tissue motion, occlusion, and limited viewpoints make camera motion and deformation difficult to disentangle. Existing surgical neural and Gaussian-splatting methods often assume static or accurate camera trajectories, while robotic kinematic priors may be noisy or unavailable. An online system must jointly estimate pose and deformation and remain stable across clean, corrupted, or absent pose priors.
method: Track2Map is an online stereo 3D Gaussian Splatting pipeline that jointly optimizes camera poses and a deformable scene representation from surgical video, using available poses only as optional initial estimates. Dense 2D point tracks are lifted to 3D to initialize sparse deformation anchors and to refine pose through motion-gated optimization. Track statistics identify camera-static periods, constrain poses to reduce drift, and allow vision-only initialization when pose priors are absent.

title: Trackerless Ultrasound Pose Estimation via Correspondence-Aware Tokenization and Flow-Matching Transformers
motivation: Trackerless freehand 3D ultrasound must infer probe motion from B-mode sequences, but speckle, shadowing, and weak visual anchors make inter-frame correspondences ambiguous. Small pose errors at each step accumulate when relative transforms are composed, causing substantial drift in reconstructed volumes. Existing methods often leave patch-level alignment implicit, motivating explicit correspondence construction and confidence-aware sequence generation.
method: The method constructs bidirectionally supported token correspondences between adjacent ultrasound frames using ViT features, aligns current-frame evidence to the previous token grid, and derives a lattice displacement cue. Entropy-based confidence weighting suppresses ambiguous speckle regions, while a Q-Former compresses correspondence-aware patch features into context tokens. A context-conditioned flow-matching DiT then generates coherent pose-delta sequences through ODE sampling.

title: Tractography-Driven Synthetic Data Generation for Fiber Bundle Segmentation in Tracer Histology
motivation: Tracer histology in non-human primates provides a high-resolution reference for validating dMRI tractography, but manually annotating fiber bundles is laborious and limits available training data. Existing segmentation methods face variability across tracers, injection sites, and brains, and approaches from other microscopy modalities do not transfer reliably to macaque tracer data. A data-efficient strategy is needed to improve cross-brain generalization while reducing manual annotation.
method: The framework uses ex vivo dMRI tractography registered to blockface images as a geometric prior for synthesizing 2D tracer-histology patches. Tract-derived foregrounds with varied fiber densities are composed with blockface backgrounds and diversified through domain randomization. A 2D U-Net is trained on mixed real and synthetic patches, so synthesis supplements limited annotation while real data retain essential supervision.

title: Training LLMs with Reinforcement Learning over Digital Twin Representations for Reasoning-Intensive Surgical VideoQA
motivation: Surgical VideoQA increasingly requires multi-step semantic, spatial, and temporal reasoning, such as understanding instrument function or tracing motion, but most methods perform single-step visual matching or compress videos into discrete tokens that fragment continuous relationships. Existing systems also bind perception and reasoning in one model, creating competing objectives and requiring extensive surgical annotations. A framework that supports structured multiscale reasoning while handling perceptual uncertainty is needed.
method: The framework trains an LLM with reinforcement learning to plan and reason over digital-twin representations generated by surgical foundation models, thereby separating visual perception from high-level reasoning. Digital twins encode semantic entities and spatial-temporal relations hierarchically at frame, temporal-window, and procedure levels, with probabilistic uncertainty estimates. Rewards combine answer-format validation, clinical plausibility, and uncertainty-aware confidence calibration, avoiding the need for annotated reasoning chains.

title: Trajectory-Aware Cross-Paradigm Transformers for Efficient System Matrix Calibration in Magnetic Particle Imaging
motivation: MPI system-matrix calibration requires dense volumetric sampling, and changes in particle materials or field-free-point trajectories force repeated recalibration that is time-consuming. Existing super-resolution approaches often lack explicit awareness of where trajectory-dependent signals are concentrated and model spatial and channel structure separately. Efficient calibration therefore needs physically guided feature prioritization and joint modeling of these coupled signal characteristics.
method: TACPT embeds field-free-point trajectory information as physically grounded positional priors in a transformer for system-matrix calibration. Its cross-paradigm feature interaction module models FFT-based inter-channel dependencies together with spatial structure, and a dynamic sparsity-gated fusion suppresses redundant or noisy responses. These components focus computation on trajectory-related, information-dense signal regions while retaining compact system-matrix representations.

title: TRIAGE-MIL: Multi-axis Instance Selection and Semantic Hypergraph Modeling for Survival Prediction from Whole-Slide Images
motivation: WSI survival prediction must find sparse prognostic signals within gigapixel tissue while remaining computationally feasible. Standard MIL treats tiles as an unordered set and can miss rare regions, whereas graph MIL usually captures only pairwise spatial relations and cannot explicitly represent coordinated interactions among multiple tissue compartments. An approach is needed that selects informative tiles without region labels and models higher-order tissue architecture.
method: TRIAGE-MIL first applies multi-axis stratified sampling (MASS) to select a fixed-size set of tiles using embedding-based proxies for morphologic heterogeneity, tissue regularity, microenvironmental interface, and tissue diversity. It then constructs a semantic hierarchical hypergraph whose constrained hyperedges follow MASS groupings to represent intra- and inter-tissue higher-order relations. This two-stage design enriches prognostic instances and enables relational reasoning beyond pairwise graph edges without region-level labels.

title: TriFlow: Triplane Latent Conditional Flow Matching for Efficient 3D Skull Shape Completion
motivation: Patient-specific skull implants must match complex defect boundaries accurately, but manual CAD design is slow, costly, and difficult to scale. Existing learning and generative methods often struggle to achieve anatomical consistency and boundary accuracy together with efficient 3D computation; diffusion models additionally require costly iterative sampling. A fast conditional generator that preserves 3D geometry is needed for practical cranioplasty planning.
method: TriFlow encodes a defective skull TSDF into three aligned orthogonal feature planes using a 3D autoencoder, then learns a conditional flow-matching velocity field from the defective latent to a complete-skull latent. A triplane-aware module applies within-plane self-attention, cross-plane attention, and AdaLN conditioning to preserve surface continuity and geometric alignment. Inference solves the conditional ODE with a fixed-step Euler method, decodes the completed skull, and obtains the implant by subtracting the defect input.

title: Tri-KA: Tri-level knowledge anchoring test-time adaptation for source-free cross-site MRI rectal cancer segmentation
motivation: Rectal tumor and rectal-wall segmentation on MRI is highly sensitive to scanner and protocol shifts across sites, especially with low contrast and highly anisotropic sagittal images. Generic TTA methods can produce noisy gradients, semantic drift, and structural distortion, while BN-based updates conflict with common 3D Instance Normalization pipelines and source data cannot be shared for privacy reasons. Adaptation therefore needs to use compressed source priors while preserving invariant anatomy and network stability.
method: Tri-KA performs source-free test-time adaptation using three privacy-preserving source priors without changing the base 3D network. At the input level, an energy-calibrated Fourier module blends target amplitudes with a source amplitude prior while preserving phase and the DC component; at the feature level, deep semantic prototypes anchor frozen deep layers while shallow anisotropic layers adapt to target texture. At the output level, anatomical KL-divergence regularization constrains macroscopic predictions to suppress structural hallucinations.

title: TRUST: Efficient Abdominal Trauma Recognition via Image-to-Ultrasound-Video Transfer Learning
motivation: Abdominal ultrasound is important for rapid, noninvasive trauma triage, but diagnosis requires interpreting subtle dynamic cues across continuous multi-view scans. This process is time-intensive and operator-dependent, while ultrasound speckle, varied scanning dynamics, and heterogeneous acquisition conditions challenge PEIVTL models and make static temporal or text representations insufficient. A scan-aware method is therefore needed for reliable and generalizable ultrasound video understanding.
method: TRUST is a scan-aware PEIVTL framework built on a CLIP-style contrastive pipeline that progressively refines spatial, temporal, and semantic representations. Its Cross-Frequency Collaborative Adapter exchanges constraints between wavelet low- and high-frequency components to suppress speckle-driven responses while preserving detail. The Multi-Granularity Motion-Aware module combines local temporal convolutions with motion-prior-guided global attention, and Visual Query Semantic Aggregation dynamically synthesizes text prototypes from visual features for adaptive cross-modal alignment.

title: TrustSyn: Reliable and Divergent Synergy for Mixed-Domain Fundus Segmentation
motivation: Fundus segmentation supports ophthalmic diagnosis, but dense manual delineation is labor-intensive and models trained on one center degrade under scanner, protocol, and population shifts. Mixed-domain semi-supervised methods can exploit unlabeled multi-center data, yet collaborative frameworks often use coarse reliability estimates that propagate pixel-level errors and encourage the conventional model to mimic the foundation model. The task requires spatially selective supervision while preserving complementary model representations.
method: TrustSyn uses a synergistic Teacher-Student framework for mixed-domain semi-supervised fundus segmentation. Spatial Reliability Assessment estimates pixel-level reliability, and Uncertainty Weighting selectively modulates supervision to generate more reliable pseudo-labels using global context. A Feature Discrepancy constraint keeps the foundation and conventional models’ latent representations divergent, so prediction agreement can arise from complementary inference mechanisms rather than representational collapse.

title: Trustworthy Endoscopic Super-Resolution
motivation: Super-resolution can improve endoscopic and robotic-surgery imagery under hardware constraints, but it may hallucinate structures or amplify noise. Existing uncertainty approaches for continuous SR outputs often require multiple forward passes, architectural changes, or yield only difficult-to-interpret heatmaps, without operational guarantees for failure decisions. A real-time, model-agnostic mechanism is needed to localize unreliable reconstructions and support safe clinical use.
method: The framework adds a lightweight Reconstruction Error Network to a frozen SR model, using intermediate representations to predict pixel-wise reconstruction error with low latency. It defines reconstruction failure levels and applies conformal risk control to choose rejection thresholds that produce binary Conformal Failure Masks. These masks identify output regions that should not be trusted while providing distribution-free control over tolerated error and false-negative miscoverage, without modifying or correcting the SR model.

title: TSegAgent: Zero-Shot Tooth Segmentation via Geometry-Aware Vision-Language Agents
motivation: Tooth segmentation and identification from intra-oral 3D scans support orthodontic diagnosis, treatment planning, and prosthodontic design. Existing supervised 3D networks require densely annotated dental datasets and often generalize poorly to scans from unseen scanners, sources, or patient populations; recent foundation-model adaptations still require dental-specific training or lack error verification. A training-free formulation that uses anatomical structure is needed to reduce annotation dependence and improve reliability across diverse scans.
method: TSegAgent reformulates tooth analysis as zero-shot geometric reasoning using general-purpose foundation models rather than task-specific dental training. It renders multi-view scans with curvature information, uses SAM3 for zero-shot instance segmentation, merges masks into face-level labels, and reorders instances according to dental-arch geometry. A vision-language agent then identifies teeth through multi-round reasoning over visual evidence and explicit constraints such as arch structure, symmetry, and volumetric relationships, with verification to reduce ambiguity.

title: Tumor-Aware Direct Preference Optimization for Longitudinal Post-operative MRI Generation
motivation: Longitudinal post-operative MRI simulation could help clinicians assess structural change, tumor progression, and likely surgical outcomes in glioblastoma. However, clinically meaningful trajectories depend on resection extent, tumor location and infiltration, and evolution across follow-up times, while conventional generative models often produce indistinct or clinically misaligned resection regions. A generation method must therefore incorporate patient-specific clinical preferences and focus on tumor progression structures.
method: TADPO uses Direct Preference Optimization to align longitudinal post-operative MRI generation from pre-operative MRI with clinically preferred outcomes at multiple follow-up times. It constructs preference pairs by treating clinically relevant ground-truth follow-up MRIs as winning examples and plausible but inconsistent generated images as losing examples. A tumor-aware optimization strategy gives additional emphasis to tumor regions and boundaries, improving representation of resection and progression dynamics rather than optimizing preference uniformly over the whole image.

title: TumorFlow: Physics-Guided Longitudinal MRI Synthesis of Glioblastoma Growth
motivation: Glioblastoma infiltrates surrounding brain tissue beyond what routine MRI visibly captures, making true tumor extent and future growth difficult to estimate for treatment planning and follow-up. Biophysical models provide interpretable continuous tumor-concentration fields, but they do not operate directly in clinical image space, while mask- or volume-conditioned generators offer only coarse control and often lack temporal coherence. A framework is needed to connect mechanistic growth modeling with controllable MRI synthesis.
method: TumorFlow trains a 3D generative flow-matching model on preoperative brain MRI conditioned on modality, tissue segmentations, and spatially continuous tumor-concentration fields. The concentration field provides finer control over infiltration than a binary tumor mask and can be propagated through a biophysical brain-tumor growth model. During inference, the propagated fields condition the generator to synthesize patient-specific, anatomically preserved, and temporally coherent growth trajectories.

title: Two-Stage Cross-Domain Cervical Abnormality Screening with Cytopathological Image Synthesis and Knowledge Distillation
motivation: Cross-institutional cervical cytology detection is hindered by differences in sample preparation and staining, while the subtle and continuous visual changes across lesion stages increase category ambiguity. Feature-level domain adaptation alone may be insufficient when appearance shifts are large, and single-level or independent distillation does not capture the hierarchical roles of structural and semantic representations. The task needs both artifact-free image translation and progressive multi-level knowledge transfer.
method: The method first uses Spatially-Continuous Unpaired Neural Schrödinger Bridge translation to construct an intermediate domain between institutions. Its Dense Normalization interpolates patch statistics into continuous pixel-level fields, reducing boundary drift and tiling artifacts in ultra-high-resolution images. A knowledge-distillation stage then performs dual-level alignment: Loose Feature Alignment transfers shallow structural information, while Compact Feature Alignment transfers high-level semantic knowledge from source to target.

title: Ultrafast Echocardiography Based on Dynamic Subspace-Guided and Temporal Adaptive Diffusion
motivation: Diverging-wave echocardiography offers very high frame rates, but obtaining high-quality images normally requires multi-angle motion-compensated compounding that reduces temporal resolution. Direct reconstruction methods rely on strong spatial correspondence assumptions, while existing diffusion approaches emphasize realistic synthesis without sufficient anatomical constraints and may lose inter-frame coherence. A reconstruction method must preserve both cardiac anatomy and temporal dynamics at an ultrafast frame rate.
method: ST-CODE reconstructs high-quality ultrafast echocardiography through conditional reverse diffusion using only three steered DW transmissions. Dynamic Subspace Guidance models sequence-level anatomy as a basis-invariant low-dimensional subspace on the Grassmann manifold and conditions denoising on its structural projections. Temporal Correlation Sampling introduces spatially adaptive correlation between consecutive initial noise samples, propagating inter-frame dependency through inference without changing diffusion training.

title: UltraStar: Semantic-Aware Star Graph Modeling for Echocardiography Navigation
motivation: Echocardiography probe navigation requires sonographers to use prior exploratory feedback to locate standard cardiac views, but skilled operators are scarce. Single-frame methods lack enough context, while sequential models treat history as a chain and overfit redundant, noisy trial-and-error motions, causing localization to degrade as sequences grow. Navigation therefore needs a representation that uses history for global localization rather than trajectory reconstruction.
method: UltraStar reformulates probe navigation as anchor-based global localization and represents history with a Star Graph. Historical keyframes connect directly to the current view, allowing the model to learn geometric constraints to landmarks instead of reproducing a noisy sequential trajectory. A semantic-aware sampling strategy selects representative landmarks with high semantic divergence, producing a compact and informative history map that scales to long inputs.

title: Uncertainty-Aware Bayesian Prompt Adaptation for Robust Cross-Modality Medical Segmentation
motivation: Medical segmentation models often fail when imaging modality, device, protocol, or patient population changes, with ultrasound-to-MRI shifts being especially severe. Although SAM2 provides promptable general segmentation, few-shot cross-modality adaptation must avoid overfitting while remaining calibrated and reliable; existing parameter-efficient or test-time approaches do not directly integrate predictive uncertainty. A data-efficient adaptation strategy is needed that regularizes updates and conditions prompts on modality-specific uncertainty.
method: BayesPrompt adapts SAM2 for few-shot cross-modality segmentation through Bayesian regularization and uncertainty-aware prompting. Bayesian Meta-Prior Adaptation aligns the posterior of lightweight decoder parameters with a source-derived meta-prior to limit overfitting under scarce labels. The Probabilistic Prompt Module summarizes class-wise support statistics and predictive uncertainty into attention-conditioned prompt tokens, and the framework supports either gradient-free prompting or efficient Bayesian fine-tuning.

title: Uncertainty-Aware Hypergraph Consistency Learning for Semi-supervised Medical Image Segmentation
motivation: Semi-supervised medical image segmentation aims to reduce the costly need for expert pixel annotations, but common consistency-learning methods mainly constrain pixels or features and miss higher-order anatomical structure. Uncertain predictions near low-contrast regions and lesion boundaries can either propagate noise when enforced or discard valuable diagnostic information when ignored, motivating a method that models structure while learning from ambiguity.
method: UAHC reformulates consistency learning at the hypergraph level to represent high-order anatomical dependencies. Its dual branches use Certain-Region Hypergraph Consistency (CHC) for stable regions and Uncertain-Region Hypergraph Consistency (UHC) for ambiguous regions, with density-guided modulation to limit noise. Pixel uncertainty is propagated to hyperedges so diagnostically important but uncertain structures receive adaptive weighting.

title: Uncertainty-Aware Spatio-Semantic Contextual Prompts for Multimodal Medical Segmentation
motivation: Medical imaging varies substantially across modalities, scanners, protocols, and resolutions, while labeled data are scarce, making segmentation knowledge transfer difficult. Few-shot and cross-domain methods require retraining, in-context methods are mainly 2D and within-modality, and interactive foundation-model prompting is slow and difficult to scale. A modality-agnostic, automatic 3D prompting strategy is therefore needed.
method: The framework derives a spatial prior by deformably registering an annotated support volume to a query volume and a semantic prior by matching query features with support foreground prototypes using the frozen SAM-Med3D encoder. It fuses these priors into a dense prompt with voxel-wise entropy-based dynamic gating, while preserving boundary uncertainty through soft spatial maps. The fused prompt is supplied to the frozen SAM-Med3D segmentation model, enabling training-free cross-modal and intra-modal 3D segmentation.

title: Uncertainty-Aware Spatiotemporal Graph Learning for Individualized Cortical Parcellation and Somato-Cognitive Integration in the Developing Brain
motivation: Individualized cortical parcellation is difficult because functional topography varies substantially between people, especially during development and in transitional regions. Group-averaged atlases can impose overly rigid boundaries and do not adequately represent these individual differences, motivating temporally informed and uncertainty-calibrated parcellation from vertex-wise fMRI.
method: STGraph-Parcel combines a population adolescent atlas as a soft group prior with explicit temporal and spatial graph modeling of vertex-wise fMRI signals. A dual-channel GRU integrates raw signals with attention-weighted neighborhood representations, and GCNs then aggregate the resulting temporal embeddings over the cortical mesh. Probabilistic parcel predictions are quantified with entropy to expose uncertain integration zones.

title: Uncertainty-Guided Conservative Propagation for Coronary Artery Segmentation
motivation: Coronary arteries have elongated tubular structures whose connectivity and branch integrity are clinically important, so local discontinuities or spurious connections can remain harmful even when overlap scores are high. Existing point-wise models lack an inference-stage mechanism that jointly uses neighborhood structure and uncertainty, while topology losses and post-processing act separately from the prediction update.
method: UGCP treats segmentation inference as a finite-step state evolution in logit space rather than a single point-wise prediction. Constrained neighborhood updates use local prediction discrepancies and voxel-wise uncertainty so confident regions guide unstable regions, while a source term anchors the process to the initial logits. The framework is dimension-agnostic and can be applied to convolutional or Transformer backbones.

title: Uncovering Interpretable Point-Wise Image Correspondences from Deep Segmentation Features
motivation: Point-wise correspondences are needed for motion tracking, shape analysis, and spatial normalization, but deformable registration is difficult to interpret and supervised landmark methods require costly annotations. Weakly supervised alternatives still need dedicated training and depend on synthetic transformations that may not reflect anatomical variation. A generic, label- and training-efficient way to exploit anatomical representations is therefore needed.
method: The training-free framework extracts feature maps from multiple layers of a pretrained segmentation network, upsamples them to image resolution, and sums voxel-wise similarities between two images. For a query point, softmax converts similarities into an interpretable correspondence probability map, whose maximum gives the estimated match. The same probabilities can be propagated across image sequences, with entropy identifying stable salient keypoints; geometric constraints can also support coupled landmark estimation.

title: Understanding Model Behavior in Monocular Polyp Sizing
motivation: Polyp size determines surveillance and treatment decisions, yet monocular colonoscopy lacks a reliable metric reference and clinicians often estimate size inaccurately. Apparent scale is confounded by camera behavior, models generalize poorly across centers, and it is unclear whether reported performance reflects metric reasoning or shortcuts. A controlled audit is needed to identify the separate limitations of scale information and segmentation quality.
method: The work performs a diagnostic audit of binary monocular polyp-size classification across multiple public multicenter datasets, model families, input modalities, and patient-stratified validation. Oracle scale ladders at frame, polyp, and global granularities isolate the headroom from missing metric scale, while shortcut partitions test reliance on examination behavior. Mask substitution compares ground-truth and predicted masks to measure segmentation robustness under distribution shift.

title: Uni-Brain: Anatomy-Informed Diffusion for Multi-Tracer Synthesis and Counterfactual Prognosis from Cross-Sectional Data
motivation: MRI is accessible and structural, whereas PET provides molecular specificity for Alzheimer’s disease but is invasive, radioactive, and costly for repeated monitoring. Existing cross-modal synthesis is usually static, while longitudinal methods often require paired longitudinal scans and discretized clinical variables weaken smooth control. A unified approach is needed for multi-tracer synthesis, prognosis, and counterfactual PET simulation from cross-sectional data.
method: Uni-Brain learns a shared MRI-PET latent space and uses a conditional latent diffusion model to generate target-tracer PET under anatomical and clinical conditions. MRI latent codes provide dense spatial conditioning to preserve subject-specific anatomy, while continuous and discrete clinical covariates are encoded separately for controllable simulation. The same formulation supports tracer switching, longitudinal prognosis by changing target age, and counterfactual clinical interventions without paired longitudinal training scans.

title: UniCT: A Unified Joint Multi-Task Framework for 3D Chest CT Abnormality Analysis
motivation: The growing volume of chest CT examinations creates a need for automated abnormality classification, localization, and reporting, but 3D data and heterogeneous abnormalities make each task difficult. Existing systems usually optimize classification, segmentation, or report generation separately, preventing them from exploiting their strong clinical and semantic interdependence. Joint modeling is especially underexplored because aligned labels, segmentations, and reports are scarce.
method: UniCT jointly processes 3D chest CT for multi-label abnormality classification, segmentation, and report generation in one end-to-end model. A multi-task fusion mechanism enables bidirectional information exchange among the branches, while segmentation-conditioned feature modulation injects spatial localization into shared representations. This design couples semantic and spatial reasoning so localization can support reporting and contextual language cues can refine abnormality recognition.

title: UniFCHarm: Unified Prompt-Guided Harmonization of fMRI Functional Connectivity Across Scanners and Atlases
motivation: Multi-site fMRI functional connectivity is affected by scanner and protocol variability, which shifts distributions and harms cross-site biomarker generalization while risking loss of subject-specific biology. Existing harmonization methods often map everything to one reference site, depend on a particular atlas, and apply non-selective global corrections that can over-correct multiscale effects. Flexible target conditioning and coarse-to-fine correction are therefore needed.
method: UniFCHarm pretrains GraphCLIP on acquisition- and atlas-aware FC-prompt pairs to align FC graphs and structured prompts in a shared latent space. A target prompt then directs harmonization toward a chosen scanner, protocol, and atlas rather than a fixed reference. Hierarchical processing first corrects subnetwork-to-subnetwork connectivity and then refines ROI-to-ROI connections, limiting over-correction across scales.

title: Unified Multimodal Model for Brain MRI Imputation and Understanding
motivation: Brain MRI analysis requires specialized knowledge and often combines multiple modalities, but clinical scans frequently lack one or more modalities. Explicit imputation followed by analysis is a disconnected two-stage pipeline, whereas implicit methods may improve downstream tasks at the expense of image fidelity; both are limited by scarce fine-grained medical multimodal data. A unified model is needed to make generated modalities useful for understanding while remaining robust during long autoregressive reasoning.
method: UniBrain formulates missing-modality imputation and brain MRI understanding as one autoregressive, interleaved multimodal sequence, generating missing images before producing diagnostic impressions. A self-alignment objective conditions the generation expert on dense ViT embeddings to learn fine-grained anatomical information without detailed captions. Dynamic hidden states using training-time context help the model account for self-generated artifacts and reduce exposure bias during long multimodal inference.

title: UniField: A Unified Field-Aware MRI Enhancement Framework
motivation: MRI field-strength enhancement can make accessible low-field scans approach clinical quality and can approximate ultra-high-field detail from clinical scans. Existing methods are trained separately for narrow field transitions or modalities on small paired cohorts, limiting generalization and wasting shared degradation information. Slice-wise processing also loses 3D continuity, while flow-matching methods can over-smooth diagnostically important high-frequency anatomy.
method: UniField jointly learns multiple MRI modalities and field-strength enhancement tasks to exploit shared degradation patterns. It uses pre-trained 3D foundation models to encode volumetric anatomical structure rather than processing independent slices. A Field-Aware Spectral Rectification Mechanism incorporates field-strength-dependent magnetic physics to apply customized frequency-domain correction and preserve high-frequency details.

title: UniLiver: Gradient-Conditioned Unified Model for Multi-target Hepatic Segmentation
motivation: Precise segmentation of hepatic vessels, Couinaud segments, and tumors is needed for liver-surgery planning, and these structures have a physiological hierarchy. Most methods segment them independently, missing useful vascular, segmental, and lesion dependencies. Naive joint learning also creates conflicts because thin vessels, regional segments, and tumors require different feature scales, shapes, and spatial priors.
method: UniLiver uses a shared DynUNet-based encoder-decoder for vessels, Couinaud segments, and tumors. Its Multi-Target Gradient-Conditioned Adapter uses per-target gradient coherence to modulate shared features and suppress conflicting optimization signals. Target-Aware Spectral-Spatial Encoding provides target-adaptive frequency filtering and positional cues, and VCT Sequential Denoising propagates anatomical information from vessels to segments and tumors through directed cross-attention.

title: UniSpine-GS: An Efficient Physics-Aware Gaussian Framework for Cross-Modality Multi-view Spine Image Synthesis
motivation: Three-dimensional spinal assessment is important for diagnosing and planning treatment for spinal disorders, but dedicated 3D imaging is expensive and often unavailable. Low-cost X-ray and portable ultrasound have substantially different formation mechanisms and appearances, making cross-modality, multi-view synthesis difficult to generalize. Sparse views further make it hard to preserve anatomical consistency, boundaries, and local detail.
method: UniSpine-GS represents spinal anatomy with optimizable 3D Gaussian primitives and renders projections through a unified differentiable radiative forward operator, avoiding explicit 3D reconstruction. Scanner geometry and cuboid Gaussian-center initialization provide spatial and pose priors for sparse-view optimization. For ultrasound, it uses a projectable scalar-field proxy with the DRR operator, while a warm-up Structure Prior Weight Map reweights reconstruction loss toward boundaries and texture-informative regions.

title: Unleashing Video Language Models for Fine-grained HRCT Report Generation
motivation: Accurate HRCT reports could reduce radiology workload and standardize interpretation, but 3D volumes contain hundreds of slices and clinically important abnormalities are sparse and diverse. Existing CT-specific methods can require substantial medical data and computation, while their whole-volume abnormality coverage remains insufficiently explored. VideoLMs offer sequence-level spatial reasoning, but natural-video pretraining lacks the clinical knowledge needed for fine-grained HRCT interpretation.
method: AbSteering adapts general-domain VideoLMs to HRCT report generation in two stages. An abnormality-centric Chain-of-Thought scheme uses structured reports to require finding-first reasoning before producing the final report. It then applies Direct Preference Optimization with clinically confusable abnormalities in the same anatomical region as hard negatives, encouraging fine-grained discrimination and reducing hallucinated findings.

title: Unlocking the Power of Medical Tabular Data via Semantic-Aware Multimodal Pre-training

categories.value: Multimodal Integration with Clinical / Genomic / Biomarkers

motivation: Structured clinical tables contain dense quantitative diagnostic phenotypes that complement medical images, but expert labels are scarce. Existing image-tabular pre-training often treats tables as flat vectors, masks all features uniformly, and reconstructs values with continuous regression. This ignores unequal diagnostic importance and makes nearly equivalent clinical semantic values an unstable, ill-posed reconstruction target.
method: AID combines a ViT image encoder, a structured-feature Transformer, and a cross-attention multimodal encoder for image-tabular pre-training. Its Importance-Aware Adaptive Masking derives label-free feature importance from an offline frozen meta-learning prior and masks more salient clinical features more often. A Soft-Label Discretized Module converts continuous feature values into distributions over adjacent semantic intervals, retaining ordinal relationships while using exact values for cross-modal alignment.

title: Unsupervised and Segmentation-Free Phase Unwrapping for 4D Flow MRI Using Deep Image Prior
motivation: 4D flow MRI measures clinically relevant blood-flow quantities from image phase, but the venc setting creates a trade-off between velocity-to-noise ratio and phase wrapping. Low venc improves VNR but can wrap velocities beyond the encoding range, biasing downstream quantification. Existing dual-venc methods increase scan time, single-venc methods may fail under severe wrapping or low SNR, and supervised learning requires difficult-to-obtain paired data and often manual segmentation.
method: PUDIP-Flow formulates phase unwrapping as gradient-domain optimization that enforces consistency with wrapped spatiotemporal phase gradients. It fits a 3D U-Net as a deep image prior directly to each individual scan, avoiding paired training data. An automated weighting mask combines phase-contrast MR angiography features and temporal variance to down-weight stationary background tissue without manual region segmentation.

title: Unsupervised Brain Anomaly Detection as a Bayesian Inverse Problem with Diffusion Prior
motivation: Unsupervised medical anomaly detection must localize abnormalities without pixel-level annotations by reconstructing pseudo-healthy images that are both anatomically plausible and subject-specific. Diffusion-based approaches balance anomaly removal and subject preservation through heuristic noise schedules, corruptions, or synthetic anomalies. Although diffusion priors work well for Bayesian inverse problems, UAD lacks a known forward model relating a healthy image to an abnormal observation.
method: The method formulates diffusion-based UAD as Bayesian inference over a latent pseudo-healthy image and a probabilistic spatial anomaly mask. It approximates the unavailable anomaly-generation forward model with a likelihood that enforces image consistency in normal regions and attributes unexplained deviations to the mask. A diffusion prior for healthy anatomy, a spatially regularized Gaussian Markov random field mask prior, and annealed intermediate posterior sampling jointly infer the image and mask.

title: Unsupervised Domain Adaptation for Pelvic Landmark Localization in CT and MR Using Landmark-Conditioned Synthesis
motivation: Accurate 3D pelvic landmark localization supports hip morphology assessment and surgical planning, but models trained in one modality degrade markedly in another because CT and MR differ in appearance and imaging characteristics. Target-domain landmark annotation, especially on bone in MR, is difficult and costly. Existing synthesis-based UDA struggles to preserve semantics with sparse landmark labels and often does not adequately refine noisy target pseudo-labels.
method: The framework couples a CycleGAN-based synthesis module with landmark localization. Landmark-Conditioned Adversarial Learning uses class- and laterality-conditioned local discriminators around each landmark to preserve landmark semantics during CT-MR translation. Two modality-specific detectors enforce prediction consistency across real and synthesized images, while PLEM ensembles localization confidence and cross-prediction spatial consistency to generate target-domain pseudo-labels.

title: Unveiling Brain-Body Axis Interactions in Psychiatric-Endocrine Disorder with Deep Graph Causal Neural Network

categories.value: AI for Population Health, Public Health & Epidemiology

motivation: Psychiatric and endocrine disorders are associated with brain-body interactions, but the direction of influence among brain microstructure, organ physiology, and disease remains unclear. Prior studies largely assess isolated correlations, which cannot determine whether brain changes precede organ dysfunction or the reverse. Population-scale multimodal data are also high-dimensional and incomplete, making causal structure learning vulnerable to missing-data bias.
method: The framework first imputes missing UK Biobank measurements with a masked autoencoder. It then applies DAG-GNN causal structure learning to diffusion MRI features from major white-matter bundles, organ-level physiological indicators, and psychiatric and endocrine disease outcomes. The resulting directed acyclic graph is intended to provide an interpretable joint model of directional brain-body-disease dependencies.

title: U-ReLSE: Voxel-Wise Evidential Uncertainty-Regularized MIL for Vertebral Metastasis Detection with Hybrid Supervision
motivation: Vertebral metastases can cause severe complications, yet CT lesions may be subtle or obscured, creating a need for vertebra-level detection. Dense lesion masks and curated vertebra labels are limited, whereas report-mined vertebra labels are abundant but noisy. Standard MIL pooling ignores voxel reliability, so ambiguous regions and label noise can destabilize detection, particularly under domain shift.
method: U-ReLSE trains a shared 3D vertebra-ROI encoder with lesion-segmentation and evidential heads, jointly using verified voxel masks, verified vertebra labels, and noisy report-derived vertebra labels. Segmentation supervision learns voxel-wise Dirichlet certainty, which is used as deterministic reliability weights in a mask-aware log-sum-exp MIL pooling operator. The unified objective combines Dice, evidential, and vertebra-level BCE losses, producing vertebra malignancy probabilities together with lesion-localization and uncertainty maps.

title: URLCF: Universal Representation Learning for Cross-Domain Few-Shot Autism Spectrum Disorder Detection
motivation: Reliable autism spectrum disorder detection from resting-state fMRI is limited by the scarcity of labeled data at individual sites. Combining sites introduces scanner- and protocol-related heterogeneity, while harmonization requires reprocessing new sites and domain adaptation depends on target data, limiting generalization to unseen domains. A universal representation that can rapidly adapt with very few unseen-domain samples is therefore needed.
method: URLCF first trains separate domain-specific teacher networks, then distills their knowledge into a universal student model. Domain data are passed through both models; masked student features are reconstructed by domain-specific generators to align representations, while a domain discriminator encourages domain invariance. The student is frozen and a lightweight adaptive module performs few-shot fine-tuning on an unseen domain.

title: UT-MIL: Uncertainty-Rectified and TME-Decoupling Dual-Stream Aggregation for Robust WSI Survival Prediction
motivation: Whole-slide image survival prediction must model continuous risk from weakly supervised, spatially heterogeneous tissue containing artifacts and ambiguous morphology. Standard MIL can dilute localized high-risk malignant foci or fail to represent the multifaceted tumor microenvironment, and it usually lacks explicit feature reliability modeling, leading to overconfident predictions on noisy inputs. A method that manages uncertainty while separating local malignant evidence from global TME context is needed.
method: UT-MIL uses an Uncertainty-Guided Feature Rectifier to estimate feature uncertainty from perturbation sensitivity and a Histomorphological Memory Bank. Its tri-branch routing removes highly uncertain features, preserves reliable ones, and rectifies ambiguous features through prototype retrieval. A TME-Decoupling Contextual Aggregator then combines a Critical Stream for high-risk malignant foci with a Context Stream of learnable latent queries that captures global TME patterns.

title: VA-Adapter: Adapting Ultrasound Foundation Model to Echocardiography Probe Guidance
motivation: Echocardiography probe guidance could reduce the shortage of skilled operators, but individual differences in 2D image appearance and 3D cardiac anatomy make precise navigation difficult. Existing guidance systems are developed separately from diagnostic ultrasound foundation models and do not exploit their learned structural representations. The missing capability is an efficient way to add patient-specific 3D and action understanding to those models.
method: VA-Adapter inserts a parameter-efficient Vision-Action Adapter into deeper layers of a pretrained ultrasound foundation model while keeping the image encoder largely frozen. It encodes historical vision-action sequences so the model can infer patient-specific 3D cardiac anatomy and reason about probe adjustments. This transfers diagnostic image representations to probe guidance with a small number of trainable parameters.

title: Validation of simulation-based evaluation by inclusion of unlabeled data and meta-ablation
motivation: Many registration and reconstruction tasks lack dense, accurate, unseen ground-truth data, making direct evaluation difficult. Simulation supplies exact labels but simplified models may omit real variation, creating a realism gap and overly optimistic metrics, especially when simulations guide learning-based development. A label-free way to validate simulation adequacy and identify which model extensions matter is needed.
method: The paper combines simulated and real data to expose mismatches between compensated simulations and their ground truth when real-world variation is added. It introduces meta-ablation, which jointly varies simulation components and the compensation method to identify residual errors and iteratively adjust the simulation model. The approach is demonstrated for label-free validation of non-uniform 3D OCT registration and can guide successive model improvements.

title: VarDeFlow: Variational Deformation Learning with Flow Matching for Multi-organ Cross-Modality Medical Image Synthesis
motivation: Cross-modality synthesis must handle residual spatial misalignment from non-rigid organ deformation and local anatomical variation that remains after registration. Existing methods either add a separate pre-registration pipeline or discard registration modules at inference because target images are unavailable, limiting correction of anatomy-specific residuals; diffusion sampling is also computationally costly. A unified model should learn plausible deformations from the source and synthesize aligned targets efficiently across anatomies.
method: VarDeFlow learns a source-conditioned variational distribution over plausible, anatomy-specific deformation fields, using a VAE-style network with latent stochasticity and regularization. Stochastically warped source volumes provide informed priors to a conditional 3D U-Net trained with flow matching to synthesize the target modality. Joint training learns residual alignment and translation, and a small number of Euler integration steps enables efficient inference without paired target inputs.

title: VCDA-Net: Graph-Guided Voxel-Cluster Density Attention for Global-Regional Brain Age Gap Estimation
motivation: Brain age gap from structural MRI can quantify neurodegenerative burden, but many deep models optimize global age accuracy while offering little anatomical interpretation. Global representations can obscure localized changes such as hippocampal atrophy, while existing architectures may miss fine geometry, inter-regional dependencies, or natural anatomical variation. A multi-scale model is needed to estimate age accurately and profile regional BAG across the Alzheimer’s disease continuum.
method: VCDA-Net extracts high-saliency voxel-cluster density cues to represent stable regional geometry. It constructs a multi-attributed brain graph with Multi-Edge Attention using dot-product, Euclidean, and cosine relations, and a Transformer models long-range dependencies across 32 structures. Gated fusion combines the graph representation with U-Net bottleneck features for global age regression and structure-wise BAG estimation.

title: VDSB-GWSyn: Diffusion Schrödinger Bridge for Controllable and Anatomically Feasible Guidewire Synthesis in Coronary Angiography
motivation: Guidewire endpoint localization in coronary angiography is hindered by scarce pixel and tip annotations, weak guidewire visibility, and complex anatomical backgrounds. Existing synthesis pipelines often assume a valid guidewire mask, do not explicitly enforce vessel-feasible trajectories, and provide limited trajectory and background diversity. A controllable generator that preserves real anatomy and supplies usable masks and endpoints is needed for reliable augmentation.
method: VDSB-GWSyn first learns guidewire shape priors, then generates guidewire masks constrained by vessel segmentation while directly producing endpoint coordinates. It treats appearance synthesis as targeted inpainting on real CAG images, preserving the anatomical background, and uses a Diffusion Schrödinger Bridge conditioned with SPADE to maintain spatial alignment. Region-normalized training reduces gradient dilution caused by sparse guidewire pixels, yielding directly usable masks and coordinates for augmentation.

title: VecHeart: Holistic Four-Chamber Cardiac Anatomy Modeling via Hybrid VecSets
motivation: Holistic four-chamber cardiac modeling requires preserving each structure while capturing correlations among chambers. Existing implicit methods often model a single object or rely on expensive test-time optimization with complete surfaces, whereas clinical inputs may be sparse and omit entire chambers depending on the imaging view. A feed-forward representation that reconstructs consistent whole-heart anatomy from incomplete modalities is needed.
method: VecHeart extends VecSet-style implicit representation with part-specific queries and a Hybrid Part Transformer that alternates intra-part and inter-part attention. Anatomical Completion Masking randomly hides chambers during training so complete four-chamber anatomy can be inferred from partial observations. Modality Alignment makes codes from sparse CMR slices consistent with codes from dense surface samples, and the representation can be extended with flow matching to generate 3D+t mesh sequences.

title: VEGA: Vision Enhanced Generative Augmentation for Cross-Subject Electrocardiogram Generalization
motivation: ECG analysis suffers from substantial inter-subject morphology differences, and deep models can learn identity-related features that fail to generalize to new subjects. Domain adaptation and subject-invariant learning are often task-specific and may risk data leakage, while training high-fidelity ECG generators from scratch requires large datasets unavailable in subject-limited settings. A data-efficient, leakage-free augmentation strategy is needed for cross-subject robustness.
method: VEGA converts 1D ECG signals into 2D visual representations and uses a visual masked autoencoder pretrained on natural images to reconstruct missing regions and generate augmented signals. To adapt the generator with limited ECG data, its visual MLP and attention layers are frozen while only Layer Normalization parameters are fine-tuned with frequency-adaptive alignment. Generated signals retain the original task labels and are used to reduce distribution differences between training and unseen subjects.

title: VesselSim: learning 3D blood vessel segmentation without expert annotations
motivation: 3D blood vessel segmentation is clinically important but expert annotation is scarce because vessels have delicate geometry, low and variable contrast, and broad spatial distribution. Existing data-efficient methods still use real vascular labels, while simulation approaches may be domain-specific or lack realistic curving topology; domain shifts further reduce robustness, and 3D test-time adaptation remains underexplored. A geometry-rich synthetic training pipeline combined with annotation-free adaptation is needed for cross-domain segmentation.
method: VesselSim generates angiographic volumes from stochastic, geometry-driven simulations that model recursive branching, curvature-controlled growth, collision-aware topology, and randomized intensities. A 3D U-Net is trained only on these synthetic volumes. During inference, a self-supervised mask-reconstruction decoder performs test-time adaptation on each real scan, bridging synthetic-to-real shifts without voxel annotations or prior target-domain knowledge.

title: VigilSAM3: Reinforcement-Optimized Memory Gating for Ultra-Long Surgical Video Segmentation
motivation: Laparoscopic hepatectomy requires real-time segmentation of thin, deformable, and often occluded vascular structures and bleeding points to support safer vessel management. In ultra-long videos, severe class imbalance and intermittent target visibility make memory-based segmentation susceptible to irreversible temporal drift after corrupted predictions are stored. Existing methods do not reliably decide when a prediction should enter memory or receive correction without repeated clinician prompting.
method: VigilSAM3 builds on SAM3 with a hierarchical memory firewall that screens memory writes at pixel, class, and frame levels. A causal-Transformer agent chooses Trust, Correct, or Reset for each frame; it is initialized by supervised imitation and refined with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) using class-aware rewards. This combines autonomous correction scheduling with memory-quality gating to limit error propagation with minimal surgeon interaction.

title: VIHD: Visual Intervention-Based Hallucination Detection for Medical Visual Question Answering
motivation: Medical MLLMs can produce plausible answers that are unsupported or contradicted by visual evidence, creating risk for clinical decision-making. Supervised detectors need costly annotations, external verification adds tools and computation, and existing introspective methods rely on heuristic, context-agnostic input perturbations. A self-contained detector is needed that directly tests whether generated content depends on relevant visual evidence.
method: VIHD is a training-free hallucination detector that probes internal visual dependence during MLLM decoding. Visual Dependency Probing identifies decoder layers with strong attention to visual tokens, and Visual Intervention Decoding masks the most attended visual tokens in those layers to generate intervened responses. It fuses semantic distributions from normal and intervened samples and uses Calibrated Semantic Entropy as the hallucination signal.

title: ViPSAM: Visual Prompting Medical Image Segmentation Using Segment Anything Model
motivation: Accurate liver lesion delineation on respiratory-gated NCCT is essential for proton therapy planning but is difficult because lesions have low contrast and anatomy varies with respiration. Manual reference to contrast-enhanced MRI is time-consuming and variable, while single-modality U-Net and SAM-based approaches struggle with indistinct lesion boundaries. Automated NCCT segmentation needs to exploit the complementary information clinicians use from MRI without requiring segmentation on the contrast-enhanced image.
method: ViPSAM performs lesion segmentation on NCCT while using matched contrast-enhanced MRI only as a visual prompt. A visual prompt encoder extracts complementary contrast cues, and a visual-guided cross-attention module conditions NCCT features on those prompts to strengthen lesion-relevant representations. The SAM mask decoder is adapted with LoRA for parameter-efficient use of the visual prompts.

title: Virtual 3D H&E Staining from Phase-Contrast Back-Illumination Interference Tomography
motivation: Conventional H&E pathology examines thin 2D sections and misses much of tissue microarchitecture, whereas current 3D pathology techniques require complex preparation such as sectioning, staining, or clearing. BIT can rapidly image unprocessed tissue volumetrically, but its phase contrast differs from clinically interpretable H&E and varies with specimen position. Unsupervised virtual staining also lacks quantitative benchmarks for verifying preservation of 3D cellular structure.
method: The work introduces HistoBIT3D, a voxel-wise registered 3D BIT and fluorescence-nuclei dataset with unpaired H&E images, enabling structural validation against nuclear ground truth. Its GAN-based virtual-staining framework translates shift-variant BIT volumes to H&E using bidirectional multiscale content consistency to preserve hierarchical structure. AdaIN-based reuse of learned H&E style features improves perceptual realism across domains.

title: Vis2Reg: Visibility-Aware Landmark-Free Geometric 3D–2D Registration for Liver Laparoscopy
motivation: AR-guided laparoscopic liver surgery requires accurate alignment of preoperative 3D anatomy with intraoperative views, yet only a partial, occluded, and noisy liver surface is visible. Landmark- and correspondence-based approaches are fragile under low overlap, while learning-based methods lack abundant 3D ground-truth supervision. Existing self-supervision does not explicitly restrict deformation learning to the mask-consistent surface that is actually visible.
method: Vis2Reg is a fully self-supervised, landmark-free framework that aligns a preoperative liver model to partial intraoperative observations. It uses differentiable point rasterization and mask-guided back-projection to derive mask-consistent visible-domain 3D supervision, constraining learning to observable geometry. A robust geometric rigid initializer is combined with an implicit neural deformation field for subsequent non-rigid alignment; masks are used for supervision but are not required at inference.

title: VisiFAT: Estimating Visceral Fat from Dual-View DXA Scans Using Cross-View Attention
motivation: VAT is an important cardiometabolic-risk biomarker, but reference CT and MRI measurements are costly or difficult to scale, while anthropometric measures cannot distinguish visceral from subcutaneous fat. Routine spine DXA scans offer a low-radiation, accessible opportunity for opportunistic estimation, but prior work relies on one projection and may miss three-dimensional body-composition cues. A method that combines complementary DXA views and patient factors is needed for more generalizable VAT estimation.
method: VisiFAT estimates VAT from lateral-spine and posteroanterior-spine DXA scans plus sex, age, height, and weight. Separate partially frozen MobileNetV2 encoders preserve view-specific image features, while a demographic encoder produces a patient-level embedding. A cross-view attention module with consistency regularization adaptively exchanges and aligns complementary spatial information before regression.

title: Vision-Based Force Estimation Using Brain Surface Deformation Models
motivation: Neurosurgical training simulators need accurate haptic feedback because excessive forces can injure delicate brain tissue, yet the relevant forces are often very low. Instrumented force sensing requires specialized hardware, and FEM primarily predicts deformation from known forces rather than efficiently inferring force from observed deformation. Vision-based inverse estimation for brain tissue is therefore needed, particularly to avoid spurious high-force predictions that could yield unsafe haptic feedback.
method: D2FNet estimates spatial contact-force magnitudes from monocular brain-surface deformation fields. It is trained on FEM simulations generated in SOFA and processes normalized displacement, displacement magnitude, brain mask, and divergence features through a multiscale convolutional network with pyramid pooling and attention. An asymmetric anti-ghost loss penalizes overprediction in low-force regions to reduce erroneous high haptic-force estimates.

title: Visual-Query Curriculum Learning for Rare Fetal Biometry Plane Detection in Blind-Sweep Ultrasound Video
motivation: Blind-sweep ultrasound could broaden antenatal screening access in LMICs, but scans acquired without targeted views may not contain usable fetal-biometry content. Frames suitable for head circumference, abdominal circumference, or femur length are brief, off-axis, motion-blurred, and highly variable, making manual review burdensome and conventional frame-based detection unreliable. Automated quality assessment must cope with domain shift and extremely sparse labels to identify scans that require rapid reacquisition.
method: The method frames biometry-plane detection as visual-query-guided retrieval over long blind-sweep ultrasound videos. A spatio-temporal transformer matches a canonical query image with candidate frames, and an ultrasound-specific curriculum leverages the query under extreme label sparsity.
