Scale-robust visual encoding and domain-adversarial training transfer knowledge from a larger freehand dataset to blind sweeps.

title: VL-RewardGen: Vision–Language Reward Driven Skin Lesion Image Generation
motivation: Medical image generation can help address limited data and underrepresented rare phenotypes, but clinically useful dermatology synthesis requires control over subtle lesion attributes and their combinations. Fine-grained dermoscopic labels and diverse attribute compositions are scarce, while prior RL-based diffusion approaches depend on predefined or supervised task-specific rewards. A scalable reward signal is needed to produce images aligned with clinical concepts without requiring further attribute annotations.
method: VL-RewardGen fine-tunes a dermatology-adapted Stable Diffusion model through DDPO with parameter-efficient LoRA updates. It uses MONET, a dermatology-specific vision-language model, to score alignment between generated images and target lesion-class and dermoscopic-attribute texts. These scores form lesion and attribute rewards that directly optimize image-concept consistency without training additional supervised reward predictors.

title: VM-NeXT UNet: Synergizing ConvNeXT and Visual Mamba for Robust Medical Image Segmentation
motivation: Medical image segmentation needs both local boundary detail and broad anatomical context. CNNs are strong at local features but have limited receptive fields, whereas Transformer self-attention is expensive and can lose fine spatial detail; pure SSM Mamba-UNet still has weak local representation, noisy skip fusion, and limited small-target reconstruction. A more effective hybrid design is needed for high-resolution segmentation and hard, imbalanced cases.
method: VM-NeXT UNet combines parallel ConvNeXT and Visual Mamba/VSS encoders, using residual fusion to capture local textures and long-range dependencies. Its channel-spatial attention gating module filters skip-connection features, while decoder multi-scale convolutions support detailed reconstruction of boundaries and small targets. Training uses combined FocalLoss and DiceLoss to emphasize hard and imbalanced examples.

title: VOGeo-Gaze: Calibration-Free, Geometry-Aware Deep Learning for Real-Time Gaze Tracking in Clinical Video-Oculography
motivation: Clinical video-oculography requires accurate quantitative eye-movement measurements, but conventional systems depend on device-specific settings, camera calibration, or precise gaze labels. Existing geometric and label-driven approaches can lose robustness under headset misalignment and low-amplitude motion, while public gaze annotations may be indirect and clinically limited. A calibration-free, interpretable method that works across devices is therefore needed.
method: VOGeo-Gaze reconstructs latent anatomical eyeball parameters, including eye center, optic axis, and pupil radius, with a differentiable refraction-aware two-sphere eye model. A neural network uses segmentation supervision plus weak projection-based directional constraints, so geometric parameters and gaze can be learned without accurate angular labels. The gaze vector is derived from the reconstructed optic axis, eliminating subject-specific calibration and camera-intrinsic requirements.

title: VolDiT: Controllable Volumetric Medical Image Synthesis with Diffusion Transformers
motivation: High-fidelity volumetric medical synthesis is commonly built on 3D convolutional U-Nets, whose locality bias, costly receptive-field expansion, and repeated resampling can limit global anatomical modeling and fine-detail preservation. Hybrid transformer-convolutional methods leave fully global 3D transformer diffusion largely unexplored. A scalable architecture with flexible spatial conditioning is needed for coherent native volumetric generation.
method: VolDiT replaces the conventional 3D U-Net diffusion backbone with transformer blocks operating on tokens formed from non-overlapping volumetric latent patches. A pretrained 3D VQ-GAN supplies the compressed but reconstructable latent representation, while global self-attention models dependencies across the whole volume. Its timestep-gated control adapter converts segmentation masks into control tokens and injects them with layer-wise, diffusion-step-dependent modulation for anatomically precise conditioning.

title: Volume-Fused Super-Resolution OCT Reveals Cellular-Level Structures in the Outer Segment Across Wider Fields Without Adaptive Optics
motivation: Ophthalmic OCT volumes are affected by eye motion, distortion, illumination variation, shot noise, and speckle, which make en face structural features difficult to resolve. Adaptive-optics systems improve transverse resolution but require complex, expensive hardware, small fields, and often pupil dilation. Existing super-resolution OCT methods have limited scope and do not comprehensively model these artifacts, motivating a robust computational approach for wider-field cellular imaging.
method: The method registers repeated OCT volumes acquired with orthogonally alternating fast scan directions and compensates motion, geometric distortion, illumination variation, and artifacts to form a consistent oversampled 3D point cloud. It then solves a regularized inverse imaging problem to reconstruct a deconvolved volume with higher sample density and reduced blur. This computational pipeline enables visualization of cellular-scale outer-segment structures over a wider non-adaptive-optics field.

title: VoxShield: Protecting 3D Medical Datasets from Unauthorized Training via Frequency-Aware Inter-Slice Disruption
motivation: Public 3D medical segmentation datasets accelerate research but can be scraped and reused for unauthorized model training despite licensing restrictions. Existing unlearnable-example defenses mainly target 2D data and overlook the inter-slice anatomical consistency that 3D segmentation networks rely on. A volumetric protection method must disrupt this structural prior while preserving the visual fidelity of the released images.
method: VoxShield generates imperceptible perturbations for released 3D medical volumes using a surrogate segmentation model. Its Inter-Slice Frequency Consistency Disruption maximizes spectral differences between adjacent slices, attacking the cross-slice continuity exploited by 3D convolutions. A Semantic Prediction Disruption module additionally maximizes the L1 divergence between clean and perturbed logits, pushing the perturbation through the network to corrupt semantic predictions while remaining within an imperceptibility bound.

title: VRUGA: Visual and Reasoning Uncertainty Guided Active Learning for Medical MLLM Post-training
motivation: Medical MLLMs can answer visual questions, but unstable visual grounding and multi-step reasoning errors undermine reliability. GRPO-based post-training needs expert references, whose cost makes it essential to select high-value cases under a limited annotation budget. Standard active-learning uncertainty and similarity measures do not capture generative reasoning risk and can select redundant difficult examples that induce policy drift.
method: VRUGA first applies Dual-Uncertainty Quantification to jointly measure visual-grounding instability and reasoning-trajectory inconsistency in medical MLLM outputs. Logic-Aware Diversity Sampling then selects a non-redundant active set using decoder hidden-state embeddings that represent latent reasoning patterns. During GRPO post-training, Cross-Threshold Pseudo-Labeling combines expert corrections for high-uncertainty cases with majority-voted pseudo-label anchors from high-confidence cases to reduce policy overfitting and drift.

title: WaCT-US: Cyclic-Alignment Scaled Contour Tubes for Efficient, Calibrated Uncertainty in Echocardiography
motivation: Echocardiography artifacts and scanner variation create ambiguous boundaries, and small contour errors can substantially affect clinical measurements. Pixel-wise or sampling-heavy uncertainty methods do not match contour-based clinical workflows and are costly for real-time use. Existing conformal segmentation approaches also fail to naturally handle closed-curve indexing and local heteroscedastic ambiguity, motivating calibrated contour-native prediction sets.
method: WaCT-US predicts a segmentation contour together with a spatially varying heteroscedastic scale profile. Cyclic landmark alignment resolves the arbitrary start index of closed curves, allowing stable contour-space discrepancy computation. Split conformal calibration fits one global scale on held-out data to produce a contour tube with user-chosen marginal coverage, requiring a single forward pass and lightweight post-processing.

title: Wasserstein-Aligned Localisation for VLM-Based Distributional OOD Detection in Medical Imaging
motivation: Zero-shot VLM anomaly localization is promising for rare pathologies, but models lack healthy reference context, are sensitive to anatomical mismatch in references, and show high run-to-run variance. Random or overly similar reference selection can create biased comparisons and unstable localization. A training-free framework is needed to choose informative diverse references and aggregate spatial predictions reliably.
method: WALDO represents query and healthy-reference images as DINOv3 patch distributions and selects references using an entropy-weighted Sliced Wasserstein distance that preserves anatomical structure. It samples references from a moderate-similarity Goldilocks zone and uses a determinantal point process for diversity. The VLM performs differential prompting with these references, while confidence-weighted non-maximum suppression aggregates initial boxes and a second stage refines the final localization.

title: WaveDE: Wavelet-Routed Dual-Expert Network for Fundus Photograph Enhancement
motivation: Fundus photographs frequently contain compound degradations such as uneven illumination, blur, and noise, while many enhancement methods are designed for a single degradation and generalize poorly to mixed conditions. Enhancement also must reconcile global appearance correction with fine-detail recovery, which can create conflicting optimization objectives. A frequency-disentangled and anatomically constrained design is needed to improve both visual quality and structural fidelity.
method: WaveDE routes decoder features through a discrete wavelet transform into dedicated low- and high-frequency experts. The low-frequency expert performs global illumination and structural correction and supplies guidance to an orientation-selective high-frequency expert that restores texture while suppressing noise. A high-frequency-injected VAE decoder recovers details lost during latent compression, and frozen vessel and optic-disc teachers provide anatomical consistency regularization during training.

title: WaveDiT: Distribution-Aware Wavelet Flow Matching for Efficient 3D Brain MRI Synthesis
motivation: Full-resolution 3D brain MRI synthesis could augment scarce and demographically imbalanced cohorts, but pixel-space diffusion is computationally prohibitive and latent compression can discard subtle anatomical detail. Wavelet representations preserve invertibility, yet existing wavelet generators usually treat all subbands uniformly despite their different, input-dependent statistics. An efficient full-resolution model therefore needs frequency-aware volumetric attention and uncertainty modeling.
method: WaveDiT performs conditional flow matching directly on coefficients from a 3D Haar discrete wavelet transform, avoiding lossy learned latent compression while reducing spatial cost. Its transformer uses factorized intra-slice and inter-slice attention for volumetric modeling. The Morpheus auxiliary network predicts band-wise, state-dependent precision from higher-order wavelet statistics, and the resulting log-variance guides both the flow loss and conditioning to account for heavy-tailed, heteroscedastic detail.

title: Wavelet-Enhanced Coarse-to-Fine Radiology Report Generation with Large Language Models
motivation: Automatic chest X-ray reporting must capture subtle visual abnormalities and describe them in clinical context, but feature compression and cross-modal alignment can attenuate fine details. Most systems use a single study and underuse prior images or patient-level information, limiting diagnostic continuity. A report generator should therefore preserve detail while combining clinical context, longitudinal priors, and diagnostic supervision.
method: WERG is a coarse-to-fine multimodal LLM framework that first generates a draft report and then refines it using clinical context, prior images, and observation-aligned retrieved report snippets. Its Frequency-domain Detail Enhancement module applies wavelet decomposition to intermediate visual features, strengthening high-frequency abnormalities while retaining low-frequency anatomy. Diagnosis-Guided Visual Feature Calibration uses weak report-derived observation labels to align enhanced features with diagnostic semantics.

title: Wavelet-Guided Spectral–Spatial Learning for Medical Hyperspectral Image Segmentation
motivation: Medical hyperspectral image segmentation must jointly exploit spatial morphology and rich spectral signatures, but high dimensionality, strong inter-band redundancy, and multi-scale spectral structure make representation learning difficult. Existing methods usually flatten spectra into channels or token sequences and do not explicitly separate global biochemical trends from local variations, while high-frequency components may be less discriminative and reliable. A structured spectral representation is therefore needed for stable and effective segmentation.
method: The framework decomposes each pixel spectrum with a one-dimensional wavelet transform, separating low-frequency biochemical trends from high-frequency variations. A per-pixel adaptive gate injects the low-frequency component as a structural prior while retaining the original spectrum, and multi-scale spectral processing models local continuity. Band-Aware Aggregation fuses grouped-band features across encoder stages, while Spectral-Enhanced Skip Connections preserve spectral cues during decoding.

title: wBCAM: Windowed Bi-directional Cross-Attention with Mamba for Enhanced 3D Vascular Reconstruction in Free-Hand Photoacoustic and Ultrasound Imaging
motivation: Free-hand PAUS could provide flexible 3D vascular imaging without motorized stages or trackers, but reconstructing a coherent volume from sequential 2D frames requires accurate scan-motion estimation. The preliminary approach based on US images was not accurate enough, and small trajectory errors accumulate to disrupt microvascular continuity and topology. Methods relying only on local frame alignment also suffer from drift because they do not model long-range temporal dependencies.
method: wBCAM encodes adjacent PAUS frames into temporal local tokens processed in overlapping windows. Local-to-global cross-attention writes motion evidence into learnable global tokens, which are sequentially updated by a Mamba selective state-space module to provide long-range motion memory. Global-to-local cross-attention then feeds the updated context back to local tokens for motion-consistent estimation and reconstruction.

title: Weakly-Supervised Coronary Artery Segmentation from DSA Sequence via Motion-Aware Modeling
motivation: Coronary artery segmentation from DSA is clinically important, but single-key-frame models discard temporal contrast wash-in cues that help distinguish vessels from dark tubular artifacts and recover low-contrast segments. Existing sequence models use only a few nearby frames and commonly assume spatial alignment, so cardiac non-rigid motion causes feature blurring and misses long-range perfusion dynamics. A weakly supervised approach is needed because clinical annotations are typically available only for the maximally opacified key frame.
method: MACOS uses a shared U-Net encoder and a motion-aware GRU at multiple scales to process the full DSA sequence. The GRU estimates inter-frame displacement fields, warps the previous hidden state, and aggregates motion-aligned features before decoding the key-frame vessel map. A global motion loss supervises displacement through masked photometric consistency, while a physics-informed vessel loss regularizes unlabeled intermediate predictions using the monotonic contrast wash-in process.

title: Weakly-Supervised Temporal Decomposition with Graph Neural Networks for Parkinsonian Turning Assessment
motivation: Turning difficulty is a sensitive indicator of Parkinson’s disease because turning involves distinct stages and complex coordination, with deficits often pronounced in the late-turn phase. Existing skeleton methods globally pool sequences without exploiting these phases, or require costly frame-level phase annotations that are impractical clinically. A weakly supervised method is needed to discover diagnostically informative temporal structure from video-level labels while retaining clinical interpretability.
method: The framework detects motion-gradient transitions and uses learned soft masks to decompose a turning sequence into temporally relevant instances. Spatial-temporal graph convolutional networks process each instance, while attention aggregation combines instance-level diagnostic evidence. A learnable adjacency adapts skeleton connections, and decoupling boundary detection from classification allows the discovered phases to remain independently interpretable.

title: When Brains Disagree: Biological Ambiguity Underlies the Challenge of Amyloid PET Synthesis from Structural MRI
motivation: Amyloid PET directly measures amyloid pathology needed for Alzheimer’s diagnosis and treatment eligibility, but it is costly, less available, and exposes patients to radiation, whereas MRI is widely acquired but mainly reflects neurodegeneration. Because amyloid accumulation and neurodegeneration can be temporally decoupled, similar MRI patterns may correspond to different amyloid states, creating an intrinsically one-to-many mapping. This biological ambiguity may explain the widely inconsistent performance of MRI-to-amyloid PET synthesis and cannot necessarily be solved by increasing architectural complexity.
method: The study controls the training distribution by separating paired MRI-PET data into concordant and discordant amyloid/neurodegeneration profiles, then evaluates standard pix2pix and latent diffusion synthesis models under matched settings. A second experiment augments MRI with plasma biomarkers to provide orthogonal molecular information. Comparing these controlled conditions tests whether ambiguity, rather than architectural capacity, limits synthesis and whether multimodal input stabilizes the mapping.

title: When Does Uncertainty Become Meaningful in Medical Vision-Language Models? Alignment Enables Disease-wise Uncertainty and Risk-Aware Prediction
motivation: Chest X-ray VLMs can perform zero-shot interpretation, but clinical use requires reliable disease-wise uncertainty for selective automation and referral. Existing similarity-based uncertainty methods target single-label OOD detection and become unreliable in multi-label diagnosis, especially when affirmative and negated disease prompts are not semantically aligned; contrastive training can also produce overconfident incorrect scores. A method must align disease hypotheses and regularize evidence to make uncertainty reflect clinical decision risk.
method: Bi-EDL fine-tunes a medical VLM with bidirectional multiple-choice questions that align each image with affirmative and negated disease hypotheses. At inference, image-prompt similarities for each presence/absence pair are interpreted as evidence and parameterize a Beta distribution within evidential deep learning. This alignment and evidence regularization produce disease-wise uncertainty scores for selective prediction under normal and covariate-shifted conditions.

title: When Tissue Speaks: Vibroacoustic Monitoring of Tissue Response During Electrosurgery
motivation: During electrosurgical coagulation, surgeons must avoid both insufficient treatment and excessive thermal damage, yet tissue state is inferred mainly from visual cues that can be obscured and do not reliably reveal subsurface effects. Impedance feedback controls electrical properties but does not directly communicate local tissue state or thermal progression. Structure-borne vibrations at the tool-tissue interface could provide a non-invasive, workflow-compatible signal for monitoring coagulation and distinguishing tissue responses.
method: The study places a sensor on the proximal surgical instrument to capture structure-borne VA vibrations generated at the bipolar tool-tissue interface. It analyzes prolonged coagulation signals in time and time-frequency domains to characterize temporal phases, and compares signals from ex vivo liver, muscle, and fat to identify tissue-specific responses. Non-linear embedding is used to examine separation of tissue signatures without modifying standard instruments or workflows.

title: When Views Disagree: Conflict-Aware Evidential Inference for Multi-view Mammography
motivation: CC and MLO mammography views provide complementary evidence, but acquisition quality and anatomical coverage can differ and produce genuine diagnostic conflict. Deterministic fusion methods absorb disagreement into a shared representation and may therefore make brittle, overconfident predictions in screening. A clinically robust model should represent each view’s uncertainty and selectively moderate only the class hypotheses that conflict.
method: CEI-Net converts localized evidence from each mammography view into view-specific Dirichlet belief states. It derives view reliability from predictive uncertainty and fuses evidence with reliability-weighted, class-conditional conflict gating based on Jensen–Shannon divergence. The gating attenuates diagnostic hypotheses disputed between views while preserving evidence supported consistently or reliably by one view.

title: When, Where, and How: Adaptive Binning for Tabular Self-supervised Learning
motivation: Medical tabular data are abundant, but labels often require expert adjudication, making self-supervised representation learning valuable; heterogeneous categorical and numerical variables also lack the spatial or sequential structure exploited by other deep-learning domains. Existing binning-based tabular SSL fixes one global quantile discretization and uses feature-agnostic squared-error targets, so it cannot adapt resolution to feature learning or jointly handle ordinal and categorical structure. A training-adaptive, type-aware discretization objective is needed for effective and reproducible medical tabular SSL.
method: Adaptive Binning replaces fixed global quantiles with a feature-wise coarse-to-fine discretization curriculum during tabular pretraining. Plateau-triggered refinement determines when a feature should be split, while representation-aware selection chooses splits that improve value concentration and representation coherence. A heterogeneity-aware reconstruction objective combines categorical reconstruction with ordinal supervision for numerical variables, and the framework is evaluated through linear probing and fine-tuning under standardized medical tabular protocols.

title: Where Is the Needle Tip? VA Sensing Reveals Hidden Needle-Tissue Transitions During US Guidance
motivation: Crossing tissue boundaries is a critical event during ultrasound-guided needle procedures, but needle-tip visibility can deteriorate with insertion geometry, speckle, shadowing, or low contrast. Image localization and external tracking add limitations such as degraded robustness, extra hardware, or workflow complexity, and they do not directly measure mechanical interaction changes at boundaries. Proximal VA sensing may offer complementary transition feedback without modifying the distal needle.
method: The method records VA signals at the needle hub during synchronized ultrasound-guided insertions into layered ex vivo tissue. It computes a multiscale time-frequency representation and compares segments with tissue-specific references using first-order Wasserstein distance. A log-distance-ratio signal identifies regime changes and estimates the transition time, which can be compared with US annotations across different needle-tip visibility conditions.

title: WHO-CXRBench: A CXR Benchmark for Diagnostic Rule Retrieval in CLIP-Style MedVLMs
motivation: CLIP-style MedVLMs perform well on coarse image-level recognition and report retrieval, but similarity-based alignment does not ensure that specific diagnostic evidence is complete or clinically consistent. Real radiology workflows require findings to be linked to authoritative diagnostic rules, so fine-grained, evidence-driven retrieval needs a realistic benchmark.
method: WHO-CXRBench is a WHO-guideline-based benchmark for fine-grained diagnostic rule retrieval from patient-level CXRs. It uses an outline-guided, disease-isolated RAG pipeline and schema-constrained LLM extraction to convert guidelines into traceable structured rules, then matches report-derived personalized rules to each case. Retrieval is evaluated with ranking metrics, and the personalized rules are also tested as contextual evidence for CXR VQA.

title: Wrist Camera Pose-Guided Multi-view Fusion for Occlusion Reconstruction in Robot-Assisted Microsurgical Anastomosis
motivation: Microsurgical sutures are thin, deformable, and topologically complex, so existing segmentation methods often produce fragmented predictions or fail to infer occluded segments. Single-view completion is limited by missing information, while naïve multi-view fusion cannot handle the large 6-DoF pose variation of wrist-mounted cameras. Robust pose-aware fusion is therefore needed for fine-grained surgical perception and downstream robotic manipulation.
method: The method introduces a Camera Pose-Guided Geometry-Aware Transformer for fusing complementary wrist-camera views during occlusion reconstruction. An implicit camera-pose encoding injects 3D perspective and 2D geometric cues into patch embeddings, enabling cross-view alignment and feature aggregation despite arbitrary wrist-camera motion. A calibrated multi-view suturing-thread dataset supports evaluation across different occlusion ratios and numbers of views.

title: X2Bone: Reconstructing 3D Bone Structures from 2D Biplanar X-Rays via Cross-RWKV
motivation: Patient-specific 3D bone geometry is useful for orthopedic diagnosis and surgical planning, but CT is costly, equipment-intensive, and exposes patients to more radiation. Reconstructing from AP and LAT X-rays is clinically attractive yet ill-posed because of depth ambiguity and anatomical overlap. Existing methods inadequately model long-range structure and cross-view complementarity, causing ambiguity and missing details.
method: X2Bone is an end-to-end framework that reconstructs 3D pelvic bone structures from AP and LAT radiographs. Its Cross-RWKV module performs long-range bidirectional cross-view alignment and fusion with linear complexity, while the 3D Expand module uses view-dependent depth probability modulation to lift fused 2D features into volumetric space. Together, these components target global dependency modeling and information-preserving 2D-to-3D reconstruction.

title: X-Edit: Exact, Explicit, and Explainable Null-Space Editing for Medical Vision Transformers
motivation: Medical ViTs deployed in changing clinical environments inevitably encounter long-tail cases and domain shifts that produce misclassifications. Fine-tuning on these errors can cause catastrophic forgetting, compromising previously reliable diagnostic behavior. A controllable and interpretable intervention is needed to fix targeted failures while providing protection against collateral degradation.
method: X-Edit provides a null-space model-editing pipeline for correcting ViT predictions on newly encountered medical errors. Causal tracing first localizes influential transformer layers, after which an orthogonal null-space projection is constructed from anchor samples and used to compute an exact closed-form parameter update. The update targets edit samples while constraining anchor representations to preserve established diagnostic knowledge.

title: XTinyU-Net: Training-Free U-Net Scaling via Initialization-Time Sensitivity
motivation: Although U-Net remains highly competitive for medical segmentation, deploying it on point-of-care and portable systems requires aggressive compression. The smallest width that preserves accuracy depends on dataset properties, so exhaustive train-and-evaluate sweeps are computationally prohibitive. A training-free way to detect the dataset-specific capacity-collapse boundary is needed.
method: XTinyU-Net selects a dataset-specific U-Net width directly at initialization without training candidate models. It computes a Jacobian-based sensitivity score on a small set of unlabeled images for discretely width-capped variants, then analyzes total variation in the sensitivity curve to locate the boundary before representational collapse. The selected pre-collapse configuration is used as the lightweight XTinyU-Net within the nnU-Net protocol.

title: Zero-Shot CT Super-Resolution Using Diffusion-Based 2D Projection Priors and Signed 3D Gaussians
motivation: High-resolution CT improves diagnosis but requires higher radiation exposure, whereas low-dose acquisition reduces spatial resolution and can obscure anatomy. Supervised 3D SR depends on paired HR-LR volumes that are scarce, and existing zero-shot methods relying only on LR volumes often produce over-smoothed structures. The task needs external structural priors while retaining consistency with the measured LR data.
method: The framework performs zero-shot 3D CT super-resolution in two stages. A diffusion model trained on abundant 2D X-ray data is adapted with DDNM to upsample LR CT projections while enforcing measurement consistency. The resulting HR projections guide 3D reconstruction with Negative Alpha Blending Gaussian Splatting, which allows positive and negative Gaussian densities to represent signed residuals relative to an upsampled LR volume.
